129/// The commit the cells' source came from and whether the tree is dirty: the
130/// named `source_sha` of a Git-less snapshot (clean by construction), else
131/// what Git reports for the checkout at `root`.
132fn source_identity(root: &Path, source_sha: Option<&str>) -> Result<(String, bool), String> {
133    match source_sha {
134        Some(sha) => {
135            validate_source_snapshot(root, sha)?;
136            Ok((sha.to_string(), false))
137        }
138        None => Ok((
139            git(root, &["rev-parse", "HEAD"])?,
140            !git(root, &["status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"])?.is_empty(),
141        )),
142    }
143}
144
145/// A `--source-sha` must name one commit exactly: 40 lowercase hex digits, the
146/// spelling `git rev-parse HEAD` records in `hermit_sha`.
147pub fn validate_source_sha(sha: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
148    if sha.len() == 40
149        && sha
150            .bytes()
151            .all(|byte| matches!(byte, b'0'..=b'9' | b'a'..=b'f'))
152    {
153        Ok(())
154    } else {
155        Err(format!(
156            "--source-sha must be a full 40-digit lowercase commit sha, got {sha:?}; \
157             pass the output of `git rev-parse HEAD` for the archived commit"
158        ))
159    }
160}
161
162/// A `--source-sha` names the commit of a Git-less snapshot at `root`, which
163/// is then recorded as clean. A directory holding files Git tracks is refused:
164/// Git reports their commit and whether they are dirty, and the name would
165/// override both. A root with no `.git` at or above it (an RE worker's input
166/// tree, whether or not git is installed there) is accepted, and so is a
167/// snapshot extracted inside a checkout but not tracked by it
168/// (ci/buck-e2e/staged/src). Inside a checkout, a git that cannot answer
169/// (a corrupt index, an unusable `.git`, no git to run) is refused: the files
170/// might be tracked. The search for `.git` starts from the resolved root, so
171/// a symlink to tracked files is looked up where the files are.
172///
173/// The SHA cannot stand in for this check: it is the claim being checked, and
174/// nothing in it says whether an enclosing checkout tracks the root.
175/// [`SNAPSHOT_GIT_ENV`] may name the git to ask.
176pub fn validate_source_snapshot(root: &Path, sha: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
177    let git = std::env::var_os(SNAPSHOT_GIT_ENV)
178        .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
179        .map_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("git"), PathBuf::from);
180    validate_source_snapshot_with(root, sha, &git)
181}
182
183fn validate_source_snapshot_with(root: &Path, sha: &str, git: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
184    validate_source_sha(sha)?;
185    let resolved = std::fs::canonicalize(root).map_err(|error| {
186        format!(
187            "cannot resolve --repo-root {}: {error}; pass an existing directory",
188            root.display()
189        )
190    })?;
191    if !resolved
192        .ancestors()
193        .any(|dir| dir.join(".git").symlink_metadata().is_ok())
194    {
195        return Ok(());
196    }
197    let tracked = crate::git_environment::git_command_at(git)
198        .arg("-C")
199        .arg(root)
200        .args(["ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", "."])
201        .stdout(Stdio::null())
202        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
203        .output();
204    match tracked {
205        // `--error-unmatch` exits 1 when Git tracks nothing under the path.
206        Ok(output) if output.status.code() == Some(1) => Ok(()),
207        Ok(output) if output.status.success() => Err(format!(
208            "--source-sha names the commit of a Git-less `git archive` snapshot, but Git \
209             tracks files under {}, and Git reports their commit and whether they are dirty; \
210             drop --source-sha, or pass --repo-root naming the archive",
211            root.display()
212        )),
213        Ok(output) => Err(format!(
214            "--source-sha names the commit of a Git-less snapshot, but {} is inside a Git \
215             checkout and `git ls-files` there failed ({}: {}), so whether Git tracks its files \
216             is unknown; repair the checkout, or pass --repo-root naming an archive outside it",
217            root.display(),
218            output.status,
219            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()
220        )),
221        Err(error) => Err(format!(
222            "--source-sha names the commit of a Git-less snapshot, but {} is inside a Git \
223             checkout and git cannot run ({error}), so whether Git tracks its files is unknown; \
224             install git, or pass --repo-root naming an archive outside the checkout",
225            root.display()
226        )),
227    }
228}

233/// logger for each call, about 0.04 CPU-s against 0.015 for the one command.

240/// Closed vocabulary for manifest `requires` tokens.
241///
242/// The optional value is the host capability whose proven absence may withhold
243/// a cell. A token mapped to `None` is still validated, but can never suppress
244/// execution. Keeping the mapping here gives the manifest validator and the
245/// executable harness one authority.
246pub const REQUIRES_VOCABULARY: &[(&str, Option<HostCapability>)] = &[
247    ("ar", None),
248    ("bash", None),
249    ("cc", None),
250    ("cpuid", Some(HostCapability::CpuidFaulting)),
251    ("cxx", None),
252    ("date", None),
253    ("du", None),
254    ("find", None),
255    ("gawk", None),
256    ("git", None),
257    ("hexdump", None),
258    ("jq", None),
259    ("kvm", None),
260    ("linux", None),
261    ("lua5.4", None),
262    ("m4", None),
263    ("node", None),
264    ("openssl", None),
265    ("perl", None),
266    ("ptrace", None),
267    ("python3", None),
268    ("ruby", None),
269    ("rustc", None),
270    ("sqlite3", None),
271    ("tclsh", None),
272    ("userns", None),
273    // The host kernel exports `__vdso_getrandom` (Linux 6.11+ on x86-64). A
274    // golden that prints the vDSO getrandom leg is only reachable on such a
275    // kernel; see [`VDSO_GETRANDOM_GOLDEN_MARKER`]. Descriptive only, like
276    // `cc`: nothing probes it, so on an older kernel the cell runs and fails
277    // with the declared prerequisite named, instead of being withheld.
278    ("vdso-getrandom", None),
279    ("x86_64", None),
280    ("zstd", None),
281];
282
283/// The text tests/c/random_sources.c prints only when the host kernel exports
284/// `__vdso_getrandom`. On an older kernel it prints `vdso-getrandom
285/// unavailable` instead, so an exact golden carrying this marker has a kernel
286/// floor, and the test must declare it with the `vdso-getrandom` requires token.
287pub const VDSO_GETRANDOM_GOLDEN_MARKER: &str = "vdso-getrandom[";
288
289/// Refuse a verify golden that silently assumes a Linux 6.11+ host.
290///
291/// The manifest must say which host a golden was measured on when the golden
292/// cannot be produced elsewhere; otherwise an older-kernel FAIL reads as a
293/// determinism regression.
294pub fn validate_golden_kernel_floor(
295    id: &str,
296    requires: &[String],
297    modes: &BTreeMap<String, ModeRecipe>,
298) -> Result<(), String> {
299    if requires.iter().any(|token| token == "vdso-getrandom") {
300        return Ok(());
301    }
302    for (mode, recipe) in modes {
303        for (key, table) in [
304            ("expected_stdout", &recipe.expected_stdout),
305            ("expected_stdout_contains", &recipe.expected_stdout_contains),
306        ] {
307            if let Some(backend) = table.iter().find_map(|(backend, text)| {
308                text.contains(VDSO_GETRANDOM_GOLDEN_MARKER)
309                    .then_some(backend)
310            }) {
311                return Err(format!(
312                    "{id}: {mode} {key}.{backend} prints the vDSO getrandom leg, which only a \
313                     Linux 6.11+ host exports; declare `vdso-getrandom` in requires"
314                ));
315            }
316        }
317    }
318    Ok(())
319}

321/// The host capability a backend itself needs, independent of any `requires`
322/// token: a kvm cell cannot run where KVM is proven absent, and a cell of
323/// either in-guest LiteInst backend (`liteinst`, and `in-guest-trap`, the same
324/// runtime with syscall site patching off) cannot run where CPUID faulting is
325/// proven absent, because that runtime arms CPUID faulting before the guest's
326/// first instruction and refuses to start without it
327/// (`detcore-liteinst: initialization failed: CPUID faulting is unavailable`).
328///
329/// Each required plan row carries this capability in
330/// `requires_host_capabilities`, so the harness withholds the cell on such a
331/// host, the validation planner counts it, and the Buck cell generator
332/// (`ci/buck-e2e/defs.bzl`) runs it locally rather than on a remote execution
333/// worker, which may lack the capability.
334pub fn backend_capability(backend: &str) -> Option<HostCapability> {
335    match backend {
336        "kvm" => Some(HostCapability::Kvm),
337        "liteinst" | "in-guest-trap" => Some(HostCapability::CpuidFaulting),
338        _ => None,
339    }
340}
341
342/// CPUID faulting needed by a cell's ptrace execution, beyond its backend's
343/// unconditional requirements. Plan routing and runtime admission share this
344/// decision. Verify retains its existing host-dependent relaxed form; replay
345/// always subscribes to CPUID through the recorder/replayer subscription list.
346pub fn ptrace_cell_capability(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<HostCapability> {
347    if !matches!(cell.id.backend.as_deref(), Some("ptrace" | "e9patch")) {
348        return None;
349    }
350    let needs_cpuid = match cell.id.mode.as_str() {
351        "replay" | "chaos" => true,
352        "custom" => {
353            // Only Hermit options count: a guest argument after `--` cannot
354            // change the tracer's subscriptions or bypass its execution.
355            !cell.test.modes["custom"]
356                .args
357                .iter()
358                .take_while(|arg| arg.as_str() != "--")
359                .any(|arg| {
360                    matches!(
361                        arg.as_str(),
362                        "--no-virtualize-cpuid" | "--namespace-only" | "--lite" | "--strace-only"
363                    )
364                })
365        }
366        _ => false,
367    };
368    needs_cpuid.then_some(HostCapability::CpuidFaulting)
369}

371/// Whether a verify cell on `backend` has a relaxed form: the ptrace backend
372/// and e9patch preprocessing on it, whose verify cells this harness runs at the
373/// relaxed level ([`RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS`]) on a host without CPUID faulting or
374/// an exact retired-conditional-branch counter, and which `max_level` may cap.
375///
376/// It does not decide which cells the hermit binary refuses on an inexact
377/// counter: [`strict_run_arms_the_preemption_timer`] does, and it also names
378/// KVM, which reads the same counter for its preemption timer but has no
379/// relaxed form. Relaxing a KVM cell would turn off the preemption timer its
380/// cell was qualified with, and KVM does not need CPUID faulting, so a KVM cell
381/// is withheld on such a host instead ([`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]).
382pub fn pmu_clock_backend(backend: &str) -> bool {
383    matches!(backend, "ptrace" | "e9patch")
384}
385
386/// Whether `hermit run --strict` on `backend` arms the PMU preemption timer,
387/// whose retired-conditional-branch counter is then the run's virtual clock, so
388/// the hermit binary refuses the run where it reports no `exact_branch_counter`
389/// unless the run has no timeslice. It mirrors the CLI's capability table:
390/// hermit-cli's `backend_delivers_preemption_timer`, the backend's
391/// `delivers_preemption_timer_events` capability (ptrace, e9patch preprocessing
392/// on it, and KVM since Reverie 9443a6b2), on which
393/// `RunOpts::reads_the_branch_counter` keys the `--strict` refusal.
394///
395/// Unlike [`backend_capability`], this is decided on the machine that runs the
396/// cell and never enters a plan row: a plan row that names a host capability
397/// routes the cell off remote execution, and remote workers differ in CPU
398/// model, so the plan cannot say which of them count exactly.
399pub fn strict_run_arms_the_preemption_timer(backend: &str) -> bool {
400    matches!(backend, "ptrace" | "e9patch" | "kvm")
401}
402
403/// Whether the hermit binary refuses `cell` where it reports no
404/// `exact_branch_counter`, as `RunOpts::refuse_strict_with_inexact_branch_counter`
405/// does (hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/run.rs): the run is `--strict`, its backend
406/// arms the PMU preemption timer ([`strict_run_arms_the_preemption_timer`]:
407/// ptrace, e9patch and kvm), and it has a maximum timeslice, the condition of
408/// `RunOpts::reads_the_branch_counter`.
409///
410/// Verify and chaos cells always pass `--strict` to `run`, and replay cells to
411/// `record start`, which refuses in the same way
412/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3810>). A custom cell passes it
413/// when its arguments before any `--` say so, unless they also select
414/// `--namespace-only` (alias `--lite`), which arms no branch counter. A naked
415/// cell runs no hermit.
416///
417/// The timeslice is the one hermit resolves from the flags the cell passes
418/// ([`SelectedCell::strictness`], [`MaxTimeslice::from_options`]), so every
419/// spelling hermit reads as no timer leaves the cell unrefused: `disabled` or
420/// 0, after `=` or as the next argument, under `--max-timeslice` or its alias
421/// `--preemption-timeout`. Without a timeslice Detcore uses no branch count
422/// (Reverie still sets the counters up), so Hermit does not refuse the run
423/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4291>). A verify cell at the
424/// relaxed strictness level passes `--max-timeslice=disabled`
425/// ([`RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS`]) unless its recipe names its own timeslice, which
426/// the relaxed level then leaves in place. KVM has no relaxed form
427/// ([`pmu_clock_backend`]), so a KVM cell is refused exactly when the flags it
428/// declares leave it a timeslice.
429pub fn refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter(cell: &SelectedCell) -> bool {
430    let strict_run = match cell.id.mode.as_str() {
431        "verify" | "chaos" | "replay" => true,
432        "custom" => {
433            let options: Vec<&str> = cell.test.modes["custom"]
434                .args
435                .iter()
436                .map(String::as_str)
437                .take_while(|arg| *arg != "--")
438                .collect();
439            options.contains(&"--strict")
440                && !options.contains(&"--namespace-only")
441                && !options.contains(&"--lite")
442        }
443        _ => false,
444    };
445    strict_run
446        && cell
447            .id
448            .backend
449            .as_deref()
450            .is_some_and(strict_run_arms_the_preemption_timer)
451        && cell
452            .strictness()
453            .is_some_and(|strictness| strictness.max_timeslice != MaxTimeslice::Disabled)
454}

456pub fn requires_capability(token: &str) -> Result<Option<HostCapability>, String> {
457    REQUIRES_VOCABULARY
458        .iter()
459        .find(|(name, _)| *name == token)
460        .map(|(_, capability)| *capability)
461        .ok_or_else(|| {
462            format!(
463                "unknown `requires` token `{token}`; the vocabulary is closed and an unrecognized \
464                 name is refused rather than treated as a reason to omit a cell"
465            )
466        })
467}

529/// A `/proc` level, as Hermit's `--proc` spells it.

534    Standard,
535}
536
537impl ProcLevel {
538    /// The Hermit flag that selects this level.
539    pub fn flag(self) -> &'static str {
540        match self {
541            Self::Minimal => "--proc=minimal",
542            Self::Standard => "--proc=standard",
543        }
544    }
545}

564#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
565pub struct Observation {

567    pub stdout: bool,
568    pub stderr: bool,
569    #[serde(default)]
570    pub artifacts: Vec<String>,
571}

573/// Why a verify mode's `hermit_args` relax determinism: one reason for every
574/// backend's flags, or a mapping with one reason for each backend that has
575/// flags, so each cell's relaxation records only its own.
576#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
577#[serde(untagged)]
578pub enum HermitArgsReason {
579    Shared(String),
580    PerBackend(BTreeMap<String, String>),
581}
582
583impl HermitArgsReason {
584    /// The reason for `backend`'s flags.
585    pub fn for_backend(&self, backend: &str) -> Option<&str> {
586        match self {
587            Self::Shared(reason) => Some(reason),
588            Self::PerBackend(reasons) => reasons.get(backend).map(String::as_str),
589        }
590    }
591}
592
593impl From<&str> for HermitArgsReason {
594    fn from(reason: &str) -> Self {
595        Self::Shared(reason.to_string())
596    }
597}
598
599impl From<String> for HermitArgsReason {
600    fn from(reason: String) -> Self {
601        Self::Shared(reason)
602    }
603}

605#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
606#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
607pub struct ModeRecipe {
608    pub ci: CiSelectionSpec,
609    pub ci_disabled_reason: Option<CiDisabledReasonSpec>,
610    #[serde(default)]
611    pub backends_enabled: Vec<String>,
612    #[serde(default)]
613    pub backends_disabled: BTreeMap<String, String>,
614    #[serde(default)]
615    pub guest_args: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
616    pub workdir: Option<String>,
617    pub runs: Option<u64>,
618    pub seeds: Option<Vec<i64>>,
619    pub assert: Option<Assertions>,
620    pub outcome_classes: Option<u64>,
621    #[serde(default)]
622    pub args: Vec<String>,
623    pub compare_io_buffers: Option<bool>,
624    pub compare_io_buffers_disabled_reason: Option<String>,
625    pub rcb_time: Option<bool>,
626    pub rcb_time_disabled_reason: Option<String>,
627    #[serde(default)]
628    pub timeout_seconds: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
629    #[serde(default)]
630    pub cpu_timeout_seconds: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
631    #[serde(default)]
632    pub slow_reason: BTreeMap<String, String>,
633    pub expected_guest_exit: Option<ExpectedGuestExit>,
634    /// The exact guest stdout a verify cell requires, per enabled backend.
635    ///
636    /// A matched verify comparison proves the two runs agree with each other;
637    /// it cannot notice that both printed the same wrong bytes. Naming the
638    /// bytes here makes the cell also require both compared runs' stdout to
639    /// equal them, so declaring the same bytes for two backends of one test
640    /// makes those backends agree with each other as well.
641    #[serde(default)]
642    pub expected_stdout: BTreeMap<String, String>,
643    /// Text a verify cell's guest stdout must contain, per enabled backend.
644    ///
645    /// For output that is repeatable within one host but not byte-stable
646    /// across hosts (addresses, timing deltas), the exact bytes cannot be
647    /// declared. The cell can still require the success marker the guest
648    /// prints, so two runs that agree on output lacking it do not pass.
649    #[serde(default)]
650    pub expected_stdout_contains: BTreeMap<String, String>,
651    /// The exact guest stderr a verify cell requires, per enabled backend,
652    /// as `expected_stdout` is for stdout: a tool whose diagnostic is the
653    /// stderr half of its answer (numastat's, on a machine with no NUMA
654    /// nodes to read) has no stdout to name, and the wording is the test.
655    #[serde(default)]
656    pub expected_stderr: BTreeMap<String, String>,
657    /// Hermit `run` flags a verify cell adds after the runner's own, per
658    /// enabled backend, for a test whose recorded policy runs a specific
659    /// configuration on that backend. Only the flags in ALLOWED_HERMIT_ARGS
660    /// are accepted, each relaxes determinism, so `hermit_args_reason` is
661    /// required and both are recorded as relaxations.
662    #[serde(default)]
663    pub hermit_args: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
664    pub hermit_args_reason: Option<HermitArgsReason>,
665    /// Guest environment variables a verify cell adds, as `--env NAME=VALUE`,
666    /// after the runner's fixed guest environment. A name the runner sets is
667    /// refused rather than silently overridden. A replay cell inherits its
668    /// verify recipe's unless it declares its own; an empty mapping there
669    /// declares that it adds none. This module's private `cell_mode_env`
670    /// applies that rule.
671    #[serde(default)]
672    pub env: Option<BTreeMap<String, String>>,
673    /// Verify-only guest additions on the named enabled backend, merged with
674    /// `env` without replacing any common or runner-owned name. Replay inherits
675    /// the effective verify environment unless it declares its own `env`.
676    #[serde(default)]
677    pub env_by_backend: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
678    /// The comparison a verify cell's two runs must pass. `strict` (the
679    /// default) is the canonical full-observation comparison that can
680    /// establish L2. `stripped` is Hermit's default `--verify` comparison:
681    /// below L2, kept only for corpora whose recorded verdict policy is that
682    /// comparison, never counted as bitwise parity, and a relaxation that
683    /// requires `comparator_reason` and is recorded.
684    pub comparator: Option<Comparator>,
685    pub comparator_reason: Option<String>,
686    /// Backends on which this verify cell is a DIAGNOSTIC, each with the
687    /// standing reason: a product failure of the cell is reported and counted
688    /// as a diagnostic failure, recorded as a relaxation, and does not fail
689    /// the run. Every other outcome keeps its meaning, so an ERROR (the cell
690    /// could not produce a product verdict) still fails it. Only a
691    /// `comparator: stripped` cell may declare one: a canonical cell exists to
692    /// supply L2 evidence, and its divergence must keep failing.
693    #[serde(default)]
694    pub diagnostic: BTreeMap<String, String>,
695    /// Why a product failure of this verify cell is final. Every other cell
696    /// except a replay cell is retried once after a product failure (see
697    /// [`retries_product_failures`]); this one gets one attempt, for a corpus
698    /// whose recorded verdict was a single run (the strict compatibility
699    /// corpus), so a first-attempt failure stays a failure.
700    pub no_retry_reason: Option<String>,
701    /// Run-type labels of this mode's cell on an enabled backend, added to the
702    /// test's own `labels` for that cell only. See [`cell_labels`].
703    #[serde(default)]
704    pub labels: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
705    /// The deepest strictness level this verify cell runs at. `relaxed` caps a
706    /// test whose result does not depend on preemption or CPUID
707    /// virtualization at the relaxed level on every host, so it never has a
708    /// second, strict form ([`SelectedCell::strictness_level`]). Only
709    /// `relaxed` may be written, with `max_level_reason`, and only on a verify
710    /// mode with a ptrace or e9patch cell, the backends that have a relaxed
711    /// form.
712    pub max_level: Option<StrictnessLevel>,
713    pub max_level_reason: Option<String>,
714}

716/// The run type of a cell that names none: the full validation, whose
717/// required cells ci/expected-e2e-plan.json lists and whose bucket nodes (and
718/// the portable, hosted and quick profiles' subsets of them) select no label.
719pub const DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE: &str = "full";
720
721/// The expected-pass nightly run type. A cell earns this test-row label only
722/// after passing in the hermetic validation image at a stated head.
723pub const SUPER_RUN_TYPE: &str = "super";
724
725/// The negative-space nightly run type for tests that have not yet qualified
726/// for [`SUPER_RUN_TYPE`]. Their results structure the backlog; they are not
727/// expected-pass regression cells.
728pub const PRESSURE_RUN_TYPE: &str = "pressure";
729
730/// Manifest buckets whose every test row must carry exactly one tier marker.
731const TIERED_BUCKETS: [&str; 2] = ["gvisor", "rr"];
732
733/// The one tier marker shared by the gVisor and rr corpora and their
734/// selectors. It is authored as a test-row [`TestRecipe::labels`] value;
735/// selectors consume it through `--label super|pressure`.
736#[derive(
737    Clone,
738    Copy,
739    Debug,
740    Deserialize,
741    Serialize,
742    PartialEq,
743    Eq,
744    PartialOrd,
745    Ord
746)]
747#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
748pub enum CellTier {
749    Super,
750    Pressure,
751}
752
753impl CellTier {
754    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
755        match self {
756            Self::Super => SUPER_RUN_TYPE,
757            Self::Pressure => PRESSURE_RUN_TYPE,
758        }
759    }
760
761    fn from_labels(labels: &BTreeSet<&str>) -> Result<Option<Self>, String> {
762        match (
763            labels.contains(SUPER_RUN_TYPE),
764            labels.contains(PRESSURE_RUN_TYPE),
765        ) {
766            (true, false) => Ok(Some(Self::Super)),
767            (false, true) => Ok(Some(Self::Pressure)),
768            (false, false) => Ok(None),
769            (true, true) => Err(format!(
770                "labels contain both `{SUPER_RUN_TYPE}` and `{PRESSURE_RUN_TYPE}`"
771            )),
772        }
773    }
774}
775
776/// This cell's derived tier: `Some(Super)` or `Some(Pressure)` when the
777/// resolved labels carry that one marker, and `None` when they carry
778/// neither (every row outside the tiered buckets, and any untiered cell).
779/// A mode label can put a cell in a tier on its own: the compat corpus's
780/// heavy rows carry mode-level `super`, so their cells return
781/// `Some(CellTier::Super)` with no test-row marker. Manifest validation
782/// rejects a resolved cell carrying both markers, so a validated
783/// manifest cannot make this return an error.
784pub fn cell_tier(
785    test: &TestRecipe,
786    recipe: &ModeRecipe,
787    backend: Option<&str>,
788) -> Result<Option<CellTier>, String> {
789    CellTier::from_labels(&cell_labels(test, recipe, backend))
790        .map_err(|error| format!("{}: {error}", test.id))
791}
792
793/// The run types a cell belongs to: its test's `labels`, plus its mode's
794/// `labels` for its backend, or [`DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE`] alone when both are
795/// empty. A selection keeps a cell when the cell's run types meet the
796/// selection's `--label`s, and a selection without `--label` selects the
797/// default run type, so a cell labelled only with a focused run type (such as
798/// `sabre-compat-only`) is required there and nowhere else. On an archived
799/// backend ([`crate::archived`]) the default run type is
800/// [`crate::archived::ARCHIVED_RUN_TYPE`] instead.
801pub fn cell_labels<'a>(
802    test: &'a TestRecipe,
803    recipe: &'a ModeRecipe,
804    backend: Option<&str>,
805) -> BTreeSet<&'a str> {
806    let mut labels: BTreeSet<&str> = test.labels.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
807    if let Some(mode_labels) = backend.and_then(|backend| recipe.labels.get(backend)) {
808        labels.extend(mode_labels.iter().map(String::as_str));
809    }
810    if labels.is_empty() {
811        labels.insert(DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE);
812    }
813    if backend.is_some_and(crate::archived::is_archived_backend) && labels.remove(DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE)
814    {
815        labels.insert(crate::archived::ARCHIVED_RUN_TYPE);
816    }
817    labels
818}
819
820/// Why full validation does not select a cell whose run types exclude
821/// [`DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE`], or `None` when the cell is full's.
822pub fn focused_run_type_reason(
823    test: &TestRecipe,
824    recipe: &ModeRecipe,
825    backend: Option<&str>,
826) -> Option<String> {
827    let labels = cell_labels(test, recipe, backend);
828    (!labels.contains(DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE)).then(|| {
829        format!(
830            "Only the {} run type selects this cell, by its manifest label; full validation does not.",
831            labels.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
832        )
833    })
834}

845/// The Hermit an import run (`E2E_IMPORT_RESULTS`) compares logs with: `HERMIT_BIN`, else
846/// the Hermit ci/buck-e2e/stage staged for the imported Buck cells
847/// (`ci/buck-e2e/staged/hermit`, which `-c hermit_e2e.hermit=staged` cells run). An import
848/// runs no cell, but its parity post-pass runs `hermit log-diff`, and a Buck run builds no
849/// target/debug/hermit for it to fall back on.
850pub fn resolve_import_hermit_bin(root: &Path, hermit_bin: Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> PathBuf {
851    resolve_hermit_bin(
852        root,
853        Some(hermit_bin.unwrap_or_else(|| "ci/buck-e2e/staged/hermit".into())),
854    )
855}

857/// The Hermit the harness runs: `HERMIT_BIN`, else target/debug/hermit. A
858/// relative path names a checkout path, like the default, because cells start
859/// Hermit from their own working directories; an absolute path is kept.
860pub fn resolve_hermit_bin(root: &Path, hermit_bin: Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> PathBuf {
861    root.join(
862        hermit_bin
863            .map(PathBuf::from)
864            .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("target/debug/hermit")),
865    )
866}

868/// Whether a product failure of `cell` earns the runner's one retry: false
869/// for a replay cell and for a verify cell that declares `no_retry_reason`.
870///
871/// A replay cell records the program and replays that recording, and its
872/// product failure is a replay that diverged from the recording or a
873/// recording that did not complete. A second, fresh recording that happens to
874/// replay cleanly does not answer whether the first one did, so a replay
875/// failure is final, as it was on the retired rr lane, which ran each program
876/// once.
877pub fn retries_product_failures(cell: &SelectedCell) -> bool {
878    cell.id.mode != "replay"
879        && cell
880            .test
881            .modes
882            .get(&cell.id.mode)
883            .is_none_or(|mode| mode.no_retry_reason.is_none())
884}
885
886/// A stripped cell's report must hold the comparison it declared: Hermit's
887/// stripped log comparison, with virtual time, over a non-empty event stream
888/// on both runs. A report without one is incomplete evidence, never a pass.
889/// The scorecard admits a stripped PASS by this same rule.
890pub fn require_stripped_comparison(report: &VerificationReport) -> Result<(), String> {
891    let counts = report.compared_log_messages.as_ref();
892    let Some(comparison) = report.comparison.as_ref() else {
893        return Err(format!(
894            "stripped verification recorded no comparison at all (verdict={})",
895            report.verdict
896        ));
897    };
898    if comparison.strictness == crate::canonical_verdict::LogCompareStrictness::Stripped
899        && comparison.compare_logs
900        && comparison.virtualize_time == Some(true)
901        && counts.is_some_and(|counts| counts.left > 0 && counts.right > 0)
902    {
903        Ok(())
904    } else {
905        Err(format!(
906            "stripped verification did not compare non-vacuous stripped evidence with virtual time: strictness={} compare_logs={} virtualize_time={:?} messages={}/{}",
907            comparison.strictness,
908            comparison.compare_logs,
909            comparison.virtualize_time,
910            counts.map_or(0, |counts| counts.left),
911            counts.map_or(0, |counts| counts.right),
912        ))
913    }
914}
915
916/// The report the real Hermit wrote for `run --strict --verify
917/// --base-env=minimal -- /bin/echo hermit-compat` at hermit d44bbbb79acd
918/// (validate profile): its default, stripped comparison. One copy for every
919/// test that reads a stripped report (runner, ledger cell verdict, schema 10).
920#[cfg(test)]
921pub(crate) const PRODUCER_STRIPPED_REPORT: &str = r#"{"verified":true,"bitwise_parity":false,"verdict":"matched","no_result_reason":null,"infrastructure_error":null,"comparison":{"strictness":"stripped","display_name":"Stripped","compare_logs":true,"compare_io_buffers":true,"log_scope":"deterministic","record_envelope":"all_records_v1","virtualize_time":true,"strip_lines":true,"canonicalize_addresses":false,"full_trace":false,"exact_remainder":false,"stripped_prefixes":["real-wall-clock-prefix/v1","unsafe-numeric-address-and-path-normalization/v1"],"canonicalizations":[],"ignore_lines":false,"skip_commit":false,"skip_detlog":false},"compared_log_messages":{"left":243,"right":243},"compared_outputs":{"left":{"exit_code":0,"signal":null,"stdout_sha256":"26d1520b716304e2aab518cbf28242104d67fc9127d28c3de4193abe8aa87ba1","stdout_bytes":14,"stderr_sha256":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855","stderr_bytes":0},"right":{"exit_code":0,"signal":null,"stdout_sha256":"26d1520b716304e2aab518cbf28242104d67fc9127d28c3de4193abe8aa87ba1","stdout_bytes":14,"stderr_sha256":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855","stderr_bytes":0}},"runtime":{"run1":{"scheduler_turns":6,"virtual_nanoseconds":4126085,"syscalls":40},"run2":{"scheduler_turns":6,"virtual_nanoseconds":4126085,"syscalls":40}},"guest_exit_code":0,"guest_signal":null,"first_divergent_scheduler_turn":null,"first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds":null,"first_divergent_record":null,"first_divergent_syscall":null,"first_divergent_left_message":null,"first_divergent_right_message":null}"#;
922
923/// The comparison a verify cell requires; see [`ModeRecipe::comparator`].
924#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
925#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
926pub enum Comparator {
927    Strict,
928    Stripped,
929}
930
931/// The one guest disposition a verify cell requires: nonzero there, while
932/// a replay recipe may instead restate success where record mode answers
933/// a different disposition from run mode.
934///
935/// Hermit's default `--verify` policy rejects a first run that does not exit
936/// 0, so a guest that fails on purpose never reaches a comparison. Naming the
937/// exact status here runs the cell with `--verify-allow=failure` and then
938/// requires the report's guest disposition AND Hermit's own process status to
939/// match it, so a different code, a different signal, or a success all fail.
940///
941/// Hermit reports a guest's signal death either by dying from the same signal
942/// or, where it cannot re-raise it, by exiting `128 + signo`; both are the
943/// same disposition, and the report's `guest_signal` pins which signal it was.
944#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
945#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
946pub struct ExpectedGuestExit {
947    pub code: Option<i32>,
948    pub signal: Option<i32>,
949    pub reason: String,
950}
951
952impl ExpectedGuestExit {
953    /// Whether Hermit's own process status reports this guest disposition.
954    pub fn hermit_status_matches(&self, code: Option<i32>, signal: Option<i32>) -> bool {
955        match (self.code, self.signal) {
956            (Some(expected), None) => code == Some(expected) && signal.is_none(),
957            (None, Some(expected)) => {
958                (code.is_none() && signal == Some(expected))
959                    || (code == Some(128 + expected) && signal.is_none())
960            }
961            _ => false,
962        }
963    }
964
965    fn describe(&self) -> String {
966        match (self.code, self.signal) {
967            (Some(code), None) => format!("exit code {code}"),
968            (None, Some(signal)) => format!("signal {signal}"),
969            _ => "an invalid expectation".into(),
970        }
971    }
972
973    /// Check the completed comparison's guest disposition and Hermit's status.
974    fn check(
975        &self,
976        guest_exit_code: Option<i32>,
977        guest_signal: Option<i32>,
978        hermit_code: Option<i32>,
979        hermit_signal: Option<i32>,
980    ) -> Result<(), String> {
981        let observed = match (guest_exit_code, guest_signal) {
982            (Some(code), None) => format!("exit code {code}"),
983            (None, Some(signal)) => format!("signal {signal}"),
984            (None, None) => "no guest disposition".into(),
985            (Some(code), Some(signal)) => format!("exit code {code} and signal {signal}"),
986        };
987        if guest_exit_code != self.code || guest_signal != self.signal {
988            return Err(format!(
989                "guest ended with {observed}, but the manifest expects {}",
990                self.describe()
991            ));
992        }
993        if !self.hermit_status_matches(hermit_code, hermit_signal) {
994            let hermit = match (hermit_code, hermit_signal) {
995                (Some(code), _) => format!("exited with status {code}"),
996                (None, Some(signal)) => format!("was killed by signal {signal}"),
997                (None, None) => "reported no status".into(),
998            };
999            return Err(format!(
1000                "guest ended with {observed}, but hermit {hermit}, which does not report {}",
1001                self.describe()
1002            ));
1003        }
1004        Ok(())
1005    }
1006}
1007
1008/// The recipes a cell reads its guest inputs and expectations from, most
1009/// specific first.
1010///
1011/// `record start --verify` records and replays the same program that
1012/// `run --verify` checks, so a replay cell inherits each guest input (argv,
1013/// workdir, environment) from its verify recipe unless the replay recipe
1014/// declares that field itself. Every other mode reads only its own recipe. The
1015/// runner and the cell metadata both read through this; the expectations a
1016/// replay cell inherits are in [`expectation_recipe`].
1017fn inherited_recipes(cell: &SelectedCell) -> impl Iterator<Item = &ModeRecipe> {
1018    let verify = (cell.id.mode == "replay")
1019        .then(|| cell.test.modes.get("verify"))
1020        .flatten();
1021    cell.test.modes.get(&cell.id.mode).into_iter().chain(verify)
1022}
1023
1024/// The first value `pick` finds in [`inherited_recipes`].
1025fn inherited<'a, T>(
1026    cell: &'a SelectedCell,
1027    pick: impl FnMut(&'a ModeRecipe) -> Option<T>,
1028) -> Option<T> {
1029    inherited_recipes(cell).find_map(pick)
1030}
1031
1032/// The recipe whose declared stdout (and, absent a replay override, guest
1033/// exit) a cell's verdict checks.
1034///
1035/// Validation admits stdout declarations only on a verify recipe, so a replay
1036/// cell reads its verify recipe's, and no other mode has any; the same field
1037/// on another mode's recipe is not authority for a pass there. A replay
1038/// recipe may declare its own guest exit instead (see
1039/// [`cell_expected_guest_exit`]).
1040fn expectation_recipe(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<&ModeRecipe> {
1041    if cell.id.mode == "replay" {
1042        // A replay recipe that declares its own guest exit restates record
1043        // mode's expectations whole: its stream declarations (or their
1044        // absence) govern, not the verify recipe's.
1045        let own = cell
1046            .test
1047            .modes
1048            .get("replay")
1049            .filter(|recipe| recipe.expected_guest_exit.is_some());
1050        if own.is_some() {
1051            return own;
1052        }
1053        return cell.test.modes.get("verify");
1054    }
1055    matches!(cell.id.mode.as_str(), "verify")
1056        .then(|| cell.test.modes.get("verify"))
1057        .flatten()
1058}
1059
1060/// The guest arguments a selected cell runs on `backend`.
1061pub(crate) fn cell_guest_args(cell: &SelectedCell, backend: &str) -> Vec<String> {
1062    inherited(cell, |recipe| recipe.guest_args.get(backend).cloned()).unwrap_or_default()
1063}

1065/// The guest working directory a selected cell names, if any.
1066pub(crate) fn cell_workdir(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
1067    inherited(cell, |recipe| recipe.workdir.clone())
1068}

1070/// The guest environment variables a selected cell adds after the runner's own.
1071///
1072/// Verify merges common `env` with only this backend's additions. A replay
1073/// recipe's declared `env`, even an empty one, replaces the effective verify
1074/// environment rather than inheriting variables it was never meant to carry.
1075fn cell_mode_env(cell: &SelectedCell) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
1076    inherited(cell, |recipe| {
1077        let backend_env = cell
1078            .id
1079            .backend
1080            .as_ref()
1081            .and_then(|backend| recipe.env_by_backend.get(backend));
1082        if recipe.env.is_none() && backend_env.is_none() {
1083            return None;
1084        }
1085        let mut env = recipe.env.clone().unwrap_or_default();
1086        if let Some(additions) = backend_env {
1087            env.extend(additions.clone());
1088        }
1089        Some(env)
1090    })
1091    .unwrap_or_default()
1092}

1094/// The declared guest disposition for a selected verify or replay cell.
1095///
1096/// A replay recipe's own declaration wins for its cell, so record mode can
1097/// require success (or another exact disposition) where its verify recipe
1098/// requires a failure; without one a replay cell inherits verify's, as
1099/// `expectation_recipe` chooses for its stdout.
1100pub fn cell_expected_guest_exit(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<ExpectedGuestExit> {
1101    expectation_recipe(cell)?.expected_guest_exit.clone()
1102}

1104/// The exact stdout a selected verify or replay cell requires, if its backend declares one.
1105fn cell_expected_stdout(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
1106    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_ref()?;
1107    expectation_recipe(cell)?
1108        .expected_stdout
1109        .get(backend)
1110        .cloned()
1111}

1113/// The stdout text a selected verify or replay cell must contain, if its backend declares one.
1114fn cell_expected_stdout_contains(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
1115    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_ref()?;
1116    expectation_recipe(cell)?
1117        .expected_stdout_contains
1118        .get(backend)
1119        .cloned()
1120}

1122/// The exact stderr a selected verify or replay cell requires, if its backend declares one.
1123fn cell_expected_stderr(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
1124    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_ref()?;
1125    expectation_recipe(cell)?
1126        .expected_stderr
1127        .get(backend)
1128        .cloned()

1131/// Both stdout assertions a selected verify or replay cell declares for its
1132/// backend, in the form a skid attempt records them ([`DeclaredStdout`]).
1133pub fn cell_declared_stdout(cell: &SelectedCell) -> DeclaredStdout {
1134    DeclaredStdout {
1135        exact: cell_expected_stdout(cell),
1136        contains: cell_expected_stdout_contains(cell),
1137        stderr_exact: cell_expected_stderr(cell),
1138    }

1141/// A per-backend stdout assertion is verify-only and keyed by enabled backends.
1142///
1143/// A key for a disabled backend would be an assertion that ordinary runs never
1144/// execute, so it is refused rather than kept as a silent, unchecked claim.
1145fn validate_verify_stdout_table(
1146    id: &str,
1147    mode: &str,
1148    key: &str,
1149    table: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
1150    enabled: &BTreeSet<&str>,
1151) -> Result<(), String> {
1152    if table.is_empty() {
1153        return Ok(());
1154    }
1155    if mode != "verify" {
1156        return Err(format!("{id}: {key} is supported only by verify mode"));
1157    }
1158    for backend in table.keys() {
1159        if !enabled.contains(backend.as_str()) {
1160            return Err(format!(
1161                "{id}: verify {key} names backend {backend} outside backends_enabled"
1162            ));
1163        }
1164    }
1165    Ok(())
1166}
1167
1168/// `expected_stdout` is a verify-only assertion keyed by enabled backends.
1169pub fn validate_expected_stdout(
1170    id: &str,
1171    mode: &str,
1172    expected: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
1173    enabled: &BTreeSet<&str>,
1174) -> Result<(), String> {
1175    validate_verify_stdout_table(id, mode, "expected_stdout", expected, enabled)
1176}
1177
1178/// `expected_stdout_contains` is verify-only, keyed by enabled backends, and
1179/// names non-empty text: every stream contains the empty string, so an empty
1180/// declaration would read as an assertion while checking nothing.
1181pub fn validate_expected_stdout_contains(
1182    id: &str,
1183    mode: &str,
1184    contains: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
1185    enabled: &BTreeSet<&str>,
1186) -> Result<(), String> {
1187    validate_verify_stdout_table(id, mode, "expected_stdout_contains", contains, enabled)?;
1188    if let Some(backend) = contains
1189        .iter()
1190        .find_map(|(backend, text)| text.is_empty().then_some(backend))
1191    {
1192        return Err(format!(
1193            "{id}: verify expected_stdout_contains.{backend} must not be empty"
1194        ));
1195    }
1196    Ok(())
1197}
1198
1199/// Why a verify report does not satisfy a declared `expected_stdout`.
1200#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
1201enum ExpectedStdoutError {
1202    /// The report has no per-run outputs, so the assertion cannot be decided.
1203    Unevidenced(String),
1204    /// A compared run printed different bytes.
1205    Mismatch(String),
1206}
1207
1208/// The reason a verify attempt FAILs when the `run` ("first" or "second")
1209/// compared run's stdout is not the cell's declared `expected_stdout`.
1210///
1211/// This text is the only record of that failure: the attempt carries no
1212/// timeout and no error kind. The scorecard reader
1213/// (ci/compat-envelope/scorecard.rs) and the series `failed_match` evidence
1214/// recognize it through [`parse_expected_output_failure_reason`], which
1215/// rebuilds it with this function, so the writer and the readers share one
1216/// spelling.
1217pub fn expected_stdout_mismatch_reason(
1218    run: &str,
1219    observed_bytes: u64,
1220    observed_sha256: &str,
1221    expected_bytes: u64,
1222    expected_sha256: &str,
1223) -> String {
1224    format!(
1225        "verify {run} run stdout ({observed_bytes} bytes, sha256 {observed_sha256}) differs from the declared expected_stdout ({expected_bytes} bytes, sha256 {expected_sha256})"
1226    )
1227}
1228
1229/// The reason a verify attempt FAILs when its captured stdout, which equals
1230/// both compared runs' stdout, omits the cell's declared
1231/// `expected_stdout_contains` text. Shared with the scorecard reader exactly
1232/// as [`expected_stdout_mismatch_reason`] is.
1233/// The reason a verify attempt FAILs when a compared run's stderr is not the
1234/// declared `expected_stderr` bytes. Shared with the scorecard reader exactly
1235/// as [`expected_stdout_mismatch_reason`] is.
1236pub fn expected_stderr_mismatch_reason(
1237    run: &str,
1238    observed_bytes: u64,
1239    observed_sha256: &str,
1240    expected_bytes: u64,
1241    expected_sha256: &str,
1242) -> String {
1243    format!(
1244        "verify {run} run stderr ({observed_bytes} bytes, sha256 {observed_sha256}) differs from the declared expected_stderr ({expected_bytes} bytes, sha256 {expected_sha256})"
1245    )
1246}
1247
1248pub fn expected_stdout_contains_mismatch_reason(
1249    captured_bytes: u64,
1250    captured_sha256: &str,
1251    text: &str,
1252) -> String {
1253    format!(
1254        "verify stdout ({captured_bytes} bytes, sha256 {captured_sha256}) does not contain the declared expected_stdout_contains text {text:?}"
1255    )
1256}
1257
1258/// What a reason written by [`expected_stdout_mismatch_reason`] or
1259/// [`expected_stdout_contains_mismatch_reason`] says. The scorecard reader and
1260/// the series `failed_match` evidence both recognize those reasons through
1261/// [`parse_expected_output_failure_reason`], so the runner, the scorecard and
1262/// the series schema share one spelling and one parser.
1263#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
1264pub enum ExpectedOutputFailureReason {
1265    /// The named compared run's stdout is not the declared exact bytes.
1266    Exact {
1267        run: String,
1268        observed_bytes: u64,
1269        observed_sha256: String,
1270        declared_bytes: u64,
1271        declared_sha256: String,
1272    },
1273    /// The named compared run's stderr is not the declared exact bytes.
1274    ExactStderr {
1275        run: String,
1276        observed_bytes: u64,
1277        observed_sha256: String,
1278        declared_bytes: u64,
1279        declared_sha256: String,
1280    },
1281    /// The captured stdout, which equals both compared runs' stdout, omits
1282    /// the declared text.
1283    Contains {
1284        captured_bytes: u64,
1285        captured_sha256: String,
1286        text: String,
1287    },
1288}
1289
1290impl ExpectedOutputFailureReason {
1291    /// Why the runner could not have written this reason for a verify
1292    /// attempt whose two compared runs matched, judged from the reason alone,
1293    /// or `None`. The runner names the first run whose stdout differs, and
1294    /// both runs of a matched pair print the same bytes; it fails only
1295    /// declared stdout that differs from the observed stdout; and it finds an
1296    /// empty declared text in any stdout.
1297    pub fn contradiction(&self) -> Option<&'static str> {
1298        match self {
1299            Self::Exact {
1300                run,
1301                observed_bytes,
1302                observed_sha256,
1303                declared_bytes,
1304                declared_sha256,
1305            } => {
1306                if !is_lower_sha256(observed_sha256) || !is_lower_sha256(declared_sha256) {
1307                    Some("a stdout digest is not SHA-256")
1308                } else if run != "first" {
1309                    Some(
1310                        "it names a later run, but the first run of a matched pair printed the same bytes",
1311                    )
1312                } else if observed_bytes == declared_bytes && observed_sha256 == declared_sha256 {
1313                    Some("the declared stdout is the observed stdout")
1314                } else {
1315                    None
1316                }
1317            }
1318            Self::ExactStderr {
1319                run,
1320                observed_bytes,
1321                observed_sha256,
1322                declared_bytes,
1323                declared_sha256,
1324            } => {
1325                if !is_lower_sha256(observed_sha256) || !is_lower_sha256(declared_sha256) {
1326                    Some("a stderr digest is not SHA-256")
1327                } else if run != "first" {
1328                    Some(
1329                        "it names a later run, but the first run of a matched pair printed the same bytes",
1330                    )
1331                } else if observed_bytes == declared_bytes && observed_sha256 == declared_sha256 {
1332                    Some("the declared stderr is the observed stderr")
1333                } else {
1334                    None
1335                }
1336            }
1337            Self::Contains {
1338                captured_sha256,
1339                text,
1340                ..
1341            } => {
1342                if !is_lower_sha256(captured_sha256) {
1343                    Some("the stdout digest is not SHA-256")
1344                } else if text.is_empty() {
1345                    Some("the runner finds an empty declared text in any stdout")
1346                } else {
1347                    None
1348                }
1349            }
1350        }
1351    }
1352}
1353
1354fn is_lower_sha256(value: &str) -> bool {
1355    value.len() == 64
1356        && value
1357            .bytes()
1358            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&byte))
1359}
1360
1361/// Split `<bytes> bytes, sha256 <digest>)<rest>`.
1362fn split_sized_digest(text: &str) -> Option<(u64, &str, &str)> {
1363    let (bytes, rest) = text.split_once(" bytes, sha256 ")?;
1364    let (digest, rest) = rest.split_once(')')?;
1365    Some((bytes.parse().ok()?, digest, rest))
1366}
1367
1368/// Invert Rust's `{:?}` rendering of a string, which is how the runner quotes
1369/// a declared expected_stdout_contains text. The caller still requires the
1370/// re-rendered reason to reproduce the original exactly, so a lenient decode
1371/// here cannot admit a text the runner would not write.
1372fn parse_debug_string(quoted: &str) -> Option<String> {
1373    let inner = quoted.strip_prefix('"')?.strip_suffix('"')?;
1374    let mut text = String::new();
1375    let mut chars = inner.chars();
1376    while let Some(character) = chars.next() {
1377        match character {
1378            '"' => return None,
1379            '\\' => text.push(match chars.next()? {
1380                't' => '\t',
1381                'r' => '\r',
1382                'n' => '\n',
1383                '0' => '\0',
1384                '\\' => '\\',
1385                '"' => '"',
1386                '\'' => '\'',
1387                'u' => {
1388                    let (hex, rest) = chars.as_str().strip_prefix('{')?.split_once('}')?;
1389                    let decoded = char::from_u32(u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?)?;
1390                    chars = rest.chars();
1391                    decoded
1392                }
1393                _ => return None,
1394            }),
1395            other => text.push(other),
1396        }
1397    }
1398    Some(text)
1399}
1400
1401/// Recognize the runner's reason for a failed stdout expectation, or `None`
1402/// for any other text. Only a reason that the runner's own formatter
1403/// rebuilds byte for byte is recognized.
1404pub fn parse_expected_output_failure_reason(reason: &str) -> Option<ExpectedOutputFailureReason> {
1405    if let Some(rest) = reason.strip_prefix("verify stdout (") {
1406        let (captured_bytes, captured_sha256, rest) = split_sized_digest(rest)?;
1407        let quoted =
1408            rest.strip_prefix(" does not contain the declared expected_stdout_contains text ")?;
1409        let text = parse_debug_string(quoted)?;
1410        (expected_stdout_contains_mismatch_reason(captured_bytes, captured_sha256, &text) == reason)
1411            .then(|| ExpectedOutputFailureReason::Contains {
1412                captured_bytes,
1413                captured_sha256: captured_sha256.into(),
1414                text,
1415            })
1416    } else if reason.contains(" run stderr (") {
1417        let (run, rest) = reason
1418            .strip_prefix("verify ")?
1419            .split_once(" run stderr (")?;
1420        let (observed_bytes, observed_sha256, rest) = split_sized_digest(rest)?;
1421        let rest = rest.strip_prefix(" differs from the declared expected_stderr (")?;
1422        let (declared_bytes, declared_sha256, rest) = split_sized_digest(rest)?;
1423        (rest.is_empty()
1424            && expected_stderr_mismatch_reason(
1425                run,
1426                observed_bytes,
1427                observed_sha256,
1428                declared_bytes,
1429                declared_sha256,
1430            ) == reason)
1431            .then(|| ExpectedOutputFailureReason::ExactStderr {
1432                run: run.into(),
1433                observed_bytes,
1434                observed_sha256: observed_sha256.into(),
1435                declared_bytes,
1436                declared_sha256: declared_sha256.into(),
1437            })
1438    } else {
1439        let (run, rest) = reason
1440            .strip_prefix("verify ")?
1441            .split_once(" run stdout (")?;
1442        let (observed_bytes, observed_sha256, rest) = split_sized_digest(rest)?;
1443        let rest = rest.strip_prefix(" differs from the declared expected_stdout (")?;
1444        let (declared_bytes, declared_sha256, rest) = split_sized_digest(rest)?;
1445        (rest.is_empty()
1446            && expected_stdout_mismatch_reason(
1447                run,
1448                observed_bytes,
1449                observed_sha256,
1450                declared_bytes,
1451                declared_sha256,
1452            ) == reason)
1453            .then(|| ExpectedOutputFailureReason::Exact {
1454                run: run.into(),
1455                observed_bytes,
1456                observed_sha256: observed_sha256.into(),
1457                declared_bytes,
1458                declared_sha256: declared_sha256.into(),
1459            })
1460    }
1461}
1462
1463/// Compare both runs a verify report compared with the declared stdout bytes.
1464///
1465/// The report carries each run's stdout digest and length, so the check needs
1466/// no captured stream: a run whose stdout differs in any byte fails. A report
1467/// without per-run outputs cannot satisfy the assertion and is never a pass.
1468fn check_expected_stdout(
1469    expected: &str,
1470    report: &VerificationReport,
1471) -> Result<(), ExpectedStdoutError> {
1472    let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
1473        ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(
1474            "verification report omitted compared_outputs, so the declared expected_stdout cannot be checked".into(),
1475        )
1476    })?;
1477    let expected_sha256 = hex_digest(expected.as_bytes());
1478    let expected_bytes = expected.len() as u64;
1479    for (run, output) in [("first", &outputs.left), ("second", &outputs.right)] {
1480        if output.stdout_sha256 != expected_sha256 || output.stdout_bytes != expected_bytes {
1481            return Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(
1482                expected_stdout_mismatch_reason(
1483                    run,
1484                    output.stdout_bytes,
1485                    &output.stdout_sha256,
1486                    expected_bytes,
1487                    &expected_sha256,
1488                ),
1489            ));
1490        }
1491    }
1492    Ok(())
1493}
1494
1495/// Compare both runs a verify report compared with the declared stderr bytes,
1496/// as [`check_expected_stdout`] does for stdout.
1497fn check_expected_stderr(
1498    expected: &str,
1499    report: &VerificationReport,
1500) -> Result<(), ExpectedStdoutError> {
1501    let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
1502        ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(
1503            "verification report omitted compared_outputs, so the declared expected_stderr cannot be checked".into(),
1504        )
1505    })?;
1506    let expected_sha256 = hex_digest(expected.as_bytes());
1507    let expected_bytes = expected.len() as u64;
1508    for (run, output) in [("first", &outputs.left), ("second", &outputs.right)] {
1509        if output.stderr_sha256 != expected_sha256 || output.stderr_bytes != expected_bytes {
1510            return Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(
1511                expected_stderr_mismatch_reason(
1512                    run,
1513                    output.stderr_bytes,
1514                    &output.stderr_sha256,
1515                    expected_bytes,
1516                    &expected_sha256,
1517                ),
1518            ));
1519        }
1520    }
1521    Ok(())
1522}
1523
1524/// Require the captured verify stdout to contain the declared text.
1525///
1526/// The report describes both compared runs' stdout only by digest and length,
1527/// so the captured stream is evidence for both runs only when it equals both of
1528/// them; only then is the text searched for. A capture that is not those bytes,
1529/// or a report without per-run outputs, decides nothing and is never a pass.
1530fn check_expected_stdout_contains(
1531    text: &str,
1532    captured: &[u8],
1533    report: &VerificationReport,
1534) -> Result<(), ExpectedStdoutError> {
1535    let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
1536        ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(
1537            "verification report omitted compared_outputs, so the declared expected_stdout_contains cannot be checked".into(),
1538        )
1539    })?;
1540    let captured_sha256 = hex_digest(captured);
1541    let captured_bytes = captured.len() as u64;
1542    for (run, output) in [("first", &outputs.left), ("second", &outputs.right)] {
1543        if output.stdout_sha256 != captured_sha256 || output.stdout_bytes != captured_bytes {
1544            return Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(format!(
1545                "captured verify stdout ({captured_bytes} bytes, sha256 {captured_sha256}) is not the {run} compared run's stdout ({} bytes, sha256 {}), so the declared expected_stdout_contains cannot be checked",
1546                output.stdout_bytes, output.stdout_sha256
1547            )));
1548        }
1549    }
1550    let needle = text.as_bytes();
1551    if needle.is_empty()
1552        || captured
1553            .windows(needle.len())
1554            .any(|window| window == needle)
1555    {
1556        Ok(())
1557    } else {
1558        Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(
1559            expected_stdout_contains_mismatch_reason(captured_bytes, &captured_sha256, text),
1560        ))
1561    }
1562}
1563
1564/// The first declared stdout assertion of `spec` that the compared runs of
1565/// `report` do not satisfy: the exact `expected_stdout`
1566/// ([`check_expected_stdout`]), then the `expected_stdout_contains` text
1567/// searched in the verify stdout captured at `stdout_path`
1568/// ([`check_expected_stdout_contains`]). `None` when the cell declares
1569/// neither or every declared assertion holds.
1570fn declared_stdout_error(
1571    spec: &CellRunSpec,
1572    report: &VerificationReport,
1573    stdout_path: &Path,
1574) -> Option<ExpectedStdoutError> {
1575    if let Some(Err(error)) = spec
1576        .expected_stdout
1577        .as_deref()
1578        .map(|expected| check_expected_stdout(expected, report))
1579    {
1580        return Some(error);
1581    }
1582    if let Some(Err(error)) = spec
1583        .expected_stderr
1584        .as_deref()
1585        .map(|expected| check_expected_stderr(expected, report))
1586    {
1587        return Some(error);
1588    }
1589    spec.expected_stdout_contains
1590        .as_deref()
1591        .and_then(|text| match fs::read(stdout_path) {
1592            Ok(captured) => check_expected_stdout_contains(text, &captured, report).err(),
1593            Err(error) => Some(ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(format!(
1594                "cannot read captured verify stdout {}: {error}, so the declared expected_stdout_contains cannot be checked",
1595                stdout_path.display()
1596            ))),
1597        })
1598}
1599
1600pub fn validate_expected_guest_exit(
1601    id: &str,
1602    mode: &str,
1603    expected: Option<&ExpectedGuestExit>,
1604) -> Result<(), String> {
1605    let Some(expected) = expected else {
1606        return Ok(());
1607    };
1608    if !matches!(mode, "verify" | "replay") {
1609        return Err(format!(
1610            "{id}: expected_guest_exit is supported only by verify and replay modes"
1611        ));
1612    }
1613    match (expected.code, expected.signal) {
1614        // A replay declaration restates record mode's disposition, which
1615        // may be the success a verify declaration cannot name.
1616        (Some(code), None) if mode == "replay" && (0..=255).contains(&code) => {}
1617        (Some(code), None) if (1..=255).contains(&code) => {}
1618        (Some(code), None) => {
1619            return Err(format!(
1620                "{id}: {mode} expected_guest_exit.code must be an exit status in {}..=255, not {code}",
1621                if mode == "replay" { 0 } else { 1 }
1622            ));
1623        }
1624        (None, Some(signal)) if (1..=64).contains(&signal) => {}
1625        (None, Some(signal)) => {
1626            return Err(format!(
1627                "{id}: {mode} expected_guest_exit.signal must be a signal number in 1..=64, not {signal}"
1628            ));
1629        }
1630        _ => {
1631            return Err(format!(
1632                "{id}: {mode} expected_guest_exit must name exactly one of code or signal"
1633            ));
1634        }
1635    }
1636    if expected.reason.trim().is_empty() {
1637        return Err(format!(
1638            "{id}: {mode} expected_guest_exit.reason must be substantive"
1639        ));
1640    }
1641    Ok(())
1642}
1643
1644/// Check a declared guest exit that a result row, or a series row built from
1645/// one, carries in `mode`. A replay cell carries its own replay recipe's
1646/// declaration where it has one, else its verify recipe's
1647/// ([`cell_expected_guest_exit`]), and passes on it only through the verify
1648/// cell's gate (a matched canonical replay whose guest and Hermit both end
1649/// exactly that way), so a row is checked by its own mode's rules.
1650pub fn validate_result_expected_guest_exit(
1651    id: &str,
1652    mode: &str,
1653    expected: Option<&ExpectedGuestExit>,
1654) -> Result<(), String> {
1655    validate_expected_guest_exit(id, mode, expected)
1656}
1657
1658/// Whether `hermit_args`, an attempt's argv before the guest separator, is an
1659/// invocation the runner writes for a cell whose declared nonzero exit it
1660/// checks: a verify cell's comparison with `--verify-allow=failure`, or a
1661/// replay cell's `record start`, whose comparison takes `--verify-allow=both`
1662/// (`verified_invocation_argv`). A reader re-deciding a declared exit from a
1663/// retained row requires one of these.
1664pub fn invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit<S: AsRef<str>>(mode: &str, hermit_args: &[S]) -> bool {
1665    let has = |flag: &str| hermit_args.iter().any(|arg| arg.as_ref() == flag);
1666    match mode {
1667        "verify" => has("--verify-allow=failure"),
1668        "replay" => {
1669            has("--verify-allow=both")
1670                && hermit_args
1671                    .windows(2)
1672                    .any(|pair| pair[0].as_ref() == "record" && pair[1].as_ref() == "start")
1673        }
1674        _ => false,
1675    }
1676}

1703const SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_E2E_SCHEDULED_JOBS";
1704const ISOLATED_WORKDIR_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_E2E_EMPTY_WORKDIR";
1705const HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR: &str = "/test";
1706const FIXED_GUEST_WORKDIR: &str = "/tmp/test";
1707const FIXED_WORKDIR_SOURCE_DIR: &str = "workdir";
1708
1709/// One per-cell input directory a verify cell binds to a fixed guest path.
1710#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
1711pub struct EqualizedInput {
1712    /// The directory below the cell directory (`prepare_dirs` creates it).
1713    pub cell_subdir: &'static str,
1714    /// The guest environment variable that names the directory.
1715    pub env: &'static str,
1716    /// Where the guest sees the directory: below [`EQUALIZED_INPUT_ROOT`].
1717    pub guest_path: &'static str,
1718}
1719
1720/// Guest directory below which a verify cell's per-cell inputs are bound.
1721///
1722/// Every cell runs from its own directory, and that directory's name contains
1723/// the backend (see [`cell_artifact_path`]). Handing the guest those host
1724/// paths gives the ptrace and candidate runs of one test a different HOME,
1725/// XDG_CONFIG_HOME, fixture directory and program path, and those strings
1726/// alone make ptrace diverge from ptrace: 16 of 18 pairs in the S0 control
1727/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301#issuecomment-5874842696>).
1728/// Binding each directory to the same guest path, and naming only guest paths
1729/// in the guest's environment and argv, gives every backend the same
1730/// guest-visible inputs. The dbt backend applies `--bind` in its own per-run
1731/// mount namespace (`common/test-workdir`), which needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so a
1732/// dbt cell runs in the pinned root.
1733///
1734/// It is below guest `/tmp` because `--bind` accepts only targets there;
1735/// every such guest gets a private tmpfs `/tmp`, in which the bind targets
1736/// are created.
1737pub const EQUALIZED_INPUT_ROOT: &str = "/tmp/e2e";
1738
1739/// The inputs bound below [`EQUALIZED_INPUT_ROOT`], in argv order.
1740pub const EQUALIZED_INPUTS: [EqualizedInput; 3] = [
1741    EqualizedInput {
1742        cell_subdir: "home",
1743        env: "HOME",
1744        guest_path: "/tmp/e2e/home",
1745    },
1746    EqualizedInput {
1747        cell_subdir: "xdg-config",
1748        env: "XDG_CONFIG_HOME",
1749        guest_path: "/tmp/e2e/xdg-config",
1750    },
1751    EqualizedInput {
1752        cell_subdir: "fixtures",
1753        env: "E2E_FIXTURE_DIR",
1754        guest_path: "/tmp/e2e/fixtures",
1755    },
1756];
1757
1758/// Whether a cell's guest is given the equalized inputs.
1759///
1760/// Only `verify` cells are, on every backend, because only they are compared
1761/// across backends (the parity post-pass). Other modes keep the host paths
1762/// they always had.
1763pub fn equalizes_guest_inputs(mode: &str) -> bool {
1764    mode == "verify"
1765}
1766
1767/// The guest path of a host path at or below one of `cell_dir`'s equalized
1768/// input directories, or `None` for any other value.
1769fn equalized_guest_path(cell_dir: &Path, value: &str) -> Option<String> {
1770    EQUALIZED_INPUTS.iter().find_map(|input| {
1771        let host = cell_dir.join(input.cell_subdir);
1772        let host = host.to_str()?;
1773        if value == host {
1774            Some(input.guest_path.to_string())
1775        } else {
1776            value
1777                .strip_prefix(host)
1778                .filter(|rest| rest.starts_with('/'))
1779                .map(|rest| format!("{}{rest}", input.guest_path))
1780        }
1781    })
1782}
1783
1784/// Where a verify guest sees the validation's compatibility fixtures,
1785/// `{{VALIDATE_RUN_STATE}}/strict-compat/real-compat-fixtures` on the host.
1786pub const COMPAT_FIXTURES_GUEST_PATH: &str = "/tmp/e2e/compat-fixtures";
1787
1788/// Where a verify guest sees the repository checkout, `{{ROOT_DIR}}` on the
1789/// host.
1790pub const REPOSITORY_GUEST_PATH: &str = "/tmp/e2e/repo";
1791
1792/// The compatibility fixtures, below the validation's run-state directory.
1793const COMPAT_FIXTURES_RUN_STATE_SUBDIR: &str = "strict-compat/real-compat-fixtures";
1794
1795/// A host directory outside the cell directory that a verify cell's argv may
1796/// name, and the guest path it is bound at when it does.
1797///
1798/// The ptrace reference and each candidate backend run as separate cells.
1799/// Under Buck each cell has its own run-state directory and its own bundle
1800/// checkout, so a fixture or repository file named by its host path is a
1801/// different string in every cell, and the parity post-pass diverged on the
1802/// path alone: 22 cells in the f406d84f validation
1803/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4337>). Naming the guest path
1804/// instead gives every run of the test the same arguments.
1805#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
1806struct EqualizedRoot {
1807    host: String,
1808    guest: &'static str,
1809    /// Host directories below `host` that it does not cover: the harness's
1810    /// own per-run trees, whose paths would still differ from cell to cell.
1811    except: Vec<String>,
1812}
1813
1814/// The equalized roots of `context` with run-state directory `run_state`,
1815/// the most specific first: the fixtures are below the run state, which is
1816/// commonly below the checkout. The checkout root does not cover the
1817/// harness's result, build and run-state trees.
1818fn equalized_roots(context: &RunContext, run_state: Option<&OsStr>) -> Vec<EqualizedRoot> {
1819    let text = |path: &Path| path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
1820    let run_state = run_state.filter(|state| !state.is_empty()).map(Path::new);
1821    let mut roots = Vec::new();
1822    if let Some(state) = run_state {
1823        roots.push(EqualizedRoot {
1824            host: text(&state.join(COMPAT_FIXTURES_RUN_STATE_SUBDIR)),
1825            guest: COMPAT_FIXTURES_GUEST_PATH,
1826            except: Vec::new(),
1827        });
1828    }
1829    roots.push(EqualizedRoot {
1830        host: text(&context.root),
1831        guest: REPOSITORY_GUEST_PATH,
1832        except: [
1833            Some(context.result_root.as_path()),
1834            Some(context.build_root.as_path()),
1835            run_state,
1836        ]
1837        .into_iter()
1838        .flatten()
1839        .map(text)
1840        .collect(),
1841    });
1842    roots
1843}
1844
1845/// `value` with the host directory `host` replaced by `guest`, when `value`
1846/// is that directory or a path below it.
1847fn rebased(host: &str, guest: &str, value: &str) -> Option<String> {
1848    if value == host {
1849        Some(guest.to_string())
1850    } else {
1851        value
1852            .strip_prefix(host)
1853            .filter(|rest| rest.starts_with('/'))
1854            .map(|rest| format!("{guest}{rest}"))
1855    }
1856}
1857
1858/// `guest_argv` with each argument that names a path in one of the cell's
1859/// equalized input directories, or below one of `roots`, rewritten to its
1860/// guest path, so the program is launched as `/tmp/e2e/fixtures/program`. An
1861/// environment assignment (`env NAME=PATH`) has its value rewritten the same
1862/// way. A path embedded in any other longer argument is left alone; it still
1863/// names a host file the guest can read, and the parity post-pass then sees
1864/// unequal argv and reports the comparison as not equalized. Also returns the
1865/// roots some argument named, which the run must bind.
1866fn equalized_guest_argv(
1867    cell_dir: &Path,
1868    roots: &[EqualizedRoot],
1869    guest_argv: Vec<String>,
1870) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<EqualizedRoot>) {
1871    let mut named = Vec::new();
1872    let mut rewrite = |value: &str| -> Option<String> {
1873        equalized_guest_path(cell_dir, value).or_else(|| {
1874            roots.iter().find_map(|root| {
1875                if root
1876                    .except
1877                    .iter()
1878                    .any(|except| rebased(except, "", value).is_some())
1879                {
1880                    return None;
1881                }
1882                let rewritten = rebased(&root.host, root.guest, value)?;
1883                if !named.contains(root) {
1884                    named.push(root.clone());
1885                }
1886                Some(rewritten)
1887            })
1888        })
1889    };
1890    let argv = guest_argv
1891        .into_iter()
1892        .map(|arg| {
1893            if let Some(rewritten) = rewrite(&arg) {
1894                return rewritten;
1895            }
1896            match arg.split_once('=') {
1897                Some((name, value)) if is_environment_name(name) => rewrite(value)
1898                    .map(|value| format!("{name}={value}"))
1899                    .unwrap_or(arg),
1900                _ => arg,
1901            }
1902        })
1903        .collect();
1904    (argv, named)
1905}
1906
1907/// Whether `name` can be an environment variable's name, as `env NAME=VALUE`
1908/// takes it.
1909fn is_environment_name(name: &str) -> bool {
1910    let mut chars = name.chars();
1911    chars
1912        .next()
1913        .is_some_and(|first| first == '_' || first.is_ascii_alphabetic())
1914        && chars.all(|c| c == '_' || c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
1915}
1916
1917/// The cell environment as the guest of an equalized cell sees it: each
1918/// equalized variable names its guest path. The row keeps the host paths,
1919/// which name where the directories really are.
1920fn equalized_guest_env(env: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
1921    let mut env = env.clone();
1922    for input in EQUALIZED_INPUTS {
1923        env.insert(input.env.into(), input.guest_path.into());
1924    }
1925    env
1926}
1927
1928/// Bind each equalized input directory of `cell_dir` to its guest path, and
1929/// each equalized root the cell's argv names.
1930fn append_equalized_input_binds(argv: &mut Vec<String>, cell_dir: &Path, roots: &[EqualizedRoot]) {
1931    for input in EQUALIZED_INPUTS {
1932        argv.push(format!(
1933            "--bind={}:{}",
1934            cell_dir.join(input.cell_subdir).to_string_lossy(),
1935            input.guest_path
1936        ));
1937    }
1938    for root in roots {
1939        argv.push(format!("--bind={}:{}", root.host, root.guest));
1940    }
1941}
1942
1943fn fixed_workdir_source_for_attempt(cell_dir: &Path, attempt: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
1944    let mut components = Path::new(attempt).components();
1945    let is_one_normal_component = matches!(
1946        (components.next(), components.next()),
1947        (Some(Component::Normal(component)), None) if component == OsStr::new(attempt)
1948    );
1949    if !is_one_normal_component {
1950        return Err(format!(
1951            "invalid attempt label {attempt:?}: expected exactly one normal path component"
1952        ));
1953    }
1954    Ok(cell_dir.join(FIXED_WORKDIR_SOURCE_DIR).join(attempt))
1955}

1976    /// needs. Those cells stay in the local `full` and `portable` profiles; the

1981    pub execution_backends: Option<BTreeSet<String>>,

1983    /// committed caller is the quick profile's pinned-root verify smoke, which

1986    pub exclude_categories: Vec<String>,

1990    /// at least one of these labels; when empty, the default run type's.
1991    pub labels: Vec<String>,
1992    /// Every run type's cells, ignoring `labels`: a census of the cells in
1993    /// the manifest (the metadata export), not a run of one run type.
1994    pub all_run_types: bool,

1996    /// (`with_parity_inputs`), so its log can be compared with ptrace's.
1997    pub parity_inputs: bool,
