1999
2000/// The in-guest backends refuse a preemption timer: every verify cell of
2001/// theirs that the manifests enable runs with this flag.
2002const IN_GUEST_PARITY_HERMIT_ARGS: &[&str] = &["--max-timeslice=disabled"];
2003/// The recorded reason for the in-guest parity probe flag (`--max-timeslice=disabled`).
2004pub const PARITY_PROBE_HERMIT_ARGS_REASON: &str = "Parity probe of a disabled cell: in-guest \
2005     LiteInst refuses a preemption timer, so the probe runs this backend with the maximum \
2006     timeslice disabled, as every enabled cell of it runs";
2007
2008/// `test` with its disabled verify cell on `backend` given ptrace's inputs, for
2009/// a parity probe (`test-harness run --probe-disabled --parity-inputs`, which
2010/// `ci/compat-envelope/pressure-test.rs run --parity-all` uses): ptrace's
2011/// guest arguments where the manifest names none for `backend`, and on
2012/// liteinst and in-guest-trap the `--max-timeslice=disabled` every enabled
2013/// cell of theirs carries, with its own reason. A parity comparison needs the
2014/// same guest arguments on both sides, and an in-guest probe without the flag
2015/// is only a refusal. The probe keeps the cell's own wall and CPU budget, the
2016/// one the pressure test sizes its enclosing allowance from. Nothing the
2017/// manifest declares for `backend` is replaced, and an enabled cell is never
2018/// touched.
2019fn with_parity_inputs(test: &TestRecipe, backend: &str) -> TestRecipe {
2020    let mut test = test.clone();
2021    let Some(verify) = test.modes.get_mut("verify") else {
2022        return test;
2023    };
2024    if verify
2025        .backends_enabled
2026        .iter()
2027        .any(|enabled| enabled == backend)
2028        || !verify
2029            .backends_enabled
2030            .iter()
2031            .any(|enabled| enabled == "ptrace")
2032    {
2033        return test;
2034    }
2035    if let Some(args) = verify.guest_args.get("ptrace").cloned() {
2036        verify.guest_args.entry(backend.to_string()).or_insert(args);
2037    }
2038    if matches!(backend, "liteinst" | "in-guest-trap") && !verify.hermit_args.contains_key(backend)
2039    {
2040        verify.hermit_args.insert(
2041            backend.to_string(),
2042            IN_GUEST_PARITY_HERMIT_ARGS
2043                .iter()
2044                .map(|arg| arg.to_string())
2045                .collect(),
2046        );
2047        // The probe's flag carries its own reason. A shared reason written
2048        // for the other backends' flags is kept for exactly those backends.
2049        let reason = PARITY_PROBE_HERMIT_ARGS_REASON.to_string();
2050        let mut reasons = match verify.hermit_args_reason.take() {
2051            None => BTreeMap::new(),
2052            Some(HermitArgsReason::PerBackend(reasons)) => reasons,
2053            Some(HermitArgsReason::Shared(shared)) => verify
2054                .hermit_args
2055                .keys()
2056                .filter(|flagged| flagged.as_str() != backend)
2057                .map(|flagged| (flagged.clone(), shared.clone()))
2058                .collect(),
2059        };
2060        reasons.insert(backend.to_string(), reason);
2061        verify.hermit_args_reason = Some(HermitArgsReason::PerBackend(reasons));
2062    }
2063    test
2064}

2084/// How deep a cell's run goes. A host with a PMU and CPUID faulting runs every

2086/// which adds [`RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS`]; a verify cell may cap itself at the
2087/// relaxed level ([`ModeRecipe::max_level`]). One run per test, at the deepest
2088/// level the host and the cell allow, and the row records which
2089/// ([`CellResult::strictness`]).
2090#[derive(
2091    Clone,

2095    Deserialize,

2102#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]

2111impl StrictnessLevel {

2119
2120/// How one cell ran: its strictness level and the Hermit settings it ran
2121/// with, recorded on its result row ([`CellResult::strictness`]) and its
2122/// series observation.
2123#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
2124#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
2125pub struct CellStrictness {

2127    /// Whether Hermit virtualized CPUID (no `--no-virtualize-cpuid`).
2128    pub virtualize_cpuid: bool,
2129    /// The preemption timeslice Hermit ran with: its `--max-timeslice`, or
2130    /// Hermit's default when the cell passed none.
2131    pub max_timeslice: MaxTimeslice,
2132    /// Whether the cell's recipe caps it at the relaxed level
2133    /// ([`ModeRecipe::max_level`]).
2134    pub capped: bool,
2135}
2136
2137/// A `--max-timeslice` value: `"disabled"` in JSON, or the timeslice in
2138/// virtual nanoseconds as a number.
2139#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
2140pub enum MaxTimeslice {
2141    Disabled,
2142    Nanoseconds(u64),
2143}
2144
2145/// The long names `hermit run` takes its maximum timeslice under: the flag
2146/// and its alias, `#[clap(long, visible_alias = "preemption-timeout")]` on
2147/// `Config::max_timeslice` in detcore-model/src/config.rs. clap accepts each
2148/// as `--NAME=VALUE` or as `--NAME VALUE`, and no abbreviation of either.
2149pub const MAX_TIMESLICE_FLAGS: [&str; 2] = ["--max-timeslice", "--preemption-timeout"];
2150
2151impl MaxTimeslice {
2152    /// A maximum-timeslice value as hermit reads it, or why hermit refuses
2153    /// it. This restates detcore-model's `parse_timeslice`
2154    /// (detcore-model/src/config.rs), the flag's clap `value_parser`: a
2155    /// number as `str::parse::<u64>` reads it, so `00` and `+0` are numbers
2156    /// too, where 0 turns the timer off and 1 to 9 are below one RCB
2157    /// (`NANOS_PER_RCB`, 10 virtual nanoseconds); or the word `disabled`.
2158    /// Anything else is refused.
2159    pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
2160        let one_rcb = detcore_model::time::NANOS_PER_RCB as u64;
2161        match value.parse::<u64>() {
2162            Ok(0) => Ok(Self::Disabled),
2163            Ok(nanoseconds) if nanoseconds < one_rcb => Err(format!(
2164                "`{value}` is below one RCB ({one_rcb} virtual nanoseconds), which hermit refuses"
2165            )),
2166            Ok(nanoseconds) => Ok(Self::Nanoseconds(nanoseconds)),
2167            Err(_) if value == "disabled" => Ok(Self::Disabled),
2168            Err(_) => Err(format!(
2169                "`{value}` is neither `disabled` nor a non-negative integer, which hermit refuses"
2170            )),
2171        }
2172    }
2173
2174    /// The maximum timeslice `hermit run` resolves from `options`, its
2175    /// command-line options in order, or `Ok(None)` where none names it and
2176    /// hermit runs with `MaxTimeslice::hermit_default`. An option is either
2177    /// name in [`MAX_TIMESLICE_FLAGS`] with its value after `=` or in the next
2178    /// element, read by [`MaxTimeslice::parse`]; nothing after a `--` is an
2179    /// option. As clap does, this refuses a second occurrence under either
2180    /// name ("cannot be used multiple times"), a name whose next element is
2181    /// missing or starts with `-`, and a value hermit refuses.
2182    pub fn from_options(options: &[String]) -> Result<Option<Self>, String> {
2183        let mut resolved = None;
2184        let mut options = options.iter().take_while(|option| option.as_str() != "--");
2185        while let Some(option) = options.next() {
2186            let value = if MAX_TIMESLICE_FLAGS.contains(&option.as_str()) {
2187                match options.next() {
2188                    Some(value) if !value.starts_with('-') => value.as_str(),
2189                    _ => return Err(format!("`{option}` has no value, which hermit refuses")),
2190                }
2191            } else if let Some(value) = MAX_TIMESLICE_FLAGS.iter().find_map(|flag| {
2192                option
2193                    .strip_prefix(flag)
2194                    .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_prefix('='))
2195            }) {
2196                value
2197            } else {
2198                continue;
2199            };
2200            if resolved.is_some() {
2201                return Err(format!(
2202                    "`{option}` names the maximum timeslice a second time ({} are one \
2203                     option), which hermit refuses",
2204                    MAX_TIMESLICE_FLAGS.join(" and ")
2205                ));
2206            }
2207            resolved = Some(Self::parse(value).map_err(|error| format!("`{option}`: {error}"))?);
2208        }
2209        Ok(resolved)
2210    }
2211
2212    /// The timeslice Hermit runs with when it is given no `--max-timeslice`.
2213    fn hermit_default() -> Self {
2214        detcore_model::config::Config::default()
2215            .max_timeslice
2216            .map_or(Self::Disabled, |nanoseconds| {
2217                Self::Nanoseconds(nanoseconds.get())
2218            })
2219    }
2220}
2221
2222impl Serialize for MaxTimeslice {
2223    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
2224        match self {
2225            Self::Disabled => serializer.serialize_str("disabled"),
2226            Self::Nanoseconds(nanoseconds) => serializer.serialize_u64(*nanoseconds),
2227        }
2228    }
2229}
2230
2231impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for MaxTimeslice {
2232    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
2233        #[derive(Deserialize)]
2234        #[serde(untagged)]
2235        enum Repr {
2236            Word(String),
2237            Nanoseconds(u64),
2238        }
2239        match Repr::deserialize(deserializer)? {
2240            Repr::Word(word) if word == "disabled" => Ok(Self::Disabled),
2241            Repr::Word(word) => Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!(
2242                "max_timeslice must be \"disabled\" or a positive number, got {word:?}"
2243            ))),
2244            Repr::Nanoseconds(0) => Err(serde::de::Error::custom(
2245                "max_timeslice must be \"disabled\" or a positive number, got 0",
2246            )),
2247            Repr::Nanoseconds(nanoseconds) => Ok(Self::Nanoseconds(nanoseconds)),
2248        }
2249    }
2250}

2252/// The strictness level a host runs, and why when it is not strict.
2253#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
2254pub struct HostLevel {
2255    pub level: StrictnessLevel,
2256    /// Why the host runs the relaxed level; `None` at the strict level.
2257    pub reason: Option<String>,
2258}
2259
2260/// The environment variable that makes a host run the relaxed level although
2261/// it could run the strict one. Its only accepted value is `relaxed`: nothing
2262/// can make a host without the capabilities run the strict level.
2263pub const STRICTNESS_LEVEL_ENV: &str = "E2E_STRICTNESS_LEVEL";
2264
2265/// The Hermit `run` flags a verify cell adds at the relaxed level: CPUID
2266/// virtualization off, which needs CPUID faulting, and the preemption timer
2267/// off, which needs an exact retired-branch counter. Without the timer
2268/// `hermit run --strict` does not refuse an inexact counter.
2269pub const RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS: [&str; 2] = ["--no-virtualize-cpuid", "--max-timeslice=disabled"];
2270
2271/// The strictness level of this host: relaxed when it lacks CPUID faulting,
2272/// when the hermit binary reports its retired-branch counter inexact, or when
2273/// `forced` (the value of [`STRICTNESS_LEVEL_ENV`]) is `relaxed`; strict
2274/// otherwise. A binary that gives no counter verdict does not relax the host,
2275/// as it does not make a cell HOST-INAPPLICABLE. Any other forced value is
2276/// refused.
2277pub fn host_strictness(
2278    host_capabilities: &HostCapabilities,
2279    exact_branch_counter: Option<&CapabilityVerdict>,
2280    forced: Option<&str>,
2281) -> Result<HostLevel, String> {
2282    let relaxed = |reason: String| HostLevel {
2283        level: StrictnessLevel::Relaxed,
2284        reason: Some(reason),
2285    };
2286    match forced {
2287        None | Some("") => {}
2288        Some("relaxed") => return Ok(relaxed(format!("{STRICTNESS_LEVEL_ENV}=relaxed"))),
2289        Some(other) => {
2290            return Err(format!(
2291                "{STRICTNESS_LEVEL_ENV} must be `relaxed` or unset, got {other:?}; a host runs the \
2292                 strict level whenever it can, and nothing can make it run the strict level when \
2293                 it cannot"
2294            ));
2295        }
2296    }
2297    let mut missing = Vec::new();
2298    match host_capabilities.get(&HostCapability::CpuidFaulting) {
2299        Some(verdict) if verdict.present => {}
2300        Some(verdict) => missing.push(format!("no CPUID faulting ({})", verdict.evidence)),
2301        None => missing.push("no CPUID faulting verdict".to_string()),
2302    }
2303    // No verdict is not a verdict of absence: like the HOST-INAPPLICABLE
2304    // rule ([`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]'s caller), the level
2305    // relaxes only where the binary reported the counter inexact.
2306    if let Some(verdict) = exact_branch_counter.filter(|verdict| !verdict.present) {
2307        missing.push(format!("no exact branch counter ({})", verdict.evidence));
2308    }
2309    Ok(if missing.is_empty() {
2310        HostLevel::default()
2311    } else {
2312        relaxed(format!("this host has {}", missing.join(" and ")))
2313    })
2314}
2315
2316impl SelectedCell {
2317    /// The strictness level this cell runs at, or `None` for a naked cell,
2318    /// which runs no Hermit.
2319    ///
2320    /// Only a verify cell on a backend with a relaxed form ([`pmu_clock_backend`]:
2321    /// ptrace and e9patch) runs relaxed: on a relaxed host, or when its recipe
2322    /// caps it. Every other cell runs as declared, at the strict level; a KVM
2323    /// cell with a timeslice, or a chaos or replay cell, that needs the counter
2324    /// is not run on a host without it ([`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]).
2325    pub fn strictness_level(&self) -> Option<StrictnessLevel> {
2326        (self.id.mode != "naked").then(|| {
2327            if self.relaxed_level_reason().is_some() {
2328                StrictnessLevel::Relaxed
2329            } else {
2330                StrictnessLevel::Strict
2331            }
2332        })
2333    }
2334
2335    /// How this cell runs ([`CellStrictness`]), or `None` for a naked cell.
2336    /// The settings are read from the Hermit flags the cell passes: a verify
2337    /// cell's recipe flags, level flags and probe flag, or a custom cell's
2338    /// arguments. Chaos and replay cells pass none. The timeslice is the one
2339    /// hermit resolves from them ([`MaxTimeslice::from_options`]).
2340    pub fn strictness(&self) -> Option<CellStrictness> {
2341        let level = self.strictness_level()?;
2342        let recipe = &self.test.modes[&self.id.mode];
2343        let flags: Vec<String> = match (self.id.mode.as_str(), self.id.backend.as_deref()) {
2344            ("verify", Some(backend)) => cell_hermit_args(recipe, backend)
2345                .iter()
2346                .cloned()
2347                .chain(
2348                    self.level_relaxations()
2349                        .into_iter()
2350                        .map(|(arg, _)| arg.to_string()),
2351                )
2352                .chain(probe_relaxation(self, backend).map(str::to_string))
2353                .collect(),
2354            ("custom", _) => recipe.args.clone(),
2355            _ => Vec::new(),
2356        };
2357        // The timeslice hermit resolves from these flags. Manifest validation
2358        // refuses timeslice flags hermit would refuse, so the default stands
2359        // in only where no flag names one, or for a cell built without that
2360        // validation.
2361        let max_timeslice = MaxTimeslice::from_options(&flags)
2362            .ok()
2363            .flatten()
2364            .unwrap_or_else(MaxTimeslice::hermit_default);
2365        Some(CellStrictness {
2366            level,
2367            virtualize_cpuid: !flags.iter().any(|flag| flag == "--no-virtualize-cpuid"),
2368            max_timeslice,
2369            capped: self.id.mode == "verify" && recipe.max_level == Some(StrictnessLevel::Relaxed),
2370        })
2371    }
2372
2373    /// Why this cell runs at the relaxed level, or `None` when it does not.
2374    /// The cell's own cap is named first: it holds on every host.
2375    fn relaxed_level_reason(&self) -> Option<String> {
2376        if self.id.mode != "verify" || !self.id.backend.as_deref().is_some_and(pmu_clock_backend) {
2377            return None;
2378        }
2379        let recipe = &self.test.modes[&self.id.mode];
2380        if recipe.max_level == Some(StrictnessLevel::Relaxed) {
2381            return Some(format!(
2382                "the cell caps itself at the relaxed level: {}",
2383                recipe
2384                    .max_level_reason
2385                    .as_deref()
2386                    .unwrap_or("reason missing")
2387            ));
2388        }
2389        (self.host_level.level == StrictnessLevel::Relaxed).then(|| {
2390            format!(
2391                "the host runs the relaxed level: {}",
2392                self.host_level
2393                    .reason
2394                    .as_deref()
2395                    .unwrap_or("reason missing")
2396            )
2397        })
2398    }
2399
2400    /// The [`RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS`] this cell adds at the relaxed level, each
2401    /// with the reason, leaving out a flag its recipe already declares.
2402    pub fn level_relaxations(&self) -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {
2403        let Some(reason) = self.relaxed_level_reason() else {
2404            return Vec::new();
2405        };
2406        let declared = self
2407            .id
2408            .backend
2409            .as_deref()
2410            .map(|backend| cell_hermit_args(&self.test.modes[&self.id.mode], backend))
2411            .unwrap_or_default();
2412        let flag_name = |arg: &str| arg.split_once('=').map_or(arg, |(flag, _)| flag).to_owned();
2413        RELAXED_LEVEL_ARGS
2414            .into_iter()
2415            .filter(|arg| {
2416                !declared
2417                    .iter()
2418                    .any(|declared| flag_name(declared) == flag_name(arg))
2419            })
2420            .map(|arg| (arg, reason.clone()))
2421            .collect()
2422    }
2423}
2424
2425/// Named manifest bytes captured once for shared parsing and provenance.
2426/// Keeping these inputs together prevents a consumer from hashing one revision
2427/// while independently parsing another revision at the same paths.
2428pub(crate) struct ManifestInputs {
2429    sources: Vec<(PathBuf, String)>,
2430}
2431
2432impl ManifestInputs {
2433    pub(crate) fn read(root: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
2434        let dir = root.join("tests/e2e/manifests");
2435        let defaults_path = dir.join(DEFAULTS_FILE);
2436        let defaults_source = fs::read_to_string(&defaults_path)
2437            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", defaults_path.display()))?;
2438        let mut paths = fs::read_dir(&dir)
2439            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", dir.display()))?
2440            .map(|entry| {
2441                entry
2442                    .map(|entry| entry.path())
2443                    .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read an entry in {}: {e}", dir.display()))
2444            })
2445            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?
2446            .into_iter()
2447            .filter(|path| {
2448                path.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "yaml")
2449                    && path.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name != DEFAULTS_FILE)
2450            })
2451            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2452        paths.sort();
2453        if paths.is_empty() {
2454            return Err(format!("no YAML manifests found in {}", dir.display()));
2455        }
2456        let mut sources = vec![(defaults_path, defaults_source)];
2457        for path in paths {
2458            let source = fs::read_to_string(&path)
2459                .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
2460            sources.push((path, source));
2461        }
2462        sources.sort_by(|left, right| left.0.cmp(&right.0));
2463        Ok(Self { sources })
2464    }
2465
2466    pub(crate) fn named_sources(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&Path, &str)> {
2467        self.sources
2468            .iter()
2469            .map(|(path, source)| (path.as_path(), source.as_str()))
2470    }
2471}
2472
2473fn bucket_image(set: &ManifestSet, category: &str) -> Option<String> {
2474    set.documents
2475        .iter()
2476        .find(|document| document.bucket == category)
2477        .and_then(|document| document.image.clone())
2478}
2479
2480impl ManifestSet {
2481    pub fn load(root: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
2482        Self::from_inputs(root, &ManifestInputs::read(root)?)
2483    }
2484
2485    pub(crate) fn from_inputs(root: &Path, inputs: &ManifestInputs) -> Result<Self, String> {
2486        let (defaults_path, defaults_source) = inputs
2487            .named_sources()
2488            .find(|(path, _)| path.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name == DEFAULTS_FILE))
2489            .ok_or_else(|| "captured manifest inputs lack defaults.yaml".to_string())?;
2490        let defaults: ManifestDefaults = serde_yaml::from_str(defaults_source)
2491            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: invalid YAML: {e}", defaults_path.display()))?;
2492        if defaults.schema != MANIFEST_SCHEMA {
2493            return Err(format!(
2494                "{}: schema must be {MANIFEST_SCHEMA}",
2495                defaults_path.display()
2496            ));
2497        }
2498        let global_timeout_seconds =
2499            validate_timeout_seconds(defaults.timeout_seconds, "global default")?;
2500        let global_cpu_timeout_seconds =
2501            validate_timeout_seconds(defaults.cpu_timeout_seconds, "global CPU default")?;
2502        let mut nextest_filters = BTreeSet::new();
2503        for timeout in &defaults.nextest {
2504            if timeout.filter.trim().is_empty() {
2505                return Err("nextest timeout filter must not be empty".into());
2506            }
2507            validate_timeout_seconds(timeout.timeout_seconds, &timeout.filter)?;
2508            if timeout.timeout_seconds == global_timeout_seconds {
2509                return Err(format!(
2510                    "nextest timeout {} redundantly repeats the global default",
2511                    timeout.filter
2512                ));
2513            }
2514            if timeout.slow_reason.trim().is_empty() {
2515                return Err(format!(
2516                    "nextest timeout {} requires a non-empty slow_reason",
2517                    timeout.filter
2518                ));
2519            }
2520            if !nextest_filters.insert(timeout.filter.as_str()) {
2521                return Err(format!(
2522                    "duplicate nextest timeout filter: {}",
2523                    timeout.filter
2524                ));
2525            }
2526        }
2527        let mut documents = Vec::new();
2528        let mut tests = BTreeMap::new();
2529        for (path, source) in inputs
2530            .named_sources()
2531            .filter(|(path, _)| path.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name != DEFAULTS_FILE))
2532        {
2533            let document: ManifestDocument = serde_yaml::from_str(source)
2534                .map_err(|e| format!("{}: invalid YAML: {e}", path.display()))
2535                .and_then(|value| {
2536                    crate::manifest_corpus::expand_corpus(value)
2537                        .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
2538                })
2539                .and_then(|value| {
2540                    serde_yaml::from_value(value)
2541                        .map_err(|e| format!("{}: invalid manifest: {e}", path.display()))
2542                })?;
2543            let stem = path.file_stem().and_then(OsStr::to_str).unwrap_or_default();
2544            validate_document_with_cpu(
2545                &document,
2546                stem,
2547                root,
2548                global_timeout_seconds,
2549                global_cpu_timeout_seconds,
2550            )?;
2551            let bucket_timeout_seconds =
2552                resolve_timeout_seconds(global_timeout_seconds, document.timeout_seconds, None);
2553            for test in &document.test {
2554                if tests
2555                    .insert(
2556                        test.id.clone(),
2557                        (
2558                            document.bucket.clone(),
2559                            bucket_timeout_seconds,
2560                            global_cpu_timeout_seconds,
2561                            test.clone(),
2562                        ),
2563                    )
2564                    .is_some()
2565                {
2566                    return Err(format!("duplicate test id: {}", test.id));
2567                }
2568            }
2569            documents.push(document);
2570        }
2571        Ok(Self { documents, tests })
2572    }
2573
2574    /// Is `id` a test this manifest set has ever heard of?
2575    ///
2576    /// ⚠️ THIS EXISTS TO SEPARATE "NO CELLS" FROM "NO SUCH TEST". `select` returns an
2577    /// empty vector for both, and they mean opposite things: an unfiltered population
2578    /// that is legitimately empty ("no gaps") versus a filter naming something that
2579    /// does not exist (a typo). A caller that cannot tell them apart must either
2580    /// refuse a good answer or accept a meaningless one.
2581    pub fn knows_test(&self, id: &str) -> bool {
2582        self.tests.contains_key(id)
2583    }
2584
2585    pub fn select(&self, selection: &Selection) -> Result<Vec<SelectedCell>, String> {
2586        // A label no cell carries is a typo, not an empty run type: with
2587        // --allow-empty it would otherwise select nothing and pass.
2588        if let Some(label) = selection.labels.iter().find(|label| {
2589            !self.tests.values().any(|(_, _, _, test)| {
2590                test.modes.values().any(|recipe| {
2591                    std::iter::once(None)
2592                        .chain(recipe.backends_enabled.iter().map(|b| Some(b.as_str())))
2593                        .any(|backend| cell_labels(test, recipe, backend).contains(label.as_str()))
2594                })
2595            })
2596        }) {
2597            return Err(format!("--label {label} names no test in any manifest"));
2598        }
2599        // Without --label, a selection is the default run type's.
2600        let wanted_labels: BTreeSet<&str> = if selection.labels.is_empty() {
2601            BTreeSet::from([DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE])
2602        } else {
2603            selection.labels.iter().map(String::as_str).collect()
2604        };
2605        let labelled = |test: &TestRecipe, recipe: &ModeRecipe, backend: Option<&str>| {
2606            selection.all_run_types
2607                || !cell_labels(test, recipe, backend).is_disjoint(&wanted_labels)
2608        };
2609        // An excluded category no manifest has is a typo that would exclude nothing.
2610        if let Some(category) = selection.exclude_categories.iter().find(|category| {
2611            !self
2612                .tests
2613                .values()
2614                .any(|(bucket, _, _, _)| bucket == *category)
2615        }) {
2616            return Err(format!(
2617                "--exclude-category {category} names no manifest category"
2618            ));
2619        }
2620        let population = selection.population.unwrap_or(Population::Enabled);
2621        let mut cells = Vec::new();
2622        for (id, (category, bucket_timeout_seconds, default_cpu_timeout_seconds, test)) in
2623            &self.tests
2624        {
2625            if selection
2626                .lane
2627                .as_deref()
2628                .is_some_and(|lane| lane != test.lane)
2629                || selection
2630                    .category
2631                    .as_deref()
2632                    .is_some_and(|value| value != category)
2633                || selection.test.as_deref().is_some_and(|value| value != id)
2634                || selection.exclude_categories.contains(category)
2635                || (!selection.include_occasional && test.occasional)
2636            {
2637                continue;
2638            }
2639            for (mode, recipe) in &test.modes {
2640                if selection.mode.as_deref().is_some_and(|value| value != mode) {
2641                    continue;
2642                }
2643                if mode == "naked" {
2644                    let enabled = recipe
2645                        .backends_enabled
2646                        .iter()
2647                        .any(|value| value == "native");
2648                    let ci = ci_selection(recipe)?.selected("native");
2649                    let accepted = match population {
2650                        Population::Required => {
2651                            enabled
2652                                && (ci
2653                                    || selection.mode.as_deref() == Some("naked")
2654                                    || selection.include_manual)
2655                        }
2656                        other => population_accepts(other, ci, enabled),
2657                    };
2658                    if selection
2659                        .backend
2660                        .as_deref()
2661                        .is_some_and(|backend| backend != "native")
2662                        || !accepted
2663                        || !labelled(test, recipe, None)
2664                    {
2665                        continue;
2666                    }
2667                    cells.push(SelectedCell {
2668                        image: bucket_image(self, category),
2669                        category: category.clone(),
2670                        test: test.clone(),
2671                        id: CellId {
2672                            test: id.clone(),
2673                            mode: mode.clone(),
2674                            backend: None,
2675                        },
2676                        enabled,
2677                        timeout_seconds: resolve_timeout_seconds(
2678                            *bucket_timeout_seconds,
2679                            None,
2680                            recipe.timeout_seconds.get("native").copied(),
2681                        ),
2682                        cpu_timeout_seconds: recipe
2683                            .cpu_timeout_seconds
2684                            .get("native")
2685                            .copied()
2686                            .unwrap_or(*default_cpu_timeout_seconds),
2687                        host_level: HostLevel::default(),
2688                    });
2689                    continue;
2690                }
2691                let backends: Vec<_> = match population {
2692                    Population::Disabled => recipe.backends_disabled.keys().cloned().collect(),
2693                    _ => recipe.backends_enabled.clone(),
2694                };
2695                let ci = ci_selection(recipe)?;
2696                for backend in backends {
2697                    if selection
2698                        .backend
2699                        .as_deref()
2700                        .is_some_and(|value| value != backend)
2701                        || selection.exclude_backends.contains(&backend)
2702                        || !labelled(test, recipe, Some(&backend))
2703                    {
2704                        continue;
2705                    }
2706                    let enabled = recipe.backends_enabled.contains(&backend);
2707                    if population == Population::Required
2708                        && !selection.include_manual
2709                        && !ci.selected(&backend)
2710                    {
2711                        continue;
2712                    }
2713                    if !population_accepts(population, ci.selected(&backend), enabled) {
2714                        continue;
2715                    }
2716                    let probed = (selection.parity_inputs && !enabled && mode == "verify")
2717                        .then(|| with_parity_inputs(test, &backend));
2718                    let cell_test = probed.as_ref().unwrap_or(test);
2719                    let recipe = probed
2720                        .as_ref()
2721                        .and_then(|probed| probed.modes.get(mode.as_str()))
2722                        .unwrap_or(recipe);
2723                    let timeout_seconds = resolve_timeout_seconds(
2724                        *bucket_timeout_seconds,
2725                        None,
2726                        recipe.timeout_seconds.get(&backend).copied(),
2727                    );
2728                    let cpu_timeout_seconds = recipe
2729                        .cpu_timeout_seconds
2730                        .get(&backend)
2731                        .copied()
2732                        .unwrap_or(*default_cpu_timeout_seconds);
2733                    cells.push(SelectedCell {
2734                        image: bucket_image(self, category),
2735                        category: category.clone(),
2736                        test: cell_test.clone(),
2737                        id: CellId {
2738                            test: id.clone(),
2739                            mode: mode.clone(),
2740                            backend: Some(backend),
2741                        },
2742                        enabled,
2743                        timeout_seconds,
2744                        cpu_timeout_seconds,
2745                        host_level: HostLevel::default(),
2746                    });
2747                }
2748            }
2749        }
2750        cells.sort_by(|a, b| a.id.cmp(&b.id));
2751        if let Some(backends) = &selection.execution_backends {
2752            if backends.is_empty() {
2753                return Err("execution owner has no backends".into());
2754            }
2755            cells.retain(|cell| backends.contains(cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native")));
2756        }
2757        Ok(cells)
2758    }
2759
2760    pub fn all_tests(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, u64, u64, &TestRecipe)> {
2761        self.tests
2762            .values()
2763            .map(|(category, timeout_seconds, cpu_timeout_seconds, test)| {
2764                (
2765                    category.as_str(),
2766                    *timeout_seconds,
2767                    *cpu_timeout_seconds,
2768                    test,
2769                )
2770            })
2771    }
2772}
2773
2774fn population_accepts(population: Population, ci: bool, enabled: bool) -> bool {
2775    match population {
2776        Population::Required => ci && enabled,
2777        Population::Enabled => enabled,
2778        Population::Disabled => !enabled,
2779    }
2780}
2781
2782/// Where a manifest program stands in this checkout. Every consumer
2783/// that resolves manifest programs (this validator, the scorecard and
2784/// generator through it, test-harness, manifest-metadata) goes
2785/// through [`resolve_program`] so they cannot disagree.
2786#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2787pub enum ProgramResolution {
2788    /// Present on disk here.
2789    Present,
2790    /// Inside a submodule this checkout deliberately leaves
2791    /// uninitialized (missing or empty directory): the sources are
2792    /// populated where validation builds guests, so absence here is
2793    /// not a defect in the row.
2794    NotAvailableHere,
2795    /// Absent where it should exist (including a typo inside a
2796    /// populated submodule): a real missing-program defect.
2797    Missing,
2798}
2799
2800/// Submodule paths declared in the checkout's `.gitmodules`, if any.
2801fn submodule_paths(root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
2802    let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join(".gitmodules")) else {
2803        return Vec::new();
2804    };
2805    text.lines()
2806        .filter_map(|line| line.trim().strip_prefix("path = "))
2807        .map(|path| path.trim().trim_end_matches('/').to_string())
2808        .collect()
2809}
2810
2811/// The one resolver for manifest program paths (see
2812/// [`ProgramResolution`]). Validation checkouts leave update=none
2813/// submodules empty by design (third-party/rr for the rr corpus), so
2814/// existence is only refused where this checkout could have known.
2815pub fn resolve_program(root: &Path, program: &str) -> ProgramResolution {
2816    if root.join(program).exists() {
2817        return ProgramResolution::Present;
2818    }
2819    for submodule in submodule_paths(root) {
2820        if program.starts_with(&format!("{submodule}/")) {
2821            let dir = root.join(&submodule);
2822            let uninitialized = match std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {
2823                Ok(mut entries) => entries.next().is_none(),
2824                Err(_) => true,
2825            };
2826            if uninitialized {
2827                return ProgramResolution::NotAvailableHere;
2828            }
2829        }
2830    }
2831    ProgramResolution::Missing
2832}
2833
2834#[cfg(test)]
2835fn validate_document(
2836    document: &ManifestDocument,
2837    stem: &str,
2838    root: &Path,
2839    global_timeout_seconds: u64,
2840) -> Result<(), String> {
2841    validate_document_with_cpu(
2842        document,
2843        stem,
2844        root,
2845        global_timeout_seconds,
2846        DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
2847    )
2848}
2849
2850fn validate_document_with_cpu(
2851    document: &ManifestDocument,
2852    stem: &str,
2853    root: &Path,
2854    global_timeout_seconds: u64,
2855    global_cpu_timeout_seconds: u64,
2856) -> Result<(), String> {
2857    if document.schema != MANIFEST_SCHEMA {
2858        return Err(format!("{stem}: schema must be {MANIFEST_SCHEMA}"));
2859    }
2860    if document.bucket != stem {
2861        return Err(format!(
2862            "{stem}: bucket `{}` must equal file stem",
2863            document.bucket
2864        ));
2865    }
2866    if document.test.is_empty() {
2867        return Err(format!("{stem}: test list must not be empty"));
2868    }
2869    match (document.timeout_seconds, document.slow_reason.as_deref()) {
2870        (Some(timeout), Some(reason)) if !reason.trim().is_empty() => {
2871            validate_timeout_seconds(timeout, &format!("{stem} bucket"))?;
2872            if timeout == global_timeout_seconds {
2873                return Err(format!(
2874                    "{stem}: bucket timeout_seconds redundantly repeats the global default"
2875                ));
2876            }
2877        }
2878        (Some(_), _) => {
2879            return Err(format!(
2880                "{stem}: bucket timeout_seconds requires a non-empty slow_reason"
2881            ));
2882        }
2883        (None, Some(_)) => {
2884            return Err(format!("{stem}: bucket slow_reason has no timeout_seconds"));
2885        }
2886        (None, None) => {}
2887    }
2888    let bucket_timeout_seconds =
2889        resolve_timeout_seconds(global_timeout_seconds, document.timeout_seconds, None);
2890    for test in &document.test {
2891        if !test.id.starts_with(&format!("{stem}/")) {
2892            return Err(format!("{}: id must start with {stem}/", test.id));
2893        }
2894        if !matches!(test.lane.as_str(), "portable" | "privileged") {
2895            return Err(format!("{}: invalid lane `{}`", test.id, test.lane));
2896        }
2897        for token in &test.requires {
2898            requires_capability(token).map_err(|error| format!("{}.requires: {error}", test.id))?;
2899        }
2900        validate_golden_kernel_floor(&test.id, &test.requires, &test.modes)?;
2901        match (&test.program, &test.direct) {
2902            (Some(program), None) => {
2903                let below_tests = program.starts_with("tests/")
2904                    || program.starts_with("third-party/rr/src/test/");
2905                if !below_tests || resolve_program(root, program) == ProgramResolution::Missing {
2906                    return Err(format!("{}: missing program {program}", test.id));
2907                }
2908            }
2909            (None, Some(DirectCommand::Shell(command))) if !command.trim().is_empty() => {}
2910            (None, Some(DirectCommand::Argv(argv))) if !argv.is_empty() => {
2911                crate::manifest_corpus::check_direct_placeholders(&test.id, argv)?;
2912            }
2913            (Some(_), Some(_)) => return Err(format!("{}: set only program or direct", test.id)),
2914            _ => return Err(format!("{}: missing executable program/direct", test.id)),
2915        }
2916        let actual: BTreeSet<_> = test.modes.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
2917        let expected: BTreeSet<_> = MODES.into_iter().collect();
2918        if actual != expected {
2919            return Err(format!("{}: modes must be exactly {expected:?}", test.id));
2920        }
2921        validate_labels(&test.id, &test.labels)?;
2922        validate_tier_marker(&test.id, stem, &test.labels)?;
2923        // The tier is resolved per cell: a mode may add `super` for one
2924        // backend (the compat corpus's heavy rows do), but no resolved
2925        // cell may carry both tier markers.
2926        for (mode, recipe) in &test.modes {
2927            for backend in &recipe.backends_enabled {
2928                cell_tier(test, recipe, Some(backend))
2929                    .map_err(|error| format!("{}: {mode} on {backend}: {error}", test.id))?;
2930            }
2931        }
2932        for (mode, recipe) in &test.modes {
2933            validate_mode_with_cpu(
2934                &test.id,
2935                mode,
2936                recipe,
2937                bucket_timeout_seconds,
2938                global_cpu_timeout_seconds,
2939            )?;
2940            validate_mode_extensions(&test.id, mode, recipe)?;
2941        }
2942    }
2943    Ok(())
2944}
2945
2946#[cfg(test)]
2947fn validate_mode(
2948    id: &str,
2949    mode: &str,
2950    recipe: &ModeRecipe,
2951    bucket_timeout_seconds: u64,
2952) -> Result<(), String> {
2953    validate_mode_with_cpu(
2954        id,
2955        mode,
2956        recipe,
2957        bucket_timeout_seconds,
2958        DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
2959    )

2961
2962fn validate_mode_with_cpu(
2963    id: &str,
2964    mode: &str,
2965    recipe: &ModeRecipe,
2966    bucket_timeout_seconds: u64,
2967    default_cpu_timeout_seconds: u64,
2968) -> Result<(), String> {
2969    validate_mode_workdir(
2970        id,
2971        mode,
2972        recipe.workdir.as_deref(),
2973        &recipe.backends_enabled,
2974    )?;
2975    let expected: BTreeSet<&str> = if mode == "naked" {
2976        ["native"].into_iter().collect()
2977    } else {
2978        BACKENDS.into_iter().collect()
2979    };
2980    let enabled: BTreeSet<_> = recipe.backends_enabled.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
2981    let disabled: BTreeSet<_> = recipe
2982        .backends_disabled
2983        .keys()
2984        .map(String::as_str)
2985        .collect();
2986    if enabled.len() != recipe.backends_enabled.len()
2987        || !enabled.is_disjoint(&disabled)
2988        || enabled.union(&disabled).copied().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>() != expected
2989    {
2990        return Err(format!("{id}: {mode} does not partition {expected:?}"));
2991    }
2992    if recipe
2993        .backends_disabled
2994        .values()
2995        .any(|reason| reason.trim().is_empty())
2996    {
2997        return Err(format!("{id}: {mode} has an empty backend-disabled reason"));
2998    }
2999    let wall_timeout_keys: BTreeSet<_> =
3000        recipe.timeout_seconds.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
3001    let cpu_timeout_keys: BTreeSet<_> = recipe
3002        .cpu_timeout_seconds
3003        .keys()
3004        .map(String::as_str)
3005        .collect();
3006    let reason_keys: BTreeSet<_> = recipe.slow_reason.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
3007    if wall_timeout_keys != cpu_timeout_keys || wall_timeout_keys != reason_keys {
3008        return Err(format!(
3009            "{id}: {mode} timeout_seconds, cpu_timeout_seconds, and slow_reason must name the same backends"
3010        ));
3011    }
3012    for (backend, timeout) in &recipe.timeout_seconds {
3013        if !enabled.contains(backend.as_str()) {
3014            return Err(format!(
3015                "{id}: {mode} timeout_seconds names disabled backend {backend}"
3016            ));
3017        }
3018        validate_timeout_seconds(*timeout, &format!("{id}: {mode}/{backend}"))?;
3019        let reason = recipe.slow_reason.get(backend).ok_or_else(|| {
3020            format!("{id}: {mode}/{backend} timeout_seconds requires slow_reason")
3021        })?;
3022        if reason.trim().is_empty() {
3023            return Err(format!(
3024                "{id}: {mode}/{backend} slow_reason must be non-empty"
3025            ));
3026        }
3027    }
3028    for (backend, timeout) in &recipe.cpu_timeout_seconds {
3029        if !enabled.contains(backend.as_str()) {
3030            return Err(format!(
3031                "{id}: {mode} cpu_timeout_seconds names disabled backend {backend}"
3032            ));
3033        }
3034        validate_timeout_seconds(*timeout, &format!("{id}: {mode}/{backend} CPU"))?;
3035        let reason = recipe.slow_reason.get(backend).ok_or_else(|| {
3036            format!("{id}: {mode}/{backend} cpu_timeout_seconds requires slow_reason")
3037        })?;
3038        if reason.trim().is_empty() {
3039            return Err(format!(
3040                "{id}: {mode}/{backend} slow_reason must be non-empty"
3041            ));
3042        }
3043    }
3044    for backend in &wall_timeout_keys {
3045        if recipe.timeout_seconds[*backend] == bucket_timeout_seconds
3046            && recipe.cpu_timeout_seconds[*backend] == default_cpu_timeout_seconds
3047        {
3048            return Err(format!(
3049                "{id}: {mode}/{backend} timeout pair redundantly repeats its inherited values"
3050            ));
3051        }
3052    }
3053    let ci = CiSelection::validate(
3054        &enabled
3055            .iter()
3056            .map(|backend| (*backend).to_string())
3057            .collect(),
3058        &disabled
3059            .iter()
3060            .map(|backend| (*backend).to_string())
3061            .collect(),
3062        &recipe.ci,
3063        recipe.ci_disabled_reason.as_ref(),
3064    )
3065    .map_err(|error| format!("{id}: {mode} {error}"))?;
3066    if mode == "naked" && ci.any_selected() {
3067        return Err(format!(
3068            "{id}: naked is opt-in meta-CI and must set ci=false"
3069        ));
3070    }
3071    for (backend, args) in &recipe.guest_args {
3072        if !enabled.contains(backend.as_str()) && !disabled.contains(backend.as_str()) {
3073            return Err(format!(
3074                "{id}: {mode} guest_args names backend {backend} outside backends_enabled/backends_disabled"
3075            ));
3076        }
3077        if args.iter().any(|argument| argument.contains('\0')) {
3078            return Err(format!(
3079                "{id}: {mode} guest_args.{backend} contains a NUL byte, which Linux argv cannot represent"
3080            ));
3081        }
3082    }
3083    // `compare_io_buffers=false` is refused with or without a reason: the
3084    // runner would pass `--no-detlog-io-buffers`, under which Hermit never
3085    // reports `bitwise_parity` (`is_bitwise_parity` in
3086    // hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/verify.rs), so the cell could never reach a
3087    // canonical match. Every reason is therefore refused as well.
3088    match (
3089        mode,
3090        recipe.compare_io_buffers,
3091        recipe.compare_io_buffers_disabled_reason.as_deref(),
3092    ) {
3093        ("verify", None | Some(true), None) => {}
3094        ("verify", Some(false), _) => {
3095            return Err(format!(
3096                "{id}: verify compare_io_buffers=false is refused, with or without a reason: \
3097                 under --no-detlog-io-buffers Hermit never reports bitwise_parity, so the cell \
3098                 could never reach a canonical match"
3099            ));
3100        }
3101        ("verify", None | Some(true), Some(_)) => {
3102            return Err(format!(
3103                "{id}: verify comparison reason is stale while I/O-buffer comparison is enabled"
3104            ));
3105        }
3106        (_, None, None) => {}
3107        _ => {
3108            return Err(format!(
3109                "{id}: compare_io_buffers is supported only by verify mode"
3110            ));
3111        }
3112    }
3113    match (
3114        mode,
3115        recipe.rcb_time,
3116        recipe.rcb_time_disabled_reason.as_deref(),
3117    ) {
3118        ("verify", None | Some(true), None) | ("verify", Some(false), Some(_)) => {}
3119        ("verify", Some(false), None) => {
3120            return Err(format!(
3121                "{id}: verify rcb_time=false requires rcb_time_disabled_reason"
3122            ));
3123        }
3124        ("verify", None | Some(true), Some(_)) => {
3125            return Err(format!(
3126                "{id}: verify RCB-time reason is stale while RCB time is enabled"
3127            ));
3128        }
3129        (_, None, None) => {}
3130        _ => {
3131            return Err(format!("{id}: rcb_time is supported only by verify mode"));
3132        }
3133    }
3134    if recipe
3135        .rcb_time_disabled_reason
3136        .as_deref()
3137        .is_some_and(|reason| reason.trim().is_empty())
3138    {
3139        return Err(format!(
3140            "{id}: rcb_time_disabled_reason must be substantive"
3141        ));
3142    }
3143    validate_expected_guest_exit(id, mode, recipe.expected_guest_exit.as_ref())?;
3144    validate_expected_stdout(id, mode, &recipe.expected_stdout, &enabled)?;
3145    validate_expected_stdout_contains(id, mode, &recipe.expected_stdout_contains, &enabled)?;
3146    validate_verify_stdout_table(
3147        id,
3148        mode,
3149        "expected_stderr",
3150        &recipe.expected_stderr,
3151        &enabled,
3152    )?;
3153    Ok(())
3154}

3156pub fn validate_mode_workdir(
3157    id: &str,
3158    mode: &str,
3159    workdir: Option<&str>,
3160    _backends_enabled: &[String],
3161) -> Result<(), String> {
3162    let Some(workdir) = workdir else {
3163        return Ok(());
3164    };
3165    if !matches!(mode, "verify" | "chaos" | "custom") {
3166        return Err(format!(
3167            "{id}: {mode} workdir is supported only by Hermit run modes"
3168        ));
3169    }
3170    if !Path::new(workdir).is_absolute() {
3171        return Err(format!("{id}: {mode} workdir must be an absolute path"));
3172    }
3173    Ok(())
3174}
3175
3176fn supports_test_workdir(mode: &str, _backend: &str) -> bool {
3177    matches!(mode, "verify" | "replay" | "chaos" | "custom")
3178}
3179
3180/// Whether `result` records the relaxations `cell` runs with on the host that
3181/// produced it: [`cell_relaxations`] with that host's strictness level.
3182///
3183/// A level relaxation names its host's level ([`host_strictness`]), and a row
3184/// imported from another host does not share the importing host's: a Buck RE
3185/// worker without CPUID faulting runs `--no-virtualize-cpuid` where this host
3186/// does not (on 2026-10-19 that refused the skid-overshoot retry of
3187/// c-programs/sigreturn-preemption whose retry had passed). The producing
3188/// host's level is the one the row's own capability verdicts give, or, when
3189/// the row records an uncapped relaxed level, the forced relaxed level
3190/// ([`STRICTNESS_LEVEL_ENV`]). Every relaxation the manifest declares is still
3191/// the cell's own, and a row this host produced is held to this host's level.
3192pub fn row_records_cell_relaxations(cell: &SelectedCell, result: &CellResult) -> bool {
3193    let at_level = |forced: Option<&str>| {
3194        host_strictness(
3195            &result.host_capabilities,
3196            result.exact_branch_counter.as_ref(),
3197            forced,
3198        )
3199        .ok()
3200        .map(|host_level| {
3201            let mut producer = cell.clone();
3202            producer.host_level = host_level;
3203            cell_relaxations(&producer)
3204        })
3205    };
3206    let recorded_relaxed = result.strictness.as_ref().is_some_and(|strictness| {
3207        strictness.level == StrictnessLevel::Relaxed && !strictness.capped
3208    });
3209    result.relaxations == cell_relaxations(cell)
3210        || at_level(None).as_ref() == Some(&result.relaxations)
3211        || (recorded_relaxed && at_level(Some("relaxed")).as_ref() == Some(&result.relaxations))
3212}
3213
3214/// The relaxations a row of `cell` records ([`CellResult::relaxations`]): each
3215/// weaker-than-default setting its manifest recipe selects, with its reason.
3216/// A retained row whose relaxations differ was recorded under another recipe,
3217/// so its evidence does not decide this cell. The recipe of the cell's own
3218/// mode must exist, as it does for every planned cell.
3219pub fn cell_relaxations(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Vec<String> {
3220    let recipe = &cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode];
3221    let mut relaxations = Vec::new();
3222    if recipe.compare_io_buffers == Some(false) {
3223        relaxations.push(format!(
3224            "--no-detlog-io-buffers: {}",
3225            recipe
3226                .compare_io_buffers_disabled_reason
3227                .as_deref()
3228                .unwrap_or("reason missing")
3229        ));
3230    }
3231    if recipe.rcb_time == Some(false) {
3232        relaxations.push(format!(
3233            "--no-rcb-time: {}",
3234            recipe
3235                .rcb_time_disabled_reason
3236                .as_deref()
3237                .unwrap_or("reason missing")
3238        ));
3239    }
3240    let reason =
3241        |reason: &Option<String>| reason.as_deref().unwrap_or("reason missing").to_string();
3242    if let Some(backend) = cell.id.backend.as_deref() {
3243        let args_reason = recipe
3244            .hermit_args_reason
3245            .as_ref()
3246            .and_then(|reason| reason.for_backend(backend))
3247            .unwrap_or("reason missing");
3248        for arg in cell_hermit_args(recipe, backend) {
3249            relaxations.push(format!("{arg}: {args_reason}"));
3250        }
3251        for (arg, reason) in cell.level_relaxations() {
3252            relaxations.push(format!("{arg}: {LEVEL_RELAXATION_PREFIX}{reason}"));
3253        }
3254        if let Some(arg) = probe_relaxation(cell, backend) {
3255            relaxations.push(format!("{arg}: {PROBE_RELAXATION_REASON}"));
3256        }
3257    }
3258    if recipe.comparator == Some(Comparator::Stripped) {
3259        relaxations.push(format!(
3260            "{STRIPPED_COMPARATOR_RELAXATION_PREFIX}{}",
3261            reason(&recipe.comparator_reason)
3262        ));
3263    }
3264    if let Some(reason) = cell_diagnostic_reason(cell) {
3265        relaxations.push(format!("{DIAGNOSTIC_RELAXATION_PREFIX}{reason}"));
3266    }
3267    relaxations
3268}
3269
3270/// What follows the flag in the relaxation that records a flag the relaxed
3271/// strictness level added ([`SelectedCell::level_relaxations`]).
3272pub const LEVEL_RELAXATION_PREFIX: &str = "strictness level relaxed: ";
3273
3274/// The relaxation that records a stripped-comparator cell and its reason. The
3275/// ledger reads it back to judge the cell by the comparison it declared.
3276pub const STRIPPED_COMPARATOR_RELAXATION_PREFIX: &str = "comparator=stripped: ";
3277
3278/// The relaxation that records a diagnostic cell and its reason. It is the
3279/// one place a result row says which cell was diagnostic, so
3280/// [`diagnostic_failure_reason`] reads it back by this exact prefix.
3281const DIAGNOSTIC_RELAXATION_PREFIX: &str = "diagnostic (a product failure does not fail the run): ";
3282
3283/// The manifest's diagnostic reason for this cell's backend, if it is one.
3284fn cell_diagnostic_reason(cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<&str> {
3285    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_deref()?;
3286    cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode]
3287        .diagnostic
3288        .get(backend)
3289        .map(String::as_str)
3290}
3291
3292/// Whether the manifest declares this cell a diagnostic on its backend.
3293pub fn is_diagnostic_cell(cell: &SelectedCell) -> bool {
3294    cell.enabled && cell_diagnostic_reason(cell).is_some()
3295}
3296
3297/// A result row's classification: `disabled` for a cell outside
3298/// `backends_enabled`, `diagnostic` for an enabled cell the manifest declares
3299/// diagnostic on this backend, `required` for every other enabled cell.
3300fn cell_classification(cell: &SelectedCell) -> &'static str {
3301    if !cell.enabled {
3302        "disabled"
3303    } else if cell_diagnostic_reason(cell).is_some() {
3304        "diagnostic"
3305    } else {
3306        "required"
3307    }
3308}
3309
3310/// The reason one cell's attempt history ends in a NON-BLOCKING diagnostic
3311/// failure, or `None` when it must count as an ordinary result.
3312///
3313/// Only a history whose LAST attempt is a measured FAIL of a `diagnostic`
3314/// cell qualifies: a product failure, or the cell exceeding its own time
3315/// budget (a timed-out compatibility probe was a product failure of its node
3316/// before these probes became cells). A PASS is a pass; an ERROR, or a FAIL
3317/// with any other no-result cause, keeps failing the run, including an ERROR
3318/// retry after a product FAIL, as does a diagnostic row that lost its
3319/// recorded reason.
3320pub fn diagnostic_failure_reason(history: &[CellResult]) -> Option<&str> {
3321    row_diagnostic_reason(history.last()?)
3322}
3323
3324fn row_diagnostic_reason(result: &CellResult) -> Option<&str> {
3325    terminal_diagnostic_reason(
3326        &result.classification,
3327        &result.outcome,
3328        result.failure_class,
3329        result.result,
3330        &result.relaxations,
3331    )
3332}
3333
3334/// The row-level rule behind [`diagnostic_failure_reason`], over the fields a
3335/// result reader has: a measured FAIL (a product failure, or a timeout) of a
3336/// `diagnostic` cell whose relaxations record exactly one non-blank
3337/// diagnostic reason. The scorecard applies it to the terminal attempt's row.
3338pub fn terminal_diagnostic_reason<'a>(
3339    classification: &str,
3340    outcome: &str,
3341    failure_class: Option<FailureClass>,
3342    result: Option<ObservedResult>,
3343    relaxations: &'a [String],
3344) -> Option<&'a str> {
3345    let measured = failure_class == Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure)
3346        || result == Some(ObservedResult::Timeout);
3347    if classification != "diagnostic" || outcome != "FAIL" || !measured {
3348        return None;
3349    }
3350    recorded_relaxation_reason(relaxations, DIAGNOSTIC_RELAXATION_PREFIX)
3351}
3352
3353/// Whether relaxations record the stripped comparator with a reason.
3354pub fn records_stripped_comparator(relaxations: &[String]) -> bool {
3355    recorded_relaxation_reason(relaxations, STRIPPED_COMPARATOR_RELAXATION_PREFIX).is_some()
3356}
3357
3358/// The comparator a verify row was judged by, as its relaxations record it:
3359/// `stripped` when they record the stripped comparator with a reason
3360/// ([`records_stripped_comparator`]), the runner's default `strict`
3361/// otherwise. A row that records it malformed is therefore held to `strict`.
3362pub fn row_comparator(result: &CellResult) -> Comparator {
3363    if records_stripped_comparator(&result.relaxations) {
3364        Comparator::Stripped
3365    } else {
3366        Comparator::Strict
3367    }
3368}
3369
3370/// The reason of the one non-blank relaxation with `prefix`; `None` when there
3371/// is none, or more than one, since the runner records each at most once.
3372fn recorded_relaxation_reason<'a>(relaxations: &'a [String], prefix: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
3373    let mut reasons = relaxations
3374        .iter()
3375        .filter_map(|relaxation| relaxation.strip_prefix(prefix))
3376        .filter(|reason| !reason.trim().is_empty());
3377    let reason = reasons.next()?;
3378    reasons.next().is_none().then_some(reason)
3379}
3380
3381fn ci_selection(recipe: &ModeRecipe) -> Result<CiSelection, String> {
3382    CiSelection::validate(
3383        &recipe.backends_enabled.iter().cloned().collect(),
3384        &recipe.backends_disabled.keys().cloned().collect(),
3385        &recipe.ci,
3386        recipe.ci_disabled_reason.as_ref(),
3387    )
3388}

3433/// The existing pressure-test result vocabulary for one executed cell.
3434///
3435/// This is separate from [`FailureClass`]: two product failures can have
3436/// different results (`determinism-failure` and `crash-error`), while both are
3437/// still product failures. Keeping both values on the framework-written row
3438/// preserves that per-attempt distinction without asking pressure-test to
3439/// reconstruct it from process status and retained report files.
3440#[derive(
3441    Clone,
3442    Copy,
3443    Debug,
3444    Deserialize,
3445    Eq,
3446    Ord,
3447    PartialEq,
3448    PartialOrd,
3449    Serialize
3450)]
3451#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
3452pub enum ObservedResult {
3453    Pass,
3454    DeterminismFailure,
3455    ParityFailure,
3456    ReplayFailure,
3457    CrashError,
3458    Timeout,
3459    Oom,
3460    SandboxDenied,
3461    InfrastructureError,
3462    /// A chaos cell whose every attempt matched, failed by its own population
3463    /// floor (`assert.min_distinct`, `min_passes`, `min_failures` or
3464    /// `min_normalized_entropy`): the schedules no longer expose what the cell
3465    /// exists to observe. No attempt crashed, so it is not a crash-error, and
3466    /// none diverged, so it is not a determinism failure.
3467    ChaosFloorFailure,
3468}
3469
3470impl ObservedResult {
3471    pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
3472        match value {
3473            "pass" => Ok(Self::Pass),
3474            "determinism-failure" => Ok(Self::DeterminismFailure),
3475            "parity-failure" => Ok(Self::ParityFailure),
3476            "replay-failure" => Ok(Self::ReplayFailure),
3477            "crash-error" => Ok(Self::CrashError),
3478            "timeout" => Ok(Self::Timeout),
3479            "oom" => Ok(Self::Oom),
3480            "chaos-floor-failure" => Ok(Self::ChaosFloorFailure),
3481            "sandbox-denied" => Err(
3482                "pressure summary contains a sandbox-denied operation; refusing to store it as product behavior"
3483                    .into(),
3484            ),
3485            "infrastructure-error" => Err(
3486                "pressure summary contains an infrastructure error; refusing to store it as product behavior"
3487                    .into(),
3488            ),
3489            other => Err(format!("unknown pressure result `{other}`")),
3490        }
3491    }
3492
3493    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
3494        match self {
3495            Self::Pass => "pass",
3496            Self::DeterminismFailure => "determinism-failure",
3497            Self::ParityFailure => "parity-failure",
3498            Self::ReplayFailure => "replay-failure",
3499            Self::CrashError => "crash-error",
3500            Self::Timeout => "timeout",
3501            Self::Oom => "oom",
3502            Self::SandboxDenied => "sandbox-denied",
3503            Self::InfrastructureError => "infrastructure-error",
3504            Self::ChaosFloorFailure => "chaos-floor-failure",
3505        }
3506    }
3507
3508    pub fn carries_divergence_position(self) -> bool {
3509        matches!(
3510            self,
3511            Self::DeterminismFailure | Self::ParityFailure | Self::ReplayFailure
3512        )
3513    }
3514
3515    pub fn failure_class(self) -> Option<FailureClass> {
3516        match self {
3517            Self::Pass => None,
3518            Self::DeterminismFailure
3519            | Self::ParityFailure
3520            | Self::ReplayFailure
3521            | Self::CrashError
3522            | Self::ChaosFloorFailure => Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure),
3523            Self::Timeout | Self::Oom => Some(FailureClass::NoResult),
3524            Self::SandboxDenied | Self::InfrastructureError => {
3525                Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
3526            }
3527        }
3528    }
3529}
3530
3531/// Attribution for a non-passing cell result.
3532///
3533/// These are the owner's four existing failure classes. `None` is reserved for
3534/// a pass or a retained row written before this field existed; every current
3535/// non-pass written by the framework carries one of these values.
3536#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
3537#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
3538pub enum FailureClass {
3539    ProductFailure,
3540    UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure,
3541    UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure,
3542    NoResult,
3543}
3544
3545impl FailureClass {
3546    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
3547        match self {
3548            Self::ProductFailure => "product_failure",
3549            Self::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure => "understood_infrastructure_failure",
3550            Self::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure => "understood_prerequisite_failure",
3551            Self::NoResult => "no_result",
3552        }
3553    }
3554
3555    pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
3556        match value {
3557            "product_failure" => Ok(Self::ProductFailure),
3558            "understood_infrastructure_failure" => Ok(Self::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure),
3559            "understood_prerequisite_failure" => Ok(Self::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure),
3560            "no_result" => Ok(Self::NoResult),
3561            other => Err(format!("unknown failure_class `{other}`")),
3562        }
3563    }
3564}

3566#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
3567pub struct AttemptResult {
3568    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3569    pub command_binding: Option<crate::executable_binding::ExecutableIdentity>,
3570    pub index: String,
3571    pub outcome: String,
3572    pub error_kind: Option<String>,
3573    pub status: Option<i32>,
3574    pub signal: Option<i32>,
3575    pub timed_out: bool,
3576    #[serde(default)]
3577    pub duration_ms: u128,
3578    /// CPU consumed by the launched command. Rows written before the
3579    /// ptrace golden-log normalization was removed
3580    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301>) also include that
3581    /// normalization process for `E2E_KEEP_VERIFY_LOGS=1` ptrace verify cells.
3582    ///
3583    /// Completed commands use `wait4`; a CPU timeout retains the last live
3584    /// observation when that is larger. The live observation is the CPU of the
3585    /// command's own invocation cgroup or, in a run that declared it has no
3586    /// cgroups, of the leader's live process group; `cpu_observations` names
3587    /// which. It is not inferred from wall time, so it stays attributable when
3588    /// cells execute concurrently.
3589    #[serde(default)]
3590    pub cpu_usage_usec: Option<u64>,
3591    /// Explicit measurement mode; absence in historical rows means ordinary custom execution.
3592    #[serde(default)]
3593    pub capture_custom_runs: bool,
3594    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3595    pub single_run_capture: Option<String>,
3596    /// This worker thread's post-exit adoption/hash CPU, excluding child CPU.
3597    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3598    pub capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: Option<u64>,
3599    /// A post-exit bound, distinct from the child's `timed_out` fact.
3600    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3601    pub capture_adoption_timeout: Option<String>,
3602    pub observation_sha256: Option<String>,
3603    pub argv: Vec<String>,
3604    pub guest_argv: Vec<String>,
3605    pub env: BTreeMap<String, String>,
3606    pub cwd: String,
3607    pub shell_command: String,
3608    #[serde(default)]
3609    pub stdout: String,
3610    #[serde(default)]
3611    pub stderr: String,
3612    pub verification_report: Option<String>,
3613    pub verification_report_sha256: Option<String>,
3614    /// Runtime totals for the two executions compared by this attempt.
3615    pub runtime: Option<VerificationRuntime>,
3616    /// The divergence position, LIFTED OUT of `verification_report` so it is a
3617    /// field rather than a substring.
3618    ///
3619    /// `verification_report` already contained these numbers, but as a
3620    /// JSON-ENCODED STRING, so every consumer had to parse the row and then
3621    /// parse a string inside it. That is why no cell has ever reported where
3622    /// its divergence began: the value was present and unreachable. One
3623    /// attempt is one observation, so this is the level the position belongs
3624    /// at -- a cell with three attempts has three of them.
3625    pub first_divergent_scheduler_turn: Option<u64>,
3626    /// Companion to the field above, in virtual-nanosecond units.
3627    pub first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: Option<u64>,
3628    /// The coordinate that LOCATES the divergence rather than bounding it.
3629    pub first_divergent_record: Option<u64>,
3630    /// Syscalls the guest completed before diverging. A different keyspace from
3631    /// every other coordinate here; see the note in canonical_verdict.
3632    pub first_divergent_syscall: Option<u64>,
3633    /// First differing compared message from the left execution, with only the
3634    /// separately recorded syscall number, scheduler turn, and committed time
3635    /// removed.
3636    pub first_divergent_left_message: Option<String>,
3637    /// Corresponding first differing compared message from the right execution.
3638    pub first_divergent_right_message: Option<String>,
3639    pub sabre_path_evidence: Option<String>,
3640    pub sabre_path_evidence_sha256: Option<String>,
3641    pub reason: Option<String>,
3642}

3644/// The stdout assertions a verify cell declares for its backend: the exact
3645/// `expected_stdout` and the `expected_stdout_contains` text, each `null`
3646/// when the cell declares none.
3647///
3648/// Both members must be present when a row is read. Serde would otherwise
3649/// read an omitted member as `None`, so a row that dropped `exact` would read
3650/// as a cell that declares no exact stdout, and the skid checks would
3651/// re-decide the attempts against an empty declaration instead of the one
3652/// the runner recorded. The runner always writes both members.
3653#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Deserialize, Eq, PartialEq, Serialize)]
3654#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
3655pub struct DeclaredStdout {
3656    #[serde(deserialize_with = "deserialize_required_nullable")]
3657    pub exact: Option<String>,
3658    #[serde(deserialize_with = "deserialize_required_nullable")]
3659    pub contains: Option<String>,
3660    /// The exact stderr bytes declared, where any. Defaulted so a row
3661    /// written before the field existed still reads.
3662    #[serde(default)]
3663    pub stderr_exact: Option<String>,
3664}
3665
3666/// Reads a member that must be present but may be `null`. A field with a
3667/// `deserialize_with` and no `default` is a missing-field error when omitted.
3668fn deserialize_required_nullable<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>
3669where
3670    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
3671{
3672    Option::<String>::deserialize(deserializer)
3673}
