3675/// One test-harness cell observation written to `results.jsonl`.
3676///
3677/// This is not [`crate::ledger::CellResult`]. That type is the validation
3678/// ledger's compact cell verdict; this type is the test framework's complete
3679/// execution result, including invocation, attempts, timing, and retained
3680/// evidence.
3681#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
3682pub struct CellResult {
3683    pub schema: u64,
3684    pub run_id: String,
3685    /// Short machine name measured with this row. A hostname alone is not a
3686    /// stable host class, but it is the existing per-machine key used by the
3687    /// parent store.
3688    #[serde(default)]
3689    pub machine_shortname: String,
3690    /// `uname -r` for the kernel under which this cell ran.
3691    #[serde(default)]
3692    pub kernel_version: String,
3693    /// The complete closed set of capability verdicts that determined which
3694    /// cells could execute on this host.
3695    #[serde(default)]
3696    pub host_capabilities: HostCapabilities,
3697    /// The run's hermit binary's own `exact_branch_counter` verdict (whether
3698    /// the retired-branch counter that ptrace and e9patch runs read their
3699    /// virtual clock from is exact here; see
3700    /// [`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]), recorded in every row so
3701    /// that a cell which ran is known to have run on an exact counter or not.
3702    /// It is outside the closed `host_capabilities` record, whose set the
3703    /// stress series froze. `None` when the binary was not probed or did not
3704    /// answer, and in a row written before this field.
3705    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3706    pub exact_branch_counter: Option<CapabilityVerdict>,
3707    /// The cell attempt that produced this observation. A retry is a second
3708    /// observation, so it receives the next positive ordinal instead of
3709    /// replacing the earlier row.
3710    #[serde(default = "first_attempt")]
3711    pub attempt: u64,
3712    /// Pressure-test repetition number supplied to the test framework.
3713    /// Ordinary validate rows leave this absent and use `attempt` as their
3714    /// series run index.
3715    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3716    pub run_index: Option<u64>,
3717    /// HEAD of the CHECKOUT the harness ran in. NOT the provenance of the
3718    /// binary that produced this measurement, despite the name.
3719    ///
3720    /// The harness cannot learn a binary's provenance from a path, and
3721    /// `hermit_bin` defaults to `target/debug/hermit` -- whatever file happens
3722    /// to be there. During any rebase-and-rerun loop the checkout moves and the
3723    /// binary does not, so this names a commit that never built the artifact.
3724    /// Read [`CellResult::binary_build_sha`] for that; read this only as "where
3725    /// the harness was standing".
3726    pub hermit_sha: String,
3727    /// Dirtiness of that same CHECKOUT at run time -- again not a statement
3728    /// about the binary, which may have been built from a different tree in a
3729    /// different state.
3730    pub source_tree_dirty: bool,
3731    pub binary_sha256: Option<String>,
3732    /// The separately retained core comparator when physical work uses a
3733    /// selected static entry. This never substitutes for that entry's digest.
3734    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3735    pub comparator_binary_sha256: Option<String>,
3736    /// What the BINARY says about its own origin: the commit it was compiled
3737    /// from, with a `-dirty` suffix when that tree was dirty.
3738    ///
3739    /// `binary_sha256` proves WHICH file ran; this says WHERE THAT FILE CAME
3740    /// FROM. Together they are a complete attribution, and neither substitutes
3741    /// for the other. `None` means the binary could not be asked or did not
3742    /// answer recognisably -- deliberately distinct from a value, so "not
3743    /// established" never reads as agreement.
3744    pub binary_build_sha: Option<String>,
3745    #[serde(default)]
3746    pub test_sha256: String,
3747    pub test: String,
3748    pub category: String,
3749    pub lane: String,
3750    pub mode: String,
3751    pub backend: Option<String>,
3752    pub classification: String,
3753    pub outcome: String,
3754    /// What this cell attempt observed, using the same closed vocabulary that
3755    /// pressure summaries and the scorecard consume. `None` means either an
3756    /// infrastructure result or a retained row written before this field.
3757    #[serde(default)]
3758    pub result: Option<ObservedResult>,
3759    /// Who the non-pass is attributed to. This is deliberately separate from
3760    /// `error_kind`, which retains the more specific mechanism such as
3761    /// `backend-unavailable` or `incomplete-verification-evidence`.
3762    #[serde(default)]
3763    pub failure_class: Option<FailureClass>,
3764    pub error_kind: Option<String>,
3765    /// The cell wall-clock bound recorded by schema 4. It remains the fixture
3766    /// preparation and inner-invocation wall bound; the additive fields below
3767    /// describe the post-preparation policy without changing this field's
3768    /// meaning for existing readers.
3769    #[serde(default)]
3770    pub timeout_seconds: u64,
3771    /// Aggregate post-preparation CPU budget across attempts and seeds.
3772    /// Absent only on rows written before this policy became explicit.
3773    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3774    pub execution_cpu_timeout_seconds: Option<u64>,
3775    /// Outer post-preparation wall backstop for a near-zero-CPU wedge.
3776    /// Absent only on rows written before this policy became explicit.
3777    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3778    pub execution_wall_timeout_seconds: Option<u64>,
3779    /// Measured wall time for a cell that reached execution. Absent when the
3780    /// cell never ran; a measured zero remains a valid sub-millisecond result.
3781    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3782    pub duration_ms: Option<u128>,
3783    /// CPU consumed by this cell's preparation, launched attempts, and parity
3784    /// comparison.
3785    ///
3786    /// Null when the cell never reached execution or the runner could not
3787    /// obtain a complete measurement. A measured zero remains a real value.
3788    #[serde(default)]
3789    pub cpu_usage_usec: Option<u64>,
3790    /// Per-invocation observations, independent of the charged aggregate.
3791    #[serde(
3792        default,
3793        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none",
3794        deserialize_with = "crate::cpu_evidence::deserialize_present"
3795    )]
3796    pub cpu_observations: Option<crate::cpu_evidence::CellCpuObservationsV1>,
3797    #[serde(default)]
3798    pub capture_custom_runs: bool,
3799    /// Sum of worker-thread capture charges; `cpu_usage_usec` remains child CPU.
3800    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3801    pub capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: Option<u64>,
3802    /// Runtime totals from the first attempt that produced them.
3803    pub runtime: Option<VerificationRuntime>,
3804    pub log_level: Option<String>,
3805    #[serde(default)]
3806    pub effective_args: Vec<String>,
3807    pub argv: Vec<String>,
3808    pub guest_argv: Vec<String>,
3809    pub env: BTreeMap<String, String>,
3810    pub cwd: String,
3811    pub shell_command: String,
3812    #[serde(default)]
3813    pub relaxations: Vec<String>,
3814    /// How the cell ran ([`SelectedCell::strictness`]): its strictness level
3815    /// and the Hermit settings that level and the recipe selected. `None` for
3816    /// a naked cell, which runs no Hermit, and in a row written before this
3817    /// field; a reader must treat that as not recorded and never infer it from
3818    /// the host.
3819    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3820    pub strictness: Option<CellStrictness>,
3821    pub execution_path: Option<JsonValue>,
3822    pub diversity: Option<JsonValue>,
3823    pub attempts: Vec<AttemptResult>,
3824    /// Cell-level divergence position: the FIRST attempt that located one.
3825    ///
3826    /// This mirrors `reason` exactly, which is also
3827    /// `attempts.iter().find_map(...)`. Two other rules were available and both
3828    /// are worse here: the LAST attempt would let a passing retry erase the
3829    /// position a failing attempt found, and a min across attempts would be a
3830    /// one-run aggregate that reads like the cross-run `ObservedRange`
3831    /// earliest/latest without having a sample behind it. The per-attempt
3832    /// fields are still present, so a consumer that wants a different rule can
3833    /// apply it rather than being stuck with this one.
3834    pub first_divergent_scheduler_turn: Option<u64>,
3835    /// Companion to the field above, selected by the same first-attempt rule.
3836    /// Selected INDEPENDENTLY, so a report carrying only some of the three
3837    /// coordinates still contributes the ones it has.
3838    pub first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: Option<u64>,
3839    /// The coordinate that LOCATES the divergence. Same first-attempt rule.
3840    pub first_divergent_record: Option<u64>,
3841    /// Syscalls completed before diverging. Same first-attempt rule.
3842    pub first_divergent_syscall: Option<u64>,
3843    /// First differing compared message from the first attempt that recorded
3844    /// message content.
3845    pub first_divergent_left_message: Option<String>,
3846    /// Corresponding first differing compared message from that same attempt.
3847    pub first_divergent_right_message: Option<String>,
3848    pub reason: Option<String>,
3849    /// Where this cell's retained evidence lives.
3850    ///
3851    /// Carried on the result rather than recomputed by readers: the directory
3852    /// is `<result_root>/runs/<run_id>/<slug>` for attempt 1 and uses an
3853    /// `-attempt-N` suffix for a retry. The slug is built in exactly one place
3854    /// (`cell_artifact_dir`). A consumer that rebuilds it from `test`, `mode`,
3855    /// `backend`, and `attempt` becomes a second definition that goes stale
3856    /// silently, and a path that points at nothing is worse than no path at all.
3857    pub artifact_dir: String,
3858    /// The one nonzero guest disposition this verify cell declares.
3859    ///
3860    /// A matched verify attempt that ends with a nonzero status or a signal is
3861    /// indistinguishable, from the attempt alone, from a cell that crashed
3862    /// deterministically without saying it should. Recording the manifest's
3863    /// declaration here lets a reader admit exactly the declared disposition
3864    /// and keep refusing every other one. Absent for cells that declare none,
3865    /// so rows for ordinary cells are unchanged.
3866    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3867    pub expected_guest_exit: Option<ExpectedGuestExit>,
3868    /// The stdout assertions this verify cell declares, recorded on every row
3869    /// with at least one attempt whose retained verification report has the
3870    /// verdict `infrastructure_error`, and absent from every other row, so
3871    /// rows for ordinary cells are unchanged.
3872    ///
3873    /// [`skid_overshoot_only_reports`] re-decides these assertions from each
3874    /// attempt's own report and captured stdout instead of trusting how the
3875    /// attempt was classified, and a row without this record (one written
3876    /// before it existed) never has a skid-only history
3877    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>).
3878    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
3879    pub declared_stdout: Option<DeclaredStdout>,
3880}
3881
3882impl CellResult {
3883    /// Bind supplied CPU evidence to this row; historical absence adds no requirements.
3884    pub fn require_cpu_observations(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3885        let Some(observations) = &self.cpu_observations else {
3886            return Ok(());
3887        };
3888        use crate::ledger::RequiredNullable;
3889        let binding = crate::cpu_evidence::CellCpuBinding {
3890            run_id: self.run_id.clone(),
3891            hermit_sha: self.hermit_sha.clone(),
3892            lane: self.lane.clone(),
3893            category: self.category.clone(),
3894            test: self.test.clone(),
3895            mode: self.mode.clone(),
3896            backend: self
3897                .backend
3898                .clone()
3899                .map_or(RequiredNullable::Null, RequiredNullable::Value),
3900            outer_attempt: self.attempt,
3901            run_index: self
3902                .run_index
3903                .map_or(RequiredNullable::Null, RequiredNullable::Value),
3904        };
3905        observations.validate_binding(&binding)?;
3906        for attempt in &self.attempts {
3907            observations.validate_attempt(
3908                &attempt.index,
3909                &attempt.argv,
3910                &attempt.cwd,
3911                &attempt.env,
3912            )?;
3913        }
3914        observations.require_timeout_prerequisites(
3915            self.attempts
3916                .iter()
3917                .map(|attempt| (attempt.index.as_str(), Some(attempt.timed_out))),
3918        )?;
3919        Ok(())
3920    }
3921
3922    /// Human-facing explanation without manufacturing a cause the producer did
3923    /// not record.
3924    pub fn reason_for_display(&self) -> &str {
3925        self.reason
3926            .as_deref()
3927            .unwrap_or(match self.outcome.as_str() {
3928                "FAIL" => "no specific failure reason was recorded",
3929                "ERROR" => "no specific error reason was recorded",
3930                "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" => "no prerequisite reason was recorded",
3931                _ => "no reason was recorded",
3932            })
3933    }
3934
3935    /// Validate the additive timeout fields while keeping earlier schema-4 rows
3936    /// readable. `timeout_seconds` retains its original wall-bound meaning;
3937    /// only rows carrying both new fields claim the execution CPU/backstop
3938    /// policy.
3939    pub fn validate_timeout_policy(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3940        match (
3941            self.execution_cpu_timeout_seconds,
3942            self.execution_wall_timeout_seconds,
3943        ) {
3944            (None, None) => Ok(()),
3945            (Some(cpu), Some(wall)) if cpu > 0 && wall == self.timeout_seconds && wall > cpu => {
3946                Ok(())
3947            }
3948            (cpu, wall) => Err(format!(
3949                "timeout policy disagrees: timeout_seconds={} execution_cpu_timeout_seconds={cpu:?} execution_wall_timeout_seconds={wall:?}",
3950                self.timeout_seconds
3951            )),
3952        }
3953    }
3954
3955    /// Require evidence emitted by the current runner rather than a readable
3956    /// schema-4 row written before the additive timeout fields existed.
3957    pub fn require_current_timeout_policy(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3958        self.validate_timeout_policy()?;
3959        if self.execution_cpu_timeout_seconds.is_none()
3960            || self.execution_wall_timeout_seconds.is_none()
3961        {
3962            return Err("current result omitted explicit execution timeout bounds".into());
3963        }
3964        Ok(())
3965    }
3966
3967    /// Check the classification fields written by the current framework.
3968    ///
3969    /// Both fields remain optional in the deserializer because schema 4 also
3970    /// names retained rows written before they existed. Current publication is
3971    /// stricter: every result is recorded, and every non-pass is attributed.
3972    pub fn require_current_classification(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
3973        match self.outcome.as_str() {
3974            "PASS" => {
3975                if self.result != Some(ObservedResult::Pass) || self.failure_class.is_some() {
3976                    return Err(format!(
3977                        "PASS result must carry result=pass and no failure_class, got result={:?} failure_class={:?}",
3978                        self.result, self.failure_class
3979                    ));
3980                }
3981            }
3982            "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" => {
3983                if self.result.is_some()
3984                    || self.failure_class != Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure)
3985                {
3986                    return Err(format!(
3987                        "HOST-INAPPLICABLE result must carry understood_prerequisite_failure and no observed result, got result={:?} failure_class={:?}",
3988                        self.result, self.failure_class
3989                    ));
3990                }
3991            }
3992            "FAIL" => {
3993                let failure_class = self.failure_class.ok_or_else(|| {
3994                    format!(
3995                        "{} result has no failure_class; current non-passes must be attributed",
3996                        self.outcome
3997                    )
3998                })?;
3999                let result = self.result.ok_or_else(|| {
4000                    "FAIL result has no observed result; the failure kind was lost".to_string()
4001                })?;
4002                let expected = result.failure_class().ok_or_else(|| {
4003                    format!("FAIL result cannot carry the passing result {result:?}")
4004                })?;
4005                if failure_class != expected {
4006                    return Err(format!(
4007                        "observed result {} requires failure_class {:?}, got {:?}",
4008                        result.as_str(),
4009                        expected,
4010                        failure_class
4011                    ));
4012                }
4013            }
4014            "ERROR" => match (self.result, self.failure_class) {
4015                (
4016                    Some(ObservedResult::SandboxDenied | ObservedResult::InfrastructureError),
4017                    Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure),
4018                ) => {}
4019                (
4020                    None,
4021                    Some(
4022                        FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure
4023                        | FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure
4024                        | FailureClass::NoResult,
4025                    ),
4026                )
4027                | (
4028                    Some(ObservedResult::Timeout | ObservedResult::Oom),
4029                    Some(FailureClass::NoResult),
4030                ) => {}
4031                other => {
4032                    return Err(format!(
4033                        "ERROR result must carry a non-product observation/classification, got {other:?}"
4034                    ));
4035                }
4036            },
4037            other => return Err(format!("unknown cell outcome {other:?}")),
4038        }
4039        Ok(())
4040    }
4041
4042    /// Retained schema-4 rows predate these fields. Accept that exact legacy
4043    /// absence, but validate any row that carries either half of the contract.
4044    pub fn validate_recorded_classification(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
4045        if self.result.is_none() && self.failure_class.is_none() {
4046            return Ok(());
4047        }
4048        self.require_current_classification()
4049    }
4050}

4052#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
4053pub struct ScheduledWorkerCapacity(usize);
4054
4055impl ScheduledWorkerCapacity {
4056    pub fn new(configured: usize) -> Self {
4057        assert!(configured > 0, "scheduled worker capacity must be positive");
4058        Self(configured)
4059    }
4060
4061    pub fn configured(self) -> usize {
4062        self.0
4063    }
4064
4065    pub fn workers_for(self, count: usize) -> usize {
4066        self.0.min(count)
4067    }
4068}

4070#[derive(Clone)]
4071pub struct RunContext {
4072    pub command_bindings: BTreeMap<String, crate::executable_binding::HeldExecutable>,
4073    pub root: PathBuf,
4074    pub hermit_bin: PathBuf,
4075    pub result_root: PathBuf,
4076    pub build_root: PathBuf,
4077    pub run_id: String,
4078    pub machine_shortname: String,
4079    pub kernel_version: String,
4080    pub host_capabilities: HostCapabilities,
4081    /// The hermit binary's own `exact_branch_counter` verdict, from
4082    /// `hermit host-capabilities --json`; `None` when the binary was not
4083    /// probed or did not answer. Where it is absent, the cells that the binary
4084    /// then refuses are HOST-INAPPLICABLE (see
4085    /// [`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]).
4086    pub exact_branch_counter: Option<CapabilityVerdict>,
4087    pub attempt: u64,
4088    pub run_index: Option<u64>,
4089    /// One concrete CLI input shared by comparison operands and outer retries.
4090    pub epoch: String,
4091    pub source_sha: String,
4092    pub source_dirty: bool,
4093    /// Provenance the hermit binary reports about itself, probed once per run.
4094    /// See [`CellResult::binary_build_sha`].
4095    pub binary_build_sha: Option<String>,
4096    pub prebuilt: bool,
4097    /// `E2E_KEEP_VERIFY_LOGS=1`: retain every verify cell's logs through
4098    /// `hermit run --keep-logs`, which keeps one golden log (run 1's) after a
4099    /// match and both logs after a divergence. Retention adds no process to
4100    /// the cell and cannot change its outcome.
4101    pub keep_logs: bool,
4102    /// Opt in to one producer-owned capture per custom repetition.
4103    /// Unlike keep_logs, this changes the invocation and can cause refusal.
4104    pub capture_custom_runs: bool,
4105    /// `(test, backend)` verify cells whose logs are retained for the parity
4106    /// post-pass even without `keep_logs`. This is the selection closure of
4107    /// [`crate::parity::retention_closure`]: retention only, the same
4108    /// `--keep-logs` retention as `keep_logs`, adding no process to the cell.
4109    pub parity_retained: BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
4110    /// The tests whose ptrace verify run names the parity golden's CPU profile
4111    /// ([`PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG`]): [`crate::parity::planned_comparisons`]
4112    /// of the verify cells this run plans. Read from the plan alone, so the
4113    /// parity post-pass's switches, which change only what is reported, never
4114    /// change how a cell runs.
4115    pub parity_compared: BTreeSet<String>,
4116    pub run_verify_strict: bool,
4117    pub record_verify_strict: bool,
4118    /// Per-machine scaling for individual test CPU and wall bounds. This is execution policy,
4119    /// not part of the canonical manifest.
4120    pub timeout_multipliers: TimeoutMultipliers,
4121    pub scheduled_worker_capacity: ScheduledWorkerCapacity,
4122    pub isolated_workdir: Option<PathBuf>,
4123    /// Whether verify and chaos attempts run their two executions under
4124    /// `hermit verify-inputs`, sharing one sealed copy of the host's
4125    /// `/etc/ld.so.cache` (`shared_inputs_argv`). Decided once per run:
4126    /// true where the host has the cache.
4127    pub shares_ld_so_cache: bool,
4128    /// The bundle-shipped x86-64-v2 guest rootfs (an oci-dir) active for
4129    /// this attempt only: the harness retry of a loader-rejected verify or
4130    /// chaos cell on the KVM or ptrace backend (issue 5476). The base
4131    /// context never carries one; the attempt loop sets it on the retry
4132    /// attempt's context ([`RunContext::with_v2_retry`]) when the previous
4133    /// attempt is a typed loader rejection ([`loader_v2_rejected`]) and the
4134    /// run was given a rootfs. An attempt with one runs inside it via
4135    /// `hermit run --image`; a KVM attempt also binds the host's
4136    /// `/sys/module` in so strict KVM binder admission can inspect the host
4137    /// kernel.
4138    pub v2_retry_oci_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
4139}
4140
4141/// The epoch a cell gets when `HERMIT_EPOCH` is unset, re-exported for the
4142/// scripts that build on this crate.
4143pub use detcore_model::config::CANONICAL_TEST_EPOCH;
4144
4145/// The epoch every cell gives its guests: `HERMIT_EPOCH` verbatim, or the
4146/// canonical test epoch. Never the host clock: a run whose epoch came from the
4147/// host could be reproduced only from a recording, and `hermit run --strict`
4148/// refuses it.
4149/// The environment variable naming the bundle-shipped x86-64-v2 guest
4150/// rootfs (an oci-dir) a loader-rejected verify or chaos cell, on KVM or
4151/// ptrace, is retried under (issue 5476). `cell.sh` sets it from the
4152/// bundle alone when the bundle carries `v2-rootfs/oci-layout`; unset, no
4153/// v2 retry is launched.
4154pub const V2_OCI_DIR_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_E2E_V2_OCI_DIR";
4155
4156/// The v2 rootfs a run may retry loader-rejected verify and chaos cells under,
4157/// from [`V2_OCI_DIR_ENV`]: `None` when unset, else the absolute path it
4158/// names, which must hold an OCI layout (`oci-layout` file) as
4159/// `hermit run --image=oci-dir:` reads it. Anything else refuses the run
4160/// by name rather than silently disabling the retry.
4161pub fn v2_oci_dir_from_env(value: Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, String> {
4162    let Some(value) = value else {
4163        return Ok(None);
4164    };
4165    let dir = PathBuf::from(value);
4166    if !dir.is_absolute() {
4167        return Err(format!(
4168            "{V2_OCI_DIR_ENV} must be an absolute oci-dir path, got {}",
4169            dir.display()
4170        ));
4171    }
4172    if !dir.join("oci-layout").is_file() {
4173        return Err(format!(
4174            "{V2_OCI_DIR_ENV}={} holds no oci-layout file, so it is not an oci-dir",
4175            dir.display()
4176        ));
4177    }
4178    Ok(Some(dir))
4179}
4180
4181fn capture_custom_runs_from_env(value: Option<&OsStr>) -> Result<bool, String> {
4182    match value {
4183        None => Ok(false),
4184        Some(value) if value == "1" => Ok(true),
4185        Some(value) => Err(format!(
4186            "E2E_CAPTURE_CUSTOM_RUNS must be unset or exactly 1, got {value:?}"
4187        )),
4188    }
4189}
4190
4191fn resolve_run_epoch(explicit: Option<std::ffi::OsString>) -> Result<String, String> {
4192    match explicit {
4193        // Preserve the supported input exactly, including invalid values that
4194        // the CLI must reject.
4195        Some(epoch) => epoch
4196            .into_string()
4197            .map_err(|_| "HERMIT_EPOCH must be valid Unicode".to_owned()),
4198        None => Ok(CANONICAL_TEST_EPOCH.to_owned()),
4199    }
4200}
4201
4202/// The `HERMIT_EPOCH` a harness process started now would give every guest:
4203/// the environment's value verbatim, or the canonical test epoch. A caller
4204/// that launches several harness processes whose logs are compared (the
4205/// pressure test's parity post-pass) resolves this once and passes it to each.
4206pub fn run_epoch_from_env() -> Result<String, String> {
4207    resolve_run_epoch(std::env::var_os("HERMIT_EPOCH"))
4208}

4210impl RunContext {
4211    /// A copy of this context whose result row and retained artifacts use the
4212    /// given cell-attempt ordinal.
4213    pub fn with_attempt(&self, attempt: u64) -> Self {
4214        Self {
4215            attempt,
4216            ..self.clone()
4217        }
4218    }
4219
4220    /// A copy of this context whose verify and chaos attempts run inside the
4221    /// bundle-shipped v2 rootfs at `oci_dir` (see
4222    /// [`RunContext::v2_retry_oci_dir`]). Only the harness attempt loop
4223    /// calls this, for the one retry attempt a loader rejection earns.
4224    pub fn with_v2_retry(mut self, oci_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
4225        self.v2_retry_oci_dir = Some(oci_dir);
4226        self
4227    }
4228
4229    /// `source_sha` names the commit a Git-less source snapshot at `root` was
4230    /// archived from (`--source-sha`); without it, Git describes the checkout.
4231    pub fn from_env(
4232        root: PathBuf,
4233        prebuilt: bool,
4234        source_sha: Option<&str>,
4235    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
4236        Self::from_env_probing(root, prebuilt, source_sha, true)
4237    }
4238
4239    /// The context of a run that executes no cell: `E2E_IMPORT_RESULTS`
4240    /// re-publishes rows another harness process wrote. No cell launches the
4241    /// Hermit binary, so it is [`resolve_import_hermit_bin`]'s choice and the
4242    /// fields that describe the binary stay empty; the parity post-pass runs
4243    /// it for `hermit log-diff`. It is still asked for `exact_branch_counter`,
4244    /// which describes this machine: a producer's claim that a strict ptrace
4245    /// or e9patch cell is inapplicable counts only when this machine confirms
4246    /// it. Every other field is read as `from_env` reads it.
4247    pub fn for_import(root: PathBuf, source_sha: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, String> {
4248        Self::from_env_probing(root, true, source_sha, false)
4249    }
4250
4251    fn from_env_probing(
4252        root: PathBuf,
4253        prebuilt: bool,
4254        source_sha: Option<&str>,
4255        probe_hermit: bool,
4256    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
4257        let (source_sha, source_dirty) = source_identity(&root, source_sha)?;
4258        let result_root = std::env::var_os("E2E_RESULT_ROOT")
4259            .map(PathBuf::from)
4260            .unwrap_or_else(|| root.join("ignored/e2e"));
4261        let run_id = std::env::var("E2E_RUN_ID").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
4262            format!(
4263                "local-{}-{}",
4264                SystemTime::now()
4265                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
4266                    .unwrap_or_default()
4267                    .as_secs(),
4268                std::process::id()
4269            )
4270        });
4271        let run_index = std::env::var(E2E_RUN_INDEX_ENV)
4272            .ok()
4273            .map(|value| {
4274                value.parse::<u64>().map_err(|_| {
4275                    format!("{E2E_RUN_INDEX_ENV} must be a non-negative integer, got {value:?}")
4276                })
4277            })
4278            .transpose()?;
4279        let machine_name = match std::env::var(E2E_MACHINE_SHORTNAME_ENV) {
4280            Ok(value) if !value.is_empty() => value,
4281            _ => command_text("hostname", &["-s"])
4282                .or_else(|_| command_text("hostname", &[]))
4283                .map_err(|error| format!("cannot establish machine_shortname: {error}"))?,
4284        };
4285        let machine_shortname = machine_name
4286            .split('.')
4287            .next()
4288            .unwrap_or_default()
4289            .to_string();
4290        if machine_shortname.is_empty() || machine_shortname.contains('/') {
4291            return Err(format!(
4292                "machine_shortname must be one nonempty path segment, got {machine_shortname:?}"
4293            ));
4294        }
4295        let kernel_version = match std::env::var(E2E_KERNEL_VERSION_ENV) {
4296            Ok(value) if !value.trim().is_empty() => value,
4297            _ => command_text("uname", &["-r"])
4298                .map_err(|error| format!("cannot establish kernel_version: {error}"))?,
4299        };
4300        let host_capabilities = probe_host_capabilities();
4301        let build_root = std::env::var_os("E2E_BUILD_ROOT")
4302            .map(PathBuf::from)
4303            .unwrap_or_else(|| result_root.join("build").join(&source_sha));
4304        let hermit_bin = if probe_hermit {
4305            resolve_hermit_bin(&root, std::env::var_os("HERMIT_BIN"))
4306        } else {
4307            resolve_import_hermit_bin(&root, std::env::var_os("HERMIT_BIN"))
4308        };
4309        // Ask the binary where it came from, the same way this function already
4310        // asks it what flags it supports. `source_sha` above describes the
4311        // checkout; only the binary can describe the binary.
4312        let binary_build_sha = probe_hermit
4313            .then(|| probe_binary_build_sha(&hermit_bin))
4314            .flatten();
4315        // Only the binary can run Reverie's counter validation, and it is the
4316        // binary that refuses `--strict` when the validation fails. An import
4317        // asks too: the verdict describes this machine, not the binary, and it
4318        // is what confirms a producer's claim that a strict ptrace or e9patch
4319        // cell is inapplicable here.
4320        let exact_branch_counter = probe_exact_branch_counter(&hermit_bin);
4321        // Published main still exposes the legacy `--verify-strict` spelling;
4322        // the canonical-only cutover removes it and makes bare `--verify`
4323        // canonical.  Detect the running binary rather than keying behavior to
4324        // a source SHA.  Whichever spelling executes is retained verbatim in
4325        // the result row, so this bridge cannot hide the comparison policy.
4326        let run_verify_strict = probe_hermit
4327            && command_help_contains(&hermit_bin, &["run", "--help"], "--verify-strict")?;
4328        let isolated_workdir = match std::env::var_os(ISOLATED_WORKDIR_ENV) {
4329            None => None,
4330            Some(value) if value == HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR => {
4331                Some(PathBuf::from(HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR))
4332            }
4333            Some(value) => {
4334                return Err(format!(
4335                    "{ISOLATED_WORKDIR_ENV} must be {HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR}, got {}",
4336                    PathBuf::from(value).display()
4337                ));
4338            }
4339        };
4340        let record_verify_strict = probe_hermit
4341            && command_help_contains(
4342                &hermit_bin,
4343                &["record", "start", "--help"],
4344                "--verify-strict",
4345            )?;
4346        let command_bindings = crate::executable_binding::read_bindings(
4347            std::env::var_os("HERMIT_E2E_COMMAND_BINDINGS")
4348                .as_deref()
4349                .map(Path::new),
4350        )?;
4351        for binding in command_bindings.values() {
4352            let entry = &binding.identity.executable;
4353            if probe_binary_build_sha(entry).as_deref()
4354                != Some(binding.identity.binary_build_sha.as_str())
4355            {
4356                return Err(
4357                    "catalog entry's actual version stamp differs from its producer binding".into(),
4358                );
4359            }
4360            if command_help_contains(entry, &["run", "--help"], "--verify-strict")?
4361                != run_verify_strict
4362                || command_help_contains(entry, &["record", "start", "--help"], "--verify-strict")?
4363                    != record_verify_strict
4364            {
4365                return Err(
4366                    "catalog entry and core comparator have different strict invocation contracts"
4367                        .into(),
4368                );
4369            }
4370            binding.recheck()?;
4371        }
4372        Ok(Self {
4373            command_bindings,
4374            root,
4375            hermit_bin,
4376            result_root,
4377            build_root,
4378            run_id,
4379            machine_shortname,
4380            kernel_version,
4381            host_capabilities,
4382            exact_branch_counter,
4383            attempt: 1,
4384            run_index,
4385            epoch: resolve_run_epoch(std::env::var_os("HERMIT_EPOCH"))?,
4386            source_sha,
4387            source_dirty,
4388            binary_build_sha,
4389            prebuilt,
4390            keep_logs: std::env::var("E2E_KEEP_VERIFY_LOGS").as_deref() == Ok("1"),
4391            capture_custom_runs: capture_custom_runs_from_env(
4392                std::env::var_os("E2E_CAPTURE_CUSTOM_RUNS").as_deref(),
4393            )?,
4394            parity_retained: BTreeSet::new(),
4395            parity_compared: BTreeSet::new(),
4396            run_verify_strict,
4397            record_verify_strict,
4398            timeout_multipliers: timeout_multipliers_from_env()?,
4399            scheduled_worker_capacity: ScheduledWorkerCapacity::new(1),
4400            isolated_workdir,
4401            shares_ld_so_cache: Path::new(LD_SO_CACHE_PATH).exists(),
4402            v2_retry_oci_dir: None,
4403        })
4404    }
4405
4406    /// Retain the verify logs of these `(test, backend)` cells for the parity
4407    /// post-pass. See [`RunContext::parity_retained`].
4408    pub fn with_parity_retained(mut self, cells: BTreeSet<(String, String)>) -> Self {
4409        self.parity_retained = cells;
4410        self
4411    }
4412
4413    /// Whether this verify cell's logs are kept after the run.
4414    pub fn retains_verify_logs(&self, test: &str, backend: &str) -> bool {
4415        self.keep_logs
4416            || self
4417                .parity_retained
4418                .contains(&(test.to_string(), backend.to_string()))
4419    }
4420
4421    /// The tests whose ptrace verify run names the parity golden's CPU
4422    /// profile. See [`RunContext::parity_compared`].
4423    pub fn with_parity_compared(mut self, tests: BTreeSet<String>) -> Self {
4424        self.parity_compared = tests;
4425        self
4426    }
4427
4428    /// Whether this run plans `test`'s ptrace verify cell and at least one
4429    /// candidate's ([`RunContext::parity_compared`]). Derived from the plan,
4430    /// never listed: a test gains it with its first planned candidate and
4431    /// loses it with its last. Its ptrace verify run then names
4432    /// [`PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG`].
4433    pub fn parity_compares(&self, test: &str) -> bool {
4434        self.parity_compared.contains(test)
4435    }
4436
4437    pub fn with_scheduled_worker_capacity(
4438        mut self,
4439        scheduled_worker_capacity: ScheduledWorkerCapacity,
4440    ) -> Self {
4441        self.scheduled_worker_capacity = scheduled_worker_capacity;
4442        self
4443    }
4444}
4445
4446/// One initial execution plus one retry, scoped to one selected cell.
4447/// This is the generic per-cell retry bound (product, timeout and
4448/// host-input causes); a typed skid-overshoot-only history has its own
4449/// separate budget ([`MAX_SKID_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL`]).
4450pub const MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL: u64 = 2;
4451
4452/// Attempts a cell whose every attempt is a typed PMU skid overshoot and
4453/// nothing else ([`skid_overshoot_only_reports`]) gets in all: the one
4454/// shared skid budget ([`detcore_model::SKID_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`]),
4455/// separate from the generic [`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL`] bound. A history
4456/// may run past the generic bound only while every attempt so far is
4457/// skid-only; the first non-skid attempt returns the cell to the generic
4458/// bound. Exhausting this budget selects the [`SKID_INFRA_VERDICT`]
4459/// verdict, not a test failure.
4460pub const MAX_SKID_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL: u64 = detcore_model::SKID_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS as u64;
4461
4462/// The selected verdict of a cell whose attempts were all typed PMU skid
4463/// overshoots and nothing else: the host's interrupt latency refused
4464/// every measurement, so the cell produced no product result. The one
4465/// shared spelling ([`detcore_model::SKID_INFRA_VERDICT`]). Per-attempt
4466/// rows keep their `ERROR` infrastructure classification (every raw-row
4467/// reader accepts an `infrastructure_error` report only on that
4468/// classification); this names what the whole history selected.
4469pub const SKID_INFRA_VERDICT: &str = detcore_model::SKID_INFRA_VERDICT;
4470
4471/// Select the outcome that the framework reports for one cell's complete
4472/// attempt history.
4473///
4474/// A passing retry makes the cell pass, while the appended rows still retain
4475/// the failure it recovered from. If no attempt passes, any product failure
4476/// keeps the cell failed even when a later attempt ends in an infrastructure
4477/// error. A history containing only infrastructure errors remains an error.
4478/// Host-inapplicable is terminal and cannot be mixed with executed attempts.
4479pub fn outcome_after_retries<'a>(
4480    attempts: impl IntoIterator<Item = (u64, &'a str)>,
4481) -> Result<&'static str, String> {
4482    let mut expected_attempt = 1;
4483    let mut saw_pass = false;
4484    let mut saw_failure = false;
4485    let mut saw_error = false;
4486    let mut saw_host_inapplicable = false;
4487
4488    for (attempt, outcome) in attempts {
4489        // The hard ceiling is the skid budget: a history past the generic
4490        // [`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL`] bound is produced only by skid-only
4491        // retries. This selector sees outcome strings only, so it cannot
4492        // check that evidence itself: readers must first apply
4493        // `history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified` to the full rows
4494        // (the harness, import policy, framework census and validate's
4495        // cell-results reader do; `cell_result_after_retries` applies it
4496        // internally). Selection itself is unchanged — a product failure
4497        // anywhere in a long history still selects FAIL.
4498        if attempt > MAX_SKID_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL {
4499            return Err(format!(
4500                "cell result attempt {attempt} exceeds the shared maximum of {MAX_SKID_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL}"
4501            ));
4502        }
4503        if attempt != expected_attempt {
4504            return Err(format!(
4505                "cell result attempt {attempt} does not follow the preceding attempts; expected {expected_attempt}"
4506            ));
4507        }
4508        if saw_pass || saw_host_inapplicable {
4509            return Err(format!(
4510                "cell result attempt {attempt} follows terminal outcome {}",
4511                if saw_pass {
4512                    "PASS"
4513                } else {
4514                    "HOST-INAPPLICABLE"
4515                }
4516            ));
4517        }
4518        match outcome {
4519            "PASS" => saw_pass = true,
4520            "FAIL" => saw_failure = true,
4521            "ERROR" => saw_error = true,
4522            "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" => saw_host_inapplicable = true,
4523            other => {
4524                return Err(format!(
4525                    "cell result attempt {attempt} has unknown outcome {other:?}"
4526                ));
4527            }
4528        }
4529        expected_attempt += 1;
4530    }
4531
4532    if expected_attempt == 1 {
4533        return Err("cell result has no attempts".into());
4534    }
4535    if saw_host_inapplicable && (saw_failure || saw_error) {
4536        return Err("HOST-INAPPLICABLE cannot be mixed with executed cell attempts".into());
4537    }
4538    Ok(if saw_pass {
4539        "PASS"
4540    } else if saw_failure {
4541        "FAIL"
4542    } else if saw_error {
4543        "ERROR"
4544    } else {
4545        "HOST-INAPPLICABLE"
4546    })
4547}
4548
4549/// Termination grace per attempt in the generic lifecycle wall below,
4550/// the same 10 s the validate and pressure headroom proofs allow.
4551pub const SKID_LIFECYCLE_GRACE_SECONDS: u64 = 10;
4552
4553/// The wall-clock lifecycle the generic attempt bound was sized
4554/// against for one cell: [`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL`] attempts, each with
4555/// two wall windows (preparation + execution, the non-prebuilt worst
4556/// case) at the cell's `timeout_seconds`, plus grace per attempt.
4557/// Skid retries past the generic bound must fit inside this same
4558/// lifecycle, so raising the skid attempt count never widens the
4559/// enclosing node timeout any node's headroom proof was sized on:
4560/// fast skid-prone cells get all five attempts, a cell whose attempts
4561/// each burn their full wall window stops at the generic bound.
4562pub fn generic_lifecycle_wall_ms(timeout_seconds: u64) -> u128 {
4563    u128::from(MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL)
4564        * (2 * u128::from(timeout_seconds) + u128::from(SKID_LIFECYCLE_GRACE_SECONDS))
4565        * 1000
4566}
4567
4568/// The cumulative measured wall time of `results`, or `None` when any
4569/// row that reached execution recorded no duration.
4570fn cumulative_duration_ms(results: &[CellResult]) -> Option<u128> {
4571    results
4572        .iter()
4573        .map(|result| result.duration_ms)
4574        .sum::<Option<u128>>()
4575}
4576
4577/// Whether a history past the generic [`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL`] bound is
4578/// admitted by retained skid-only evidence: every attempt before the
4579/// final one must re-decide as skid-only
4580/// ([`skid_overshoot_only_reports`]) and the whole history's measured
4581/// wall time must fit the generic lifecycle
4582/// ([`generic_lifecycle_wall_ms`]) — exactly the conditions under
4583/// which the harness launched each attempt past the generic bound. A
4584/// history at or below the generic bound needs no such evidence.
4585/// Raw-row readers that select an outcome from outcome strings alone
4586/// (`outcome_after_retries`) must apply this check (or select through
4587/// [`cell_result_after_retries`], which applies it) before admitting a
4588/// longer history.
4589pub fn history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(results: &[CellResult]) -> bool {
4590    let Some(last_attempt) = results.iter().map(|result| result.attempt).max() else {
4591        return true;
4592    };
4593    if last_attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL {
4594        return true;
4595    }
4596    let Some(last) = results.iter().max_by_key(|result| result.attempt) else {
4597        return true;
4598    };
4599    let Some(cumulative) = cumulative_duration_ms(results) else {
4600        return false;
4601    };
4602    cumulative <= generic_lifecycle_wall_ms(last.timeout_seconds)
4603        && results
4604            .iter()
4605            .filter(|result| result.attempt < last_attempt)
4606            .all(|result| skid_overshoot_only_reports(result).is_some())
4607}
4608
4609/// Whether one more skid attempt of the cell whose history ends in
4610/// `results` can start without the history leaving the generic
4611/// lifecycle: the measured wall so far plus one full attempt window
4612/// (two wall windows at the cell's timeout, plus grace) must fit
4613/// [`generic_lifecycle_wall_ms`]. An attempt with no recorded duration
4614/// is charged its full timeout, never zero.
4615pub fn skid_retry_within_generic_lifecycle(results: &[CellResult]) -> bool {
4616    let Some(last) = results.iter().max_by_key(|result| result.attempt) else {
4617        return true;
4618    };
4619    let timeout_ms = u128::from(last.timeout_seconds) * 1000;
4620    let spent: u128 = results
4621        .iter()
4622        .map(|result| result.duration_ms.unwrap_or(timeout_ms))
4623        .sum();
4624    let reserve = 2 * timeout_ms + u128::from(SKID_LIFECYCLE_GRACE_SECONDS) * 1000;
4625    spent + reserve <= generic_lifecycle_wall_ms(last.timeout_seconds)
4626}
4627
4628/// Return the framework result row that carries the outcome selected by
4629/// [`outcome_after_retries`]. All attempt rows remain in `results.jsonl`; this
4630/// row is the one used for the cell's JUnit and summary entry. A history
4631/// past the generic bound is refused unless it is skid-qualified
4632/// ([`history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified`]).
4633pub fn cell_result_after_retries(results: &[CellResult]) -> Result<&CellResult, String> {
4634    // Name the cell in every refusal that its rows can name (report 279:
4635    // a bare "cell result has no attempts" / "expected 1" left the reader
4636    // hunting 762 cells for the one history at fault). An empty history
4637    // has no row to name it by; callers that know the cell name it there.
4638    let cell = results.first().map(|result| {
4639        format!(
4640            "{} ({}/{})",
4641            result.test,
4642            result.mode,
4643            result.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native")
4644        )
4645    });
4646    let named = |error: String| match &cell {
4647        Some(cell) => format!("{cell}: {error}"),
4648        None => error,
4649    };
4650    if !history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(results) {
4651        return Err(named(format!(
4652            "cell result history of {} attempt(s) exceeds the generic maximum of {MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_CELL} without skid-only evidence for every attempt before the final one",
4653            results.len()
4654        )));
4655    }
4656    let outcome = outcome_after_retries(
4657        results
4658            .iter()
4659            .map(|result| (result.attempt, result.outcome.as_str())),
4660    )
4661    .map_err(named)?;
4662    results
4663        .iter()
4664        .rev()
4665        .find(|result| result.outcome == outcome)
4666        .ok_or_else(|| {
4667            named(format!(
4668                "cell result history selected {outcome} without a matching row"
4669            ))
4670        })
4671}
4672
4673/// Return both the selected result row and the number of attempts in its
4674/// validated history. The selected row keeps its own ordinal and artifact;
4675/// the separate count is what structured summaries report.
4676pub fn cell_result_and_attempts_after_retries(
4677    results: &[CellResult],
4678) -> Result<(&CellResult, u64), String> {
4679    let selected = cell_result_after_retries(results)?;
4680    let attempts = results.last().map(|result| result.attempt).ok_or_else(|| {
4681        // Unreachable after a successful selection above, but name the
4682        // shape of the failure, never a bare refusal.
4683        "cell result has no attempts".to_string()
4684    })?;
4685    Ok((selected, attempts))
4686}
4687
4688/// The reason the runner records for a verify attempt whose verification
4689/// report is Hermit's typed `skid_overshoot` infrastructure error.
4690///
4691/// The classifier writes this reason and [`skid_overshoot_only_reports`] reads
4692/// it back, so the retry gate keys on exactly the text the classifier
4693/// produced and on nothing a guest could print.
4694pub fn skid_overshoot_reason(count: u64) -> String {
4695    format!("verification recorded {count} HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT report(s)")
4696}
4697
4698/// The reason the runner records for a verify attempt whose verification
4699/// report is Hermit's typed `host_input_changed` infrastructure error
4700/// (`change`). [`host_input_change_only`] reads it back, as
4701/// [`skid_overshoot_only_reports`] reads back [`skid_overshoot_reason`].
4702pub fn host_input_changed_reason(change: &InfrastructureError) -> String {
4703    format!("verification diverged and Hermit found the cause outside the guest: {change}")
4704}
4705
4706/// Whether `result` is a verify attempt whose only failure is a divergence
4707/// that a host file changing during one run explains: Hermit's typed
4708/// `host_input_changed` report (see `detcore_model::host_input`).
4709///
4710/// Such an attempt measured a change of the host's files, not the guest's
4711/// determinism, so the runner gives the cell one fresh attempt, even a cell
4712/// that declares `no_retry_reason`: that declaration keeps a PRODUCT
4713/// failure final, and this is not one. The fresh attempt decides the cell by
4714/// the ordinary rules: a second divergence fails it, and a divergence for
4715/// any other reason was never this. Nothing here turns a divergence green.
4716///
4717/// Every condition must hold, from the row and from each inner attempt's own
4718/// retained evidence, so that a label alone cannot claim it: the row is a
4719/// verify `ERROR` of failure class `understood_infrastructure_failure` and
4720/// error kind `infrastructure` whose reason is its first attempt's, and whose
4721/// retained SaBRe path evidence is the evidence the executor summarized into
4722/// its recorded execution path (`retained_path_evidence_error`; the executor
4723/// makes a row whose evidence does not summarize an
4724/// `invalid-backend-evidence` `ERROR`, and judges the path's eligibility only
4725/// on a `PASS`, so an ineligible path does not disqualify); each inner
4726/// attempt is an `ERROR` of error kind `infrastructure` that did not time
4727/// out, whose retained exit status, stdout and stderr carry no failure its
4728/// producer classified (`producer_failure`, which the executor decides
4729/// before it reads any report), whose retained verification report is the
4730/// bytes its recorded
4731/// `verification_report_sha256` names and parses as a current report with
4732/// verdict `infrastructure_error`, a `host_input_changed` error, a comparison
4733/// that is complete under the comparator the row records ([`row_comparator`];
4734/// the check the classifier makes before it labels a host-input attempt, so a
4735/// row it did not classify, such as an imported one, cannot skip it) and no
4736/// `no_result_reason`, whose reason is [`host_input_changed_reason`]
4737/// of that error, and whose report and captured stdout meet the cell's
4738/// declared stdout assertions, which the row records
4739/// ([`CellResult::declared_stdout`]; a row without that record never
4740/// qualifies). A host change explains the divergence, not a declared output
4741/// either run got wrong.
4742pub fn host_input_change_only(result: &CellResult) -> bool {
4743    let Some(declared) = result.declared_stdout.as_ref() else {
4744        return false;
4745    };
4746    if result.mode != "verify"
4747        || result.outcome != "ERROR"
4748        || result.failure_class != Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
4749        || result.error_kind.as_deref() != Some("infrastructure")
4750        || result.attempts.is_empty()
4751        || result
4752            .attempts
4753            .first()
4754            .is_none_or(|first| result.reason != first.reason)
4755        || retained_path_evidence_error(result).is_some()
4756    {
4757        return false;
4758    }
4759    result.attempts.iter().all(|attempt| {
4760        if attempt.outcome != "ERROR"
4761            || attempt.timed_out
4762            || attempt.error_kind.as_deref() != Some("infrastructure")
4763        {
4764            return false;
4765        }
4766        // The executor reads no report over a failure its producer classified
4767        // on stderr, so an attempt whose retained process evidence carries one
4768        // never reached this label.
4769        if producer_failure(
4770            &result.mode,
4771            result.backend.as_deref(),
4772            attempt.status == Some(0),
4773            attempt.timed_out,
4774            &attempt.stdout,
4775            &attempt.stderr,
4776        )
4777        .is_some()
4778        {
4779            return false;
4780        }
4781        let Some(raw) = attempt.verification_report.as_deref() else {
4782            return false;
4783        };
4784        if attempt.verification_report_sha256.as_deref()
4785            != Some(hex_digest(raw.as_bytes()).as_str())
4786        {
4787            return false;
4788        }
4789        let Ok(report) = current_verification_report(raw.as_bytes()) else {
4790            return false;
4791        };
4792        // The comparison must be the complete one the row's comparator
4793        // requires, the check the classifier makes before it labels a
4794        // host-input attempt as one: an incomplete comparison is incomplete
4795        // verification evidence instead.
4796        let complete = || match row_comparator(result) {
4797            Comparator::Strict => report.require_canonical_comparison(),
4798            Comparator::Stripped => require_stripped_comparison(&report),
4799        };
4800        match &report.infrastructure_error {
4801            Some(change @ InfrastructureError::HostInputChanged { .. }) => {
4802                report.verdict == Verdict::InfrastructureError
4803                    && report.no_result_reason.is_none()
4804                    && report.comparison.is_some()
4805                    && complete().is_ok()
4806                    && attempt.reason.as_deref() == Some(host_input_changed_reason(change).as_str())
4807                    && declared
4808                        .exact
4809                        .as_deref()
4810                        .is_none_or(|expected| check_expected_stdout(expected, &report).is_ok())
4811                    && declared
4812                        .stderr_exact
4813                        .as_deref()
4814                        .is_none_or(|expected| check_expected_stderr(expected, &report).is_ok())
4815                    && declared.contains.as_deref().is_none_or(|text| {
4816                        check_expected_stdout_contains(text, attempt.stdout.as_bytes(), &report)
4817                            .is_ok()
4818                    })
4819            }
4820            _ => false,
4821        }
4822    })
4823}
4824
4825/// The number of `HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT` reports behind `result`, when, and
4826/// only when, the cell is a verify cell and its failure is a precise-timer
4827/// overshoot and nothing else
4828/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>).
4829///
4830/// A precise timer is armed `skid_margin` retired conditional branches before
4831/// its target and then single-stepped to it. When the counter's overflow
4832/// interrupt lands more than `skid_margin` branches late, the guest has
4833/// already run past the target and the preemption point cannot be moved back.
4834/// Hermit then refuses the comparison with the typed verdict
4835/// `infrastructure_error` / `skid_overshoot` and exit status 122, taking the
4836/// count from its own in-process counter rather than from guest-visible text.
4837/// Such an attempt measured the host's interrupt latency, not the guest's
4838/// determinism, so a fresh attempt of the same cell is a new measurement.
4839///
4840/// Every condition below must hold; a single unmet one returns `None`, which
4841/// leaves the attempt to the ordinary rules:
4842///
4843/// - the cell is a `verify` cell whose row is an `ERROR` with no typed
4844///   product result, failure class `understood_infrastructure_failure`, error
4845///   kind `infrastructure`, and the reason of its first attempt (so a later
4846///   cell-level override, such as the Hermit binary changing during the cell,
4847///   is not mistaken for a skid);
4848/// - it has at least one inner attempt, the inner attempts' indices are
4849///   nonempty and distinct (as the runner writes them, and as the pressure
4850///   test's and the stress series' history readers require), and every inner
4851///   attempt is a skid
4852///   attempt: an `ERROR` with error kind `infrastructure` that did not time
4853///   out, exited with Hermit's policy-refusal status
4854///   (`HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`, 122) and no signal, whose retained
4855///   verification report is the exact bytes its recorded
4856///   `verification_report_sha256` names and parses as a current report with verdict
4857///   `infrastructure_error` and `skid_overshoot` count greater than zero and
4858///   no `no_result_reason`, whose reason is [`skid_overshoot_reason`] of that
4859///   count, and whose stderr carries at least one `HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT `
4860///   line and the line `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal
4861///   cause=skid-overshoot count=<that count>`, no other Hermit classification
4862///   line ([`HERMIT_CLASSIFICATION_PREFIXES`]), and no comparator refusal line
4863///   (`REFUSING to compare:`);
4864/// - every such report records a completed comparison of both runs (its
4865///   `comparison` and `compared_outputs` are present) that meets the
4866///   requirements of the comparator the row records ([`row_comparator`]),
4867///   the same requirements the classifier applies before it accepts a skid
4868///   report: for `strict`, a canonical comparison
4869///   ([`VerificationReport::require_canonical_comparison`]); for `stripped`,
4870///   the stripped comparison ([`require_stripped_comparison`]); and its guest
4871///   disposition and both compared runs' dispositions are the one the cell
4872///   accepts ([`accepted_guest_disposition`] of the row's
4873///   `expected_guest_exit`);
4874/// - every such report satisfies the backend evidence a passing attempt of
4875///   the row's backend must carry (`dispatch_record_error` finds nothing in
4876///   its `runtime`), and the row's execution-path evidence is the one its own
4877///   retained attempts decide ([`retained_execution_path_error`] finds
4878///   nothing: SaBRe evidence bytes that match their digests, summarized to
4879///   the row's recorded `execution_path`, eligible). Both are checked only on
4880///   a `PASS` elsewhere, so an `ERROR` attempt would otherwise reach a retry
4881///   without them.
4882/// - every inner attempt's retained runtime and divergence coordinates are
4883///   the ones the runner copies onto it from its report, and the row's are
4884///   the ones the runner gives a row from its attempts
4885///   (`attempt_copies_its_report`, `row_copies_its_attempts`), so no retained
4886///   copy carries evidence, such as another backend's dispatch record, that
4887///   the report the checks above read does not;
4888/// - every inner attempt's command line, and the row's copies of the first
4889///   attempt's, are the verify invocation the executor writes for the row's
4890///   backend, relaxations, expected guest exit and comparator
4891///   ([`retained_verify_invocation_error`] finds nothing), so a row whose
4892///   command line selects another backend, carries a run flag its
4893///   relaxations do not record, or ran another guest is not judged by labels
4894///   that do not describe it;
4895///
4896/// - the row records the stdout assertions its cell declares
4897///   ([`CellResult::declared_stdout`]), and every attempt's own evidence
4898///   satisfies them: the exact `expected_stdout` is checked against both
4899///   compared runs' stdout digests in the attempt's report
4900///   (`check_expected_stdout`), and the `expected_stdout_contains` text is
4901///   searched in the attempt's captured stdout, which must be the bytes of
4902///   both compared runs (`check_expected_stdout_contains`). An assertion
4903///   that fails or cannot be decided, or a row that records no declaration
4904///   (one written before the record existed), disqualifies the row.
4905///
4906/// The classifier decides the same assertions first: a skid attempt whose
4907/// compared runs violate one, or whose assertion cannot be checked, keeps the
4908/// plain skid attempt's infrastructure classification, but its reason names
4909/// the assertion as well as the overshoot count, so it is not
4910/// [`skid_overshoot_reason`] of the count. The re-decision above is what
4911/// makes a row the classifier did not produce (an imported row, or one from
4912/// an older producer) unable to claim a skid-only history by its labels
4913/// alone, and the report digest is what ties the re-decided report to the
4914/// bytes the runner read.
4915///
4916/// The last condition is positive evidence that both guests ran to an
4917/// accepted end. Hermit also writes a `skid_overshoot` report, exits 122 and
4918/// prints only the skid refusal line when the overshoot sits beside a second
4919/// failure:
4920///
4921/// - run 1 ended with a status the verify policy rejects (a crash, a signal,
4922///   an unexpected exit code): no second run or comparison happened, and the
4923///   report carries that rejected disposition;
4924/// - run 1 or run 2 failed for another reason (a tracer error, a run timeout,
4925///   a container death) while also overshooting: Hermit attaches the
4926///   overshoot to that error, and the report has no comparison;
4927/// - both runs completed but one ended differently (run 2 crashed): the
4928///   comparison's divergence becomes the skid verdict, and
4929///   `compared_outputs` carries the crash.
4930///
4931/// None of these is skid-only, and a passing fresh attempt must not replace
4932/// them.
4933///
4934/// A `diverged` or `no_result` report, a timeout, a missing or unreadable
4935/// report, an environmental block, any other exit status, a stderr marker
4936/// without the typed report, or a typed report without the stderr markers
4937/// never qualifies. Neither does an overshoot whose comparison the comparator
4938/// refused (a log cut at its size bound): Hermit then writes the refusal as
4939/// the report (verdict `no_result`, reason `comparison_refused`) and prints
4940/// the `REFUSING to compare:` line, and that refusal is a second failure a
4941/// fresh attempt must not hide. The `no_result_reason` guard below repeats
4942/// the report parser's own refusal of a reason beside any other verdict, so
4943/// the predicate does not depend on that parser alone. The
4944/// skid report's own first-divergence fields are not a second class: Hermit
4945/// decides the verdict's precedence, and an overshoot moves the preemption
4946/// point, so its two runs are expected to differ there.
4947pub fn skid_overshoot_only_reports(result: &CellResult) -> Option<u64> {
4948    if result.mode != "verify"
4949        || result.outcome != "ERROR"
4950        || result.result.is_some()
4951        || result.failure_class != Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
4952        || result.error_kind.as_deref() != Some("infrastructure")
4953        || retained_execution_path_error(result).is_some()
4954        || !row_copies_its_attempts(result)
4955        || retained_verify_invocation_error(result).is_some()
4956    {
4957        return None;
4958    }
4959    let first = result.attempts.first()?;
4960    if result.reason != first.reason {
4961        return None;
4962    }
4963    let mut indices = BTreeSet::new();
4964    if result
4965        .attempts
4966        .iter()
4967        .any(|attempt| attempt.index.trim().is_empty() || !indices.insert(attempt.index.as_str()))
4968    {
4969        return None;
4970    }
4971    let declared = result.declared_stdout.as_ref()?;
4972    let accepted = accepted_guest_disposition(result.expected_guest_exit.as_ref());
4973    let backend = result.backend.as_deref();
4974    let comparator = row_comparator(result);
4975    result.attempts.iter().try_fold(0u64, |reports, attempt| {
4976        reports.checked_add(attempt_skid_overshoot_reports(
4977            attempt, declared, accepted, backend, comparator,
4978        )?)
4979    })
4980}
4981
4982/// The total number of `HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT` reports behind a cell's
4983/// complete attempt history, when, and only when, every attempt in the
4984/// history is skid-only ([`skid_overshoot_only_reports`]): the cell's
4985/// selected verdict is [`SKID_INFRA_VERDICT`]. Any other history — a
4986/// pass, a product failure, an ordinary infrastructure error, a mixed
4987/// history — returns `None`, so a real failure beside a skid can never
4988/// be reported as skid infrastructure.
4989pub fn skid_infra_reports(results: &[CellResult]) -> Option<u64> {
4990    if results.is_empty() {
4991        return None;
4992    }
4993    results.iter().try_fold(0u64, |reports, result| {
4994        reports.checked_add(skid_overshoot_only_reports(result)?)
4995    })
4996}
4997
4998/// Whether `attempt` retains a verification report whose verdict is
4999/// `infrastructure_error`, the attempts whose rows record the cell's declared
5000/// stdout assertions ([`CellResult::declared_stdout`]).
5001fn attempt_has_infrastructure_report(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> bool {
5002    attempt
5003        .verification_report
5004        .as_deref()
5005        .and_then(|report| current_verification_report(report.as_bytes()).ok())
5006        .is_some_and(|report| report.verdict == Verdict::InfrastructureError)
5007}
5008
5009/// The guest disposition, as `(exit code, signal)`, that a verify cell
5010/// accepts from each run: the one its manifest declares in
5011/// `expected_guest_exit`, or a clean exit 0 when it declares none. These are
5012/// the dispositions Hermit's `--verify` admits to a comparison for the cell,
5013/// in the representation the verification report records.
5014pub fn accepted_guest_disposition(
5015    expected: Option<&ExpectedGuestExit>,
5016) -> (Option<i32>, Option<i32>) {
5017    expected.map_or((Some(0), None), |expected| (expected.code, expected.signal))
5018}
5019
5020/// The prefixes of the one-line classifications Hermit prints when a run does
5021/// not end with the guest's own status: a policy refusal, an internal failure,
5022/// a signal death, a run timeout or a deadlock under Hermit's model. A skid attempt's stderr
5023/// may carry exactly one kind of these, its own skid refusal; any other is a
5024/// second failure.
5025pub const HERMIT_CLASSIFICATION_PREFIXES: [&str; 5] = [
5026    "HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL",
5027    "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE",
5028    "HERMIT_SIGNAL_DEATH",
5029    "HERMIT_RUN_TIMEOUT",
5030    "HERMIT_MODEL_DEADLOCK",
5031];
5032
5033/// The line Hermit's log comparator prints when it declines to compare two
5034/// logs, a no-result rather than a match or a difference.
5035const COMPARISON_REFUSAL_PREFIX: &str = "REFUSING to compare:";
5036
5037/// The overshoot count of one inner attempt that is a typed skid attempt of a
5038/// cell on `backend` declaring the stdout assertions `declared`, accepting
5039/// the guest disposition `accepted` and judged by `comparator`, as defined by
5040/// [`skid_overshoot_only_reports`].
5041fn attempt_skid_overshoot_reports(
5042    attempt: &AttemptResult,
5043    declared: &DeclaredStdout,
5044    accepted: (Option<i32>, Option<i32>),
5045    backend: Option<&str>,
5046    comparator: Comparator,
5047) -> Option<u64> {
5048    if attempt.outcome != "ERROR"
5049        || attempt.timed_out
5050        || attempt.error_kind.as_deref() != Some("infrastructure")
5051        || attempt.status != Some(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT)
5052        || attempt.signal.is_some()
5053    {
5054        return None;
5055    }
5056    // The retained report must be the bytes the runner read and hashed: every
5057    // decision below is made from it.
5058    let raw = attempt.verification_report.as_deref()?;
5059    if attempt.verification_report_sha256.as_deref() != Some(hex_digest(raw.as_bytes()).as_str()) {
5060        return None;
5061    }
5062    let report = current_verification_report(raw.as_bytes()).ok()?;
5063    if report.verdict != Verdict::InfrastructureError
5064        || report.no_result_reason.is_some()
5065        || !attempt_copies_its_report(attempt, &report)
5066    {
5067        return None;
5068    }
5069    // The backend evidence a passing attempt must carry.
5070    if backend
5071        .and_then(|backend| dispatch_record_error(backend, report.runtime.as_ref()))
5072        .is_some()
5073    {
5074        return None;
5075    }
5076    // Both runs completed, were compared, and ended as the cell accepts.
5077    let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_ref()?;
5078    if report.comparison.is_none()
5079        || (report.guest_exit_code, report.guest_signal) != accepted
5080        || [&outputs.left, &outputs.right]
5081            .into_iter()
5082            .any(|output| (output.exit_code, output.signal) != accepted)
5083    {
5084        return None;
5085    }
5086    // The comparison is the complete one the comparator requires, the check
5087    // the classifier makes before it reports a skid attempt as one: an
5088    // incomplete comparison is incomplete verification evidence instead.
5089    let complete = match comparator {
5090        Comparator::Strict => report.require_canonical_comparison(),
5091        Comparator::Stripped => require_stripped_comparison(&report),
5092    };
5093    if complete.is_err() {
5094        return None;
5095    }
5096    // The cell's declared stdout assertions, re-decided from this attempt's
5097    // own report and captured stdout rather than read from its labels.
5098    if declared
5099        .exact
5100        .as_deref()
5101        .is_some_and(|expected| check_expected_stdout(expected, &report).is_err())
5102        || declared
5103            .stderr_exact
5104            .as_deref()
5105            .is_some_and(|expected| check_expected_stderr(expected, &report).is_err())
5106        || declared.contains.as_deref().is_some_and(|text| {
5107            check_expected_stdout_contains(text, attempt.stdout.as_bytes(), &report).is_err()
5108        })
5109    {
5110        return None;
5111    }
5112    let Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count }) = report.infrastructure_error else {
5113        return None;
5114    };
5115    let refusal =
5116        format!("HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal cause=skid-overshoot count={count}");
5117    let mut overshoot_marked = false;
5118    let mut refusal_marked = false;
5119    for line in attempt.stderr.lines() {
5120        let line = line.trim_end();
5121        if line.starts_with("HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT ") {
5122            overshoot_marked = true;
5123        } else if line == refusal {
5124            refusal_marked = true;
5125        } else if line.starts_with(COMPARISON_REFUSAL_PREFIX)
5126            || HERMIT_CLASSIFICATION_PREFIXES
5127                .iter()
5128                .any(|prefix| line.starts_with(prefix))
5129        {
5130            return None;
5131        }
5132    }
5133    (count > 0
5134        && overshoot_marked
5135        && refusal_marked
5136        && attempt.reason.as_deref() == Some(skid_overshoot_reason(count).as_str()))
5137    .then_some(count)
5138}
5139
5140/// The first-line prefix of every producer failure class the executor keeps
5141/// as an `ERROR` whatever report is present (a refused guest launch, an
5142/// unavailable backend, backend evidence for another backend, Hermit's
5143/// generic command-line error).
5144const HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_CLASS_PREFIX: &str = "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=";
5145
5146/// Why a retained verify `PASS` row is not one the executor would have
5147/// written from its own retained evidence, or `None` when it is.
5148///
5149/// A reader that has the row but not the cell (the pressure test re-reading a
5150/// result history) re-decides the pass from what the row itself retains,
5151/// with the checks the executor applies before it writes `PASS`:
5152///
5153/// - the row is a verify `PASS` labelled as the executor labels one (typed
5154///   result `pass`, and no failure class, error kind or reason), and its
5155///   execution path is the eligible one its own retained attempts decide
5156///   ([`retained_execution_path_error`]);
5157/// - every inner attempt's command line, and the row's copies of the first
5158///   attempt's, are the verify invocation the executor writes for the row's
5159///   backend, relaxations, expected guest exit and comparator
5160///   ([`retained_verify_invocation_error`]);
5161/// - it has at least one inner attempt, and every inner attempt has a
5162///   nonblank index no other attempt shares and is a `PASS` with no error
5163///   kind, reason or timeout, whose first stderr line carries no Hermit
5164///   internal-failure class (the executor keeps four such classes as an
5165///   `ERROR` after a failed exit; this refuses every one of them, after any
5166///   exit, so it never admits a row the executor would not);
5167/// - every inner attempt's retained verification report is the exact bytes
5168///   its `verification_report_sha256` names and parses as a current report
5169///   that passes the comparator the row's relaxations record
5170///   ([`row_comparator`]): for `strict`, a canonical comparison with a
5171///   canonical match; for `stripped`, the stripped comparison
5172///   ([`require_stripped_comparison`]), a verified `matched` verdict and
5173///   matching exact outputs;
5174/// - every inner attempt's retained runtime and divergence coordinates are
5175///   its report's, which the runner copies onto it, and the row's are the
5176///   first runtime and the divergence position its attempts give, so no
5177///   retained copy carries evidence that only a copy, not the report, holds;
5178/// - the report satisfies the stream assertions `declared` (the exact
5179///   stdout and stderr bytes against both compared runs' digests, and the
5180///   contained text in the attempt's captured stdout, which must be both
5181///   runs' stdout);
5182/// - the attempt ended as the row's recorded `expected_guest_exit` requires
5183///   (that guest disposition and the Hermit status reporting it), or with
5184///   Hermit exit status 0 when the row records none;
5185/// - the report carries the dispatch record a passing attempt of the row's
5186///   backend must carry (`dispatch_record_error`).
5187///
5188/// The row records its comparator, backend and expected exit. It records its
5189/// declared stdout only on an infrastructure row, so the caller passes the
5190/// declaration an earlier skid row of the same cell recorded
5191/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>).
5192pub fn retained_verify_pass_error(
5193    result: &CellResult,
5194    declared: &DeclaredStdout,
5195) -> Option<String> {
5196    if result.mode != "verify" || result.outcome != "PASS" {
5197        return Some(format!(
5198            "the row is a {} {} row, not a verify PASS",
5199            result.mode, result.outcome
5200        ));
5201    }
5202    if result.result != Some(ObservedResult::Pass)
5203        || result.failure_class.is_some()
5204        || result.error_kind.is_some()
5205        || result.reason.is_some()
5206    {
5207        return Some(
5208            "the row is not labelled as a verify PASS is: typed result pass, and no failure class, error kind or reason"
5209                .into(),
5210        );
5211    }
5212    if let Some(error) = retained_execution_path_error(result) {
5213        return Some(format!(
5214            "the row's execution-path evidence does not decide a pass: {error}"
5215        ));
5216    }
5217    if result.attempts.is_empty() {
5218        return Some("the row retains no inner attempt".into());
5219    }
5220    if let Some(error) = retained_verify_invocation_error(result) {
5221        return Some(format!(
5222            "the row's command lines are not a verify invocation the executor writes: {error}"
5223        ));
5224    }
5225    let comparator = row_comparator(result);
5226    let mut indices = BTreeSet::new();
5227    for attempt in &result.attempts {
5228        let index = attempt.index.as_str();
5229        if index.trim().is_empty() || !indices.insert(index) {
5230            return Some(format!(
5231                "inner attempt index {index:?} is blank or repeated"
5232            ));
5233        }
5234        if attempt.outcome != "PASS"
5235            || attempt.error_kind.is_some()
5236            || attempt.reason.is_some()
5237            || attempt.timed_out
5238        {
5239            return Some(format!(
5240                "inner attempt {index} is not a PASS without an error kind, reason or timeout"
5241            ));
5242        }
5243        let first_line = attempt.stderr.lines().next().unwrap_or_default();
5244        if first_line.starts_with(HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE_CLASS_PREFIX) {
