5245            return Some(format!(
5246                "inner attempt {index}'s first stderr line is a Hermit internal-failure class ({first_line}), which is never a pass"
5247            ));
5248        }
5249        let Some(raw) = attempt.verification_report.as_deref() else {
5250            return Some(format!(
5251                "inner attempt {index} retains no verification report"
5252            ));
5253        };
5254        if attempt.verification_report_sha256.as_deref()
5255            != Some(hex_digest(raw.as_bytes()).as_str())
5256        {
5257            return Some(format!(
5258                "inner attempt {index}'s retained verification report is not the bytes its verification_report_sha256 names"
5259            ));
5260        }
5261        let report = match current_verification_report(raw.as_bytes()) {
5262            Ok(report) => report,
5263            Err(error) => {
5264                return Some(format!(
5265                    "inner attempt {index}'s verification report is not a current report: {error}"
5266                ));
5267            }
5268        };
5269        // The runner copies a passing attempt's runtime and divergence
5270        // coordinates from its report, so a retained copy that differs is not
5271        // one the runner wrote, and the checks below, which read the report,
5272        // would never decide what the copy carries.
5273        if !attempt_copies_its_report(attempt, &report) {
5274            return Some(format!(
5275                "inner attempt {index}'s retained runtime or divergence coordinates differ from its verification report's"
5276            ));
5277        }
5278        let comparison = match comparator {
5279            Comparator::Strict => report
5280                .require_canonical_comparison()
5281                .and_then(|()| report.require_canonical_match()),
5282            Comparator::Stripped => require_stripped_comparison(&report)
5283                .and_then(|()| {
5284                    (report.verified && report.verdict == Verdict::Matched)
5285                        .then_some(())
5286                        .ok_or_else(|| {
5287                            format!(
5288                                "stripped verification did not match: verified={} verdict={}",
5289                                report.verified, report.verdict
5290                            )
5291                        })
5292                })
5293                .and_then(|()| report.require_exact_output_match()),
5294        };
5295        if let Err(error) = comparison {
5296            return Some(format!(
5297                "inner attempt {index}'s verification report does not pass the row's {comparator:?} comparator: {error}"
5298            ));
5299        }
5300        let stdout = declared
5301            .exact
5302            .as_deref()
5303            .map(|expected| check_expected_stdout(expected, &report))
5304            .transpose()
5305            .and_then(|_| {
5306                declared
5307                    .stderr_exact
5308                    .as_deref()
5309                    .map(|expected| check_expected_stderr(expected, &report))
5310                    .transpose()
5311            })
5312            .and_then(|_| {
5313                declared
5314                    .contains
5315                    .as_deref()
5316                    .map(|text| {
5317                        check_expected_stdout_contains(text, attempt.stdout.as_bytes(), &report)
5318                    })
5319                    .transpose()
5320            });
5321        if let Err(error) = stdout {
5322            let error = match error {
5323                ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(error) | ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error) => {
5324                    error
5325                }
5326            };
5327            return Some(format!(
5328                "inner attempt {index} does not satisfy a declared stdout assertion: {error}"
5329            ));
5330        }
5331        let disposition = match &result.expected_guest_exit {
5332            Some(expected) => expected.check(
5333                report.guest_exit_code,
5334                report.guest_signal,
5335                attempt.status,
5336                attempt.signal,
5337            ),
5338            None if attempt.status == Some(0) && attempt.signal.is_none() => Ok(()),
5339            None => Err(format!(
5340                "Hermit ended with status {:?} and signal {:?}, not exit status 0",
5341                attempt.status, attempt.signal
5342            )),
5343        };
5344        if let Err(error) = disposition {
5345            return Some(format!(
5346                "inner attempt {index} did not end as the row requires: {error}"
5347            ));
5348        }
5349        if let Some(error) = result
5350            .backend
5351            .as_deref()
5352            .and_then(|backend| dispatch_record_error(backend, report.runtime.as_ref()))
5353        {
5354            return Some(format!(
5355                "inner attempt {index} lacks its backend's dispatch evidence: {error}"
5356            ));
5357        }
5358    }
5359    // The runner gives the row the first runtime its attempts carry and the
5360    // divergence position its attempts give (`cell_divergence_position`).
5361    if !row_copies_its_attempts(result) {
5362        return Some(
5363            "the row's runtime or divergence coordinates are not the ones its inner attempts retain"
5364                .into(),
5365        );
5366    }
5367    None
5368}
5369
5370/// Whether `attempt`'s retained runtime and divergence coordinates are the
5371/// ones the executor copies onto it from `report`, the attempt's own parsed
5372/// verification report.
5373///
5374/// The executor copies the runtime from every report it parses, and the
5375/// divergence coordinates from every one except a refused guest launch's or
5376/// an unavailable backend's. Those two attempts are an `ERROR` whose first
5377/// stderr line is a Hermit internal-failure class, which neither a verify
5378/// `PASS` ([`retained_verify_pass_error`]) nor a skid attempt
5379/// ([`skid_overshoot_only_reports`]) may carry, so for those readers a copy
5380/// that differs from the report is one the executor did not write.
5381fn attempt_copies_its_report(attempt: &AttemptResult, report: &VerificationReport) -> bool {
5382    attempt.runtime == report.runtime
5383        && attempt.first_divergent_scheduler_turn == report.first_divergent_scheduler_turn
5384        && attempt.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds == report.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds
5385        && attempt.first_divergent_record == report.first_divergent_record
5386        && attempt.first_divergent_syscall == report.first_divergent_syscall
5387        && attempt.first_divergent_left_message == report.first_divergent_left_message
5388        && attempt.first_divergent_right_message == report.first_divergent_right_message
5389}
5390
5391/// Whether `result`'s runtime and divergence coordinates are the ones the
5392/// executor gives a row from its inner attempts: the first runtime an
5393/// attempt carries, and the divergence position the attempts give
5394/// (`cell_divergence_position`).
5395fn row_copies_its_attempts(result: &CellResult) -> bool {
5396    let position = cell_divergence_position(&result.attempts);
5397    result.runtime
5398        == result
5399            .attempts
5400            .iter()
5401            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.runtime.clone())
5402        && result.first_divergent_scheduler_turn == position.scheduler_turn
5403        && result.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds == position.virtual_nanoseconds
5404        && result.first_divergent_record == position.record
5405        && result.first_divergent_syscall == position.syscall
5406        && result.first_divergent_left_message == position.left_message
5407        && result.first_divergent_right_message == position.right_message
5408}
5409
5410/// Why `row`'s Hermit commands do not run its guest at the `/proc` level
5411/// `cell`'s test declares, if they do not. The row's command line and every
5412/// attempt's must each end with `--` and its guest argv, and carry before that
5413/// exactly the flag the runner writes for that test ([`ProcLevel::flag`]), or
5414/// no `--proc` option when the test declares no level. A naked row runs no
5415/// Hermit. A row with no command line and no attempt has none to check (an
5416/// infrastructure ERROR); one with attempts but no command line is refused.
5417pub fn proc_level_mismatch(row: &CellResult, cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
5418    if row.mode == "naked" {
5419        return None;
5420    }
5421    if row.argv.is_empty() {
5422        return (!row.attempts.is_empty())
5423            .then(|| "the row records attempts but no command line".into());
5424    }
5425    let declared: Vec<&str> = cell.test.proc.map(ProcLevel::flag).into_iter().collect();
5426    let commands = std::iter::once(("the row".to_owned(), &row.argv, &row.guest_argv)).chain(
5427        row.attempts.iter().map(|attempt| {
5428            (
5429                format!("attempt {}", attempt.index),
5430                &attempt.argv,
5431                &attempt.guest_argv,
5432            )
5433        }),
5434    );
5435    for (whose, argv, guest_argv) in commands {
5436        let Some(end) = argv
5437            .len()
5438            .checked_sub(guest_argv.len() + 1)
5439            .filter(|&end| argv[end] == "--" && argv[end + 1..] == guest_argv[..])
5440        else {
5441            return Some(format!(
5442                "{whose}'s argv does not end with `--` and its guest argv"
5443            ));
5444        };
5445        let levels: Vec<&str> = argv[..end]
5446            .iter()
5447            .map(String::as_str)
5448            .filter(|arg| arg.starts_with("--proc"))
5449            .collect();
5450        if levels != declared {
5451            return Some(format!(
5452                "{whose} runs with the /proc options {levels:?}, and the cell's test declares {declared:?}"
5453            ));
5454        }
5455    }
5456    None
5457}
5458
5459/// Why `result`'s retained command lines are not the verify invocation the
5460/// executor writes for a row with its recorded backend, relaxations, expected
5461/// guest exit and comparator, or `None` when they are.
5462///
5463/// The executor builds every verify attempt's argv in one place
5464/// (`verified_invocation_argv`) from the cell the row records: `<hermit> --log
5465/// info --backend <backend> run`, the runner's own flags, the run flags the
5466/// row's relaxations record, `--verify` with the expected-exit allowance
5467/// exactly when the row records an expected guest exit, the report path, the
5468/// optional retained-log directory, the guest's execution root and
5469/// environment, and `--` before the attempt's guest argv. It records that argv
5470/// on the attempt beside the shell command rendered from it
5471/// ([`shell_command`]), and copies the first attempt's command fields onto the
5472/// row, with the argv after the Hermit path as `effective_args` and log level
5473/// `info`. A reader re-deciding a retained row from what it retains
5474/// ([`skid_overshoot_only_reports`], [`retained_verify_pass_error`]) judges it
5475/// by its recorded backend, relaxations and expected exit, so those must
5476/// describe the command that ran
5477/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>):
5478///
5479/// - each attempt's argv selects the row's backend (`native` when the row
5480///   records none, as the executor does) once, before `run`, and no token
5481///   before `--` selects a backend again;
5482/// - every token between `run` and `--` is one the executor writes, in the
5483///   order it writes them, and every valued flag carries a value that does
5484///   not start with `-` (a token Hermit's parser would not take as the value);
5485/// - the run flags in the argv are exactly the ones the row's relaxations
5486///   record, `--verify-allow=failure` is present exactly when the row records
5487///   an expected guest exit, and `--verify-strict` is absent under the
5488///   stripped comparator ([`row_comparator`]);
5489/// - the tokens after `--` are the attempt's guest argv, and its shell command
5490///   is the one rendered from its cwd, env and argv;
5491/// - the row's argv, guest argv, env, cwd and shell command are its first
5492///   attempt's, its effective args are that argv after the Hermit path, and
5493///   its log level is `info`.
5494pub fn retained_verify_invocation_error(result: &CellResult) -> Option<String> {
5495    let Some(first) = result.attempts.first() else {
5496        return Some("the row retains no inner attempt".into());
5497    };
5498    if result.argv != first.argv
5499        || result.guest_argv != first.guest_argv
5500        || result.env != first.env
5501        || result.cwd != first.cwd
5502        || result.shell_command != first.shell_command
5503    {
5504        return Some(
5505            "the row's argv, guest argv, env, cwd or shell command is not its first inner attempt's"
5506                .into(),
5507        );
5508    }
5509    if result.effective_args.as_slice() != result.argv.get(1..).unwrap_or_default()
5510        || result.log_level.as_deref() != Some("info")
5511    {
5512        return Some(
5513            "the row's effective args or log level are not the ones the executor records with its argv"
5514                .into(),
5515        );
5516    }
5517    let backend = result.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native");
5518    let mut relaxation_flags: Vec<&str> = result
5519        .relaxations
5520        .iter()
5521        .filter_map(|relaxation| relaxation.split_once(": "))
5522        .map(|(flag, _)| flag)
5523        .filter(|flag| flag.starts_with("--"))
5524        .collect();
5525    relaxation_flags.sort_unstable();
5526    let expects_exit = result.expected_guest_exit.is_some();
5527    let comparator = row_comparator(result);
5528    let mut first_level = None;
5529    for attempt in &result.attempts {
5530        let index = attempt.index.as_str();
5531        let level = match verify_attempt_invocation_error(
5532            attempt,
5533            backend,
5534            &relaxation_flags,
5535            expects_exit,
5536            comparator,
5537        ) {
5538            Ok(level) => level,
5539            Err(error) => return Some(format!("inner attempt {index}'s command line {error}")),
5540        };
5541        // Every attempt of one row runs at the one `/proc` level its test
5542        // declares.
5543        let first = *first_level.get_or_insert(level);
5544        if first != level {
5545            return Some(format!(
5546                "inner attempt {index} runs at the /proc level {level:?}, not the first attempt's {first:?}"
5547            ));
5548        }
5549        if attempt.shell_command != shell_command(&attempt.cwd, &attempt.env, &attempt.argv) {
5550            return Some(format!(
5551                "inner attempt {index}'s shell command is not the one rendered from its cwd, env and argv"
5552            ));
5553        }
5554    }
5555    None
5556}
5557
5558/// Why `attempt`'s argv is not one `verified_invocation_argv` writes for a
5559/// verify attempt on `backend` whose row's relaxations record the run flags
5560/// `relaxation_flags` (sorted), that expects a guest exit when `expects_exit`
5561/// and that is judged by `comparator`, as [`retained_verify_invocation_error`]
5562/// defines it. When it is one, its `/proc` level, if it names one.
5563fn verify_attempt_invocation_error<'a>(
5564    attempt: &'a AttemptResult,
5565    backend: &str,
5566    relaxation_flags: &[&str],
5567    expects_exit: bool,
5568    comparator: Comparator,
5569) -> Result<Option<&'a str>, String> {
5570    let Some(binding) = &attempt.command_binding else {
5571        return verify_selector_attempt_invocation_error(
5572            attempt,
5573            backend,
5574            relaxation_flags,
5575            expects_exit,
5576            comparator,
5577        );
5578    };
5579    binding.validate()?;
5580    if binding.backend != backend {
5581        return Err("retained static executable selects a different cell backend".into());
5582    }
5583    let mut normalized = attempt.clone();
5584    normalized.argv =
5585        crate::executable_binding::selector_argv(&attempt.argv, &attempt.guest_argv, binding)?;
5586    match verify_selector_attempt_invocation_error(
5587        &normalized,
5588        backend,
5589        relaxation_flags,
5590        expects_exit,
5591        comparator,
5592    )? {
5593        None => Ok(None),
5594        Some("minimal") => Ok(Some("minimal")),
5595        Some("standard") => Ok(Some("standard")),
5596        Some(other) => Err(format!("unexpected validated proc level {other}")),
5597    }
5598}
5599
5600fn verify_selector_attempt_invocation_error<'a>(
5601    attempt: &'a AttemptResult,
5602    backend: &str,
5603    relaxation_flags: &[&str],
5604    expects_exit: bool,
5605    comparator: Comparator,
5606) -> Result<Option<&'a str>, String> {
5607    // The paired program ([`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`]): the comparison, then the
5608    // run command, optionally below the original single sealed-input owner.
5609    // A mapped image and the host linker cache share that same manifest.
5610    let mapped_holder = attempt
5611        .argv
5612        .get(1..=MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len())
5613        .is_some_and(|words| words.iter().map(String::as_str).eq(MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX));
5614    let (paired, shared) = if mapped_holder {
5615        let rest = &attempt.argv[1 + MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()..];
5616        let cache = rest.get(..2).is_some_and(|words| {
5617            words
5618                .iter()
5619                .map(String::as_str)
5620                .eq(["--input", LD_SO_CACHE_INPUT])
5621        });
5622        (&rest[if cache { 2 } else { 0 }..], cache)
5623    } else {
5624        let shared = attempt
5625            .argv
5626            .get(1..=SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len())
5627            .is_some_and(|words| words.iter().map(String::as_str).eq(SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX));
5628        if attempt.argv.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("verify-inputs") && !shared {
5629            return Err(
5630                "does not use the original input holder with its exact manifest descriptor".into(),
5631            );
5632        }
5633        (
5634            &attempt.argv[if shared {
5635                1 + SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()
5636            } else {
5637                0
5638            }..],
5639            shared,
5640        )
5641    };
5642    let program = ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT, VERIFY_PAIR_NAME];
5643    if paired
5644        .get(..program.len())
5645        .is_none_or(|words| words.iter().map(String::as_str).ne(program))
5646    {
5647        return Err("is not the paired verification program the executor runs".into());
5648    }
5649    // Both commands start with the Hermit binary; the run starts at its
5650    // second appearance, as the script finds it.
5651    let commands = &paired[program.len()..];
5652    let run_start = commands
5653        .iter()
5654        .skip(1)
5655        .position(|word| Some(word) == commands.first())
5656        .map(|offset| offset + 1)
5657        .ok_or("has no run command after its comparison")?;
5658    let (comparison, argv) = commands.split_at(run_start);
5659    if mapped_holder && (attempt.argv.first() != argv.first() || backend != "in-guest-trap") {
5660        return Err("mapped-input holder differs from the run's executable or backend".into());
5661    }
5662    if shared && attempt.argv.first() != argv.first() {
5663        return Err("seals its shared inputs with a Hermit other than the run's".into());
5664    }
5665    let head = ["--log", "info", "--backend", backend, "run"];
5666    if argv
5667        .get(1..=head.len())
5668        .is_none_or(|words| words.iter().map(String::as_str).ne(head))
5669    {
5670        return Err(format!(
5671            "does not start `<hermit> --log info --backend {backend} run`"
5672        ));
5673    }
5674    let options_start = 1 + head.len();
5675    let separator = argv[options_start..]
5676        .iter()
5677        .position(|arg| arg == "--")
5678        .map(|offset| options_start + offset)
5679        .ok_or("has no `--` before the guest command")?;
5680    if argv[separator + 1..] != attempt.guest_argv[..] {
5681        return Err("does not end with the attempt's guest argv".into());
5682    }
5683    let options = &argv[options_start..separator];
5684    if let Some(selector) = options
5685        .iter()
5686        .find(|arg| *arg == "--backend" || arg.starts_with("--backend="))
5687    {
5688        return Err(format!("selects a backend again after `run` ({selector})"));
5689    }
5690    let mut tokens = InvocationTokens(options);
5691    // Written since runs record their CPU profile; absent from earlier rows.
5692    let manifest_always = tokens.flag(crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG);
5693    // The parity golden's profile (`names_parity_golden_profile`): only right
5694    // after the manifest flag, which the executor always writes before it (a
5695    // row with neither flag predates both), only on the reference backend,
5696    // and (below) only in a run that virtualizes CPUID.
5697    let golden_profile = tokens.flag(PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG);
5698    if golden_profile && !manifest_always {
5699        return Err(format!(
5700            "names `{PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG}` without `{}` right before it, where the \
5701             executor writes it",
5702            crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG
5703        ));
5704    }
5705    if golden_profile && backend != crate::parity::PARITY_REFERENCE_BACKEND {
5706        return Err(format!(
5707            "names `{PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG}` on {backend}, which is not the parity reference"
5708        ));
5709    }
5710    tokens.require("--base-env=minimal")?;
5711    tokens.require("--strict")?;
5712    let level = tokens.prefixed("--proc=");
5713    if let Some(level) = level {
5714        if !matches!(level, "minimal" | "standard") {
5715            return Err(format!(
5716                "selects the /proc level {level:?}, which Hermit lacks"
5717            ));
5718        }
5719    }
5720    if tokens.flag("--verify-strict") && comparator == Comparator::Stripped {
5721        return Err(
5722            "asks for the canonical comparison (`--verify-strict`) under the stripped comparator"
5723                .into(),
5724        );
5725    }
5726    let mut run_flags = Vec::new();
5727    while let Some(arg) = tokens.next_if(allowed_hermit_arg) {
5728        run_flags.push(arg);
5729    }
5730    for flag in ["--no-detlog-io-buffers", "--no-rcb-time"] {
5731        if tokens.flag(flag) {
5732            run_flags.push(flag);
5733        }
5734    }
5735    run_flags.sort_unstable();
5736    if run_flags != relaxation_flags {
5737        return Err(format!(
5738            "carries the run flags {run_flags:?}, not the ones the row's relaxations record ({relaxation_flags:?})"
5739        ));
5740    }
5741    if golden_profile && run_flags.contains(&NO_VIRTUALIZE_CPUID_ARG) {
5742        return Err(format!(
5743            "names `{PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG}` in a run with `{NO_VIRTUALIZE_CPUID_ARG}`, which \
5744             presents no profile"
5745        ));
5746    }
5747    if tokens.value("--verify-run")? != Some(VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER) {
5748        return Err(format!(
5749            "lacks `--verify-run {VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER}` where the executor writes it"
5750        ));
5751    }
5752    let cache_only_holder = shared && !mapped_holder;
5753    if tokens.flag(SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG) != cache_only_holder {
5754        return Err(if cache_only_holder {
5755            format!("seals shared inputs but its run lacks `{SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG}`")
5756        } else if mapped_holder {
5757            format!(
5758                "carries `{SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG}` although the mapped-input holder uses only fd 197"
5759            )
5760        } else {
5761            format!("carries `{SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG}` without the `hermit verify-inputs` holder")
5762        });
5763    }
5764    paired_comparison_error(comparison, &argv[0], expects_exit)
5765        .map_err(|error| format!("compares with a command that {error}"))?;
5766    // The execution root (`append_execution_root_args`): a tmpfs mounted at
5767    // the workdir, a workdir alone, a per-attempt directory bound at the fixed
5768    // guest workdir, or none.
5769    let mount = tokens.prefixed("--mount=type=tmpfs,target=");
5770    let fixed_bind = format!(":{FIXED_GUEST_WORKDIR}");
5771    let fixed = mount.is_none()
5772        && matches!(tokens.0, [bind, workdir, ..]
5773            if bind.starts_with("--bind=") && bind.ends_with(&fixed_bind) && workdir == "--workdir");
5774    if fixed {
5775        tokens.0 = &tokens.0[1..];
5776    }
5777    let workdir = tokens.value("--workdir")?;
5778    if mount.is_some_and(|target| workdir != Some(target))
5779        || (fixed && workdir != Some(FIXED_GUEST_WORKDIR))
5780    {
5781        return Err("mounts or binds an execution root that is not its workdir".into());
5782    }
5783    // The equalized inputs' binds, then the guest environment.
5784    while tokens.prefixed("--bind=").is_some() {}
5785    while let Some(assignment) = tokens.value("--env")? {
5786        if !assignment.contains('=') {
5787            return Err(format!(
5788                "gives `--env` the value {assignment:?}, which assigns nothing"
5789            ));
5790        }
5791    }
5792    if mapped_holder {
5793        tokens.require("--in-guest-exec-stop")?;
5794        tokens.require("--native-exec-shared-inputs=197")?;
5795    }
5796    match tokens.0.first() {
5797        Some(token) => Err(format!(
5798            "carries `{token}` where the executor writes nothing of the kind"
5799        )),
5800        None => Ok(level),
5801    }
5802}
5803
5804/// Why `comparison` is not the `hermit log-diff --verify-json` command
5805/// [`verified_invocation_argv`] writes for a paired verify attempt run with
5806/// the Hermit binary `hermit`, which expects a guest exit when
5807/// `expects_exit`.
5808fn paired_comparison_error(
5809    comparison: &[String],
5810    hermit: &str,
5811    expects_exit: bool,
5812) -> Result<(), String> {
5813    if comparison.first().map(String::as_str) != Some(hermit)
5814        || comparison.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("log-diff")
5815    {
5816        return Err("does not start `<hermit> log-diff` with the run's Hermit".into());
5817    }
5818    let mut tokens = InvocationTokens(&comparison[2..]);
5819    tokens
5820        .value("--verify-json")?
5821        .ok_or("lacks `--verify-json <path>` where the executor writes it")?;
5822    if tokens.flag("--verify-allow=failure") != expects_exit {
5823        return Err(format!(
5824            "{} `--verify-allow=failure`, but the row {} an expected guest exit",
5825            if expects_exit { "lacks" } else { "carries" },
5826            if expects_exit {
5827                "records"
5828            } else {
5829                "records no"
5830            },
5831        ));
5832    }
5833    tokens.value("--verify-log-dir")?;
5834    let [first, second] = tokens.0 else {
5835        return Err(format!(
5836            "does not end with exactly the two run directories ({:?})",
5837            tokens.0
5838        ));
5839    };
5840    let first = Path::new(first);
5841    if !first.ends_with("run1")
5842        || first.parent().map(|parent| parent.join("run2")).as_deref() != Some(Path::new(second))
5843    {
5844        return Err("does not compare the attempt's run1 and run2 directories".into());
5845    }
5846    Ok(())
5847}
5848
5849/// The Hermit options of a retained command line, read front to back by
5850/// [`verify_attempt_invocation_error`]. Each method consumes the next token
5851/// only when it is the one asked for.
5852struct InvocationTokens<'a>(&'a [String]);
5853
5854impl<'a> InvocationTokens<'a> {
5855    /// Consume the next token if `accept` takes it.
5856    fn next_if(&mut self, accept: impl FnOnce(&str) -> bool) -> Option<&'a str> {
5857        let (first, rest) = self.0.split_first()?;
5858        accept(first).then(|| {
5859            self.0 = rest;
5860            first.as_str()
5861        })
5862    }
5863
5864    /// Consume `flag` if it is next.
5865    fn flag(&mut self, flag: &str) -> bool {
5866        self.next_if(|token| token == flag).is_some()
5867    }
5868
5869    /// Consume `flag`, which the executor always writes next.
5870    fn require(&mut self, flag: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
5871        self.flag(flag)
5872            .then_some(())
5873            .ok_or_else(|| format!("lacks `{flag}` where the executor writes it"))
5874    }
5875
5876    /// Consume the next token if it is `prefix` followed by a nonempty value,
5877    /// and return the value.
5878    fn prefixed(&mut self, prefix: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
5879        let value = self
5880            .0
5881            .first()?
5882            .strip_prefix(prefix)
5883            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())?;
5884        self.0 = &self.0[1..];
5885        Some(value)
5886    }
5887
5888    /// Consume `flag` and its value if `flag` is next: `Ok(None)` when it is
5889    /// not, and an error when its value is missing, empty or starts with `-`.
5890    fn value(&mut self, flag: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a str>, String> {
5891        let [first, rest @ ..] = self.0 else {
5892            return Ok(None);
5893        };
5894        if first != flag {
5895            return Ok(None);
5896        }
5897        match rest {
5898            [value, rest @ ..] if !value.is_empty() && !value.starts_with('-') => {
5899                self.0 = rest;
5900                Ok(Some(value.as_str()))
5901            }
5902            _ => Err(format!("gives `{flag}` no value Hermit would take")),
5903        }
5904    }
5905}
5906
5907fn command_text(program: &str, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
5908    let output = Command::new(program)
5909        .args(args)
5910        .output()
5911        .map_err(|error| format!("cannot execute {program}: {error}"))?;
5912    if !output.status.success() {
5913        return Err(format!("{program} exited {}", output.status));
5914    }
5915    let value = String::from_utf8(output.stdout)
5916        .map_err(|error| format!("{program} output is not UTF-8: {error}"))?
5917        .trim()
5918        .to_string();
5919    if value.is_empty() {
5920        return Err(format!("{program} returned an empty value"));
5921    }
5922    Ok(value)
5923}
5924
5925pub fn prepare_test(
5926    context: &RunContext,
5927    cell: &SelectedCell,
5928    dir: &Path,
5929) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
5930    let timeouts = cell_timeouts(context, cell)?;
5931    prepare_test_until(
5932        context,
5933        cell,
5934        dir,
5935        execution_deadline_after_preparation(Instant::now(), timeouts.wall_seconds)?,
5936        timeouts.wall_seconds,
5937        &mut Vec::new(),
5938    )
5939    .map(|(guest, _cpu_usage_usec)| guest)
5940}
5941
5942fn prepare_test_until(
5943    context: &RunContext,
5944    cell: &SelectedCell,
5945    dir: &Path,
5946    deadline: Instant,
5947    wall_timeout_seconds: u64,
5948    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
5949) -> Result<(Vec<String>, u64), String> {
5950    prepare_dirs(&context.root, dir)?;
5951    let mut cpu_usage_usec = 0u64;
5952    if context.prebuilt && cell.test.program.is_some() {
5953        let source = context
5954            .build_root
5955            .join(cell.test.id.replace('/', "-"))
5956            .join("fixtures");
5957        if !source.is_dir() {
5958            return Err(format!("prebuilt fixture is missing: {}", source.display()));
5959        }
5960        let destination = dir.join("fixtures");
5961        if destination.exists() {
5962            fs::remove_dir_all(&destination)
5963                .map_err(|e| format!("cannot clear {}: {e}", destination.display()))?;
5964        }
5965        copy_tree(&source, &destination)?;
5966    }
5967    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native");
5968    let guest_args = cell_guest_args(cell, backend);
5969    let mut guest = match (&cell.test.program, &cell.test.direct) {
5970        (Some(program), None) if program.ends_with(".c") => {
5971            let output = dir.join("fixtures/program");
5972            if !context.prebuilt {
5973                let _ = fs::remove_file(&output);
5974                // rr guests include generated syscall-enum headers via
5975                // util.h. Header generation and compilation run as ONE
5976                // preparation process (prepare-rr-guest.sh) so the cell
5977                // keeps a single Preparation CPU observation.
5978                let rr_include = cell
5979                    .test
5980                    .preprocessors
5981                    .iter()
5982                    .any(|value| value == "rr-generated-headers")
5983                    .then(|| dir.join("fixtures/rr-generated"));
5984                let mut args = vec!["-std=c11", "-O2", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror"]
5985                    .into_iter()
5986                    .map(str::to_string)
5987                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
5988                if let Some(generated) = &rr_include {
5989                    args.push("-I".into());
5990                    args.push(generated.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
5991                }
5992                args.extend(
5993                    cell.test
5994                        .build
5995                        .as_ref()
5996                        .map(|b| b.cflags.clone())
5997                        .unwrap_or_default(),
5998                );
5999                args.push(context.root.join(program).to_string_lossy().into_owned());
6000                args.push("-o".into());
6001                args.push(output.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
6002                let (prep_program, prep_args) = match &rr_include {
6003                    Some(generated) => {
6004                        let wrapper = context
6005                            .root
6006                            .join("tests/e2e/rr/prepare-rr-guest.sh")
6007                            .to_string_lossy()
6008                            .into_owned();
6009                        let mut wrapped =
6010                            vec![generated.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), "cc".into()];
6011                        wrapped.extend(args);
6012                        (wrapper, wrapped)
6013                    }
6014                    None => ("cc".to_string(), args),
6015                };
6016                cpu_usage_usec = cpu_usage_usec
6017                    .checked_add(run_preparation(
6018                        context,
6019                        dir,
6020                        &prep_program,
6021                        &prep_args,
6022                        deadline,
6023                        wall_timeout_seconds,
6024                        observations,
6025                    )?)
6026                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
6027            }
6028            require_executable_program(&output, &dir.join("captures"))?;
6029            vec![output.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]
6030        }
6031        (Some(program), None) if program.ends_with(".rs") => {
6032            let output = dir.join("fixtures/program");
6033            if !context.prebuilt {
6034                let _ = fs::remove_file(&output);
6035                let mut args = vec!["-O".to_string()];
6036                args.extend(
6037                    cell.test
6038                        .build
6039                        .as_ref()
6040                        .map(|b| b.rustflags.clone())
6041                        .unwrap_or_default(),
6042                );
6043                args.push(context.root.join(program).to_string_lossy().into_owned());
6044                args.push("-o".into());
6045                args.push(output.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
6046                cpu_usage_usec = cpu_usage_usec
6047                    .checked_add(run_preparation(
6048                        context,
6049                        dir,
6050                        "rustc",
6051                        &args,
6052                        deadline,
6053                        wall_timeout_seconds,
6054                        observations,
6055                    )?)
6056                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
6057            }
6058            require_executable_program(&output, &dir.join("captures"))?;
6059            vec![output.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]
6060        }
6061        (Some(program), None) if program.ends_with(".sh") => {
6062            let path = context.root.join(program).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
6063            if !context.prebuilt {
6064                cpu_usage_usec = cpu_usage_usec
6065                    .checked_add(run_preparation(
6066                        context,
6067                        dir,
6068                        &path,
6069                        &["--prepare".into()],
6070                        deadline,
6071                        wall_timeout_seconds,
6072                        observations,
6073                    )?)
6074                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
6075            }
6076            vec![path, "--run".into()]
6077        }
6078        (None, Some(DirectCommand::Shell(command))) => {
6079            let mut argv = vec!["bash".into(), "-c".into(), command.clone()];
6080            if !guest_args.is_empty() {
6081                argv.push("--".into());
6082            }
6083            argv
6084        }
6085        (None, Some(DirectCommand::Argv(argv))) => {
6086            // The cell's XDG configuration copy is named by its host path
6087            // here; an equalized (verify) cell's argv then names it at its
6088            // guest path, /tmp/e2e/xdg-config ([`equalized_guest_argv`]).
6089            crate::manifest_corpus::resolve_direct_placeholders(
6090                &cell.test.id,
6091                argv,
6092                &context.root,
6093                crate::manifest_corpus::validate_run_state().as_deref(),
6094                Some(&dir.join("xdg-config")),
6095            )?
6096        }
6097        _ => return Err(format!("{} has unsupported program kind", cell.test.id)),
6098    };
6099    guest.extend(guest_args);
6100    if context.isolated_workdir.is_some() || supports_test_workdir(&cell.id.mode, backend) {
6101        resolve_repo_guest_args(&context.root, &mut guest);
6102    }
6103    Ok((guest, cpu_usage_usec))
6104}
6105
6106fn resolve_repo_guest_args(root: &Path, argv: &mut [String]) {
6107    for arg in argv {
6108        let path = Path::new(arg);
6109        if path.is_absolute() || arg == "." || arg == ".." {
6110            continue;
6111        }
6112        // `./examples/x` names the same file as `examples/x`. Joining it
6113        // verbatim leaves `<root>/./examples/x` in the recorded command, and
6114        // the retained-evidence renderer rightly refuses a `.` component after
6115        // a provenance root (validate_cell_results.rs), so drop it here.
6116        let resolved = root.join(
6117            path.components()
6118                .filter(|component| !matches!(component, Component::CurDir))
6119                .collect::<PathBuf>(),
6120        );
6121        let looks_like_repo_path = arg.starts_with("./") || arg.contains('/') || resolved.is_file();
6122        if looks_like_repo_path && resolved.exists() {
6123            *arg = resolved.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
6124        }
6125    }
6126}
6127
6128/// What the preparation child actually said, stderr first.
6129///
6130/// The child's output is already captured to `prepare.stderr` / `prepare.stdout`;
6131/// this is the only thing that carries it back to the caller. It matters beyond
6132/// readability: validate classifies an environmentally-blocked gate by reading
6133/// the FAILING NODE's own output region and nothing else, deliberately, so that
6134/// an unrelated concurrent host denial cannot excuse a real red. A build step
6135/// that swallows its compiler's stderr therefore hides the very evidence the
6136/// classifier is looking for, and a host denial gets recorded as a product
6137/// failure. Measured 2026-08-17 in one cold run: `build.manifest_guests`
6138/// reported three guests as "missing or not executable" with no diagnostic while
6139/// the jailer had denied their `cc`/`ld`, and `build.runtime_release` in the SAME
6140/// run propagated its banner, was classified `bpfjailer-banner`, and was retried.
6141fn preparation_diagnostic(captures: &Path) -> String {
6142    fs::read_to_string(captures.join("prepare.stderr"))
6143        .ok()
6144        .filter(|text| !text.trim().is_empty())
6145        .or_else(|| {
6146            fs::read_to_string(captures.join("prepare.stdout"))
6147                .ok()
6148                .filter(|text| !text.trim().is_empty())
6149        })
6150        .unwrap_or_default()
6151}
6152
6153/// Append a captured diagnostic to `message`, or say plainly that there was none.
6154///
6155/// The empty case is spelled out rather than left blank: "no output was captured"
6156/// is a different and much more suspicious fact than a compiler error, and a
6157/// reader who cannot tell them apart cannot tell a denial from a broken guest.
6158fn with_diagnostic(message: String, captures: &Path) -> String {
6159    let diagnostic = preparation_diagnostic(captures);
6160    if diagnostic.is_empty() {
6161        format!(
6162            "{message}\n  (no output was captured in {}; the preparation command produced none)",
6163            captures.display()
6164        )
6165    } else {
6166        format!("{message}\n{diagnostic}")
6167    }
6168}
6169
6170fn remaining_cell_time(deadline: Instant) -> Duration {
6171    remaining_cell_time_at(deadline, Instant::now())
6172}
6173
6174fn remaining_cell_seconds(deadline: Instant) -> u64 {
6175    let remaining = remaining_cell_time(deadline);
6176    if remaining.is_zero() {
6177        return 1;
6178    }
6179    remaining
6180        .as_secs()
6181        .saturating_add(u64::from(remaining.subsec_nanos() != 0))
6182}
6183
6184fn remaining_cell_time_at(deadline: Instant, now: Instant) -> Duration {
6185    deadline.saturating_duration_since(now)
6186}

6206fn execution_deadline_after_preparation(
6207    prepared_at: Instant,
6208    wall_timeout_seconds: u64,
6209) -> Result<Instant, String> {
6210    prepared_at
6211        .checked_add(Duration::from_secs(wall_timeout_seconds))
6212        .ok_or_else(|| format!("wall timeout {wall_timeout_seconds}s exceeds clock range"))
6213}
6214
6215fn require_executable_program(path: &Path, captures: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
6216    let executable = path
6217        .metadata()
6218        .is_ok_and(|metadata| metadata.is_file() && metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0);
6219    if executable {
6220        return Ok(());
6221    }
6222    Err(with_diagnostic(
6223        format!(
6224            "compiled guest is missing or not executable: {}",
6225            path.display()
6226        ),
6227        captures,
6228    ))
6229}
6230
6231fn run_preparation(
6232    context: &RunContext,
6233    dir: &Path,
6234    program: &str,
6235    args: &[String],
6236    deadline: Instant,
6237    cell_timeout_seconds: u64,
6238    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
6239) -> Result<u64, String> {
6240    let captures = dir.join("captures");
6241    let request = ProcessRequest::new(
6242        InvocationRole::Preparation,
6243        &context.root,
6244        program,
6245        args,
6246        &preparation_env(dir),
6247        &captures.join("prepare.stdout"),
6248        &captures.join("prepare.stderr"),
6249    );
6250    if remaining_cell_time(deadline).is_zero() {
6251        record_not_started(
6252            request,
6253            false,
6254            NotStartedReason::WallBudgetAlreadyExhausted,
6255            observations,
6256        );
6257        return Err(with_diagnostic(
6258            format!("cell exceeded {cell_timeout_seconds} s during fixture preparation"),
6259            &captures,
6260        ));
6261    }
6262    let output = execute_process(request, (deadline, None), observations)?;
6263    if output.timeout.is_some() || !output.status.success() {
6264        // Carry the child's own words back. This used to return the bare sentence
6265        // and drop `prepare.stderr` on the floor, which turned every denied or
6266        // broken compile into the same uninformative line.
6267        let how = if output.timeout.is_some() {
6268            format!("cell exceeded {cell_timeout_seconds} s during fixture preparation")
6269        } else {
6270            match output.status.code() {
6271                Some(code) => format!("exited {code}"),
6272                None => "was killed by a signal".to_string(),
6273            }
6274        };
6275        return Err(with_diagnostic(
6276            format!("fixture preparation failed for {program}: {how}"),
6277            &captures,
6278        ));
6279    }
6280    Ok(output.cpu_usage_usec)
6281}
6282
6283pub fn build_spec(
6284    context: &RunContext,
6285    cell: &SelectedCell,
6286    dir: PathBuf,
6287    guest_argv: Vec<String>,
6288    attempt: &str,
6289    seed: Option<i64>,
6290    timeout_seconds: u64,
6291) -> Result<CellRunSpec, String> {
6292    // The label is used in verdict, log, evidence, and capture paths. Reject
6293    // traversal and multi-component values before any of those paths are
6294    // created. The ordinary host-bound workdir uses the same guard; the
6295    // hermetic tmpfs path does not remove this path-safety property.
6296    let fixed_workdir_source = fixed_workdir_source_for_attempt(&dir, attempt)?;
6297    let backend = cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native");
6298    let equalized_inputs = equalizes_guest_inputs(&cell.id.mode);
6299    // The recorded guest argv is the argv after `--`, so both carry the guest
6300    // paths of an equalized cell.
6301    let (guest_argv, named_roots) = if equalized_inputs {
6302        let roots = equalized_roots(
6303            context,
6304            crate::manifest_corpus::validate_run_state().as_deref(),
6305        );
6306        equalized_guest_argv(&dir, &roots, guest_argv)
6307    } else {
6308        (guest_argv, Vec::new())
6309    };
6310    let mode_recipe = &cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode];
6311    let mut env = execution_cell_env(context, &dir, cell.id.mode != "naked");
6312    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME") {
6313        let home = PathBuf::from(home);
6314        if cell.image.is_some() {
6315            // Hermit finds the podman store under the invoking user's data
6316            // home; the cell's isolated HOME would hide it. The store is a
6317            // host input like the Hermit binary itself.
6318            env.insert(
6319                "XDG_DATA_HOME".into(),
6320                home.join(".local/share").to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6321            );
6322        }
6323        // One cache directory for every Hermit cell. Image cells share the
6324        // materialized-rootfs cache (keyed by resolved image ID; roots are
6325        // read-only), so each cell does not copy the image again inside its
6326        // CPU budget. Every cell shares Hermit's host qualification cache:
6327        // with no profile named, Hermit qualifies the host for x86-64-v3
6328        // (seconds) and caches a pass by host, boot and binary, which each
6329        // cell's isolated HOME would otherwise measure again. Hermit reads
6330        // the variable itself; the guest's environment is RUNNER_GUEST_ENV
6331        // alone, and a naked cell's program gets nothing extra.
6332        if cell.image.is_some() || cell.id.mode != "naked" {
6333            env.insert(
6334                "XDG_CACHE_HOME".into(),
6335                home.join(".cache").to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6336            );
6337        }
6338    }
6339    if cell.id.mode != "naked" {
6340        // An environment input preserves explicit custom --epoch precedence.
6341        // append_guest_env_args intentionally does not forward this CLI input.
6342        env.insert("HERMIT_EPOCH".into(), context.epoch.clone());
6343        // Which CPU profile each run presents is copied from its manifest
6344        // (`cpu_profile_record`): every `hermit run` writes one
6345        // (`MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG`, a flag, so no variable of its own reaches a
6346        // guest) into the cell's stage directory, which Hermit creates and the
6347        // runner moves to the attempt's own once the attempt ends. `hermit
6348        // run` takes that directory only from this variable. The path is the
6349        // same for every attempt because a guest can see it: a custom cell
6350        // outside the hermetic lane runs under Hermit's default
6351        // `--base-env=host`, and its assertions compare its attempts.
6352        let data = crate::cpu_profile_record::stage_dir(&dir);
6353        env.insert(
6354            crate::cpu_profile_record::DATA_DIR_ENV.into(),
6355            data.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6356        );
6357    }
6358    let sabre_path_evidence = (backend == "sabre").then(|| {
6359        dir.join("captures")
6360            .join(format!("{}-{attempt}.sabre-path.jsonl", cell.id.mode))
6361    });
6362    if let Some(path) = &sabre_path_evidence {
6363        fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().expect("evidence path has a parent"))
6364            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
6365        fs::write(path, b"").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
6366        env.insert(
6367            "HERMIT_SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE".into(),
6368            path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6369        );
6370    }
6371    // The explicit hermetic path is available only where the launched backend
6372    // can honour a guest working directory. Replay is included there because
6373    // `record start` accepts the same mount and workdir arguments as `run`.
6374    let supports_test_workdir = supports_test_workdir(&cell.id.mode, backend);
6375    if context.isolated_workdir.is_some() && !supports_test_workdir {
6376        return Err(format!(
6377            "hermetic validation cannot isolate a {} cell on the {backend} backend at /test",
6378            cell.id.mode
6379        ));
6380    }
6381    // `record start` has no `--bind`, so outside the hermetic path a replay cell
6382    // runs in its manifest workdir or the runner's working directory.
6383    let bound_workdir_source = matches!(cell.id.mode.as_str(), "verify" | "chaos" | "custom")
6384        .then_some(fixed_workdir_source.as_path());
6385    let isolated = context.isolated_workdir.is_some();
6386    let verdict = dir.join(format!("verify-{attempt}.json"));
6387    let mut verification_log_dir = None;
6388    let verify_runs = matches!(cell.id.mode.as_str(), "verify" | "chaos" | "replay")
6389        .then(|| dir.join("verify-runs").join(attempt));
6390    let single_run_capture = (cell.id.mode == "custom" && context.capture_custom_runs)
6391        .then(|| dir.join("custom-capture/run"));
6392    let (argv, verdict_path) = match cell.id.mode.as_str() {
6393        "naked" => (guest_argv.clone(), None),
6394        mode @ ("verify" | "replay" | "chaos") => {
6395            let invocation = match mode {
6396                "verify" => VerifiedInvocation::Verify,
6397                "replay" => VerifiedInvocation::Replay {
6398                    record_timeout_seconds: timeout_seconds,
6399                },
6400                _ => VerifiedInvocation::Chaos {
6401                    seed: seed.ok_or_else(|| "chaos attempt requires a seed".to_string())?,
6402                },
6403            };
6404            if matches!(invocation, VerifiedInvocation::Verify)
6405                && context.retains_verify_logs(&cell.id.test, backend)
6406            {
6407                let logs = dir.join(format!("verify-logs/verify-{attempt}"));
6408                fs::create_dir_all(&logs).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
6409                verification_log_dir = Some(logs);
6410            }
6411            let argv = verified_invocation_argv(VerifiedInvocationArgs {
6412                context,
6413                cell,
6414                backend,
6415                invocation,
6416                verdict: &verdict,
6417                verification_log_dir: verification_log_dir.as_deref(),
6418                verify_runs: verify_runs.as_deref(),
6419                bound_workdir_source,
6420                equalized_inputs_dir: equalized_inputs.then_some(dir.as_path()),
6421                equalized_roots: &named_roots,
6422                env: &env,
6423                guest_argv: &guest_argv,
6424            });
6425            (argv, Some(verdict))
6426        }
6427        "custom" => {
6428            let mut argv = vec![
6429                context.hermit_bin.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6430                "--log".into(),
6431                "info".into(),
6432                "--backend".into(),
6433                backend.into(),
6434                "run".into(),
6435                crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG.into(),
6436            ];
6437            argv.extend(cell.test.proc.map(|level| level.flag().to_string()));
6438            argv.extend(cell.test.modes["custom"].args.clone());
6439            if let Some(stage) = &single_run_capture {
6440                argv.extend([
6441                    "--verify-strict".into(),
6442                    "--verify-run".into(),
6443                    stage.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6444                ]);
6445            }
6446            if isolated {
6447                require_minimal_base_env(&mut argv)?;
6448                append_guest_env_args(&mut argv, &env, true);
6449            } else {
6450                append_scheduled_jobs_env_arg(&mut argv, &env);
6451            }
6452            append_execution_root_args(
6453                &mut argv,
6454                backend,
6455                context.isolated_workdir.as_deref(),
6456                mode_recipe.workdir.as_deref(),
6457                bound_workdir_source,
6458            );
6459            argv.push("--".into());
6460            argv.extend(guest_argv.clone());
6461            (argv, None)
6462        }
6463        mode => return Err(format!("unsupported mode {mode}")),
6464    };
6465    let command_binding = if cell.id.mode == "naked" {
6466        None
6467    } else {
6468        context.command_bindings.get(backend).cloned()
6469    };
6470    let argv = if let Some(binding) = &command_binding {
6471        binding.recheck()?;
6472        crate::executable_binding::static_argv(
6473            &argv,
6474            &context.hermit_bin,
6475            &guest_argv,
6476            &binding.identity,
6477        )?
6478    } else {
6479        argv
6480    };
6481    Ok(CellRunSpec {
6482        command_binding,
6483        id: cell.id.clone(),
6484        lane: cell.test.lane.clone(),
6485        category: cell.category.clone(),
6486        cwd: context.root.clone(),
6487        env,
6488        argv,
6489        guest_argv,
6490        timeout_seconds,
6491        verdict_path,
6492        verification_log_dir,
6493        verify_runs,
6494        single_run_capture,
6495        sabre_path_evidence,
6496        cell_dir: dir,
6497        expected_guest_exit: cell_expected_guest_exit(cell),
6498        expected_stdout: cell_expected_stdout(cell),
6499        expected_stdout_contains: cell_expected_stdout_contains(cell),
6500        expected_stderr: cell_expected_stderr(cell),
6501        comparator: if cell.id.mode == "verify" {
6502            mode_recipe.comparator.unwrap_or(Comparator::Strict)
6503        } else {
6504            Comparator::Strict
6505        },
6506        attempt: attempt.into(),
6507        fixed_workdir_source,
6508    })
6509}
6510
6511/// The Hermit subcommand a verified cell runs and the arguments only it takes.
6512enum VerifiedInvocation {
6513    /// Two `hermit run --verify-run` runs, compared by `hermit log-diff
6514    /// --verify-json` ([`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`]).
6515    Verify,
6516    /// `hermit record start --verify-run`, then the same command replaying
6517    /// that recording (`--verify-replay-of`), compared by `hermit log-diff
6518    /// --verify-json`.
6519    Replay { record_timeout_seconds: u64 },
6520    /// The same pair, each run under one random schedule (`--chaos`).
6521    Chaos { seed: i64 },
6522}
6523
6524struct VerifiedInvocationArgs<'a> {
6525    context: &'a RunContext,
6526    cell: &'a SelectedCell,
6527    backend: &'a str,
6528    invocation: VerifiedInvocation,
6529    verdict: &'a Path,
6530    verification_log_dir: Option<&'a Path>,
6531    /// The attempt's `verify-runs/<attempt>` directory, for a verify or chaos
6532    /// attempt ([`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`]).
6533    verify_runs: Option<&'a Path>,
6534    bound_workdir_source: Option<&'a Path>,
6535    /// The cell directory whose inputs are bound at their guest paths, for an
6536    /// equalized cell.
6537    equalized_inputs_dir: Option<&'a Path>,
6538    /// The equalized roots the cell's argv names, bound beside its inputs.
6539    equalized_roots: &'a [EqualizedRoot],
6540    env: &'a BTreeMap<String, String>,
6541    guest_argv: &'a [String],
6542}
6543
6544/// The backends that run Detcore inside the guest process with in-guest
6545/// LiteInst. Hermit refuses to run them with a preemption timer, which their
6546/// in-guest Tool host cannot deliver yet, so every enabled cell of theirs
6547/// declares `--max-timeslice=disabled`
6548/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3745).
6549const IN_GUEST_LITEINST_BACKENDS: [&str; 2] = ["liteinst", "in-guest-trap"];
6550
6551/// Why a probe of a disabled in-guest LiteInst cell runs with
6552/// `--max-timeslice=disabled` (see [`probe_relaxation`]).
6553const PROBE_RELAXATION_REASON: &str = "a probe of a disabled in-guest LiteInst cell runs without a preemption timer, which Hermit refuses to start that backend with (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3745)";
6554
6555/// The relaxation a probe of a disabled verify cell (`test-harness run
6556/// --probe-disabled`) adds to the cell's own flags: `--max-timeslice=disabled`
6557/// for an in-guest LiteInst backend when the cell names no `--max-timeslice`
6558/// of its own. A disabled cell usually declares no flags for its backend, and
6559/// without that one Hermit refuses every in-guest LiteInst run before the
6560/// guest starts, so the probe would measure the refusal instead of the
6561/// program. The flag stays in the recorded argv, which is where an enabled
6562/// cell's declared relaxation is recorded too.
6563fn probe_relaxation(cell: &SelectedCell, backend: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
6564    let declared = cell_hermit_args(&cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode], backend);
6565    (!cell.enabled
6566        && cell.id.mode == "verify"
6567        && IN_GUEST_LITEINST_BACKENDS.contains(&backend)
6568        && !declared
6569            .iter()
6570            .any(|arg| arg.starts_with("--max-timeslice")))
6571    .then_some("--max-timeslice=disabled")
6572}
6573
6574/// The program every verify, chaos and replay attempt runs: two executions of
6575/// the guest, each writing its evidence to a `--verify-run` directory, then
6576/// `hermit log-diff --verify-json` over the two directories
6577/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4275). For a verify or chaos
6578/// cell both are `hermit run`s; for a replay cell the first is `hermit record
6579/// start` and the second replays its recording, the run command's
6580/// [`VERIFY_REPLAY_OF_PLACEHOLDER`] becoming `--verify-replay-of <run1>` there
6581/// and nothing in the first.
6582///
6583/// It is run as `bash -c VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT VERIFY_PAIR_NAME COMPARISON...
6584/// RUN...`, so the attempt is one process tree: the executor's CPU budget,
6585/// timeout and CPU evidence cover all three commands, as they covered the
6586/// single `run --verify` or `record start --verify` they replace. COMPARISON
6587/// is the `log-diff` command, whose last two words are the run directories;
6588/// RUN is the guest command,
6589/// with [`VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER`] where each execution's directory goes.
6590/// Both start with the Hermit binary, which no other word of COMPARISON is,
6591/// so its second appearance is where RUN starts.
6592///
6593/// It follows `run --verify`: run 2 starts only when run 1 left a record and
6594/// its exit status is one `--verify-allow` admits (a replay cell admits
6595/// every status, as `record start --verify` replays every recording), and
6596/// when a run leaves no
6597/// record (Hermit refused it before it started) the attempt ends with that
6598/// run's status and output, after the comparison has stamped its report. Each
6599/// run's own stderr is passed on, run 1's first. Each run reads stdin through
6600/// its own open file description, a reopening of `/proc/self/fd/0`, so a
6601/// frozen stdin (`hermit verify-inputs`) reaches both from its start rather
6602/// than through one shared offset. The two runs execute one
6603/// after the other, on the same workdir and inputs, as `run --verify`'s do: a
6604/// bind source's host path is visible to the guest in /proc/self/mountinfo,
6605/// so two concurrent runs could not each have their own without the guest
6606/// seeing the difference.
6607///
6608/// Each run also writes to the same path, `run` beside the two directories,
6609/// which is moved to its own directory once the run has ended. Hermit is
6610/// the guest's PID 1, so its command line and its open files are the
6611/// guest's to read (`ps aux` prints `/proc/1/cmdline`): a run told
6612/// `--verify-run .../run1` and one told `.../run2` were two different
6613/// guests, and compat/ps, compat/pgrep and compat/pkill diverged on exactly
6614/// that. `run --verify` gave its two runs one command line; this gives them
6615/// one too.
6616const VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT: &str = r#"set -u
6617for ((start = 2; start <= $#; start++)); do
6618  [[ ${!start} == "$1" ]] && break
6619done
6620comparison=("${@:1:start-1}")
6621run=("${@:start}")
6622directories=("${comparison[@]: -2}")
6623allow=success
6624for word in "${comparison[@]}"; do
6625  case $word in --verify-allow=*) allow=${word#--verify-allow=} ;; esac
6626done
6627staging=${directories[0]%/*}/run
6628verify_run() {
6629  local directory=$1 status word words=()
6630  for word in "${run[@]}"; do
6631    if [[ $word == @VERIFY_REPLAY_OF@ ]]; then
6632      [[ $directory == "${directories[1]}" ]] && words+=(--verify-replay-of "${directories[0]}")
6633      continue
6634    fi
6635    [[ $word == @VERIFY_RUN_DIR@ ]] && word=$staging
6636    words+=("$word")
6637  done
6638  "${words[@]}" </proc/self/fd/0 >"$staging.stdout" 2>"$staging.stderr"
6639  status=$?
6640  mv "$staging.stdout" "$directory.stdout"
6641  mv "$staging.stderr" "$directory.stderr"
6642  if [[ -e $staging ]]; then
6643    mv "$staging" "$directory"
6644  fi
6645  return "$status"
6646}
6647end_without_comparison() {
6648  cat "$1.stdout"
6649  "${comparison[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1
6650  exit "$2"
6651}
6652verify_run "${directories[0]}"
6653status=$?
6654cat "${directories[0]}.stderr" >&2
6655[[ -e ${directories[0]}/verify-run.json ]] || end_without_comparison "${directories[0]}" "$status"
6656case $allow in
6657  success) admitted=$((status == 0)) ;;
6658  failure) admitted=$((status != 0)) ;;
6659  *) admitted=1 ;;
6660esac
6661if ((admitted)); then
6662  verify_run "${directories[1]}"
6663  status=$?
6664  cat "${directories[1]}.stderr" >&2
6665  [[ -e ${directories[1]}/verify-run.json ]] || end_without_comparison "${directories[1]}" "$status"
6666fi
6667exec "${comparison[@]}"
6668"#;
6669
6670/// `$0` of [`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`], which names it in the shell's own messages.
6671const VERIFY_PAIR_NAME: &str = "hermit-verify-pair";
6672
6673/// The word of a paired run command that `VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT` replaces with
6674/// the one path both executions write their `--verify-run` directory at.
6675pub const VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER: &str = "@VERIFY_RUN_DIR@";
6676
6677/// The word of a paired `record start` command that [`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`]
6678/// drops from the recording's command and replaces with `--verify-replay-of
6679/// <run1>` in the replay's.
6680const VERIFY_REPLAY_OF_PLACEHOLDER: &str = "@VERIFY_REPLAY_OF@";
6681
6682/// The descriptor `hermit verify-inputs` places a verified attempt's
6683/// shared-input manifest at: above 2 and outside the native adapter's
6684/// reserved 198-204.
6685const SHARED_INPUTS_FD: &str = "9";
6686
6687/// The run option that adopts that manifest, the same word in both runs, so
6688/// the two guests still see one Hermit command line.
6689const SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG: &str = "--native-exec-shared-inputs=9";
6690
6691/// The host's dynamic-linker cache, as the holder seals it: Hermit binds the
6692/// copy the run adopts under this role in place of reading the host's file
6693/// at each run's setup.
6694const LD_SO_CACHE_PATH: &str = "/etc/ld.so.cache";
6695const LD_SO_CACHE_INPUT: &str = "ld-so-cache:/etc/ld.so.cache";
6696
6697/// The words before a paired program that [`shared_inputs_argv`] puts there,
6698/// after the Hermit binary.
6699///
6700/// No `--` ends the holder's options: the program follows them directly, so
6701/// the first `--` of the recorded command line is still the run's guest
6702/// separator, where its readers ([`ParityGuestInputs`](crate::parity), the
6703/// SaBRe selection, the scorecard) find the end of Hermit's options.
6704const MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX: [&str; 4] = [
6705    "verify-inputs",
6706    "--in-guest-exec-stop",
6707    "--manifest-fd",
6708    "197",
6709];
6710
6711const SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX: [&str; 5] = [
6712    "verify-inputs",
6713    "--manifest-fd",
6714    SHARED_INPUTS_FD,
6715    "--input",
6716    LD_SO_CACHE_INPUT,
6717];
6718
6719/// `paired` run under `hermit verify-inputs`, which seals the host's
6720/// `/etc/ld.so.cache` once for the attempt and hands both runs that one copy.
6721///
6722/// A host package manager replaces the cache many times an hour. Each run
6723/// used to freeze its own copy when its container was set up, so a
6724/// replacement between the two runs gave them different caches: the
6725/// loader's `fstat` of it differed, and the comparison reported a
6726/// divergence that no host-input check could name
6727/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4693).
6728fn shared_inputs_argv(hermit: &str, mut paired: Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
6729    if paired
6730        .get(1..=MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len())
6731        .is_some_and(|words| words.iter().map(String::as_str).eq(MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX))
6732    {
6733        // Reuse the mapped holder, rather than nesting a second process whose
6734        // manifest would replace the first owner at CLI entry.
6735        paired.splice(
6736            1 + MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()..1 + MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len(),
6737            ["--input".into(), LD_SO_CACHE_INPUT.into()],
6738        );
6739        return paired;
6740    }
6741    let mut argv = vec![hermit.to_owned()];
6742    argv.extend(SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.map(String::from));
6743    argv.extend(paired);
6744    argv
6745}
6746
6747/// The `--verify-run` directories of a paired attempt, below its
6748/// `verify-runs/<attempt>` directory.
6749fn verify_run_directories(verify_runs: &Path) -> [PathBuf; 2] {
6750    [verify_runs.join("run1"), verify_runs.join("run2")]
6751}
6752
6753/// The CPU profile the ptrace verify run of a parity-compared test names
6754/// ([`names_parity_golden_profile`]), right after `run`.
6755///
6756/// The ptrace verify log is the parity golden
6757/// ([`crate::parity::PARITY_REFERENCE_BACKEND`]), and no candidate backend can
6758/// carry x86-64-v3: with no profile named, auto presents x86-64-v3 on a
6759/// qualifying ptrace host and x86-64-v2 on every other backend. The two
6760/// profiles answer CPUID differently, so the guest's C library takes other
6761/// paths and selects other routines, and Detcore's records (each CPUID
6762/// check-in, every retired-branch count) differ from the first instructions:
6763/// the post-pass would compare two different guests. Naming x86-64-v2 on the
6764/// golden alone gives both sides the same profile. A candidate's auto already
6765/// resolves to x86-64-v2 and its record keeps auto's reason, and a test
6766/// planned with no candidate keeps auto, so the e2e cells still run auto's
6767/// x86-64-v3 where nothing compares it across backends. Which tests are named
6768/// follows the plan alone ([`crate::parity::planned_comparisons`]), never the
6769/// post-pass's own switches, which change only what is reported.
6770pub const PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG: &str = "--cpu-profile=x86-64-v2";
6771
6772/// The flag with which a run presents the host's CPUID instead of a profile.
6773const NO_VIRTUALIZE_CPUID_ARG: &str = "--no-virtualize-cpuid";
6774
6775/// Whether this verified run names [`PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG`]: a `verify`
6776/// run on the parity reference backend, of a test whose ptrace verify cell
6777/// this run plans beside at least one candidate's
6778/// ([`RunContext::parity_compares`]), in a run that virtualizes CPUID. A run
6779/// with [`NO_VIRTUALIZE_CPUID_ARG`] (the manifest's own policy, the relaxed
6780/// level or a probe) presents no profile, so naming one would only make its
6781/// record claim a profile its guest never saw.
6782fn names_parity_golden_profile(
6783    context: &RunContext,
6784    cell: &SelectedCell,
6785    backend: &str,
6786    invocation: &VerifiedInvocation,
6787) -> bool {
6788    matches!(invocation, VerifiedInvocation::Verify)
6789        && backend == crate::parity::PARITY_REFERENCE_BACKEND
6790        && context.parity_compares(&cell.id.test)
6791        && !cell_hermit_args(&cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode], backend)
6792            .iter()
6793            .map(String::as_str)
6794            .chain(cell.level_relaxations().into_iter().map(|(arg, _)| arg))
6795            .chain(probe_relaxation(cell, backend))
6796            .any(|arg| arg == NO_VIRTUALIZE_CPUID_ARG)
6797}
6798
6799/// The one argv builder for verify, replay and chaos cells.
6800///
6801/// The three modes run the same guest under the same base environment,
6802/// strictness, execution root and guest environment; only the subcommand and
6803/// the arguments in [`VerifiedInvocation`] differ. Building them in one place is
6804/// what keeps a replay cell from silently running a different guest than the
6805/// verify cell it records. Every one runs its guest command under
6806/// [`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`].
6807fn verified_invocation_argv(args: VerifiedInvocationArgs<'_>) -> Vec<String> {
6808    let VerifiedInvocationArgs {
6809        context,
6810        cell,
6811        backend,
6812        invocation,
6813        verdict,
6814        verification_log_dir,
6815        verify_runs,
6816        bound_workdir_source,
6817        equalized_inputs_dir,
6818        equalized_roots,
6819        env,
6820        guest_argv,
6821    } = args;
6822    let mode_recipe = &cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode];
6823    let hermit = context.hermit_bin.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
6824    let mut argv = vec![
6825        hermit.clone(),
6826        "--log".into(),
6827        "info".into(),
6828        "--backend".into(),
6829        backend.into(),
6830    ];
6831    let verify_strict = match invocation {
6832        VerifiedInvocation::Replay { .. } => {
6833            argv.extend(["record".into(), "start".into()]);
6834            context.record_verify_strict
6835        }
6836        VerifiedInvocation::Verify | VerifiedInvocation::Chaos { .. } => {
6837            // A run writes its manifest (`cpu_profile_record`); `record start
6838            // --verify-run` writes none, so it is not asked for one.
6839            argv.extend([
6840                "run".into(),
6841                crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG.into(),
6842            ]);
6843            if names_parity_golden_profile(context, cell, backend, &invocation) {
6844                argv.push(PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG.into());
6845            }
6846            context.run_verify_strict
6847        }
6848    };
6849    argv.extend(["--base-env=minimal".into(), "--strict".into()]);
6850    // A bucket with a hermetic image runs the cell inside it: Hermit is the
6851    // container, the cell workdir is bound at /work, and the image root
6852    // stays read-only. Native cells keep the host execution.
6853    // A v2 retry attempt (RunContext::v2_retry_oci_dir) runs inside the
6854    // bundle-shipped v2 rootfs instead of any bucket image: the retry
6855    // exists because the host userspace's loader refused the v2 CPU, and
6856    // the bucket image, where a cell has one, is not that rootfs. The
6857    // attempt loop sets it only on a verify or chaos retry, on KVM or
6858    // ptrace, of a cell with no bucket image, so the two never compete in an
6859    // executed run.
6860    let v2_image = context
6861        .v2_retry_oci_dir
6862        .as_ref()
6863        .map(|dir| format!("oci-dir:{}", dir.display()));
6864    debug_assert!(
6865        v2_image.is_none() || cell.image.is_none(),
6866        "a v2 retry is never given to a cell with a bucket image ({:?})",
6867        cell.image
6868    );
6869    let cell_image = if backend == "native" {
6870        None
6871    } else if let Some(image) = v2_image.as_deref() {
6872        Some(image)
6873    } else {
6874        cell.image.as_deref()
6875    };
6876    if let Some(image) = cell_image {
6877        argv.extend(["--image".into(), image.to_owned()]);
6878    }
6879    if v2_image.is_some() && backend == "kvm" {
6880        // Strict KVM binder admission inspects the host kernel through
6881        // /sys/module from inside the image rootfs, where no sysfs is
6882        // mounted; bind the host's in read-only so the inspection reads
6883        // the kernel it exists to read. The guest can then list host
6884        // module names under /sys/module; that visibility is the named
6885        // cost of the KVM retry (issue 5476, E-b item 4). A ptrace retry
6886        // has no such admission, so it gets no host sysfs.
6887        argv.push("--bind=/sys/module:/sys/module:ro".into());
6888    }
6889    argv.extend(cell.test.proc.map(|level| level.flag().to_string()));
6890    if verify_strict && mode_recipe.comparator != Some(Comparator::Stripped) {
6891        argv.push("--verify-strict".into());
6892    }
6893    // Validation admits these relaxations only on a verify recipe, and a
6894    // replay cell does not inherit them: `record start` has no such flags.
6895    // Validation refuses `compare_io_buffers=false` outright; the flag is
6896    // still rendered for a recipe built without validation, such as one that
6897    // reproduces a retained row recorded before the refusal.
6898    argv.extend(cell_hermit_args(mode_recipe, backend).iter().cloned());
6899    argv.extend(
6900        cell.level_relaxations()
6901            .into_iter()
6902            .map(|(arg, _)| arg.to_string()),
6903    );
6904    argv.extend(probe_relaxation(cell, backend).map(str::to_string));
6905    if mode_recipe.compare_io_buffers == Some(false) {
6906        argv.push("--no-detlog-io-buffers".into());
6907    }
6908    if mode_recipe.rcb_time == Some(false) {
6909        argv.push("--no-rcb-time".into());
6910    }
6911    // The allowance `run --verify` would take, which the paired comparison
6912    // takes in its place.
6913    let verify_allow = match &invocation {
6914        // `record start --verify` replays and compares every recording,
6915        // whatever its status; `both` has the paired program do the same,
6916        // and a recording's comparison applies no allowance.
6917        VerifiedInvocation::Chaos { .. } | VerifiedInvocation::Replay { .. } => {
6918            Some("--verify-allow=both")
6919        }
6920        // The exact disposition is enforced on the report after the
6921        // comparison; this only lets a failing first run be compared.
6922        VerifiedInvocation::Verify if cell_expected_guest_exit(cell).is_some() => {
6923            Some("--verify-allow=failure")
6924        }
6925        VerifiedInvocation::Verify => None,
6926    };
6927    // A `record start` takes no shared inputs, and a host without a cache has
6928    // none to seal. Nor does a run inside an image, a bucket image or the v2
6929    // retry rootfs (issue 5476): its loader reads the image's own
6930    // /etc/ld.so.cache, or none. Hermit's image container binds no host file
6931    // there, so a sealed host cache would be a host input that nothing in the
6932    // guest reads.
6933    let shares_ld_so_cache = !matches!(invocation, VerifiedInvocation::Replay { .. })
6934        && context.shares_ld_so_cache
6935        && cell_image.is_none();
6936    match invocation {
6937        VerifiedInvocation::Replay {
6938            record_timeout_seconds,
6939        } => {
6940            argv.extend([
6941                "--verify-run".into(),
6942                VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER.into(),
6943                VERIFY_REPLAY_OF_PLACEHOLDER.into(),
6944                "--record-timeout".into(),
6945                record_timeout_seconds.to_string(),
6946            ]);
6947        }
6948        VerifiedInvocation::Verify => {
6949            argv.extend(["--verify-run".into(), VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER.into()]);
6950            argv.extend(shares_ld_so_cache.then(|| SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG.to_owned()));
6951        }
6952        VerifiedInvocation::Chaos { seed } => {
6953            argv.extend(["--verify-run".into(), VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER.into()]);
6954            argv.extend(shares_ld_so_cache.then(|| SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG.to_owned()));
6955            argv.extend([
6956                "--chaos".into(),
6957                "--sched-heuristic=random".into(),
6958                format!("--seed={seed}"),
6959            ]);
6960        }
6961    }
6962    let mut comparison = vec![
6963        hermit.clone(),
6964        "log-diff".into(),
6965        "--verify-json".into(),
6966        verdict.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6967    ];
6968    comparison.extend(verify_allow.map(str::to_string));
6969    if let Some(logs) = verification_log_dir {
6970        comparison.extend([
6971            "--verify-log-dir".into(),
6972            logs.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
6973        ]);
6974    }
6975    let verify_runs = verify_runs.expect("a verified attempt has its verify-run directories");
6976    comparison.extend(
6977        verify_run_directories(verify_runs)
6978            .iter()
6979            .map(|directory| directory.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
6980    );
6981    if cell_image.is_some() {
6982        // The built guest program lives in the cell's fixtures directory;
