6983        // bind it at /work (the program is /work/program). The repository
6984        // (for script cells) is bound beside it at /work/repo.
6985        if let Some(source) = env.get("E2E_FIXTURE_DIR") {
6986            argv.push(format!("--bind={source}:/work"));
6987        } else if let Some(source) = bound_workdir_source.or(context.isolated_workdir.as_deref()) {
6988            argv.push(format!("--bind={}:/work", source.display()));
6989        }
6990        if guest_argv
6991            .iter()
6992            .any(|arg| arg.starts_with(REPOSITORY_GUEST_PATH) || arg.starts_with("./"))
6993        {
6994            argv.push(format!("--bind={}:/repo", context.root.display()));
6995        }
6996        argv.extend(["--workdir".into(), "/work".into()]);
6997    } else {
6998        append_execution_root_args(
6999            &mut argv,
7000            backend,
7001            context.isolated_workdir.as_deref(),
7002            cell_workdir(cell).as_deref(),
7003            bound_workdir_source,
7004        );
7005    }
7006    let isolated = context.isolated_workdir.is_some();
7007    if cell_image.is_some() {
7008        // No equalized-input binds inside the image (their /tmp/e2e targets
7009        // do not exist there); /work is the equalized fixture path.
7010        let mut guest_env = env.clone();
7011        guest_env.insert("E2E_FIXTURE_DIR".into(), "/work".into());
7012        append_guest_env_args(&mut argv, &guest_env, isolated);
7013    } else if let Some(cell_dir) = equalized_inputs_dir {
7014        append_equalized_input_binds(&mut argv, cell_dir, equalized_roots);
7015        append_guest_env_args(&mut argv, &equalized_guest_env(env), isolated);
7016    } else {
7017        append_guest_env_args(&mut argv, env, isolated);
7018    }
7019    for (name, value) in cell_mode_env(cell) {
7020        argv.extend(["--env".into(), format!("{name}={value}")]);
7021    }
7022    argv.push("--".into());
7023    if cell_image.is_some() {
7024        // Inside the image the guest binary is reached through /work.
7025        let mut guest = guest_argv.to_vec();
7026        // Only the host-built cell program moves to /work; image programs
7027        // (shells, coreutils) keep their image paths. Any argument naming
7028        // the repository (direct shell commands) is remapped to /repo.
7029        for arg in guest.iter_mut() {
7030            if arg.ends_with("/program") || arg.as_str() == "program" {
7031                *arg = "/work/program".into();
7032            } else if let Some(rest) = arg.strip_prefix(REPOSITORY_GUEST_PATH) {
7033                *arg = format!("/repo{rest}");
7034            } else if let Some(rest) = arg.strip_prefix("./") {
7035                *arg = format!("/repo/{rest}");
7036            }
7037        }
7038        argv.extend(guest);
7039    } else {
7040        argv.extend(guest_argv.iter().cloned());
7041    }
7042    let paired = paired_verification_argv(comparison, argv);
7043    if shares_ld_so_cache {
7044        shared_inputs_argv(&hermit, paired)
7045    } else {
7046        paired
7047    }
7048}
7049
7050/// The argv of `VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT` comparing two executions of the `run`
7051/// command with the `comparison` command, as the executor runs every
7052/// verified attempt. `run` carries `--verify-run @VERIFY_RUN_DIR@`; the last
7053/// two words of `comparison` are the attempt's run1 and run2 directories.
7054pub fn paired_verification_argv(comparison: Vec<String>, mut run: Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
7055    // Reuse the existing holder and pair script: only the retained runtime
7056    // transport changes. Both runs keep one command line and independent
7057    // open descriptions of the holder's frozen stdin.
7058    let separator = run.iter().position(|word| word == "--");
7059    let mapped =
7060        separator.is_some_and(|end| run[..end].iter().any(|word| word == "--in-guest-exec-stop"));
7061    let holder = mapped.then(|| run[0].clone());
7062    if mapped {
7063        // The original cache-sharing command used fd 9. Both resources now
7064        // travel in the mapped owner's fd 197; keep exactly one run option.
7065        if let Some(index) = run[..separator.unwrap()]
7066            .iter()
7067            .position(|arg| arg == SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG)
7068        {
7069            run.remove(index);
7070        }
7071        let separator = run.iter().position(|word| word == "--").unwrap();
7072        run.insert(separator, "--native-exec-shared-inputs=197".into());
7073    }
7074    let mut paired = vec![
7075        "bash".into(),
7076        "-c".into(),
7077        VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT.into(),
7078        VERIFY_PAIR_NAME.into(),
7079    ];
7080    paired.extend(comparison);
7081    paired.extend(run);
7082    if let Some(hermit) = holder {
7083        let mut owned = vec![hermit];
7084        owned.extend(MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX.map(String::from));
7085        owned.extend(paired);
7086        owned
7087    } else {
7088        paired
7089    }
7090}
7091
7092fn current_verification_report(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<VerificationReport, String> {
7093    VerificationReport::from_current_json_slice(bytes)
7094}
7095
7096/// Backends whose every completed run must carry a dispatch record.
7097const DISPATCH_RECORD_BACKENDS: [&str; 4] = ["ptrace", "liteinst", "in-guest-trap", "sabre"];
7098
7099/// Why a passing verify report's runtime does not carry each run's dispatch
7100/// record for `backend`, or `None` when it does.
7101///
7102/// Only a run whose summary was read is checked: a report without runtime has
7103/// nothing to carry the record in. KVM and DBT have no record, and native runs
7104/// no backend, so they are not checked.
7105///
7106/// `in-guest-trap` is held to more. Its pass claims that both executions ran
7107/// with syscall site patching off, and only the dispatch records show that, so
7108/// the report must carry the runtime, both runs' summaries and both records,
7109/// and each record must report no syscall site patched and none considered
7110/// for patching, and must have measured something: every syscall of a run
7111/// with patching off reaches the Tool as an in-guest `SIGSYS`, so a record
7112/// with no signal trap is the empty record of a run whose guests collected no
7113/// statistics, whose zeros are not measurements. And otherwise: a patched site (a guest that turned patching back on, or a
7114/// Hermit that stopped forcing it off) makes the cell's result a liteinst
7115/// result under the wrong name, and missing evidence cannot rule that out.
7116fn dispatch_record_error(backend: &str, runtime: Option<&VerificationRuntime>) -> Option<String> {
7117    if !DISPATCH_RECORD_BACKENDS.contains(&backend) {
7118        return None;
7119    }
7120    let requires_every_run = backend == "in-guest-trap";
7121    let Some(runtime) = runtime else {
7122        return requires_every_run.then(|| {
7123            "verification report carries no runtime, so it cannot show that both in-guest-trap \
7124             runs patched no syscall site"
7125                .to_owned()
7126        });
7127    };
7128    [
7129        ("run1", runtime.run1.as_ref()),
7130        ("run2", runtime.run2.as_ref()),
7131    ]
7132    .into_iter()
7133    .find_map(|(run, stats)| {
7134        let Some(stats) = stats else {
7135            return requires_every_run.then(|| {
7136                format!(
7137                    "verification runtime.{run} is missing, so it cannot show that this \
7138                     in-guest-trap run patched no syscall site"
7139                )
7140            });
7141        };
7142        let Some(record) = &stats.dispatch else {
7143            return Some(format!(
7144                "verification runtime.{run} carries no {backend} dispatch record"
7145            ));
7146        };
7147        if record.backend != backend {
7148            return Some(format!(
7149                "verification runtime.{run} dispatch record names backend {}, expected {backend}",
7150                record.backend
7151            ));
7152        }
7153        let inconsistencies = record.inconsistencies();
7154        if !inconsistencies.is_empty() {
7155            return Some(format!(
7156                "verification runtime.{run} dispatch record is inconsistent: {}",
7157                inconsistencies.join("; ")
7158            ));
7159        }
7160        let shown = |count: Option<u64>| {
7161            count.map_or_else(|| "unmeasured".to_owned(), |count| count.to_string())
7162        };
7163        if requires_every_run && record.counters.signal_traps.is_none_or(|traps| traps == 0) {
7164            return Some(format!(
7165                "verification runtime.{run} in-guest-trap dispatch record counts {} signal \
7166                 traps, so its guests measured nothing and its zero patched sites are not a \
7167                 measurement",
7168                shown(record.counters.signal_traps)
7169            ));
7170        }
7171        (requires_every_run
7172            && (record.sites.patched != Some(0) || record.sites.candidates != Some(0)))
7173        .then(|| {
7174            format!(
7175                "verification runtime.{run} in-guest-trap dispatch record reports {} patched \
7176                 and {} candidate syscall sites, expected 0 and 0",
7177                shown(record.sites.patched),
7178                shown(record.sites.candidates)
7179            )
7180        })
7181    })
7182}
7183pub fn execute_spec(spec: &CellRunSpec) -> Result<AttemptResult, String> {
7184    execute_spec_until(
7185        spec,
7186        execution_deadline_after_preparation(Instant::now(), spec.timeout_seconds)?,
7187        spec.timeout_seconds,
7188        spec.timeout_seconds,
7189        None,
7190        &mut Vec::new(),
7191    )
7192}
7193
7194/// The failure an attempt's producer classified on the first line of its
7195/// stderr, before any verification report is read. The executor gives each
7196/// its own ERROR kind, and no report read afterwards may supersede it.
7197#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
7198enum ProducerFailure {
7199    /// The guest program was not found or not executable, so no guest was
7200    /// created.
7201    LaunchRefused,
7202    /// The runner cannot start the requested backend. The first line is the
7203    /// producer-owned class emitted before human prose; matching a broader
7204    /// nonzero exit would hide real regressions. KVM currently bypasses
7205    /// ensure_available, so its availability failures do not enter this class.
7206    BackendUnavailable,
7207    /// A backend-unavailable class for another backend or execution shape: it
7208    /// is unavailable evidence, not a product crash, and the human error line
7209    /// must never override the mismatched class into FAIL.
7210    InvalidBackendEvidence,
7211    /// The producer wrote a class that does not establish a more specific
7212    /// result. That absence stays a no-result instead of letting the following
7213    /// English line manufacture a product failure.
7214    UnclassifiedInternal,
7215}
7216
7217/// Which [`ProducerFailure`] the executor finds for an attempt of a `mode`
7218/// cell on `backend` whose Hermit process `succeeded` (exit status 0) or not,
7219/// `timed_out` or not, and wrote `stdout` and `stderr`; `None` when it finds
7220/// none. The executor classifies its own attempt with this, and
7221/// [`host_input_change_only`] re-decides a retained attempt with it.
7222fn producer_failure(
7223    mode: &str,
7224    backend: Option<&str>,
7225    succeeded: bool,
7226    timed_out: bool,
7227    stdout: &str,
7228    stderr: &str,
7229) -> Option<ProducerFailure> {
7230    if succeeded {
7231        return None;
7232    }
7233    let line = stderr.lines().next().unwrap_or_default();
7234    if mode != "naked"
7235        && stdout.is_empty()
7236        && matches!(
7237            line,
7238            "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=guest-program-not-found"
7239                | "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=guest-program-not-executable"
7240        )
7241    {
7242        return Some(ProducerFailure::LaunchRefused);
7243    }
7244    if timed_out {
7245        return None;
7246    }
7247    if mode != "naked"
7248        && stdout.is_empty()
7249        && backend.is_some_and(|backend| {
7250            line == format!("HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=backend-unavailable backend={backend}")
7251        })
7252    {
7253        return Some(ProducerFailure::BackendUnavailable);
7254    }
7255    if line.starts_with("HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=backend-unavailable backend=") {
7256        return Some(ProducerFailure::InvalidBackendEvidence);
7257    }
7258    if line == "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=cli-error" {
7259        return Some(ProducerFailure::UnclassifiedInternal);
7260    }
7261    None
7262}
7263
7264fn execute_spec_until(
7265    spec: &CellRunSpec,
7266    deadline: Instant,
7267    cpu_timeout_seconds: u64,
7268    wall_timeout_seconds: u64,
7269    remaining_cpu_usec: Option<u64>,
7270    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
7271) -> Result<AttemptResult, String> {
7272    // The attempt label comes from the spec rather than a parallel parameter.
7273    // `build_spec` already stored it, and every caller passed the same value to
7274    // both, so a separate argument was a second definition that could go stale
7275    // against the workdir and capture paths built from the first.
7276    let index = spec.attempt.as_str();
7277    if spec.argv.is_empty() {
7278        return Err("empty cell argv".into());
7279    }
7280    if let Some(verdict) = &spec.verdict_path {
7281        let _ = fs::remove_file(verdict);
7282    }
7283    let tmp = spec.cell_dir.join("tmp");
7284    if tmp.exists() {
7285        fs::remove_dir_all(&tmp).map_err(|e| format!("cannot reset {}: {e}", tmp.display()))?;
7286    }
7287    fs::create_dir_all(&tmp).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", tmp.display()))?;
7288    // The ordinary-host fallback binds this exact per-attempt directory at
7289    // /tmp/test. The explicit hermetic path mounts a fresh tmpfs at /test and
7290    // ignores the directory, but keeping the reset unconditional preserves the
7291    // fallback and makes switching paths a pure precedence decision.
7292    let workdir = &spec.fixed_workdir_source;
7293    if workdir.exists() {
7294        fs::remove_dir_all(workdir)
7295            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot reset {}: {e}", workdir.display()))?;
7296    }
7297    fs::create_dir_all(workdir).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", workdir.display()))?;
7298    // The cell's Hermit data stage and this attempt's own data directory start
7299    // empty, so no earlier attempt's manifest is read as this one's.
7300    let hermit_data = crate::cpu_profile_record::attempt_dirs(&spec.env, index);
7301    if let Some((stage, retained)) = &hermit_data {
7302        crate::cpu_profile_record::reset_attempt(stage, retained)?;
7303    }
7304    // Each `--verify-run` directory must be new, so no earlier attempt's
7305    // evidence can be read as this one's.
7306    if let Some(verify_runs) = &spec.verify_runs {
7307        if verify_runs.exists() {
7308            fs::remove_dir_all(verify_runs)
7309                .map_err(|e| format!("cannot reset {}: {e}", verify_runs.display()))?;
7310        }
7311        fs::create_dir_all(verify_runs)
7312            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", verify_runs.display()))?;
7313    }
7314    if let Some(stage) = &spec.single_run_capture {
7315        let retained = single_run_retained_path(spec);
7316        if stage.try_exists().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
7317            || retained.try_exists().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
7318        {
7319            return Err("refusing stale custom capture stage or retained destination".into());
7320        }
7321        fs::create_dir_all(stage.parent().expect("capture stage has parent"))
7322            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
7323    }
7324    let captures = spec.cell_dir.join("captures");
7325    fs::create_dir_all(&captures).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
7326    let stdout_path = captures.join(format!("{}-{index}.stdout", spec.id.mode));
7327    let stderr_path = captures.join(format!("{}-{index}.stderr", spec.id.mode));
7328    let request = ProcessRequest::new(
7329        InvocationRole::Execution {
7330            attempt_index: spec.attempt.clone(),
7331            backend: spec
7332                .id
7333                .backend
7334                .clone()
7335                .map_or(RequiredNullable::Null, RequiredNullable::Value),
7336        },
7337        &spec.cwd,
7338        &spec.argv[0],
7339        &spec.argv[1..],
7340        &spec.env,
7341        &stdout_path,
7342        &stderr_path,
7343    );
7344    let started = Instant::now();
7345    let remaining = remaining_cell_time(deadline);
7346    let exhausted = if remaining.is_zero() {
7347        Some(ProcessTimeout::Wall)
7348    } else if remaining_cpu_usec == Some(0) {
7349        Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu)
7350    } else {
7351        None
7352    };
7353    if let Some(timeout) = exhausted {
7354        record_not_started(
7355            request,
7356            remaining_cpu_usec.is_some(),
7357            match timeout {
7358                ProcessTimeout::Cpu => NotStartedReason::CpuBudgetAlreadyExhausted,
7359                ProcessTimeout::Wall => NotStartedReason::WallBudgetAlreadyExhausted,
7360            },
7361            observations,
7362        );
7363        fs::write(&stdout_path, b"").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
7364        fs::write(&stderr_path, b"").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
7365        return Ok(cell_timeout_attempt(
7366            spec,
7367            cpu_timeout_seconds,
7368            wall_timeout_seconds,
7369            started.elapsed(),
7370            timeout,
7371        ));
7372    }
7373    if let Some(binding) = &spec.command_binding {
7374        binding.recheck()?;
7375    }
7376    let output = execute_process(request, (deadline, remaining_cpu_usec), observations);
7377    // However the process ended, what its Hermit runs wrote becomes this
7378    // attempt's before the next attempt reuses the stage.
7379    let retained = hermit_data.as_ref().map_or(Ok(()), |(stage, retained)| {
7380        crate::cpu_profile_record::retain_stage(stage, retained)
7381    });
7382    if let Some(binding) = &spec.command_binding {
7383        binding.recheck()?;
7384    }
7385    let output = output?;
7386    retained?;
7387    let stdout = fs::read_to_string(&stdout_path).unwrap_or_default();
7388    let stderr = fs::read_to_string(&stderr_path).unwrap_or_default();
7389    let mut outcome = if output.timeout.is_some() || !output.status.success() {
7390        "FAIL"
7391    } else {
7392        "PASS"
7393    }
7394    .to_string();
7395    let mut reason = output
7396        .timeout
7397        .map(|kind| kind.reason(cpu_timeout_seconds, wall_timeout_seconds));
7398    let mut error_kind = None;
7399    let failure_class_line = stderr.lines().next().unwrap_or_default();
7400    let producer_class = producer_failure(
7401        &spec.id.mode,
7402        spec.command_binding
7403            .as_ref()
7404            .map(|held| held.identity.producer_backend.as_str())
7405            .or(spec.id.backend.as_deref()),
7406        output.status.success(),
7407        output.timeout.is_some(),
7408        &stdout,
7409        &stderr,
7410    );
7411    let launch_refusal = producer_class == Some(ProducerFailure::LaunchRefused);
7412    if launch_refusal {
7413        outcome = "ERROR".into();
7414        error_kind = Some("guest-launch-refused".into());
7415        reason = Some(format!(
7416            "guest launch refused before execution: {}",
7417            stderr
7418                .lines()
7419                .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Error: "))
7420                .unwrap_or("unknown launch refusal")
7421        ));
7422    }
7423    // A runner that cannot start the requested backend and a backend that ran
7424    // but produced no canonical comparison are different failures
7425    // ([`ProducerFailure::BackendUnavailable`]).
7426    let backend_unavailable = producer_class == Some(ProducerFailure::BackendUnavailable);
7427    if backend_unavailable {
7428        outcome = "ERROR".into();
7429        error_kind = Some("backend-unavailable".into());
7430        reason = Some(format!(
7431            "backend unavailable on this runner, so nothing was measured: {}",
7432            stderr
7433                .lines()
7434                .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Error: "))
7435                .unwrap_or("unknown backend unavailability")
7436        ));
7437    }
7438    // A producer class that cannot satisfy the requested backend or execution
7439    // shape ([`ProducerFailure::InvalidBackendEvidence`]).
7440    let invalid_backend_evidence = producer_class == Some(ProducerFailure::InvalidBackendEvidence);
7441    if invalid_backend_evidence {
7442        outcome = "ERROR".into();
7443        error_kind = Some("invalid-backend-evidence".into());
7444        reason = Some(format!(
7445            "backend availability evidence does not match this attempt: {failure_class_line}"
7446        ));
7447    }
7448    // The producer did write a class, but it did not establish a more specific
7449    // result ([`ProducerFailure::UnclassifiedInternal`]).
7450    let unclassified_internal_failure =
7451        producer_class == Some(ProducerFailure::UnclassifiedInternal);
7452    if unclassified_internal_failure {
7453        outcome = "ERROR".into();
7454        error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7455        reason = stderr
7456            .lines()
7457            .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Error: "))
7458            .filter(|detail| !detail.trim().is_empty())
7459            .map(str::to_owned);
7460    }
7461    let producer_failure_classified = producer_class.is_some();
7462    let mut report_json = None;
7463    let mut report_sha = None;
7464    let mut runtime = None;
7465    let mut first_divergent_scheduler_turn = None;
7466    let mut first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = None;
7467    let mut first_divergent_record = None;
7468    let mut first_divergent_syscall = None;
7469    let mut first_divergent_left_message = None;
7470    let mut first_divergent_right_message = None;
7471    let (sabre_path_evidence, sabre_path_evidence_sha256) = spec
7472        .sabre_path_evidence
7473        .as_ref()
7474        .and_then(|path| fs::read(path).ok())
7475        .map(|bytes| {
7476            (
7477                Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned()),
7478                Some(hex_digest(&bytes)),
7479            )
7480        })
7481        .unwrap_or((None, None));
7482    if let Some(path) = &spec.verdict_path {
7483        match fs::read(path) {
7484            Ok(bytes) => {
7485                report_sha = Some(hex_digest(&bytes));
7486                report_json = Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).into_owned());
7487                match current_verification_report(&bytes) {
7488                    Ok(report) => {
7489                        runtime = report.runtime.clone();
7490                        // Recorded BEFORE the classification chain below,
7491                        // because where the divergence began is a fact about
7492                        // the report rather than a consequence of how the
7493                        // attempt is classified -- a FAIL and an ERROR can both
7494                        // carry a located divergence.
7495                        //
7496                        // Guarded on `launch_refusal` for the same reason the
7497                        // arm below refuses to reclassify: no guest was ever
7498                        // created, so any report present cannot describe an
7499                        // executed guest's divergence position.
7500                        if !launch_refusal && !backend_unavailable {
7501                            first_divergent_scheduler_turn = report.first_divergent_scheduler_turn;
7502                            first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds =
7503                                report.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds;
7504                            first_divergent_record = report.first_divergent_record;
7505                            first_divergent_syscall = report.first_divergent_syscall;
7506                            first_divergent_left_message =
7507                                report.first_divergent_left_message.clone();
7508                            first_divergent_right_message =
7509                                report.first_divergent_right_message.clone();
7510                        }
7511                        let typed_run_failure = matches!(
7512                            report.no_result_reason,
7513                            Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::RunFailed { .. })
7514                        );
7515                        if producer_failure_classified
7516                            && !(unclassified_internal_failure && typed_run_failure)
7517                        {
7518                            // The producer's classified failure, or a
7519                            // contradiction in that evidence, cannot be
7520                            // superseded by a pre-stamped or unrelated report.
7521                            // A `run_failed` report is neither: it is the
7522                            // class an unclassified `cli-error` line lacks.
7523                        } else if let Some(
7524                            crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::ContainerFailed(failure),
7525                        ) = &report.no_result_reason
7526                        {
7527                            match failure.require_reporter_exit(
7528                                output.status.code(),
7529                                std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal(&output.status),
7530                                output.timeout.is_some(),
7531                            ) {
7532                                Ok(()) => {
7533                                    outcome = "FAIL".into();
7534                                    error_kind = None;
7535                                    reason = Some(format!(
7536                                        "sandbox failed during {:?}: {:?}; no guest disposition or comparison was returned",
7537                                        failure.run, failure.disposition
7538                                    ));
7539                                }
7540                                Err(error) => {
7541                                    outcome = "ERROR".into();
7542                                    error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7543                                    reason = Some(error);
7544                                }
7545                            }
7546                        } else if let Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::RunFailed {
7547                            run,
7548                            failure,
7549                            detail,
7550                        }) = &report.no_result_reason
7551                        {
7552                            // Hermit started the run and a typed failure of it
7553                            // stopped the run: a backend failure, a recorded
7554                            // determinism loss or a policy refusal of this
7555                            // guest. That is this cell's result on this
7556                            // backend, a crash-error red with Hermit's reason,
7557                            // not a run that never happened. Hermit exits
7558                            // nonzero for each; anything else contradicts it.
7559                            if output.timeout.is_none()
7560                                && output.status.code().is_some_and(|code| code != 0)
7561                            {
7562                                outcome = "FAIL".into();
7563                                error_kind = None;
7564                                reason = Some(format!(
7565                                    "{run:?} failed ({}): {detail}",
7566                                    failure.as_str()
7567                                ));
7568                            } else {
7569                                outcome = "ERROR".into();
7570                                error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7571                                reason = Some(format!(
7572                                    "run_failed contradicts the Hermit process disposition: status={:?} timed_out={}",
7573                                    output.status.code(),
7574                                    output.timeout.is_some()
7575                                ));
7576                            }
7577                        } else if report.verdict == Verdict::InfrastructureError {
7578                            let comparison_error = report.comparison.as_ref().and_then(|_| {
7579                                match spec.comparator {
7580                                    Comparator::Strict => report.require_canonical_comparison(),
7581                                    Comparator::Stripped => require_stripped_comparison(&report),
7582                                }
7583                                .err()
7584                            });
7585                            let skid_reason = match report.infrastructure_error.as_ref() {
7586                                Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count }) => {
7587                                    skid_overshoot_reason(*count)
7588                                }
7589                                Some(change @ InfrastructureError::HostInputChanged { .. }) => {
7590                                    host_input_changed_reason(change)
7591                                }
7592                                None => unreachable!(
7593                                    "typed report parser requires an infrastructure error"
7594                                ),
7595                            };
7596                            // When both runs completed and were compared, the
7597                            // cell's declared stdout assertions are decided
7598                            // before the refusal is accepted as the attempt's
7599                            // only failure. An overshoot moves a preemption
7600                            // point and nothing else, so compared runs that
7601                            // agree on the wrong bytes, or omit the declared
7602                            // marker, carry the same product defect they carry
7603                            // without one. Such an attempt, and one whose
7604                            // assertion the evidence cannot decide, keeps the
7605                            // skid infrastructure ERROR it always had, because
7606                            // every reader of a result row (the validation
7607                            // series writer, the pressure test and the stress
7608                            // series) accepts an `infrastructure_error` report
7609                            // only on that classification. Its reason names
7610                            // both the overshoot and the assertion, and it is
7611                            // never retried, never a pass and never a
7612                            // skid-only attempt: the skid predicate requires
7613                            // the plain skid reason and re-decides the row's
7614                            // recorded declaration from the attempt's own
7615                            // evidence (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845).
7616                            // A host input change is decided the same way: it
7617                            // explains the divergence, not a declared output
7618                            // that either run got wrong, so a violated or
7619                            // undecidable assertion keeps the attempt out of
7620                            // the host-input retry as well.
7621                            let stdout_error = report
7622                                .compared_outputs
7623                                .as_ref()
7624                                .filter(|_| comparison_error.is_none() && output.timeout.is_none())
7625                                .and_then(|_| declared_stdout_error(spec, &report, &stdout_path));
7626                            if let Some(error) = comparison_error {
7627                                outcome = "ERROR".into();
7628                                error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7629                                reason = Some(error);
7630                            } else if let Some(error) = stdout_error {
7631                                outcome = "ERROR".into();
7632                                error_kind = Some("infrastructure".into());
7633                                reason = Some(match error {
7634                                    ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(error) => format!(
7635                                        "{skid_reason}, and a declared stdout assertion cannot be checked: {error}"
7636                                    ),
7637                                    ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error) => format!(
7638                                        "{skid_reason}, and its compared runs violate a declared stdout assertion: {error}"
7639                                    ),
7640                                });
7641                            } else {
7642                                outcome = "ERROR".into();
7643                                error_kind = Some("infrastructure".into());
7644                                reason = Some(skid_reason);
7645                            }
7646                        } else if report.verdict == Verdict::NoResult
7647                            && matches!(
7648                                report.no_result_reason,
7649                                Some(
7650                                    crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::ComparisonRefused { .. }
7651                                )
7652                            )
7653                        {
7654                            let Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::ComparisonRefused {
7655                                detail,
7656                            }) = report.no_result_reason.as_ref()
7657                            else {
7658                                unreachable!()
7659                            };
7660                            outcome = "ERROR".into();
7661                            error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7662                            reason = Some(detail.clone());
7663                        } else if report.verdict == Verdict::NoResult
7664                            && matches!(
7665                                report.no_result_reason,
7666                                Some(
7667                                    crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::FirstRunRejected { .. }
7668                                ) | None
7669                            )
7670                            && output.timeout.is_none()
7671                            && output.status.code().is_some_and(|code| code != 0)
7672                        {
7673                            // The producer correctly has no comparison to
7674                            // report, but an ordinary nonzero process exit is
7675                            // still a completed failure rather than unknown
7676                            // infrastructure state.
7677                            outcome = "FAIL".into();
7678                            error_kind = None;
7679                            reason = Some(format!(
7680                                "{} exited with status {} before producing a terminal comparison",
7681                                spec.id.mode,
7682                                output.status.code().unwrap()
7683                            ));
7684                        } else if let Some(error) = (spec.comparator == Comparator::Stripped)
7685                            .then(|| require_stripped_comparison(&report).err())
7686                            .flatten()
7687                        {
7688                            outcome = "ERROR".into();
7689                            error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7690                            reason = Some(error);
7691                        } else if spec.comparator == Comparator::Stripped
7692                            && !(report.verified && report.verdict == Verdict::Matched)
7693                        {
7694                            // Hermit's default --verify comparison, declared by
7695                            // the cell: it still requires a terminal matched
7696                            // verdict, but it is below L2 and never canonical.
7697                            outcome = "FAIL".into();
7698                            reason = Some(format!(
7699                                "stripped verification did not match: verified={} verdict={}",
7700                                report.verified, report.verdict
7701                            ));
7702                        } else if let Some(error) = (spec.comparator == Comparator::Stripped)
7703                            .then(|| report.require_exact_output_match().err())
7704                            .flatten()
7705                        {
7706                            // The two runs' exact outputs must agree as well;
7707                            // this does not depend on the log comparison.
7708                            outcome = "FAIL".into();
7709                            reason = Some(format!("stripped verification outputs: {error}"));
7710                        } else if let Some(error) = (spec.comparator == Comparator::Strict)
7711                            .then(|| report.require_canonical_comparison().err())
7712                            .flatten()
7713                        {
7714                            outcome = "ERROR".into();
7715                            error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7716                            reason = Some(error);
7717                        } else if let Some(error) = (spec.comparator == Comparator::Strict)
7718                            .then(|| report.require_canonical_match().err())
7719                            .flatten()
7720                        {
7721                            outcome = "FAIL".into();
7722                            reason = Some(error);
7723                        } else if let Some(error) = output
7724                            .timeout
7725                            .is_none()
7726                            .then(|| declared_stdout_error(spec, &report, &stdout_path))
7727                            .flatten()
7728                        {
7729                            // Two runs agreeing on the wrong bytes is still a
7730                            // failure when the cell names the exact bytes, and
7731                            // so are agreeing runs that omit the guest's
7732                            // success marker.
7733                            match error {
7734                                ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(error) => {
7735                                    outcome = "ERROR".into();
7736                                    error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7737                                    reason = Some(error);
7738                                }
7739                                ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error) => {
7740                                    outcome = "FAIL".into();
7741                                    reason = Some(error);
7742                                }
7743                            }
7744                        } else if let Some(expected) = spec
7745                            .expected_guest_exit
7746                            .as_ref()
7747                            .filter(|_| output.timeout.is_none())
7748                        {
7749                            // A matched comparison of the wrong disposition is
7750                            // still a failure: the cell names one exact status.
7751                            match expected.check(
7752                                report.guest_exit_code,
7753                                report.guest_signal,
7754                                output.status.code(),
7755                                std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal(&output.status),
7756                            ) {
7757                                Ok(()) => {
7758                                    outcome = "PASS".into();
7759                                    reason = None;
7760                                }
7761                                Err(error) => {
7762                                    outcome = "FAIL".into();
7763                                    reason = Some(error);
7764                                }
7765                            }
7766                        } else if output.timeout.is_none()
7767                            && (output.status.success() || spec.id.mode == "chaos")
7768                        {
7769                            // Chaos deliberately admits a reproduced nonzero
7770                            // guest class. Verify and replay still require the
7771                            // Hermit process itself to succeed unless a verify
7772                            // cell names its exact expected guest exit above,
7773                            // and no receipt may erase a timeout.
7774                            outcome = "PASS".into();
7775                            reason = None;
7776                        } else if reason.is_none() {
7777                            reason = Some(format!(
7778                                "{} exited with status {}",
7779                                spec.id.mode,
7780                                output.status.code().unwrap_or(128)
7781                            ));
7782                        }
7783                    }
7784                    Err(error) if !producer_failure_classified => {
7785                        outcome = "ERROR".into();
7786                        error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7787                        reason = Some(format!("verification report is unreadable: {error}"));
7788                    }
7789                    Err(_) => {}
7790                }
7791            }
7792            Err(_error) if producer_failure_classified => {}
7793            Err(error) => {
7794                outcome = "ERROR".into();
7795                error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7796                reason = Some(format!("verification report is missing: {error}"));
7797            }
7798        }
7799    }
7800    if outcome == "PASS" {
7801        if let Some(error) = spec
7802            .id
7803            .backend
7804            .as_deref()
7805            .and_then(|backend| dispatch_record_error(backend, runtime.as_ref()))
7806        {
7807            outcome = "ERROR".into();
7808            error_kind = Some("incomplete-verification-evidence".into());
7809            reason = Some(error);
7810        }
7811    }
7812    if let Some(timeout) = output.timeout {
7813        error_kind = Some(timeout.error_kind().into());
7814        reason = Some(timeout.reason(cpu_timeout_seconds, wall_timeout_seconds));
7815    }
7816    // A raw INFO golden does not retain guest streams or the completed status
7817    // record. Keep the pair when evidence retention was explicitly requested,
7818    // so the existing directory comparator can later judge full observations.
7819    // Ordinary matched pairs are still removed; unmatched pairs stay.
7820    let matched = report_json.as_deref().is_some_and(|json| {
7821        current_verification_report(json.as_bytes())
7822            .is_ok_and(|report| report.verdict == Verdict::Matched)
7823    });
7824    if let Some(verify_runs) = spec
7825        .verify_runs
7826        .as_ref()
7827        .filter(|_| matched && spec.verification_log_dir.is_none())
7828    {
7829        fs::remove_dir_all(verify_runs)
7830            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot remove {}: {e}", verify_runs.display()))?;
7831    }
7832    Ok(AttemptResult {
7833        command_binding: spec
7834            .command_binding
7835            .as_ref()
7836            .map(|held| held.identity.clone()),
7837        index: index.into(),
7838        outcome,
7839        error_kind,
7840        status: output.status.code(),
7841        signal: std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt::signal(&output.status),
7842        timed_out: output.timeout.is_some(),
7843        duration_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis(),
7844        cpu_usage_usec: Some(output.cpu_usage_usec),
7845        capture_custom_runs: spec.single_run_capture.is_some(),
7846        single_run_capture: None,
7847        capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: None,
7848        capture_adoption_timeout: None,
7849        observation_sha256: None,
7850        argv: spec.argv.clone(),
7851        guest_argv: spec.guest_argv.clone(),
7852        env: spec.env.clone(),
7853        cwd: spec.cwd.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
7854        shell_command: shell_command(&spec.cwd.to_string_lossy(), &spec.env, &spec.argv),
7855        stdout,
7856        stderr,
7857        verification_report: report_json,
7858        verification_report_sha256: report_sha,
7859        runtime,
7860        first_divergent_scheduler_turn,
7861        first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds,
7862        first_divergent_record,
7863        first_divergent_syscall,
7864        first_divergent_left_message,
7865        first_divergent_right_message,
7866        sabre_path_evidence,
7867        sabre_path_evidence_sha256,
7868        reason,
7869    })
7870}

7915fn record_not_started(
7916    request: ProcessRequest,
7917    cpu_enabled: bool,
7918    reason: NotStartedReason,
7919    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
7920) {
7921    // No process starts, so no cgroup is created and no CPU is measured. The
7922    // row names the source a started invocation would try first.
7923    let mut observation = InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
7924        observations.len() as u64 + 1,
7925        request.role,
7926        request.command,
7927        cpu_enabled.then_some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
7928    );
7929    observation.launch = LaunchObservation::NotStarted { reason };
7930    observations.push(observation);
7931}

7933/// Add two complete CPU measurements, refusing missing or overflowing input.
7934pub fn checked_add_cpu_usage(total: Option<u64>, usage: Option<u64>) -> Option<u64> {
7935    total.and_then(|total| usage.and_then(|usage| total.checked_add(usage)))
7936}
7937
7938fn rusage_cpu_usage_usec(usage: &libc::rusage) -> Result<u64, String> {
7939    WaitCpuObservation::from_rusage(usage).total()
7940}
7941
7942fn wait4_process(
7943    pid: u32,
7944    options: libc::c_int,
7945    operation: WaitOperation,
7946    started: Instant,
7947    final_wait: &mut FinalWaitObservation,
7948) -> Result<Option<(ExitStatus, u64)>, String> {
7949    loop {
7950        let mut status = 0;
7951        let mut usage = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::rusage>() };
7952        let waited = unsafe { libc::wait4(pid as libc::pid_t, &mut status, options, &mut usage) };
7953        if waited == 0 {
7954            return Ok(None);
7955        }
7956        if waited == pid as libc::pid_t {
7957            let cpu = WaitCpuObservation::from_rusage(&usage);
7958            let total = rusage_cpu_usage_usec(&usage);
7959            *final_wait = if libc::WIFEXITED(status) || libc::WIFSIGNALED(status) {
7960                FinalWaitObservation::Reaped {
7961                    source: FinalCpuSource::Wait4,
7962                    pid,
7963                    raw_status: status,
7964                    at: started.elapsed().into(),
7965                    cpu,
7966                }
7967            } else {
7968                FinalWaitObservation::NonterminalReturn {
7969                    source: FinalCpuSource::Wait4,
7970                    pid,
7971                    raw_status: status,
7972                    at: started.elapsed().into(),
7973                    cpu,
7974                }
7975            };
7976            return Ok(Some((ExitStatus::from_raw(status), total?)));
7977        }
7978        let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
7979        if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {
7980            continue;
7981        }
7982        let reason = format!("wait4({pid}) failed: {error}");
7983        *final_wait = FinalWaitObservation::Unavailable {
7984            operation,
7985            errno: error
7986                .raw_os_error()
7987                .map_or(RequiredNullable::Null, RequiredNullable::Value),
7988            reason: reason.clone(),
7989        };
7990        return Err(reason);
7991    }
7992}
7993
7994fn live_cpu_usage_usec(pgid: u32, seconds: f64) -> Result<u64, String> {
7995    let usec = seconds * 1_000_000.0;
7996    // u64::MAX rounds up to 2^64 as f64, so that boundary is exclusive.
7997    if !usec.is_finite() || usec.is_sign_negative() || usec >= u64::MAX as f64 {
7998        return Err(format!(
7999            "process group {pgid} returned invalid live CPU seconds {seconds}"
8000        ));
8001    }
8002    Ok(usec as u64)
8003}
8004
8005/// A pidfd for the invocation's leader, opened while the leader is this
8006/// runner's unreaped child, so it names exactly that process wherever its
8007/// process group goes.
8008struct LeaderPidFd {
8009    pid: u32,
8010    fd: Option<OwnedFd>,
8011}
8012
8013impl LeaderPidFd {
8014    fn open(pid: u32) -> Self {
8015        let fd = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_open, pid as libc::pid_t, 0) };
8016        Self {
8017            pid,
8018            // SAFETY: a nonnegative pidfd_open result is a new descriptor
8019            // that nothing else owns.
8020            fd: (fd >= 0).then(|| unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd as RawFd) }),
8021        }
8022    }
8023
8024    /// SIGKILL the leader itself. Without a pidfd (a kernel older than 5.3),
8025    /// or if the pidfd signal fails, the PID still names the leader: it is
8026    /// this runner's unreaped child, so the kernel cannot reuse it.
8027    fn kill(&self) {
8028        let sent = self.fd.as_ref().is_some_and(|fd| {
8029            let result = unsafe {
8030                libc::syscall(
8031                    libc::SYS_pidfd_send_signal,
8032                    fd.as_raw_fd(),
8033                    libc::SIGKILL,
8034                    std::ptr::null::<libc::siginfo_t>(),
8035                    0,
8036                )
8037            };
8038            result == 0 || std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() == Some(libc::ESRCH)
8039        });
8040        if !sent {
8041            unsafe {
8042                libc::kill(self.pid as libc::pid_t, libc::SIGKILL);
8043            }
8044        }
8045    }
8046}
8047
8048/// Stop the invocation: SIGTERM its process group, wait out the 10 s grace for
8049/// the leader, then SIGKILL the group, the invocation cgroup when there is one,
8050/// and the leader through its pidfd, and reap the leader.
8051fn stop_process_group(
8052    pid: u32,
8053    leader: &LeaderPidFd,
8054    cgroup: Option<&InvocationCgroup>,
8055    started: Instant,
8056    final_wait: &mut FinalWaitObservation,
8057) -> Result<(ExitStatus, u64), String> {
8058    unsafe {
8059        libc::kill(-(pid as i32), libc::SIGTERM);
8060    }
8061    let grace = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
8062    loop {
8063        if let Some(result) = wait4_process(
8064            pid,
8065            libc::WNOHANG,
8066            WaitOperation::StopGrace,
8067            started,
8068            final_wait,
8069        )? {
8070            return Ok(result);
8071        }
8072        if Instant::now() >= grace {
8073            break;
8074        }
8075        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
8076    }
8077    unsafe {
8078        libc::kill(-(pid as i32), libc::SIGKILL);
8079    }
8080    // A leader that moved to another process group, and anything that left
8081    // the group, are beyond the group SIGKILL. The invocation cgroup still
8082    // holds them all, and the pidfd still names the leader, so the blocking
8083    // wait below ends with this kill rather than whenever the leader chooses.
8084    // A cgroup.kill failure is not reported here: the pidfd kill still ends
8085    // the wait, and the cgroup's finish() fails the invocation if anything
8086    // survives.
8087    if let Some(cgroup) = cgroup {
8088        let _ = cgroup.kill();
8089    }
8090    leader.kill();
8091    wait4_process(pid, 0, WaitOperation::BlockingStop, started, final_wait)?.ok_or_else(|| {
8092        let reason = format!("blocking wait4({pid}) returned no child");
8093        *final_wait = FinalWaitObservation::Unavailable {
8094            operation: WaitOperation::BlockingStop,
8095            errno: RequiredNullable::Null,
8096            reason: reason.clone(),
8097        };
8098        reason
8099    })
8100}

8152/// Where a budgeted invocation's live CPU may come from. Production reads the
8153/// fallback marker from the environment and creates invocation cgroups under
8154/// the runner's own cgroup; a test may substitute both for its own thread.
8155#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
8156struct LiveCpuPlan {
8157    allow_process_group_scan: Result<bool, String>,
8158    cgroup_parent: Option<PathBuf>,
8159}
8160
8161#[cfg(test)]
8162thread_local! {
8163    static LIVE_CPU_PLAN_OVERRIDE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<LiveCpuPlan>> =
8164        const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
8165}
8166
8167impl LiveCpuPlan {
8168    fn current() -> Self {
8169        Self::test_override().unwrap_or_else(|| Self {
8170            allow_process_group_scan: process_group_scan_allowed(
8171                std::env::var_os(ALLOW_PROCESS_GROUP_CPU_SCAN_ENV).as_deref(),
8172            ),
8173            cgroup_parent: None,
8174        })
8175    }
8176
8177    #[cfg(test)]
8178    fn test_override() -> Option<Self> {
8179        LIVE_CPU_PLAN_OVERRIDE.with(|plan| plan.borrow().clone())
8180    }
8181
8182    #[cfg(not(test))]
8183    fn test_override() -> Option<Self> {
8184        None
8185    }
8186}

8188/// How one invocation's live CPU is measured.
8189enum LiveCpuMeter {
8190    /// The invocation has no CPU budget, so nothing is measured live.
8191    Disabled,
8192    /// The invocation runs in a cgroup of its own and is charged from that
8193    /// cgroup's `cpu.stat`.
8194    Cgroup(InvocationCgroup),
8195    /// The launcher declared a run without cgroups and none can be created
8196    /// here, so the agent-utils process-group scan measures the invocation and
8197    /// its rows name that source.
8198    ProcessGroupScan,
8199}
8200
8201/// Why a budgeted invocation was refused before anything started, and at
8202/// which launch stage its observation records that refusal.
8203struct MeterRefusal {
8204    stage: SpawnStage,
8205    reason: String,
8206}
8207
8208impl LiveCpuMeter {
8209    /// Choose the meter for a budgeted invocation, or refuse the invocation.
8210    ///
8211    /// A command whose CPU no source can measure is never launched. Started,
8212    /// it would run unmeasured until the unavailable grace stopped it, and a
8213    /// command quicker than that grace would complete and could pass. The
8214    /// grace is for a meter that was established and then failed.
8215    fn choose(plan: &LiveCpuPlan) -> Result<Self, MeterRefusal> {
8216        let allow_process_group_scan =
8217            plan.allow_process_group_scan
8218                .clone()
8219                .map_err(|reason| MeterRefusal {
8220                    stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
8221                    reason,
8222                })?;
8223        let created = match &plan.cgroup_parent {
8224            Some(parent) => InvocationCgroup::create_in(parent),
8225            None => InvocationCgroup::create(),
8226        };
8227        match created {
8228            Ok(cgroup) => Ok(Self::Cgroup(cgroup)),
8229            Err(error) if error.fallback_eligible && allow_process_group_scan => {
8230                Ok(Self::ProcessGroupScan)
8231            }
8232            Err(error) => {
8233                let fallback = if error.fallback_eligible {
8234                    format!(
8235                        "; only a run given no cgroups on purpose may set {ALLOW_PROCESS_GROUP_CPU_SCAN_ENV}=1 to measure with the process-group scan instead"
8236                    )
8237                } else {
8238                    String::new()
8239                };
8240                Err(MeterRefusal {
8241                    stage: SpawnStage::LiveCpuMeter,
8242                    reason: format!(
8243                        "cannot measure live CPU: {}{fallback}; the budgeted command was refused before launch rather than run unmeasured",
8244                        error.message
8245                    ),
8246                })
8247            }
8248        }
8249    }
8250
8251    fn source(&self) -> Option<LiveCpuSource> {
8252        match self {
8253            Self::Disabled => None,
8254            Self::Cgroup(_) => Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
8255            Self::ProcessGroupScan => Some(LiveCpuSource::AgentUtilsPairedPidfdStatV1),
8256        }
8257    }
8258}
8259
8260/// The startup clone3 probe, before this run's first cgroup-carrying
8261/// start: one dedicated probe cgroup, created exactly as a real
8262/// invocation's is (the same parent choice), probed into, reaped and
8263/// removed. It runs once per process; later calls return at once.
8264/// A probe cgroup that cannot be created is no verdict: the real
8265/// invocation's own refusal paths decide, as before.
8266/// The order the first budgeted invocation takes: the startup
8267/// probe finishes (and drops its cgroup) before the first real
8268/// invocation cgroup is allocated, so the probe never competes
8269/// with a real cgroup for the parent's last slot.
8270fn probe_before_first_real_cgroup<T>(probe: impl FnOnce(), allocate_real: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T {
8271    probe();
8272    allocate_real()
8273}
8274
8275fn probe_clone3_for_the_run(plan: &LiveCpuPlan) {
8276    let parent = plan.cgroup_parent.clone();
8277    probe_clone3_for_the_run_with(plan, &crate::vfork_spawn::CLONE3, move || {
8278        let created = match &parent {
8279            Some(parent) => InvocationCgroup::create_in(parent),
8280            None => InvocationCgroup::create(),
8281        };
8282        created.ok().map(|cgroup| {
8283            (
8284                cgroup.directory_fd(),
8285                Box::new(cgroup) as Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>,
8286            )
8287        })
8288    });
8289}
8290
8291/// [`probe_clone3_for_the_run`] with the probe cgroup's creation
8292/// given: the probe cgroup is created (and dropped) inside the one
8293/// shared initialization, before any real invocation cgroup is
8294/// allocated.
8295fn probe_clone3_for_the_run_with(
8296    plan: &LiveCpuPlan,
8297    support: &std::sync::Arc<crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support>,
8298    create_probe_cgroup: impl FnOnce() -> Option<(RawFd, Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>)>
8299    + Send
8300    + 'static,
8301) {
8302    let _ = plan;
8303    support.probe_cgroup_clone_once(create_probe_cgroup);
8304}
8305
8306/// The probe record's own run-level output, written once per
8307/// process next to the run's other files
8308/// (`<result_root>/runs/<run_id>/clone3-probe.json`). A run whose
8309/// probe never ran writes nothing.
8310/// Publish the probe record for this run. The record is mandatory
8311/// structured output: a write failure fails the cell (through
8312/// `record_cell`'s failure path) rather than silently losing the
8313/// record, because a run that cannot publish its evidence cannot
8314/// be judged from it. Only a success consumes the once: a failed
8315/// attempt is retried by the next cell.
8316/// Publish `record` (the probe's, when it has run) for this run.
8317/// Publish the probe record with its once state given.
8318fn publish_probe_record_with(
8319    context: &RunContext,
8320    record: Option<crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord>,
8321    written: &std::sync::Mutex<bool>,
8322) -> Result<(), String> {
8323    let Some(record) = record else {
8324        return Ok(());
8325    };
8326    let dir = context.result_root.join("runs").join(&context.run_id);
8327    match write_probe_record_once(&dir, &record, written) {
8328        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
8329        Err(reason) => {
8330            eprintln!("manifest-plan: {reason}");
8331            Err(reason)
8332        }
8333    }
8334}
8335
8336/// Write `record` as `clone3-probe.json` in `dir`, at most once per
8337/// successful write per `written`: `Ok(true)` only for the caller
8338/// that wrote it, and a named error the caller must not drop.
8339fn write_probe_record_once(
8340    dir: &std::path::Path,
8341    record: &crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord,
8342    written: &std::sync::Mutex<bool>,
8343) -> Result<bool, String> {
8344    let mut written = written
8345        .lock()
8346        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
8347    if *written {
8348        return Ok(false);
8349    }
8350    let path = dir.join("clone3-probe.json");
8351    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|error| {
8352        format!(
8353            "cannot create {} for the clone3 probe record: {error}",
8354            dir.display()
8355        )
8356    })?;
8357    let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(record)
8358        .map_err(|error| format!("cannot encode the clone3 probe record: {error}"))?;
8359    std::fs::write(&path, text).map_err(|error| {
8360        format!(
8361            "cannot write clone3 probe record {}: {error}",
8362            path.display()
8363        )
8364    })?;
8365    *written = true;
8366    Ok(true)
8367}
8368
8369fn execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
8370    request: ProcessRequest,
8371    limits: ProcessLimits,
8372    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
8373) -> Result<ProcessOutput, String> {
8374    let started = Instant::now();
8375    let ordinal = observations.len() as u64 + 1;
8376    let plan = LiveCpuPlan::current();
8377    let meter = if limits.cpu_budget_usec.is_some() {
8378        probe_before_first_real_cgroup(
8379            || probe_clone3_for_the_run(&plan),
8380            || LiveCpuMeter::choose(&plan),
8381        )
8382    } else {
8383        Ok(LiveCpuMeter::Disabled)
8384    };
8385    let mut meter = match meter {
8386        Ok(meter) => meter,
8387        Err(MeterRefusal { stage, reason }) => {
8388            // A malformed fallback marker, or a budgeted command no source can
8389            // measure, is refused before anything starts. The observation
8390            // names the cgroup source the boxed run required.
8391            let mut observation = InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
8392                ordinal,
8393                request.role,
8394                request.command,
8395                Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
8396            );
8397            observation.launch = LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
8398                stage,
8399                reason: reason.clone(),
8400            };
8401            observation.termination = TerminationPath::SpawnFailed;
8402            observations.push(observation);
8403            return Err(reason);
8404        }
8405    };
8406    let mut observation =
8407        InvocationCpuObservation::pending(ordinal, request.role, request.command, meter.source());
8408    let enrollment = match &meter {
8409        LiveCpuMeter::Cgroup(cgroup) => Some(Enrollment {
8410            directory: cgroup.directory_fd(),
8411            procs: cgroup.enrollment_fd(),
8412            path: cgroup.path(),
8413        }),
8414        _ => None,
8415    };
8416    let result = spawn_process(
8417        &request.cwd,
8418        &request.stdout,
8419        &request.stderr,
8420        enrollment,
8421        &mut observation,
8422    )
8423    .and_then(|child| match &meter {
8424        LiveCpuMeter::Cgroup(cgroup) => monitor_live_cpu_in(
8425            child,
8426            limits,
8427            started,
8428            &mut observation,
8429            Some(cgroup),
8430            |pid, leader_unreaped| match cgroup.kernel_path() {
8431                Some(invocation) => check_cgroup_membership(
8432                    pid,
8433                    leader_unreaped,
8434                    &invocation,
8435                    process_group_members,
8436                    process_cgroup,
8437                ),
8438                None => Err(format!(
8439                    "invocation cgroup {} is not under /sys/fs/cgroup, so its members cannot be checked",
8440                    cgroup.path().display()
8441                )),
8442            },
8443            |_| Ok(()),
8444            monotonic_cpu_sampler(|| cgroup.cpu_usage_usec()),
8445        ),
8446        LiveCpuMeter::Disabled | LiveCpuMeter::ProcessGroupScan => monitor_process(
8447            child,
8448            limits,
8449            started,
8450            &mut observation,
8451            |pid| dagrun::proccpu::ProcessGroupCpu::new(pid).map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
8452            |reader| reader.seconds().map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
8453        ),
8454    });
8455    // The leader has been reaped (or could not be). Whatever it left in its
8456    // cgroup is killed there, and the cgroup is removed; a failure to do so
8457    // fails the invocation rather than leaving processes behind unnoticed.
8458    let result = match &mut meter {
8459        LiveCpuMeter::Cgroup(cgroup) => match (result, cgroup.finish()) {
8460            (result, Ok(())) => result,
8461            (Ok(_), Err(cleanup)) => Err(cleanup),
8462            (Err(error), Err(cleanup)) => Err(format!("{error}; {cleanup}")),
8463        },
8464        _ => result,
8465    };
8466    // Retain the same observation on every error path, including successful
8467    // reap after accounting became unavailable. An error never fabricates zero.
8468    observations.push(observation);
8469    result
8470}
8471
8472/// Wrap a cgroup counter read so that a value below the highest one already
8473/// returned is a failed sample. The kernel never lowers `usage_usec`, so a
8474/// decrease means the read is not of this invocation's counter; the monitor
8475/// then treats it like any other failed sample, timed from when it returned.
8476fn monotonic_cpu_sampler(
8477    mut read: impl FnMut() -> Result<u64, String>,
8478) -> impl FnMut(u32, &()) -> Result<u64, CpuError> {
8479    let mut highest: Option<u64> = None;
8480    move |_, _| {
8481        let usage = read().map_err(|error| CpuError {
8482            stage: CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
8483            reason: format!("sampling: {error}"),
8484        })?;
8485        if let Some(highest) = highest.filter(|highest| usage < *highest) {
8486            return Err(CpuError {
8487                stage: CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
8488                reason: format!(
8489                    "sampling: cgroup CPU counter decreased from {highest} to {usage} usec"
8490                ),
8491            });
8492        }
8493        highest = Some(usage);
8494        Ok(usage)
8495    }
8496}
8497
8498/// Whether `path`, a cgroup path as the `0::` line of `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`
8499/// gives it, is `invocation` or a cgroup below it.
8500fn within_cgroup(path: &str, invocation: &str) -> bool {
8501    path == invocation
8502        || path
8503            .strip_prefix(invocation)
8504            .is_some_and(|below| below.starts_with('/'))
8505}
8506
8507/// The cgroup v2 path of `pid` from the `0::` line of `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`,
8508/// or `None` when the process no longer exists.
8509fn process_cgroup(pid: u32) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
8510    let text = match fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/cgroup")) {
8511        Ok(text) => text,
8512        Err(error) if matches!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::ENOENT | libc::ESRCH)) => {
8513            return Ok(None);
8514        }
8515        Err(error) => return Err(format!("/proc/{pid}/cgroup: {error}")),
8516    };
8517    let path = text
8518        .lines()
8519        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("0::"))
8520        .ok_or_else(|| format!("/proc/{pid}/cgroup has no cgroup v2 line"))?;
8521    // An exited process in a removed cgroup still names it, so marked.
8522    Ok(Some(
8523        path.strip_suffix(" (deleted)").unwrap_or(path).to_owned(),
8524    ))
8525}
8526
8527/// The live members of process group `pgid`, found as the agent-utils
8528/// process-group scan finds them: every numeric `/proc` entry whose `stat`
8529/// names `pgid` as its process group. A process that exits during the scan
8530/// is skipped.
8531///
8532/// Linux cannot list a process group's members, so every scan walks every
8533/// PID on the host; reading every PID's `stat` each time made one scan cost
8534/// as much as the host has processes, and an invocation is checked at every
8535/// CPU poll and at its exit ([`check_cgroup_membership`]). Under a loaded host
8536/// that turned a 15 s test into a 57 s timeout. So, as `dagrun::proccpu`
8537/// does, the scan remembers each PID's session ([`SESSION_CENSUS`]) and skips
8538/// a PID that cannot be a member: a process joins a group only within its own
8539/// session, and changes session only through `setsid`, which makes its session
8540/// its own PID. A PID is read when its cached session or the PID itself is the
8541/// group's session, when its session is unknown, or when the kernel may have
8542/// handed its number to a new task since it was cached. The group's session
8543/// comes from its leader's `stat`, or, once the leader is gone, from an earlier
8544/// scan or from [`spawn_process`], which records each group it creates; without
8545/// it every PID is read.
8546///
8547/// A Buck validation runs each e2e cell as a harness process of its own, so the
8548/// first scan of every cell read every PID on the host (about 5,300 `stat`
8549/// files, 0.12 CPU-s). With [`SESSION_CENSUS_ENV`] naming a file, the census
8550/// starts from the one the last cell on this host left there and is written
8551/// back after this process's first scan ([`SessionCensus::load`]), under the
8552/// same reuse rule: an entry is kept only while the allocator cannot have
8553/// handed its PID out again since the writer's scan began.
8554fn process_group_members(pgid: u32) -> Result<Vec<u32>, String> {
8555    let mut census = SESSION_CENSUS
8556        .get_or_init(session_census_from_env)
8557        .lock()
8558        .map_err(|_| "session census lock poisoned".to_string())?;
8559    let scan = scan_process_group(&mut census, pgid)?;
8560    if !census.saved || scan.read >= SESSION_CENSUS_SAVE_READS {
8561        if let Some(path) = std::env::var_os(SESSION_CENSUS_ENV).filter(|v| !v.is_empty()) {
8562            census.save(Path::new(&path));
8563        }
8564        census.saved = true;
8565    }
8566    Ok(scan.members)
8567}
8568
8569/// What one [`scan_process_group`] found and did.
8570struct GroupScan {
8571    members: Vec<u32>,
8572    /// How many PIDs' `stat` it read.
8573    read: usize,
8574    /// The PIDs it saw in /proc and did not read, because the census placed
8575    /// them in another session. Kept for the tests, which assert on the set.
8576    #[cfg(test)]
8577    skipped: Vec<u32>,
8578}
8579
8580/// [`process_group_members`] with `census`.
8581fn scan_process_group(census: &mut SessionCensus, pgid: u32) -> Result<GroupScan, String> {
8582    let now = PidAllocator::read();
8583    census.begin(now, read_pid_max());
8584    let group_session = match read_process_stat(pgid)? {
8585        StatRead::Bytes(stat) if stat_process_group(&stat) == Some(pgid) => {
8586            let session = stat_session(&stat);
8587            census.remember_group(pgid, session, now);
8588            session
8589        }
8590        _ => census
8591            .group_sessions
8592            .get(&pgid)
8593            .map(|(session, _)| *session),
8594    };
8595    let mut members = Vec::new();
8596    let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
8597    let mut read = 0;
8598    #[cfg(test)]
8599    let mut skipped = Vec::new();
8600    for entry in fs::read_dir("/proc").map_err(|error| format!("/proc: {error}"))? {
8601        let entry = entry.map_err(|error| format!("/proc: {error}"))?;
8602        let Some(pid) = entry
8603            .file_name()
8604            .to_str()
8605            .filter(|name| !name.is_empty() && name.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()))
8606            .and_then(|name| name.parse::<u32>().ok())
8607        else {
8608            continue;
8609        };
8610        seen.insert(pid);
8611        if group_session.is_some_and(|session| census.skip(pid, session)) {
8612            #[cfg(test)]
8613            skipped.push(pid);
8614            continue;
8615        }
8616        read += 1;
8617        let mut session = None;
8618        let group = member_process_group(
8619            pid,
8620            |pid| {
8621                let read = read_process_stat(pid)?;
8622                if let StatRead::Bytes(stat) = &read {
8623                    session = stat_session(stat);
8624                }
8625                Ok(read)
8626            },
8627            process_exists,
8628        )?;
8629        if let Some(session) = session {
8630            census.sessions.insert(pid, session);
8631        }
8632        if group == Some(pgid) {
8633            members.push(pid);
8634        }
8635    }
8636    census.sessions.retain(|pid, _| seen.contains(pid));
8637    Ok(GroupScan {
8638        members,
8639        read,
8640        #[cfg(test)]
8641        skipped,
8642    })
8643}
8644
8645/// Records the session of the process group a child of this process created
8646/// with `setpgid(0, 0)` ([`spawn_process`]), so a scan made after the leader
8647/// exited, when its `stat` is gone, can still skip by session. The group was
8648/// created in this process's session, which the child inherited, and it never
8649/// changes: a group's leader cannot call `setsid`, and a member that does
8650/// leaves the group.
8651fn remember_spawned_group(pgid: u32) {
8652    let session = u32::try_from(unsafe { libc::getsid(0) }).ok();
8653    if let Ok(mut census) = SESSION_CENSUS.get_or_init(session_census_from_env).lock() {
8654        census.remember_group(pgid, session, PidAllocator::read());
8655    }
8656}
8657
8658/// The session of each host PID an earlier [`process_group_members`] scan
8659/// read, and the session of each process group it scanned for or this
8660/// process created, valid while the kernel cannot have reused those PIDs
8661/// (judged by [`PidAllocator`]).
8662static SESSION_CENSUS: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::Mutex<SessionCensus>> =
8663    std::sync::OnceLock::new();
8664
8665/// A file the session census starts from and is written back to, shared by
8666/// the harness processes on one host (set by ci/buck-e2e/cell.sh).
8667pub const SESSION_CENSUS_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_E2E_SESSION_CENSUS";
8668const SESSION_CENSUS_SCHEMA: &str = "hermit-session-census/v1";
8669/// After its first scan, a process writes the census back only after a scan
8670/// that read at least this many `stat` files: later scans read little, and
8671/// writing after every CPU poll would cost more than it saves.
8672const SESSION_CENSUS_SAVE_READS: usize = 1024;
8673
8674fn session_census_from_env() -> std::sync::Mutex<SessionCensus> {
8675    let census = std::env::var_os(SESSION_CENSUS_ENV)
8676        .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
8677        .and_then(|path| SessionCensus::load(Path::new(&path)))
8678        .unwrap_or_default();
8679    std::sync::Mutex::new(census)
8680}
8681
8682/// The kernel instance and PID namespace a census describes: PIDs and
8683/// allocator positions mean nothing outside them.
8684fn census_scope() -> Option<String> {
8685    let boot = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id").ok()?;
8686    let pidns = fs::read_link("/proc/self/ns/pid").ok()?;
8687    Some(format!("{} {}", boot.trim(), pidns.to_str()?))
8688}
8689
8690#[derive(Default)]
8691struct SessionCensus {
8692    sessions: std::collections::HashMap<u32, u32>,
8693    /// Each group's session, with where the allocator stood when the group
8694    /// was known to exist with that session.
8695    group_sessions: std::collections::HashMap<u32, (u32, PidAllocator)>,
8696    at: Option<PidAllocator>,
8697    /// Whether this process has written the census back since it started.
8698    saved: bool,
8699}
8700
8701impl SessionCensus {
8702    /// The census a previous process saved at `path`, or `None` when there is
8703    /// none, it is unreadable, or it describes another boot or PID namespace;
8704    /// every PID is then read, as without a file. Only the PID sessions and the
8705    /// allocator position come across: [`Self::begin`] then drops each PID the
8706    /// allocator may have handed out since the writer's scan began, exactly as
8707    /// for this process's own previous scan. Group sessions stay per process.
8708    fn load(path: &Path) -> Option<Self> {
8709        Self::parse(&fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?, &census_scope()?)
8710    }
8711
8712    fn parse(text: &str, scope: &str) -> Option<Self> {
8713        let mut lines = text.lines();
8714        if lines.next()? != SESSION_CENSUS_SCHEMA || lines.next()?.strip_prefix("scope ")? != scope
8715        {
8716            return None;
8717        }
8718        let at: Vec<_> = lines.next()?.strip_prefix("at ")?.split(' ').collect();
8719        let [last_pid, tasks, forks] = at.as_slice() else {
8720            return None;
8721        };
8722        let at = PidAllocator {
8723            last_pid: last_pid.parse().ok()?,
8724            tasks: tasks.parse().ok()?,
8725            forks: forks.parse().ok()?,
8726        };
8727        let mut sessions = std::collections::HashMap::new();
8728        for line in lines {
8729            let (pid, session) = line.split_once(' ')?;
8730            sessions.insert(pid.parse().ok()?, session.parse().ok()?);
8731        }
8732        Some(Self {
8733            sessions,
8734            at: Some(at),
8735            ..Self::default()
8736        })
8737    }
8738
8739    fn render(&self, scope: &str) -> Option<String> {
8740        let at = self.at?;
8741        let mut text = format!(
8742            "{SESSION_CENSUS_SCHEMA}\nscope {scope}\nat {} {} {}\n",
8743            at.last_pid, at.tasks, at.forks
8744        );
8745        for (pid, session) in &self.sessions {
8746            text.push_str(&format!("{pid} {session}\n"));
8747        }
