8748        Some(text)
8749    }
8750
8751    /// Best effort, replacing the file whole: a process that cannot write it
8752    /// leaves the next one to read every PID, as without a file.
8753    fn save(&self, path: &Path) {
8754        let Some(text) = census_scope().and_then(|scope| self.render(&scope)) else {
8755            return;
8756        };
8757        let partial = path.with_extension(format!("{}.partial", std::process::id()));
8758        if fs::write(&partial, text).is_err() || fs::rename(&partial, path).is_err() {
8759            let _ = fs::remove_file(&partial);
8760        }
8761    }
8762
8763    /// Starts a scan at allocator position `now`, dropping each entry whose
8764    /// PID the allocator may have handed out since the previous scan began.
8765    fn begin(&mut self, now: Option<PidAllocator>, pid_max: Option<u32>) {
8766        match (self.at, now, pid_max) {
8767            (Some(previous), Some(now), Some(pid_max)) => {
8768                self.sessions
8769                    .retain(|pid, _| !previous.may_have_reused(now, pid_max, *pid));
8770            }
8771            _ => self.sessions.clear(),
8772        }
8773        match (now, pid_max) {
8774            (Some(now), Some(pid_max)) => self
8775                .group_sessions
8776                .retain(|pgid, (_, since)| !since.may_have_reused(now, pid_max, *pgid)),
8777            _ => self.group_sessions.clear(),
8778        }
8779        self.at = now;
8780    }
8781
8782    /// Records that group `pgid` existed in `session` when the allocator
8783    /// stood at `since`.
8784    fn remember_group(&mut self, pgid: u32, session: Option<u32>, since: Option<PidAllocator>) {
8785        if let (Some(session), Some(since)) = (session, since) {
8786            self.group_sessions.insert(pgid, (session, since));
8787        }
8788    }
8789
8790    /// Whether `pid` cannot be in a process group of session `session`.
8791    fn skip(&self, pid: u32, session: u32) -> bool {
8792        pid != session
8793            && self
8794                .sessions
8795                .get(&pid)
8796                .is_some_and(|cached| *cached != session)
8797    }
8798}
8799
8800/// Where the kernel's PID allocator stands: the last PID it handed out and the
8801/// number of live tasks (`/proc/loadavg`), and the tasks created since boot
8802/// (`processes` in `/proc/stat`). Threads take their IDs from the same space.
8803#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
8804struct PidAllocator {
8805    last_pid: u32,
8806    tasks: u64,
8807    forks: u64,
8808}
8809
8810/// PIDs below this are never handed out again after the allocator wraps
8811/// (Linux `RESERVED_PIDS`).
8812const RESERVED_PIDS: u64 = 300;
8813
8814impl PidAllocator {
8815    fn read() -> Option<Self> {
8816        let loadavg = fs::read_to_string("/proc/loadavg").ok()?;
8817        let fields: Vec<_> = loadavg.split_whitespace().collect();
8818        let (_, tasks) = fields.get(3)?.split_once('/')?;
8819        let stat = fs::read_to_string("/proc/stat").ok()?;
8820        let forks = stat
8821            .lines()
8822            .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("processes "))?
8823            .trim()
8824            .parse()
8825            .ok()?;
8826        Some(Self {
8827            last_pid: fields.get(4)?.parse().ok()?,
8828            tasks: tasks.parse().ok()?,
8829            forks,
8830        })
8831    }
8832
8833    /// Whether the allocator may have handed out `pid` again on its way from
8834    /// `self` to `to`. It walks the PID space in a circle, so every PID it
8835    /// handed out lies on the arc after `self.last_pid` up to `to.last_pid`,
8836    /// unless it may have gone the whole way round.
8837    fn may_have_reused(self, to: PidAllocator, pid_max: u32, pid: u32) -> bool {
8838        let Some(created) = to.forks.checked_sub(self.forks) else {
8839            return true;
8840        };
8841        let lap = u64::from(pid_max).saturating_sub(RESERVED_PIDS);
8842        if created.saturating_add(self.tasks.max(to.tasks)) >= lap {
8843            return true;
8844        }
8845        if created == 0 {
8846            return false;
8847        }
8848        // `created` counts tasks created on the whole host (/proc/stat), while
8849        // `last_pid` is this PID namespace's allocator (/proc/loadavg). In a
8850        // namespace other than the host's (the pinned root's), the host can
8851        // create tasks while this namespace creates none, so the cursor stays
8852        // put. With a full lap ruled out above, a cursor that did not move
8853        // handed out no PID.
8854        let (start, end) = (self.last_pid, to.last_pid);
8855        if start == end {
8856            return false;
8857        }
8858        if start < end {
8859            start < pid && pid <= end
8860        } else {
8861            pid > start || pid <= end
8862        }
8863    }
8864}
8865
8866fn read_pid_max() -> Option<u32> {
8867    fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max")
8868        .ok()?
8869        .trim()
8870        .parse()
8871        .ok()
8872}
8873
8874/// The session in the bytes of a `/proc/<pid>/stat` file: the field after the
8875/// process group (see [`stat_process_group`]).
8876fn stat_session(stat: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
8877    let close = stat.iter().rposition(|&byte| byte == b')')?;
8878    std::str::from_utf8(&stat[close + 1..])
8879        .ok()?
8880        .split_whitespace()
8881        .nth(3)?
8882        .parse()
8883        .ok()
8884}
8885
8886/// One read of a `/proc/<pid>/stat` file: its bytes, or that the process
8887/// no longer exists.
8888#[derive(Debug)]
8889enum StatRead {
8890    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
8891    Gone,
8892}
8893
8894/// Read `/proc/<pid>/stat` as bytes, not text: any process on the host may
8895/// name itself with bytes that are not UTF-8, and one such name must not fail
8896/// the scan.
8897fn read_process_stat(pid: u32) -> Result<StatRead, String> {
8898    match fs::read(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat")) {
8899        Ok(stat) => Ok(StatRead::Bytes(stat)),
8900        Err(error) if matches!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::ENOENT | libc::ESRCH)) => {
8901            Ok(StatRead::Gone)
8902        }
8903        Err(error) => Err(format!("/proc/{pid}/stat: {error}")),
8904    }
8905}
8906
8907/// Whether `/proc/<pid>` still exists.
8908fn process_exists(pid: u32) -> Result<bool, String> {
8909    match fs::symlink_metadata(format!("/proc/{pid}")) {
8910        Ok(_) => Ok(true),
8911        Err(error) if matches!(error.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::ENOENT | libc::ESRCH)) => Ok(false),
8912        Err(error) => Err(format!("/proc/{pid}: {error}")),
8913    }
8914}
8915
8916/// The process group of `pid` from its `stat`, or `None` when the process no
8917/// longer exists. A read whose bytes do not parse is not trusted at once: in
8918/// the validation of hermit 9e698b862c8e, two such reads refused liteinst
8919/// cells. If `/proc/<pid>` is gone the
8920/// process has exited and is skipped, as an exited process cannot be outside
8921/// the cgroup; otherwise the file is read once more. A live process whose
8922/// stat still does not parse fails the check, with both reads' lengths and
8923/// leading bytes in the error so the next occurrence shows what it read.
8924fn member_process_group(
8925    pid: u32,
8926    mut read: impl FnMut(u32) -> Result<StatRead, String>,
8927    exists: impl FnOnce(u32) -> Result<bool, String>,
8928) -> Result<Option<u32>, String> {
8929    let first = match read(pid)? {
8930        StatRead::Gone => return Ok(None),
8931        StatRead::Bytes(stat) => stat,
8932    };
8933    if let Some(group) = stat_process_group(&first) {
8934        return Ok(Some(group));
8935    }
8936    if !exists(pid)? {
8937        return Ok(None);
8938    }
8939    let reread = match read(pid)? {
8940        StatRead::Gone => return Ok(None),
8941        StatRead::Bytes(stat) => stat,
8942    };
8943    match stat_process_group(&reread) {
8944        Some(group) => Ok(Some(group)),
8945        None => Err(format!(
8946            "/proc/{pid}/stat is malformed in two reads of a live process: first {}; re-read {}",
8947            describe_stat_bytes(&first),
8948            describe_stat_bytes(&reread)
8949        )),
8950    }
8951}
8952
8953/// The length of `stat` and its first 64 bytes, escaped, for an error.
8954fn describe_stat_bytes(stat: &[u8]) -> String {
8955    let shown: String = stat
8956        .iter()
8957        .take(64)
8958        .flat_map(|&byte| std::ascii::escape_default(byte))
8959        .map(char::from)
8960        .collect();
8961    format!("{} bytes \"{shown}\"", stat.len())
8962}
8963
8964/// The process group in the bytes of a `/proc/<pid>/stat` file, or `None`
8965/// when they are malformed. The command name may hold any bytes, including
8966/// spaces, parentheses and bytes that are not UTF-8; after its last ')' come
8967/// the state, the parent PID and the process group, all ASCII.
8968fn stat_process_group(stat: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
8969    let close = stat.iter().rposition(|&byte| byte == b')')?;
8970    std::str::from_utf8(&stat[close + 1..])
8971        .ok()?
8972        .split_whitespace()
8973        .nth(2)?
8974        .parse()
8975        .ok()
8976}
8977
8978/// How many times [`check_cgroup_membership`] reads again, [`FORK_WINDOW_PAUSE`]
8979/// apart, a process whose cgroup reads as the root cgroup `/`, or as an
8980/// ancestor-only path through a nested cgroup namespace.
8981///
8982/// A child that `fork` is still creating is in the root cgroup for a moment:
8983/// `cgroup_fork` points it at `init_css_set`, `copy_process` makes it visible
8984/// in `/proc` and in its parent's process group, and only then does
8985/// `cgroup_post_fork` move it into its parent's cgroup (Linux v6.19
8986/// kernel/fork.c and kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c). A forking guest's child read
8987/// in that window is not outside: c-programs/wait-on-child (verify/sabre) was
8988/// refused that way in a box validation of hermit 6b31e9ae, and a probe that
8989/// reads each child of a forking loop as soon as it appears saw 2 of 108171
8990/// children in `/`. A reader in a nested cgroup namespace can see the same
8991/// host root as `/../../..` instead. An ancestor-only spelling does not prove
8992/// membership or even that this is the fork window: it gets the same bounded
8993/// recheck, and a process that stays outside is still refused.
8994const FORK_WINDOW_REREADS: u32 = 50;
8995const FORK_WINDOW_PAUSE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(2);
8996
8997fn possible_fork_root_cgroup(path: &str) -> bool {
8998    path == "/"
8999        || path
9000            .strip_prefix('/')
9001            .is_some_and(|relative| relative.split('/').all(|part| part == ".."))
9002}
9003
9004/// Check that every process the process-group scan could see for this
9005/// invocation is in its cgroup `invocation` or a cgroup below it: the leader
9006/// `pid` while it is unreaped (`leader_unreaped`), wherever its process group
9007/// went, and the live members of its process group `pid`. Returns why the
9008/// invocation must be refused: a process outside, or a failed check.
9009///
9010/// What this cannot see: a process other than the leader that leaves both
9011/// the process group and the invocation cgroup, and one that leaves the
9012/// cgroup and exits between two checks. The process-group scan this cgroup
9013/// replaced could not charge either of them. One evasion is weaker than that
9014/// scan and is not refused here: a command that empties its invocation
9015/// cgroup, makes it threaded through `cgroup.type` and moves back only its
9016/// thread-group leader through `cgroup.threads` passes this check while its
9017/// other threads are charged to the parent cgroup. The scan read the whole
9018/// thread group's CPU from `/proc/<pid>/stat`.
9019fn check_cgroup_membership(
9020    pid: u32,
9021    leader_unreaped: bool,
9022    invocation: &str,
9023    group_members: impl FnOnce(u32) -> Result<Vec<u32>, String>,
9024    mut cgroup_of: impl FnMut(u32) -> Result<Option<String>, String>,
9025) -> Result<(), String> {
9026    let unchecked = |error: String| {
9027        format!(
9028            "cannot check that process group {pid} stays inside its invocation cgroup {invocation}: {error}"
9029        )
9030    };
9031    let members = group_members(pid).map_err(unchecked)?;
9032    let leader = leader_unreaped.then_some(pid);
9033    for member in leader
9034        .into_iter()
9035        .chain(members.into_iter().filter(|member| Some(*member) != leader))
9036    {
9037        let mut cgroup = cgroup_of(member).map_err(unchecked)?;
9038        let mut rereads = 0;
9039        while cgroup
9040            .as_deref()
9041            .is_some_and(|path| possible_fork_root_cgroup(path) && !within_cgroup(path, invocation))
9042            && rereads < FORK_WINDOW_REREADS
9043        {
9044            std::thread::sleep(FORK_WINDOW_PAUSE);
9045            cgroup = cgroup_of(member).map_err(unchecked)?;
9046            rereads += 1;
9047        }
9048        match cgroup {
9049            Some(cgroup) if !within_cgroup(&cgroup, invocation) => {
9050                let role = if Some(member) == leader {
9051                    "the leader"
9052                } else {
9053                    "a member of the leader's process group"
9054                };
9055                return Err(format!(
9056                    "process {member} ({role}) is in cgroup {cgroup}, outside its invocation cgroup {invocation}, so that cgroup's CPU counter does not hold its CPU"
9057                ));
9058            }
9059            _ => {}
9060        }
9061    }
9062    Ok(())
9063}
9064
9065/// The invocation cgroup a child starts in: its directory, which clone3's
9066/// CLONE_INTO_CGROUP takes; its `cgroup.procs`, which the pre_exec join
9067/// writes when clone3 is refused; and its path, for messages.
9068#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
9069struct Enrollment<'a> {
9070    directory: RawFd,
9071    procs: RawFd,
9072    path: &'a Path,
9073}
9074
9075/// The leader of an invocation, which the monitor waits for by PID (wait4).
9076#[derive(Debug)]
9077struct SpawnedLeader {
9078    pid: u32,
9079}
9080
9081impl SpawnedLeader {
9082    fn id(&self) -> u32 {
9083        self.pid
9084    }
9085}
9086
9087impl From<Child> for SpawnedLeader {
9088    /// A child `Command` started. Dropping the `Child` neither waits for nor
9089    /// signals the process; the monitor reaps it with wait4.
9090    fn from(child: Child) -> Self {
9091        Self { pid: child.id() }
9092    }
9093}
9094
9095fn spawn_process(
9096    cwd: &Path,
9097    stdout: &Path,
9098    stderr: &Path,
9099    enrollment: Option<Enrollment<'_>>,
9100    observation: &mut InvocationCpuObservation,
9101) -> Result<SpawnedLeader, String> {
9102    spawn_process_with(
9103        &crate::vfork_spawn::CLONE3,
9104        cwd,
9105        stdout,
9106        stderr,
9107        enrollment,
9108        observation,
9109    )
9110}
9111
9112/// [`spawn_process`], with clone3 as `clone3` finds it.
9113fn spawn_process_with(
9114    clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support,
9115    cwd: &Path,
9116    stdout: &Path,
9117    stderr: &Path,
9118    enrollment: Option<Enrollment<'_>>,
9119    observation: &mut InvocationCpuObservation,
9120) -> Result<SpawnedLeader, String> {
9121    let mut open_capture = |path: &Path, stage| {
9122        File::create(path).map_err(|error| {
9123            let reason = format!("{}: {error}", path.display());
9124            observation.launch = LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
9125                stage,
9126                reason: reason.clone(),
9127            };
9128            observation.termination = TerminationPath::SpawnFailed;
9129            reason
9130        })
9131    };
9132    let stdout_file = open_capture(stdout, SpawnStage::StdoutCapture)?;
9133    let stderr_file = open_capture(stderr, SpawnStage::StderrCapture)?;
9134    // A child that joins a cgroup is created in it by clone3, without a copy
9135    // of this process (dh-7n47nt); only where clone3 is refused does it take
9136    // the pre_exec join below, which forks.
9137    let mut method = SpawnMethod::Command;
9138    if let Some(enrollment) = enrollment {
9139        let program = &observation.command.argv[0];
9140        let started = start_in_cgroup(
9141            clone3,
9142            &observation.command,
9143            cwd,
9144            [&stdout_file, &stderr_file],
9145            enrollment,
9146        );
9147        let failure = match started {
9148            Ok(crate::vfork_spawn::Started::Running { pid }) => {
9149                observation.launch = LaunchObservation::Spawned {
9150                    pid,
9151                    method: SpawnMethod::Clone3IntoCgroup,
9152                };
9153                remember_spawned_group(pid);
9154                return Ok(SpawnedLeader { pid });
9155            }
9156            Ok(crate::vfork_spawn::Started::Unusable { reason }) => {
9157                method = SpawnMethod::CommandAfterClone3Refused { reason };
9158                None
9159            }
9160            Ok(crate::vfork_spawn::Started::JoinFailed(error)) => Some(format!(
9161                "cannot join invocation cgroup {} before exec, so {program} was not started: {error}",
9162                enrollment.path.display()
9163            )),
9164            Ok(crate::vfork_spawn::Started::Failed(error)) | Err(error) => {
9165                Some(format!("cannot execute {program}: {error}"))
9166            }
9167        };
9168        if let Some(reason) = failure {
9169            observation.launch = LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
9170                stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
9171                reason: reason.clone(),
9172            };
9173            observation.termination = TerminationPath::SpawnFailed;
9174            return Err(reason);
9175        }
9176    }
9177    // A failed cgroup join and a failed exec reach this process as the same
9178    // bare error code, so the child writes one byte to this pipe when the join
9179    // is what failed.
9180    let join_report = match enrollment {
9181        Some(_) => match join_failure_pipe() {
9182            Ok(pipe) => Some(pipe),
9183            Err(error) => {
9184                let reason =
9185                    format!("cannot open the pipe that reports a failed cgroup join: {error}");
9186                observation.launch = LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
9187                    stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
9188                    reason: reason.clone(),
9189                };
9190                observation.termination = TerminationPath::SpawnFailed;
9191                return Err(reason);
9192            }
9193        },
9194        None => None,
9195    };
9196    let identity = &observation.command;
9197    let program = &identity.argv[0];
9198    let mut command = Command::new(program);
9199    command
9200        .args(&identity.argv[1..])
9201        .current_dir(cwd)
9202        .stdin(Stdio::null())
9203        .stdout(stdout_file)
9204        .stderr(stderr_file);
9205    command.envs(identity.env_overrides.iter());
9206    // The child leads a process group of its own. With no pre_exec closure,
9207    // std starts it with posix_spawn, which does not copy this process: a
9208    // fork() copies the address space under the memory-map lock, and every
9209    // other thread that page-faults waits for it (dh-7n47nt).
9210    command.process_group(0);
9211    let join_report_fd = join_report.as_ref().map(|(_, write)| write.as_raw_fd());
9212    if let Some(Enrollment { procs: fd, .. }) = enrollment {
9213        // Join the invocation cgroup before exec, so every CPU cycle of the
9214        // program and of anything it starts is charged to that cgroup. The
9215        // descriptor is close-on-exec, so the program never sees it. std sets
9216        // the process group before it runs this closure.
9217        unsafe {
9218            command.pre_exec(move || {
9219                let joined = loop {
9220                    let written = libc::write(fd, b"0\n".as_ptr().cast(), 2);
9221                    if written == 2 {
9222                        break Ok(());
9223                    }
9224                    if written < 0 {
9225                        let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
9226                        if error.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::EINTR) {
9227                            continue;
9228                        }
9229                        break Err(error);
9230                    }
9231                    break Err(std::io::Error::from_raw_os_error(libc::EIO));
9232                };
9233                if let Err(error) = joined {
9234                    if let Some(report) = join_report_fd {
9235                        libc::write(report, b"j".as_ptr().cast(), 1);
9236                    }
9237                    return Err(error);
9238                }
9239                Ok(())
9240            });
9241        }
9242    }
9243    let spawned = command.spawn();
9244    // The child wrote its report, if any, before it sent the error that ends
9245    // the spawn, so a failed spawn finds the byte already in the pipe.
9246    let join_failed = match (&spawned, join_report) {
9247        (Err(_), Some((read, _write))) => {
9248            let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
9249            let read = unsafe { libc::read(read.as_raw_fd(), byte.as_mut_ptr().cast(), 1) };
9250            read == 1
9251        }
9252        _ => false,
9253    };
9254    match spawned {
9255        Ok(child) => {
9256            observation.launch = LaunchObservation::Spawned {
9257                pid: child.id(),
9258                method,
9259            };
9260            remember_spawned_group(child.id());
9261            Ok(SpawnedLeader::from(child))
9262        }
9263        Err(error) => {
9264            let reason = match enrollment {
9265                Some(Enrollment { path: cgroup, .. }) if join_failed => format!(
9266                    "cannot join invocation cgroup {} before exec, so {program} was not started: {error}",
9267                    cgroup.display()
9268                ),
9269                _ => format!("cannot execute {program}: {error}"),
9270            };
9271            observation.launch = LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
9272                stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
9273                reason: reason.clone(),
9274            };
9275            observation.termination = TerminationPath::SpawnFailed;
9276            Err(reason)
9277        }
9278    }
9279}
9280
9281/// Starts `command` in `enrollment`'s cgroup with clone3, with stdin on
9282/// /dev/null and stdout and stderr on `captures`. `Err` when those
9283/// descriptors cannot be prepared.
9284fn start_in_cgroup(
9285    clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support,
9286    command: &CommandIdentity,
9287    cwd: &Path,
9288    captures: [&File; 2],
9289    enrollment: Enrollment<'_>,
9290) -> std::io::Result<crate::vfork_spawn::Started> {
9291    // Close-on-exec copies above 2, so that the child's dup3 onto 0, 1 and 2
9292    // never overwrites a source it has yet to copy.
9293    let above_stdio = |fd: RawFd| -> std::io::Result<OwnedFd> {
9294        let copy = unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 3) };
9295        if copy < 0 {
9296            return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
9297        }
9298        // SAFETY: fcntl returned a new descriptor that nothing else owns.
9299        Ok(unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(copy) })
9300    };
9301    let null = File::open("/dev/null")?;
9302    let stdin = above_stdio(null.as_raw_fd())?;
9303    let stdout = above_stdio(captures[0].as_raw_fd())?;
9304    let stderr = above_stdio(captures[1].as_raw_fd())?;
9305    Ok(crate::vfork_spawn::start(
9306        clone3,
9307        &crate::vfork_spawn::Program {
9308            argv: &command.argv,
9309            env_overrides: &command.env_overrides,
9310            cwd,
9311            stdio: [stdin.as_raw_fd(), stdout.as_raw_fd(), stderr.as_raw_fd()],
9312            cgroup: enrollment.directory,
9313        },
9314    ))
9315}
9316
9317/// A close-on-exec, nonblocking pipe, read end first, through which a child
9318/// reports that its cgroup join failed before exec.
9319fn join_failure_pipe() -> std::io::Result<(OwnedFd, OwnedFd)> {
9320    let mut fds = [0; 2];
9321    if unsafe { libc::pipe2(fds.as_mut_ptr(), libc::O_CLOEXEC | libc::O_NONBLOCK) } == -1 {
9322        return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
9323    }
9324    // SAFETY: pipe2 returned two new descriptors that nothing else owns.
9325    Ok(unsafe { (OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fds[0]), OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fds[1])) })
9326}
9327
9328/// Monitor with a reader that reports live CPU in seconds, as agent-utils
9329/// `proccpu` does. The seconds are converted to microseconds here, and a
9330/// conversion failure is a failed sample like any other.
9331fn monitor_process<R>(
9332    child: impl Into<SpawnedLeader>,
9333    limits: ProcessLimits,
9334    started: Instant,
9335    observation: &mut InvocationCpuObservation,
9336    register: impl FnOnce(u32) -> Result<R, String>,
9337    mut sample: impl FnMut(&R) -> Result<f64, String>,
9338) -> Result<ProcessOutput, String> {
9339    monitor_live_cpu(
9340        child,
9341        limits,
9342        started,
9343        observation,
9344        register,
9345        |pid, reader| {
9346            sample(reader)
9347                .map_err(|error| CpuError {
9348                    stage: CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
9349                    reason: format!("sampling: {error}"),
9350                })
9351                .and_then(|seconds| {
9352                    live_cpu_usage_usec(pid, seconds).map_err(|reason| CpuError {
9353                        stage: CpuErrorStage::Conversion,
9354                        reason,
9355                    })
9356                })
9357        },
9358    )
9359}
9360
9361/// Wait for the invocation's leader while polling its live CPU, and stop its
9362/// process group when a budget runs out or when its CPU cannot be measured for
9363/// `CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE`. `register` binds the reader once at spawn;
9364/// `sample` returns the invocation's CPU in microseconds.
9365fn monitor_live_cpu<R>(
9366    child: impl Into<SpawnedLeader>,
9367    limits: ProcessLimits,
9368    started: Instant,
9369    observation: &mut InvocationCpuObservation,
9370    register: impl FnOnce(u32) -> Result<R, String>,
9371    sample: impl FnMut(u32, &R) -> Result<u64, CpuError>,
9372) -> Result<ProcessOutput, String> {
9373    monitor_live_cpu_in(
9374        child,
9375        limits,
9376        started,
9377        observation,
9378        None,
9379        |_, _| Ok(()),
9380        register,
9381        sample,
9382    )
9383}
9384
9385/// `monitor_live_cpu` for an invocation that runs in `cgroup`, when it has one.
9386///
9387/// `membership(pid, leader_unreaped)` refuses the invocation when a process
9388/// that should be charged to the cgroup is outside it. It runs before every
9389/// live CPU sample, before a wall-clock stop, and once the leader has been
9390/// waited for. A CPU-budget stop is preceded by the check at its triggering
9391/// poll, which runs before that poll's sample so that a refusal never follows
9392/// a recorded trigger.
9393#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
9394fn monitor_live_cpu_in<R>(
9395    child: impl Into<SpawnedLeader>,
9396    limits: ProcessLimits,
9397    started: Instant,
9398    observation: &mut InvocationCpuObservation,
9399    cgroup: Option<&InvocationCgroup>,
9400    mut membership: impl FnMut(u32, bool) -> Result<(), String>,
9401    register: impl FnOnce(u32) -> Result<R, String>,
9402    mut sample: impl FnMut(u32, &R) -> Result<u64, CpuError>,
9403) -> Result<ProcessOutput, String> {
9404    let ProcessLimits {
9405        deadline,
9406        cpu_budget_usec,
9407        cpu_poll_interval,
9408    } = limits;
9409    let pid = child.into().id();
9410    let leader = LeaderPidFd::open(pid);
9411    // Authenticate once at spawn and retain this generation's owner through
9412    // final wait/stop. Disabled accounting never registers or samples a reader.
9413    let cpu_reader = cpu_budget_usec.map(|_| register(pid));
9414    if let LiveCpuObservation::Enabled(live) = &mut observation.live {
9415        live.registration = match &cpu_reader {
9416            Some(Ok(_)) => RegistrationObservation::BoundOnce,
9417            Some(Err(reason)) => RegistrationObservation::Unavailable {
9418                reason: reason.clone(),
9419            },
9420            None => unreachable!("enabled CPU observation requires the existing CPU budget"),
9421        };
9422    }
9423    let mut next_cpu_poll = Instant::now() + cpu_poll_interval;
9424    let mut cpu_accounting_missing_since = None;
9425    loop {
9426        observation.termination = TerminationPath::WaitError;
9427        if let Some((status, cpu_usage_usec)) = wait4_process(
9428            pid,
9429            libc::WNOHANG,
9430            WaitOperation::Poll,
9431            started,
9432            &mut observation.final_wait,
9433        )? {
9434            let leader_unreaped =
9435                !matches!(observation.final_wait, FinalWaitObservation::Reaped { .. });
9436            if let Err(reason) = membership(pid, leader_unreaped) {
9437                observation.termination = TerminationPath::CgroupMembershipStop;
9438                if leader_unreaped {
9439                    return match stop_process_group(
9440                        pid,
9441                        &leader,
9442                        cgroup,
9443                        started,
9444                        &mut observation.final_wait,
9445                    ) {
9446                        Ok(_) => Err(format!(
9447                            "{reason}; stopped and reaped its leader rather than charge an incomplete CPU measurement"
9448                        )),
9449                        Err(error) => Err(format!(
9450                            "{reason}; could not confirm leader stop/reap: {error}"
9451                        )),
9452                    };
9453                }
9454                // The leader is gone, so no grace can be waited out for it.
9455                // Its PID stays reserved while it names a live process group,
9456                // so this kill reaches only that group; what remains in the
9457                // invocation cgroup is killed when the cgroup is finished.
9458                unsafe {
9459                    libc::kill(-(pid as i32), libc::SIGKILL);
9460                }
9461                return Err(format!(
9462                    "{reason}; killed its process group after the leader exited rather than charge an incomplete CPU measurement"
9463                ));
9464            }
9465            let timeout = cpu_budget_usec
9466                .filter(|limit| cpu_usage_usec >= *limit)
9467                .map(|_| ProcessTimeout::Cpu);
9468            observation.termination = if timeout.is_some() {
9469                TerminationPath::FinalWaitCpuBudgetReturn
9470            } else if matches!(observation.final_wait, FinalWaitObservation::Reaped { .. }) {
9471                TerminationPath::CompletedWait4
9472            } else {
9473                TerminationPath::NonterminalWait4Return
9474            };
9475            observation.returned_cpu_charge = ReturnedCpuCharge::Value {
9476                cpu_usec: cpu_usage_usec,
9477                basis: ChargeBasis::FinalWait4,
9478            };
9479            return Ok(ProcessOutput {
9480                status,
9481                timeout,
9482                cpu_usage_usec,
9483            });
9484        }
9485        let now = Instant::now();
9486        let wall_due = now >= deadline;
9487        let poll_due = cpu_budget_usec.is_some() && now >= next_cpu_poll;
9488        if wall_due || poll_due {
9489            if let Err(reason) = membership(pid, true) {
9490                observation.termination = TerminationPath::CgroupMembershipStop;
9491                return match stop_process_group(
9492                    pid,
9493                    &leader,
9494                    cgroup,
9495                    started,
9496                    &mut observation.final_wait,
9497                ) {
9498                    Ok(_) => Err(format!(
9499                        "{reason}; stopped and reaped its leader rather than charge an incomplete CPU measurement"
9500                    )),
9501                    Err(error) => Err(format!(
9502                        "{reason}; could not confirm leader stop/reap: {error}"
9503                    )),
9504                };
9505            }
9506        }
9507        let (timeout, observed_cpu_usec) = if wall_due {
9508            (Some(ProcessTimeout::Wall), None)
9509        } else if let Some(limit) = cpu_budget_usec.filter(|_| poll_due) {
9510            next_cpu_poll = now + cpu_poll_interval;
9511            let sample_result = match &cpu_reader {
9512                Some(Ok(reader)) => sample(pid, reader),
9513                Some(Err(error)) => Err(CpuError {
9514                    stage: CpuErrorStage::Registration,
9515                    reason: format!("registration: {error}"),
9516                }),
9517                None => unreachable!("CPU budget has no invocation reader"),
9518            };
9519            let triggered = sample_result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|used| *used >= limit);
9520            if let LiveCpuObservation::Enabled(live) = &mut observation.live {
9521                live.record_poll(
9522                    now.duration_since(started),
9523                    matches!(&cpu_reader, Some(Ok(_))),
9524                    &sample_result,
9525                    triggered,
9526                );
9527            }
9528            match sample_result {
9529                Ok(used) => {
9530                    cpu_accounting_missing_since = None;
9531                    (triggered.then_some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu), Some(used))
9532                }
9533                Err(error) => {
9534                    let reason = error.reason;
9535                    // Time the grace from when the failed sample returned, not
9536                    // from `now`, which was taken before it ran. One host-wide
9537                    // /proc census can itself outlast the grace, and proccpu
9538                    // then serves its refusal again for 500 ms
9539                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3822). Timed
9540                    // from `now`, that census alone would stop the command at
9541                    // the next poll, with no fresh sample in between.
9542                    let failed_at = Instant::now();
9543                    let missing_since = cpu_accounting_missing_since.get_or_insert(failed_at);
9544                    if failed_at.duration_since(*missing_since) >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE {
9545                        observation.termination = TerminationPath::AccountingUnavailableStop;
9546                        return match stop_process_group(
9547                            pid,
9548                            &leader,
9549                            cgroup,
9550                            started,
9551                            &mut observation.final_wait,
9552                        ) {
9553                            Ok(_) => Err(format!(
9554                                "cannot measure live CPU for process group {pid}: {reason}; stopped and reaped its leader rather than silently disabling its CPU budget"
9555                            )),
9556                            Err(error) => Err(format!(
9557                                "cannot measure live CPU for process group {pid}: {reason}; could not confirm leader stop/reap: {error}"
9558                            )),
9559                        };
9560                    }
9561                    (None, None)
9562                }
9563            }
9564        } else {
9565            (None, None)
9566        };
9567        if let Some(timeout) = timeout {
9568            observation.termination = match timeout {
9569                ProcessTimeout::Cpu => TerminationPath::CpuBudgetStop,
9570                ProcessTimeout::Wall => TerminationPath::WallBudgetStop,
9571            };
9572            let (status, final_cpu_usage_usec) =
9573                stop_process_group(pid, &leader, cgroup, started, &mut observation.final_wait)?;
9574            let cpu_usage_usec = observed_cpu_usec.map_or(final_cpu_usage_usec, |observed| {
9575                observed.max(final_cpu_usage_usec)
9576            });
9577            observation.returned_cpu_charge = ReturnedCpuCharge::Value {
9578                cpu_usec: cpu_usage_usec,
9579                basis: if observed_cpu_usec.is_some() {
9580                    ChargeBasis::MaxTriggerAndFinalWait4
9581                } else {
9582                    ChargeBasis::FinalWait4
9583                },
9584            };
9585            return Ok(ProcessOutput {
9586                status,
9587                timeout: Some(timeout),
9588                cpu_usage_usec,
9589            });
9590        }
9591        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
9592    }
9593}
9594
9595fn cell_timeout_attempt(
9596    spec: &CellRunSpec,
9597    cpu_timeout_seconds: u64,
9598    wall_timeout_seconds: u64,
9599    duration: Duration,
9600    timeout: ProcessTimeout,
9601) -> AttemptResult {
9602    let index = spec.attempt.as_str();
9603    // A post-preparation bound was already exhausted before this attempt could
9604    // start, so no process exists from which to recover an exit status or signal.
9605    // Record that fact with the
9606    // same typed NotRun report Hermit uses before its first guest run.  A
9607    // synthetic exit code would make a scheduler decision look like a process
9608    // result, while a bare FAIL makes the retained attempt unreadable to every
9609    // typed consumer.
9610    let report = serde_json::to_string(&VerificationReport::no_result())
9611        .expect("the typed NotRun report must serialize");
9612    let report_sha256 = hex_digest(report.as_bytes());
9613    AttemptResult {
9614        command_binding: spec
9615            .command_binding
9616            .as_ref()
9617            .map(|held| held.identity.clone()),
9618        index: index.into(),
9619        outcome: "ERROR".into(),
9620        error_kind: Some(timeout.error_kind().into()),
9621        status: None,
9622        signal: None,
9623        timed_out: true,
9624        duration_ms: duration.as_millis(),
9625        cpu_usage_usec: None,
9626        capture_custom_runs: spec.single_run_capture.is_some(),
9627        single_run_capture: None,
9628        capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: None,
9629        capture_adoption_timeout: None,
9630        observation_sha256: None,
9631        argv: spec.argv.clone(),
9632        guest_argv: spec.guest_argv.clone(),
9633        env: spec.env.clone(),
9634        cwd: spec.cwd.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
9635        shell_command: shell_command(&spec.cwd.to_string_lossy(), &spec.env, &spec.argv),
9636        stdout: String::new(),
9637        stderr: String::new(),
9638        verification_report: Some(report),
9639        verification_report_sha256: Some(report_sha256),
9640        runtime: None,
9641        first_divergent_scheduler_turn: None,
9642        first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: None,
9643        first_divergent_record: None,
9644        first_divergent_syscall: None,
9645        first_divergent_left_message: None,
9646        first_divergent_right_message: None,
9647        sabre_path_evidence: None,
9648        sabre_path_evidence_sha256: None,
9649        reason: Some(format!(
9650            "{} before attempt {index} started",
9651            timeout.reason(cpu_timeout_seconds, wall_timeout_seconds)
9652        )),
9653    }
9654}
9655
9656/// The one definition of where a cell's retained evidence lives.
9657///
9658/// Was duplicated verbatim in `run_cell` and `infrastructure_error_result`.
9659/// Two copies of a path formula is how a log line ends up pointing at a
9660/// directory that does not exist, so surfacing the path made collapsing them a
9661/// prerequisite rather than a tidy-up.
9662fn cell_artifact_dir(context: &RunContext, cell: &SelectedCell) -> PathBuf {
9663    cell_artifact_path(
9664        &context.result_root,
9665        &context.run_id,
9666        &cell.id,
9667        context.attempt,
9668    )
9669}
9670
9671/// Construct the producer-owned path for one cell's outer attempt.
9672/// Readers use this same definition to authenticate a retained fixture's
9673/// relocation; they must still validate the recorded root and invocation.
9674pub fn cell_artifact_path(
9675    result_root: &Path,
9676    run_id: &str,
9677    cell: &CellId,
9678    attempt: u64,
9679) -> PathBuf {
9680    let base_slug = format!(
9681        "{}-{}-{}",
9682        cell.test.replace('/', "-"),
9683        cell.mode,
9684        cell.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("none")
9685    );
9686    let slug = if attempt == 1 {
9687        base_slug
9688    } else {
9689        format!("{base_slug}-attempt-{attempt}")
9690    };
9691    result_root.join("runs").join(run_id).join(slug)
9692}
9693
9694/// The verdict of `attempt`'s retained verification report, or `None` when it
9695/// retains none or one that is not a current report. A `diverged` verdict
9696/// here is what [`observed_result`] types a verify or chaos row
9697/// `determinism-failure` from; the parity post-pass reads the same verdict
9698/// from every attempt (`parity::records_mismatch`).
9699pub(crate) fn verification_verdict(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> Option<Verdict> {
9700    let report = attempt.verification_report.as_deref()?;
9701    current_verification_report(report.as_bytes())
9702        .ok()
9703        .map(|report| report.verdict)
9704}
9705
9706/// Whether `attempt` retains a current verification report whose strict
9707/// comparison matched: [`VerificationReport::require_canonical_match`], the
9708/// check a strict verify cell must pass before the runner can pass it. A
9709/// `matched` verdict from a weaker comparison does not count. The parity
9710/// post-pass reads it from the single attempt of a `FAIL` row to decide that
9711/// the row still has one deterministic log (`parity::evaluate_history`).
9712pub(crate) fn verification_matched_canonically(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> bool {
9713    attempt
9714        .verification_report
9715        .as_deref()
9716        .and_then(|report| current_verification_report(report.as_bytes()).ok())
9717        .is_some_and(|report| report.require_canonical_match().is_ok())
9718}
9719
9720/// The guest loader's refusal line a v2 retry keys on: glibc's fatal
9721/// ISA-level check, printed by the loader itself when the CPU it was
9722/// built for is not the CPU presented. The level digit is not part of
9723/// the signature: a v4-demanding loader on the v2 CPU is the same
9724/// rejection (its retry under the v2 rootfs then decides the cell).
9725pub const LOADER_V2_SIGNATURE: &str = "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v";
9726
9727/// The start of the line Hermit prints to stderr when it refuses a run whose
9728/// program interpreter aborted because the CPU presented is below the
9729/// x86-64 level the interpreter was built for, in the one case the v2 retry
9730/// exists for: a loader built for x86-64-v3, as CentOS Stream 10's is, on
9731/// the x86-64-v2 CPU (detcore/src/loader_cpu_abort.rs, `Watch::refusal`;
9732/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4695>). The interpreter and
9733/// the executable follow, then [`LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_CAUSE`].
9734pub const LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_PREFIX: &str =
9735    "--cpu-profile x86-64-v2 refused: the program interpreter ";
9736
9737/// The rest of the refusal [`LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_PREFIX`] starts: it
9738/// quotes the loader's own message and says the CPU presented is below the
9739/// level the loader was built for. The same refusal of a loader that names
9740/// another level, or under another profile, says something else here.
9741pub const LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_CAUSE: &str = " stopped before the program started, printing \
9742     \"Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v3\" and exiting 127; the x86-64-v2 \
9743     CPU this profile presents is below the x86-64-v3 it was built for;";
9744
9745/// Whether `line` is Hermit's refusal of an x86-64-v3 program interpreter's
9746/// abort on the x86-64-v2 CPU ([`LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_PREFIX`]).
9747fn is_loader_v3_on_v2_refusal(line: &str) -> bool {
9748    line.strip_prefix(LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_PREFIX)
9749        .is_some_and(|rest| rest.contains(LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_CAUSE))
9750}
9751
9752/// Whether `attempt` is a loader rejection the v2 retry exists for (issue
9753/// 5476): the guest loader refused the x86-64-v2 CPU before the guest ran.
9754/// Three shapes of retained verification report show it. In the first two
9755/// the run ends with the loader's own exit 127, beside the loader's fatal
9756/// ISA line ([`LOADER_V2_SIGNATURE`]) in this attempt's own captured output:
9757/// - a typed `first_run_rejected` with guest exit 127, with the line in the
9758///   attempt's stdout or stderr: verify stopped after a first run whose
9759///   disposition its `--verify-allow` refused;
9760/// - a `matched` comparison in which both compared runs exited 127, with the
9761///   line in the attempt's stderr: a cell that declares a non-zero guest
9762///   disposition runs with `--verify-allow=failure`, which admits the
9763///   loader's exit, so verify ran the guest twice and compared the runs.
9764///   Only a match counts. Two refused runs that diverged differ in Hermit's
9765///   own work before exec, a determinism failure the retry must not hide.
9766///
9767/// The third is Hermit's typed refusal in place of that exit. Where Hermit
9768/// watches the program interpreter (the ptrace backend; not KVM, where guest
9769/// threads are not host tasks), it refuses the run at the loader's
9770/// `exit_group(127)` and exits 122 itself:
9771/// - a typed `run_failed` of run 1 with failure `policy_refusal`, with
9772///   Hermit's refusal of an x86-64-v3 program interpreter's abort on the
9773///   x86-64-v2 CPU as a line of the attempt's stderr
9774///   ([`LOADER_V3_ON_V2_REFUSAL_PREFIX`]). The report's own detail names no
9775///   cause, so the line is the evidence of which refusal it was. Only that
9776///   refusal counts: another policy refusal (an x86-64-v3 admission refused
9777///   for the host's XCR0, say), an interpreter that names another level, or
9778///   one refused under another profile is no loader rejection of the v2 CPU.
9779///   A chaos pair admits its second run whatever the first exited, and the
9780///   report is still run 1's refusal.
9781///
9782/// Both halves come from retained typed evidence, never from the row's
9783/// reason text, and from the same attempt: a guest that merely prints the
9784/// line without such a report earns no retry, and such a report without the
9785/// line is an ordinary guest failure.
9786pub fn loader_v2_rejection(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> bool {
9787    let Some(report) = attempt
9788        .verification_report
9789        .as_deref()
9790        .and_then(|report| current_verification_report(report.as_bytes()).ok())
9791    else {
9792        return false;
9793    };
9794    let first_run_rejected = matches!(
9795        report.no_result_reason,
9796        Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::FirstRunRejected {
9797            exit_code: Some(127),
9798            ..
9799        })
9800    );
9801    let both_runs_refused = report.verdict == Verdict::Matched
9802        && report.compared_outputs.as_ref().is_some_and(|outputs| {
9803            outputs.left.exit_code == Some(127) && outputs.right.exit_code == Some(127)
9804        });
9805    let run1_policy_refused = matches!(
9806        report.no_result_reason,
9807        Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::RunFailed {
9808            run: crate::canonical_verdict::VerificationRun::Run1,
9809            failure: crate::canonical_verdict::RunFailure::PolicyRefusal,
9810            ..
9811        })
9812    );
9813    (first_run_rejected
9814        && (attempt.stdout.contains(LOADER_V2_SIGNATURE)
9815            || attempt.stderr.contains(LOADER_V2_SIGNATURE)))
9816        || (both_runs_refused && attempt.stderr.contains(LOADER_V2_SIGNATURE))
9817        || (run1_policy_refused && attempt.stderr.lines().any(is_loader_v3_on_v2_refusal))
9818}
9819
9820/// Whether any inner attempt of `result` is a loader rejection
9821/// ([`loader_v2_rejection`]), each decided from that attempt's own report and
9822/// output: the harness retry gate for the v2 retry.
9823pub fn loader_v2_rejected(result: &CellResult) -> bool {
9824    result.attempts.iter().any(loader_v2_rejection)
9825}
9826
9827/// The fixture loadability verdict the v2 rootfs carries
9828/// (fb-only/v2_rootfs/fixture_glibc_check.sh, issue 5476). It is
9829/// tab-separated: `schema 1`, then `status checked`, or `status unchecked
9830/// REASON` where the check could not run, then one `missing PATH ITEM` line
9831/// per symbol version or library that a fixture file needs and the rootfs
9832/// lacks, PATH relative to the prebuilt fixtures root (`build_root`).
9833pub const V2_ROOTFS_VERDICT_FILE: &str = "fixtures-glibc-check.tsv";
9834
9835/// The error kind of a v2 retry refused before launch because the rootfs
9836/// cannot load the cell's fixture ([`v2_retry_context`]).
9837pub const ROOTFS_MISSING_SYMBOL: &str = "rootfs-missing-symbol";
9838
9839/// The error kind of a v2 retry refused before launch because the rootfs
9840/// carries no usable fixture verdict ([`v2_retry_context`]).
9841pub const ROOTFS_UNCHECKED: &str = "rootfs-unchecked";
9842
9843/// What the v2 rootfs at `oci_dir` lacks for the files of `cell`'s prebuilt
9844/// fixture directory, by its verdict ([`V2_ROOTFS_VERDICT_FILE`]): `Ok` with
9845/// one "PATH needs ITEM" entry per lacking item, empty where the rootfs can
9846/// load every file (and for a cell with no prebuilt fixture), or `Err` with
9847/// why the verdict is unusable: absent, unreadable, malformed, or written
9848/// by a check that did not run.
9849pub fn v2_rootfs_missing(oci_dir: &Path, cell: &SelectedCell) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
9850    let path = oci_dir.join(V2_ROOTFS_VERDICT_FILE);
9851    let text = fs::read_to_string(&path)
9852        .map_err(|error| format!("cannot read {}: {error}", path.display()))?;
9853    let mut lines = text.lines();
9854    if lines.next() != Some("schema\t1") {
9855        return Err(format!("{} does not start with schema 1", path.display()));
9856    }
9857    let status = lines.next().unwrap_or_default();
9858    match status.split('\t').collect::<Vec<_>>().as_slice() {
9859        ["status", "checked"] => {}
9860        ["status", "unchecked", why] => {
9861            return Err(format!("the fixture check did not run: {why}"));
9862        }
9863        _ => {
9864            return Err(format!("{} has no status line: {status:?}", path.display()));
9865        }
9866    }
9867    // The prebuilt fixture directory of a test (`prepare_test_until`); the
9868    // slash keeps `c-programs-a/` from matching `c-programs-ab/`.
9869    let prefix = format!("{}/", cell.test.id.replace('/', "-"));
9870    let mut missing = Vec::new();
9871    for line in lines {
9872        match line.split('\t').collect::<Vec<_>>().as_slice() {
9873            ["missing", file, item] => {
9874                if file.starts_with(&prefix) {
9875                    missing.push(format!("{file} needs {item}"));
9876                }
9877            }
9878            _ => {
9879                return Err(format!("{} has a malformed line: {line:?}", path.display()));
9880            }
9881        }
9882    }
9883    Ok(missing)
9884}
9885
9886/// The context of `cell`'s v2 retry attempt inside the rootfs at `oci_dir`,
9887/// or the typed refusal that stands for that attempt where the rootfs's
9888/// fixture verdict ([`v2_rootfs_missing`]) says it cannot load the cell's
9889/// fixture, or gives no usable verdict. A refusal launches nothing: its row
9890/// is an ERROR with `understood_prerequisite_failure`, its error kind is
9891/// [`ROOTFS_MISSING_SYMBOL`] or [`ROOTFS_UNCHECKED`], and its reason names
9892/// what the rootfs lacks, or why there is no verdict. Only the v2 retry
9893/// consults the verdict; a host cell never does.
9894pub fn v2_retry_context(
9895    context: &RunContext,
9896    cell: &SelectedCell,
9897    oci_dir: &Path,
9898) -> Result<RunContext, Box<CellResult>> {
9899    let (kind, reason) = match v2_rootfs_missing(oci_dir, cell) {
9900        Ok(missing) if missing.is_empty() => {
9901            return Ok(context.clone().with_v2_retry(oci_dir.to_path_buf()));
9902        }
9903        Ok(missing) => (
9904            ROOTFS_MISSING_SYMBOL,
9905            format!(
9906                "v2 retry refused before launch: the v2 rootfs cannot load this cell's fixture: {} (issue 5476)",
9907                missing.join("; ")
9908            ),
9909        ),
9910        Err(why) => (
9911            ROOTFS_UNCHECKED,
9912            format!(
9913                "v2 retry refused before launch: the v2 rootfs has no usable fixture verdict: {why} (issue 5476)"
9914            ),
9915        ),
9916    };
9917    let mut result = infrastructure_error_result(context, cell, reason);
9918    result.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure);
9919    result.error_kind = Some(kind.into());
9920    Err(Box::new(result))
9921}
9922
9923/// Whether `result` is a v2 retry refused before launch
9924/// ([`v2_retry_context`]). Another attempt would meet the same verdict, so
9925/// the harness gives it none.
9926pub fn is_v2_retry_refusal(result: &CellResult) -> bool {
9927    matches!(
9928        result.error_kind.as_deref(),
9929        Some(ROOTFS_MISSING_SYMBOL | ROOTFS_UNCHECKED)
9930    )
9931}
9932
9933/// Whether `attempt` retains a current verification report in which Hermit
9934/// rejected the guest's first verify run (`first_run_rejected`): the guest ran
9935/// and failed, so no comparison was made. A typed failure of a run Hermit had
9936/// started (`run_failed`) is the same kind of evidence: Hermit named what
9937/// stopped the run, so its output is Hermit's report of it, not a host block.
9938fn first_run_rejected(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> bool {
9939    attempt
9940        .verification_report
9941        .as_deref()
9942        .and_then(|report| current_verification_report(report.as_bytes()).ok())
9943        .is_some_and(|report| {
9944            matches!(
9945                report.no_result_reason,
9946                Some(
9947                    crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::FirstRunRejected { .. }
9948                        | crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::RunFailed { .. }
9949                )
9950            )
9951        })
9952}
9953
9954fn observed_result(
9955    mode: &str,
9956    outcome: &str,
9957    attempts: &[AttemptResult],
9958    error_kind: Option<&str>,
9959) -> Option<ObservedResult> {
9960    // Preserve the existing terminal evidence and timeout guards before using
9961    // a typed product verdict. Incidental diagnostic text cannot erase a valid
9962    // comparison, but an earlier divergence cannot revive an unusable terminal
9963    // framework/evidence result either.
9964    let typed = observed_result_from_typed_evidence(mode, outcome, attempts, error_kind);
9965    if matches!(
9966        typed,
9967        Some(
9968            ObservedResult::Pass
9969                | ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure
9970                | ObservedResult::ReplayFailure
9971        )
9972    ) {
9973        return typed;
9974    }
9975    // A crash whose terminal attempt retains Hermit's typed rejection of the
9976    // guest's first verify run is the guest's own failure, and that attempt's
9977    // output is the guest's own output: a guest line such as "lsirq: cannot
9978    // open /proc/interrupts: Permission denied" is product behaviour, not the
9979    // host blocking a tool (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4029).
9980    if typed == Some(ObservedResult::CrashError) && attempts.last().is_some_and(first_run_rejected)
9981    {
9982        return typed;
9983    }
9984    if let Some(class) = attempts.iter().find_map(|attempt| {
9985        let output = format!("{}\n{}", attempt.stdout, attempt.stderr);
9986        environmental_block_observation(&output).block_class()
9987    }) {
9988        return Some(if class == EnvBlockClass::BpfjailerBanner {
9989            ObservedResult::SandboxDenied
9990        } else {
9991            ObservedResult::InfrastructureError
9992        });
9993    }
9994    typed
9995}
9996
9997/// A chaos cell that its population floor failed while every attempt matched
9998/// is [`ObservedResult::ChaosFloorFailure`], not the crash-error
9999/// [`observed_result`] would infer from the FAIL alone, which no attempt
10000/// supports (the stress series refused such rows: "framework result has no
10001/// supporting canonical typed attempt"). Any other result is kept: a
10002/// divergence, a timeout, a crash an attempt does support, or a framework
10003/// failure.
10004fn chaos_floor_result(
10005    result: Option<ObservedResult>,
10006    floor_failed: bool,
10007    attempts: &[AttemptResult],
10008) -> Option<ObservedResult> {
10009    let every_attempt_matched = !attempts.is_empty()
10010        && attempts
10011            .iter()
10012            .all(|attempt| verification_verdict(attempt) == Some(Verdict::Matched));
10013    if floor_failed && every_attempt_matched && result == Some(ObservedResult::CrashError) {
10014        Some(ObservedResult::ChaosFloorFailure)
10015    } else {
10016        result
10017    }
10018}
10019
10020fn observed_result_from_typed_evidence(
10021    mode: &str,
10022    outcome: &str,
10023    attempts: &[AttemptResult],
10024    error_kind: Option<&str>,
10025) -> Option<ObservedResult> {
10026    if outcome == "PASS" {
10027        return Some(ObservedResult::Pass);
10028    }
10029    // A later framework or evidence failure decides whether this cell produced
10030    // a usable product result. An earlier attempt can still retain a located
10031    // divergence in `attempts`, but it must not make a terminal infrastructure
10032    // or no-result outcome look product-attributed.
10033    if non_product_failure_class(error_kind).is_some() {
10034        return None;
10035    }
10036    if attempts.iter().any(|attempt| attempt.timed_out)
10037        || (outcome == "FAIL"
10038            && attempts
10039                .iter()
10040                .any(|attempt| attempt.capture_adoption_timeout.is_some())
10041            && attempts
10042                .iter()
10043                .all(|attempt| attempt.status == Some(0) && attempt.signal.is_none())
10044            && attempts
10045                .iter()
10046                .filter_map(|attempt| attempt.observation_sha256.as_ref())
10047                .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
10048                .len()
10049                <= 1)
10050    {
10051        return Some(ObservedResult::Timeout);
10052    }
10053    // A chaos attempt is a verify run under a perturbed schedule, so a
10054    // diverged chaos attempt is the same product failure as a diverged verify
10055    // attempt. Without the chaos arm it fell through to crash-error, and the
10056    // stress series refused the row because a crash cannot carry a divergence.
10057    if (mode == "verify" || mode == "chaos")
10058        && attempts
10059            .iter()
10060            .any(|attempt| verification_verdict(attempt) == Some(Verdict::Diverged))
10061    {
10062        return Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure);
10063    }
10064    if mode == "replay"
10065        && attempts
10066            .iter()
10067            .any(|attempt| verification_verdict(attempt) == Some(Verdict::Diverged))
10068    {
10069        return Some(ObservedResult::ReplayFailure);
10070    }
10071    (outcome == "FAIL").then_some(ObservedResult::CrashError)
10072}
10073
10074fn non_product_failure_class(error_kind: Option<&str>) -> Option<FailureClass> {
10075    match error_kind {
10076        Some(
10077            "guest-launch-refused"
10078            | "backend-unavailable"
10079            | ROOTFS_MISSING_SYMBOL
10080            | ROOTFS_UNCHECKED,
10081        ) => Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure),
10082        Some("infrastructure" | "result-publication") => {
10083            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
10084        }
10085        Some("incomplete-verification-evidence" | "invalid-backend-evidence") => {
10086            Some(FailureClass::NoResult)
10087        }
10088        _ => None,
10089    }
10090}
10091
10092fn failure_class(
10093    outcome: &str,
10094    result: Option<ObservedResult>,
10095    error_kind: Option<&str>,
10096) -> Option<FailureClass> {
10097    if outcome == "PASS" {
10098        return None;
10099    }
10100    if matches!(
10101        result,
10102        Some(ObservedResult::SandboxDenied | ObservedResult::InfrastructureError)
10103    ) {
10104        return Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure);
10105    }
10106    if let Some(failure_class) = non_product_failure_class(error_kind) {
10107        return Some(failure_class);
10108    }
10109    if let Some(result) = result {
10110        if let Some(failure_class) = result.failure_class() {
10111            return Some(failure_class);
10112        }
10113    }
10114    if outcome == "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" {
10115        Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure)
10116    } else {
10117        Some(FailureClass::NoResult)
10118    }
10119}
10120
10121/// Apply a failed chaos population assertion without erasing an attempt-level
10122/// infrastructure result. A timeout or unavailable verification report means
10123/// the population was not fully measured; it is not a product failure merely
10124/// because the incomplete sample also missed `min_passes`. A timed-out
10125/// attempt's outcome is FAIL, not ERROR, so its cause arrives as `incomplete`
10126/// ([`chaos_incomplete_reason`]) and leads the reason.
10127fn apply_failed_chaos_assertion(
10128    outcome: &mut String,
10129    reason: &mut Option<String>,
10130    incomplete: Option<&str>,
10131    assertion_reason: String,
10132) {
10133    if outcome != "ERROR" {
10134        *outcome = "FAIL".into();
10135        *reason = Some(match incomplete {
10136            Some(incomplete) => format!("{incomplete}; {assertion_reason}"),
10137            None => assertion_reason,
10138        });
10139    }
10140}
10141
10142/// A chaos population's passes, failures and timed-out attempts. A timed-out
10143/// attempt is neither a pass nor a failure, even when the guest exited 0 just
10144/// as the cell's CPU budget ran out: counting it as a pass would claim a seed
10145/// the budget refused, and counting a killed seed as a failure would satisfy
10146/// `min_failures` with no product failure.
10147fn chaos_population_counts(attempts: &[AttemptResult]) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
10148    let timed_out = attempts.iter().filter(|attempt| attempt.timed_out).count() as u64;
10149    let passes = attempts
10150        .iter()
10151        .filter(|attempt| attempt.status == Some(0) && !attempt.timed_out)
10152        .count() as u64;
10153    (
10154        passes,
10155        attempts.len() as u64 - passes - timed_out,
10156        timed_out,
10157    )
10158}
10159
10160/// Why a chaos population is incomplete: the attempt that timed out, which
10161/// stops the seed loop, and how many planned seeds never ran. An earlier
10162/// seed's reason (a product failure before the budget ran out) follows it,
10163/// naming that seed, so the timeout does not hide it.
10164fn chaos_incomplete_reason(attempts: &[AttemptResult], planned_seeds: usize) -> Option<String> {
10165    let timed_out = attempts.iter().find(|attempt| attempt.timed_out)?;
10166    let incomplete = format!(
10167        "{}: {} at {}; {} of {planned_seeds} seeds ran",
10168        timed_out.error_kind.as_deref().unwrap_or("timeout"),
10169        timed_out
10170            .reason
10171            .as_deref()
10172            .unwrap_or("the attempt timed out"),
10173        timed_out.index,
10174        attempts.len(),
10175    );
10176    let earlier = attempts
10177        .iter()
10178        .take_while(|attempt| !attempt.timed_out)
10179        .find_map(|attempt| Some((&attempt.index, attempt.reason.as_deref()?)));
10180    Some(match earlier {
10181        Some((index, reason)) => format!("{incomplete}; {index}: {reason}"),
10182        None => incomplete,
10183    })
10184}
10185
10186/// A chaos cell's reason before its population floors are checked: a
10187/// timeout's incomplete reason leads, unless an attempt-level ERROR already
10188/// explains the cell.
10189fn chaos_cell_reason(
10190    outcome: &str,
10191    reason: Option<String>,
10192    incomplete: Option<&str>,
10193) -> Option<String> {
10194    match incomplete {
10195        Some(incomplete) if outcome != "ERROR" => Some(incomplete.to_string()),
10196        _ => reason,
10197    }
10198}

10256fn record_cell(
10257    context: &RunContext,
10258    cell: &SelectedCell,
10259    run: impl FnOnce(&mut CellRunProgress) -> Result<CellResult, String>,
10260) -> Result<CellResult, CellRunFailure> {
10261    record_cell_with_probe_record(
10262        context,
10263        cell,
10264        || crate::vfork_spawn::CLONE3.cgroup_probe_record(),
10265        run,
10266    )

10268
10269/// [`record_cell`], with the probe record to publish given (the
10270/// process's own, in production).
10271fn record_cell_with_probe_record(
10272    context: &RunContext,
10273    cell: &SelectedCell,
10274    get_probe_record: impl FnOnce() -> Option<crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord>,
10275    run: impl FnOnce(&mut CellRunProgress) -> Result<CellResult, String>,
10276) -> Result<CellResult, CellRunFailure> {
10277    static WRITTEN: std::sync::Mutex<bool> = std::sync::Mutex::new(false);
10278    record_cell_with_probe_record_in_state(context, cell, get_probe_record, &WRITTEN, run)
10279}
10280
10281/// [`record_cell_with_probe_record`] with the publication once
10282/// state given (its own, in a test).
10283fn record_cell_with_probe_record_in_state(
10284    context: &RunContext,
10285    cell: &SelectedCell,
10286    get_probe_record: impl FnOnce() -> Option<crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord>,
10287    written: &std::sync::Mutex<bool>,
10288    run: impl FnOnce(&mut CellRunProgress) -> Result<CellResult, String>,
10289) -> Result<CellResult, CellRunFailure> {
10290    let mut progress = CellRunProgress::default();
10291    let outcome = run(&mut progress);
10292    // The record is read only now: the probe may have run during
10293    // this very cell (the first cell of the process), and a record
10294    // read before the run would silently publish nothing.
10295    let probe_record = get_probe_record();
10296    let mut observations = empty_cpu_observations(context, cell);
10297    observations.invocations = progress.observations;
10298    if let Err(reason) = publish_probe_record_with(context, probe_record, written) {
10299        return Err(match outcome {
10300            Ok(mut result) => {
10301                result.cpu_observations = Some(observations);
10302                CellRunFailure {
10303                    reason,
10304                    observations: Box::new(result.cpu_observations.take().expect("attached above")),
10305                    attempts: result.attempts,
10306                }
10307            }
10308            Err(_) => CellRunFailure {
10309                reason,
10310                observations: Box::new(observations),
10311                attempts: progress.attempts,
10312            },
10313        });
10314    }
10315    match outcome {
10316        Ok(mut result) => {
10317            result.cpu_observations = Some(observations);
10318            if let Err(reason) = result.require_cpu_observations() {
10319                return Err(CellRunFailure {
10320                    reason: format!("invalid generated CPU observations: {reason}"),
10321                    observations: Box::new(result.cpu_observations.take().expect("attached above")),
10322                    attempts: result.attempts,
10323                });
10324            }
10325            Ok(result)
10326        }
10327        Err(reason) => Err(CellRunFailure {
10328            reason,
10329            observations: Box::new(observations),
10330            attempts: progress.attempts,
10331        }),
10332    }
10333}

10351// All modes/backends using this fixture share the existing host inode with
10352// integration-test OFD producers. Other cells do not acquire a lease.
10353fn acquire_proc_locks_lease(
10354    cell: &SelectedCell,
10355    deadline: Instant,
10356    runtime_directory: Option<&OsStr>,
10357    host_identity: Option<&OsStr>,
10358) -> Result<Option<File>, String> {
10359    if cell.test.program.as_deref() != Some("tests/c/proc_locks.c") {
10360        return Ok(None);
10361    }
10362    use crate::proc_locks_lease;
10363    let uid = proc_locks_lease::effective_uid();
10364    let fallback = PathBuf::from(format!("/run/user/{uid}"));
10365    let acquire = || -> std::io::Result<File> {
10366        let directory =
10367            proc_locks_lease::validated_runtime_directory(runtime_directory, &fallback, uid)?;
10368        let file = proc_locks_lease::open_proc_locks_snapshot_lease_file(&directory, uid)?;
10369        proc_locks_lease::validate_proc_locks_host_identity(&file, host_identity)?;
10370        proc_locks_lease::lock_until(file, deadline)
10371    };
10372    acquire()
10373        .map(Some)
10374        .map_err(|error| format!("proc-locks snapshot lease: {error}"))
10375}
10376
10377fn selected_executable<'a>(
10378    context: &'a RunContext,
10379    cell: &SelectedCell,
10380) -> Option<&'a crate::executable_binding::HeldExecutable> {

10382        .backend
10383        .as_deref()
10384        .and_then(|backend| context.command_bindings.get(backend))
10385}

10387fn physical_binary_digest(context: &RunContext, cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
10388    binary_digest(
10389        selected_executable(context, cell)
10390            .map(|held| held.identity.executable.as_path())
10391            .unwrap_or(&context.hermit_bin),
10392    )
10393}
