10395fn comparator_binary_digest(context: &RunContext, cell: &SelectedCell) -> Option<String> {
10396    selected_executable(context, cell).and_then(|_| binary_digest(&context.hermit_bin))
10397}
10398
10399fn run_cell_inner(
10400    context: &RunContext,
10401    cell: &SelectedCell,
10402    dir: PathBuf,
10403    progress: &mut CellRunProgress,
10404) -> Result<CellResult, String> {
10405    let CellRunProgress {
10406        observations,
10407        attempts,
10408    } = progress;
10409    let started = Instant::now();
10410    let timeouts = cell_timeouts(context, cell)?;
10411    let preparation_deadline =
10412        execution_deadline_after_preparation(started, timeouts.wall_seconds)?;
10413    // Hashed once per process while the file is unchanged (bundle_record.rs);
10414    // a write or replacement is hashed afresh, here and after the cell.
10415    let binary_before = binary_digest(&context.hermit_bin);
10416    if let Some(held) = selected_executable(context, cell) {
10417        held.recheck()?;
10418    }
10419    let physical_before = physical_binary_digest(context, cell);
10420    if let Some(held) = selected_executable(context, cell) {
10421        if physical_before.as_deref() != Some(held.identity.sha256.as_str()) {
10422            return Err(
10423                "selected physical executable differs from its held producer identity".into(),
10424            );
10425        }
10426    }
10427    if let Some(recorded) = crate::bundle_record::recorded_hermit_sha256()? {
10428        if binary_before.as_deref() != Some(recorded.as_str()) {
10429            return Err(format!(
10430                "Hermit binary {} has sha256 {}, but the bundle records {recorded}; \
10431                 refusing to run a binary that is not the bundle's",
10432                context.hermit_bin.display(),
10433                binary_before.as_deref().unwrap_or("(unreadable)")
10434            ));
10435        }
10436    }
10437    let (guest, preparation_cpu_usage_usec) = prepare_test_until(
10438        context,
10439        cell,
10440        &dir,
10441        preparation_deadline,
10442        timeouts.wall_seconds,
10443        observations,
10444    )?;
10445    // Fixture preparation keeps its scaled wall-clock guard above. Post-preparation
10446    // execution uses its separately measured bound as an aggregate CPU-second budget
10447    // across all attempts/seeds, so time spent descheduled by a busy host cannot
10448    // turn a valid run into no_result. The wider wall deadline is retained only
10449    // for a wedged process that consumes no CPU and therefore cannot reach the
10450    // primary bound.
10451    let deadline = execution_deadline_after_preparation(Instant::now(), timeouts.wall_seconds)?;
10452    // Keep the guard through every repeat. Waiting consumes
10453    // this same deadline; acquisition failure returns through record_cell before
10454    // any guest attempt can be created, preserving an infrastructure no-result.
10455    let _proc_locks_lease = acquire_proc_locks_lease(
10456        cell,
10457        deadline,
10458        std::env::var_os("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR").as_deref(),
10459        std::env::var_os("HERMIT_PROC_LOCKS_LEASE_ID").as_deref(),
10460    )?;
10461    let execution_cpu_budget_usec = timeouts.cpu_seconds.saturating_mul(1_000_000);
10462    let mut execution_cpu_usage_usec = 0u64;
10463    let mode = cell.test.modes.get(&cell.id.mode).unwrap();
10464    match cell.id.mode.as_str() {
10465        "naked" => {
10466            for index in 1..=mode.runs.unwrap_or(3) {
10467                let spec = build_spec(
10468                    context,
10469                    cell,
10470                    dir.clone(),
10471                    guest.clone(),
10472                    &index.to_string(),
10473                    None,
10474                    remaining_cell_seconds(deadline),
10475                )?;
10476                attempts.push(execute_observed_until(
10477                    &spec,
10478                    &cell.test.observation,
10479                    &dir,
10480                    ExecutionBudget {
10481                        deadline,
10482                        cpu_timeout_seconds: timeouts.cpu_seconds,
10483                        wall_timeout_seconds: timeouts.wall_seconds,
10484
10485                        remaining_cpu_usec: Some(
10486                            execution_cpu_budget_usec.saturating_sub(execution_cpu_usage_usec),
10487                        ),
10488                    },
10489                    observations,
10490                )?);
10491                execution_cpu_usage_usec = execution_cpu_usage_usec
10492                    .checked_add(
10493                        attempts
10494                            .last()
10495                            .and_then(|attempt| attempt.cpu_usage_usec)
10496                            .unwrap_or(0),
10497                    )
10498                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell execution CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
10499                if attempts.last().is_some_and(|attempt| attempt.timed_out) {
10500                    break;
10501                }
10502            }
10503        }
10504        "chaos" => {
10505            let seeds = mode
10506                .seeds
10507                .as_ref()
10508                .ok_or_else(|| format!("{} chaos has no seeds", cell.id.test))?;
10509            if seeds.is_empty() {
10510                return Err(format!("{} chaos has no seeds", cell.id.test));
10511            }
10512            for seed in seeds {
10513                let index = format!("seed-{seed}");
10514                let spec = build_spec(
10515                    context,
10516                    cell,
10517                    dir.clone(),
10518                    guest.clone(),
10519                    &index,
10520                    Some(*seed),
10521                    remaining_cell_seconds(deadline),
10522                )?;
10523                attempts.push(execute_observed_until(
10524                    &spec,
10525                    &cell.test.observation,
10526                    &dir,
10527                    ExecutionBudget {
10528                        deadline,
10529                        cpu_timeout_seconds: timeouts.cpu_seconds,
10530                        wall_timeout_seconds: timeouts.wall_seconds,
10531
10532                        remaining_cpu_usec: Some(
10533                            execution_cpu_budget_usec.saturating_sub(execution_cpu_usage_usec),
10534                        ),
10535                    },
10536                    observations,
10537                )?);
10538                execution_cpu_usage_usec = execution_cpu_usage_usec
10539                    .checked_add(
10540                        attempts
10541                            .last()
10542                            .and_then(|attempt| attempt.cpu_usage_usec)
10543                            .unwrap_or(0),
10544                    )
10545                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell execution CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
10546                if attempts.last().is_some_and(|attempt| attempt.timed_out) {
10547                    break;
10548                }
10549            }
10550        }
10551        "custom" => {
10552            for index in 1..=mode.assert.as_ref().and_then(|a| a.runs).unwrap_or(1) {
10553                let spec = build_spec(
10554                    context,
10555                    cell,
10556                    dir.clone(),
10557                    guest.clone(),
10558                    &index.to_string(),
10559                    None,
10560                    remaining_cell_seconds(deadline),
10561                )?;
10562                attempts.push(execute_observed_until(
10563                    &spec,
10564                    &cell.test.observation,
10565                    &dir,
10566                    ExecutionBudget {
10567                        deadline,
10568                        cpu_timeout_seconds: timeouts.cpu_seconds,
10569                        wall_timeout_seconds: timeouts.wall_seconds,
10570
10571                        remaining_cpu_usec: Some(
10572                            execution_cpu_budget_usec.saturating_sub(execution_cpu_usage_usec),
10573                        ),
10574                    },
10575                    observations,
10576                )?);
10577                let attempt = attempts.last_mut().unwrap();
10578                let cpu = match effective_execution_cpu(attempt) {
10579                    Ok(cpu) => cpu,
10580                    Err(error) => {
10581                        // Preserve the child failure and its evidence, but no
10582                        // successor may run with an unknown cumulative charge.
10583                        capture_error(attempt, error);
10584                        break;
10585                    }
10586                };
10587                execution_cpu_usage_usec = execution_cpu_usage_usec
10588                    .checked_add(cpu)
10589                    .ok_or_else(|| "cell execution CPU usage overflowed u64".to_string())?;
10590                if attempts.last().is_some_and(|attempt| {
10591                    attempt.timed_out
10592                        || attempt.capture_adoption_timeout.is_some()
10593                        || (attempt.capture_custom_runs && attempt.outcome == "ERROR")
10594                }) {
10595                    break;
10596                }
10597            }
10598        }
10599        _ => {
10600            let spec = build_spec(
10601                context,
10602                cell,
10603                dir.clone(),
10604                guest.clone(),
10605                "1",
10606                None,
10607                remaining_cell_seconds(deadline),
10608            )?;
10609            attempts.push(execute_observed_until(
10610                &spec,
10611                &cell.test.observation,
10612                &dir,
10613                ExecutionBudget {
10614                    deadline,
10615                    cpu_timeout_seconds: timeouts.cpu_seconds,
10616                    wall_timeout_seconds: timeouts.wall_seconds,
10617
10618                    remaining_cpu_usec: Some(execution_cpu_budget_usec),
10619                },
10620                observations,
10621            )?);
10622        }
10623    }
10624    let hashes = attempts
10625        .iter()
10626        .filter_map(|attempt| attempt.observation_sha256.clone())
10627        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
10628    let distinct = hashes.iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>().len() as u64;
10629    let mut outcome = if attempts.iter().all(|attempt| attempt.outcome == "PASS") {
10630        "PASS"
10631    } else if attempts.iter().any(|attempt| attempt.outcome == "ERROR") {
10632        "ERROR"
10633    } else {
10634        "FAIL"
10635    }
10636    .to_string();
10637    let mut reason = attempts.iter().find_map(|attempt| attempt.reason.clone());
10638    let position = cell_divergence_position(attempts);
10639    let first_divergent_scheduler_turn = position.scheduler_turn;
10640    let first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = position.virtual_nanoseconds;
10641    let first_divergent_record = position.record;
10642    let first_divergent_syscall = position.syscall;
10643    let first_divergent_left_message = position.left_message;
10644    let first_divergent_right_message = position.right_message;
10645    let mut error_kind = attempts
10646        .iter()
10647        .find_map(|attempt| attempt.error_kind.clone());
10648    if cell.id.mode == "naked" {
10649        let minimum = mode
10650            .assert
10651            .as_ref()
10652            .and_then(|a| a.min_distinct)
10653            .unwrap_or(2);
10654        if distinct < minimum {
10655            outcome = "FAIL".into();
10656            reason = Some(format!(
10657                "naked observed {distinct} distinct outcomes, need {minimum}"
10658            ));
10659        }
10660    }
10661    if cell.id.mode == "custom"
10662        && !(context.capture_custom_runs && outcome == "ERROR")
10663        && mode.assert.as_ref().and_then(|a| a.repeat_identical) == Some(true)
10664        && distinct != 1
10665    {
10666        outcome = "FAIL".into();
10667        reason = Some(format!("custom observed {distinct} distinct outcomes"));
10668    }
10669    let mut chaos_floor_failed = false;
10670    if cell.id.mode == "chaos" {
10671        let assert = mode.assert.as_ref().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
10672        let (pass_count, failure_count, timed_out_count) = chaos_population_counts(attempts);
10673        let incomplete = chaos_incomplete_reason(attempts, mode.seeds.as_ref().map_or(0, Vec::len));
10674        reason = chaos_cell_reason(&outcome, reason, incomplete.as_deref());
10675        let diversity = diversity_evidence(
10676            &hashes,
10677            mode.outcome_classes,
10678            assert.min_distinct.unwrap_or(2),
10679            assert.min_normalized_entropy,
10680        );
10681        let normalized_entropy = diversity["normalized_entropy"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
10682        // ⚠️ THESE ARE FLOORS, AND A FLOOR OF ZERO IS NOT A CHECK.
10683        //
10684        // `min_passes` and `min_failures` are both unsigned, so a declared value
10685        // of 0 can never fire: `x < 0` is unsatisfiable. In a manifest
10686        // `min_failures: 0` READS like a threshold and asserts nothing, which is
10687        // the shape that let a required cell stay green while most of its seeds
10688        // exited nonzero. Five cells currently declare it; only
10689        // `chaos-c/lock-granularity` and one determinism-stress cell declare a
10690        // real value, and for those the floor is the point -- they are race
10691        // DEMONSTRATORS whose nonzero exits are the intended signal, so a run
10692        // with no failures means the race stopped being exposed.
10693        //
10694        // The matching trap on the other side is a `min_passes` of 1 against a
10695        // large seed list: it constrains exit status only to "at least one seed
10696        // exited 0", so every other seed may fail. Set `min_passes` to the seed
10697        // count unless failures are part of what the cell exists to observe.
10698        //
10699        // Neither floor bounds the population from ABOVE. Nothing here refuses a
10700        // cell whose failures grow, only one whose failures vanish.
10701        if distinct < assert.min_distinct.unwrap_or(2)
10702            || pass_count < assert.min_passes.unwrap_or(0)
10703            || failure_count < assert.min_failures.unwrap_or(0)
10704            || assert
10705                .min_normalized_entropy
10706                .is_some_and(|minimum| normalized_entropy < minimum)
10707        {
10708            chaos_floor_failed = outcome != "ERROR";
10709            apply_failed_chaos_assertion(
10710                &mut outcome,
10711                &mut reason,
10712                incomplete.as_deref(),
10713                format!(
10714                    "chaos distinct={distinct} passes={pass_count} failures={failure_count} timed_out={timed_out_count} normalized_entropy={normalized_entropy:.4}"
10715                ),
10716            );
10717        }
10718    }
10719    let execution_path = match summarize_sabre_path_evidence(attempts) {
10720        Ok(value) => value,
10721        Err(error) => {
10722            outcome = "ERROR".into();
10723            error_kind = Some("invalid-backend-evidence".into());
10724            reason = Some(error);
10725            None
10726        }
10727    };
10728    if outcome == "PASS" && execution_path_ineligible(execution_path.as_ref()) {
10729        outcome = "FAIL".into();
10730        reason = Some("SaBRe execution path is incomplete or used fallback/native sites".into());
10731    }
10732    let literal_argv = attempts
10733        .first()
10734        .map(|attempt| attempt.argv.clone())
10735        .unwrap_or_default();
10736    let literal_guest_argv = attempts
10737        .first()
10738        .map(|attempt| attempt.guest_argv.clone())
10739        .unwrap_or_else(|| guest.clone());
10740    let literal_env = attempts
10741        .first()
10742        .map(|attempt| attempt.env.clone())
10743        .unwrap_or_else(|| execution_cell_env(context, &dir, cell.id.mode != "naked"));
10744    let literal_cwd = attempts
10745        .first()
10746        .map(|attempt| attempt.cwd.clone())
10747        .unwrap_or_else(|| context.root.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
10748    let literal_shell_command = attempts
10749        .first()
10750        .map(|attempt| attempt.shell_command.clone())
10751        .unwrap_or_default();
10752    let test_sha = test_digest(&context.root, &cell.test)?;
10753    let comparator_sha = binary_digest(&context.hermit_bin);
10754    let binary_sha = physical_binary_digest(context, cell);
10755    let selected_changed =
10756        selected_executable(context, cell).is_some_and(|held| held.recheck().is_err());
10757    if (binary_before.is_some() && binary_before != comparator_sha)
10758        || (physical_before.is_some() && physical_before != binary_sha)
10759        || selected_changed
10760    {
10761        outcome = "ERROR".into();
10762        error_kind = Some("infrastructure".into());
10763        reason = Some("Hermit binary changed while the cell was executing".into());
10764    }
10765    let result = chaos_floor_result(
10766        observed_result(&cell.id.mode, &outcome, attempts, error_kind.as_deref()),
10767        chaos_floor_failed,
10768        attempts,
10769    );
10770    let failure_class = failure_class(&outcome, result, error_kind.as_deref());
10771    let cpu_usage_usec = attempts
10772        .iter()
10773        .try_fold(preparation_cpu_usage_usec, |total, attempt| {
10774            checked_add_cpu_usage(Some(total), attempt.cpu_usage_usec)
10775        });
10776    let capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec = (cell.id.mode == "custom" && context.capture_custom_runs)
10777        .then(|| {
10778            attempts.iter().try_fold(0_u64, |total, attempt| {
10779                total.checked_add(attempt.capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec?)
10780            })
10781        })
10782        .flatten();
10783    let declared_stdout = attempts
10784        .iter()
10785        .any(attempt_has_infrastructure_report)
10786        .then(|| cell_declared_stdout(cell));
10787    Ok(CellResult {
10788        capture_custom_runs: cell.id.mode == "custom" && context.capture_custom_runs,
10789        capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec,
10790        cpu_observations: None,
10791        artifact_dir: dir.display().to_string(),
10792        expected_guest_exit: cell_expected_guest_exit(cell),
10793        declared_stdout,
10794        schema: CELL_RESULT_SCHEMA,
10795        run_id: context.run_id.clone(),
10796        machine_shortname: context.machine_shortname.clone(),
10797        kernel_version: context.kernel_version.clone(),
10798        host_capabilities: context.host_capabilities.clone(),
10799        exact_branch_counter: context.exact_branch_counter.clone(),
10800        attempt: context.attempt,
10801        run_index: context.run_index,
10802        hermit_sha: context.source_sha.clone(),
10803        binary_build_sha: cell
10804            .id
10805            .backend
10806            .as_deref()
10807            .and_then(|backend| context.command_bindings.get(backend))
10808            .map(|held| held.identity.binary_build_sha.clone())
10809            .or_else(|| context.binary_build_sha.clone()),
10810        source_tree_dirty: context.source_dirty,
10811        binary_sha256: binary_sha,
10812        comparator_binary_sha256: selected_executable(context, cell).and(comparator_sha),
10813        test_sha256: test_sha,
10814        test: cell.id.test.clone(),
10815        category: cell.category.clone(),
10816        lane: cell.test.lane.clone(),
10817        mode: cell.id.mode.clone(),
10818        backend: cell.id.backend.clone(),
10819        // `required` records that the selected backend is an executable cell.
10820        // `ci` controls ordinary validate selection, not whether a manual red
10821        // measurement is real. Pressure re-runs enabled ci=false cells and
10822        // must be able to admit their evidence under the same identity.
10823        classification: cell_classification(cell).into(),
10824        outcome,
10825        result,
10826        failure_class,
10827        error_kind,
10828        timeout_seconds: timeouts.wall_seconds,
10829        execution_cpu_timeout_seconds: Some(timeouts.cpu_seconds),
10830        execution_wall_timeout_seconds: Some(timeouts.wall_seconds),
10831        duration_ms: Some(started.elapsed().as_millis()),
10832        cpu_usage_usec,
10833        runtime: attempts.iter().find_map(|attempt| attempt.runtime.clone()),
10834        log_level: (cell.id.mode != "naked").then(|| "info".into()),
10835        effective_args: literal_argv.iter().skip(1).cloned().collect(),
10836        argv: literal_argv,
10837        guest_argv: literal_guest_argv,
10838        env: literal_env,
10839        cwd: literal_cwd,
10840        shell_command: literal_shell_command,
10841        relaxations: cell_relaxations(cell),
10842        strictness: cell.strictness(),
10843        execution_path,
10844        diversity: (cell.id.mode == "chaos").then(|| {
10845            diversity_evidence(
10846                &hashes,
10847                mode.outcome_classes,
10848                mode.assert
10849                    .as_ref()
10850                    .and_then(|assert| assert.min_distinct)
10851                    .unwrap_or(2),
10852                mode.assert
10853                    .as_ref()
10854                    .and_then(|assert| assert.min_normalized_entropy),
10855            )
10856        }),
10857        attempts: std::mem::take(attempts),
10858        first_divergent_scheduler_turn,
10859        first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds,
10860        first_divergent_record,
10861        first_divergent_syscall,
10862        first_divergent_left_message,
10863        first_divergent_right_message,
10864        reason,
10865    })
10866}

10868/// Publish a durable third-outcome row when a cell could not reach execution.
10869///
10870/// Infrastructure failures are neither product failures nor admissible green
10871/// evidence.  Keeping an explicit row prevents preparation/spawn failures from
10872/// silently disappearing while leaving literal argv empty rather than
10873/// inventing a command that was never executed.
10874pub fn infrastructure_error_result(
10875    context: &RunContext,
10876    cell: &SelectedCell,
10877    reason: String,
10878) -> CellResult {
10879    let dir = cell_artifact_dir(context, cell);
10880    let timeouts = cell_timeouts(context, cell).ok();
10881    CellResult {
10882        capture_custom_runs: cell.id.mode == "custom" && context.capture_custom_runs,
10883        capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: None,
10884        cpu_observations: Some(empty_cpu_observations(context, cell)),
10885        artifact_dir: dir.display().to_string(),
10886        expected_guest_exit: cell_expected_guest_exit(cell),
10887        declared_stdout: None,
10888        schema: CELL_RESULT_SCHEMA,
10889        run_id: context.run_id.clone(),
10890        machine_shortname: context.machine_shortname.clone(),
10891        kernel_version: context.kernel_version.clone(),
10892        host_capabilities: context.host_capabilities.clone(),
10893        exact_branch_counter: context.exact_branch_counter.clone(),
10894        attempt: context.attempt,
10895        run_index: context.run_index,
10896        hermit_sha: context.source_sha.clone(),
10897        binary_build_sha: cell
10898            .id
10899            .backend
10900            .as_deref()
10901            .and_then(|backend| context.command_bindings.get(backend))
10902            .map(|held| held.identity.binary_build_sha.clone())
10903            .or_else(|| context.binary_build_sha.clone()),
10904        source_tree_dirty: context.source_dirty,
10905        binary_sha256: physical_binary_digest(context, cell),
10906        comparator_binary_sha256: comparator_binary_digest(context, cell),
10907        test_sha256: test_digest(&context.root, &cell.test).unwrap_or_default(),
10908        test: cell.id.test.clone(),
10909        category: cell.category.clone(),
10910        lane: cell.test.lane.clone(),
10911        mode: cell.id.mode.clone(),
10912        backend: cell.id.backend.clone(),
10913        classification: cell_classification(cell).into(),
10914        outcome: "ERROR".into(),
10915        result: None,
10916        failure_class: Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure),
10917        error_kind: Some("infrastructure".into()),
10918        timeout_seconds: timeouts
10919            .map(|policy| policy.wall_seconds)
10920            .unwrap_or(cell.timeout_seconds),
10921        execution_cpu_timeout_seconds: timeouts.map(|policy| policy.cpu_seconds),
10922        execution_wall_timeout_seconds: timeouts.map(|policy| policy.wall_seconds),
10923        duration_ms: None,
10924        cpu_usage_usec: None,
10925        runtime: None,
10926        log_level: (cell.id.mode != "naked").then(|| "info".into()),
10927        effective_args: Vec::new(),
10928        argv: Vec::new(),
10929        guest_argv: Vec::new(),
10930        env: execution_cell_env(context, &dir, cell.id.mode != "naked"),
10931        cwd: context.root.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
10932        shell_command: String::new(),
10933        relaxations: cell_relaxations(cell),
10934        strictness: cell.strictness(),
10935        execution_path: None,
10936        diversity: None,
10937        attempts: Vec::new(),
10938        // No attempt ran, so there is no divergence position to report. `None`
10939        // here means "never measured", which is the same value a clean run
10940        // produces -- see the note in the observation fold about those two
10941        // being indistinguishable in this field alone. The surrounding row is
10942        // what distinguishes them: this one carries an infrastructure error
10943        // kind and an empty `attempts`.
10944        first_divergent_scheduler_turn: None,
10945        first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: None,
10946        first_divergent_record: None,
10947        first_divergent_syscall: None,
10948        first_divergent_left_message: None,
10949        first_divergent_right_message: None,
10950        reason: Some(reason),
10951    }
10952}

11020        relaxations: cell_relaxations(cell),
11021        strictness: cell.strictness(),
11022        execution_path: None,
11023        diversity: None,
11024        attempts: Vec::new(),
11025        first_divergent_scheduler_turn: None,
11026        first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: None,
11027        first_divergent_record: None,
11028        first_divergent_syscall: None,
11029        first_divergent_left_message: None,

11035/// Reduce per-attempt divergence evidence to the cell-level fields.
11036///
11037/// Same first-attempt rule as `reason`, and resolved PER COORDINATE rather than
11038/// per attempt: a report that located a turn but no virtual nanosecond still
11039/// contributes the turn. Picking one attempt and taking both of its values
11040/// would silently drop the other coordinate.
11041///
11042/// Deliberately NOT a min across attempts. A min over the attempts of one run
11043/// is a one-run aggregate that would read like the cross-run `ObservedRange`
11044/// earliest/latest in ci/compat-envelope/scorecard.rs without having a sample
11045/// behind it, and this project has repeatedly been bitten by numbers that look
11046/// like a measurement and are not.
11047/// The divergence coordinates and compared messages of one cell.
11048///
11049/// A named struct rather than a tuple, deliberately: the four numeric values
11050/// are otherwise indistinguishable, and this project has already had a bare
11051/// ordinal read against the wrong axis. Each numeric field is a different
11052/// keyspace -- measured on one real divergence, the same event was record 98,
11053/// syscall 37 and scheduler turn 4. The messages retain the compared event
11054/// content without treating record position as identity.
11055#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
11056pub struct DivergencePosition {
11057    pub scheduler_turn: Option<u64>,
11058    pub virtual_nanoseconds: Option<u64>,
11059    pub record: Option<u64>,
11060    pub syscall: Option<u64>,
11061    pub left_message: Option<String>,
11062    pub right_message: Option<String>,
11063}
11064
11065fn cell_divergence_position(attempts: &[AttemptResult]) -> DivergencePosition {
11066    let messages = attempts.iter().find(|attempt| {
11067        attempt.first_divergent_left_message.is_some()
11068            || attempt.first_divergent_right_message.is_some()
11069    });
11070    DivergencePosition {
11071        scheduler_turn: attempts
11072            .iter()
11073            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_scheduler_turn),
11074        virtual_nanoseconds: attempts
11075            .iter()
11076            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds),
11077        record: attempts
11078            .iter()
11079            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_record),
11080        syscall: attempts
11081            .iter()
11082            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_syscall),
11083        left_message: messages.and_then(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_left_message.clone()),
11084        right_message: messages.and_then(|attempt| attempt.first_divergent_right_message.clone()),
11085    }
11086}
11087
11088/// Whether a row's SaBRe execution-path evidence
11089/// ([`summarize_sabre_path_evidence`]) shows that its run did not stay on
11090/// SaBRe's own path: the evidence is incomplete, or the run used fallback or
11091/// native sites. A row with no such evidence, which is every row of another
11092/// backend, is not ineligible. The runner fails a `PASS` whose evidence is
11093/// ineligible, and the parity post-pass does not score such a row from its
11094/// log (`parity::evaluate_history`).
11095pub(crate) fn execution_path_ineligible(execution_path: Option<&JsonValue>) -> bool {
11096    execution_path.is_some_and(|evidence| evidence["eligible"] != true)
11097}
11098
11099/// Whether a Hermit command line selects the SaBRe backend, the executions
11100/// that write SaBRe execution-path evidence.
11101///
11102/// Only Hermit's own arguments select a backend. The executor writes the
11103/// guest command after the first `--` (`verified_invocation_argv`, the
11104/// `custom` mode), so a `--backend sabre` pair there is an argument of the
11105/// guest, not a backend selection, and a ptrace run whose guest takes it
11106/// writes no SaBRe evidence.
11107fn argv_selects_sabre(argv: &[String]) -> bool {
11108    let hermit_args = argv
11109        .iter()
11110        .position(|arg| arg == "--")
11111        .map_or(argv, |separator| &argv[..separator]);
11112    hermit_args
11113        .windows(2)
11114        .any(|window| window[0] == "--backend" && window[1] == "sabre")
11115}
11116
11117fn attempt_selects_sabre(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> bool {
11118    let Some(binding) = &attempt.command_binding else {
11119        return argv_selects_sabre(&attempt.argv);
11120    };
11121    binding.backend == "sabre"
11122        && crate::executable_binding::selector_argv(&attempt.argv, &attempt.guest_argv, binding)
11123            .is_ok_and(|argv| argv_selects_sabre(&argv))
11124}
11125
11126/// Why `result`'s recorded execution path is not the eligible one its own
11127/// retained attempts decide, if it is not.
11128///
11129/// The runner summarizes a row's SaBRe execution-path evidence from the
11130/// evidence files its attempts wrote (`summarize_sabre_path_evidence`) and
11131/// fails a `PASS` whose summary is ineligible. A retained row carries the
11132/// summary as a label beside each attempt's retained evidence text and the
11133/// digest of the bytes the runner read, so a reader admitting such a row
11134/// re-decides the summary instead of trusting the label: every attempt
11135/// selects SaBRe exactly when the row's backend is `sabre`, every attempt's
11136/// retained evidence text is the bytes its `sabre_path_evidence_sha256`
11137/// names (both absent for an attempt that wrote none), and the summary of
11138/// those retained attempts is valid, equals the row's `execution_path`, and
11139/// is eligible (`execution_path_ineligible` is false). A row of another
11140/// backend therefore has no evidence and no `execution_path`.
11141pub fn retained_execution_path_error(result: &CellResult) -> Option<String> {
11142    if let Some(error) = retained_path_evidence_error(result) {
11143        return Some(error);
11144    }
11145    execution_path_ineligible(result.execution_path.as_ref()).then(|| {
11146        "the row's SaBRe execution path is incomplete or used fallback/native sites".into()
11147    })
11148}
11149
11150/// Why `result`'s retained SaBRe path evidence is not the evidence the
11151/// executor summarized into its recorded `execution_path`, if it is not:
11152/// [`retained_execution_path_error`] without its eligibility check.
11153///
11154/// The executor summarizes every row's evidence
11155/// (`summarize_sabre_path_evidence`), whatever its outcome, makes a row whose
11156/// evidence does not summarize an `invalid-backend-evidence` `ERROR`, and
11157/// records the summary as the row's execution path; it judges the path's
11158/// eligibility only on a `PASS`. So a non-`PASS` row this finds an error in
11159/// is not one the executor wrote, while one with an ineligible path may be.
11160fn retained_path_evidence_error(result: &CellResult) -> Option<String> {
11161    let sabre = result.backend.as_deref() == Some("sabre");
11162    for attempt in &result.attempts {
11163        let index = attempt.index.as_str();
11164        if attempt_selects_sabre(attempt) != sabre {
11165            return Some(format!(
11166                "inner attempt {index}'s command line does not select the row's backend {:?}",
11167                result.backend
11168            ));
11169        }
11170        if attempt.sabre_path_evidence_sha256
11171            != attempt
11172                .sabre_path_evidence
11173                .as_deref()
11174                .map(|text| hex_digest(text.as_bytes()))
11175        {
11176            return Some(format!(
11177                "inner attempt {index}'s retained SaBRe path evidence is not the bytes its sabre_path_evidence_sha256 names"
11178            ));
11179        }
11180    }
11181    let summary = match summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&result.attempts) {
11182        Ok(summary) => summary,
11183        Err(error) => return Some(error),
11184    };
11185    (summary != result.execution_path).then(|| {
11186        "the row's execution_path is not the summary of its retained SaBRe path evidence".into()
11187    })
11188}
11189
11190pub(crate) fn summarize_sabre_path_evidence(
11191    attempts: &[AttemptResult],
11192) -> Result<Option<JsonValue>, String> {
11193    let is_sabre = attempts.iter().any(attempt_selects_sabre);
11194    if !is_sabre {
11195        return Ok(None);
11196    }
11197    let mut executions = Vec::<PathEvidence>::new();
11198    for line in attempts
11199        .iter()
11200        .flat_map(|attempt| attempt.sabre_path_evidence.as_deref().unwrap_or("").lines())
11201    {
11202        let value = serde_json::from_str::<JsonValue>(line)
11203            .map_err(|error| format!("invalid SaBRe path-evidence record: {error}"))?;
11204        if value.get("schema").and_then(JsonValue::as_u64) != Some(u64::from(PathEvidence::SCHEMA))
11205        {
11206            return Err(format!(
11207                "invalid SaBRe path-evidence record: schema must be {}",
11208                PathEvidence::SCHEMA
11209            ));
11210        }
11211        executions.push(
11212            serde_json::from_value::<PathEvidence>(value)
11213                .map_err(|error| format!("invalid SaBRe path-evidence record: {error}"))?,
11214        );
11215    }
11216    let expected = attempts
11217        .iter()
11218        // A parity cell carries a ptrace reference attempt beside the SaBRe
11219        // candidate. Only executions which actually selected SaBRe can emit
11220        // SaBRe path evidence; counting the ptrace operand would turn every
11221        // otherwise-valid SaBRe parity measurement into an incomplete path.
11222        .filter(|attempt| attempt_selects_sabre(attempt))
11223        .map(|attempt| {
11224            if attempt
11225                .argv
11226                .iter()
11227                .any(|arg| arg == "--verify" || arg == "--verify-run")
11228            {
11229                2
11230            } else {
11231                1
11232            }
11233        })
11234        .sum::<usize>();
11235    let complete = executions.len() == expected;
11236    let mut guest_rpc_observed = complete;
11237    let mut ptrace_fallback_sites = 0usize;
11238    let mut trusted_shared_object_sites = 0usize;
11239    let mut trusted_shared_objects = BTreeSet::new();
11240    for row in &executions {
11241        // Keep this pattern exhaustive. Adding a producer field must stop this
11242        // consumer at compile time until its meaning is handled here.
11243        let PathEvidence {
11244            schema,
11245            guest_rpc_observed: observed,
11246            ptrace_fallback_sites: fallback_sites,
11247            trusted_shared_object_sites: shared_object_sites,
11248            trusted_shared_objects: shared_objects,
11249        } = row;
11250        if *schema != PathEvidence::SCHEMA {
11251            return Err(format!(
11252                "invalid SaBRe path-evidence record: schema must be {}",
11253                PathEvidence::SCHEMA
11254            ));
11255        }
11256        guest_rpc_observed &= *observed;
11257        ptrace_fallback_sites += *fallback_sites;
11258        trusted_shared_object_sites += *shared_object_sites;
11259        trusted_shared_objects.extend(shared_objects.iter().cloned());
11260    }
11261    let eligible = complete
11262        && guest_rpc_observed
11263        && ptrace_fallback_sites == 0
11264        && trusted_shared_object_sites == 0;
11265    Ok(Some(serde_json::json!({
11266        "schema": 1,
11267        "expected_execution_count": expected,
11268        "complete": complete,
11269        "execution_count": executions.len(),
11270        "guest_rpc_observed": guest_rpc_observed,
11271        "ptrace_fallback_sites": ptrace_fallback_sites,
11272        "trusted_shared_object_sites": trusted_shared_object_sites,
11273        "trusted_shared_objects": trusted_shared_objects,
11274        "eligible": eligible,
11275        "executions": executions
11276    })))
11277}
11278
11279fn diversity_evidence(
11280    hashes: &[String],
11281    outcome_classes: Option<u64>,
11282    min_distinct: u64,
11283    min_normalized_entropy: Option<f64>,
11284) -> JsonValue {
11285    let mut counts = BTreeMap::<&str, u64>::new();
11286    for hash in hashes {
11287        *counts.entry(hash).or_default() += 1;
11288    }
11289    let total = hashes.len() as f64;
11290    let entropy_bits = counts.values().fold(0.0, |entropy, count| {
11291        let share = *count as f64 / total.max(1.0);
11292        if share > 0.0 {
11293            entropy - share * share.log2()
11294        } else {
11295            entropy
11296        }
11297    });
11298    let normalized_entropy = outcome_classes
11299        .filter(|classes| *classes >= 2)
11300        .map(|classes| entropy_bits / (classes as f64).log2())
11301        .unwrap_or(0.0);
11302    let minority_share = counts
11303        .values()
11304        .min()
11305        .map(|count| *count as f64 / total.max(1.0))
11306        .unwrap_or(0.0);
11307    let histogram = counts
11308        .iter()
11309        .map(|(hash, count)| format!("{}:{count}", &hash[..hash.len().min(12)]))
11310        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
11311    serde_json::json!({
11312        "distinct": counts.len(), "outcome_classes": outcome_classes, "seeds": hashes.len(),
11313        "entropy_bits": entropy_bits, "normalized_entropy": normalized_entropy,
11314        "minority_share": minority_share,
11315        "oracle_saturated": outcome_classes.is_some_and(|classes| min_distinct >= classes),
11316        "class_histogram": histogram,
11317        "min_normalized_entropy": min_normalized_entropy,
11318    })
11319}

11321pub fn prepare_result_path(path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
11322    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
11323        fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11324    }
11325    OpenOptions::new()
11326        .create(true)
11327        .append(true)
11328        .open(path)
11329        .map(|_| ())
11330        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
11331}
11332
11333pub fn append_result(path: &Path, result: &CellResult) -> Result<(), String> {
11334    result.require_current_classification()?;
11335    result.require_current_timeout_policy()?;
11336    result.require_cpu_observations()?;
11337    // A missing prerequisite means the cell did not execute. Keep the typed
11338    // value for the harness summary and JUnit skip, but do not publish a cell
11339    // row that downstream readers could count as an observation. The validate
11340    // record names the withheld node and prerequisite separately.
11341    if result.outcome == "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" {
11342        return Ok(());
11343    }
11344    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
11345        fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11346    }
11347    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
11348        .create(true)
11349        .append(true)
11350        .open(path)
11351        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11352    // Serialize the row in memory and append it, newline included, in one
11353    // write. Serializing straight into the unbuffered file made one write(2)
11354    // per JSON token, about 2,000 for each row.
11355    let mut row = serde_json::to_vec(result).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11356    row.push(b'\n');
11357    file.write_all(&row).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11358    // The bucket runner publishes each completed cell before printing its
11359    // PASS/FAIL/ERROR line. Flush the row now rather than waiting for the
11360    // bucket's JUnit/summary epilogue, which an outer node timeout may kill.
11361    file.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
11362}
11363
11364pub fn write_junit(path: &Path, results: &[CellResult]) -> Result<(), String> {
11365    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
11366        fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11367    }
11368    let failures = results
11369        .iter()
11370        .filter(|result| result.outcome == "FAIL")
11371        .count();
11372    let errors = results
11373        .iter()
11374        .filter(|result| result.outcome == "ERROR")
11375        .count();
11376    let skipped = results
11377        .iter()
11378        .filter(|result| result.outcome == "HOST-INAPPLICABLE")
11379        .count();
11380    let mut out = format!(
11381        "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<testsuite name=\"hermit-e2e\" tests=\"{}\" failures=\"{failures}\" errors=\"{errors}\" skipped=\"{skipped}\">\n",
11382        results.len()
11383    );
11384    for result in results {
11385        let time = result
11386            .duration_ms
11387            .map(|duration_ms| format!(" time=\"{:.3}\"", duration_ms as f64 / 1000.0))
11388            .unwrap_or_default();
11389        out.push_str(&format!(
11390            "  <testcase classname=\"{}\" name=\"{}/{}/{}\"{}>",
11391            xml(&result.category),
11392            xml(&result.test),
11393            xml(&result.mode),
11394            xml(result.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("none")),
11395            time,
11396        ));
11397        if result.outcome == "FAIL" {
11398            out.push_str(&format!(
11399                "<failure>{}</failure>",
11400                xml(result.reason_for_display())
11401            ));
11402        }
11403        if result.outcome == "ERROR" {
11404            out.push_str(&format!(
11405                "<error>{}</error>",
11406                xml(result.reason_for_display())
11407            ));
11408        }
11409        if result.outcome == "HOST-INAPPLICABLE" {
11410            out.push_str(&format!(
11411                "<skipped message=\"{}\"/>",
11412                xml(result.reason_for_display())
11413            ));
11414        }
11415        out.push_str("</testcase>\n");
11416    }
11417    out.push_str("</testsuite>\n");
11418    fs::write(path, out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
11419}

11421fn prepare_dirs(root: &Path, dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
11422    for child in ["home", "xdg-config", "tmp", "fixtures", "captures"] {
11423        fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(child)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11424    }
11425    let xdg = root.join("tests/e2e/xdg-config");
11426    if xdg.is_dir() {
11427        copy_tree(&xdg, &dir.join("xdg-config"))?;
11428    }
11429    Ok(())
11430}
11431
11432fn copy_tree(source: &Path, destination: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
11433    fs::create_dir_all(destination).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11434    for entry in fs::read_dir(source).map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
11435        let entry = entry.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11436        let target = destination.join(entry.file_name());
11437        if entry.file_type().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_dir() {
11438            copy_tree(&entry.path(), &target)?;
11439        } else {
11440            // A prebuilt `fixtures/program` runs as soon as preparation
11441            // returns, so it must not be copied in-process (ETXTBSY).
11442            crate::exec_safe_fs::copy(entry.path(), target).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
11443        }
11444    }
11445    Ok(())
11446}

11488fn preparation_env(dir: &Path) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
11489    let mut env = cell_env(dir, false);
11490    let ambient_home = std::env::var_os("HOME");
11491    let rustup_home = std::env::var_os("RUSTUP_HOME");
11492    let cargo_home = std::env::var_os("CARGO_HOME");
11493    add_toolchain_homes(
11494        &mut env,
11495        rustup_home.as_deref(),
11496        cargo_home.as_deref(),
11497        ambient_home.as_deref(),
11498    );
11499    env

11501
11502fn add_toolchain_homes(
11503    env: &mut BTreeMap<String, String>,
11504    rustup_home: Option<&OsStr>,
11505    cargo_home: Option<&OsStr>,
11506    ambient_home: Option<&OsStr>,
11507) {
11508    // Guest preparation is a build-time context, not guest execution. Preserve
11509    // the invoking toolchain state even though the cell's HOME is isolated;
11510    // these values are deliberately absent from `cell_env` and never become
11511    // Hermit `--env` arguments.
11512    for (name, explicit, fallback) in [
11513        ("RUSTUP_HOME", rustup_home, ".rustup"),
11514        ("CARGO_HOME", cargo_home, ".cargo"),
11515    ] {
11516        let value = explicit
11517            .map(PathBuf::from)
11518            .or_else(|| ambient_home.map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join(fallback)));
11519        if let Some(value) = value {
11520            env.insert(name.into(), value.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
11521        }
11522    }
11523}
11524
11525/// Render recorded command fields without executing or expanding their contents.
11526pub fn shell_command(cwd: &str, env: &BTreeMap<String, String>, argv: &[String]) -> String {
11527    let mut words = vec!["cd".into(), shell_quote(cwd), "&&".into(), "env".into()];
11528    words.extend(
11529        env.iter()
11530            .map(|(name, value)| shell_quote(&format!("{name}={value}"))),
11531    );
11532    words.extend(argv.iter().map(|arg| shell_quote(arg)));
11533    words.join(" ")
11534}
11535
11536fn shell_quote(value: &str) -> String {
11537    if !value.is_empty()
11538        && value
11539            .bytes()
11540            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_@%+=:,./-".contains(&byte))
11541    {
11542        value.into()
11543    } else {
11544        format!("'{}'", value.replace('\'', "'\"'\"'"))
11545    }
11546}
11547
11548/// The guest environment the runner forwards to every Hermit cell. A
11549/// manifest's `env` may add variables but never set one of these.
11550const RUNNER_GUEST_ENV: [&str; 7] = [
11551    "LC_ALL",
11552    "TZ",
11553    "HOME",
11554    "XDG_CONFIG_HOME",
11555    "E2E_TMPDIR",
11556    "E2E_FIXTURE_DIR",
11557    SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENV,
11558];
11559
11560/// The Hermit `run` flags a manifest's `hermit_args` may add: exactly those a
11561/// recorded test policy needs. Each relaxes determinism; an entry ending in `=`
11562/// takes a value.
11563const ALLOWED_HERMIT_ARGS: &[&str] = &["--no-virtualize-cpuid", "--max-timeslice="];
11564
11565/// Whether `arg` is one of [`ALLOWED_HERMIT_ARGS`]: one of its exact flags,
11566/// or one of its valued flags with a nonempty value.
11567fn allowed_hermit_arg(arg: &str) -> bool {
11568    ALLOWED_HERMIT_ARGS
11569        .iter()
11570        .any(|flag| match flag.strip_suffix('=') {
11571            Some(_) => arg
11572                .strip_prefix(flag)
11573                .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty()),
11574            None => arg == *flag,
11575        })
11576}
11577
11578/// Validate a mode's `hermit_args`, `env` and `comparator`.
11579fn validate_mode_extensions(id: &str, mode: &str, recipe: &ModeRecipe) -> Result<(), String> {
11580    let extends = !recipe.hermit_args.is_empty()
11581        || recipe.hermit_args_reason.is_some()
11582        || recipe.comparator.is_some()
11583        || recipe.comparator_reason.is_some()
11584        || !recipe.diagnostic.is_empty()
11585        || recipe.no_retry_reason.is_some()
11586        || recipe.max_level.is_some()
11587        || recipe.max_level_reason.is_some();
11588    if extends && mode != "verify" {
11589        return Err(format!(
11590            "{id}: {mode} declares hermit_args, comparator, diagnostic, no_retry_reason or max_level, which only a verify mode accepts"
11591        ));
11592    }
11593    match (recipe.max_level, recipe.max_level_reason.as_deref()) {
11594        (None, None) => {}
11595        (Some(StrictnessLevel::Relaxed), Some(reason)) if !reason.trim().is_empty() => {
11596            if !recipe
11597                .backends_enabled
11598                .iter()
11599                .any(|backend| pmu_clock_backend(backend))
11600            {
11601                return Err(format!(
11602                    "{id}: max_level caps a ptrace or e9patch cell, and this verify mode enables neither"
11603                ));
11604            }
11605        }
11606        (Some(StrictnessLevel::Strict), _) => {
11607            return Err(format!(
11608                "{id}: max_level: strict is every cell's default; only `relaxed` caps a cell"
11609            ));
11610        }
11611        (Some(StrictnessLevel::Relaxed), _) => {
11612            return Err(format!(
11613                "{id}: max_level: relaxed requires a substantive max_level_reason"
11614            ));
11615        }
11616        (None, Some(_)) => {
11617            return Err(format!("{id}: max_level_reason without max_level"));
11618        }
11619    }
11620    // A replay cell records and replays the program its verify cell checks,
11621    // so it may restate that program's environment (see [`cell_mode_env`]);
11622    // no other mode passes a declared environment to its guest.
11623    if recipe.env.is_some() && !matches!(mode, "verify" | "replay") {
11624        return Err(format!(
11625            "{id}: {mode} declares env, which only a verify or replay mode accepts"
11626        ));
11627    }
11628    if !recipe.env_by_backend.is_empty() && mode != "verify" {
11629        return Err(format!(
11630            "{id}: {mode} declares env_by_backend, which only a verify mode accepts"
11631        ));
11632    }
11633    if recipe
11634        .no_retry_reason
11635        .as_deref()
11636        .is_some_and(|reason| reason.trim().is_empty())
11637    {
11638        return Err(format!("{id}: no_retry_reason must be substantive"));
11639    }
11640    for (backend, args) in &recipe.hermit_args {
11641        if !recipe.backends_enabled.contains(backend) {
11642            return Err(format!(
11643                "{id}: hermit_args names backend `{backend}`, which is not in backends_enabled"
11644            ));
11645        }
11646        if args.is_empty() {
11647            return Err(format!("{id}: hermit_args for `{backend}` is empty"));
11648        }
11649        // Each flag at most once. An exact repeat would repeat a relaxation
11650        // identity, which the scorecard refuses; two values for one flag would
11651        // leave the effective configuration to Hermit's argument order.
11652        let mut seen_flags = BTreeSet::new();
11653        for arg in args {
11654            let flag = arg.split_once('=').map_or(arg.as_str(), |(flag, _)| flag);
11655            if !seen_flags.insert(flag) {
11656                return Err(format!("{id}: hermit_args repeats `{flag}`"));
11657            }
11658        }
11659    }
11660    for arg in recipe.hermit_args.values().flatten() {
11661        if !allowed_hermit_arg(arg) {
11662            return Err(format!(
11663                "{id}: hermit_args entry `{arg}` is not one of {ALLOWED_HERMIT_ARGS:?}"
11664            ));
11665        }
11666        // A value hermit refuses would fail every run of the cell, and the
11667        // harness reads the cell's timeslice from this value.
11668        if let Some(value) = arg.strip_prefix("--max-timeslice=") {
11669            MaxTimeslice::parse(value)
11670                .map_err(|error| format!("{id}: hermit_args entry `{arg}`: {error}"))?;
11671        }
11672    }
11673    match (recipe.hermit_args.is_empty(), &recipe.hermit_args_reason) {
11674        (true, None) => {}
11675        (false, Some(HermitArgsReason::Shared(reason))) if !reason.trim().is_empty() => {}
11676        // One reason per backend with flags, and none for a backend without.
11677        (false, Some(HermitArgsReason::PerBackend(reasons))) => {
11678            if !reasons.keys().eq(recipe.hermit_args.keys()) {
11679                return Err(format!(
11680                    "{id}: a per-backend hermit_args_reason must name exactly the backends of hermit_args"
11681                ));
11682            }
11683            if reasons.values().any(|reason| reason.trim().is_empty()) {
11684                return Err(format!(
11685                    "{id}: hermit_args relax determinism and require a substantive hermit_args_reason"
11686                ));
11687            }
11688        }
11689        (false, _) => {
11690            return Err(format!(
11691                "{id}: hermit_args relax determinism and require a substantive hermit_args_reason"
11692            ));
11693        }
11694        (true, Some(_)) => {
11695            return Err(format!("{id}: hermit_args_reason without hermit_args"));
11696        }
11697    }
11698    for (backend, env) in &recipe.env_by_backend {
11699        if !recipe.backends_enabled.contains(backend) {
11700            return Err(format!(
11701                "{id}: env_by_backend names backend `{backend}`, which is not in backends_enabled"
11702            ));
11703        }
11704        if env.is_empty() {
11705            return Err(format!("{id}: env_by_backend for `{backend}` is empty"));
11706        }
11707        if let Some(name) = env.keys().find(|name| {
11708            recipe
11709                .env
11710                .as_ref()
11711                .is_some_and(|common| common.contains_key(*name))
11712        }) {
11713            return Err(format!(
11714                "{id}: env_by_backend for `{backend}` repeats common env name `{name}`"
11715            ));
11716        }
11717    }
11718    for (name, value) in recipe
11719        .env
11720        .iter()
11721        .flatten()
11722        .chain(recipe.env_by_backend.values().flatten())
11723    {
11724        let well_formed = name
11725            .chars()
11726            .next()
11727            .is_some_and(|first| first.is_ascii_uppercase() || first == '_')
11728            && name
11729                .chars()
11730                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '_');
11731        if !well_formed || value.contains('\0') {
11732            return Err(format!(
11733                "{id}: env entry `{name}` is not a valid NAME=VALUE"
11734            ));
11735        }
11736        if RUNNER_GUEST_ENV.contains(&name.as_str()) {
11737            return Err(format!(
11738                "{id}: env entry `{name}` is a variable the runner sets itself"
11739            ));
11740        }
11741    }
11742    let stripped = recipe.comparator == Some(Comparator::Stripped);
11743    match (stripped, recipe.comparator_reason.as_deref().map(str::trim)) {
11744        (false, None) => {}
11745        (true, Some(reason)) if !reason.is_empty() => {}
11746        (true, _) => {
11747            return Err(format!(
11748                "{id}: comparator stripped is below L2 and requires a substantive comparator_reason"
11749            ));
11750        }
11751        (false, Some(_)) => {
11752            return Err(format!(
11753                "{id}: comparator_reason without comparator stripped"
11754            ));
11755        }
11756    }
11757    if stripped
11758        && recipe
11759            .assert
11760            .as_ref()
11761            .and_then(|assert| assert.bitwise_parity)
11762            == Some(true)
11763    {
11764        return Err(format!(
11765            "{id}: comparator stripped cannot establish the bitwise_parity it asserts"
11766        ));
11767    }
11768    for (backend, labels) in &recipe.labels {
11769        if !recipe.backends_enabled.contains(backend) {
11770            return Err(format!(
11771                "{id}: {mode} labels name backend `{backend}`, which is not in backends_enabled"
11772            ));
11773        }
11774        if labels.is_empty() {
11775            return Err(format!("{id}: {mode} labels for `{backend}` are empty"));
11776        }
11777        validate_labels(&format!("{id}: {mode} on {backend}"), labels)?;
11778    }
11779    for (backend, reason) in &recipe.diagnostic {
11780        if !stripped {
11781            return Err(format!(
11782                "{id}: diagnostic is only for comparator stripped cells; a canonical cell's failure must fail the run"
11783            ));
11784        }
11785        if !recipe.backends_enabled.contains(backend) {
11786            return Err(format!(
11787                "{id}: diagnostic names backend `{backend}`, which is not in backends_enabled"
11788            ));
11789        }
11790        if reason.trim().is_empty() || reason.trim() != reason {
11791            return Err(format!(
11792                "{id}: diagnostic on `{backend}` requires a substantive, trimmed reason"
11793            ));
11794        }
11795    }
11796    // A custom cell's arguments reach `hermit run` as written. Timeslice
11797    // arguments hermit would refuse fail every run of the cell, and the
11798    // harness decides admission on the timeslice it resolves from them
11799    // ([`refused_on_an_inexact_branch_counter`]), so they are refused here.
11800    if mode == "custom" {
11801        MaxTimeslice::from_options(&recipe.args)
11802            .map_err(|error| format!("{id}: custom args: {error}"))?;
11803    }
11804    Ok(())
11805}

11807fn validate_tier_marker(id: &str, bucket: &str, labels: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
11808    let label_set: BTreeSet<&str> = labels.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
11809    let tier = CellTier::from_labels(&label_set).map_err(|error| format!("{id}: {error}"))?;
11810    if tier.is_none() && TIERED_BUCKETS.contains(&bucket) {
11811        return Err(format!(
11812            "{id}: bucket `{bucket}` requires exactly one tier label, `{SUPER_RUN_TYPE}` or `{PRESSURE_RUN_TYPE}`"
11813        ));
11814    }
11815    Ok(())
11816}
11817
11818/// Validate a test's run-type labels: lowercase words joined by `-`, unique.
11819fn validate_labels(id: &str, labels: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
11820    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
11821    for label in labels {
11822        let well_formed = !label.is_empty()
11823            && label.split('-').all(|word| {
11824                !word.is_empty()
11825                    && word
11826                        .chars()
11827                        .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit())
11828            });
11829        if !well_formed {
11830            return Err(format!(
11831                "{id}: label `{label}` is not lowercase-words-with-dashes"
11832            ));
11833        }
11834        if !seen.insert(label.as_str()) {
11835            return Err(format!("{id}: label `{label}` is repeated"));
11836        }
11837    }
11838    Ok(())
11839}

11841fn append_guest_env_args(
11842    argv: &mut Vec<String>,
11843    env: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
11844    uses_test_workdir: bool,
11845) {
11846    // Every forwarded value is harness-authored, never inherited ambient state.
11847    // PWD and OLDPWD remain absent; E2E_TMPDIR joins the fresh /test mount while
11848    // HOME/XDG retain their unique per-cell directories and seeded config.
11849    for name in RUNNER_GUEST_ENV {
11850        let value = if uses_test_workdir && name == "E2E_TMPDIR" {
11851            HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR
11852        } else {
11853            env.get(name)
11854                .expect("cell environment contains every forwarded guest value")
11855        };
11856        argv.push("--env".into());
11857        argv.push(format!("{name}={value}"));
11858    }
11859}

11861fn append_scheduled_jobs_env_arg(argv: &mut Vec<String>, env: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
11862    let value = env
11863        .get(SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENV)
11864        .expect("cell environment contains scheduled worker capacity");
11865    argv.push("--env".into());
11866    argv.push(format!("{SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENV}={value}"));
11867}

11869fn require_minimal_base_env(argv: &mut Vec<String>) -> Result<(), String> {
11870    let mut values = Vec::new();
11871    let mut index = 0;
11872    while index < argv.len() {
11873        if let Some(value) = argv[index].strip_prefix("--base-env=") {
11874            values.push(value.to_owned());
11875        } else if argv[index] == "--base-env" {
11876            index += 1;
11877            let value = argv.get(index).ok_or_else(|| {
11878                "hermetic validation received --base-env without a value".to_string()
11879            })?;
11880            values.push(value.clone());
11881        }
11882        index += 1;
11883    }
11884    match values.as_slice() {
11885        [] => argv.push("--base-env=minimal".into()),
11886        [value] if value == "minimal" => {}
11887        [value] => {
11888            return Err(format!(
11889                "hermetic validation requires --base-env=minimal, got {value}"
11890            ));
11891        }
11892        _ => return Err("hermetic validation received repeated --base-env flags".into()),
11893    }
11894    Ok(())
11895}
11896
11897/// Choose the guest's working directory. Three sources, in this order, and the
11898/// ORDER IS THE POINT.
11899///
11900///   1. `isolated_workdir` — the hermetic lane's fresh tmpfs at `/test`, enabled by
11901///      `HERMIT_E2E_EMPTY_WORKDIR` from `ci/hermetic/run-split-validate.sh`.
11902///   2. `requested_workdir` — a workdir the manifest names for itself.
11903///   3. `fixed_workdir_source` — the ordinary-host fallback binds a fresh
11904///      per-attempt directory at `/tmp/test`.
11905fn append_execution_root_args(
11906    argv: &mut Vec<String>,
11907    backend: &str,
11908    isolated_workdir: Option<&Path>,
11909    requested_workdir: Option<&str>,
11910    fixed_workdir_source: Option<&Path>,
11911) {
11912    if let Some(workdir) = isolated_workdir {
11913        // The marked DBT adapter establishes a fresh namespace and /test tmpfs
11914        // for each physical execution before constructing its runtime. It still
11915        // refuses the general --mount CLI surface, so pass only the workdir.
11916        // Other backends create their per-invocation tmpfs from this argument.
11917        if backend != "dbt" {
11918            argv.push(format!("--mount=type=tmpfs,target={}", workdir.display()));
11919        }
11920        argv.extend(["--workdir".into(), workdir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]);
11921    } else if let Some(workdir) = requested_workdir {
11922        // Outside the explicit hermetic path, a manifest that names its own
11923        // workdir keeps it and outranks the ordinary-host fallback.
11924        argv.extend(["--workdir".into(), workdir.into()]);
11925    } else if let Some(source) = fixed_workdir_source {
11926        argv.push(format!(
11927            "--bind={}:{FIXED_GUEST_WORKDIR}",
11928            source.to_string_lossy()
11929        ));
11930        argv.extend(["--workdir".into(), FIXED_GUEST_WORKDIR.into()]);
11931    }
11932}

11934fn observation_hash(observation: &Observation, attempt: &AttemptResult, dir: &Path) -> String {
11935    observation_hash_bytes(
11936        observation,
11937        attempt,
11938        dir,
11939        attempt.stdout.as_bytes(),
11940        attempt.stderr.as_bytes(),
11941    )
11942}
11943
11944fn observation_hash_bytes(
11945    observation: &Observation,
11946    attempt: &AttemptResult,
11947    dir: &Path,
11948    stdout: &[u8],
11949    stderr: &[u8],
11950) -> String {
11951    let mut digest = Sha256::new();
11952    if observation.status {
11953        digest.update(attempt.status.unwrap_or(-1).to_le_bytes());
11954        digest.update(attempt.signal.unwrap_or(0).to_le_bytes());
11955    }
11956    if observation.stdout {
11957        digest.update(stdout);
11958    }
11959    if observation.stderr {
11960        digest.update(stderr);
11961    }
11962    for artifact in &observation.artifacts {
11963        if let Ok(bytes) = fs::read(dir.join("tmp").join(artifact)) {
11964            digest.update(bytes);
11965        }
11966    }
11967    format!("{:x}", digest.finalize())
11968}

11970pub fn test_digest(root: &Path, test: &TestRecipe) -> Result<String, String> {
11971    let bytes = if let Some(program) = &test.program {
11972        fs::read(root.join(program)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
11973    } else {
11974        serde_json::to_vec(&test.direct.as_ref().map(|direct| match direct {
11975            DirectCommand::Shell(s) => vec![s.clone()],
11976            DirectCommand::Argv(v) => v.clone(),
11977        }))
11978        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
11979    };
11980    Ok(hex_digest(&bytes))
11981}

11983fn hex_digest(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
11984    format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(bytes))

11994fn git(root: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String, String> {
11995    let output = Command::new("git")
11996        .arg("-C")
11997        .arg(root)
11998        .args(args)
11999        .output()
12000        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
12001    if !output.status.success() {
12002        return Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string());
12003    }
12004    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
12005}

12007/// The binary's `exact_branch_counter` verdict, or `None` (with a note on
12008/// stderr) when it cannot be read. `None` withholds no cell: a binary that
12009/// then refuses `--strict` fails its cells loudly instead. An import
12010/// confirms no producer's inexact-counter claim without a verdict.
12011fn probe_exact_branch_counter(program: &Path) -> Option<CapabilityVerdict> {
12012    let read = || -> Result<CapabilityVerdict, String> {
12013        let output = Command::new(program)
12014            .args(["host-capabilities", "--json"])
12015            .output()
12016            .map_err(|error| format!("cannot run it: {error}"))?;
12017        if !output.status.success() {
12018            return Err(format!("it exited {}", output.status));
12019        }
12020        parse_exact_branch_counter(&output.stdout)
12021    };
12022    read()
12023        .map_err(|error| {
12024            eprintln!(
12025                "test-harness: no exact_branch_counter verdict from `{} host-capabilities --json` \
12026                 ({error}); this machine is not taken to lack an exact branch counter",
12027                program.display()
12028            )
12029        })
12030        .ok()
12031}
12032
12033fn parse_exact_branch_counter(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<CapabilityVerdict, String> {
12034    let report = serde_json::from_slice::<HostCapabilitiesReport>(bytes)
12035        .map_err(|error| format!("unreadable report: {error}"))?;
12036    report.validate()?;
12037    Ok(report.exact_branch_counter)
12038}
12039
12040/// Ask the hermit binary which commit it was built from.
12041///
12042/// The producer-owned `version --json` record is the authority. Human-readable
12043/// `--version` output is presentation and must not be parsed into provenance.
12044/// `None` means the binary could not be run, refused the current schema, or
12045/// returned an invalid revision; it is deliberately distinct from any value.
12046fn probe_binary_build_sha(program: &Path) -> Option<String> {
12047    let output = Command::new(program)
12048        .args(["version", "--json"])
12049        .output()
12050        .ok()?;
12051    if !output.status.success() {
12052        return None;
12053    }
12054    parse_binary_build_info(&output.stdout)
12055}
12056
12057fn parse_binary_build_info(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
12058    let report = serde_json::from_slice::<detcore_model::build_info::BuildInfo>(bytes).ok()?;
12059    if report.schema != detcore_model::build_info::BuildInfo::SCHEMA {
12060        return None;
12061    }
12062    let sha = report.git_sha;
12063    let hex = sha.strip_suffix("-dirty").unwrap_or(&sha);
12064    let recognised =
12065        hex == "unknown" || (hex.len() >= 7 && hex.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()));
12066    recognised.then_some(sha)
12067}
12068
12069/// Whether `program args` advertises `needle` in its help output.
12070///
12071/// This decides which verification spelling the harness passes. The previous
12072/// implementation collapsed three distinct outcomes into one `bool`: the
12073/// needle is absent, the binary could not be launched, and the binary exited
12074/// non-zero all returned `false`. `false` means `--verify-strict` is omitted,
12075/// and on a pre-cutover Hermit bare `--verify` is not strict -- so a probe
12076/// that merely FAILED silently ran the whole suite with weaker verification
12077/// than intended, and every cell still passed. The failure mode produced the
12078/// reassuring answer.
12079///
12080/// The split is by whether the binary will go on to run cells:
12081///
12082/// - The binary does not exist. Nothing will run, and every cell reports
12083///   `cannot execute <path>` exactly, so reporting absence here cannot weaken
12084///   a comparison that never happens. Answering `false` keeps that diagnosis
12085///   with the execution path that states it precisely.
12086/// - The binary exists but the probe did not answer -- it exited non-zero, or
12087///   could not be launched for any reason other than absence. Cells WILL run,
12088///   so guessing the weaker spelling here is exactly the silent downgrade.
12089///   Refuse instead.
12090fn command_help_contains(program: &Path, args: &[&str], needle: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
12091    let output = match Command::new(program).args(args).output() {
12092        Ok(output) => output,
12093        // The execution path reports an absent binary precisely; see above.
12094        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),
12095        Err(error) => {
12096            return Err(format!(
12097                "cannot launch {} {} to detect {needle} support: {error}; \
12098                 refusing to guess the verification spelling",
12099                program.display(),
12100                args.join(" ")
12101            ));
12102        }
12103    };
12104    if !output.status.success() {
12105        return Err(format!(
12106            "{} {} exited {} while detecting {needle} support; \
12107             refusing to guess the verification spelling",
12108            program.display(),
12109            args.join(" "),
12110            output
12111                .status
12112                .code()
12113                .map_or_else(|| "by signal".to_string(), |code| code.to_string()),
12114        ));
12115    }
12116    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).contains(needle)
12117        || String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).contains(needle))
12118}
