12120fn single_run_retained_path(spec: &CellRunSpec) -> PathBuf {
12121    spec.cell_dir
12122        .join("custom-capture/retained")
12123        .join(&spec.attempt)
12124}
12125
12126/// Move even incomplete evidence after process exit; never reuse an old record.
12127fn adopt_single_run(
12128    spec: &CellRunSpec,
12129    attempt: &mut AttemptResult,
12130) -> Result<crate::verify_run_record::RunOutput, String> {
12131    use crate::verify_run_record::RecordedStatus;
12132    use crate::verify_run_record::RunRole;
12133    use crate::verify_run_record::VerifyRunOutcome;
12134    use crate::verify_run_record::VerifyRunRecord;
12135
12136    let stage = spec.single_run_capture.as_ref().expect("capture requested");
12137    let retained = single_run_retained_path(spec);
12138    if retained.try_exists().map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
12139        return Err(format!("refusing stale capture {}", retained.display()));
12140    }
12141    fs::create_dir_all(retained.parent().expect("retained capture has parent"))
12142        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
12143    fs::rename(stage, &retained)
12144        .map_err(|e| format!("retaining custom capture {}: {e}", stage.display()))?;
12145    attempt.single_run_capture = Some(retained.display().to_string());
12146    let record = VerifyRunRecord::read(&retained)?;
12147    if record.backend != spec.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native")
12148        || record.role != RunRole::Run
12149        || record.comparison.strictness != crate::canonical_verdict::LogCompareStrictness::Canonical
12150    {
12151        return Err(
12152            "custom capture backend, role or canonical comparison does not match invocation".into(),
12153        );
12154    }
12155    // The CLI gives an explicit --epoch precedence over HERMIT_EPOCH and
12156    // serializes a DateTime. Compare instants, not Z versus +00:00 spelling.
12157    let args = spec
12158        .argv
12159        .iter()
12160        .take_while(|arg| arg.as_str() != "--")
12161        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
12162    let epoch = args
12163        .windows(2)
12164        .rev()
12165        .find(|pair| pair[0].as_str() == "--epoch")
12166        .map(|pair| pair[1].as_str())
12167        .or_else(|| {
12168            args.iter()
12169                .rev()
12170                .find_map(|arg| arg.strip_prefix("--epoch="))
12171        })
12172        .or_else(|| spec.env.get("HERMIT_EPOCH").map(String::as_str))
12173        .ok_or_else(|| "custom capture invocation has no explicit epoch".to_string())?;
12174    let parse_epoch = |value: &str| {
12175        chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(value)
12176            .map_err(|e| format!("invalid capture epoch {value:?}: {e}"))
12177    };
12178    if parse_epoch(&record.epoch)? != parse_epoch(epoch)? {
12179        return Err("custom capture epoch does not match invocation".into());
12180    }
12181    let VerifyRunOutcome::Completed { status, .. } = record.outcome else {
12182        return Err("custom capture has no completed guest outcome".into());
12183    };
12184    let reported_code = match status {
12185        RecordedStatus::Exited { code } if (0..=255).contains(&code) => code,
12186        RecordedStatus::Signaled { signal, .. } if (1..=64).contains(&signal) => 128 + signal,
12187        _ => return Err("custom capture contains an invalid guest wait status".into()),
12188    };
12189    if attempt.timed_out || attempt.signal.is_some() || attempt.status != Some(reported_code) {
12190        return Err("custom capture guest status disagrees with controller disposition".into());
12191    }
12192    // The full comparator later validates INFO, syscall buffers and backend
12193    // statistics. Adoption checks readable evidence, not an L2 verdict.
12194    let log = File::open(retained.join(crate::verify_run_record::LOG))
12195        .map_err(|e| format!("reading custom capture run.log: {e}"))?;
12196    if !log.metadata().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_file() {
12197        return Err("custom capture run.log is not a regular file".into());
12198    }
12199    crate::verify_run_record::read_output(&retained)
12200}
12201
12202fn capture_error(attempt: &mut AttemptResult, error: String) {
12203    // An output file can never turn a controller failure into a pass.
12204    if attempt.outcome == "PASS" {
12205        attempt.outcome = "ERROR".into();
12206        attempt.error_kind = Some("incomplete-custom-capture".into());
12207    }
12208    attempt.reason = Some(match attempt.reason.take() {
12209        Some(previous) => format!("{previous}; custom capture: {error}"),
12210        None => format!("custom capture: {error}"),
12211    });
12212}
12213
12214fn thread_cpu_usage_usec() -> Result<u64, String> {
12215    let mut usage = std::mem::MaybeUninit::<libc::rusage>::uninit();
12216    // RUSAGE_THREAD excludes children and other concurrently running cells.
12217    if unsafe { libc::getrusage(libc::RUSAGE_THREAD, usage.as_mut_ptr()) } != 0 {
12218        return Err(format!(
12219            "reading capture thread CPU: {}",
12220            std::io::Error::last_os_error()
12221        ));
12222    }
12223    rusage_cpu_usage_usec(&unsafe { usage.assume_init() })
12224}
12225
12226fn effective_execution_cpu(attempt: &AttemptResult) -> Result<u64, String> {
12227    // An unstarted timed-out child contributes zero. A requested capture needs
12228    // an actual adoption charge regardless of the child's prior outcome.
12229    let child_cpu = attempt
12230        .cpu_usage_usec
12231        .or_else(|| attempt.timed_out.then_some(0))
12232        .ok_or_else(|| "custom child CPU measurement is missing".to_string())?;
12233    let adoption_cpu = if attempt.capture_custom_runs {
12234        attempt
12235            .capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec
12236            .ok_or_else(|| "custom capture CPU measurement is missing".to_string())?
12237    } else {
12238        0
12239    };
12240    child_cpu
12241        .checked_add(adoption_cpu)
12242        .ok_or_else(|| "custom child plus capture CPU overflowed u64".into())
12243}
12244
12245fn finish_capture_budget(
12246    attempt: &mut AttemptResult,
12247    budget: &ExecutionBudget,
12248    charge: Result<u64, String>,
12249    finished: Instant,
12250) {
12251    match charge {
12252        Ok(charge) => attempt.capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec = Some(charge),
12253        Err(error) => {
12254            attempt.capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec = None;
12255            capture_error(attempt, error);
12256            return;
12257        }
12258    }
12259    let total = match effective_execution_cpu(attempt) {
12260        Ok(total) => total,
12261        Err(error) => {
12262            capture_error(attempt, error);
12263            return;
12264        }
12265    };
12266    let timeout = if finished >= budget.deadline {
12267        Some(ProcessTimeout::Wall)
12268    } else if budget
12269        .remaining_cpu_usec
12270        .is_some_and(|remaining| total >= remaining)
12271    {
12272        Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu)
12273    } else {
12274        None
12275    };
12276    if let Some(timeout) = timeout {
12277        attempt.capture_adoption_timeout = Some(
12278            match timeout {
12279                ProcessTimeout::Wall => "wall",
12280                ProcessTimeout::Cpu => "cpu",
12281            }
12282            .into(),
12283        );
12284        if attempt.outcome == "PASS" {
12285            attempt.outcome = "FAIL".into();
12286            attempt.error_kind = Some(timeout.error_kind().into());
12287        }
12288        let error = format!(
12289            "{} after custom capture adoption",
12290            timeout.reason(budget.cpu_timeout_seconds, budget.wall_timeout_seconds)
12291        );
12292        attempt.reason = Some(match attempt.reason.take() {
12293            Some(previous) => format!("{previous}; {error}"),
12294            None => error,
12295        });
12296    }
12297}
12298
12299fn execute_observed_until(
12300    spec: &CellRunSpec,
12301    observation: &Observation,
12302    dir: &Path,
12303    budget: ExecutionBudget,
12304    observations: &mut Vec<InvocationCpuObservation>,
12305) -> Result<AttemptResult, String> {
12306    let mut attempt = execute_spec_until(
12307        spec,
12308        budget.deadline,
12309        budget.cpu_timeout_seconds,
12310        budget.wall_timeout_seconds,
12311        budget.remaining_cpu_usec,
12312        observations,
12313    )?;
12314    if spec.single_run_capture.is_none() {
12315        attempt.observation_sha256 = Some(observation_hash(observation, &attempt, dir));
12316        return Ok(attempt);
12317    }
12318    let started = Instant::now();
12319    let before_cpu = thread_cpu_usage_usec();
12320    let adopted = adopt_single_run(spec, &mut attempt);
12321    match adopted {
12322        Ok(output) => {
12323            attempt.stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned();
12324            // Classifiers consume the controller's stderr. Guest stderr stays
12325            // in the retained capture and feeds the original raw observation.
12326            attempt.observation_sha256 = Some(observation_hash_bytes(
12327                observation,
12328                &attempt,
12329                dir,
12330                &output.stdout,
12331                &output.stderr,
12332            ));
12333        }
12334        Err(error) => capture_error(&mut attempt, error),
12335    }
12336    let charge = before_cpu.and_then(|before| {
12337        thread_cpu_usage_usec()?
12338            .checked_sub(before)
12339            .ok_or_else(|| "capture thread CPU moved backwards".into())
12340    });
12341    let finished = Instant::now();
12342    #[cfg(test)]
12343    let (charge, finished) =
12344        tests::capture_budget_test_measurement(&attempt, &budget, charge, finished);
12345    finish_capture_budget(&mut attempt, &budget, charge, finished);
12346    attempt.duration_ms += started.elapsed().as_millis();
12347    Ok(attempt)
12348}

12350#[cfg(test)]
12351mod tests {
12352    /// The session is the field after the process group, whatever bytes the
12353    /// command name holds.
12354    #[test]
12355    fn stat_session_reads_past_any_command_name() {
12356        assert_eq!(stat_session(b"42 (a) b) S 1 40 41 0"), Some(41));
12357        assert_eq!(stat_process_group(b"42 (a) b) S 1 40 41 0"), Some(40));
12358        assert_eq!(stat_session(b"42 (x"), None);
12359    }
12360
12361    /// A PID is suspect when the allocator passed it since the census was
12362    /// taken, including across a wrap, and every PID is once a lap may have
12363    /// been completed.
12364    #[test]
12365    fn the_census_drops_only_pids_the_allocator_may_have_reused() {
12366        let at = |last_pid, forks| PidAllocator {
12367            last_pid,
12368            tasks: 1000,
12369            forks,
12370        };
12371        let pid_max = 100_000;
12372        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(500, 10), pid_max, 400));
12373        assert!(at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(510, 20), pid_max, 505));
12374        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(510, 20), pid_max, 400));
12375        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(510, 20), pid_max, 511));
12376        // Wrapped from 99_990 to 310: both ends of the arc are suspect.
12377        assert!(at(99_990, 10).may_have_reused(at(310, 40), pid_max, 99_995));
12378        assert!(at(99_990, 10).may_have_reused(at(310, 40), pid_max, 305));
12379        assert!(!at(99_990, 10).may_have_reused(at(310, 40), pid_max, 5_000));
12380        // Enough new tasks to go round the whole space: everything is suspect.
12381        assert!(at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(400, 200_000), pid_max, 450));
12382        // A counter that went backwards proves nothing.
12383        assert!(at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(510, 5), pid_max, 400));
12384        // Host-wide tasks were created but this namespace's cursor did not
12385        // move: no PID here was handed out, on either side of the cursor.
12386        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(500, 40), pid_max, 400));
12387        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(500, 40), pid_max, 500));
12388        assert!(!at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(500, 40), pid_max, 600));
12389        // A lap is still a lap, cursor moved or not.
12390        assert!(at(500, 10).may_have_reused(at(500, 200_000), pid_max, 400));
12391    }
12392
12393    /// A group recorded after the previous scan began keeps its session at
12394    /// the next scan, though its PID lies on the allocator's arc since then,
12395    /// until the allocator passes its PID again.
12396    #[test]
12397    fn a_group_recorded_between_scans_keeps_its_session() {
12398        let at = |last_pid, forks| PidAllocator {
12399            last_pid,
12400            tasks: 1000,
12401            forks,
12402        };
12403        let pid_max = Some(100_000);
12404        let mut census = SessionCensus::default();
12405        census.begin(Some(at(500, 10)), pid_max);
12406        census.remember_group(505, Some(9), Some(at(505, 15)));
12407        census.remember_group(506, None, Some(at(506, 16)));
12408        census.begin(Some(at(520, 30)), pid_max);
12409        assert_eq!(
12410            census.group_sessions.get(&505).map(|entry| entry.0),
12411            Some(9)
12412        );
12413        assert!(
12414            !census.group_sessions.contains_key(&506),
12415            "no session, no entry"
12416        );
12417        // The allocator wraps and passes 505 again: the entry is dropped.
12418        census.begin(Some(at(510, 99_990)), pid_max);
12419        assert!(census.group_sessions.is_empty());
12420    }

12422    /// A PID is skipped only when its cached session can no longer be the
12423    /// group's: not the group's session, and not the PID itself (setsid).
12424    #[test]
12425    fn the_census_skips_only_pids_that_cannot_join_the_group() {
12426        let mut census = SessionCensus::default();
12427        census.sessions.insert(10, 7);
12428        census.sessions.insert(11, 9);
12429        assert!(census.skip(10, 9));
12430        assert!(!census.skip(11, 9));
12431        assert!(!census.skip(12, 9), "an unknown PID is read");
12432        assert!(!census.skip(9, 9), "the session leader is read");
12433    }

12435    /// The census-backed scan still finds a real process group's members,
12436    /// on a first scan and on a later one that skips what it cached.
12437    #[test]
12438    fn the_process_group_scan_finds_members_with_and_without_the_census() {
12439        use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
12440        let mut child = std::process::Command::new("sleep")
12441            .arg("30")
12442            .process_group(0)
12443            .spawn()
12444            .unwrap();
12445        let pgid = child.id();
12446        let first = process_group_members(pgid).unwrap();
12447        let second = process_group_members(pgid).unwrap();

12454    /// A census saved by one process and loaded by another finds the same
12455    /// members as a scan with none, and skips exactly what it may: the PIDs it
12456    /// knows to be in another session. A census can save reads only where such
12457    /// PIDs exist. In a PID namespace where every process shares the test's
12458    /// session (the pinned root has about 26 PIDs) there is nothing to skip, so
12459    /// the test makes that shape itself: three processes in a session of their
12460    /// own, which no scan without a census may skip and the carried census must.
12461    /// A census for another boot or PID namespace is not loaded at all.
12462    #[test]
12463    fn a_census_carried_to_another_process_finds_the_same_members() {
12464        use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
12465        assert!(
12466            PidAllocator::read().is_some() && read_pid_max().is_some(),
12467            "the census needs /proc/loadavg, /proc/stat and /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max"
12468        );
12469        // Three processes in a new session; each stays until the session is killed.
12470        let mut other = std::process::Command::new("sh");
12471        other.args(["-c", "sleep 60 & sleep 60 & exec sleep 60"]);
12472        // SAFETY: setsid is async-signal-safe; the child is not a group leader.
12473        unsafe {
12474            other.pre_exec(|| {
12475                if libc::setsid() < 0 {
12476                    return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
12477                }
12478                Ok(())
12479            });
12480        }
12481        let mut other = other.spawn().unwrap();
12482        let other_session = other.id();
12483        let in_other_session = || -> BTreeSet<u32> {
12484            fs::read_dir("/proc")
12485                .unwrap()
12486                .filter_map(|entry| entry.ok()?.file_name().to_str()?.parse::<u32>().ok())
12487                .filter(|pid| {
12488                    matches!(read_process_stat(*pid), Ok(StatRead::Bytes(stat))
12489                        if stat_session(&stat) == Some(other_session))
12490                })
12491                .collect()
12492        };
12493        let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(20);
12494        let mut skippable = in_other_session();
12495        while skippable.len() < 3 && Instant::now() < deadline {
12496            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
12497            skippable = in_other_session();
12498        }
12499        let mut child = std::process::Command::new("sleep")
12500            .arg("60")
12501            .process_group(0)
12502            .spawn()
12503            .unwrap();
12504        let pgid = child.id();
12505        let group_session = u32::try_from(unsafe { libc::getsid(0) }).unwrap();
12506        let mut writer = SessionCensus::default();
12507        let cold = scan_process_group(&mut writer, pgid).unwrap();
12508        let scope = census_scope().unwrap();
12509        let text = writer.render(&scope).unwrap();
12510        let mut reader = SessionCensus::parse(&text, &scope).unwrap();
12511        assert_eq!(reader.sessions, writer.sessions);
12512        let warm = scan_process_group(&mut reader, pgid).unwrap();
12513        // With no census at all the scan reads every PID.
12514        let none = scan_process_group(&mut SessionCensus::default(), pgid).unwrap();
12515        let still_there = in_other_session();
12516        child.kill().unwrap();
12517        child.wait().unwrap();
12518        unsafe { libc::kill(-(other_session as i32), libc::SIGKILL) };
12519        other.wait().unwrap();
12520        assert_eq!(
12521            skippable.len(),
12522            3,
12523            "the other session never had its 3 processes"
12524        );
12525        assert_eq!(
12526            still_there, skippable,
12527            "a process of the other session left early"
12528        );
12529        assert_eq!(cold.members, vec![pgid]);
12530        assert_eq!(warm.members, cold.members);
12531        assert_eq!(none.members, cold.members);
12532        // Without a census nothing may be skipped, so the other session's PIDs
12533        // are read; the carried census skips every one of them.
12534        assert_eq!(cold.skipped, Vec::<u32>::new());
12535        assert_eq!(none.skipped, Vec::<u32>::new());
12536        let skipped: BTreeSet<u32> = warm.skipped.iter().copied().collect();
12537        assert!(
12538            skippable.is_subset(&skipped),
12539            "the census skipped {skipped:?}, not all of {skippable:?}"
12540        );
12541        // And it skipped nothing it may not: each skipped PID was cached in a
12542        // session other than the group's, and is not the group's session leader.
12543        // (A count comparison of the two scans is no property of the census:
12544        // other tests create and reap processes in this session between them.)
12545        for pid in &skipped {
12546            assert_ne!(
12547                *pid, group_session,
12548                "the group's session leader was skipped"
12549            );
12550            let cached = writer.sessions.get(pid);
12551            assert!(
12552                cached.is_some_and(|session| *session != group_session),
12553                "PID {pid} was skipped with cached session {cached:?}, group session {group_session}"
12554            );
12555        }
12556        assert!(SessionCensus::parse(&text, "another-boot pid:[1]").is_none());
12557        assert!(SessionCensus::parse(&text.replace("/v1", "/v0"), &scope).is_none());
12558        assert!(SessionCensus::parse(&format!("{text}12 x\n"), &scope).is_none());
12559        assert!(
12560            SessionCensus::default().render(&scope).is_none(),
12561            "no position, no file"
12562        );
12563    }
12564
12565    /// A loaded census keeps only what the allocator cannot have reused since
12566    /// the writer's scan began.
12567    #[test]
12568    fn a_loaded_census_drops_pids_the_allocator_may_have_reused() {
12569        let at = PidAllocator {
12570            last_pid: 1000,
12571            tasks: 10,
12572            forks: 5000,
12573        };
12574        let text = format!("{SESSION_CENSUS_SCHEMA}\nscope s\nat 1000 10 5000\n900 1\n1500 2\n");
12575        let mut census = SessionCensus::parse(&text, "s").unwrap();
12576        assert_eq!(census.at, Some(at));
12577        let now = PidAllocator {
12578            last_pid: 2000,
12579            tasks: 10,
12580            forks: 6000,
12581        };
12582        census.begin(Some(now), Some(4_194_304));
12583        assert_eq!(
12584            census.sessions.get(&900),
12585            Some(&1),
12586            "900 lies behind the allocator"
12587        );
12588        assert_eq!(census.sessions.get(&1500), None, "1500 may be a new task");
12589    }

12609    /// A source snapshot names its commit; the run must not ask git, which a
12610    /// `git archive` root cannot answer. Without the name, git stays the
12611    /// authority and its failure is still an error.
12612    #[test]
12613    fn a_source_sha_replaces_git_for_a_snapshot_root() {
12614        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("runner-snapshot-{}", std::process::id()));
12615        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
12616        let sha = "03bbb83581fad247251df6363f50e61e24c2957e";
12617        let named = source_identity(&root, Some(sha));
12618        let asked = source_identity(&root, None);
12619        fs::remove_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
12620        assert_eq!(named, Ok((sha.to_string(), false)));
12621        assert!(asked.is_err(), "{asked:?}");
12622    }
12623
12624    /// Where Git tracks files it knows their commit and whether they are dirty,
12625    /// so a `--source-sha` that would override both is refused, at the
12626    /// checkout's top level and below it. A snapshot extracted inside the
12627    /// checkout but not tracked by it keeps its name.
12628    #[test]
12629    fn a_source_sha_is_refused_where_git_tracks_the_files() {
12630        let checkout = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("runner-checkout-{}", std::process::id()));
12631        let snapshot = checkout.join("snapshot");
12632        fs::create_dir_all(&snapshot).unwrap();
12633        fs::create_dir_all(checkout.join("src")).unwrap();
12634        fs::write(checkout.join("src/lib.rs"), "").unwrap();
12635        let git = |args: &[&str]| {
12636            crate::git_environment::git_command()
12637                .arg("-C")
12638                .arg(&checkout)
12639                .args(args)
12640                .status()
12641                .unwrap()
12642                .success()
12643        };
12644        let tracking = git(&["init", "-q"]) && git(&["add", "src/lib.rs"]);
12645        let sha = "03bbb83581fad247251df6363f50e61e24c2957e";
12646        let refused = [
12647            source_identity(&checkout, Some(sha)),
12648            source_identity(&checkout.join("src"), Some(sha)),
12649        ];
12650        let nested = source_identity(&snapshot, Some(sha));
12651        // A corrupt index leaves Git unable to say whether it tracks the files.
12652        fs::write(checkout.join(".git/index"), "junk").unwrap();
12653        let unreadable = [
12654            source_identity(&checkout.join("src"), Some(sha)),
12655            source_identity(&snapshot, Some(sha)),
12656        ];
12657        fs::remove_dir_all(&checkout).unwrap();
12658        assert!(tracking);
12659        for identity in refused {
12660            let error = identity.unwrap_err();
12661            assert!(error.contains("Git tracks files under"), "{error}");
12662        }
12663        assert_eq!(nested, Ok((sha.to_string(), false)));
12664        for identity in unreadable {
12665            let error = identity.unwrap_err();
12666            assert!(
12667                error.contains("`git ls-files` there failed")
12668                    && error.contains("whether Git tracks its files is unknown"),
12669                "{error}"
12670            );
12671        }
12672    }

12674    /// The git asked is the one named, and a named git that cannot run
12675    /// refuses the snapshot as an absent one does.
12676    #[test]
12677    fn a_snapshot_is_checked_with_the_named_git() {
12678        let base = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("runner-named-git-{}", std::process::id()));
12679        let checkout = base.join("checkout");
12680        let snapshot = checkout.join("snapshot");
12681        fs::create_dir_all(&snapshot).unwrap();
12682        fs::create_dir_all(checkout.join(".git")).unwrap();
12683        let says = |name: &str, status: i32| {
12684            let path = base.join(name);
12685            crate::exec_safe_fs::write_executable(
12686                &path,
12687                format!("#!/bin/sh\nexit {status}\n"),
12688                0o755,
12689            )
12690            .unwrap();
12691            path
12692        };
12693        let untracked = says("untracked-git", 1);
12694        let tracked = says("tracked-git", 0);
12695        let sha = "03bbb83581fad247251df6363f50e61e24c2957e";
12696        let accepted = validate_source_snapshot_with(&snapshot, sha, &untracked);
12697        let refused = validate_source_snapshot_with(&snapshot, sha, &tracked);
12698        let absent = validate_source_snapshot_with(&snapshot, sha, &base.join("no-git"));
12699        fs::remove_dir_all(&base).unwrap();
12700        assert_eq!(accepted, Ok(()));
12701        assert!(refused.unwrap_err().contains("Git tracks files under"));
12702        assert!(absent.unwrap_err().contains("git cannot run"));
12703    }

12705    #[test]
12706    fn a_source_sha_is_accepted_outside_any_checkout() {
12707        let archive = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("runner-archive-{}", std::process::id()));
12708        fs::create_dir_all(archive.join("src")).unwrap();
12709        // `..` out of a checkout is resolved before looking for `.git`.
12710        let checkout = archive.join("checkout");
12711        fs::create_dir_all(checkout.join(".git")).unwrap();
12712        let sha = "03bbb83581fad247251df6363f50e61e24c2957e";
12713        let outside = source_identity(&archive.join("src"), Some(sha));
12714        let climbed = source_identity(&checkout.join("../src"), Some(sha));
12715        // A root that does not resolve cannot be placed inside or outside a checkout.
12716        let missing = source_identity(&archive.join("missing"), Some(sha));
12717        fs::remove_dir_all(&archive).unwrap();
12718        assert!(
12719            !std::env::temp_dir()
12720                .ancestors()
12721                .any(|dir| dir.join(".git").exists()),
12722            "this test needs a temporary directory outside any checkout"
12723        );
12724        assert_eq!(outside, Ok((sha.to_string(), false)));
12725        assert_eq!(climbed, Ok((sha.to_string(), false)));
12726        let error = missing.unwrap_err();
12727        assert!(error.contains("cannot resolve --repo-root"), "{error}");
12728    }

12730    /// A symlink outside any checkout that points at tracked files names
12731    /// those files, so it is refused as they are.
12732    #[test]
12733    fn a_source_sha_is_refused_through_a_symlink_to_tracked_files() {
12734        let base = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("runner-symlink-{}", std::process::id()));
12735        let checkout = base.join("checkout");
12736        fs::create_dir_all(checkout.join("src")).unwrap();
12737        fs::write(checkout.join("src/lib.rs"), "").unwrap();
12738        let git = |args: &[&str]| {
12739            crate::git_environment::git_command()
12740                .arg("-C")
12741                .arg(&checkout)
12742                .args(args)
12743                .status()
12744                .unwrap()
12745                .success()
12746        };
12747        let tracking = git(&["init", "-q"]) && git(&["add", "src/lib.rs"]);
12748        let link = base.join("link");
12749        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(checkout.join("src"), &link).unwrap();
12750        let sha = "03bbb83581fad247251df6363f50e61e24c2957e";
12751        let linked = source_identity(&link, Some(sha));
12752        fs::remove_dir_all(&base).unwrap();
12753        assert!(
12754            !std::env::temp_dir()
12755                .ancestors()
12756                .any(|dir| dir.join(".git").exists()),
12757            "this test needs a temporary directory outside any checkout"
12758        );
12759        assert!(tracking);
12760        let error = linked.unwrap_err();
12761        assert!(error.contains("Git tracks files under"), "{error}");
12762    }

12764    /// The four outcomes of the verification-spelling probe.
12765    ///
12766    /// The first two are answers and must be reported as answers. The last two
12767    /// are failures to ask, and the whole point of this test is that they must
12768    /// NOT be reported as "the flag is absent" -- that reading omits
12769    /// `--verify-strict`, which on a pre-cutover Hermit silently runs the suite
12770    /// with weaker verification while every cell still passes.
12771    ///
12772    /// Reverting `command_help_contains` to the previous
12773    /// `.ok().filter(success).is_some_and(..)` form makes the two failure cases
12774    /// below return `Ok(false)` and fail; the two answer cases keep passing,
12775    /// because the defect was never in the answering path.
12776    #[test]
12777    fn the_capability_probe_separates_an_answer_from_a_failure_to_ask() {
12778        let needle = "--verify-strict";
12779
12780        // Ran and the flag is advertised.
12781        assert_eq!(
12782            command_help_contains(Path::new("/bin/echo"), &[needle], needle),
12783            Ok(true),
12784        );
12785
12786        // Ran and the flag is genuinely absent. This is the only legitimate
12787        // route to omitting the flag.
12788        assert_eq!(
12789            command_help_contains(Path::new("/bin/echo"), &["--canonical-only"], needle),
12790            Ok(false),
12791        );
12792
12793        // The binary does not exist. No cell will run, and the execution path
12794        // reports the absent binary exactly, so absence here is safe and is
12795        // what `production_run_retries_only_product_failures` depends on.
12796        assert_eq!(
12797            command_help_contains(
12798                Path::new("/nonexistent/hermit-probe-target"),
12799                &["run", "--help"],
12800                needle,
12801            ),
12802            Ok(false),
12803        );
12804
12805        // Launched but exited non-zero, so its output is not an answer. This
12806        // is the dangerous one: such a binary DOES go on to run cells.
12807        let failed = command_help_contains(Path::new("/bin/false"), &[], needle)
12808            .expect_err("a probe that exited non-zero must not answer the question");
12809        assert!(
12810            failed.contains("exited 1") && failed.contains("refusing to guess"),
12811            "the refusal must name the exit status, got: {failed}",
12812        );
12813    }

12815    /// The streamed binary digest is the digest of the whole file, across
12816    /// many read buffers, and an unreadable path has none, as `fs::read`
12817    /// gave before.
12818    #[test]
12819    fn file_digest_matches_a_whole_file_digest() {
12820        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("file-digest-{}", std::process::id()));
12821        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
12822        let path = root.join("binary");
12823        let bytes = (0..300_000u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect::<Vec<_>>();
12824        fs::write(&path, &bytes).unwrap();
12825        assert_eq!(file_digest(&path), Some(hex_digest(&bytes)));
12826        assert_eq!(file_digest(&root.join("missing")), None);
12827        assert_eq!(file_digest(&root), None);
12828        fs::remove_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
12829    }

12862    #[test]
12863    fn verification_reports_refuse_duplicate_compared_output_fields() {
12864        let report = parity_fixture_verification(Verdict::Matched);
12865        let value = serde_json::to_value(&report).unwrap();
12866        let raw = serde_json::to_string(&value).unwrap();
12867        assert_eq!(current_verification_report(raw.as_bytes()).unwrap(), report);
12868        let outputs = serde_json::to_string(&value["compared_outputs"]).unwrap();
12869        let mut duplicates = Vec::new();
12870        for first in ["null", outputs.as_str()] {
12871            duplicates.push(raw.replacen(
12872                &format!("\"compared_outputs\":{outputs}"),
12873                &format!("\"compared_outputs\":{first},\"compared_outputs\":{outputs}"),
12874                1,
12875            ));
12876        }
12877        for side in ["left", "right"] {
12878            let output = &value["compared_outputs"][side];
12879            let original = serde_json::to_string(output).unwrap();
12880            for field in [
12881                "exit_code",
12882                "signal",
12883                "stdout_sha256",
12884                "stdout_bytes",
12885                "stderr_sha256",
12886                "stderr_bytes",
12887            ] {
12888                let field_value = serde_json::to_string(&output[field]).unwrap();
12889                let conflicting = match field {
12890                    "exit_code" | "signal" => "7",
12891                    "stdout_bytes" | "stderr_bytes" => "123",
12892                    _ => "\"different-digest\"",
12893                };
12894                for first in [field_value.as_str(), conflicting] {
12895                    let changed = original.replacen(
12896                        &format!("\"{field}\":{field_value}"),
12897                        &format!("\"{field}\":{first},\"{field}\":{field_value}"),
12898                        1,
12899                    );
12900                    let changed_outputs = outputs.replacen(
12901                        &format!("\"{side}\":{original}"),
12902                        &format!("\"{side}\":{changed}"),
12903                        1,
12904                    );
12905                    duplicates.push(raw.replacen(&outputs, &changed_outputs, 1));
12906                }
12907            }
12908        }
12909        for duplicated in duplicates {
12910            assert_ne!(duplicated, raw);
12911            assert_eq!(
12912                serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&duplicated).unwrap(),
12913                value
12914            );
12915            assert!(
12916                current_verification_report(duplicated.as_bytes())
12917                    .unwrap_err()
12918                    .contains("duplicate field")
12919            );
12920        }
12921    }

12950    fn retry_outcome_preserves_recovery_and_product_failure() {

12952            outcome_after_retries([(1, "FAIL"), (2, "PASS")]).unwrap(),

12979                (4, "ERROR"),

12981            ])
12982            .unwrap(),
12983            "PASS"
12984        );
12985        assert_eq!(
12986            outcome_after_retries([(1, "ERROR"), (2, "ERROR"), (3, "FAIL"), (4, "ERROR")]).unwrap(),
12987            "FAIL"

13059    #[test]
13060    fn selected_retry_row_refuses_a_long_history_without_skid_evidence() {
13061        // A pure product history past the generic bound must not select
13062        // PASS through the widened skid ceiling: no row carries skid-only
13063        // evidence, so the selector refuses it by name.
13064        let mut product = Vec::new();
13065        for (attempt, outcome) in [(1, "FAIL"), (2, "FAIL"), (3, "PASS")] {
13066            let mut row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
13067            row.outcome = outcome.into();
13068            row.attempt = attempt;
13069            product.push(row);
13070        }
13071        let error = cell_result_after_retries(&product).unwrap_err();
13072        assert!(error.contains("without skid-only evidence"), "{error:?}");
13073        assert!(!history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(&product));
13074        // At the generic bound the same rows need no skid evidence.
13075        assert!(history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(&product[..2]));

13078    #[test]
13079    fn selected_retry_row_admits_a_proven_five_skid_history() {
13080        // The qualifying direction: five attempts that each re-decide as
13081        // skid-only from their retained evidence are admitted past the
13082        // generic bound and select their infrastructure ERROR.
13083        let skid_row = |attempt: u64| {
13084            let mut row = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![attempt_from_script(
13085                "ptrace",
13086                &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
13087                Some(&skid_report(2)),
13088            )]);
13089            row.attempt = attempt;
13090            row
13091        };
13092        let history: Vec<CellResult> = (1..=5).map(skid_row).collect();
13093        assert!(history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(&history));
13094        assert_eq!(skid_infra_reports(&history), Some(10));
13095        let (selected, attempts) = cell_result_and_attempts_after_retries(&history).unwrap();
13096        assert_eq!(
13097            (selected.outcome.as_str(), selected.attempt, attempts),
13098            ("ERROR", 5, 5)
13099        );
13100        // One product attempt in place of a skid attempt disqualifies
13101        // the whole long history.
13102        let mut mixed = history.clone();
13103        mixed[2].outcome = "FAIL".into();
13104        assert!(!history_past_generic_bound_is_skid_qualified(&mixed));
13105        assert_eq!(skid_infra_reports(&mixed), None);
13106    }

13108    fn recipe(ci: bool) -> TestRecipe {
13109        let disabled = BTreeMap::from([
13110            ("dbt".into(), "not qualified".into()),
13111            ("kvm".into(), "not qualified".into()),
13112            ("sabre".into(), "not qualified".into()),
13113            ("liteinst".into(), "not qualified".into()),
13114            ("in-guest-trap".into(), "not qualified".into()),
13115        ]);
13116        let mode = ModeRecipe {
13117            ci: CiSelectionSpec::Uniform(ci),
13118            ci_disabled_reason: (!ci)
13119                // A real sentence, because the shared-string form now carries the
13120                // same substance rule as a per-backend entry. "not selected yet"
13121                // is one of the placeholder phrases that rule bans outright.
13122                .then(|| {
13123                    CiDisabledReasonSpec::Uniform(
13124                        "fixture cell: ptrace only, other backends unmeasured here".into(),
13125                    )
13126                }),
13127            backends_enabled: vec!["ptrace".into()],
13128            backends_disabled: disabled,
13129            ..ModeRecipe::default()
13130        };
13131        TestRecipe {
13132            id: "fixture/test".into(),
13133            description: "fixture".into(),
13134            lane: "portable".into(),
13135            requires: Vec::new(),
13136            occasional: false,
13137            program: None,
13138            direct: Some(DirectCommand::Argv(vec!["/bin/true".into()])),
13139            observation: Observation {
13140                status: true,
13141                stdout: true,
13142                stderr: true,
13143                artifacts: Vec::new(),
13144            },
13145            build: None,
13146            modes: BTreeMap::from([("verify".into(), mode)]),
13147            preprocessors: Vec::new(),
13148            labels: Vec::new(),
13149            proc: None,
13150        }
13151    }

13153    /// A corpus's additional-backend flags reach the expanded verify mode's
13154    /// per-backend `hermit_args`, so the manifest validator holds them to the
13155    /// same allowlist and once-per-flag rule as any hand-written cell's, and
13156    /// the relaxation each cell records names its own flags.
13157    #[test]
13158    fn corpus_additional_backend_flags_meet_the_manifest_validator() {
13159        let corpus = r#"schema: 3
13160bucket: fixture
13161corpus:
13162  description: Fixture program
13163  lane: portable
13164  requires: [linux]
13165  backend: ptrace
13166  verify:
13167    hermit_args: [--no-virtualize-cpuid]
13168    hermit_args_reason: fixture configuration
13169    timeout_seconds: 60
13170    cpu_timeout_seconds: 59
13171    slow_reason: fixture budget
13172  additional:
13173    - backend: liteinst
13174      hermit_args: [--max-timeslice=disabled]
13175      hermit_args_reason: fixture in-guest reason
13176      rows: [echo]
13177      disabled_reason: not measured on liteinst
13178  rows:
13179    - {label: "echo", argv: ["/bin/echo", "x"]}
13180    - {label: "true", argv: ["/bin/true"]}
13181"#;
13182        let load = |text: &str| -> Result<ManifestDocument, String> {
13183            let value = crate::manifest_corpus::expand_corpus(
13184                serde_yaml::from_str(text).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?,
13185            )?;
13186            let document: ManifestDocument =
13187                serde_yaml::from_value(value).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
13188            validate_document(&document, "fixture", Path::new("/"), 15)?;
13189            Ok(document)
13190        };
13191        let document = load(corpus).unwrap();
13192        let verify = &document.test[0].modes["verify"];
13193        assert_eq!(verify.backends_enabled, ["ptrace", "liteinst"]);
13194        assert_eq!(
13195            cell_hermit_args(verify, "liteinst"),
13196            ["--max-timeslice=disabled"]
13197        );
13198        assert_eq!(
13199            cell_hermit_args(verify, "ptrace"),
13200            ["--no-virtualize-cpuid"]
13201        );
13202        // Each cell's relaxation names its own flags with its own reason.
13203        let relaxations = |backend: &str| {
13204            cell_relaxations(&SelectedCell {
13205                image: None,
13206                category: "fixture".into(),
13207                test: document.test[0].clone(),
13208                id: CellId {
13209                    test: "fixture/echo".into(),
13210                    mode: "verify".into(),
13211                    backend: Some(backend.into()),
13212                },
13213                enabled: true,
13214                timeout_seconds: 15,
13215                cpu_timeout_seconds: 15,
13216                host_level: HostLevel::default(),
13217            })
13218        };
13219        assert_eq!(
13220            relaxations("ptrace"),
13221            ["--no-virtualize-cpuid: fixture configuration"]
13222        );
13223        assert_eq!(
13224            relaxations("liteinst"),
13225            ["--max-timeslice=disabled: fixture in-guest reason"]
13226        );
13227        // A row without the additional cell keeps the lane's one reason.
13228        assert_eq!(
13229            document.test[1].modes["verify"].hermit_args_reason,
13230            Some(HermitArgsReason::from("fixture configuration"))
13231        );
13232        for refused_flag in ["--no-strict", "--chaos", "--max-timeslice=", "--epoch=1"] {
13233            let error = load(&corpus.replace(
13234                "hermit_args: [--max-timeslice=disabled]",
13235                &format!("hermit_args: [\"{refused_flag}\"]"),
13236            ))
13237            .unwrap_err();
13238            assert!(error.contains("is not one of"), "{refused_flag}: {error}");
13239        }
13240        let error = load(&corpus.replace(
13241            "hermit_args: [--max-timeslice=disabled]",
13242            "hermit_args: [--max-timeslice=1, --max-timeslice=disabled]",
13243        ))
13244        .unwrap_err();
13245        assert!(error.contains("repeats `--max-timeslice`"), "{error}");
13246        let error =
13247            load(&corpus.replace("      hermit_args_reason: fixture in-guest reason\n", ""))
13248                .unwrap_err();
13249        assert!(error.contains("require a hermit_args_reason"), "{error}");
13250    }

13252    /// A per-backend `hermit_args_reason` names exactly the backends with
13253    /// flags, each with a substantive reason, and each cell records its own.
13254    #[test]
13255    fn a_per_backend_hermit_args_reason_covers_exactly_the_flagged_backends() {
13256        let accepted = ModeRecipe {
13257            backends_enabled: vec!["ptrace".into(), "liteinst".into(), "sabre".into()],
13258            hermit_args: BTreeMap::from([
13259                ("ptrace".into(), vec!["--no-virtualize-cpuid".into()]),
13260                ("liteinst".into(), vec!["--max-timeslice=disabled".into()]),
13261            ]),
13262            hermit_args_reason: Some(HermitArgsReason::PerBackend(BTreeMap::from([
13263                (
13264                    "ptrace".into(),
13265                    "the corpus records this configuration".into(),
13266                ),
13267                (
13268                    "liteinst".into(),
13269                    "in-guest LiteInst refuses a preemption timer".into(),
13270                ),
13271            ]))),
13272            ..ModeRecipe::default()
13273        };
13274        validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", &accepted).unwrap();
13275        let reason = accepted.hermit_args_reason.as_ref().unwrap();
13276        assert_eq!(
13277            reason.for_backend("liteinst"),
13278            Some("in-guest LiteInst refuses a preemption timer")
13279        );
13280        assert_eq!(reason.for_backend("sabre"), None);
13281        let refused = |reasons: &[(&str, &str)], needle: &str| {
13282            let mut recipe = accepted.clone();
13283            recipe.hermit_args_reason = Some(HermitArgsReason::PerBackend(
13284                reasons
13285                    .iter()
13286                    .map(|(backend, reason)| (backend.to_string(), reason.to_string()))
13287                    .collect(),
13288            ));
13289            let error = validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", &recipe).unwrap_err();
13290            assert!(error.contains(needle), "{reasons:?}: {error}");
13291        };
13292        let exactly = "must name exactly the backends of hermit_args";
13293        refused(&[("ptrace", "configuration")], exactly);
13294        refused(
13295            &[
13296                ("ptrace", "configuration"),
13297                ("liteinst", "timer"),
13298                ("sabre", "no flags"),
13299            ],
13300            exactly,
13301        );
13302        refused(&[], exactly);
13303        refused(
13304            &[("ptrace", "configuration"), ("liteinst", " ")],
13305            "require a substantive hermit_args_reason",
13306        );
13307        // A per-backend reason without flags is a reason without flags.
13308        let mut bare = accepted.clone();
13309        bare.hermit_args.clear();
13310        assert!(
13311            validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", &bare)
13312                .unwrap_err()
13313                .contains("hermit_args_reason without hermit_args")
13314        );
13315        // Both spellings read from YAML.
13316        let shared: HermitArgsReason = serde_yaml::from_str("one reason").unwrap();
13317        assert_eq!(shared, HermitArgsReason::from("one reason"));
13318        let per_backend: HermitArgsReason =
13319            serde_yaml::from_str("{ptrace: a, liteinst: b}").unwrap();
13320        assert_eq!(per_backend.for_backend("ptrace"), Some("a"));
13321        assert!(serde_yaml::from_str::<HermitArgsReason>("[a, b]").is_err());
13322    }

13324    #[test]
13325    fn verify_extensions_are_verify_only_reasoned_and_allowlisted() {
13326        let accepted = ModeRecipe {
13327            backends_enabled: vec!["ptrace".into()],
13328            hermit_args: BTreeMap::from([(
13329                "ptrace".into(),
13330                vec![
13331                    "--no-virtualize-cpuid".into(),
13332                    "--max-timeslice=disabled".into(),
13333                ],
13334            )]),
13335            hermit_args_reason: Some("the corpus records this configuration".into()),
13336            env: Some(BTreeMap::from([("TMPDIR".into(), "/tmp".into())])),
13337            comparator: Some(Comparator::Stripped),
13338            comparator_reason: Some("the corpus verdict policy is the stripped comparison".into()),
13339            ..ModeRecipe::default()
13340        };
13341        validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", &accepted).unwrap();
13342        let refused = |change: &dyn Fn(&mut ModeRecipe), mode: &str, needle: &str| {
13343            let mut recipe = accepted.clone();
13344            change(&mut recipe);
13345            let error = validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", mode, &recipe).unwrap_err();
13346            assert!(error.contains(needle), "{error}");
13347        };
13348        refused(&|_| {}, "replay", "only a verify mode accepts");
13349        // Anything outside the allowlist, including every flag that would
13350        // weaken the comparison or determinism by another route.
13351        for flag in [
13352            "--no-detlog-io-buffers",
13353            "--no-rcb-time",
13354            "--no-strict",
13355            "--verify-allow=failure",
13356            "--verify-verbose",
13357            "--no-virtualize-time",
13358            "--chaos",
13359            "--epoch=1",
13360            "--max-timeslice=",
13361            "--no-virtualize-cpuid=1",
13362            "true",
13363        ] {
13364            refused(
13365                &|r| r.hermit_args = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec![flag.into()])]),
13366                "verify",
13367                "is not one of",
13368            );
13369        }
13370        refused(
13371            &|r| {
13372                r.hermit_args = BTreeMap::from([(
13373                    "ptrace".into(),
13374                    vec![
13375                        "--no-virtualize-cpuid".into(),
13376                        "--no-virtualize-cpuid".into(),
13377                    ],
13378                )])
13379            },
13380            "verify",
13381            "repeats `--no-virtualize-cpuid`",
13382        );
13383        refused(
13384            &|r| {
13385                r.hermit_args = BTreeMap::from([(
13386                    "ptrace".into(),
13387                    vec![
13388                        "--max-timeslice=1".into(),
13389                        "--max-timeslice=disabled".into(),
13390                    ],
13391                )])
13392            },
13393            "verify",
13394            "repeats `--max-timeslice`",
13395        );
13396        refused(
13397            &|r| r.hermit_args_reason = None,
13398            "verify",
13399            "require a substantive hermit_args_reason",
13400        );
13401        refused(
13402            &|r| r.hermit_args_reason = Some(" ".into()),
13403            "verify",
13404            "require a substantive hermit_args_reason",
13405        );
13406        refused(
13407            &|r| r.hermit_args.clear(),
13408            "verify",
13409            "hermit_args_reason without hermit_args",
13410        );
13411        // Flags belong to an enabled backend, and a named backend has some.
13412        refused(
13413            &|r| {
13414                r.hermit_args =
13415                    BTreeMap::from([("sabre".into(), vec!["--no-virtualize-cpuid".into()])])
13416            },
13417            "verify",
13418            "hermit_args names backend `sabre`, which is not in backends_enabled",
13419        );
13420        refused(
13421            &|r| r.hermit_args = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), Vec::new())]),
13422            "verify",
13423            "hermit_args for `ptrace` is empty",
13424        );
13425        // Run-type labels name an enabled backend and are well formed.
13426        refused(
13427            &|r| r.labels = BTreeMap::from([("sabre".into(), vec!["sabre-compat-only".into()])]),
13428            "verify",
13429            "labels name backend `sabre`, which is not in backends_enabled",
13430        );
13431        refused(
13432            &|r| r.labels = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), Vec::new())]),
13433            "verify",
13434            "labels for `ptrace` are empty",
13435        );
13436        refused(
13437            &|r| r.labels = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["Bad".into()])]),
13438            "verify",
13439            "is not lowercase-words-with-dashes",
13440        );
13441        refused(
13442            &|r| r.comparator_reason = None,
13443            "verify",
13444            "requires a substantive comparator_reason",
13445        );
13446        refused(
13447            &|r| r.no_retry_reason = Some(" ".into()),
13448            "verify",
13449            "no_retry_reason must be substantive",
13450        );
13451        refused(
13452            &|r| r.no_retry_reason = Some("single recorded run".into()),
13453            "replay",
13454            "only a verify mode accepts",
13455        );
13456        refused(
13457            &|r| r.comparator = None,
13458            "verify",
13459            "comparator_reason without comparator stripped",
13460        );
13461        refused(
13462            &|r| {
13463                r.assert = Some(Assertions {
13464                    bitwise_parity: Some(true),
13465                    ..Assertions::default()
13466                })
13467            },
13468            "verify",
13469            "cannot establish the bitwise_parity",
13470        );
13471        for owned in RUNNER_GUEST_ENV {
13472            refused(
13473                &|r| r.env = Some(BTreeMap::from([(owned.into(), "x".into())])),
13474                "verify",
13475                "a variable the runner sets itself",
13476            );
13477        }
13478        refused(
13479            &|r| r.env = Some(BTreeMap::from([("lower".into(), "x".into())])),
13480            "verify",
13481            "not a valid NAME=VALUE",
13482        );
13483        // A replay recipe may restate its environment, an empty mapping
13484        // included, under the same name checks; no other mode may declare one.
13485        let with_env = |env: BTreeMap<String, String>| ModeRecipe {
13486            env: Some(env),
13487            ..ModeRecipe::default()
13488        };
13489        for env in [
13490            BTreeMap::new(),
13491            BTreeMap::from([("MODE".into(), "x".into())]),
13492        ] {
13493            validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "replay", &with_env(env)).unwrap();
13494        }
13495        let error = validate_mode_extensions(
13496            "fixture/test",
13497            "replay",
13498            &with_env(BTreeMap::from([("lower".into(), "x".into())])),
13499        )
13500        .unwrap_err();
13501        assert!(error.contains("not a valid NAME=VALUE"), "{error}");
13502        for mode in ["naked", "chaos", "custom"] {
13503            let error = validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", mode, &with_env(BTreeMap::new()))
13504                .unwrap_err();
13505            assert!(
13506                error.contains("declares env, which only a verify or replay mode accepts"),
13507                "{error}"
13508            );
13509        }
13510        // A diagnostic is accepted only on an enabled backend of a stripped
13511        // cell, with a substantive reason, and only in verify.
13512        let diagnostic = || BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), "bounded probe".into())]);
13513        let mut with_diagnostic = accepted.clone();
13514        with_diagnostic.diagnostic = diagnostic();
13515        validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", &with_diagnostic).unwrap();
13516        refused(
13517            &|r| r.diagnostic = diagnostic(),
13518            "replay",
13519            "only a verify mode accepts",
13520        );
13521        refused(
13522            &|r| {
13523                r.diagnostic = diagnostic();
13524                r.comparator = None;
13525                r.comparator_reason = None;
13526            },
13527            "verify",
13528            "a canonical cell's failure must fail the run",
13529        );
13530        refused(
13531            &|r| r.diagnostic = BTreeMap::from([("kvm".into(), "bounded probe".into())]),
13532            "verify",
13533            "not in backends_enabled",
13534        );
13535        for reason in ["", " ", " padded"] {
13536            refused(
13537                &|r| r.diagnostic = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), reason.into())]),
13538                "verify",
13539                "requires a substantive, trimmed reason",
13540            );
13541        }
13542        // The validation is wired into document loading, not only callable.
13543        let five_modes = || {
13544            let mut test = recipe(true);
13545            for mode in ["naked", "replay", "chaos", "custom"] {
13546                let backends: &[&str] = if mode == "naked" {
13547                    &["native"]
13548                } else {
13549                    &["ptrace", "dbt", "kvm", "sabre", "liteinst", "in-guest-trap"]
13550                };
13551                test.modes.insert(
13552                    mode.into(),
13553                    ModeRecipe {
13554                        ci: CiSelectionSpec::Uniform(false),
13555                        ci_disabled_reason: Some(CiDisabledReasonSpec::Uniform(
13556                            "fixture cell: only the verify mode is measured here".into(),
13557                        )),
13558                        backends_disabled: backends
13559                            .iter()
13560                            .map(|backend| ((*backend).into(), "fixture mode is not run".into()))
13561                            .collect(),
13562                        ..ModeRecipe::default()
13563                    },
13564                );
13565            }
13566            test
13567        };
13568        let document = ManifestDocument {
13569            image: None,
13570            schema: MANIFEST_SCHEMA,
13571            bucket: "fixture".into(),
13572            timeout_seconds: None,
13573            slow_reason: None,
13574            test: vec![five_modes()],
13575        };
13576        validate_document_with_cpu(
13577            &document,
13578            "fixture",
13579            Path::new("/"),
13580            15,
13581            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13582        )
13583        .unwrap();
13584        let mut test = five_modes();
13585        test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap().hermit_args =
13586            BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["--chaos".into()])]);
13587        let document = ManifestDocument {
13588            test: vec![test],
13589            ..document
13590        };
13591        let error = validate_document_with_cpu(
13592            &document,
13593            "fixture",
13594            Path::new("/"),
13595            15,
13596            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13597        )
13598        .unwrap_err();
13599        assert!(error.contains("is not one of"), "{error}");
13600        let mut labelled = five_modes();
13601        labelled.labels = vec!["Bad".into()];
13602        let error = validate_document_with_cpu(
13603            &ManifestDocument {
13604                test: vec![labelled],
13605                ..document
13606            },
13607            "fixture",
13608            Path::new("/"),
13609            15,
13610            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13611        )
13612        .unwrap_err();
13613        assert!(
13614            error.contains("is not lowercase-words-with-dashes"),
13615            "{error}"
13616        );
13617    }

13619    #[test]
13620    fn program_in_uninitialized_submodule_is_not_available_here() {
13621        // Validation checkouts deliberately leave update=none submodules
13622        // empty (third-party/rr for the rr corpus rows). A program
13623        // inside an uninitialized submodule is not available in this
13624        // checkout, which must not read as a missing-program defect;
13625        // the same path typo'd inside a populated submodule still is.
13626        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
13627            "manifest-plan-submodule-test-{}",
13628            std::process::id()
13629        ));
13630        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
13631        std::fs::create_dir_all(root.join("third-party/rr")).unwrap();
13632        std::fs::write(
13633            root.join(".gitmodules"),
13634            "[submodule \"third-party/rr\"]\n\tpath = third-party/rr\n\turl = https://example.invalid/rr\n",
13635        )
13636        .unwrap();
13637        let five_modes = || {
13638            let mut test = recipe(true);
13639            for mode in ["naked", "replay", "chaos", "custom"] {
13640                let backends: &[&str] = if mode == "naked" {
13641                    &["native"]
13642                } else {
13643                    &["ptrace", "dbt", "kvm", "sabre", "liteinst", "in-guest-trap"]
13644                };
13645                test.modes.insert(
13646                    mode.into(),
13647                    ModeRecipe {
13648                        ci: CiSelectionSpec::Uniform(false),
13649                        ci_disabled_reason: Some(CiDisabledReasonSpec::Uniform(
13650                            "fixture cell: only the verify mode is measured here".into(),
13651                        )),
13652                        backends_disabled: backends
13653                            .iter()
13654                            .map(|backend| ((*backend).into(), "fixture mode is not run".into()))
13655                            .collect(),
13656                        ..ModeRecipe::default()
13657                    },
13658                );
13659            }
13660            test
13661        };
13662        let mut test = five_modes();
13663        test.program = Some("third-party/rr/src/test/simple.c".into());
13664        test.direct = None;
13665        let document = ManifestDocument {
13666            image: None,
13667            schema: MANIFEST_SCHEMA,
13668            bucket: "fixture".into(),
13669            timeout_seconds: None,
13670            slow_reason: None,
13671            test: vec![test.clone()],
13672        };
13673        validate_document_with_cpu(
13674            &document,
13675            "fixture",
13676            &root,
13677            15,
13678            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13679        )
13680        .unwrap();
13681        // Populated submodule, missing file: still a defect.
13682        std::fs::write(root.join("third-party/rr/README.md"), "x").unwrap();
13683        let error = validate_document_with_cpu(
13684            &document,
13685            "fixture",
13686            &root,
13687            15,
13688            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13689        )
13690        .unwrap_err();
13691        assert!(error.contains("missing program"), "{error}");
13692        // Outside tests/ (and outside any submodule): unchanged refusal.
13693        let mut outside = test;
13694        outside.program = Some("src/test/simple.c".into());
13695        let error = validate_document_with_cpu(
13696            &ManifestDocument {
13697                test: vec![outside],
13698                ..document
13699            },
13700            "fixture",
13701            &root,
13702            15,
13703            DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
13704        )
13705        .unwrap_err();
13706        assert!(error.contains("missing program"), "{error}");
13707        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
13708    }

13758    #[test]
13759    fn tier_marker_is_exactly_one_row_label() {
13760        let labels = |values: &[&str]| {
13761            values
13762                .iter()
13763                .map(|value| value.to_string())
13764                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
13765        };
13766        validate_tier_marker("gvisor/x", "gvisor", &labels(&["pressure"])).unwrap();
13767        validate_tier_marker("rr/x", "rr", &labels(&["full", "super"])).unwrap();
13768        validate_tier_marker("c-programs/x", "c-programs", &labels(&[])).unwrap();
13769        assert!(validate_tier_marker("gvisor/x", "gvisor", &labels(&[])).is_err());
13770        assert!(validate_tier_marker("rr/x", "rr", &labels(&["super", "pressure"])).is_err());
13771
13772        let mut test = recipe(true);
13773        test.labels = labels(&["full", "super"]);
13774        assert_eq!(
13775            cell_tier(&test, &test.modes["verify"], Some("ptrace")).unwrap(),
13776            Some(CellTier::Super)
13777        );
13778        test.labels = labels(&["pressure"]);
13779        assert_eq!(
13780            cell_tier(&test, &test.modes["verify"], Some("ptrace")).unwrap(),
13781            Some(CellTier::Pressure)
13782        );
13783        assert_eq!(CellTier::Super.as_str(), "super");
13784        assert_eq!(
13785            serde_json::to_string(&CellTier::Pressure).unwrap(),
13786            "\"pressure\""
13787        );
13788
13789        // A mode label may put one backend's cell in a tier (the compat
13790        // corpus's heavy rows carry mode-level `super`); the resolved
13791        // cell still may not carry both markers.
13792        let mut mode = test.modes["verify"].clone();
13793        mode.labels = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["super".into()])]);
13794        assert!(cell_tier(&test, &mode, Some("ptrace")).is_err());
13795    }

13833                    slow_reason: None,
13834                    test: vec![test],
13835                },
13836                bucket,
13837                Path::new("/"),
13838                15,

13841        };
13842        let untiered = five_modes("gvisor/x", vec![]);
13843        let error = validate("gvisor", untiered).unwrap_err();
13844        assert!(error.contains("requires exactly one tier label"), "{error}");
13845        validate("gvisor", five_modes("gvisor/x", vec!["pressure".into()])).unwrap();
13846        let mut both = five_modes("gvisor/x", vec!["pressure".into()]);
13847        both.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap().labels =

13854    /// A mode's per-backend labels put that backend's cell in their run type
13855    /// alone; the test's other cells stay in the default (full) run type, and
13856    /// per-backend hermit_args reach only their backend's cell.
13857    #[test]
13858    fn a_cell_labelled_by_its_mode_belongs_to_that_run_type_alone() {
13859        let mut test = recipe(true);
13860        let mode = test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap();
13861        mode.backends_enabled.push("sabre".into());
13862        mode.backends_disabled.remove("sabre");
13863        mode.labels = BTreeMap::from([("sabre".into(), vec!["sabre-compat-only".into()])]);
13864        mode.hermit_args =
13865            BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["--no-virtualize-cpuid".into()])]);
13866        mode.hermit_args_reason = Some("fixture configuration".into());
13867        let mode = &test.modes["verify"];
13868        validate_mode_extensions(&test.id, "verify", mode).unwrap();
13869        assert_eq!(cell_hermit_args(mode, "ptrace"), ["--no-virtualize-cpuid"]);
13870        assert!(cell_hermit_args(mode, "sabre").is_empty());
13871        assert_eq!(
13872            cell_labels(&test, mode, Some("sabre")),
13873            BTreeSet::from(["sabre-compat-only"])
13874        );
13875        assert_eq!(
13876            cell_labels(&test, mode, Some("ptrace")),
13877            BTreeSet::from([DEFAULT_RUN_TYPE])
13878        );
13879        let set = ManifestSet {
13880            documents: Vec::new(),
13881            tests: BTreeMap::from([(
13882                test.id.clone(),
13883                ("fixture".into(), 15, DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, test),
13884            )]),
13885        };
13886        let backends = |labels: &[&str], population: Population| {
13887            set.select(&Selection {
13888                population: Some(population),
13889                labels: labels.iter().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect(),
13890                ..Selection::default()
13891            })
13892            .unwrap()
13893            .into_iter()
13894            .map(|cell| cell.id.backend.unwrap())
13895            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
13896        };
13897        for population in [Population::Required, Population::Enabled] {
13898            assert_eq!(backends(&[], population), ["ptrace"]);
13899            assert_eq!(backends(&["full"], population), ["ptrace"]);
13900            assert_eq!(backends(&["sabre-compat-only"], population), ["sabre"]);
13901            assert_eq!(
13902                backends(&["full", "sabre-compat-only"], population),
13903                ["ptrace", "sabre"]
13904            );
13905        }
13906    }

13908    /// A cell on an archived backend (crate::archived) that names no focused
13909    /// run type belongs to the archived run type instead of full, so neither
13910    /// full validation nor its required plan selects it; a focused label it
13911    /// carries is kept, and other backends' cells stay full's.
13912    #[test]
13913    fn an_archived_backends_cell_leaves_full_for_the_archived_run_type() {

13921            cell_labels(&test, mode, Some("sabre")),

13927        );

13940            documents: Vec::new(),
13941            tests: BTreeMap::from([(

13948                population: Some(Population::Required),
13949                labels: labels.iter().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect(),

13953            .into_iter()
13954            .map(|cell| cell.id.backend.unwrap())

13961    #[test]
13962    fn labels_select_only_the_tests_that_carry_them() {
13963        let mut strict = recipe(true);
13964        strict.id = "fixture/strict".into();
13965        strict.labels = vec!["strict-compat".into(), "full".into()];
13966        let mut plain = recipe(true);
13967        plain.id = "fixture/plain".into();
13968        let set = ManifestSet {
13969            documents: Vec::new(),
13970            tests: [strict, plain]
13971                .into_iter()
13972                .map(|test| {

13974                        test.id.clone(),

13990        // An unlabelled test belongs to the default run type, full, so both
13991        // tests are full's; only the labelled one is strict-compat's.
13992        assert_eq!(selected(&[]), ["fixture/plain", "fixture/strict"]);

14000        // run type.

14002        set.tests.get_mut("fixture/strict").unwrap().3.labels = vec!["strict-compat".into()];
14003        let selected = |labels: &[&str]| {
14004            set.select(&Selection {
14005                labels: labels.iter().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect(),

14014        assert_eq!(selected(&["strict-compat"]), ["fixture/strict"]);
14015        let error = set
14016            .select(&Selection {
14017                labels: vec!["full".into(), "super".into()],
14018                ..Selection::default()
14019            })
14020            .unwrap_err();
14021        assert_eq!(error, "--label super names no test in any manifest");

14024    #[test]
14025    fn explicit_mapped_pair_uses_original_holder_and_guest_literals_do_not_select_it() {
14026        for (backend, is_run, explicit, mapped) in [
14027            ("in-guest-trap", true, false, false),
14028            ("in-guest-trap", true, true, true),
14029            ("ptrace", true, false, false),
14030            ("liteinst", true, false, false),
14031            ("in-guest-trap", false, false, false),
14032        ] {
14033            let mut run = vec![
14034                "hermit".into(),
14035                "--backend".into(),
14036                backend.into(),
14037                if is_run {
14038                    "run".into()
14039                } else {
14040                    "record".into()
14041                },
14042                "--verify-run".into(),
14043                VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER.into(),
14044            ];
14045            if explicit {
14046                run.push("--in-guest-exec-stop".into());
14047            }
14048            assert_eq!(
14049                run.iter()
14050                    .filter(|word| *word == "--in-guest-exec-stop")
14051                    .count(),
14052                usize::from(mapped)
14053            );
14054            run.extend(["--".into(), "guest".into(), "--in-guest-exec-stop".into()]);
14055            let comparison = vec![
14056                "hermit".into(),
14057                "log-diff".into(),
14058                "report".into(),
14059                "run1".into(),
14060                "run2".into(),
14061            ];
14062            let paired = paired_verification_argv(comparison, run);
14063            assert_eq!(
14064                paired.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("verify-inputs"),
14065                mapped
14066            );
14067            let inner = without_mapped_input_holder(&paired);
14068            assert_eq!(
14069                &inner[..4],
14070                ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT, VERIFY_PAIR_NAME]
14071            );
14072            assert_eq!(
14073                paired
14074                    .iter()
14075                    .filter(|word| *word == "--native-exec-shared-inputs=197")
14076                    .count(),
14077                usize::from(mapped)
14078            );
14079            assert_eq!(
14080                &paired[paired.len() - 3..],
14081                ["--", "guest", "--in-guest-exec-stop"]
14082            );
14083        }
14084    }

14093    /// Inspect the same paired command behind its one exact input holder.
14094    fn without_mapped_input_holder(argv: &[String]) -> &[String] {
14095        if argv.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("verify-inputs") {
14096            assert_eq!(&argv[1..5], MAPPED_INPUTS_PREFIX);
14097            let mut rest = &argv[5..];
14098            if rest.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("--input") {
14099                assert_eq!(&rest[..2], ["--input", LD_SO_CACHE_INPUT]);
14100                rest = &rest[2..];
14101            }
14102            assert_eq!(
14103                &rest[..4],
14104                ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT, VERIFY_PAIR_NAME]
14105            );
14106            rest
14107        } else {
14108            argv
14109        }
14110    }
14111
14112    /// An explicit pair API caller's inputs, taken from an ordinary cell's
14113    /// comparison and run. Manifest enrollment still selects no loader: the
14114    /// caller adds its option before the run's first guest separator, then
14115    /// uses the public pair builder and the existing single cache owner.
14116    fn explicit_mapped_pair_argv(ordinary: Vec<String>) -> Vec<String> {
14117        let shared = ordinary.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("verify-inputs");
14118        let paired = if shared {
14119            assert_eq!(
14120                &ordinary[1..=SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()],
14121                SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX
14122            );
14123            &ordinary[1 + SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()..]
14124        } else {
14125            ordinary.as_slice()
14126        };
14127        assert_eq!(
14128            &paired[..4],
14129            ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT, VERIFY_PAIR_NAME]
14130        );
14131        let commands = &paired[4..];
14132        let run_start = commands
14133            .iter()
14134            .skip(1)
14135            .position(|word| word == &commands[0])
14136            .map(|offset| offset + 1)
14137            .unwrap();
14138        let comparison = commands[..run_start].to_vec();
14139        let mut run = commands[run_start..].to_vec();
14140        assert_eq!(
14141            &run[1..6],
14142            ["--log", "info", "--backend", "in-guest-trap", "run"]
14143        );
14144        let separator = run.iter().position(|word| word == "--").unwrap();
14145        assert!(
14146            !run[..separator]
14147                .iter()
14148                .any(|word| word == "--in-guest-exec-stop")
14149        );
14150        run.insert(separator, "--in-guest-exec-stop".into());
14151        let hermit = run[0].clone();
14152        let mapped = paired_verification_argv(comparison, run);
14153        if shared {
14154            shared_inputs_argv(&hermit, mapped)
14155        } else {
14156            mapped
14157        }
14158    }

14160    /// The run flags of a verify spec: the tokens after `--strict` that its

14162    fn verify_run_flags(spec: &CellRunSpec) -> Vec<String> {
14163        spec.argv
14164            .iter()
14165            .filter(|arg| allowed_hermit_arg(arg))
14166            .cloned()
14167            .collect()
14168    }
