18403    #[test]
18404    fn every_row_records_the_binarys_exact_branch_counter_verdict() {
18405        // The cell whose remote failures came from an inexact counter
18406        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3794): a row that ran must
18407        // say whether the counter was exact, not only a withheld row's reason.
18408        let root = crate::compiled_manifest_dir!().join("../..");
18409        let cells = ManifestSet::load(&root)
18410            .unwrap()
18411            .select(&Selection {
18412                population: Some(Population::Required),
18413                test: Some("language-runtimes/python-hashseed".into()),
18414                mode: Some("verify".into()),
18415                backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
18416                ..Selection::default()
18417            })
18418            .unwrap();
18419        assert_eq!(cells.len(), 1);
18420        let cell = &cells[0];
18421        let scratch = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
18422            "hermit-runner-exact-branch-counter-row-{}",
18423            std::process::id()
18424        ));
18425        let mut context = run_context(&scratch);
18426        let verdict = CapabilityVerdict {
18427            present: false,
18428            evidence: "fixture CPU: Reverie performance-counter validation failed \
18429                       (AmdSpecLockMapShouldBeDisabled)"
18430                .into(),
18431        };
18432        context.exact_branch_counter = Some(verdict.clone());
18433        for (builder, row) in [
18434            (
18435                "infrastructure_error_result",
18436                infrastructure_error_result(&context, cell, "fixture".into()),
18437            ),
18438            (
18439                "host_inapplicable_result",
18440                host_inapplicable_result(&context, cell, "fixture".into()),
18441            ),
18442        ] {
18443            assert_eq!(
18444                row.exact_branch_counter.as_ref(),
18445                Some(&verdict),
18446                "{builder}"
18447            );
18448            let rendered = serde_json::to_value(&row).unwrap();
18449            assert_eq!(
18450                rendered["exact_branch_counter"]["present"], false,
18451                "{builder}"
18452            );
18453            assert_eq!(
18454                rendered["exact_branch_counter"]["evidence"],
18455                verdict.evidence.as_str(),
18456                "{builder}"
18457            );
18458            // The closed record keeps its frozen set.
18459            assert!(
18460                rendered["host_capabilities"]
18461                    .get("exact_branch_counter")
18462                    .is_none(),
18463                "{builder}"
18464            );
18465        }
18466        // A binary that gave no verdict leaves the key out, as a row written
18467        // before the field does.
18468        context.exact_branch_counter = None;
18469        let row = infrastructure_error_result(&context, cell, "fixture".into());
18470        let rendered = serde_json::to_value(&row).unwrap();
18471        assert!(rendered.get("exact_branch_counter").is_none());
18472        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&scratch);
18473    }

18475    #[test]
18476    fn shipped_readdir_order_identity_retains_its_resolved_timeouts() {
18477        let root = crate::compiled_manifest_dir!().join("../..");
18478        let cells = ManifestSet::load(&root)
18479            .unwrap()
18480            .select(&Selection {
18481                population: Some(Population::Required),
18482                test: Some("c-programs/readdir-order-identity".into()),
18483                mode: Some("verify".into()),
18484                backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
18485                ..Selection::default()
18486            })
18487            .unwrap();
18488        assert_eq!(cells.len(), 1);
18489        let cell = &cells[0];
18490        assert_eq!(cell.timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18491        assert_eq!(cell.cpu_timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18492
18493        let multipliers = TimeoutMultipliers {
18494            cpu: 1.25,
18495            wall: 1.5,
18496        };
18497        let resolved = resolved_cell_timeouts(cell, multipliers).unwrap();
18498        assert_eq!(resolved.cpu_seconds, 28);
18499        // Wall derives from the scaled CPU: min(8 x 28, 600) = 224,
18500        // scaled by the wall multiplier 1.5 = 336 s.
18501        assert_eq!(resolved.wall_seconds, 336);
18502        let mut context = run_context(&root);
18503        context.timeout_multipliers = multipliers;
18504        let retained = infrastructure_error_result(&context, cell, "fixture".into());
18505        assert_eq!(retained.timeout_seconds, resolved.wall_seconds);
18506        assert_eq!(
18507            retained.execution_cpu_timeout_seconds,
18508            Some(resolved.cpu_seconds)
18509        );
18510        assert_eq!(
18511            retained.execution_wall_timeout_seconds,
18512            Some(resolved.wall_seconds)
18513        );
18514    }

18516    #[test]
18517    fn shipped_plan_matches_the_frozen_timeout_calibration_partition() {
18518        let root = crate::compiled_manifest_dir!().join("../..");
18519        let manifests = ManifestSet::load(&root).unwrap();
18520        let required = manifests
18521            .select(&Selection {
18522                population: Some(Population::Required),
18523                ..Selection::default()
18524            })
18525            .unwrap();
18526        let enabled = manifests
18527            .select(&Selection {
18528                population: Some(Population::Enabled),
18529                ..Selection::default()
18530            })
18531            .unwrap();
18532        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2425 adds these two qualified
18533        // cells after the frozen calibration. Keep their identities explicit
18534        // without changing the historical population or timeout overrides.
18535        let regular_sink = required
18536            .iter()
18537            .filter(|cell| cell.id.test == "c-programs/record-replay-file-state-regular-sink")
18538            .map(|cell| (cell.id.mode.as_str(), cell.id.backend.as_deref()))
18539            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
18540        // Its KVM verify cell joins on 2026-10-08 (the KVM zero-class
18541        // qualification: three non-vacuous canonical passes on the validation
18542        // host), also with the default timeouts and no calibration change.
18543        // Its DBT verify cell joins the same day on the same evidence (the DBT
18544        // zero-class qualification), again with the default timeouts.
18545        // Its liteinst and in-guest-trap verify cells join the same day too,
18546        // from ten clean in-guest verify runs each with the maximum timeslice
18547        // disabled (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3745), again with
18548        // the default timeouts. Its SaBRe verify cell left the required
18549        // population when SaBRe was archived on 2026-10-25 (crate::archived).
18550        // Its ptrace replay cell joins on 2026-10-30 with the 338-cell flip
18551        // of sweep-clean cells, with the default timeouts (22 CPU s, 57 s
18552        // wall, like its verify cells) and no calibration change.
18553        assert_eq!(
18554            regular_sink,
18555            BTreeSet::from([
18556                ("verify", Some("dbt")),
18557                ("verify", Some("in-guest-trap")),
18558                ("verify", Some("kvm")),
18559                ("verify", Some("liteinst")),
18560                ("verify", Some("ptrace")),
18561                ("replay", Some("ptrace")),
18562            ])
18563        );
18564        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3231 qualifies three new
18565        // cells without revising the frozen calibration or any timeout override.
18566        // DBT verification now joins after whole-fixture qualification, with
18567        // the same default bounds and no calibration change.
18568        for population in [&required, &enabled] {
18569            let rng = population
18570                .iter()
18571                .filter(|cell| cell.id.test == "c-programs/random-readv-stream")
18572                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
18573            assert_eq!(rng.len(), 4);
18574            assert_eq!(
18575                rng.iter()
18576                    .map(|cell| (cell.id.mode.as_str(), cell.id.backend.as_deref()))
18577                    .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>(),
18578                BTreeSet::from([
18579                    ("verify", Some("ptrace")),
18580                    ("verify", Some("dbt")),
18581                    ("verify", Some("kvm")),
18582                    ("replay", Some("ptrace")),
18583                ])
18584            );
18585            for cell in rng {
18586                assert_eq!(cell.cpu_timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18587                assert_eq!(cell.timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18588            }
18589        }
18590        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3580 selects ptrace replay of
18591        // the two select programs, with the ordinary bounds.
18592        for population in [&required, &enabled] {
18593            for test in SELECT_REPLAY_2026_10_03_TESTS {
18594                let replay = population
18595                    .iter()
18596                    .filter(|cell| cell.id.test == test && cell.id.mode == "replay")
18597                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
18598                assert_eq!(replay.len(), 1, "{test}");
18599                assert_eq!(replay[0].id.backend.as_deref(), Some("ptrace"), "{test}");
18600                assert_eq!(
18601                    replay[0].cpu_timeout_seconds,
18602                    DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
18603                );
18604                assert_eq!(replay[0].timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18605            }
18606        }
18607        // How many cells are required is not pinned: the committed plan
18608        // records it, the manifest gate holds the plan to the manifests, and
18609        // a cell flip shows up as a diff of that plan
18610        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3606). The checks here
18611        // are of the named batches' bounds.
18612        // The SaBRe verify selections of 2026-10-03 have the ordinary bounds,
18613        // and the ones that were enabled with ci:false became required. Since
18614        // SaBRe was archived on 2026-10-25 (crate::archived) they are required
18615        // by the archived run type instead of full.
18616        fn sabre_verify<'a>(
18617            population: &'a [SelectedCell],
18618            test: &str,
18619        ) -> Option<&'a SelectedCell> {
18620            population.iter().find(|cell| {
18621                cell.id.test == test
18622                    && cell.id.mode == "verify"
18623                    && cell.id.backend.as_deref() == Some("sabre")
18624            })
18625        }
18626        let archived = manifests
18627            .select(&Selection {
18628                population: Some(Population::Required),
18629                labels: vec![crate::archived::ARCHIVED_RUN_TYPE.into()],
18630                ..Selection::default()
18631            })
18632            .unwrap();
18633        for test in SABRE_2026_10_03_PROMOTED_CI_FALSE_TESTS {
18634            assert!(
18635                sabre_verify(&required, test).is_none(),
18636                "{test} verify/sabre is required by full though SaBRe is archived"
18637            );
18638            let cell = sabre_verify(&archived, test)
18639                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{test} verify/sabre is not required"));
18640            assert_eq!(cell.cpu_timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18641            assert_eq!(cell.timeout_seconds, DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS);
18642        }
18643        // Slice S13 of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301 selected three
18644        // DBT verify cells that were enabled with ci:false and enabled one new
18645        // ci:false DBT verify cell; the timeouts module names them.
18646        let dbt_verify = |population: &[SelectedCell], test: &str| {
18647            population.iter().any(|cell| {
18648                cell.id.test == test
18649                    && cell.id.mode == "verify"
18650                    && cell.id.backend.as_deref() == Some("dbt")
18651            })
18652        };
18653        for test in DBT_MATRIX_2026_09_29_PROMOTED_CI_FALSE_TESTS {
18654            assert!(
18655                dbt_verify(&required, test),
18656                "{test} verify/dbt is not required"
18657            );
18658        }
18659        for test in DBT_MATRIX_2026_09_29_ENABLED_CI_FALSE_TESTS {
18660            assert!(
18661                dbt_verify(&enabled, test),
18662                "{test} verify/dbt is not enabled"
18663            );
18664            // The whole io-uring fallback verify/DBT cell is now required after
18665            // 20 independent strict canonical pairs passed at ed4a5dd90da2.
18666            assert!(
18667                dbt_verify(&required, test),
18668                "{test} verify/dbt is not required"
18669            );
18670        }
18671
18672        // The two dated LiteInst groups were qualified on the ptrace-owned
18673        // hybrid. The owner reset of 2026-10-04 switched every LiteInst cell
18674        // off while in-guest Detcore replaces it
18675        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3745, step 1 of
18676        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3520), and the groups are
18677        // history: they qualify nothing. LiteInst cells came back on
18678        // 2026-10-08 only on the new architecture, with fresh evidence: verify
18679        // cells of in-guest LiteInst (liteinst, and in-guest-trap with site
18680        // patching off) that passed ten clean verify runs each with the
18681        // maximum timeslice disabled, which in-guest LiteInst requires. So
18682        // every enabled LiteInst or in-guest-trap cell, a hybrid-group member
18683        // included, must be a verify cell that carries exactly that
18684        // relaxation and the default bounds, never a hybrid-era calibration.
18685        // The census covers every run type and the occasional tests, so a
18686        // cell that full validation would skip is caught too.
18687        let enabled_anywhere = manifests
18688            .select(&Selection {
18689                population: Some(Population::Enabled),
18690                all_run_types: true,
18691                include_occasional: true,
18692                ..Selection::default()
18693            })
18694            .unwrap();
18695        let in_guest = enabled_anywhere
18696            .iter()
18697            .filter(|cell| {
18698                matches!(
18699                    cell.id.backend.as_deref(),
18700                    Some("liteinst" | "in-guest-trap")
18701                )
18702            })
18703            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
18704        assert!(!in_guest.is_empty());
18705        for cell in &in_guest {
18706            let backend = cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap();
18707            let name = format!("{} {}/{backend}", cell.id.test, cell.id.mode);
18708            assert_eq!(cell.id.mode, "verify", "{name}");
18709            assert_eq!(
18710                cell_hermit_args(&cell.test.modes[&cell.id.mode], backend),
18711                ["--max-timeslice=disabled"],
18712                "{name}"
18713            );
18714            assert_eq!(
18715                (cell.cpu_timeout_seconds, cell.timeout_seconds),
18716                (
18717                    DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
18718                    DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
18719                ),
18720                "{name}"
18721            );
18722        }
18723        let hybrid_group_cells = LITEINST_2026_09_16_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS
18724            .iter()
18725            .chain(&LITEINST_2026_09_17_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18726            .filter(|calibration| {
18727                in_guest.iter().any(|cell| {
18728                    cell.id.test == calibration.test
18729                        && cell.id.mode == calibration.mode
18730                        && cell.id.backend.as_deref() == Some(calibration.backend)
18731                })
18732            })
18733            .count();
18734        // Hybrid-group cells do come back, on the in-guest evidence above, so
18735        // the checks above are not vacuous for them.
18736        assert!(hybrid_group_cells > 0);
18737
18738        let observed = enabled
18739            .iter()
18740            .filter(|cell| {
18741                cell.cpu_timeout_seconds != DEFAULT_TEST_CPU_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
18742                    || cell.timeout_seconds != DEFAULT_TEST_WALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
18743            })
18744            .map(|cell| {
18745                (
18746                    (
18747                        cell.id.test.as_str(),
18748                        cell.id.mode.as_str(),
18749                        cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap_or("native"),
18750                    ),
18751                    (cell.cpu_timeout_seconds, cell.timeout_seconds),
18752                )
18753            })
18754            .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>();
18755        // The strict compatibility corpus (fold 1 of
18756        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3448) keeps the 60 s wall
18757        // bound its generated validation nodes carried, with CPU one second
18758        // below it (a cell's CPU budget must stay below its wall). Its five
18759        // former 20-second diagnostics are ordinary cells since the corpus
18760        // became strict (2026-10-07). These literals are the check; they are
18761        // not read back from compat.yaml.
18762        let (compat, observed): (BTreeMap<_, _>, BTreeMap<_, _>) = observed
18763            .into_iter()
18764            .partition(|((test, _, _), _)| test.starts_with("compat/"));
18765        // Its replay cells, the full run's since 2026-10-20, keep the rr run
18766        // type's identical bounds.
18767        let (compat_replay, compat): (BTreeMap<_, _>, BTreeMap<_, _>) = compat
18768            .into_iter()
18769            .partition(|((_, mode, _), _)| *mode == "replay");
18770        assert_eq!(
18771            compat_replay.len(),
18772            COMPAT_REPLAY_FULL_2026_10_20_ENABLED_CELL_COUNT
18773        );
18774        // java, javac and rustc replay under a 177 s wall backstop, three
18775        // times the shared 59 s CPU budget (compat.yaml's replay `slow`).
18776        for ((test, _, backend), bounds) in &compat_replay {
18777            assert_eq!(*backend, "ptrace", "{test}");
18778            let wall = if [
18779                "compat/java-compile",
18780                "compat/java-run",
18781                "compat/javac-compile",
18782                "compat/javac-run",
18783                "compat/rustc",
18784            ]
18785            .contains(test)
18786            {
18787                177
18788            } else {
18789                60
18790            };
18791            assert_eq!(*bounds, (59, wall), "{test}");
18792        }
18793        // The four compat DBT cells with a `slow` budget (git, ld, node,
18794        // pkg-config at 33/57) are not ptrace corpus cells; assert them
18795        // apart and return them to the calibrated set below.
18796        let (compat_dbt_slow, compat): (BTreeMap<_, _>, BTreeMap<_, _>) = compat
18797            .into_iter()
18798            .partition(|((_, _, backend), _)| *backend == "dbt");
18799        assert_eq!(compat_dbt_slow.len(), 4);
18800        for ((test, mode, _), bounds) in &compat_dbt_slow {
18801            assert_eq!(*mode, "verify", "{test}");
18802            assert_eq!(*bounds, (33, 57), "{test}");
18803        }
18804        let observed: BTreeMap<_, _> = observed.into_iter().chain(compat_dbt_slow).collect();
18805        assert_eq!(
18806            compat.len(),
18807            STRICT_COMPAT_FOLD_2026_10_01_SELECTED_CI_CELL_COUNT
18808        );
18809        for ((test, mode, backend), bounds) in &compat {
18810            assert_eq!((*mode, *backend), ("verify", "ptrace"), "{test}");
18811            assert_eq!(*bounds, (59, 60), "{test}");
18812        }
18813        let expected = EXPLICIT_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS
18814            .iter()
18815            .chain(&KVM_RATCHET_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18816            .chain(&DBT_2026_10_25_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18817            .chain(&DBT_FLIP_2026_10_27_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18818            .chain(&FLIP_2026_10_30_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18819            .chain(&KVM_2026_11_08_TIMEOUT_CALIBRATIONS)
18820            .map(|calibration| {
18821                (
18822                    (calibration.test, calibration.mode, calibration.backend),
18823                    (
18824                        calibration.configured_cpu_seconds,
18825                        calibration.configured_wall_seconds,
18826                    ),
18827                )
18828            })
18829            .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>();
18830        assert_eq!(observed, expected);
18831    }

18857    fn cell_timeout_requires_the_same_named_reason() {
18858        let mut mode = recipe(true).modes.remove("verify").unwrap();
18859        mode.timeout_seconds.insert("ptrace".into(), 30);
18860        assert_eq!(
18861            validate_mode("fixture/test", "verify", &mode, 15).unwrap_err(),

18899            "hermit-runner-prelaunch-timeout-{}",

18901        ));

18903        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
18904        let spec = CellRunSpec {
18905            command_binding: None,
18906            id: CellId {
18907                test: "fixture/prelaunch-timeout".into(),
18908                mode: "verify".into(),
18909                backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
18910            },
18911            lane: "portable".into(),
18912            category: "fixture".into(),
18913            cwd: root.clone(),
18914            env: BTreeMap::new(),
18915            argv: vec!["/bin/false".into()],
18916            guest_argv: vec!["fixture".into()],
18917            timeout_seconds: 15,
18918            verdict_path: Some(root.join("verdict.json")),
18919            verification_log_dir: None,
18920            verify_runs: None,
18921            single_run_capture: None,
18922            sabre_path_evidence: None,
18923            cell_dir: root.clone(),
18924            expected_guest_exit: None,
18925            expected_stdout: None,
18926            expected_stdout_contains: None,
18927            expected_stderr: None,
18928            comparator: Comparator::Strict,
18929            attempt: "1".into(),
18930            fixed_workdir_source: root.join("workdir/1"),
18931        };
18932
18933        // This is the exact boundary reached when the aggregate execution
18934        // backstop is gone before a later attempt starts: no child process can
18935        // exist or have an exit status.
18936        let attempt =
18937            execute_spec_until(&spec, Instant::now(), 15, 57, None, &mut Vec::new()).unwrap();
18938        assert_eq!(attempt.outcome, "ERROR");
18939        assert_eq!(attempt.error_kind.as_deref(), Some("wall-timeout"));
18940        assert!(attempt.timed_out);
18941        assert_eq!((attempt.status, attempt.signal), (None, None));
18942        let report = attempt
18943            .verification_report
18944            .as_deref()
18945            .expect("pre-launch timeout must carry typed NotRun evidence");
18946        let report_sha256 = hex_digest(report.as_bytes());
18947        assert_eq!(
18948            attempt.verification_report_sha256.as_deref(),
18949            Some(report_sha256.as_str())
18950        );
18951        let report = VerificationReport::from_json_slice(report.as_bytes()).unwrap();
18952        assert_eq!(report.verdict, Verdict::NoResult);
18953        assert_eq!(
18954            report.no_result_reason,
18955            Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::NotRun)
18956        );
18957        assert_eq!(
18958            failure_class(
18959                &attempt.outcome,
18960                observed_result(
18961                    "verify",
18962                    &attempt.outcome,
18963                    std::slice::from_ref(&attempt),
18964                    attempt.error_kind.as_deref()
18965                ),
18966                attempt.error_kind.as_deref(),
18967            ),
18968            Some(FailureClass::NoResult)
18969        );
18970        let runtime = root.join("runtime");
18971        fs::create_dir(&runtime).unwrap();
18972        fs::set_permissions(&runtime, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700)).unwrap();
18973        let mut cell = ptrace_cell("verify");
18974        let context = run_context(&root);
18975        // An unrelated recipe must never inspect the invalid lease transport.
18976        assert!(
18977            acquire_proc_locks_lease(
18978                &cell,
18979                Instant::now(),
18980                Some(OsStr::new("/missing/lease")),
18981                Some(OsStr::new("invalid")),
18982            )
18983            .unwrap()
18984            .is_none()
18985        );
18986        cell.test.program = Some("tests/c/proc_locks.c".into());
18987        let mut reached_guest = false;
18988        let failure = record_cell(&context, &cell, |_| {
18989            let _lease =
18990                acquire_proc_locks_lease(&cell, Instant::now(), Some(runtime.as_os_str()), None)?;
18991            reached_guest = true;
18992            unreachable!("expired lease deadline cannot reach guest launch")
18993        })
18994        .unwrap_err();
18995        assert!(!reached_guest);
18996        assert!(failure.attempts.is_empty());
18997        assert!(failure.observations.invocations.is_empty());
18998        let result = failure.into_result(&context, &cell);
18999        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR");
19000        assert_eq!(
19001            result.failure_class,
19002            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
19003        );
19004        assert!(result.result.is_none());
19005        assert!(
19006            result
19007                .reason
19008                .as_deref()
19009                .unwrap()
19010                .contains("execution deadline before guest launch")
19011        );
19012        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19013    }

19080    thread_local! {
19081        /// How many times this thread has called fork(), counted by a
19082        /// `pthread_atfork` prepare handler. glibc runs the handlers in the
19083        /// thread that calls fork() and not for posix_spawn, which starts the
19084        /// child without copying this process.
19085        static FORKS_ON_THIS_THREAD: std::cell::Cell<u64> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(0) };
19086    }
19087
19088    /// How many times this process has called fork(), on any thread:
19089    /// the same prepare handler, counted process-wide. Only exact in
19090    /// a process running one test (the child
19091    /// [`alone_in_a_child_process`] starts).
19092    static FORKS_IN_PROCESS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);
19093
19094    fn forks_in_process() -> u64 {
19095        forks_on_this_thread();
19096        FORKS_IN_PROCESS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
19097    }
19098
19099    /// The number of fork() calls this thread has made since the counter was
19100    /// installed in this process.
19101    fn forks_on_this_thread() -> u64 {
19102        extern "C" fn count_fork() {
19103            FORKS_ON_THIS_THREAD.with(|forks| forks.set(forks.get() + 1));
19104            FORKS_IN_PROCESS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19105        }
19106        static INSTALL: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
19107        INSTALL.call_once(|| {
19108            assert_eq!(
19109                unsafe { libc::pthread_atfork(Some(count_fork), None, None) },
19110                0
19111            );
19112        });
19113        FORKS_ON_THIS_THREAD.with(std::cell::Cell::get)
19114    }
19115
19116    /// An invocation with no CPU budget, and so no invocation cgroup, starts
19117    /// without fork() of this process (dh-7n47nt). fork() copies the address
19118    /// space under the memory-map lock: in loaded library runs each one took a
19119    /// median 94-177 ms and up to 2.3 s, and every other thread that page-faulted
19120    /// meanwhile waited, so CPU readers and census walks in the same process
19121    /// stalled off-CPU. The child still leads a process group of its own.
19122    #[test]
19123    fn an_invocation_without_a_cgroup_starts_without_forking_this_process() {
19124        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
19125            "hermit-runner-no-cgroup-spawn-{}",
19126            std::process::id()
19127        ));
19128        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
19129        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
19130        let mut observations = Vec::new();
19131        let before = forks_on_this_thread();
19132        let output = execute_process(
19133            ProcessRequest::new(
19134                InvocationRole::Execution {
19135                    attempt_index: "1".into(),
19136                    backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
19137                },
19138                &root,
19139                "/bin/sh",
19140                &[
19141                    "-c".into(),
19142                    "printf '%s ' $$; cut -d' ' -f5 /proc/$$/stat".into(),
19143                ],
19144                &BTreeMap::new(),
19145                &root.join("group.stdout"),
19146                &root.join("group.stderr"),
19147            ),
19148            (Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60), None),
19149            &mut observations,
19150        )
19151        .unwrap();
19152        let forks = forks_on_this_thread() - before;
19153        assert!(output.status.success());
19154        assert_eq!(forks, 0, "starting the invocation forked this process");
19155        let reported = fs::read_to_string(root.join("group.stdout")).unwrap();
19156        let (pid, pgid) = reported.trim().split_once(' ').unwrap();
19157        assert_eq!(
19158            pid, pgid,
19159            "the invocation does not lead its own process group"
19160        );
19161        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19162    }
19163
19164    /// A budgeted invocation, which joins an invocation cgroup, starts
19165    /// without fork() of this process (dh-7n47nt stage 2): the cgroup join is
19166    /// made by clone3's CLONE_INTO_CGROUP instead of a pre_exec closure, which
19167    /// forces fork(). Its program is in the invocation cgroup from its first
19168    /// instruction.
19169    #[test]
19170    fn an_invocation_in_a_cgroup_starts_without_forking_this_process() {
19171        let test = "an_invocation_in_a_cgroup_starts_without_forking_this_process";
19172        if !alone_in_a_child_process(&format!("runner::tests::{test}")) {
19173            return;
19174        }
19175        let Some(mut probe) = crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)
19176        else {
19177            return;
19178        };
19179        probe.finish().unwrap();
19180        let root =
19181            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("hermit-runner-cgroup-spawn-{}", std::process::id()));
19182        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
19183        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
19184        let mut observations = Vec::new();
19185        let before = forks_on_this_thread();
19186        let output = execute_process(
19187            ProcessRequest::new(
19188                InvocationRole::Execution {
19189                    attempt_index: "1".into(),
19190                    backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
19191                },
19192                &root,
19193                "/bin/cat",
19194                &["/proc/self/cgroup".into()],
19195                &BTreeMap::new(),
19196                &root.join("cgroup.stdout"),
19197                &root.join("cgroup.stderr"),
19198            ),
19199            (Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60), Some(5_000_000)),
19200            &mut observations,
19201        )
19202        .unwrap();
19203        let forks = forks_on_this_thread() - before;
19204        assert!(output.status.success());
19205        let LiveCpuObservation::Enabled(live) = &observations[0].live else {
19206            panic!("a budgeted invocation enables live CPU observation");
19207        };
19208        assert_eq!(live.source, LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1);
19209        assert_eq!(forks, 0, "starting the invocation forked this process");
19210        // The startup probe must not fork at all: it starts its
19211        // child with clone3, on its setup thread, before this
19212        // invocation. This process runs only this test, so the
19213        // count is exact.
19214        assert_eq!(
19215            forks_in_process(),
19216            0,
19217            "the startup probe must not fork this process"
19218        );
19219        assert!(
19220            crate::vfork_spawn::CLONE3.cgroup_probe_record().is_some(),
19221            "the startup probe ran before the first invocation"
19222        );
19223        let cgroup = fs::read_to_string(root.join("cgroup.stdout")).unwrap();
19224        let invocation = format!("/hermit-e2e-invocation-{}-", std::process::id());
19225        assert!(
19226            cgroup.starts_with("0::/") && cgroup.contains(&invocation),
19227            "the program was not in its invocation cgroup: {cgroup:?}"
19228        );
19229        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19230    }
19231
19232    /// This process's zombie children that were created by this thread and
19233    /// never execed: a child that clone3 made keeps the creating thread's
19234    /// name until it execs, and libtest names each test's thread after the
19235    /// test. A failed start that did not reap its child leaves one here.
19236    ///
19237    /// The kernel keeps only 15 bytes of a thread's name, and every
19238    /// `runner::tests::` thread's is "runner::tests::", so in the parallel
19239    /// libtest process this also sees another test's child that failed to
19240    /// exec and is not reaped yet. A test that asserts on it runs alone, in
19241    /// the child process [`alone_in_a_child_process`] starts.
19242    fn unreaped_children_of_this_thread() -> Vec<String> {
19243        let me = std::process::id().to_string();
19244        let comm = fs::read_to_string("/proc/thread-self/comm").unwrap();
19245        let mut zombies = Vec::new();
19246        for entry in fs::read_dir("/proc").unwrap().flatten() {
19247            let Ok(stat) = fs::read_to_string(entry.path().join("stat")) else {
19248                continue;
19249            };
19250            let (Some(open), Some(close)) = (stat.find('('), stat.rfind(')')) else {
19251                continue;
19252            };
19253            let name = &stat[open + 1..close];
19254            let fields: Vec<&str> = stat[close + 1..].split_whitespace().collect();
19255            if fields.first() == Some(&"Z")
19256                && fields.get(1) == Some(&me.as_str())
19257                && name == comm.trim_end()
19258            {
19259                zombies.push(stat[..open].trim().to_string());
19260            }
19261        }
19262        zombies
19263    }
19264
19265    /// Whether this is the child process that runs the test `case` alone.
19266    /// In the libtest process, this runs `case` in a child libtest process
19267    /// with no other test, asserts that the child ran it and that it passed,
19268    /// and returns false: the caller then returns.
19269    fn alone_in_a_child_process(case: &str) -> bool {
19270        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_TEST_ALONE_IN_A_CHILD_PROCESS";
19271        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some_and(|value| value == case) {
19272            return true;
19273        }
19274        let output = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
19275            .args(["--exact", case, "--nocapture"])
19276            .env(CHILD, case)
19277            .output()
19278            .unwrap();
19279        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
19280        assert!(
19281            output.status.success(),
19282            "{stdout}\n{}",
19283            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
19284        );
19285        assert!(
19286            stdout.contains("test result: ok. 1 passed;"),
19287            "the child process did not run {case}: {stdout}"
19288        );
19289        print!("{stdout}");
19290        false
19291    }
19292
19293    /// Waits for and reaps `leader`, and returns how it ended.
19294    fn wait_for_leader(leader: &SpawnedLeader) -> ExitStatus {
19295        let mut status = 0;
19296        let waited = unsafe { libc::waitpid(leader.id() as libc::pid_t, &mut status, 0) };
19297        assert_eq!(waited, leader.id() as libc::pid_t, "waitpid failed");
19298        ExitStatus::from_raw(status)
19299    }
19300
19301    /// What a program `spawn_process` started in a fresh invocation cgroup
19302    /// did, once it exited.
19303    struct CgroupSpawned {
19304        status: ExitStatus,
19305        stdout: String,
19306        stderr: String,
19307        method: SpawnMethod,
19308    }
19309
19310    /// Starts `program` with `args` and environment overrides `env` through
19311    /// `spawn_process` in a fresh invocation cgroup, waits for it, removes the
19312    /// cgroup, and asserts that clone3 created the program. `None` when this
19313    /// environment declares it has no cgroups.
19314    fn spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup(
19315        test: &str,
19316        root: &Path,
19317        program: &str,
19318        args: &[&str],
19319        env: &[(&str, &str)],
19320    ) -> Option<Result<CgroupSpawned, String>> {
19321        let spawned = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(
19322            &crate::vfork_spawn::CLONE3,
19323            test,
19324            root,
19325            program,
19326            args,
19327            env,
19328        )?;
19329        if let Ok(spawned) = &spawned {
19330            assert_eq!(spawned.method, SpawnMethod::Clone3IntoCgroup);
19331        }
19332        Some(spawned)
19333    }
19334
19335    /// [`spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup`] with clone3 as `clone3` finds it, whatever
19336    /// method started the program.
19337    fn spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(
19338        clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support,
19339        test: &str,
19340        root: &Path,
19341        program: &str,
19342        args: &[&str],
19343        env: &[(&str, &str)],
19344    ) -> Option<Result<CgroupSpawned, String>> {
19345        spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_in(clone3, test, root, root, program, args, env, &|_| {})
19346    }
19347
19348    /// [`spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with`], with `cwd` as the program's working
19349    /// directory, and `prepare` given the cgroup's path before the spawn.
19350    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
19351    fn spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_in(
19352        clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support,
19353        test: &str,
19354        root: &Path,
19355        cwd: &Path,
19356        program: &str,
19357        args: &[&str],
19358        env: &[(&str, &str)],
19359        prepare: &dyn Fn(&Path),
19360    ) -> Option<Result<CgroupSpawned, String>> {
19361        let mut cgroup = crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)?;
19362        prepare(cgroup.path());
19363        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
19364            InvocationRole::Execution {
19365                attempt_index: "1".into(),
19366                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
19367            },
19368            cwd,
19369            program,
19370            &args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
19371            &env.iter()
19372                .map(|(key, value)| (key.to_string(), value.to_string()))
19373                .collect(),
19374            &root.join("spawned.stdout"),
19375            &root.join("spawned.stderr"),
19376        );
19377        let mut observation = InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
19378            1,
19379            request.role,
19380            request.command,
19381            Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
19382        );
19383        let spawned = spawn_process_with(
19384            clone3,
19385            &request.cwd,
19386            &request.stdout,
19387            &request.stderr,
19388            Some(Enrollment {
19389                directory: cgroup.directory_fd(),
19390                procs: cgroup.enrollment_fd(),
19391                path: cgroup.path(),
19392            }),
19393            &mut observation,
19394        )
19395        .map(|child| CgroupSpawned {
19396            status: wait_for_leader(&child),
19397            stdout: fs::read_to_string(&request.stdout).unwrap(),
19398            stderr: fs::read_to_string(&request.stderr).unwrap(),
19399            method: match &observation.launch {
19400                LaunchObservation::Spawned { method, .. } => method.clone(),
19401                other => panic!("a started program records Spawned, not {other:?}"),
19402            },
19403        });
19404        cgroup.finish().unwrap();
19405        Some(spawned)
19406    }

19418
19419    /// Each kind of clone3 refusal takes its own path (dh-7n47nt):
19420    /// - ENOSYS, E2BIG and EINVAL mean clone3 cannot be used here (an older
19421    ///   kernel or a seccomp filter), and so does EPERM when a probe without
19422    ///   CLONE_INTO_CGROUP is refused too (a filter). The program starts
19423    ///   through `Command` with the pre_exec join, still in its invocation
19424    ///   cgroup, and the refusal is remembered, with one notice: the next
19425    ///   spawn does not call clone3.
19426    /// - EBADF, EACCES, ENOENT, EROFS, ENODEV, EBUSY and EOPNOTSUPP are about
19427    ///   the cgroup: a failed join, not remembered; so is EPERM when the probe
19428    ///   is not refused (see
19429    ///   `an_eperm_from_the_cgroup_fails_that_spawn_and_the_next_uses_clone3`).
19430    /// - Anything else, such as EAGAIN or ENOMEM, means no child: a failed
19431    ///   spawn, not remembered.
19432    #[test]
19433    fn each_kind_of_clone3_refusal_takes_its_own_path() {
19434        let test = "each_kind_of_clone3_refusal_takes_its_own_path";
19435        let root = spawn_test_root("clone3-refusals");
19436        let invocation = format!("/hermit-e2e-invocation-{}-", std::process::id());
19437        let attempts = |clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support| {
19438            clone3.attempts.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
19439        };
19440        for errno in [libc::ENOSYS, libc::E2BIG, libc::EINVAL, libc::EPERM] {
19441            let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing(errno);
19442            let probes = if errno == libc::EPERM { 1 } else { 0 };
19443            let reason = format!(
19444                "clone3 with CLONE_INTO_CGROUP was refused: {}",
19445                std::io::Error::from_raw_os_error(errno)
19446            );
19447            for spawn in 1..=2 {
19448                let Some(spawned) = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(
19449                    &clone3,
19450                    test,
19451                    &root,
19452                    "/bin/cat",
19453                    &["/proc/self/cgroup"],
19454                    &[],
19455                ) else {
19456                    return;
19457                };
19458                let spawned = spawned.unwrap();
19459                assert!(spawned.status.success(), "{}", spawned.stderr);
19460                assert!(
19461                    spawned.stdout.contains(&invocation),
19462                    "errno {errno}: not in its invocation cgroup: {:?}",
19463                    spawned.stdout
19464                );
19465                assert_eq!(
19466                    spawned.method,
19467                    SpawnMethod::CommandAfterClone3Refused {
19468                        reason: reason.clone()
19469                    },
19470                    "errno {errno}, spawn {spawn}"
19471                );
19472                assert_eq!(attempts(&clone3), 1, "errno {errno}, spawn {spawn}");
19473                assert_eq!(
19474                    clone3.probes.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
19475                    probes,
19476                    "errno {errno}, spawn {spawn}"
19477                );
19478                assert_eq!(
19479                    clone3.notices.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
19480                    1,
19481                    "errno {errno}, spawn {spawn}"
19482                );
19483            }
19484        }
19485        for errno in [
19486            libc::EBADF,
19487            libc::EACCES,
19488            libc::ENOENT,
19489            libc::EROFS,
19490            libc::ENODEV,
19491            libc::EBUSY,
19492            libc::EOPNOTSUPP,
19493        ] {
19494            let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing(errno);
19495            let tail = format!(
19496                " before exec, so /bin/true was not started: {}",
19497                std::io::Error::from_raw_os_error(errno)
19498            );
19499            for spawn in 1..=2 {
19500                let Some(spawned) =
19501                    spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(&clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19502                else {
19503                    return;
19504                };
19505                let error = spawned
19506                    .err()
19507                    .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("errno {errno} started"));
19508                assert!(
19509                    error.starts_with("cannot join invocation cgroup /") && error.ends_with(&tail),
19510                    "errno {errno}: {error}"
19511                );
19512                assert_eq!(attempts(&clone3), spawn, "errno {errno}");
19513            }
19514        }
19515        for errno in [libc::EAGAIN, libc::ENOMEM] {
19516            let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing(errno);
19517            for spawn in 1..=2 {
19518                let Some(spawned) =
19519                    spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(&clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19520                else {
19521                    return;
19522                };
19523                assert_eq!(
19524                    spawned.err(),
19525                    Some(format!(
19526                        "cannot execute /bin/true: {}",
19527                        std::io::Error::from_raw_os_error(errno)
19528                    )),
19529                    "errno {errno}"
19530                );
19531                assert_eq!(attempts(&clone3), spawn, "errno {errno}");
19532            }
19533        }
19534        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19535    }

19537    /// An EPERM from a clone3 with CLONE_INTO_CGROUP, where clone3 itself is
19538    /// allowed (the probe without CLONE_INTO_CGROUP is not refused), is the
19539    /// cgroup's permission check refusing the child: that spawn's join fails,
19540    /// nothing is remembered, and the next spawn uses clone3 (dh-7n47nt F1).
19541    #[test]
19542    fn an_eperm_from_the_cgroup_fails_that_spawn_and_the_next_uses_clone3() {
19543        let test = "an_eperm_from_the_cgroup_fails_that_spawn_and_the_next_uses_clone3";
19544        let root = spawn_test_root("clone3-eperm-once");
19545        // The probe answered EINVAL by injection, and made for real (this
19546        // host has no filter on clone3, so it answers EINVAL too).
19547        let injected =
19548            crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing_once_with_probe(libc::EPERM, libc::EINVAL);
19549        let real = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing_once(libc::EPERM);
19550        for clone3 in [&injected, &real] {
19551            let Some(first) =
19552                spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19553            else {
19554                return;
19555            };
19556            let error = first.err().expect("the first spawn's join fails");
19557            assert!(
19558                error.starts_with("cannot join invocation cgroup /")
19559                    && error.ends_with(" before exec, so /bin/true was not started: Operation not permitted (os error 1)"),
19560                "{error}"
19561            );
19562            let second = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19563                .unwrap()
19564                .unwrap();
19565            assert!(second.status.success(), "{}", second.stderr);
19566            assert_eq!(second.method, SpawnMethod::Clone3IntoCgroup);
19567            let count = |counter: &std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize| {
19568                counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
19569            };
19570            assert_eq!(count(&clone3.attempts), 2);
19571            assert_eq!(count(&clone3.probes), 1);
19572            assert_eq!(count(&clone3.notices), 0);
19573        }
19574        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19575    }

19577    /// A target cgroup this process may not write to refuses the child for
19578    /// real (EACCES from the kernel's permission check on its cgroup.procs):
19579    /// that spawn's join fails, and the next spawn, into a writable cgroup,
19580    /// still uses clone3.
19581    #[test]
19582    fn an_unwritable_cgroup_fails_that_spawn_and_the_next_uses_clone3() {
19583        let test = "an_unwritable_cgroup_fails_that_spawn_and_the_next_uses_clone3";
19584        // Mode 0444 refuses only a writer without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, so as root
19585        // this refusal cannot be produced this way.
19586        if unsafe { libc::geteuid() } == 0 {
19587            println!(
19588                "SKIPPED {test}: running as root, which mode 0444 on cgroup.procs does not refuse"
19589            );
19590            return;
19591        }
19592        let root = spawn_test_root("clone3-unwritable");
19593        let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::new();
19594        let read_only = |cgroup: &Path| {
19595            fs::set_permissions(
19596                cgroup.join("cgroup.procs"),
19597                fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o444),
19598            )
19599            .unwrap();
19600        };
19601        let Some(first) = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_in(
19602            &clone3,
19603            test,
19604            &root,
19605            &root,
19606            "/bin/true",
19607            &[],
19608            &[],
19609            &read_only,
19610        ) else {
19611            return;
19612        };
19613        let error = first
19614            .err()
19615            .expect("the spawn into an unwritable cgroup fails");
19616        assert!(
19617            error.starts_with("cannot join invocation cgroup /")
19618                && error.ends_with(
19619                    " before exec, so /bin/true was not started: Permission denied (os error 13)"
19620                ),
19621            "{error}"
19622        );
19623        let second = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(&clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19624            .unwrap()
19625            .unwrap();
19626        assert!(second.status.success(), "{}", second.stderr);
19627        assert_eq!(second.method, SpawnMethod::Clone3IntoCgroup);
19628        assert_eq!(
19629            clone3.attempts.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
19630            2
19631        );
19632        assert_eq!(clone3.notices.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed), 0);
19633        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19634    }

19636    /// A well-formed clone3 with CLONE_INTO_CGROUP is accepted by this
19637    /// kernel: none of its argument checks refuses it (EINVAL, E2BIG), so a
19638    /// regression in the arguments fails here instead of quietly sending
19639    /// every spawn back to fork() (dh-7n47nt F3). Kernels older than 5.7,
19640    /// which have no CLONE_INTO_CGROUP, are skipped.
19641    #[test]
19642    fn clone3_into_a_cgroup_is_accepted_by_this_kernel() {
19643        let test = "clone3_into_a_cgroup_is_accepted_by_this_kernel";
19644        let release = fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease").unwrap();
19645        let mut numbers = release
19646            .trim()
19647            .split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
19648            .map(|part| part.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0));
19649        let version = (numbers.next().unwrap_or(0), numbers.next().unwrap_or(0));
19650        if version < (5, 7) {
19651            eprintln!(
19652                "{test}: skipped, kernel {} has no CLONE_INTO_CGROUP",
19653                release.trim()
19654            );
19655            return;
19656        }
19657        let root = spawn_test_root("clone3-accepted");
19658        let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::new();
19659        let Some(spawned) =
19660            spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(&clone3, test, &root, "/bin/true", &[], &[])
19661        else {
19662            return;
19663        };
19664        let spawned = spawned.unwrap();
19665        assert!(spawned.status.success(), "{}", spawned.stderr);
19666        assert_eq!(spawned.method, SpawnMethod::Clone3IntoCgroup);
19667        assert_eq!(clone3.notices.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed), 0);
19668        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19669    }

19675    fn a_child_killed_before_exec_reads_as_a_started_program_killed_by_the_signal() {

19731    /// In the PATH search, a program found but not executable (EACCES) is
19732    /// reported over a later directory that lacks it (ENOENT), and a later
19733    /// directory that has it runs it, as execvp does; through clone3 as
19734    /// through `Command`.
19735    #[test]
19736    fn the_path_search_reports_a_denied_program_over_a_missing_one() {
19737        let test = "the_path_search_reports_a_denied_program_over_a_missing_one";
19738        let root = spawn_test_root("path-eacces");
19739        let denied = root.join("denied");
19740        let empty = root.join("empty");
19741        let runnable = root.join("runnable");
19742        for dir in [&denied, &empty, &runnable] {
19743            fs::create_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
19744        }
19745        let name = "hermit-spawn-eacces-probe";
19746        fs::write(denied.join(name), "#!/bin/sh\nprintf denied\n").unwrap();
19747        fs::set_permissions(denied.join(name), fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
19748        fs::write(runnable.join(name), "#!/bin/sh\nprintf ran\n").unwrap();
19749        fs::set_permissions(runnable.join(name), fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();
19750        let denied_then_missing = format!("{}:{}", denied.display(), empty.display());
19751        let denied_then_runnable = format!("{}:{}", denied.display(), runnable.display());
19752        let command = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing(libc::ENOSYS);
19753        let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::new();
19754        for support in [&command, &clone3] {
19755            let Some(spawned) = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(
19756                support,
19757                test,
19758                &root,
19759                name,
19760                &[],
19761                &[("PATH", &denied_then_missing)],
19762            ) else {
19763                return;
19764            };
19765            assert_eq!(
19766                spawned.err(),
19767                Some(format!(
19768                    "cannot execute {name}: Permission denied (os error 13)"
19769                ))
19770            );
19771            let spawned = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup_with(
19772                support,
19773                test,
19774                &root,
19775                name,
19776                &[],
19777                &[("PATH", &denied_then_runnable)],
19778            )
19779            .unwrap()
19780            .unwrap();
19781            assert!(spawned.status.success(), "{}", spawned.stderr);
19782            assert_eq!(spawned.stdout, "ran");
19783        }
19784        assert_eq!(
19785            clone3.attempts.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
19786            2
19787        );
19788        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19789    }

19876    /// The program starts as std::process::Command starts one: leading a
19877    /// process group of its own, in its working directory, with stdin on
19878    /// /dev/null, no blocked signals and SIGPIPE at its default action.
19879    #[test]
19880    fn a_program_in_a_cgroup_starts_with_the_process_state_command_gives() {
19881        let test = "a_program_in_a_cgroup_starts_with_the_process_state_command_gives";
19882        let root = spawn_test_root("process-state");
19883        let script = "set -e; \
19884            read -r _ _ _ _ pgid _ < /proc/$$/stat; \
19885            printf 'group=%s\\n' \"$([ \"$pgid\" = $$ ] && echo own || echo other)\"; \
19886            printf 'cwd=%s\\n' \"$(pwd -P)\"; \
19887            printf 'stdin=%s\\n' \"$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/0)\"; \
19888            grep -E '^(SigBlk|SigIgn):' /proc/$$/status";
19889        let Some(spawned) = spawn_in_a_fresh_cgroup(test, &root, "/bin/sh", &["-c", script], &[])
19890        else {
19891            return;
19892        };
19893        let spawned = spawned.unwrap();
19894        assert!(spawned.status.success(), "{}", spawned.stderr);
19895        let line = |key: &str| {
19896            spawned
19897                .stdout
19898                .lines()
19899                .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(key))
19900                .map(str::trim)
19901                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {key} in {:?}", spawned.stdout))
19902                .to_string()
19903        };
19904        assert_eq!(line("group="), "own");
19905        assert_eq!(line("cwd="), root.canonicalize().unwrap().to_str().unwrap());
19906        assert_eq!(line("stdin="), "/dev/null");
19907        assert_eq!(line("SigBlk:"), "0000000000000000");
19908        let ignored = u64::from_str_radix(&line("SigIgn:"), 16).unwrap();
19909        assert_eq!(
19910            ignored & (1 << (libc::SIGPIPE - 1)),
19911            0,
19912            "SIGPIPE is ignored in the program: SigIgn {ignored:016x}"
19913        );
19914        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
19915    }

19917    fn bounded_process(
19918        root: &Path,
19919        label: &str,
19920        script: &str,
19921        wall: Duration,
19922        cpu_budget_usec: u64,
19923    ) -> ProcessOutput {
19924        let mut observations = Vec::new();
19925        let output = execute_process(
19926            ProcessRequest::new(
19927                InvocationRole::Execution {
19928                    attempt_index: "1".into(),
19929                    backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
19930                },
19931                root,
19932                "/bin/sh",
19933                &["-c".into(), script.into()],
19934                &BTreeMap::new(),

19947    fn live_cpu_accounting_excludes_an_unrelated_process_group() {
19948        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
19949            "hermit-runner-owned-cpu-accounting-{}",
19950            std::process::id()
19951        ));
19952        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
19953        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
19954        let mut command = Command::new("/bin/sleep");
19955        command.arg("3");
19956        unsafe {
19957            command.pre_exec(|| {
19958                if libc::setpgid(0, 0) == -1 {
19959                    return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());

19966        let reader = dagrun::proccpu::ProcessGroupCpu::new(pid).unwrap();
19967        // `stop_process_group` below owns the matching wait4; discard only the
19968        // std handle so the test exercises the production reaper.
19969        drop(child);
19970        let unrelated = bounded_process(
19971            &root,
19972            "unrelated",
19973            "while :; do :; done",
19974            Duration::from_millis(650),
19975            5_000_000,
19976        );

19978        let used = live_cpu_usage_usec(
19979            pid,
19980            reader
19981                .seconds()
19982                .expect("the launched sleeper must remain measurable"),
19983        )
19984        .unwrap();
19985        assert!(
19986            used < 100_000,
19987            "an idle process group unexpectedly included unrelated CPU: {used} usec"
19988        );
19989        stop_process_group(
19990            pid,
19991            &LeaderPidFd::open(pid),
19992            None,
19993            Instant::now(),
19994            &mut FinalWaitObservation::NotApplicable,
19995        )
19996        .unwrap();
19997        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();

20013    /// Substitute the live-CPU plan for the current test thread until dropped,
20014    /// in place of the fallback marker and the runner's own cgroup.
20015    struct LiveCpuPlanOverride;
20016
20017    impl LiveCpuPlanOverride {
20018        fn set(
20019            allow_process_group_scan: Result<bool, String>,
20020            cgroup_parent: Option<PathBuf>,
20021        ) -> Self {
20022            LIVE_CPU_PLAN_OVERRIDE.with(|plan| {
20023                *plan.borrow_mut() = Some(LiveCpuPlan {
20024                    allow_process_group_scan,
20025                    cgroup_parent,
20026                });
20027            });
20028            Self
20029        }
20030    }

20032    impl Drop for LiveCpuPlanOverride {
20033        fn drop(&mut self) {
20034            LIVE_CPU_PLAN_OVERRIDE.with(|plan| *plan.borrow_mut() = None);
20035        }
20036    }

20084    /// Spawn `program` with `enrollment` standing in for an invocation
20085    /// cgroup's directory and `cgroup.procs` descriptor, with clone3 as
20086    /// `clone3` finds it, and return the spawn error.
20087    fn spawn_error_with_enrollment(
20088        clone3: &crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support,
20089        root: &Path,
20090        label: &str,
20091        program: &str,
20092        enrollment: &File,
20093    ) -> (String, InvocationCpuObservation) {
20094        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
20095            InvocationRole::Execution {
20096                attempt_index: label.into(),
20097                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
20098            },
20099            root,
20100            program,
20101            &[],
20102            &BTreeMap::new(),
20103            &root.join(format!("{label}.stdout")),
20104            &root.join(format!("{label}.stderr")),
20105        );
20106        let mut observation = InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
20107            1,
20108            request.role,
20109            request.command,
20110            Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
20111        );
20112        let error = spawn_process_with(
20113            clone3,
20114            &request.cwd,
20115            &request.stdout,
20116            &request.stderr,
20117            Some(Enrollment {
20118                directory: enrollment.as_raw_fd(),
20119                procs: enrollment.as_raw_fd(),
20120                path: Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup/stand-in-invocation"),
20121            }),
20122            &mut observation,
20123        )
20124        .expect_err("the spawn must fail");
20125        (error, observation)
20126    }

20128    #[test]
20129    fn a_failed_spawn_names_the_exec_or_the_cgroup_join_whichever_failed() {
20130        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("spawn-failure-step");
20131        // Where clone3 is refused, the child joins in a pre_exec closure.
20132        let refused = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::refusing(libc::ENOSYS);
20133        // The join's write succeeds on /dev/null, so only the exec can fail,
20134        // and its reason reads exactly as it does without a cgroup.
20135        let accepting = OpenOptions::new().write(true).open("/dev/null").unwrap();
20136        let missing = root.join("missing-program");
20137        let (error, observation) = spawn_error_with_enrollment(
20138            &refused,
20139            &root,
20140            "exec",
20141            missing.to_str().unwrap(),
20142            &accepting,
20143        );
20144        let exec_failure = format!(
20145            "cannot execute {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)",
20146            missing.display()
20147        );
20148        assert_eq!(error, exec_failure);
20149        assert_eq!(
20150            observation.launch,
20151            LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
20152                stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
20153                reason: exec_failure,
20154            }
20155        );
20156        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
20157        // A descriptor opened read-only refuses the join's write, so the join
20158        // fails before an existing program could be started.
20159        let refusing = File::open("/dev/null").unwrap();
20160        let join_failure = "cannot join invocation cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/stand-in-invocation before exec, so /bin/true was not started: Bad file descriptor (os error 9)";
20161        let (error, observation) =
20162            spawn_error_with_enrollment(&refused, &root, "join", "/bin/true", &refusing);
20163        assert_eq!(error, join_failure);
20164        assert_eq!(
20165            observation.launch,
20166            LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
20167                stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
20168                reason: join_failure.into(),
20169            }
20170        );
20171        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
20172        // clone3 refuses a directory descriptor that is no cgroup (EBADF), and
20173        // that reads as the same failed join.
20174        let clone3 = crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::new();
20175        let (error, observation) =
20176            spawn_error_with_enrollment(&clone3, &root, "clone3-join", "/bin/true", &refusing);
20177        assert_eq!(error, join_failure);
20178        assert_eq!(
20179            observation.launch,
20180            LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
20181                stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
20182                reason: join_failure.into(),
20183            }
20184        );
20185        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
20186        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20187    }

20189    fn owned_child_is_reaped(pid: u32) -> bool {
20190        let mut status = 0;
20191        let waited = unsafe { libc::waitpid(pid as libc::pid_t, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) };
20192        let error = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
20193        waited == -1 && error.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::ECHILD)
20194    }
20195
20196    fn enabled_cpu(observation: &InvocationCpuObservation) -> &crate::cpu_evidence::LiveCpuEnabled {
20197        let LiveCpuObservation::Enabled(live) = &observation.live else {
20198            panic!("expected enabled live CPU observation: {observation:?}");
20199        };
20200        live
20201    }
20202
20203    fn measured_final_cpu(observation: &InvocationCpuObservation) -> u64 {
20204        let LaunchObservation::Spawned { pid, .. } = observation.launch else {
20205            panic!("expected a real launched process: {observation:?}");
20206        };
20207        let FinalWaitObservation::Reaped {
20208            pid: waited,
20209            cpu:
20210                WaitCpuObservation::Measured {
20211                    user_usec,
20212                    system_usec,
20213                    total_usec,
20214                },
20215            ..
20216        } = &observation.final_wait
20217        else {
20218            panic!("expected actual wait4 CPU and reap: {observation:?}");
20219        };
20220        assert_eq!(*waited, pid);
20221        assert_eq!(user_usec.checked_add(*system_usec), Some(*total_usec));
20222        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20223        *total_usec
20224    }

20226    fn validate_native_observation(observation: &InvocationCpuObservation) {

20228            version: 1,
20229            binding: CellCpuBinding {
20230                run_id: "native-cpu-fixture".into(),
20231                hermit_sha: "0".repeat(40),
20232                lane: "portable".into(),
20233                category: "fixture".into(),
20234                test: "fixture/native-cpu".into(),
20235                mode: "naked".into(),
20236                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
20237                outer_attempt: 1,
20238                run_index: RequiredNullable::Null,
20239            },

20241        }

20246    fn assert_process_observation(observation: &InvocationCpuObservation, output: &ProcessOutput) {
20247        let final_cpu = measured_final_cpu(observation);
20248        let (cpu_usec, basis) = match &observation.returned_cpu_charge {
20249            ReturnedCpuCharge::Value { cpu_usec, basis } => (*cpu_usec, basis),
20250            ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable => panic!("successful monitor return lost CPU charge"),
20251        };
20252        assert_eq!(cpu_usec, output.cpu_usage_usec);
20253        match observation.termination {
20254            TerminationPath::CpuBudgetStop => {
20255                let live = enabled_cpu(observation);
20256                let RequiredNullable::Value(trigger) = &live.timeout_trigger else {
20257                    panic!("CPU stop must retain its actual triggering sample");
20258                };
20259                assert_eq!(basis, &ChargeBasis::MaxTriggerAndFinalWait4);
20260                assert_eq!(cpu_usec, final_cpu.max(trigger.cpu_usec));
20261                assert_eq!(output.timeout, Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu));
20262            }
20263            TerminationPath::CompletedWait4
20264            | TerminationPath::FinalWaitCpuBudgetReturn
20265            | TerminationPath::WallBudgetStop => {
20266                assert_eq!(basis, &ChargeBasis::FinalWait4);
20267                assert_eq!(cpu_usec, final_cpu);
20268            }
20269            _ => panic!("unexpected successful monitor termination: {observation:?}"),
20270        }
20271        validate_native_observation(observation);
20272    }

20274    fn assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(row: &CellResult) {
20275        use crate::cpu_evidence::CellCpuHistoryV1;
20276        use crate::ledger::read_schema10_source_result;
20277
20278        let source = read_schema10_source_result(&serde_json::to_vec(row).unwrap()).unwrap();
20279        let history = CellCpuHistoryV1::from_source_rows(&[(row.attempt, source.clone())])
20280            .unwrap()
20281            .unwrap();
20282        // How a process was started is kept in memory only (LaunchObservation's
20283        // `method` is not serialized, dh-7n47nt), so every record reads back as
20284        // SpawnMethod::Unrecorded. The round trip must give back everything
20285        // else exactly, and that one field as Unrecorded.
20286        let mut recorded = row.cpu_observations.clone();
20287        for invocation in recorded.iter_mut().flat_map(|o| o.invocations.iter_mut()) {
20288            if let LaunchObservation::Spawned { method, .. } = &mut invocation.launch {
20289                *method = crate::cpu_evidence::SpawnMethod::Unrecorded;
20290            }
20291        }
20292        assert_eq!(history.attempts[0].observations(), recorded.as_ref());
20293        // `method` is #[serde(skip)] (cpu_evidence.rs:153): each read-back Spawned is Unrecorded.
20294        let read_back = history.attempts[0].observations();
20295        for invocation in read_back.iter().flat_map(|o| o.invocations.iter()) {
20296            if let LaunchObservation::Spawned { method, .. } = &invocation.launch {
20297                assert_eq!(*method, crate::cpu_evidence::SpawnMethod::Unrecorded);
20298            }
20299        }
20300        for pointer in [
20301            "/cpu_observations/binding/run_id",
20302            "/cpu_observations/invocations/0/live/polls",
20303            "/cpu_observations/invocations/0/final_wait/cpu/user_usec",
20304        ] {
20305            let mut invalid = source.clone();
20306            if let Some(value) = invalid.pointer_mut(pointer) {
20307                *value = JsonValue::String("tampered".into());
20308                assert!(
20309                    read_schema10_source_result(&serde_json::to_vec(&invalid).unwrap()).is_err(),
20310                    "{pointer}"
20311                );
20312            }
20313        }
20314    }

20316    #[test]
20317    fn owned_cpu_reader_lives_until_each_invocation_is_reaped() {
20318        use std::cell::Cell;
20319        use std::rc::Rc;
20320
20321        // The monitor must bind the real reader once and keep it until the
20322        // child is reaped; that lifetime is what this test checks. Its samples
20323        // are synthetic so the counts below stay exact on any host. A real
20324        // sample is a census of the whole host /proc with a one-second scan
20325        // deadline, and it fails as a whole when a member of this fixture's
20326        // group (the shell reaps a `sleep` every 20 ms) is reaped while the
20327        // census pairs its pidfd with its stat file ("pidfd/stat generation
20328        // mismatch"); either failure is then served to every call for 500 ms
20329        // by proccpu's shared snapshot
20330        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3822). Real samples
20331        // through the monitor, with the monitor's one-second grace for
20332        // unavailable samples, are checked by
20333        // native_zombie_then_reaped_child_has_no_double_cpu_charge (every
20334        // sample, across several 500 ms snapshots) and
20335        // a_valid_cpu_sample_resets_the_unavailable_grace (one sample).
20336        struct ObservedReader {
20337            _reader: dagrun::proccpu::ProcessGroupCpu,
20338            pid: u32,
20339            registered: Instant,
20340            dropped_after_reap: Rc<Cell<bool>>,
20341        }
20342        impl Drop for ObservedReader {
20343            fn drop(&mut self) {
20344                self.dropped_after_reap.set(owned_child_is_reaped(self.pid));
20345            }
20346        }
20347
20348        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("owned-reader-lifetime");
20349        let registered_invocations = Cell::new(0);
20350        for label in ["first", "second"] {
20351            let done = root.join(format!("{label}.done"));
20352            let (child, started, mut observation) = spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(
20353                &root,
20354                label,
20355                &format!("while [ ! -f {label}.done ]; do sleep 0.02; done"),
20356                true,
20357            );
20358            let pid = child.id();
20359            let registrations = Cell::new(0);
20360            let samples = Cell::new(0);
20361            let dropped_after_reap = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
20362            let output = monitor_process(
20363                child,
20364                ProcessLimits {
20365                    deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5),
20366                    cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20367                    cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20368                },
20369                started,
20370                &mut observation,
20371                |registered_pid| {
20372                    assert_eq!(registered_pid, pid);
20373                    registrations.set(registrations.get() + 1);
20374                    registered_invocations.set(registered_invocations.get() + 1);
20375                    dagrun::proccpu::ProcessGroupCpu::new(pid)
20376                        .map(|reader| ObservedReader {
20377                            _reader: reader,
20378                            pid,
20379                            registered: Instant::now(),
20380                            dropped_after_reap: Rc::clone(&dropped_after_reap),
20381                        })
20382                        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
20383                },
20384                |reader| {
20385                    assert!(!dropped_after_reap.get());
20386                    samples.set(samples.get() + 1);
20387                    let seconds = samples.get() as f64 / 1000.0;
20388                    if samples.get() >= 3
20389                        && reader.registered.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(700)
20390                    {
20391                        fs::write(&done, b"complete").map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
20392                    }
20393                    Ok(seconds)
20394                },
20395            )
20396            .unwrap();
20397            assert!(output.status.success());
20398            assert_eq!(output.timeout, None);
20399            assert_eq!(registrations.get(), 1);
20400            assert!(samples.get() >= 3);
20401            assert!(done.is_file(), "monitor must sample the reader for 700 ms");
20402            assert!(dropped_after_reap.get());
20403            assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20404            assert_process_observation(&observation, &output);
20405            let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20406            assert_eq!(live.registration, RegistrationObservation::BoundOnce);
20407            assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, samples.get());
20408            assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, samples.get());
20409            assert_eq!(live.unavailable_polls, 0);
20410        }
20411        // Reaped invocations may legitimately reuse a numeric PID. Each still
20412        // constructs and drops its own reader through the factory above.
20413        assert_eq!(registered_invocations.get(), 2);
20414        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20415    }
