20417    #[test]
20418    fn unavailable_cpu_registration_sampling_and_conversion_reap_the_owned_child() {
20419        use std::cell::Cell;
20420
20421        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("unavailable-reader");
20422        for failure in ["registration", "sampling", "conversion"] {
20423            let (child, started, mut observation) =
20424                spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(&root, failure, "exec sleep 20", true);
20425            let pid = child.id();
20426            let registrations = Cell::new(0);
20427            let samples = Cell::new(0);
20428            let error = monitor_process(
20429                child,
20430                ProcessLimits {
20431                    // A hang guard only (dh-ravrz): the accounting grace
20432                    // refuses at about a second; a 5 s wall deadline could
20433                    // fire first on a loaded host and return a timed-out
20434                    // Ok, hiding the refusal this test exists to see.
20435                    deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(60),
20436                    cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20437                    cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20438                },
20439                started,
20440                &mut observation,
20441                |registered_pid| {
20442                    assert_eq!(registered_pid, pid);
20443                    registrations.set(registrations.get() + 1);
20444                    if failure == "registration" {
20445                        Err("fixture registration unavailable".into())
20446                    } else {
20447                        dagrun::proccpu::ProcessGroupCpu::new(pid)
20448                            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
20449                    }
20450                },
20451                |_| {
20452                    samples.set(samples.get() + 1);
20453                    if failure == "sampling" {
20454                        Err("fixture sample unavailable".into())
20455                    } else {
20456                        Ok(f64::NAN)
20457                    }
20458                },
20459            )
20460            .map(|_| ())
20461            .expect_err("unavailable accounting must refuse the command");
20462            assert!(started.elapsed() >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE);
20463            assert_eq!(
20464                registrations.get(),
20465                1,
20466                "never retry numeric-PID registration"
20467            );
20468            if failure == "registration" {
20469                assert_eq!(samples.get(), 0);
20470                assert!(error.contains("registration: fixture registration unavailable"));
20471            } else {
20472                assert!(samples.get() > 1);
20473                if failure == "sampling" {
20474                    assert!(error.contains("sampling: fixture sample unavailable"));
20475                } else {
20476                    assert!(error.contains("invalid live CPU seconds NaN"));
20477                }
20478            }
20479            assert!(error.contains("stopped and reaped its leader"), "{error}");
20480            assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid), "{failure}: {error}");
20481            measured_final_cpu(&observation);
20482            assert_eq!(
20483                observation.termination,
20484                TerminationPath::AccountingUnavailableStop
20485            );
20486            assert_eq!(
20487                observation.returned_cpu_charge,
20488                ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable
20489            );
20490            let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20491            assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, samples.get());
20492            assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 0);
20493            assert!(live.unavailable_polls >= 2);
20494            let RequiredNullable::Value(last_error) = &live.last_error else {
20495                panic!("unavailability must retain its typed error");
20496            };
20497            assert_eq!(
20498                last_error.stage,
20499                match failure {
20500                    "registration" => CpuErrorStage::Registration,
20501                    "sampling" => CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
20502                    _ => CpuErrorStage::Conversion,
20503                }
20504            );
20505            validate_native_observation(&observation);
20506        }
20507        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20508    }

20510    #[test]
20511    fn completed_or_cpu_disabled_commands_do_not_require_live_cpu_samples() {

20514        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("optional-reader");

20517                spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(&root, "complete", "exit 0", cpu_budget_usec.is_some());
20518            let pid = child.id();
20519            let registrations = Cell::new(0);
20520            let output = monitor_process(
20521                child,
20522                ProcessLimits {
20523                    deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5),
20524                    cpu_budget_usec,
20525                    cpu_poll_interval: Duration::from_secs(5),
20526                },
20527                started,
20528                &mut observation,
20529                |_| -> Result<(), String> {
20530                    assert!(
20531                        cpu_budget_usec.is_some(),
20532                        "disabled accounting must not register"
20533                    );
20534                    registrations.set(registrations.get() + 1);
20535                    Err("fixture registration unavailable".into())
20536                },
20537                |_| panic!("wait4 completion must precede live sampling"),
20538            )
20539            .unwrap();
20540            assert!(output.status.success());
20541            assert_eq!(output.timeout, None);
20542            assert_eq!(registrations.get(), usize::from(cpu_budget_usec.is_some()));
20543            assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20544            assert_process_observation(&observation, &output);
20545            if cpu_budget_usec.is_some() {
20546                let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20547                assert_eq!(live.polls, 0);
20548                assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, 0);
20549                assert!(matches!(
20550                    live.registration,
20551                    RegistrationObservation::Unavailable { .. }
20552                ));
20553            } else {
20554                assert_eq!(observation.live, LiveCpuObservation::Disabled);
20555            }
20556        }
20557        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20558    }

20560    #[test]
20561    fn a_valid_cpu_sample_resets_the_unavailable_grace() {
20562        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("reader-grace-reset");
20563        let done = root.join("done");
20564        let (child, started, mut observation) = spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(
20565            &root,
20566            "reset",
20567            "while [ ! -f done ]; do sleep 0.02; done",
20568            true,
20569        );
20570        let pid = child.id();
20571        let mut first_missing = None;
20572        let mut valid_samples = 0;
20573        let mut missing_after_valid = 0;
20574        // The one valid sample comes one poll interval before the original grace
20575        // ends, and it is synthetic, so the sequence does not depend on host
20576        // load. A failed poll before it is less than the grace after the first
20577        // failure, and any later poll is itself the valid one, so the original
20578        // grace cannot stop the command first. The grace then restarts at the next
20579        // failure, about one grace after the first one, and `done` is written at
20580        // that first post-valid failure, which leaves the whole restarted grace
20581        // for the child to exit and be reaped (dh-ravrz).
20582        //
20583        // This test used to take the valid sample at 500 ms from a real host-wide
20584        // /proc census (`ProcessGroupCpu::seconds`), which under load can be slow
20585        // or refused (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3822), and it left
20586        // the child about 0.4 s to exit (measured: done written at 1.32 s, the
20587        // restarted grace due at 1.72 s). It failed under host load 155-173.
20588        let output = monitor_process(
20589            child,
20590            ProcessLimits {
20591                // A hang guard only: the run ends about 1.4 s in (measured 1.34 to
20592                // 1.37 s with the earlier timeline, free or pinned to one CPU).
20593                deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5),
20594                cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20595                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20596            },
20597            started,
20598            &mut observation,
20599            |_| Ok(()),
20600            |_| {
20601                let first = *first_missing.get_or_insert_with(Instant::now);
20602                if valid_samples == 0
20603                    && first.elapsed() >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE - CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL
20604                {
20605                    valid_samples += 1;
20606                    return Ok(0.0);
20607                }
20608                if valid_samples > 0 {
20609                    missing_after_valid += 1;
20610                    // Write `done` at the FIRST missing sample after the
20611                    // valid one (dh-ravrz): the child then has the whole
20612                    // restarted grace - about a second of wall, however
20613                    // the polls are spaced under load - to exit and be
20614                    // reaped before the grace can stop it. The wall-timed
20615                    // write before (grace + 200 ms) left that exit to the
20616                    // last fifth of the window and failed under load.
20617                    fs::write(&done, b"complete").map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
20618                }
20619                Err("fixture transient sample unavailable".into())
20620            },
20621        )
20622        .unwrap();
20623        assert!(output.status.success());
20624        assert_eq!(output.timeout, None);
20625        assert_eq!(valid_samples, 1);
20626        assert!(missing_after_valid > 0);
20627        assert!(
20628            done.is_file(),
20629            "must survive beyond the original missing grace"
20630        );
20631        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20632        assert_process_observation(&observation, &output);
20633        let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20634        assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 1);
20635        assert!(live.unavailable_polls > 1);
20636        assert!(matches!(live.last_error, RequiredNullable::Value(_)));
20637        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20638    }

20640    #[test]
20641    fn a_slow_failed_sample_does_not_use_up_the_unavailable_grace() {
20642        // One host-wide /proc census can outlast the whole grace. proccpu then
20643        // refuses it ("scan deadline") and serves that refusal again for 500 ms
20644        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3822). The grace is timed
20645        // from when the failed sample returned, so the refusal served right
20646        // after a slow census cannot stop the command before a fresh sample
20647        // runs. The samples are synthetic so the sequence is exact on any host.
20648        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("reader-slow-failure");
20649        let done = root.join("done");
20650        let (child, started, mut observation) = spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(
20651            &root,
20652            "slow",
20653            "while [ ! -f done ]; do sleep 0.02; done",
20654            true,
20655        );
20656        let pid = child.id();
20657        let mut samples = 0;
20658        let output = monitor_process(
20659            child,
20660            ProcessLimits {
20661                deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10),
20662                cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20663                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20664            },
20665            started,
20666            &mut observation,
20667            |_| Ok(()),
20668            |_| {
20669                samples += 1;
20670                match samples {
20671                    1 => {
20672                        std::thread::sleep(CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE + Duration::from_millis(200));
20673                        Err("fixture scan deadline".into())
20674                    }
20675                    2 => Err("fixture scan deadline".into()),
20676                    _ => {
20677                        fs::write(&done, b"complete").map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
20678                        Ok(0.0)
20679                    }
20680                }
20681            },
20682        )
20683        .expect("a slow failed sample followed by a valid one must not stop the command");
20684        assert!(output.status.success());
20685        assert_eq!(output.timeout, None);
20686        assert!(started.elapsed() > CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE);
20687        assert!(samples >= 3);
20688        assert!(done.is_file());
20689        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20690        assert_process_observation(&observation, &output);
20691        let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20692        assert_eq!(live.unavailable_polls, 2);
20693        assert!(live.valid_polls >= 1);
20694        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20695    }

20697    #[test]
20698    fn a_slow_census_that_keeps_failing_still_stops_the_command() {
20699        // The refusal above never clears here: every fresh census takes 1 s and
20700        // fails, and its refusal is served again for 500 ms, as proccpu does
20701        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3822). The command must
20702        // still be stopped and reaped through the accounting stop, at least
20703        // the grace after the first failed census returned. The grace is only
20704        // checked when a sample returns, so the census running when it expires
20705        // adds its own length: there is no fixed stop time.
20706        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("reader-slow-permanent-failure");
20707        let (child, started, mut observation) =
20708            spawn_cpu_reader_fixture(&root, "permanent", "exec sleep 30", true);
20709        let pid = child.id();
20710        let mut censuses = 0;
20711        let mut last_census_returned: Option<Instant> = None;
20712        let mut first_census_returned: Option<Instant> = None;
20713        let result = monitor_process(
20714            child,
20715            ProcessLimits {
20716                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(15),
20717                cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20718                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20719            },
20720            started,
20721            &mut observation,
20722            |_| Ok(()),
20723            |_| {
20724                if last_census_returned
20725                    .is_none_or(|returned| returned.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(500))
20726                {
20727                    censuses += 1;
20728                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1));
20729                    let returned = Instant::now();
20730                    last_census_returned = Some(returned);
20731                    first_census_returned.get_or_insert(returned);
20732                }
20733                Err("fixture scan deadline".into())
20734            },
20735        );
20736        let error = result
20737            .map(|_| ())
20738            .expect_err("a census that never succeeds must stop the command");
20739        assert!(error.contains("sampling: fixture scan deadline"), "{error}");
20740        assert_eq!(
20741            observation.termination,
20742            TerminationPath::AccountingUnavailableStop
20743        );
20744        assert!(first_census_returned.unwrap().elapsed() >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE);
20745        // The cached refusal ends 500 ms after the first census returns, inside
20746        // the grace, so a fresh census ran before the stop.
20747        assert!(censuses >= 2, "{censuses}");
20748        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20749        let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20750        assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 0);
20751        assert!(live.unavailable_polls >= 2);
20752        measured_final_cpu(&observation);
20753        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20754    }

20756    #[test]
20757    fn monotonic_cpu_sampler_refuses_a_decrease_and_keeps_the_high_value() {
20758        let mut reads = vec![
20759            Ok(5),
20760            Ok(5),
20761            Ok(7),
20762            Ok(6),
20763            Err("fixture read failure".to_string()),
20764            Ok(6),
20765            Ok(7),
20766            Ok(9),
20767        ]
20768        .into_iter();
20769        let mut sample = monotonic_cpu_sampler(move || reads.next().unwrap());
20770        let decreased = Err(CpuError {
20771            stage: CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
20772            reason: "sampling: cgroup CPU counter decreased from 7 to 6 usec".into(),
20773        });
20774        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), Ok(5));
20775        assert_eq!(
20776            sample(1, &()),
20777            Ok(5),
20778            "an unchanged counter is a valid sample"
20779        );
20780        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), Ok(7));
20781        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), decreased);
20782        assert_eq!(
20783            sample(1, &()),
20784            Err(CpuError {
20785                stage: CpuErrorStage::Sampling,
20786                reason: "sampling: fixture read failure".into(),
20787            })
20788        );
20789        // The refused values never lower the bar: 6 is still below 7.
20790        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), decreased);
20791        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), Ok(7));
20792        assert_eq!(sample(1, &()), Ok(9));
20793    }

20795    #[test]
20796    fn a_decreasing_cgroup_sample_is_refused_after_the_unavailable_grace() {
20797        use std::cell::Cell;
20798
20799        // The kernel never lowers a cgroup's usage_usec, so a lower reading is
20800        // not this invocation's counter. It is a failed sample, timed from when
20801        // it returned, and a counter that stays low stops the command once the
20802        // unavailable grace has passed, exactly as a failed proccpu census does.
20803        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("cgroup-decrease");
20804        let (child, started, mut observation) = spawn_fixture_with_source(
20805            &root,
20806            "decrease",
20807            "exec sleep 30",
20808            Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
20809        );
20810        let pid = child.id();
20811        let reads = Cell::new(0u64);
20812        let first_decrease_returned = Cell::new(None::<Instant>);
20813        let error = monitor_live_cpu(
20814            child,
20815            ProcessLimits {
20816                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(15),
20817                cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
20818                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
20819            },
20820            started,
20821            &mut observation,
20822            |_| Ok(()),
20823            monotonic_cpu_sampler(|| {
20824                reads.set(reads.get() + 1);
20825                Ok(match reads.get() {
20826                    1 => 100,
20827                    2 => 200,
20828                    _ => {
20829                        if first_decrease_returned.get().is_none() {
20830                            first_decrease_returned.set(Some(Instant::now()));
20831                        }
20832                        150
20833                    }
20834                })
20835            }),
20836        )
20837        .map(|_| ())
20838        .expect_err("a cgroup counter that stays below its high value must stop the command");
20839        assert!(
20840            error.contains("sampling: cgroup CPU counter decreased from 200 to 150 usec"),
20841            "{error}"
20842        );
20843        assert!(error.contains("stopped and reaped its leader"), "{error}");
20844        assert_eq!(
20845            observation.termination,
20846            TerminationPath::AccountingUnavailableStop
20847        );
20848        assert!(
20849            first_decrease_returned.get().unwrap().elapsed() >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE,
20850            "stopped before the grace had passed since the first decrease"
20851        );
20852        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
20853        measured_final_cpu(&observation);
20854        assert_eq!(
20855            observation.returned_cpu_charge,
20856            ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable
20857        );
20858        let live = enabled_cpu(&observation);
20859        assert_eq!(live.source, LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1);
20860        assert_eq!(live.registration, RegistrationObservation::BoundOnce);
20861        assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 2);
20862        assert!(live.unavailable_polls >= 2);
20863        assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, live.polls);
20864        let (RequiredNullable::Value(high), RequiredNullable::Value(last)) =
20865            (&live.high_water, &live.last)
20866        else {
20867            panic!("two valid samples must leave points: {live:?}");
20868        };
20869        assert_eq!((high.cpu_usec, last.cpu_usec), (200, 200));
20870        let RequiredNullable::Value(last_error) = &live.last_error else {
20871            panic!("a refused decrease must retain its typed error");
20872        };
20873        assert_eq!(last_error.stage, CpuErrorStage::Sampling);
20874        validate_native_observation(&observation);
20875        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
20876    }

20942    #[test]
20943    fn live_cpu_conversion_refuses_unrepresentable_values() {
20944        assert_eq!(live_cpu_usage_usec(42, 0.0), Ok(0));
20945        assert_eq!(live_cpu_usage_usec(42, 0.125), Ok(125_000));
20946        for seconds in [
20947            -0.0,
20948            -1.0,
20949            f64::NAN,
20950            f64::INFINITY,
20951            f64::NEG_INFINITY,
20952            u64::MAX as f64 / 1_000_000.0,
20953        ] {
20954            assert!(live_cpu_usage_usec(42, seconds).is_err(), "{seconds}");
20955        }
20956        // Converting the adjacent float to seconds and back rounds up to 2^64.
20957        let adjacent_usec = f64::from_bits((u64::MAX as f64).to_bits() - 1);
20958        assert!(live_cpu_usage_usec(42, adjacent_usec / 1_000_000.0).is_err());
20959        let representable_usec = f64::from_bits((u64::MAX as f64).to_bits() - 2);
20960        assert!(live_cpu_usage_usec(42, representable_usec / 1_000_000.0).is_ok());
20961    }

21008    #[test]
21009    fn actual_fd_reserve_refusal_preserves_unavailable_cpu_and_reap() {
21010        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_TEST_CPU_FD_RESERVE_CHILD";
21011        const CASE: &str =
21012            "runner::tests::actual_fd_reserve_refusal_preserves_unavailable_cpu_and_reap";
21013        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_none() {
21014            // setrlimit is process-wide: keep it out of the parallel libtest
21015            // process, and select only this case in the isolated child.
21016            let output = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
21017                .args(["--exact", CASE, "--nocapture"])
21018                .env(CHILD, "1")
21019                .output()
21020                .unwrap();
21021            assert!(
21022                output.status.success(),
21023                "{}\n{}",
21024                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
21025                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
21026            );
21027            print!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));
21028            return;
21029        }
21030        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("actual-fd-reserve");
21031        // The descriptor reserve is the agent-utils reader's own refusal, and
21032        // the runner uses that reader only for a run without cgroups. Run as
21033        // one: the fallback marker is set and no cgroup can be created.
21034        let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(true), Some(root.join("missing-cgroup-parent")));
21035        let context = run_context(&root);
21036        let cell = native_cpu_cell("exec sleep 20", 1);
21037        let mut limit = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::rlimit>() };
21038        assert_eq!(
21039            unsafe { libc::getrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_NOFILE, &mut limit) },
21040            0
21041        );
21042        assert!(limit.rlim_cur >= 32);
21043        limit.rlim_cur = 32;
21044        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::setrlimit(libc::RLIMIT_NOFILE, &limit) }, 0);
21045        let started = Instant::now();
21046        let failure =
21047            run_cell(&context, &cell).expect_err("real descriptor reserve refusal must fail");
21048        assert!(started.elapsed() >= CELL_CPU_ACCOUNTING_GRACE, "{failure}");
21049        assert!(
21050            failure
21051                .to_string()
21052                .contains("registration: descriptor reserve"),
21053            "{failure}"
21054        );
21055        let row = failure.into_result(&context, &cell);
21056        assert_eq!(row.outcome, "ERROR");
21057        assert_eq!(row.cpu_usage_usec, None);
21058        assert!(row.attempts.is_empty());
21059        row.require_cpu_observations().unwrap();
21060        let observations = row.cpu_observations.as_ref().unwrap();
21061        assert_eq!(observations.invocations.len(), 1);
21062        let invocation = &observations.invocations[0];
21063        assert_eq!(
21064            invocation.termination,
21065            TerminationPath::AccountingUnavailableStop
21066        );
21067        assert_eq!(
21068            invocation.returned_cpu_charge,
21069            ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable
21070        );
21071        measured_final_cpu(invocation);
21072        let live = enabled_cpu(invocation);
21073        assert_eq!(live.source, LiveCpuSource::AgentUtilsPairedPidfdStatV1);
21074        assert_eq!(
21075            live.registration,
21076            RegistrationObservation::Unavailable {
21077                reason: "descriptor reserve".into()
21078            }
21079        );
21080        assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, 0);
21081        assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 0);
21082        assert!(live.unavailable_polls >= 2);
21083        assert_eq!(live.first, RequiredNullable::Null);
21084        assert_eq!(live.high_water, RequiredNullable::Null);
21085        assert_eq!(live.timeout_trigger, RequiredNullable::Null);
21086        let ledger = root.join("results.jsonl");
21087        append_result(&ledger, &row).unwrap();
21088        let bytes = fs::read(&ledger).unwrap();
21089        let decoded: CellResult = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).unwrap();
21090        decoded.require_cpu_observations().unwrap();
21091        assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(&decoded);
21092        println!(
21093            "CPU_FD_REFUSAL_ROW {}",
21094            String::from_utf8(bytes).unwrap().trim()
21095        );
21096        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21097    }

21099    /// The cgroup v2 directory named by the unified line of a saved copy of
21100    /// `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.
21101    fn saved_cgroup_directory(saved: &Path) -> PathBuf {
21102        let text = fs::read_to_string(saved).unwrap();
21103        let relative = text
21104            .lines()
21105            .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("0::"))
21106            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no unified cgroup line in {text:?}"));
21107        Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup").join(relative.trim_start_matches('/'))
21108    }

21110    #[test]
21111    fn a_boxed_run_whose_invocation_cgroup_cannot_be_created_still_stops_the_cell() {
21112        // A boxed run carries no fallback marker. When it cannot create the
21113        // invocation cgroup, it has no CPU source, so the command is refused
21114        // before it starts and the cell is an ERROR. It is never measured some
21115        // other way, its budget is never dropped, and it never runs unmeasured,
21116        // not even for the unavailable grace.
21117        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("boxed-without-cgroup");
21118        let plain = root.join("plain-directory");
21119        fs::create_dir(&plain).unwrap();
21120        for (label, parent) in [
21121            ("missing", root.join("missing-cgroup-parent")),
21122            ("plain", plain.clone()),
21123        ] {
21124            let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(false), Some(parent.clone()));
21125            let case = root.join(label);
21126            fs::create_dir(&case).unwrap();
21127            let ran = case.join("command-started");
21128            let context = run_context(&case);
21129            let cell = native_cpu_cell(
21130                &format!("printf started > '{}'; exec sleep 20", ran.display()),
21131                1,
21132            );
21133            let failure = run_cell(&context, &cell)
21134                .expect_err("a budgeted command with no CPU source must not complete");
21135            assert!(!ran.exists(), "{label}: a refused command ran: {failure}");
21136            let message = failure.to_string();
21137            for expected in [
21138                parent.to_str().unwrap(),
21139                "only a run given no cgroups on purpose may set HERMIT_E2E_ALLOW_PROCESS_GROUP_CPU_SCAN=1",
21140                "refused before launch",
21141            ] {
21142                assert!(
21143                    message.contains(expected),
21144                    "{label}: {expected:?} in {message}"
21145                );
21146            }
21147            let row = failure.into_result(&context, &cell);
21148            assert_eq!(row.outcome, "ERROR", "{label}");
21149            assert_eq!(row.cpu_usage_usec, None, "{label}");
21150            assert!(row.attempts.is_empty(), "{label}");
21151            row.require_cpu_observations().unwrap();
21152            let observations = row.cpu_observations.as_ref().unwrap();
21153            assert_eq!(observations.invocations.len(), 1, "{label}");
21154            let invocation = &observations.invocations[0];
21155            assert_eq!(
21156                invocation.termination,
21157                TerminationPath::SpawnFailed,
21158                "{label}"
21159            );
21160            assert_eq!(
21161                invocation.returned_cpu_charge,
21162                ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable,
21163                "{label}"
21164            );
21165            assert_eq!(
21166                invocation.final_wait,
21167                FinalWaitObservation::NotApplicable,
21168                "{label}"
21169            );
21170            let launch = serde_json::to_value(&invocation.launch).unwrap();
21171            assert_eq!(launch["state"], "spawn_failed", "{label}: {launch}");
21172            assert_eq!(launch["stage"], "live_cpu_meter", "{label}: {launch}");
21173            assert!(
21174                launch["reason"]
21175                    .as_str()
21176                    .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains(parent.to_str().unwrap())),
21177                "{label}: {launch}"
21178            );
21179            let live = enabled_cpu(invocation);
21180            assert_eq!(
21181                live.source,
21182                LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1,
21183                "{label}"
21184            );
21185            assert_eq!(
21186                live.registration,
21187                RegistrationObservation::NotAttempted,
21188                "{label}"
21189            );
21190            assert_eq!(live.polls, 0, "{label}");
21191            assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, 0, "{label}");
21192            assert_eq!(live.valid_polls, 0, "{label}");
21193            assert_eq!(live.last_error, RequiredNullable::Null, "{label}");
21194            assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(&row);
21195        }
21196        assert_eq!(fs::read_dir(&plain).unwrap().count(), 0);
21197        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21198    }

21200    #[test]
21201    fn a_boxed_run_without_an_invocation_cgroup_refuses_quick_commands_before_any_runs() {
21202        // Two commands that would each finish well inside the one-second
21203        // unavailable grace. A meter that was never established is not a live
21204        // meter that failed: the first command is refused before it starts,
21205        // so neither runs unmeasured and the cell can never pass.
21206        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("boxed-quick-without-cgroup");
21207        let parent = root.join("missing-cgroup-parent");
21208        let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(false), Some(parent.clone()));
21209        let ran = root.join("commands-that-ran");
21210        let context = run_context(&root);
21211        // Each run prints its own leader PID, so the naked cell's rule that
21212        // its two runs differ is met and nothing but the refusal can fail it.
21213        let cell = native_cpu_cell(
21214            &format!("printf ran >> '{}'; printf '%s\\n' \"$$\"", ran.display()),
21215            2,
21216        );
21217        let failure = match run_cell(&context, &cell) {
21218            Ok(row) => panic!(
21219                "a budgeted command with no CPU source completed as {} with CPU {:?}; \
21220                 commands that ran: {:?}",
21221                row.outcome,
21222                row.cpu_usage_usec,
21223                fs::read_to_string(&ran)
21224            ),
21225            Err(failure) => failure,
21226        };
21227        assert!(
21228            !ran.exists(),
21229            "refused commands ran: {:?}: {failure}",
21230            fs::read_to_string(&ran)
21231        );
21232        let message = failure.to_string();
21233        assert!(message.contains(parent.to_str().unwrap()), "{message}");
21234        assert!(message.contains("refused before launch"), "{message}");
21235        let row = failure.into_result(&context, &cell);
21236        assert_eq!(row.outcome, "ERROR");
21237        assert_eq!(row.cpu_usage_usec, None);
21238        assert!(row.attempts.is_empty());
21239        row.require_cpu_observations().unwrap();
21240        let observations = row.cpu_observations.as_ref().unwrap();
21241        assert_eq!(observations.invocations.len(), 1);
21242        let invocation = &observations.invocations[0];
21243        assert_eq!(invocation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
21244        assert_eq!(invocation.final_wait, FinalWaitObservation::NotApplicable);
21245        let launch = serde_json::to_value(&invocation.launch).unwrap();
21246        assert_eq!(launch["stage"], "live_cpu_meter", "{launch}");
21247        assert_eq!(enabled_cpu(invocation).polls, 0);
21248        assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(&row);
21249        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21250    }

21252    #[test]
21253    fn the_fallback_marker_does_not_hide_an_ineligible_cgroup_failure() {
21254        // The marker allows the process-group scan only when no cgroup can be
21255        // made here at all. A parent that is not a directory is a broken setup,
21256        // not a run without cgroups, so the command is still refused, before
21257        // even its capture files are created.
21258        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("marker-ineligible");
21259        let parent = root.join("regular-file");
21260        fs::write(&parent, b"").unwrap();
21261        let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(true), Some(parent.clone()));
21262        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
21263            InvocationRole::Execution {
21264                attempt_index: "1".into(),
21265                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
21266            },
21267            &root,
21268            "/bin/sh",
21269            &["-c".into(), "exec sleep 20".into()],
21270            &BTreeMap::new(),
21271            &root.join("ineligible.stdout"),
21272            &root.join("ineligible.stderr"),
21273        );
21274        let mut observations = Vec::new();
21275        let started = Instant::now();
21276        let error = execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
21277            request,
21278            ProcessLimits {
21279                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(10),
21280                cpu_budget_usec: Some(5_000_000),
21281                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
21282            },
21283            &mut observations,
21284        )
21285        .map(|_| ())
21286        .expect_err("an ineligible cgroup failure must refuse the command");
21287        assert!(error.contains("refused before launch"), "{error}");
21288        assert!(error.contains("Not a directory"), "{error}");
21289        assert!(!error.contains("only a run given no cgroups"), "{error}");
21290        assert!(!root.join("ineligible.stdout").exists(), "{error}");
21291        assert!(!root.join("ineligible.stderr").exists(), "{error}");
21292        assert_eq!(observations.len(), 1);
21293        let observation = &observations[0];
21294        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
21295        assert_eq!(observation.final_wait, FinalWaitObservation::NotApplicable);
21296        assert_eq!(
21297            observation.returned_cpu_charge,
21298            ReturnedCpuCharge::Unavailable
21299        );
21300        let launch = serde_json::to_value(&observation.launch).unwrap();
21301        assert_eq!(launch["stage"], "live_cpu_meter", "{launch}");
21302        let live = enabled_cpu(observation);
21303        assert_eq!(live.source, LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1);
21304        assert_eq!(live.registration, RegistrationObservation::NotAttempted);
21305        assert_eq!(live.polls, 0);
21306        assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, 0);
21307        validate_native_observation(observation);
21308        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21309    }

21311    #[test]
21312    fn a_run_without_cgroups_measures_with_the_process_group_scan_under_its_own_source_name() {
21313        const CHILD: &str = "HERMIT_TEST_PROCESS_GROUP_SCAN_ROW_CHILD";
21314        const CASE: &str = "runner::tests::a_run_without_cgroups_measures_with_the_process_group_scan_under_its_own_source_name";
21315        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_none() {
21316            // The assertion below is that a budgeted command that lives long
21317            // enough is polled at least once. In the parallel libtest process
21318            // every other test's monitor queues on the same process-global CPU
21319            // registry and session census, and a monitor can be delayed past
21320            // its command's whole life, so the measurement is made in an
21321            // isolated child process, as the descriptor-reserve test above
21322            // isolates its process-wide rlimit.
21323            let output = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
21324                .args(["--exact", CASE, "--nocapture"])
21325                .env(CHILD, "1")
21326                .output()
21327                .unwrap();
21328            assert!(
21329                output.status.success(),
21330                "{}\n{}",
21331                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
21332                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
21333            );
21334            print!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));
21335            return;
21336        }
21337        // With the marker set and no cgroup available, the agent-utils scan
21338        // measures the command, and every row says so: no row of such a run
21339        // carries the cgroup source, so no reader can count it as one.
21340        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("declared-without-cgroup");
21341        let plain = root.join("plain-directory");
21342        fs::create_dir(&plain).unwrap();
21343        for (label, parent) in [
21344            ("missing", root.join("missing-cgroup-parent")),
21345            ("plain", plain.clone()),
21346        ] {
21347            let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(true), Some(parent));
21348            let case = root.join(label);
21349            fs::create_dir(&case).unwrap();
21350            let context = run_context(&case);
21351            // Long enough for a poll after the scan's registration, which can
21352            // take most of its 1 s deadline on a loaded host.
21353            let cell = native_cpu_cell("exec sleep 1.5", 1);
21354            let row = run_cell(&context, &cell).unwrap();
21355            // A naked cell needs two distinct outcomes to pass, so this single
21356            // run is judged by its attempt: the command ran to a normal exit.
21357            assert_eq!(row.error_kind, None, "{label}: {row:?}");
21358            assert_eq!(row.attempts.len(), 1, "{label}: {row:?}");
21359            assert_eq!(row.attempts[0].outcome, "PASS", "{label}: {row:?}");
21360            assert_eq!(row.attempts[0].status, Some(0), "{label}");
21361            row.require_cpu_observations().unwrap();
21362            let observations = row.cpu_observations.as_ref().unwrap();
21363            assert_eq!(observations.invocations.len(), 1, "{label}");
21364            let invocation = &observations.invocations[0];
21365            assert_eq!(
21366                invocation.termination,
21367                TerminationPath::CompletedWait4,
21368                "{label}"
21369            );
21370            let live = enabled_cpu(invocation);
21371            assert_eq!(
21372                live.source,
21373                LiveCpuSource::AgentUtilsPairedPidfdStatV1,
21374                "{label}"
21375            );
21376            assert_eq!(
21377                live.registration,
21378                RegistrationObservation::BoundOnce,
21379                "{label}"
21380            );
21381            assert!(live.polls >= 1, "{label}: {live:?}");
21382            assert_eq!(live.source_sample_calls, live.polls, "{label}");
21383            let json = serde_json::to_string(&row).unwrap();
21384            assert!(
21385                json.contains(r#""source":"agent_utils_paired_pidfd_stat_v1""#),
21386                "{label}: {json}"
21387            );
21388            assert!(
21389                !json.contains("cgroup_v2_invocation_cpu_stat_v1"),
21390                "{label}: {json}"
21391            );
21392            assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(&row);
21393        }
21394        assert_eq!(fs::read_dir(&plain).unwrap().count(), 0);
21395        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21396    }

21413                output.status.success(),

21421        let test = "a_budgeted_cell_row_names_the_invocation_cgroup_as_its_cpu_source";
21422        let Some(probe) = crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)
21423        else {

21427        // The production plan, minus the marker: the cgroup is created under

21444        assert_eq!(row.attempts[0].outcome, "PASS", "{row:?}");

21477    /// The production order, driven through the same helper the
21478    /// budgeted path calls: with room for exactly one live cgroup
21479    /// at a time, the probe is created and dropped before the real
21480    /// allocation, and both complete. Reversing the helper's order
21481    /// leaves the slot held when the probe asks for it, the probe
21482    /// records `unavailable`, and this test fails.
21483    #[test]
21484    fn the_probe_finishes_before_the_first_real_cgroup_is_allocated() {
21485        use std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize;
21486        struct Slot {
21487            live: std::sync::Arc<AtomicUsize>,
21488            events: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<&'static str>>>,
21489        }
21490        impl Drop for Slot {
21491            fn drop(&mut self) {
21492                self.events.lock().unwrap().push("probe-drop");
21493                self.live.fetch_sub(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
21494            }
21495        }
21496        let live = std::sync::Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
21497        let events = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
21498        let plan = LiveCpuPlan {
21499            allow_process_group_scan: Ok(false),
21500            cgroup_parent: None,
21501        };
21502        let support = std::sync::Arc::new(crate::vfork_spawn::Clone3Support::new());
21503        let create =
21504            |live: &std::sync::Arc<AtomicUsize>,
21505             events: &std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<&'static str>>>| {
21506                if live.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) != 0 {
21507                    live.fetch_sub(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
21508                    return None;
21509                }
21510                events.lock().unwrap().push("probe-create");
21511                Some((
21512                    -1,
21513                    Box::new(Slot {
21514                        live: std::sync::Arc::clone(live),
21515                        events: std::sync::Arc::clone(events),
21516                    }) as Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>,
21517                ))
21518            };
21519        let real = probe_before_first_real_cgroup(
21520            || {
21521                let live = std::sync::Arc::clone(&live);
21522                let events = std::sync::Arc::clone(&events);
21523                probe_clone3_for_the_run_with(&plan, &support, move || create(&live, &events))
21524            },
21525            || {
21526                if live.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) != 0 {
21527                    live.fetch_sub(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
21528                    return Err("the probe still holds the only cgroup slot".to_string());
21529                }
21530                events.lock().unwrap().push("real-create");
21531                Ok(())
21532            },
21533        );
21534        assert_eq!(real, Ok(()));
21535        let record = support.cgroup_probe_record().expect("probe ran");
21536        assert_eq!(record.outcome, "no_verdict");
21537        assert_eq!(
21538            events.lock().unwrap().as_slice(),
21539            ["probe-create", "probe-drop", "real-create"]
21540        );
21541    }
21542
21543    /// The run-level probe record is written exactly once, even
21544    /// when cells finish concurrently: one writer wins, and the file
21545    /// holds that record.
21546    #[test]
21547    fn the_probe_record_file_is_written_once() {
21548        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("probe-record-once");
21549        let dir = root.join("runs").join("fixture-run");
21550        let record = crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord {
21551            outcome: "usable".to_string(),
21552            kernel: "test-kernel".to_string(),
21553            reason: None,
21554            child_wait: "pidfd".to_string(),
21555        };
21556        let written = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(false));
21557        let wins = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
21558        let threads: Vec<_> = (0..8)
21559            .map(|_| {
21560                let dir = dir.clone();
21561                let record = record.clone();
21562                let written = std::sync::Arc::clone(&written);
21563                let wins = std::sync::Arc::clone(&wins);
21564                std::thread::spawn(move || {
21565                    if write_probe_record_once(&dir, &record, &written).unwrap() {
21566                        wins.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
21567                    }
21568                })
21569            })
21570            .collect();
21571        for thread in threads {
21572            thread.join().unwrap();
21573        }
21574        assert_eq!(wins.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed), 1);
21575        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("clone3-probe.json")).unwrap();
21576        let back: crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
21577        assert_eq!(back, record);
21578        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21579    }
21580
21581    /// A failed probe-record write is a named error, and it does not
21582    /// consume the once: with the obstacle gone, the next attempt
21583    /// writes the record.
21584    /// The record_cell failed-write path at cell level: the write
21585    /// is refused (the run directory's parent is a file), the cell
21586    /// fails by that name, and the failure still carries the
21587    /// completed attempt's invocations.
21588    #[test]
21589    fn a_failed_probe_record_write_fails_the_cell_with_its_invocations() {
21590        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("probe-record-cell");
21591        let mut context = run_context(&root);
21592        let blocker = root.join("blocker");
21593        std::fs::write(&blocker, b"not a directory").unwrap();
21594        context.result_root = blocker;
21595        let cell = native_cpu_cell("/bin/true", 1);
21596        let record = crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord {
21597            outcome: "usable".to_string(),
21598            kernel: "test-kernel".to_string(),
21599            reason: None,
21600            child_wait: "pidfd".to_string(),
21601        };
21602        let failure = record_cell_with_probe_record_in_state(
21603            &context,
21604            &cell,
21605            || Some(record.clone()),
21606            &std::sync::Mutex::new(false),
21607            |progress| {
21608                progress
21609                    .observations
21610                    .push(InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
21611                        1,
21612                        InvocationRole::Preparation,
21613                        CommandIdentity {
21614                            argv: vec!["/bin/true".to_string()],
21615                            cwd: "/".to_string(),
21616                            env_overrides: BTreeMap::new(),
21617                        },
21618                        None,
21619                    ));
21620                Err("cell failed".to_string())
21621            },
21622        )
21623        .expect_err("the record write must fail this cell");
21624        assert!(
21625            failure.reason.contains("clone3 probe record"),
21626            "{}",
21627            failure.reason
21628        );
21629        assert_eq!(failure.observations.invocations.len(), 1);
21630        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21631    }

21633    /// The first cell of a process publishes the probe record
21634    /// that only came into existence during that cell: the record
21635    /// is read after the run, not snapshotted before it. With the
21636    /// old order (read before the run) the getter sees nothing and
21637    /// no file is written, and this test fails.
21638    #[test]
21639    fn the_first_cell_publishes_the_probe_record_it_ran_with() {
21640        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("probe-record-first-cell");
21641        let context = run_context(&root);
21642        let cell = native_cpu_cell("/bin/true", 1);
21643        let during_run = std::cell::RefCell::new(None);
21644        let result = record_cell_with_probe_record_in_state(
21645            &context,
21646            &cell,
21647            || during_run.borrow().clone(),
21648            &std::sync::Mutex::new(false),
21649            |_progress| {
21650                *during_run.borrow_mut() = Some(crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord {
21651                    outcome: "usable".to_string(),
21652                    kernel: "test-kernel".to_string(),
21653                    reason: None,
21654                    child_wait: "pidfd".to_string(),
21655                });
21656                Err("cell failed".to_string())
21657            },
21658        );
21659        assert!(result.is_err());
21660        let file = root
21661            .join("results")
21662            .join("runs")
21663            .join("fixture")
21664            .join("clone3-probe.json");
21665        let text =
21666            std::fs::read_to_string(&file).expect("the first cell must publish its probe record");
21667        let back: crate::vfork_spawn::CgroupProbeRecord = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
21668        assert_eq!(back.outcome, "usable");
21669        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21670    }

21693    #[test]
21694    fn a_malformed_fallback_marker_refuses_the_budgeted_command_before_launch() {
21695        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("malformed-marker");
21696        for value in ["0", "yes", ""] {
21697            let allow = process_group_scan_allowed(Some(OsStr::new(value)));
21698            assert!(allow.is_err(), "{value:?}");
21699            let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(allow, None);
21700            let label = format!("marker-{}", value.len());
21701            let request = |label: &str| {
21702                ProcessRequest::new(
21703                    InvocationRole::Execution {
21704                        attempt_index: "1".into(),
21705                        backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
21706                    },
21707                    &root,
21708                    "/bin/sh",
21709                    &["-c".into(), "exit 0".into()],
21710                    &BTreeMap::new(),
21711                    &root.join(format!("{label}.stdout")),
21712                    &root.join(format!("{label}.stderr")),
21713                )
21714            };
21715            let mut observations = Vec::new();
21716            let error = execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
21717                request(&label),
21718                ProcessLimits {
21719                    deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5),
21720                    cpu_budget_usec: Some(1_000_000),
21721                    cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
21722                },
21723                &mut observations,
21724            )
21725            .map(|_| ())
21726            .expect_err("a malformed marker must refuse a budgeted command");
21727            assert!(error.contains(ALLOW_PROCESS_GROUP_CPU_SCAN_ENV), "{error}");
21728            assert!(error.contains(&format!("{value:?}")), "{error}");
21729            assert!(!root.join(format!("{label}.stdout")).exists());
21730            assert!(!root.join(format!("{label}.stderr")).exists());
21731            assert_eq!(observations.len(), 1);
21732            let observation = &observations[0];
21733            assert_eq!(
21734                observation.launch,
21735                LaunchObservation::SpawnFailed {
21736                    stage: SpawnStage::Spawn,
21737                    reason: error.clone(),
21738                }
21739            );
21740            assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::SpawnFailed);
21741            assert_eq!(observation.final_wait, FinalWaitObservation::NotApplicable);
21742            validate_native_observation(observation);
21743
21744            // An invocation without a CPU budget measures nothing live, so the
21745            // marker plays no part in it.
21746            let mut observations = Vec::new();
21747            let output = execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
21748                request(&format!("{label}-unbudgeted")),
21749                ProcessLimits {
21750                    deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5),
21751                    cpu_budget_usec: None,
21752                    cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
21753                },
21754                &mut observations,
21755            )
21756            .unwrap();
21757            assert!(output.status.success());
21758            assert_eq!(observations[0].live, LiveCpuObservation::Disabled);
21759            assert_process_observation(&observations[0], &output);
21760        }
21761        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21762    }

21764    #[test]
21765    fn an_escaped_setsid_burner_is_charged_and_killed_through_the_invocation_cgroup() {
21766        let test = "an_escaped_setsid_burner_is_charged_and_killed_through_the_invocation_cgroup";
21767        let Some(probe) = crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)
21768        else {
21769            return;
21770        };
21771        drop(probe);
21772        let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(false), None);
21773        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("escaped-burner");
21774        let pid_file = root.join("burner.pid");
21775        let saved = root.join("burner.cgroup");
21776        // If an assertion fails before the cgroup kills it, the burner must not
21777        // outlive the test.
21778        struct KillBurner(PathBuf);
21779        impl Drop for KillBurner {
21780            fn drop(&mut self) {
21781                if let Some(pid) = fs::read_to_string(&self.0)
21782                    .ok()
21783                    .and_then(|text| text.trim().parse::<libc::pid_t>().ok())
21784                {
21785                    unsafe {
21786                        libc::kill(pid, libc::SIGKILL);
21787                    }
21788                }
21789            }
21790        }
21791        let _burner_guard = KillBurner(pid_file.clone());
21792        // The burner starts a session of its own, so it is outside the leader's
21793        // process group: the process-group scan would not count it and the
21794        // group stop would not reach it. It is still in the invocation cgroup.
21795        let script = format!(
21796            "setsid /bin/sh -c 'echo $$ > {}; cat /proc/self/cgroup > {}; while :; do :; done' & exec sleep 60",
21797            pid_file.display(),
21798            saved.display()
21799        );
21800        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
21801            InvocationRole::Execution {
21802                attempt_index: "1".into(),
21803                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
21804            },
21805            &root,
21806            "/bin/sh",
21807            &["-c".into(), script],
21808            &BTreeMap::new(),
21809            &root.join("burner.stdout"),
21810            &root.join("burner.stderr"),
21811        );
21812        let mut observations = Vec::new();
21813        let started = Instant::now();
21814        let output = execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
21815            request,
21816            ProcessLimits {
21817                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(30),
21818                cpu_budget_usec: Some(150_000),
21819                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
21820            },
21821            &mut observations,
21822        )
21823        .expect("the CPU budget stop must return the charge");
21824        assert_eq!(
21825            output.timeout,
21826            Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu),
21827            "{observations:?}"
21828        );
21829        let observation = &observations[0];
21830        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::CpuBudgetStop);
21831        assert_process_observation(observation, &output);
21832        let live = enabled_cpu(observation);
21833        assert_eq!(live.source, LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1);
21834        let RequiredNullable::Value(trigger) = &live.timeout_trigger else {
21835            panic!("a CPU stop must retain its trigger: {live:?}");
21836        };
21837        let leader_cpu = measured_final_cpu(observation);
21838        assert!(trigger.cpu_usec >= 150_000, "{trigger:?}");
21839        assert!(
21840            trigger.cpu_usec > leader_cpu,
21841            "the leader's wait4 ({leader_cpu} usec) must not include the escaped burner ({trigger:?})"
21842        );
21843        assert_eq!(output.cpu_usage_usec, trigger.cpu_usec);
21844        // The cgroup killed the burner after the leader was reaped, and was
21845        // then removed.
21846        let directory = saved_cgroup_directory(&saved);
21847        let name = directory
21848            .file_name()
21849            .unwrap()
21850            .to_string_lossy()
21851            .into_owned();
21852        assert!(name.starts_with("hermit-e2e-invocation-"), "{name}");
21853        assert!(!directory.exists(), "{}", directory.display());
21854        let burner: libc::pid_t = fs::read_to_string(&pid_file)
21855            .unwrap()
21856            .trim()
21857            .parse()
21858            .unwrap();
21859        if let Ok(stat) = fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{burner}/stat")) {
21860            let state = stat.rsplit_once(") ").map(|(_, rest)| rest.chars().next());
21861            // A zombie waiting for its new parent is dead; any other process
21862            // with this PID must be a later one outside the invocation cgroup.
21863            if state != Some(Some('Z')) {
21864                let cgroup =
21865                    fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{burner}/cgroup")).unwrap_or_default();
21866                assert!(!cgroup.contains(&name), "burner {burner} survived: {stat}");
21867            }
21868        }
21869        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21870    }

21872    const GROUP_LEAVING_LEADER_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_RUNNER_TEST_GROUP_LEAVING_LEADER";
21873    const GROUP_LEAVING_CHILD_ENV: &str = "HERMIT_RUNNER_TEST_GROUP_LEAVING_CHILD";
21874
21875    /// A shell script that execs this test binary as
21876    /// `group_leaving_leader_helper`, so the leader is a process whose every
21877    /// step is known: no interpreter or wrapper stands between it and the
21878    /// runner.
21879    fn group_leaving_leader_script(moved: &Path, escaped_child: bool) -> String {
21880        let exe = std::env::current_exe().unwrap();
21881        format!(
21882            "export {GROUP_LEAVING_LEADER_ENV}='{}'; {}exec '{}' --exact runner::tests::group_leaving_leader_helper --nocapture --test-threads=1",
21883            moved.display(),
21884            if escaped_child {
21885                format!("export {GROUP_LEAVING_CHILD_ENV}=1; ")
21886            } else {
21887                String::new()
21888            },
21889            exe.display()
21890        )
21891    }
21892
21893    /// Does nothing unless `group_leaving_leader_script` started it. Then it
21894    /// moves into its parent's process group (the runner's), optionally starts
21895    /// a child in a session of its own that sleeps for 60 s, writes the file
21896    /// named by its environment, and sleeps for 25 s before exiting 0.
21897    #[test]
21898    fn group_leaving_leader_helper() {
21899        let Some(moved) = std::env::var_os(GROUP_LEAVING_LEADER_ENV) else {
21900            return;
21901        };
21902        if unsafe { libc::setpgid(0, libc::getpgid(libc::getppid())) } != 0 {
21903            std::process::exit(3);
21904        }
21905        if std::env::var_os(GROUP_LEAVING_CHILD_ENV).is_some() {
21906            match unsafe { libc::fork() } {
21907                0 => unsafe {
21908                    libc::setsid();
21909                    libc::sleep(60);
21910                    libc::_exit(0);
21911                },
21912                -1 => std::process::exit(4),
21913                _ => {}
21914            }
21915        }
21916        fs::write(moved, b"").unwrap();
21917        thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(25));
21918        std::process::exit(0);
21919    }

21921    #[test]
21922    fn a_leader_that_joins_the_runners_process_group_is_killed_when_the_stop_grace_ends() {
21923        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("leader-left-its-group");
21924        let moved = root.join("moved");
21925        // The leader moves into the runner's own process group, so neither the
21926        // SIGTERM nor the SIGKILL sent to its original group reaches it. Left
21927        // alone it sleeps for 25 s and then exits 0.
21928        let script = group_leaving_leader_script(&moved, false);
21929        let (child, started, mut observation) = spawn_fixture_with_source(
21930            &root,
21931            "left-group",
21932            &script,
21933            Some(LiveCpuSource::AgentUtilsPairedPidfdStatV1),
21934        );
21935        let pid = child.id();
21936        let mut triggered_at = None;
21937        let output = monitor_live_cpu(
21938            child,
21939            ProcessLimits {
21940                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(60),
21941                cpu_budget_usec: Some(100_000),
21942                cpu_poll_interval: Duration::from_millis(100),
21943            },
21944            started,
21945            &mut observation,
21946            |_| Ok(()),
21947            |_, _| {
21948                if !moved.exists() {
21949                    return Ok(0);
21950                }
21951                triggered_at.get_or_insert_with(Instant::now);
21952                Ok(200_000)
21953            },
21954        )
21955        .expect("the CPU stop must reap the leader");
21956        let stopped_at = Instant::now();
21957        let triggered_at = triggered_at.expect("the leader must have left its process group");
21958        assert_eq!(output.timeout, Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu), "{observation:?}");
21959        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::CpuBudgetStop);
21960        let FinalWaitObservation::Reaped { raw_status, .. } = observation.final_wait else {
21961            panic!("the stop must reap the leader: {observation:?}");
21962        };
21963        assert!(
21964            libc::WIFSIGNALED(raw_status) && libc::WTERMSIG(raw_status) == libc::SIGKILL,
21965            "the leader must be killed, not exit by itself: raw wait status {raw_status:#x}, {:?} after the trigger",
21966            stopped_at.duration_since(triggered_at)
21967        );
21968        // The whole 10 s TERM grace is waited out; the kill that follows reaps
21969        // the leader at once, long before its 25 s sleep would end.
21970        let stop = stopped_at.duration_since(triggered_at);
21971        assert!(
21972            stop >= Duration::from_secs(10) && stop < Duration::from_secs(12),
21973            "stopped {stop:?} after the trigger"
21974        );
21975        assert!(owned_child_is_reaped(pid));
21976        assert_process_observation(&observation, &output);
21977        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
21978    }

21980    #[test]
21981    fn the_stop_kills_the_invocation_cgroup_before_it_waits_for_a_leader_that_left_its_group() {
21982        let test =
21983            "the_stop_kills_the_invocation_cgroup_before_it_waits_for_a_leader_that_left_its_group";
21984        let Some(mut cgroup) =
21985            crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)
21986        else {
21987            return;
21988        };
21989        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("stop-kills-cgroup");
21990        let moved = root.join("moved");
21991        // The leader moves into the runner's process group and starts a child
21992        // in a session of its own; both stay in the invocation cgroup. Left
21993        // alone, the leader exits after 25 s and its child after 60 s.
21994        let script = group_leaving_leader_script(&moved, true);
21995        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
21996            InvocationRole::Execution {
21997                attempt_index: "1".into(),
21998                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
21999            },
22000            &root,
22001            "/bin/sh",
22002            &["-c".into(), script],
22003            &BTreeMap::new(),
22004            &root.join("leader.stdout"),
22005            &root.join("leader.stderr"),
22006        );
22007        let mut observation = InvocationCpuObservation::pending(
22008            1,
22009            request.role,
22010            request.command,
22011            Some(LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1),
22012        );
22013        let started = Instant::now();
22014        let child = spawn_process(
22015            &request.cwd,
22016            &request.stdout,
22017            &request.stderr,
22018            Some(Enrollment {
22019                directory: cgroup.directory_fd(),
22020                procs: cgroup.enrollment_fd(),
22021                path: cgroup.path(),
22022            }),
22023            &mut observation,
22024        )
22025        .unwrap();
22026        let output = monitor_live_cpu_in(
22027            child,
22028            ProcessLimits {
22029                deadline: started + Duration::from_secs(60),
22030                cpu_budget_usec: Some(100_000),
22031                cpu_poll_interval: Duration::from_millis(100),
22032            },
22033            started,
22034            &mut observation,
22035            Some(&cgroup),
22036            |_, _| Ok(()),
22037            |_| Ok(()),
22038            |_, _| Ok(if moved.exists() { 200_000 } else { 0 }),
22039        )
22040        .expect("the CPU stop must reap the leader");
22041        assert_eq!(output.timeout, Some(ProcessTimeout::Cpu), "{observation:?}");
22042        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::CpuBudgetStop);
22043        // The stop itself killed everything in the cgroup, the escaped child
22044        // included, before finish() had a chance to.
22045        let emptied_by = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
22046        while cgroup.populated().unwrap() {
22047            assert!(
22048                Instant::now() < emptied_by,
22049                "the stop left a live process in the invocation cgroup, {:?} after launch",
22050                started.elapsed()
22051            );
22052            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
22053        }
22054        cgroup.finish().unwrap();
22055        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
22056    }

22119        let Some(probe) = crate::invocation_cgroup::tests::real_cgroup_or_declared_absent(test)
22120        else {
22121            return;
22122        };
22123        drop(probe);
22124        let _plan = LiveCpuPlanOverride::set(Ok(false), None);
22125        let root = cpu_reader_test_root("nested-populated-cgroup");
22126        let saved = root.join("leader.cgroup");
22127        let pid_file = root.join("nested.pid");
22128        let _leftovers = RemoveLeftoverCgroup(saved.clone());
22129        let _sleeper = KillPidFile(pid_file.clone());
22130        // The leader starts a child in a session of its own, beyond the stop's
22131        // process-group signals, which moves into a nested cgroup and sleeps.
22132        // The leader then sleeps past its wall budget.
22133        let script = format!(
22134            r#"cat /proc/self/cgroup > '{saved}'; {OWN_CGROUP_SH}mkdir "$cg/nested" && setsid /bin/sh -c 'echo $$ > "$1/cgroup.procs" && echo $$ > "$2" && exec sleep 60' sh "$cg/nested" '{pid}' & while [ ! -s '{pid}' ]; do sleep 0.05; done; exec sleep 60"#,
22135            saved = saved.display(),
22136            pid = pid_file.display()
22137        );
22138        let request = ProcessRequest::new(
22139            InvocationRole::Execution {
22140                attempt_index: "1".into(),
22141                backend: RequiredNullable::Null,
22142            },
22143            &root,
22144            "/bin/sh",
22145            &["-c".into(), script],
22146            &BTreeMap::new(),
22147            &root.join("leader.stdout"),
22148            &root.join("leader.stderr"),
22149        );
22150        let mut observations = Vec::new();
22151        let output = execute_process_with_cpu_poll_interval(
22152            request,
22153            ProcessLimits {
22154                deadline: Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(3),
22155                cpu_budget_usec: Some(60_000_000),
22156                cpu_poll_interval: CELL_CPU_POLL_INTERVAL,
22157            },
22158            &mut observations,
22159        )
22160        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("the wall stop must return its outcome: {error}"));
22161        assert_eq!(
22162            output.timeout,
22163            Some(ProcessTimeout::Wall),
22164            "{observations:?}"
22165        );
22166        let observation = &observations[0];
22167        assert_eq!(observation.termination, TerminationPath::WallBudgetStop);
22168        assert_eq!(
22169            enabled_cpu(observation).source,
22170            LiveCpuSource::CgroupV2InvocationCpuStatV1
22171        );
22172        let directory = saved_cgroup_directory(&saved);
22173        let name = directory
22174            .file_name()
22175            .unwrap()
22176            .to_string_lossy()
22177            .into_owned();
22178        assert!(name.starts_with("hermit-e2e-invocation-"), "{name}");
22179        assert!(
22180            !directory.exists(),
22181            "{} is left behind",
22182            directory.display()
22183        );
22184        let sleeper: libc::pid_t = fs::read_to_string(&pid_file)
22185            .unwrap()
22186            .trim()
22187            .parse()
22188            .unwrap();
22189        if let Ok(stat) = fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{sleeper}/stat")) {
22190            let state = stat.rsplit_once(") ").map(|(_, rest)| rest.chars().next());
22191            // A zombie waiting for its new parent is dead; a live process with
22192            // this PID must be a later one outside the removed cgroup.
22193            if state != Some(Some('Z')) {
22194                let membership =
22195                    fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{sleeper}/cgroup")).unwrap_or_default();
22196                assert!(
22197                    !membership.contains(&name),
22198                    "sleeper {sleeper} survived: {stat}"
22199                );
22200            }
22201        }
22202        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
22203    }

22205    #[test]
22206    fn a_child_still_in_the_root_cgroup_while_forked_is_read_again() {
22207        let invocation = "/runner/hermit-e2e-invocation-1";
22208        // Process 8's cgroup reads as each entry of `reads` in turn, then as
22209        // the last one; 7, the leader, is inside.
22210        let check = |reads: &[Option<&str>]| {
22211            let reads: Vec<Option<String>> =
22212                reads.iter().map(|read| read.map(str::to_owned)).collect();
22213            let seen = std::cell::Cell::new(0);
22214            let result = check_cgroup_membership(
22215                7,
22216                true,
22217                invocation,
22218                |_| Ok(vec![7, 8]),
22219                |pid| match pid {
22220                    7 => Ok(Some(invocation.to_owned())),
22221                    8 => {
22222                        let read = reads[seen.get().min(reads.len() - 1)].clone();
22223                        seen.set(seen.get() + 1);
22224                        Ok(read)
22225                    }
22226                    other => panic!("process {other} was not expected to be checked"),
22227                },
22228            );
22229            (result, seen.get())
22230        };
22231        // In the root cgroup while fork creates it, then in the invocation.
22232        assert_eq!(check(&[Some("/"), Some(invocation)]), (Ok(()), 2));
22233        assert_eq!(
22234            check(&[
22235                Some("/"),
22236                Some("/"),
22237                Some("/runner/hermit-e2e-invocation-1/x")
22238            ]),
22239            (Ok(()), 3)
22240        );
22241        // Gone before a re-read: not outside.
22242        assert_eq!(check(&[Some("/"), None]), (Ok(()), 2));
22243        // A reader in a nested cgroup namespace sees the host root through
22244        // parent components. It is still outside until a later read proves
22245        // the child joined this invocation (or the child has exited).
22246        for root in ["/..", "/../..", "/../../../../../.."] {
22247            assert_eq!(check(&[Some(root), Some(invocation)]), (Ok(()), 2));
22248            assert_eq!(
22249                check(&[Some(root), Some("/runner/hermit-e2e-invocation-1/x")]),
22250                (Ok(()), 2)
22251            );
22252            assert_eq!(check(&[Some(root), None]), (Ok(()), 2));
22253            let (stays, reads) = check(&[Some(root)]);
22254            assert!(stays.unwrap_err().contains("outside its invocation cgroup"));
22255            assert_eq!(reads, 1 + FORK_WINDOW_REREADS as usize);
22256        }
22257        // Only the ancestor-only spelling receives the bounded fork check;
22258        // neither a sibling nor a malformed path is a transient root claim.
22259        for outside in [
22260            "/../other",
22261            "/../../other",
22262            "/./..",
22263            "/..//..",
22264            "../..",
22265            "/../",
22266        ] {
22267            let (result, reads) = check(&[Some(outside), Some(invocation)]);
22268            assert!(
22269                result
22270                    .unwrap_err()
22271                    .contains("outside its invocation cgroup")
22272            );
22273            assert_eq!(reads, 1, "{outside}");
22274        }
22275        // Read again only for the root cgroup: a parent cgroup is refused at once.
22276        let (parent, reads) = check(&[Some("/runner"), Some(invocation)]);
22277        assert!(parent.unwrap_err().contains("process 8 (a member"));
22278        assert_eq!(reads, 1);
22279        // Still in the root cgroup after every re-read: refused.
22280        let (stays, reads) = check(&[Some("/")]);
22281        let refusal = stays.unwrap_err();
22282        assert!(
22283            refusal.contains("process 8 (a member of the leader's process group) is in cgroup /,"),
22284            "{refusal}"
22285        );
22286        assert_eq!(reads, 1 + FORK_WINDOW_REREADS as usize);
22287    }
