24716    /// A verify cell's guest sees its home, xdg-config and fixture directories
24717    /// only at the fixed guest paths below `/tmp/e2e`, so the ptrace and
24718    /// candidate cells of one test, which run from different cell directories,
24719    /// give their guests the same argv and environment in both runner shapes,
24720    /// dbt included. Every mode the parity post-pass does not compare keeps the
24721    /// host paths. The row's own environment keeps the
24722    /// host paths, which name where the directories are.
24723    #[test]
24724    fn verify_cells_give_every_bindable_backend_the_same_guest_inputs() {
24725        // build_spec creates the sabre path-evidence file, so the root is real.
24726        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
24727            "hermit-manifest-equalized-inputs-{}",
24728            std::process::id()
24729        ));
24730        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
24731        for isolated in [None, Some(PathBuf::from("/test"))] {
24732            let mut context = run_context(&root);
24733            context.isolated_workdir = isolated.clone();
24734            let spec_for = |backend: &str, mode: &str| {
24735                let mut cell = ptrace_cell(mode);
24736                cell.id.backend = Some(backend.into());
24737                let dir = cell_artifact_path(&context.result_root, &context.run_id, &cell.id, 1);
24738                let host = dir.display().to_string();
24739                let guest = vec![
24740                    format!("{host}/fixtures/program"),
24741                    format!("{host}/home/test/.rc"),
24742                    format!("{host}/xdg-config"),
24743                    format!("{host}/xdg-config/git/config"),
24744                    // Embedded and look-alike paths are not rewritten.
24745                    format!("--input={host}/fixtures/data"),
24746                    format!("{host}/fixtures-extra"),
24747                    "plain".into(),
24748                ];
24749                let spec = build_spec(&context, &cell, dir, guest, "1", Some(1), 15).unwrap();
24750                (host, spec)
24751            };
24752            let after_separator = |spec: &CellRunSpec| {
24753                let argv = without_mapped_input_holder(&spec.argv);
24754                let separator = argv.iter().position(|arg| arg == "--").unwrap();
24755                argv[separator + 1..].to_vec()
24756            };
24757            // What the guest can see: argv, environment and each bind target.
24758            let guest_view = |spec: &CellRunSpec| {
24759                let argv = without_mapped_input_holder(&spec.argv);
24760                let separator = argv.iter().position(|arg| arg == "--").unwrap();
24761                let before = &argv[..separator];
24762                let targets = before
24763                    .iter()
24764                    .filter_map(|arg| arg.strip_prefix("--bind="))
24765                    .map(|bind| bind.split_once(':').unwrap().1.to_string())
24766                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
24767                (guest_env_args(before), targets, after_separator(spec))
24768            };
24769
24770            let (reference_dir, reference) = spec_for("ptrace", "verify");
24771            let jobs = "1";
24772            let tmp = if isolated.is_some() {
24773                "/test"
24774            } else {
24775                "/tmp/hermit-e2e"
24776            };
24777            assert_equalized_guest_env(&reference.argv, &reference_dir, tmp, jobs);
24778            assert_eq!(
24779                reference.guest_argv,
24780                vec![
24781                    "/tmp/e2e/fixtures/program".to_string(),
24782                    "/tmp/e2e/home/test/.rc".to_string(),
24783                    "/tmp/e2e/xdg-config".to_string(),
24784                    "/tmp/e2e/xdg-config/git/config".to_string(),
24785                    format!("--input={reference_dir}/fixtures/data"),
24786                    format!("{reference_dir}/fixtures-extra"),
24787                    "plain".to_string(),
24788                ]
24789            );
24790            assert_eq!(after_separator(&reference), reference.guest_argv);
24791            for (name, subdir) in [
24792                ("HOME", "home"),
24793                ("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "xdg-config"),
24794                ("E2E_FIXTURE_DIR", "fixtures"),
24795            ] {
24796                assert_eq!(
24797                    reference.env.get(name),
24798                    Some(&format!("{reference_dir}/{subdir}")),
24799                    "{name}"
24800                );
24801            }
24802            if isolated.is_none() {
24803                assert_eq!(
24804                    bound_workdir_source(&reference),
24805                    PathBuf::from(format!("{reference_dir}/workdir/1"))
24806                );
24807            }
24808
24809            for backend in ["dbt", "kvm", "liteinst", "in-guest-trap", "sabre"] {
24810                let (dir, candidate) = spec_for(backend, "verify");
24811                assert_ne!(dir, reference_dir);
24812                assert_equalized_guest_env(&candidate.argv, &dir, tmp, jobs);
24813                // Only the embedded and look-alike arguments still differ.
24814                let (env, targets, argv) = guest_view(&candidate);
24815                let (reference_env, reference_targets, reference_argv) = guest_view(&reference);
24816                assert_eq!((env, targets), (reference_env, reference_targets));
24817                assert_eq!(argv[..4], reference_argv[..4], "{backend}");
24818                assert_eq!(argv[6], reference_argv[6], "{backend}");
24819            }
24820
24821            // dbt refuses --mount: its adapter mounts the hermetic /test itself,
24822            // and outside the hermetic shape it binds the workdir like the rest.
24823            let (dir, dbt) = spec_for("dbt", "verify");
24824            assert!(!dbt.argv.iter().any(|arg| arg.starts_with("--mount=")));
24825            assert_eq!(
24826                dbt.argv
24827                    .iter()
24828                    .any(|arg| *arg == format!("--bind={dir}/workdir/1:/tmp/test")),
24829                isolated.is_none()
24830            );
24831
24832            for mode in ["chaos", "replay", "custom"] {
24833                let (dir, spec) = spec_for("ptrace", mode);
24834                assert!(
24835                    !spec
24836                        .argv
24837                        .iter()
24838                        .any(|arg| arg.contains(EQUALIZED_INPUT_ROOT)),
24839                    "{mode} binds nothing below {EQUALIZED_INPUT_ROOT}: {:?}",
24840                    spec.argv
24841                );
24842                assert_eq!(spec.guest_argv[0], format!("{dir}/fixtures/program"));
24843                assert_eq!(spec.guest_argv[2], format!("{dir}/xdg-config"));
24844                assert_eq!(spec.guest_argv[3], format!("{dir}/xdg-config/git/config"));
24845            }
24846        }
24847        assert!(equalizes_guest_inputs("verify"));
24848        assert!(!equalizes_guest_inputs("naked"));
24849        fs::remove_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
24850    }

24852    // The acceptance test of slice S8 of
24853    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301, one test per id
24854    // measured in
24855    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301#issuecomment-5874842696,
24856    // each paired with the candidate whose cell directory its second ptrace
24857    // run is given. In that measurement ptrace given each of these
24858    // candidates' unequalized inputs diverged from ptrace given its own
24859    // (control C1: record 14 for five pairs, record 93 for epoll with the
24860    // sabre directory). Whether an unequalized pair diverges depends on its
24861    // host path lengths, which here include the test process id: with the
24862    // equalization disabled, five of these pairs diverged in this layout
24863    // (records 14, 105 and 107) and epoll with the sabre directory matched by
24864    // coincidence. So each test also requires the parity record to say the
24865    // inputs were equalized, which no unequalized pair can.
24866

24900    /// The Hermit the acceptance test runs: `HERMIT_BIN`, else the verified
24901    /// artifact that validate publishes before `test.regular_crates`
24902    /// (`target/ci/hermit-e2e-artifact.path`), else `target/debug/hermit`.
24903    /// Without one the test fails, because a pass that ran no guest would
24904    /// measure nothing.
24905    fn acceptance_hermit(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
24906        if let Some(bin) = std::env::var_os("HERMIT_BIN") {
24907            return PathBuf::from(bin);
24908        }
24909        let pointer = root.join("target/ci/hermit-e2e-artifact.path");
24910        if pointer.is_file() {
24911            let output = Command::new(root.join("ci/verify-hermit-e2e-artifact.sh"))
24912                .arg(&pointer)
24913                .output()
24914                .expect("run ci/verify-hermit-e2e-artifact.sh");
24915            assert!(
24916                output.status.success(),
24917                "{} names no verified Hermit artifact:\n{}",
24918                pointer.display(),
24919                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
24920            );
24921            return PathBuf::from(String::from_utf8(output.stdout).unwrap().trim()).join("hermit");
24922        }
24923        let debug = root.join("target/debug/hermit");
24924        assert!(
24925            debug.is_file(),
24926            "the equal-inputs acceptance test runs a real Hermit: set HERMIT_BIN, publish \
24927             {} (validate's build.e2e_artifact does), or build {}",
24928            pointer.display(),
24929            debug.display()
24930        );
24931        debug
24932    }
24933
24934    /// Ptrace given `candidate`'s cell inputs through the equalization matches
24935    /// ptrace given its own on `test`, so a parity comparison of the two earns
24936    /// full credit with equal inputs. It runs the id's real ptrace verify cell
24937    /// twice, once in its own cell directory and once in the candidate's, and
24938    /// hands both rows to the parity post-pass with the second relabelled as
24939    /// the candidate. The runner shape follows the environment, so validate's
24940    /// `HERMIT_E2E_EMPTY_WORKDIR=/test` runs the hermetic shape. One id per
24941    /// test keeps each inside the per-test Nextest CPU bound (22 CPU-s): with
24942    /// the debug Hermit that validate publishes, hashing that binary three
24943    /// times per cell costs more CPU than the guest runs do.
24944    fn ptrace_given_equalized_inputs_matches_ptrace(test: &str, candidate: &str) {
24945        let root = crate::compiled_manifest_dir!().join("../..");
24946        let root = root.canonicalize().unwrap();
24947        let hermit_bin = acceptance_hermit(&root);
24948        let scratch = root.join(format!(
24949            "target/equalized-input-acceptance-{}-{}",
24950            std::process::id(),
24951            test.replace('/', "-")
24952        ));
24953        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&scratch);
24954        let isolated_workdir = std::env::var_os(ISOLATED_WORKDIR_ENV).map(|value| {
24955            assert_eq!(value, HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR, "{ISOLATED_WORKDIR_ENV}");
24956            PathBuf::from(HERMETIC_TEST_WORKDIR)
24957        });
24958        let context = RunContext {
24959            command_bindings: BTreeMap::new(),
24960            root: root.clone(),
24961            hermit_bin: hermit_bin.clone(),
24962            result_root: scratch.join("results"),
24963            build_root: scratch.join("build"),
24964            run_id: "equalized-inputs".into(),
24965            machine_shortname: "acceptance".into(),
24966            kernel_version: command_text("uname", &["-r"]).unwrap(),
24967            host_capabilities: probe_host_capabilities(),
24968            attempt: 1,
24969            run_index: None,
24970            epoch: resolve_run_epoch(std::env::var_os("HERMIT_EPOCH")).unwrap(),
24971            source_sha: "0".repeat(40),
24972            source_dirty: false,
24973            binary_build_sha: probe_binary_build_sha(&hermit_bin),
24974            prebuilt: false,
24975            keep_logs: true,
24976            capture_custom_runs: false,
24977            parity_retained: BTreeSet::new(),
24978            parity_compared: BTreeSet::new(),
24979            run_verify_strict: command_help_contains(
24980                &hermit_bin,
24981                &["run", "--help"],
24982                "--verify-strict",
24983            )
24984            .unwrap(),
24985            record_verify_strict: false,
24986            timeout_multipliers: crate::timeouts::timeout_multipliers_from_env().unwrap(),
24987            scheduled_worker_capacity: ScheduledWorkerCapacity::new(1),
24988            isolated_workdir,
24989            shares_ld_so_cache: false,
24990            exact_branch_counter: None,
24991            v2_retry_oci_dir: None,
24992        };
24993        let manifests = ManifestSet::load(&root).unwrap();
24994        let [cell] = manifests
24995            .select(&Selection {
24996                population: Some(Population::Enabled),
24997                test: Some(test.into()),
24998                mode: Some("verify".into()),
24999                backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
25000                ..Selection::default()
25001            })
25002            .unwrap()
25003            .try_into()
25004            .unwrap_or_else(|cells: Vec<_>| panic!("{test}: {} ptrace verify cells", cells.len()));
25005        let own = run_cell(&context, &cell)
25006            .unwrap_or_else(|failure| panic!("{test} in its own directory: {}", failure.reason));
25007        let candidate_id = CellId {
25008            backend: Some(candidate.into()),
25009            ..cell.id.clone()
25010        };
25011        let candidate_dir = cell_artifact_path(
25012            &context.result_root,
25013            &context.run_id,
25014            &candidate_id,
25015            context.attempt,
25016        );
25017        let mut given =
25018            run_cell_in(&context, &cell, candidate_dir.clone()).unwrap_or_else(|failure| {
25019                panic!("{test} in the {candidate} directory: {}", failure.reason)
25020            });
25021        for (row, dir) in [
25022            (&own, cell_artifact_dir(&context, &cell)),
25023            (&given, candidate_dir),
25024        ] {
25025            assert_eq!(row.outcome, "PASS", "{test}: {row:?}");
25026            // The inputs came from that cell's directory.
25027            assert_eq!(row.artifact_dir, dir.to_string_lossy(), "{test}");
25028            assert_eq!(
25029                row.env.get("E2E_FIXTURE_DIR"),
25030                Some(&format!("{}/fixtures", dir.display())),
25031                "{test}"
25032            );
25033        }
25034        given.backend = Some(candidate.into());
25035
25036        let scope = BTreeSet::from([crate::parity::ParityCellId {
25037            test_id: test.into(),
25038            backend: crate::parity::ParityBackend::parse(candidate).unwrap(),
25039        }]);
25040        let artifacts = scratch.join("parity");
25041        fs::create_dir_all(&artifacts).unwrap();
25042        let report = crate::parity::post_pass(
25043            &crate::parity::PostPassConfig::new(
25044                &artifacts,
25045                &hermit_bin,
25046                &context.run_id,
25047                &context.source_sha,
25048            ),
25049            &scope,
25050            &[own, given],
25051        )
25052        .unwrap();
25053        assert_eq!(report.log_diff_runs, 1, "{test}");
25054        let [record] = report.records.as_slice() else {
25055            panic!("{test}: {} parity records", report.records.len());
25056        };
25057        record.validate().unwrap();
25058        assert_eq!(
25059            record.verdict,
25060            crate::parity::ParityVerdict::Matched,
25061            "{record:?}"
25062        );
25063        assert!(record.inputs_equalized, "{record:?}");
25064        assert_eq!(record.credit, Some(1.0), "{record:?}");
25065        assert_eq!(record.unequalized_credit, None, "{record:?}");
25066        // A match of two near-empty logs would prove nothing. The measurement
25067        // above recorded 115 to 173 records for these ids.
25068        assert!(
25069            record.left_len.is_some_and(|len| len >= 100)
25070                && record.left_len == record.right_len
25071                && record.matched_prefix == record.left_len,
25072            "{record:?}"
25073        );
25074        assert!(
25075            report.summary_line().contains(
25076                "mean credit 1.0000 over 1 measured with equal inputs; \
25077                 none measured with unequal inputs"
25078            ),
25079            "{}",
25080            report.summary_line()
25081        );
25082        fs::remove_dir_all(&scratch).unwrap();
25083    }

25305    fn attempt_with_divergence(
25306        turn: Option<u64>,
25307        nanos: Option<u64>,
25308        record: Option<u64>,
25309        syscall: Option<u64>,
25310    ) -> AttemptResult {
25311        let mut attempt = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("");
25312        attempt.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = turn;
25313        attempt.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = nanos;
25314        attempt.first_divergent_record = record;
25315        attempt.first_divergent_syscall = syscall;
25316        attempt
25317    }
25318
25319    /// The cell-level position is the FIRST attempt that located one, matching
25320    /// how `reason` is chosen, and NOT the last -- otherwise a passing retry
25321    /// would erase the position the failing attempt found.
25322    #[test]
25323    fn cell_divergence_takes_the_first_attempt_that_located_one() {
25324        let mut attempts = vec![
25325            attempt_with_divergence(None, None, None, None),
25326            attempt_with_divergence(Some(4), Some(400), Some(40), Some(14)),
25327            attempt_with_divergence(Some(1), Some(100), Some(10), Some(2)),
25328        ];
25329        attempts[1].first_divergent_left_message = Some("left event A".into());
25330        attempts[1].first_divergent_right_message = Some("right event A".into());
25331        attempts[2].first_divergent_left_message = Some("left event B".into());
25332        attempts[2].first_divergent_right_message = Some("right event B".into());
25333        assert_eq!(
25334            cell_divergence_position(&attempts),
25335            DivergencePosition {
25336                scheduler_turn: Some(4),
25337                virtual_nanoseconds: Some(400),
25338                record: Some(40),
25339                syscall: Some(14),
25340                left_message: Some("left event A".into()),
25341                right_message: Some("right event A".into()),
25342            },
25343            "the first located position wins; a later, earlier-diverging attempt \
25344             must not silently replace it, and this is NOT a min across attempts"
25345        );
25346    }
25347
25348    /// Resolved per coordinate, so a report that located only some of the four
25349    /// still contributes the ones it has. Each coordinate here comes from a
25350    /// DIFFERENT attempt, which a per-attempt rule could not produce.
25351    #[test]
25352    fn cell_divergence_resolves_each_coordinate_independently() {
25353        let attempts = vec![
25354            attempt_with_divergence(None, Some(900), None, None),
25355            attempt_with_divergence(Some(7), None, None, None),
25356            attempt_with_divergence(None, None, Some(3), None),
25357            attempt_with_divergence(None, None, None, Some(5)),
25358        ];
25359        assert_eq!(
25360            cell_divergence_position(&attempts),
25361            DivergencePosition {
25362                scheduler_turn: Some(7),
25363                virtual_nanoseconds: Some(900),
25364                record: Some(3),
25365                syscall: Some(5),
25366                left_message: None,
25367                right_message: None,
25368            }
25369        );
25370    }
25371
25372    /// A located record with NO syscall is a real state, not a gap: a run can
25373    /// diverge before any syscall has completed. Measured on a real log --
25374    /// diverging at record 12 reported syscall `None`, because no
25375    /// `finish syscall #N` had been written yet.
25376    #[test]
25377    fn a_divergence_before_any_syscall_completes_reports_no_syscall() {
25378        let attempts = vec![attempt_with_divergence(Some(1), None, Some(12), None)];
25379        let position = cell_divergence_position(&attempts);
25380        assert_eq!(position.record, Some(12));
25381        assert_eq!(position.syscall, None);
25382    }
25383
25384    /// A clean cell reports no position at all.
25385    #[test]
25386    fn cell_divergence_is_absent_when_no_attempt_located_one() {
25387        let attempts = vec![attempt_with_divergence(None, None, None, None)];
25388        assert_eq!(
25389            cell_divergence_position(&attempts),
25390            DivergencePosition::default()
25391        );
25392        assert_eq!(cell_divergence_position(&[]), DivergencePosition::default());
25393    }

25395    /// ⚠️ ABSENCE OF THIS KEY IS RESERVED FOR "WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIELD
25396    /// EXISTED", AND NOTHING ELSE. A row that ran, compared, and located no
25397    /// divergence must carry the key with an explicit null.
25398    ///
25399    /// WHY IT NEEDS A TEST RATHER THAN BEING OBVIOUS. `CELL_RESULT_SCHEMA` was
25400    /// NOT bumped when these coordinates were added, so the schema number
25401    /// cannot separate the two meanings. Within schema 4 the only thing that
25402    /// distinguishes "this predates the field" from "this ran and found nothing"
25403    /// is whether the key is present at all.
25404    ///
25405    /// ⚠️ THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS THE DURABLE ONE; THE COUNTS ARE NOT. Schema 4
25406    /// contains BOTH rows with the key and rows without it, while schemas 1, 2
25407    /// and 3 never carry it -- that is what makes the schema number useless as a
25408    /// discriminator, and agent(hermit-106) reproduced it independently across
25409    /// 1478 rows. The row COUNTS behind it move: this file measured 28899 without
25410    /// and 17540 with over 6215 retained `results.jsonl`, and a sample of 1200 of
25411    /// those files gave a different ratio. Both are honest. The corpus lives in
25412    /// gitignored run directories that agents create and delete, so it is not a
25413    /// fixed population and a count taken from it is true of one moment. Do not
25414    /// treat these numbers as a baseline to compare against.
25415    ///
25416    /// That distinction currently holds only because no
25417    /// `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` is attached to these
25418    /// fields -- an entirely natural tidy-up for a field that is null on the
25419    /// large majority of rows. Adding one would silently convert every future
25420    /// "ran and found nothing" row into a row indistinguishable from a
25421    /// pre-field one, and no existing test would notice. This is that test.
25422    ///
25423    /// It asserts PRESENCE and NULLNESS separately from any value, so it fails
25424    /// on the skip attribute rather than on a changed position.
25425    /// ⚠️ THE ROW, NOT ONLY THE ATTEMPT. The measurement in the docstring above is
25426    /// about `results.jsonl` ROWS, and a row is a `CellResult` with its attempts
25427    /// nested inside it. An earlier version of this test guarded `AttemptResult`
25428    /// alone, which left the level the evidence actually describes uncovered:
25429    /// agent(hermit-106) put `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` on all four
25430    /// `CellResult` coordinates and the whole package stayed GREEN, 126 tests, 0
25431    /// failures, INCLUDING this test. A check that stays green while the hazard it
25432    /// names is open is the failure this file is full of warnings about.
25433    fn cell_result_that_located_nothing() -> CellResult {
25434        CellResult {
25435            capture_custom_runs: false,
25436            capture_adoption_cpu_usage_usec: None,
25437            cpu_observations: None,
25438            schema: CELL_RESULT_SCHEMA,
25439            run_id: "fixture".into(),
25440            machine_shortname: "fixture-host".into(),
25441            kernel_version: "7.1.3-fixture".into(),
25442            host_capabilities: fixture_host_capabilities(),
25443            exact_branch_counter: None,
25444            attempt: 1,
25445            run_index: None,
25446            hermit_sha: "sha".into(),
25447            binary_build_sha: None,
25448            source_tree_dirty: false,
25449            binary_sha256: None,
25450            comparator_binary_sha256: None,
25451            test_sha256: "digest".into(),
25452            test: "fixture/test".into(),
25453            category: "fixture".into(),
25454            lane: "portable".into(),
25455            mode: "verify".into(),
25456            backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
25457            classification: "required".into(),
25458            outcome: "PASS".into(),
25459            result: Some(ObservedResult::Pass),
25460            failure_class: None,
25461            error_kind: None,
25462            timeout_seconds: 3,
25463            execution_cpu_timeout_seconds: Some(1),
25464            execution_wall_timeout_seconds: Some(3),
25465            duration_ms: Some(1),
25466            cpu_usage_usec: Some(1),
25467            runtime: None,
25468            log_level: None,
25469            effective_args: Vec::new(),
25470            argv: vec!["hermit".into()],
25471            guest_argv: vec!["guest".into()],
25472            env: BTreeMap::new(),
25473            cwd: "/repo".into(),
25474            shell_command: "cd /repo && hermit".into(),
25475            relaxations: Vec::new(),
25476            execution_path: None,

25493    #[test]
25494    fn only_a_reasoned_product_failure_of_a_diagnostic_cell_is_a_diagnostic_failure() {
25495        let reason = "bounded probe";
25496        let diagnostic = |outcome: &str, class: Option<FailureClass>, relaxations: Vec<String>| {
25497            let mut row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
25498            row.classification = "diagnostic".into();
25499            row.outcome = outcome.into();
25500            row.failure_class = class;
25501            row.relaxations = relaxations;
25502            row
25503        };
25504        let recorded = || vec![format!("{DIAGNOSTIC_RELAXATION_PREFIX}{reason}")];
25505        let failure = diagnostic("FAIL", Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure), recorded());
25506        assert_eq!(
25507            diagnostic_failure_reason(std::slice::from_ref(&failure)),
25508            Some(reason)
25509        );
25510        // The cell exceeding its own budget is a measured failure too.
25511        let mut timeout = diagnostic("FAIL", Some(FailureClass::NoResult), recorded());
25512        timeout.result = Some(ObservedResult::Timeout);
25513        timeout.error_kind = Some("wall-timeout".into());
25514        assert_eq!(diagnostic_failure_reason(&[timeout]), Some(reason));
25515        assert_eq!(diagnostic_failure_reason(&[]), None);
25516        // A retried product failure that ends in an ERROR has no terminal product verdict.
25517        let mut error_retry = diagnostic("ERROR", Some(FailureClass::NoResult), recorded());
25518        error_retry.attempt = 2;
25519        assert_eq!(
25520            diagnostic_failure_reason(&[failure.clone(), error_retry]),
25521            None
25522        );
25523        let mut fail_retry = failure.clone();
25524        fail_retry.attempt = 2;
25525        assert_eq!(
25526            diagnostic_failure_reason(&[failure.clone(), fail_retry]),
25527            Some(reason)
25528        );
25529        let mut required = failure.clone();
25530        required.classification = "required".into();
25531        for (name, row) in [
25532            ("a required cell", required),
25533            ("a pass", diagnostic("PASS", None, recorded())),
25534            (
25535                "an error",
25536                diagnostic("ERROR", Some(FailureClass::NoResult), recorded()),
25537            ),
25538            (
25539                "a FAIL with no product verdict that is not a timeout",
25540                diagnostic("FAIL", Some(FailureClass::NoResult), recorded()),
25541            ),
25542            (
25543                "an infrastructure failure",
25544                diagnostic(
25545                    "FAIL",
25546                    Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure),
25547                    recorded(),
25548                ),
25549            ),
25550            (
25551                "a row that lost its reason",
25552                diagnostic("FAIL", Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure), Vec::new()),
25553            ),
25554            (
25555                "a row with two reasons",
25556                diagnostic(
25557                    "FAIL",
25558                    Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure),
25559                    [recorded(), recorded()].concat(),
25560                ),
25561            ),
25562        ] {
25563            assert_eq!(diagnostic_failure_reason(&[row]), None, "{name}");
25564        }
25565    }

25567    #[test]
25568    fn a_located_nothing_row_still_carries_all_divergence_fields() {
25569        let attempt = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("evidence");
25570        let rendered = serde_json::to_value(&attempt).expect("attempt serializes");
25571        let object = rendered.as_object().expect("attempt is a JSON object");
25572        for key in [
25573            "first_divergent_record",
25574            "first_divergent_syscall",
25575            "first_divergent_scheduler_turn",
25576            "first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds",
25577            "first_divergent_left_message",
25578            "first_divergent_right_message",
25579        ] {
25580            let found = object.get(key).unwrap_or_else(|| {
25581                panic!(
25582                    "{key} is absent from a serialized attempt that located nothing. \
25583                     Absence is how a consumer recognises a row written before this \
25584                     field existed; emitting it for a row that simply found nothing \
25585                     merges two different facts that no later reader can separate."
25586                )
25587            });
25588            assert!(
25589                found.is_null(),
25590                "{key} must be an explicit null when nothing was located, got {found}"
25591            );
25592        }
25593
25594        // THE ROW LEVEL, which is what a `results.jsonl` line actually is and what
25595        // every count in the docstring above was measured over.
25596        let row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
25597        let rendered = serde_json::to_value(&row).expect("row serializes");
25598        let object = rendered.as_object().expect("row is a JSON object");
25599        assert!(
25600            !object.contains_key("run_index"),
25601            "ordinary validate rows must not invent a pressure repetition"
25602        );
25603        assert_eq!(object["machine_shortname"], "fixture-host");
25604        assert_eq!(object["kernel_version"], "7.1.3-fixture");
25605        assert_eq!(
25606            object["host_capabilities"]["cpuid-faulting"]["present"],
25607            true
25608        );
25609        assert_eq!(object["host_capabilities"]["kvm"]["present"], false);
25610        for key in [
25611            "first_divergent_record",
25612            "first_divergent_syscall",
25613            "first_divergent_scheduler_turn",
25614            "first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds",
25615            "first_divergent_left_message",
25616            "first_divergent_right_message",
25617        ] {
25618            let found = object.get(key).unwrap_or_else(|| {
25619                panic!(
25620                    "{key} is absent from a serialized RESULT ROW that located nothing. \
25621                     A results.jsonl line is a CellResult, so this is the level every \
25622                     count in this test's docstring was measured over; absence here is \
25623                     how a reader recognises a row written before the field existed."
25624                )
25625            });
25626            assert!(
25627                found.is_null(),
25628                "{key} must be an explicit null on the row when nothing was located, got {found}"
25629            );
25630        }
25631
25632        let decoded: CellResult =
25633            serde_json::from_value(rendered).expect("the producer-owned result type reads its row");
25634        assert_eq!(decoded.attempt, 1);
25635        assert_eq!(decoded.run_index, None);
25636        assert_eq!(decoded.attempts.len(), 1);
25637
25638        let mut pressure_row = row;
25639        pressure_row.run_index = Some(4);
25640        let rendered = serde_json::to_value(&pressure_row).expect("pressure row serializes");
25641        assert_eq!(rendered["run_index"], 4);
25642        let decoded: CellResult = serde_json::from_value(rendered)
25643            .expect("the producer-owned result type reads a pressure row");
25644        assert_eq!(decoded.run_index, Some(4));
25645    }

25647    #[test]
25648    fn schema4_keeps_its_wall_field_and_adds_explicit_execution_bounds() {
25649        let row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
25650        let mut rendered = serde_json::to_value(&row).expect("cell result serializes");
25651        assert_eq!(rendered["timeout_seconds"], 3);
25652        assert_eq!(rendered["execution_cpu_timeout_seconds"], 1);
25653        assert_eq!(rendered["execution_wall_timeout_seconds"], 3);
25654        row.require_current_timeout_policy().unwrap();
25655
25656        let mut half_present = row.clone();
25657        half_present.execution_wall_timeout_seconds = None;
25658        assert!(half_present.validate_timeout_policy().is_err());
25659        let publication = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
25660            "hermit-runner-timeout-policy-publication-{}",
25661            std::process::id()
25662        ));
25663        let _ = fs::remove_file(&publication);
25664        assert!(append_result(&publication, &half_present).is_err());
25665        assert!(
25666            !publication.exists(),
25667            "a malformed current timeout policy reached the results file"
25668        );
25669        let mut wrong_cpu = row.clone();
25670        wrong_cpu.execution_cpu_timeout_seconds = Some(3);
25671        assert!(wrong_cpu.validate_timeout_policy().is_err());
25672        let mut wrong_wall = row.clone();
25673        wrong_wall.execution_wall_timeout_seconds = Some(2);
25674        assert!(wrong_wall.validate_timeout_policy().is_err());
25675
25676        let object = rendered.as_object_mut().unwrap();
25677        object.remove("execution_cpu_timeout_seconds");
25678        object.remove("execution_wall_timeout_seconds");
25679        let retained: CellResult = serde_json::from_value(rendered)
25680            .expect("a schema-4 row written before the additive fields remains readable");
25681        assert_eq!(retained.timeout_seconds, 3);
25682        assert_eq!(retained.execution_cpu_timeout_seconds, None);
25683        assert_eq!(retained.execution_wall_timeout_seconds, None);
25684        retained.validate_timeout_policy().unwrap();
25685        assert!(retained.require_current_timeout_policy().is_err());
25686    }

25731    fn loader_rejected_attempt(exit_code: i32, stderr: &str) -> AttemptResult {
25732        let mut report = VerificationReport::no_result();
25733        report.no_result_reason =
25734            Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::FirstRunRejected {
25735                exit_code: Some(exit_code),
25736                signal: None,
25737                stdout_bytes: 0,
25738                stderr_bytes: stderr.len() as u64,
25739            });
25740        let mut attempt = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("unused");
25741        attempt.verification_report = Some(serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap());
25742        attempt.stderr = stderr.into();
25743        attempt
25744    }

25746    #[test]
25747    fn loader_v2_rejection_needs_the_typed_127_and_the_loader_line() {
25748        let line = "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v3\n";
25749        assert!(loader_v2_rejection(&loader_rejected_attempt(127, line)));
25750        // The level digit is not part of the signature.
25751        assert!(loader_v2_rejection(&loader_rejected_attempt(
25752            127,
25753            "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v4\n"
25754        )));
25755        // A typed rejection at another status is an ordinary guest failure.
25756        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&loader_rejected_attempt(1, line)));
25757        // Exit 127 without the loader line is not a loader rejection.
25758        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&loader_rejected_attempt(
25759            127,
25760            "guest: command not found\n"
25761        )));
25762        // The line without the typed report earns nothing.
25763        let mut untyped = loader_rejected_attempt(127, line);
25764        untyped.verification_report = None;
25765        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&untyped));
25766    }

25768    /// An attempt whose retained report compared two runs under `verdict`,
25769    /// the left run exiting `left` and the right `right`, with `stderr`
25770    /// captured.
25771    fn compared_runs_attempt(
25772        verdict: Verdict,
25773        left: i32,
25774        right: i32,
25775        stderr: &str,
25776    ) -> AttemptResult {
25777        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
25778        report.verdict = verdict;
25779        report.verified = verdict == Verdict::Matched;
25780        report.bitwise_parity = verdict == Verdict::Matched;
25781        let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
25782        outputs.left.exit_code = Some(left);
25783        outputs.right.exit_code = Some(right);
25784        report.guest_exit_code = Some(left);
25785        let mut attempt = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("unused");
25786        attempt.verification_report = Some(serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap());
25787        attempt.stderr = stderr.into();
25788        attempt
25789    }

25791    /// A cell that declares a non-zero guest disposition runs with
25792    /// `--verify-allow=failure`, so a loader rejection reaches a comparison of
25793    /// two runs that both exited 127 instead of `first_run_rejected` (issue
25794    /// 5476; c-programs/nanosleep-threads-simple, which declares signal 11).
25795    /// A matched comparison of two runs at 127, with the loader's line in the
25796    /// attempt's stderr, is a loader rejection. It is not one without the
25797    /// line, with one run at another status, with the line only in stdout,
25798    /// or when the runs diverged. Each inner attempt is decided from its own
25799    /// report and output: one qualifying attempt is enough, and halves from
25800    /// two attempts never combine.
25801    #[test]
25802    fn loader_v2_rejection_takes_a_matched_pair_of_refused_runs() {
25803        let line = "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v3\n";
25804        let refused = compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 127, 127, line);
25805        assert!(loader_v2_rejection(&refused));
25806        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&compared_runs_attempt(
25807            Verdict::Matched,
25808            127,
25809            127,
25810            "guest: command not found\n"
25811        )));
25812        for (left, right) in [(127, 0), (0, 127), (127, 1)] {
25813            assert!(
25814                !loader_v2_rejection(&compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, left, right, line)),
25815                "runs exited {left} and {right}"
25816            );
25817        }
25818        let mut in_stdout = compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 127, 127, "");
25819        in_stdout.stdout = line.into();
25820        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&in_stdout));
25821        // Two refused runs that diverged differ in Hermit's own work before
25822        // exec: a determinism failure, which stays visible.
25823        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&compared_runs_attempt(
25824            Verdict::Diverged,
25825            127,
25826            127,
25827            line
25828        )));
25829
25830        let mut row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
25831        row.attempts = vec![
25832            compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 0, 0, ""),
25833            refused.clone(),
25834        ];
25835        assert!(loader_v2_rejected(&row));
25836        // One attempt has both runs at 127 but no line, the other the line
25837        // beside runs that exited 0: neither is a rejection on its own.
25838        row.attempts = vec![
25839            compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 127, 127, ""),
25840            compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 0, 0, line),
25841        ];
25842        assert!(!loader_v2_rejected(&row));
25843    }
25844
25845    /// An attempt whose retained report is a typed `run_failed` of `run` with
25846    /// `failure`, as `hermit log-diff` writes one from a `--verify-run` record,
25847    /// with `stderr` captured. The detail is Hermit's own words for a policy
25848    /// refusal, which name no cause.
25849    fn run_failed_attempt(
25850        run: crate::canonical_verdict::VerificationRun,
25851        failure: crate::canonical_verdict::RunFailure,
25852        stderr: &str,
25853    ) -> AttemptResult {
25854        let mut report = VerificationReport::no_result();
25855        report.no_result_reason = Some(crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::RunFailed {
25856            run,
25857            failure,
25858            detail: "Hermit refused the run: a fail-closed policy stopped it before completion. \
25859                     This is not a hermit failure; the refusal reason is above."
25860                .into(),
25861        });
25862        let mut attempt = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("unused");
25863        attempt.verification_report = Some(serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap());
25864        attempt.stderr = stderr.into();
25865        attempt
25866    }
25867
25868    /// The stderr of a run Hermit refused with `refusal` on the ptrace
25869    /// backend, as measured: the refusal line, the policy-refusal class line,
25870    /// then Hermit's error.
25871    fn refused_run_stderr(refusal: &str) -> String {
25872        format!(
25873            "{refusal}\nHERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal\nError: Hermit refused the \
25874             run: a fail-closed policy stopped it before completion. This is not a hermit \
25875             failure; the refusal reason is above.\n"
25876        )
25877    }
25878
25879    /// Hermit's refusal of a program interpreter's CPU-level abort under
25880    /// `profile`, the interpreter having printed glibc's message for `level`,
25881    /// followed by `why` (detcore/src/loader_cpu_abort.rs, `Watch::refusal`).
25882    fn interpreter_refusal(profile: &str, level: &str, why: &str) -> String {
25883        format!(
25884            "--cpu-profile {profile} refused: the program interpreter \
25885             /usr/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 of /work/program stopped before the program \
25886             started, printing \"Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support {level}\" and exiting \
25887             127; {why}"
25888        )
25889    }
25890
25891    /// Where Hermit watches the program interpreter (the ptrace backend), it
25892    /// replaces the loader's exit 127 with a typed refusal and exits 122
25893    /// itself (detcore/src/loader_cpu_abort.rs). A typed `run_failed` of run 1
25894    /// with failure `policy_refusal`, beside Hermit's refusal of an x86-64-v3
25895    /// interpreter on the x86-64-v2 CPU as a line of the attempt's stderr, is
25896    /// a loader rejection, whether or not a chaos pair ran its second run.
25897    /// Another policy refusal is not, nor an interpreter refusal that quotes
25898    /// another level or comes under another profile (Hermit's CPU table would
25899    /// then lack a feature, a defect to report, not a host's loader), nor the
25900    /// refusal line beside another failure, a refusal of run 2, in stdout,
25901    /// inside another line, or without a report. Each inner attempt is decided
25902    /// from its own report and output. The refusal texts are the ones Hermit
25903    /// printed in the measured runs, with the paths replaced.
25904    #[test]
25905    fn loader_v2_rejection_takes_the_typed_interpreter_refusal() {
25906        use crate::canonical_verdict::RunFailure;
25907        use crate::canonical_verdict::VerificationRun;
25908        let v3_on_v2 = interpreter_refusal(
25909            "x86-64-v2",
25910            "x86-64-v3",
25911            "the x86-64-v2 CPU this profile presents is below the x86-64-v3 it was built for; \
25912             rerun with --cpu-profile x86-64-v3, on a host that qualifies for it",
25913        );
25914        let policy_refused = |stderr: &str| {
25915            run_failed_attempt(VerificationRun::Run1, RunFailure::PolicyRefusal, stderr)
25916        };
25917        let refused = policy_refused(&refused_run_stderr(&v3_on_v2));
25918        assert!(loader_v2_rejection(&refused));
25919        // A chaos pair admits its second run, which is refused the same way;
25920        // the report is still run 1's refusal.
25921        let twice = refused_run_stderr(&v3_on_v2).repeat(2);
25922        assert!(loader_v2_rejection(&policy_refused(&twice)));
25923
25924        let defect = "Hermit's CPU table lacks a feature the loader checks, so please report this \
25925                      message";
25926        for (label, stderr) in [
25927            (
25928                "an x86-64-v3 admission refused for the host's XCR0",
25929                "HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal\nError: --cpu-profile x86-64-v3 \
25930                 refused: XCR0 0x2ff enables components the XINUSE probe does not cover (it \
25931                 covers 0x2e7)\n     > Hermit refused the run: a fail-closed policy stopped it \
25932                 before completion. This is not a hermit failure; the refusal reason is above.\n"
25933                    .to_string(),
25934            ),
25935            (
25936                "an x86-64-v2 interpreter on the x86-64-v2 CPU",
25937                refused_run_stderr(&interpreter_refusal(
25938                    "x86-64-v2",
25939                    "x86-64-v2",
25940                    &format!(
25941                        "although this profile presents x86-64-v2, which satisfies x86-64-v2: {defect}"
25942                    ),
25943                )),
25944            ),
25945            (
25946                "an x86-64-v3 interpreter under the x86-64-v3 profile",
25947                refused_run_stderr(&interpreter_refusal(
25948                    "x86-64-v3",
25949                    "x86-64-v3",
25950                    &format!(
25951                        "although this profile presents x86-64-v3, which satisfies x86-64-v3: {defect}"
25952                    ),
25953                )),
25954            ),
25955            (
25956                "the loader's own line alone",
25957                "Fatal glibc error: CPU does not support x86-64-v3\n".to_string(),
25958            ),
25959            (
25960                "the refusal inside another line",
25961                format!("guest: {v3_on_v2}\n"),
25962            ),
25963        ] {
25964            assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&policy_refused(&stderr)), "{label}");
25965        }
25966        for (run, failure) in [
25967            (VerificationRun::Run1, RunFailure::BackendFailure),
25968            (VerificationRun::Run2, RunFailure::PolicyRefusal),
25969        ] {
25970            assert!(
25971                !loader_v2_rejection(&run_failed_attempt(
25972                    run,
25973                    failure,
25974                    &refused_run_stderr(&v3_on_v2)
25975                )),
25976                "{run:?} {failure:?}"
25977            );
25978        }
25979        let mut in_stdout = policy_refused("");
25980        in_stdout.stdout = refused_run_stderr(&v3_on_v2);
25981        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&in_stdout));
25982        let mut untyped = refused.clone();
25983        untyped.verification_report = None;
25984        assert!(!loader_v2_rejection(&untyped));
25985
25986        // One attempt has run 1's policy refusal without the line, the other
25987        // the line beside runs that exited 0: neither is a rejection on its
25988        // own, and together they are not one.
25989        let mut row = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
25990        row.attempts = vec![
25991            policy_refused("HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal\n"),
25992            compared_runs_attempt(Verdict::Matched, 0, 0, &refused_run_stderr(&v3_on_v2)),
25993        ];
25994        assert!(!loader_v2_rejected(&row));
25995        row.attempts.push(refused);
25996        assert!(loader_v2_rejected(&row));
25997    }

26000    fn v2_oci_dir_env_must_name_an_absolute_oci_layout() {

26009        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
26010        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
26011        assert!(
26012            v2_oci_dir_from_env(Some(dir.clone().into_os_string()))
26013                .unwrap_err()
26014                .contains("holds no oci-layout file")
26015        );
26016        fs::write(
26017            dir.join("oci-layout"),
26018            b"{\"imageLayoutVersion\": \"1.0.0\"}\n",
26019        )
26020        .unwrap();
26021        assert_eq!(
26022            v2_oci_dir_from_env(Some(dir.clone().into_os_string())).unwrap(),
26023            Some(dir.clone())
26024        );
26025        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();

26028    #[test]
26029    fn current_cell_result_carries_result_and_failure_class() {
26030        let passed = serde_json::to_value(cell_result_that_located_nothing()).unwrap();
26031        assert_eq!(passed["result"], "pass");
26032        assert_eq!(passed["failure_class"], JsonValue::Null);
26033
26034        let mut failed = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26035        failed.outcome = "FAIL".into();
26036        failed.result = Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure);
26037        failed.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure);
26038        let failed = serde_json::to_value(failed).unwrap();
26039        assert_eq!(failed["result"], "determinism-failure");
26040        assert_eq!(failed["failure_class"], "product_failure");
26041
26042        let mut missing = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26043        missing.outcome = "FAIL".into();
26044        missing.result = Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure);
26045        missing.failure_class = None;
26046        assert_eq!(
26047            missing.require_current_classification().unwrap_err(),
26048            "FAIL result has no failure_class; current non-passes must be attributed"
26049        );
26050
26051        let mut legacy = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26052        legacy.outcome = "FAIL".into();
26053        legacy.result = None;
26054        legacy.failure_class = None;
26055        legacy
26056            .validate_recorded_classification()
26057            .expect("retained pre-field schema-4 row remains readable");
26058        assert!(legacy.require_current_classification().is_err());
26059
26060        let mut error_with_product_result = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26061        error_with_product_result.outcome = "ERROR".into();
26062        error_with_product_result.result = Some(ObservedResult::CrashError);
26063        error_with_product_result.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure);
26064        assert_eq!(
26065            error_with_product_result
26066                .require_current_classification()
26067                .unwrap_err(),
26068            "ERROR result must carry a non-product observation/classification, got (Some(CrashError), Some(ProductFailure))"
26069        );
26070
26071        let mut timeout = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26072        timeout.outcome = "ERROR".into();
26073        timeout.result = Some(ObservedResult::Timeout);
26074        timeout.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::NoResult);
26075        timeout.require_current_classification().unwrap();
26076
26077        let mut sandbox_denied = cell_result_that_located_nothing();
26078        sandbox_denied.outcome = "ERROR".into();
26079        sandbox_denied.result = Some(ObservedResult::SandboxDenied);
26080        sandbox_denied.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure);
26081        sandbox_denied
26082            .require_current_classification()
26083            .expect("typed sandbox denial is a current non-product result");

26086    /// A chaos cell its population floor failed while every attempt matched
26087    /// is a chaos-floor failure: a product failure no attempt contradicts,
26088    /// where the FAIL alone would have been inferred a crash-error that no
26089    /// attempt supports. A divergence, an attempt that did not match, or a
26090    /// FAIL the floor did not cause keeps its own result.
26091    #[test]
26092    fn a_chaos_floor_failure_over_matched_attempts_is_named_not_a_crash() {
26093        let mut matched = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("");
26094        matched.verification_report =
26095            Some(serde_json::to_string(&canonical_verification_report()).unwrap());
26096        let attempts = vec![matched.clone(), matched.clone()];
26097        let inferred = observed_result("chaos", "FAIL", &attempts, None);
26098        assert_eq!(inferred, Some(ObservedResult::CrashError));
26099        assert_eq!(
26100            chaos_floor_result(inferred, true, &attempts),
26101            Some(ObservedResult::ChaosFloorFailure)
26102        );
26103        assert_eq!(
26104            ObservedResult::ChaosFloorFailure.failure_class(),
26105            Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure)
26106        );
26107        // Not caused by the floor: unchanged.
26108        assert_eq!(chaos_floor_result(inferred, false, &attempts), inferred);
26109        // An attempt without a matched report: the crash stands.
26110        let mut unmatched = matched.clone();
26111        unmatched.verification_report = None;
26112        let mixed = vec![matched.clone(), unmatched];
26113        assert_eq!(
26114            chaos_floor_result(inferred, true, &mixed),
26115            Some(ObservedResult::CrashError)
26116        );
26117        // A divergence keeps its own result.
26118        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
26119        report.verified = false;
26120        report.bitwise_parity = false;
26121        report.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
26122        let mut diverged = matched.clone();
26123        diverged.verification_report = Some(serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap());
26124        let with_divergence = vec![matched, diverged];
26125        let divergence = observed_result("chaos", "FAIL", &with_divergence, None);
26126        assert_eq!(divergence, Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure));
26127        assert_eq!(
26128            chaos_floor_result(divergence, true, &with_divergence),
26129            Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure)
26130        );
26131        assert_eq!(chaos_floor_result(None, true, &attempts), None);
26132    }

26275    #[test]
26276    fn a_diverged_chaos_cell_is_a_determinism_failure_as_in_verify() {
26277        // A chaos cell compares two runs of one seed with the strict comparator,
26278        // as a verify cell compares its two runs, so the same diverged
26279        // comparison is the same product failure in both modes. Typed
26280        // crash-error instead, the row carried divergence evidence that the
26281        // stress series refuses for any outcome but diverged.
26282        let report = r#"{"verified":false,"bitwise_parity":false,"verdict":"diverged","comparison":{"strictness":"canonical","compare_logs":true,"record_envelope":"all_records_v1","display_name":"BitwiseInfoV1","compare_io_buffers":true,"log_scope":"info","virtualize_time":true,"strip_lines":false,"canonicalize_addresses":true,"full_trace":true,"exact_remainder":true,"stripped_prefixes":["real-wall-clock-prefix/v1"],"canonicalizations":["host-address-to-first-appearance-ordinal/v1"],"ignore_lines":false,"skip_commit":false,"skip_detlog":false},"compared_log_messages":{"left":1,"right":1},"first_divergent_scheduler_turn":4,"first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds":7,"first_divergent_record":9,"first_divergent_syscall":2,"first_divergent_left_message":"left","first_divergent_right_message":"right","compared_outputs":{"left":{"exit_code":null,"signal":null,"stdout_sha256":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","stdout_bytes":0,"stderr_sha256":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","stderr_bytes":0},"right":{"exit_code":null,"signal":null,"stdout_sha256":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","stdout_bytes":0,"stderr_sha256":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","stderr_bytes":0}},"no_result_reason":null,"infrastructure_error":null,"guest_exit_code":null,"guest_signal":null}"#;
26283        let mut diverged = attempt_with_sabre_evidence("");
26284        diverged.outcome = "FAIL".into();
26285        diverged.status = Some(1);
26286        diverged.verification_report = Some(report.into());
26287        assert_eq!(verification_verdict(&diverged), Some(Verdict::Diverged));
26288        for mode in ["verify", "chaos"] {
26289            let result = observed_result(mode, "FAIL", std::slice::from_ref(&diverged), None);
26290            assert_eq!(result, Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure), "{mode}");
26291            assert_eq!(
26292                failure_class("FAIL", result, None),
26293                Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure),
26294                "{mode}"
26295            );
26296
26297            // A failure without a diverged attempt is still a crash.
26298            let mut crashed = diverged.clone();
26299            crashed.verification_report = None;
26300            assert_eq!(
26301                observed_result(mode, "FAIL", &[crashed], None),
26302                Some(ObservedResult::CrashError),
26303                "{mode}"
26304            );
26305
26306            // The timeout and non-product guards still decide first.
26307            let mut timed_out = diverged.clone();
26308            timed_out.index = "2".into();
26309            timed_out.timed_out = true;
26310            assert_eq!(
26311                observed_result(mode, "FAIL", &[diverged.clone(), timed_out], None),
26312                Some(ObservedResult::Timeout),
26313                "{mode}"
26314            );
26315            for error_kind in ["infrastructure", "incomplete-verification-evidence"] {
26316                assert_eq!(
26317                    observed_result(
26318                        mode,
26319                        "ERROR",
26320                        std::slice::from_ref(&diverged),
26321                        Some(error_kind)
26322                    ),
26323                    None,
26324                    "{mode}, {error_kind}"
26325                );
26326            }
26327        }
26328    }

26444    #[test]
26445    fn sabre_path_evidence_requires_every_execution_and_no_fallback() {
26446        let clean = r#"{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}"#;
26447        let complete = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(&format!("{clean}\n{clean}\n"));
26448        assert_eq!(
26449            summarize_sabre_path_evidence(std::slice::from_ref(&complete))
26450                .unwrap()
26451                .unwrap()["eligible"],
26452            true
26453        );
26454
26455        let mut ptrace_reference = complete.clone();
26456        ptrace_reference.index = "parity-reference".into();
26457        ptrace_reference.argv[2] = "ptrace".into();
26458        ptrace_reference.sabre_path_evidence = None;
26459        ptrace_reference.sabre_path_evidence_sha256 = None;
26460        assert_eq!(
26461            summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&[complete, ptrace_reference])
26462                .unwrap()
26463                .unwrap()["eligible"],
26464            true,
26465            "a ptrace parity operand is not a missing SaBRe execution"
26466        );
26467
26468        let short = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(&format!("{clean}\n"));
26469        let summary = summarize_sabre_path_evidence(std::slice::from_ref(&short))
26470            .unwrap()
26471            .unwrap();
26472        assert_eq!(summary["complete"], false);
26473        assert_eq!(summary["eligible"], false);
26474
26475        let malformed = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(
26476            r#"{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":"0","trusted_shared_object_sites":"0","trusted_shared_objects":"none"}
26477{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":"0","trusted_shared_object_sites":"0","trusted_shared_objects":"none"}
26478"#,
26479        );
26480        assert!(summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&[malformed]).is_err());
26481
26482        let unknown = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(
26483            r#"{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[],"unexpected":0}
26484{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}
26485"#,
26486        );
26487        let error = summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&[unknown]).unwrap_err();
26488        assert!(error.contains("unknown field `unexpected`"), "{error}");
26489
26490        let missing = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(
26491            r#"{"schema":1,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}
26492{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}
26493"#,
26494        );
26495        let error = summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&[missing]).unwrap_err();
26496        assert!(
26497            error.contains("missing field `guest_rpc_observed`"),
26498            "{error}"
26499        );
26500
26501        let future = attempt_with_sabre_evidence(
26502            r#"{"schema":2,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[],"future_field":"value"}
26503{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}
26504"#,
26505        );
26506        assert_eq!(
26507            summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&[future]).unwrap_err(),
26508            "invalid SaBRe path-evidence record: schema must be 1"
26509        );
26510    }

26596    fn parity_fixture_verification(verdict: Verdict) -> VerificationReport {
26597        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
26598        let output = parity_fixture_output();
26599        report.guest_exit_code = Some(0);
26600        report.compared_outputs = Some(crate::canonical_verdict::ComparedOutputs {
26601            left: output.clone(),
26602            right: output,
26603        });
26604        if verdict == Verdict::Diverged {
26605            report.verified = false;
26606            report.bitwise_parity = false;
26607            report.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
26608            report.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = Some(7);
26609            report.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = Some(18);
26610            report.first_divergent_record = Some(2);
26611            report.first_divergent_syscall = Some(1);
26612            report.first_divergent_left_message = Some("candidate-left".into());
26613            report.first_divergent_right_message = Some("candidate-right".into());
26614        }
26615        report
26616    }

26618    /// Run one verify cell through the production `run_cell` path against a
26619    /// fixture Hermit. The fixture records each invocation. It also records any
26620    /// `log-diff` call and fails it, so a reintroduced cross-backend comparison
26621    /// cannot pass silently.
26622    ///
26623    /// `verdict` is the fixture's own same-backend strict-verification verdict.
26624    /// A `Diverged` fixture writes a diverged report and exits 1, the shape a
26625    /// real `hermit run --verify` produces when its two runs differ.
26626    fn run_production_verify_fixture(
26627        backend: &str,
26628        verdict: Verdict,
26629    ) -> (CellResult, String, bool) {
26630        run_production_verify_fixture_with_retention(backend, verdict, true, |_| {})
26631    }
26632
26633    fn run_production_verify_fixture_with_retention(
26634        backend: &str,
26635        verdict: Verdict,
26636        keep_logs: bool,
26637        inspect: impl FnOnce(&CellResult),
26638    ) -> (CellResult, String, bool) {
26639        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
26640            "hermit-runner-production-verify-{}-{:?}-{backend}-{verdict:?}",
26641            std::process::id(),
26642            std::thread::current().id()
26643        ));
26644        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
26645        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
26646        fs::write(
26647            root.join("verification.json"),
26648            serde_json::to_vec(&parity_fixture_verification(verdict)).unwrap(),
26649        )
26650        .unwrap();
26651        let exit_status = if verdict == Verdict::Diverged {
26652            "1"
26653        } else {
26654            "0"
26655        };
26656        fs::write(root.join("exit-status"), exit_status).unwrap();
26657
26658        let hermit = root.join("hermit");
26659        crate::exec_safe_fs::write_executable(
26660            &hermit,
26661            r#"#!/bin/sh
26662set -eu
26663if [ "${1-}" = "log-diff" ] && [ "${2-}" != "--verify-json" ]; then
26664  printf 'log-diff\n' >> "$PWD/invocations"
26665  exit 3
26666fi
26667
26668backend=
26669verdict=
26670logdir=
26671rundir=
26672while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
26673  case "$1" in
26674    --backend) backend=$2; shift 2 ;;
26675    --verify-json) verdict=$2; shift 2 ;;
26676    --verify-log-dir) logdir=$2; shift 2 ;;
26677    --verify-run) rundir=$2; shift 2 ;;
26678    *) shift ;;
26679  esac
26680done
26681
26682if [ -n "$rundir" ]; then
26683  # One run of the pair ([`VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT`]).
26684  printf 'run:%s\n' "$backend" >> "$PWD/invocations"
26685  mkdir "$rundir"
26686  printf '{}\n' > "$rundir/verify-run.json"
26687  printf 'pair guest output\n' > "$rundir/stdout"
26688  printf 'pair guest stderr\n' > "$rundir/stderr"
26689  printf 'INFO detcore: only\n' > "$rundir/run.log"
26690  if [ -n "${HERMIT_SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE-}" ]; then
26691    printf '%s\n' '{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}' >> "$HERMIT_SABRE_PATH_EVIDENCE"
26692  fi
26693  exit 0
26694fi
26695printf 'compare\n' >> "$PWD/invocations"
26696
26697# This log differs from anything a ptrace run of the same guest would write.
26698# Before https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301 that difference was a
26699# ParityFailure; now nothing compares it with another backend.
26700if [ -n "$logdir" ]; then
26701  mkdir -p "$logdir"
26702  printf 'INFO detcore: only\n' > "$logdir/run1_log_fixture.log"
26703fi
26704
26705cp "$PWD/verification.json" "$verdict"
26706exit "$(cat "$PWD/exit-status")"
26707"#,
26708            0o755,
26709        )
26710        .unwrap();
26711
26712        let mut cell = ptrace_cell("verify");
26713        cell.test.id = "fixture/ordinary-verify-production".into();
26714        cell.id.test = cell.test.id.clone();
26715        cell.id.backend = Some(backend.into());
26716        cell.enabled = false;
26717        cell.cpu_timeout_seconds = 5;
26718        cell.timeout_seconds = 10;
26719        let mut context = run_context(&root);
26720        context.hermit_bin = hermit;
26721        context.run_verify_strict = true;
26722        context.keep_logs = keep_logs;
26723
26724        let result = run_cell(&context, &cell).unwrap();
26725        assert_cpu_source_roundtrip(&result);
26726        let invocations = fs::read_to_string(root.join("invocations")).unwrap_or_default();
26727        let retained_parity_report = std::fs::read_dir(&result.artifact_dir)
26728            .into_iter()
26729            .flatten()
26730            .filter_map(Result::ok)
26731            .any(|entry| {
26732                entry
26733                    .file_name()
26734                    .to_string_lossy()
26735                    .contains("backend-parity")
26736            });
26737        inspect(&result);
26738        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
26739        (result, invocations, retained_parity_report)
26740    }

26742    /// Every candidate verify cell full validation selects, of every test in
26743    /// the parity population (every test whose ptrace verify cell full
26744    /// validation selects, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301),
26745    /// hands its guest the same arguments as the ptrace reference, so a
26746    /// parity comparison of the two can be labelled equal-input. The only
26747    /// exceptions are the cells pinned in `DELIBERATELY_UNEQUAL`, each with
26748    /// why: their guests are told which backend they run on, so their argv
26749    /// differs from ptrace's and their parity comparison is labelled
26750    /// unequal-input (`parity::inputs_equalized` compares argv). A new
26751    /// difference fails here until it is fixed or pinned with its reason, and
26752    /// a pinned cell that stops differing fails too.
26753    #[test]
26754    fn population_parity_candidates_preserve_identical_guest_arguments() {
26755        const DELIBERATELY_UNEQUAL: &[(&str, &str, &str)] = &[
26756            (
26757                "c-programs/inotify-blocking-read",
26758                "dbt",
26759                "`--no-received` skips the received descriptor, which DBT discovers with the \
26760                 O_NONBLOCK Detcore set on its sender's description, as it does a received pipe end",
26761            ),
26762            (
26763                "c-programs/inotify-blocking-read",
26764                "kvm",
26765                "`--no-zero-read` skips the zero-count read, which KVM's executor refuses by name \
26766                 because it cannot show that the host read returns at once",
26767            ),
26768            (
26769                "c-programs/inotify-blocking-signal",
26770                "kvm",
26771                "`--no-process-signal` skips the signal sent to the process, which KVM refuses by \
26772                 name for a process of several threads \
26773                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034)",
26774            ),
26775            (
26776                "c-programs/madvise-determinism",
26777                "kvm",
26778                "`--kvm` adds the guest's KVM-only madvise advice checks",
26779            ),
26780            (
26781                "c-programs/pipe2-errno-precedence",
26782                "kvm",
26783                "the kvm cell passes no expected pipe capacity (ptrace, dbt and sabre pass \
26784                 8192), so its guest prints F_GETPIPE_SZ without asserting Detcore's pin",
26785            ),
26786            (
26787                "c-programs/proc-own-links",
26788                "dbt",
26789                "`--no-leader-exit`, `--no-exe-changes` and `--base-exe-truncation` skip the \
26790                 process whose leader exits, whose remaining thread's readlinks fail with ESRCH \
26791                 under DBT (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4697), and the exec'd copy's \
26792                 changes to its own image, whose exe link DBT refuses by name, and check its exe \
26793                 answer for a short buffer as DBT's base EINVAL \
26794                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4711), both as at the base",
26795            ),
26796            (
26797                "c-programs/proc-own-links",
26798                "kvm",
26799                "`--no-leader-exit` and `--no-fs-threads` skip the process whose leader exits, \
26800                 whose join of the exited leader waits in one run and not in another under KVM \
26801                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4563), and the thread created without \
26802                 CLONE_FS, which KVM refuses (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4698)",
26803            ),
26804            (
26805                "c-programs/proc-own-links",
26806                "liteinst",
26807                "`--no-threads` and `--no-exec` skip the thread, the process whose leader exits \
26808                 and the exec'd copy: in-guest LiteInst creates no threads and runs no exec",
26809            ),
26810            (
26811                "c-programs/proc-own-links",
26812                "in-guest-trap",
26813                "`--no-threads` and `--no-exec` skip the thread, the process whose leader exits \
26814                 and the exec'd copy: in-guest LiteInst creates no threads and runs no exec",
26815            ),
26816            (
26817                "c-programs/proc-fd-directory",
26818                "kvm",
26819                "`--no-private-tables` and `--no-fifo-threads` skip the two checks KVM cannot \
26820                 run: it gives no thread a descriptor table of its own, and its executor holds \
26821                 the turn in a blocking FIFO open",
26822            ),
26823            (
26824                "c-programs/proc-locks",
26825                "kvm",
26826                "`rendered` requires Linux's answers to vectored reads of /proc/locks, which \
26827                 Detcore renders itself on KVM (package K slice K8-h of \
26828                 https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4213); ptrace serves a snapshot of the \
26829                 kernel's file, whose vectored reads are ENOSYS, a named limitation. `ofd` takes \
26830                 OFD locks instead of the record locks LOCK_API=1 selects: KVM's provider holds a \
26831                 record lock as an OFD lock (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/1223), \
26832                 whose /proc/locks rows Detcore refuses by name",
26833            ),
26834            (
26835                "c-programs/robust-list-owner-death-routes",
26836                "kvm",
26837                "`skip-exec-sibling` leaves out the exec that ends an owning sibling: KVM hangs at \
26838                 an exec by a process with another live thread \
26839                 (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4904)",
26840            ),
26841            (
26842                "c-programs/scm-rights-received-descriptors",
26843                "in-guest-trap",
26844                "`--no-exec` skips the exec check: in-guest LiteInst refuses execve",
26845            ),
26846            (
26847                "c-programs/scm-rights-received-descriptors",
26848                "liteinst",
26849                "`--no-exec` skips the exec check: in-guest LiteInst refuses execve",
26850            ),
26851        ];
26852        let root = crate::compiled_manifest_dir!().join("../..");
26853        let manifests = ManifestSet::load(&root).unwrap();
26854        let cells = manifests
26855            .select(&Selection {
26856                population: Some(Population::Required),
26857                mode: Some("verify".into()),
26858                ..Selection::default()
26859            })
26860            .unwrap();
26861        let population = cells
26862            .iter()
26863            .filter(|cell| cell.id.backend.as_deref() == Some("ptrace"))
26864            .map(|cell| cell.id.test.clone())
26865            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
26866        let candidates = cells
26867            .iter()
26868            .filter(|cell| population.contains(&cell.id.test))
26869            .filter(|cell| cell.id.backend.as_deref() != Some("ptrace"))
26870            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
26871        // The population's selected candidates (`generate-parity-cells`
26872        // counts 536 at this change), on every candidate backend that has one.
26873        assert!(candidates.len() > 500, "{}", candidates.len());
26874        let backends = candidates
26875            .iter()
26876            .filter_map(|cell| cell.id.backend.as_deref())
26877            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
26878        assert!(
26879            ["dbt", "kvm"]
26880                .iter()
26881                .all(|backend| backends.contains(backend)),
26882            "{backends:?}"
26883        );
26884        // SaBRe is archived (crate::archived): full validation selects none
26885        // of its cells, so none is a selected candidate.
26886        assert!(!backends.contains("sabre"), "{backends:?}");
26887        assert!(
26888            candidates
26889                .iter()
26890                .any(|cell| cell.id.test == "c-programs/readdir-order-identity"
26891                    && cell.id.backend.as_deref() == Some("kvm"))
26892        );
26893        let mut unequal = BTreeMap::new();
26894        for cell in candidates {
26895            let candidate = cell.id.backend.as_deref().unwrap();
26896            let (theirs, ours) = (
26897                cell_guest_args(cell, candidate),
26898                cell_guest_args(cell, "ptrace"),
26899            );
26900            if theirs != ours {
26901                unequal.insert(
26902                    (cell.id.test.clone(), candidate.to_string()),
26903                    format!("{theirs:?} vs ptrace {ours:?}"),
26904                );
26905            }
26906            if cell.id.test == "c-programs/readdir-order-identity" {
26907                let required = [
26908                    "--require-small-determinized",
26909                    "--require-large-determinized",
26910                ];
26911                assert_eq!(theirs, required);
26912                assert_eq!(ours, required);
26913            }
26914        }
26915        let pinned = DELIBERATELY_UNEQUAL
26916            .iter()
26917            .map(|(test, backend, _)| (test.to_string(), backend.to_string()))
26918            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
26919        assert_eq!(
26920            unequal.keys().cloned().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>(),
26921            pinned,
26922            "candidates whose guest arguments differ from ptrace's: {unequal:#?}"
26923        );
26924    }
