26926    /// The kvm, liteinst and sabre candidates checked above used to add a ptrace reference run and a `hermit log-diff` comparison, and the
26927    /// comparison could overwrite their outcome. Since
26928    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301 each one runs only its own
26929    /// backend's strict verification, even when its log differs from ptrace's.
26930    #[test]
26931    fn non_ptrace_verify_cells_run_only_their_own_backend() {
26932        for backend in ["kvm", "liteinst", "sabre"] {
26933            let (result, invocations, retained_parity_report) =
26934                run_production_verify_fixture(backend, Verdict::Matched);
26935            assert_eq!(result.outcome, "PASS", "{backend}: {result:#?}");
26936            assert_eq!(result.result, Some(ObservedResult::Pass), "{backend}");
26937            assert_eq!(result.failure_class, None, "{backend}");
26938            assert_eq!(result.error_kind, None, "{backend}");
26939            assert!(!retained_parity_report, "{backend}");
26940            assert_eq!(result.attempts.len(), 1, "{backend}");
26941            assert_eq!(result.attempts[0].index, "1", "{backend}");
26942            assert_eq!(
26943                verification_verdict(&result.attempts[0]),
26944                Some(Verdict::Matched),
26945                "{backend}"
26946            );
26947            assert_eq!(
26948                invocations,
26949                format!("run:{backend}\nrun:{backend}\ncompare\n")
26950            );
26951            let observations = &result.cpu_observations.as_ref().unwrap().invocations;
26952            assert_eq!(observations.len(), 1, "{backend}: {observations:#?}");
26953            assert!(
26954                matches!(
26955                    &observations[0].role,
26956                    InvocationRole::Execution { attempt_index, .. } if attempt_index == "1"
26957                ),
26958                "{backend}: {observations:#?}"
26959            );
26960            if backend == "sabre" {
26961                assert_eq!(result.execution_path.as_ref().unwrap()["eligible"], true);
26962            }
26963        }
26964    }
26965
26966    /// The failing half of the test above. Before
26967    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3301 a non-ptrace cell whose
26968    /// own strict verification diverged was a determinism failure, and a SaBRe
26969    /// cell kept that result only while its path evidence was eligible. Removing
26970    /// the ptrace reference run must not change either fact: the cell fails as a
26971    /// product determinism failure, keeps the divergence position its own report
26972    /// located, and still runs its backend exactly once.
26973    #[test]
26974    fn non_ptrace_verify_cells_fail_on_their_own_divergence() {
26975        for backend in ["kvm", "liteinst", "sabre"] {
26976            let (result, invocations, retained_parity_report) =
26977                run_production_verify_fixture(backend, Verdict::Diverged);
26978            assert_eq!(result.outcome, "FAIL", "{backend}: {result:#?}");
26979            assert_eq!(
26980                result.result,
26981                Some(ObservedResult::DeterminismFailure),
26982                "{backend}"
26983            );
26984            assert_eq!(
26985                result.failure_class,
26986                Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure),
26987                "{backend}"
26988            );
26989            assert_eq!(result.error_kind, None, "{backend}");
26990            assert!(!retained_parity_report, "{backend}");
26991            assert_eq!(result.attempts.len(), 1, "{backend}");
26992            assert_eq!(
26993                verification_verdict(&result.attempts[0]),
26994                Some(Verdict::Diverged),
26995                "{backend}"
26996            );
26997            assert_eq!(
26998                invocations,
26999                format!("run:{backend}\nrun:{backend}\ncompare\n")
27000            );
27001            assert_eq!(result.first_divergent_scheduler_turn, Some(7), "{backend}");
27002            assert_eq!(
27003                result.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds,
27004                Some(18),
27005                "{backend}"
27006            );
27007            assert_eq!(result.first_divergent_record, Some(2), "{backend}");
27008            assert_eq!(result.first_divergent_syscall, Some(1), "{backend}");
27009            assert_eq!(
27010                result.first_divergent_left_message.as_deref(),
27011                Some("candidate-left"),
27012                "{backend}"
27013            );
27014            assert_eq!(
27015                result.first_divergent_right_message.as_deref(),
27016                Some("candidate-right"),
27017                "{backend}"
27018            );
27019            if backend == "sabre" {
27020                assert_eq!(result.execution_path.as_ref().unwrap()["eligible"], true);
27021            }
27022        }
27023    }

27109            verify_runs: None,
27110            single_run_capture: None,
27111            sabre_path_evidence: None,
27112            cell_dir: dir.clone(),
27113            expected_guest_exit: None,
27114            expected_stdout: None,
27115            expected_stdout_contains: None,
27116            expected_stderr: None,

27118            attempt: "1".into(),
27119            fixed_workdir_source: dir.join("workdir/1"),
27120        };
27121        let result = execute_spec(&spec).unwrap();
27122        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();

27126    #[test]
27127    fn skid_overshoot_receipt_is_an_infrastructure_error_with_comparison_evidence() {
27128        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
27129        report.verified = false;
27130        report.bitwise_parity = false;
27131        report.verdict = Verdict::InfrastructureError;
27132        report.infrastructure_error = Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count: 2 });
27133        let report = serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap();
27134
27135        let result = attempt_from_script(
27136            "ptrace",
27137            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 122",
27138            Some(&report),
27139        );
27140
27141        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR");
27142        assert_eq!(result.error_kind.as_deref(), Some("infrastructure"));
27143        assert_eq!(result.status, Some(122));
27144        assert!(
27145            result
27146                .reason
27147                .as_deref()
27148                .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains("2 HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT")),
27149            "infrastructure error must retain the recorded count: {result:?}"
27150        );
27151        assert!(
27152            result
27153                .verification_report
27154                .as_deref()
27155                .is_some_and(|json| json.contains("\"comparison\":{")),
27156            "infrastructure error must retain the completed comparison: {result:?}"
27157        );
27158
27159        let mut before_comparison = canonical_verification_report();
27160        before_comparison.verified = false;
27161        before_comparison.bitwise_parity = false;
27162        before_comparison.verdict = Verdict::InfrastructureError;
27163        before_comparison.infrastructure_error =
27164            Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count: 1 });
27165        before_comparison.comparison = None;
27166        before_comparison.compared_log_messages = None;
27167        let before_comparison = serde_json::to_string(&before_comparison).unwrap();
27168        let result = attempt_from_script(
27169            "ptrace",
27170            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 122",
27171            Some(&before_comparison),
27172        );
27173        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR");
27174        assert_eq!(result.error_kind.as_deref(), Some("infrastructure"));
27175        assert!(
27176            result
27177                .reason
27178                .as_deref()
27179                .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains("1 HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT")),
27180            "comparison-null infrastructure error must retain its cause: {result:?}"
27181        );
27182    }

27184    /// The verify cell a row records: the fixture cell on the row's backend,
27185    /// whose recipe selects exactly the row's relaxations and expected guest
27186    /// exit.
27187    fn cell_recorded_by(row: &CellResult) -> SelectedCell {
27188        let mut cell = ptrace_cell("verify");
27189        cell.id.backend = row.backend.clone();
27190        let backend = row.backend.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "native".into());
27191        let recipe = cell.test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap();
27192        for relaxation in &row.relaxations {
27193            if let Some(reason) = relaxation.strip_prefix(DIAGNOSTIC_RELAXATION_PREFIX) {
27194                recipe.diagnostic.insert(backend.clone(), reason.into());
27195                continue;
27196            }
27197            let (flag, reason) = relaxation.split_once(": ").unwrap();
27198            match flag {
27199                "--no-detlog-io-buffers" => {
27200                    recipe.compare_io_buffers = Some(false);
27201                    recipe.compare_io_buffers_disabled_reason = Some(reason.into());
27202                }
27203                "--no-rcb-time" => {
27204                    recipe.rcb_time = Some(false);
27205                    recipe.rcb_time_disabled_reason = Some(reason.into());
27206                }
27207                "comparator=stripped" => {
27208                    recipe.comparator = Some(Comparator::Stripped);
27209                    recipe.comparator_reason = Some(reason.into());
27210                }
27211                flag if allowed_hermit_arg(flag) => {
27212                    recipe
27213                        .hermit_args
27214                        .entry(backend.clone())
27215                        .or_default()
27216                        .push(flag.into());
27217                    recipe.hermit_args_reason = Some(reason.into());
27218                }
27219                other => panic!("a fixture row records the relaxation {other:?}"),
27220            }
27221        }
27222        recipe.expected_guest_exit = row.expected_guest_exit.clone();
27223        assert_eq!(cell_relaxations(&cell), row.relaxations);
27224        assert_eq!(cell_expected_guest_exit(&cell), row.expected_guest_exit);
27225        cell
27226    }
27227
27228    /// `row` with the command fields the executor writes for the cell it
27229    /// records ([`cell_recorded_by`]) under `context`: each attempt's argv,
27230    /// guest argv, env, cwd and shell command as `build_spec` renders them,
27231    /// and the row's copies of the first attempt's (`run_cell_inner`). The
27232    /// fixture attempts execute a shell script in place of Hermit, so the
27233    /// command they record is the script's, which no retained row may carry
27234    /// ([`retained_verify_invocation_error`]).
27235    fn with_executor_invocation_in(row: CellResult, context: &RunContext) -> CellResult {
27236        let cell = cell_recorded_by(&row);
27237        with_executor_invocation_for(row, context, &cell)
27238    }
27239
27240    /// `row` with the command fields the executor writes for `cell` under
27241    /// `context`, as [`with_executor_invocation_in`] writes them for the cell
27242    /// the row records. A caller passes a cell whose recipe adds what a row
27243    /// does not record (a workdir, a guest environment) or a context with
27244    /// another execution root or log retention.
27245    fn with_executor_invocation_for(
27246        row: CellResult,
27247        context: &RunContext,
27248        cell: &SelectedCell,
27249    ) -> CellResult {
27250        with_executor_invocation_argv_for(row, context, cell, |argv| argv)
27251    }
27252
27253    /// Build the pair before recording any command fields. Explicit pair
27254    /// callers use the same cell's comparison/run inputs through the public
27255    /// pair API; ordinary manifest rows keep `build_spec`'s argv unchanged.
27256    fn with_executor_invocation_argv_for(
27257        mut row: CellResult,
27258        context: &RunContext,
27259        cell: &SelectedCell,
27260        build_pair: impl Fn(Vec<String>) -> Vec<String>,
27261    ) -> CellResult {
27262        let dir = context.root.join("results/cell");
27263        for (position, attempt) in row.attempts.iter_mut().enumerate() {
27264            let mut spec = build_spec(
27265                context,
27266                cell,
27267                dir.clone(),
27268                attempt.guest_argv.clone(),
27269                &(position + 1).to_string(),
27270                None,
27271                3,
27272            )
27273            .unwrap();
27274            spec.argv = build_pair(spec.argv);
27275            attempt.cwd = spec.cwd.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
27276            attempt.shell_command = shell_command(&attempt.cwd, &spec.env, &spec.argv);
27277            attempt.argv = spec.argv;
27278            attempt.guest_argv = spec.guest_argv;
27279            attempt.env = spec.env;
27280        }
27281        if let Some(first) = row.attempts.first() {
27282            row.argv = first.argv.clone();
27283            row.guest_argv = first.guest_argv.clone();
27284            row.env = first.env.clone();
27285            row.cwd = first.cwd.clone();
27286            row.shell_command = first.shell_command.clone();
27287        }
27288        row.effective_args = row.argv.iter().skip(1).cloned().collect();
27289        row.log_level = Some("info".into());
27290        row
27291    }
27292
27293    /// [`with_executor_invocation_in`] under the fixture context, with the
27294    /// canonical comparison flag Hermit's probe enables.
27295    fn with_executor_invocation(row: CellResult) -> CellResult {
27296        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
27297            "hermit-runner-executor-invocation-{}-{:?}",
27298            std::process::id(),
27299            std::thread::current().id()
27300        ));
27301        let mut context = run_context(&root);
27302        context.run_verify_strict = true;
27303        let row = with_executor_invocation_in(row, &context);
27304        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
27305        row
27306    }
27307
27308    /// A retained verify row is re-decided by what it records: its backend,
27309    /// relaxations, expected guest exit and comparator. Its command lines must
27310    /// therefore be the invocation the executor writes for exactly those
27311    /// ([`retained_verify_invocation_error`],
27312    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>). Every shape the
27313    /// executor writes is accepted, whatever execution root, log retention,
27314    /// workdir, guest environment, relaxations or declared exit produced it.
27315    /// Each row below that differs from an accepted one in one respect is
27316    /// refused by the named check, and so by the skid predicate and the
27317    /// retained-pass check.
27318    #[test]
27319    fn a_retained_command_line_must_be_the_executor_invocation_its_row_records() {
27320        fn at(argv: &[String], token: &str) -> usize {
27321            argv.iter()
27322                .position(|arg| arg == token)
27323                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{token} is not in {argv:?}"))
27324        }
27325        // `row` with each attempt's argv edited by `edit`, its shell command
27326        // rendered again and the row's copies taken again, so that the
27327        // command line is the row's only defect.
27328        fn with_argv(row: &CellResult, edit: impl Fn(&mut Vec<String>)) -> CellResult {
27329            let mut row = row.clone();
27330            for attempt in &mut row.attempts {
27331                edit(&mut attempt.argv);
27332                attempt.shell_command = shell_command(&attempt.cwd, &attempt.env, &attempt.argv);
27333            }
27334            row.argv = row.attempts[0].argv.clone();
27335            row.shell_command = row.attempts[0].shell_command.clone();
27336            row.effective_args = row.argv[1..].to_vec();
27337            row
27338        }
27339        fn insert_before(token: &str, inserted: &[&str]) -> impl Fn(&mut Vec<String>) {
27340            let token = token.to_owned();
27341            let inserted: Vec<String> = inserted.iter().map(|arg| (*arg).to_owned()).collect();
27342            move |argv| {
27343                let index = at(argv, &token);
27344                argv.splice(index..index, inserted.iter().cloned());
27345            }
27346        }
27347        fn replace_after(flag: &str, value: &str) -> impl Fn(&mut Vec<String>) {
27348            let (flag, value) = (flag.to_owned(), value.to_owned());
27349            move |argv| {
27350                let index = at(argv, &flag);
27351                argv[index + 1] = value.clone();
27352            }
27353        }
27354        fn replace_flag(old: &str, new: &str) -> impl Fn(&mut Vec<String>) {
27355            let (old, new) = (old.to_owned(), new.to_owned());
27356            move |argv| {
27357                let index = at(argv, &old);
27358                argv[index] = new.clone();
27359            }
27360        }
27361        fn without(token: &str, values: usize) -> impl Fn(&mut Vec<String>) {
27362            let token = token.to_owned();
27363            move |argv| {
27364                let index = at(argv, &token);
27365                argv.drain(index..=index + values);
27366            }
27367        }
27368        fn accepted(label: &str, row: &CellResult) {
27369            assert_eq!(
27370                retained_verify_invocation_error(row),
27371                None,
27372                "{label} is a command line the executor writes: {:?}",
27373                row.argv
27374            );
27375        }
27376        fn accepted_skid(label: &str, row: &CellResult, count: u64) {
27377            accepted(label, row);
27378            assert_eq!(
27379                skid_overshoot_only_reports(row),
27380                Some(count),
27381                "{label} is a skid-only row: {:?}",
27382                row.argv
27383            );
27384        }
27385        fn refused(label: &str, row: &CellResult, check: &str) {
27386            let error = retained_verify_invocation_error(row)
27387                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label} was accepted: {:?}", row.argv));
27388            assert!(
27389                error.contains(check),
27390                "{label} was refused by another check: {error}"
27391            );
27392            assert_eq!(
27393                skid_overshoot_only_reports(row),
27394                None,
27395                "{label} still reads as a skid-only row"
27396            );
27397        }
27398
27399        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
27400            "hermit-runner-invocation-shapes-{}-{:?}",
27401            std::process::id(),
27402            std::thread::current().id()
27403        ));
27404        let context = |edit: &dyn Fn(&mut RunContext)| {
27405            let mut context = run_context(&root);
27406            context.run_verify_strict = true;
27407            edit(&mut context);
27408            context
27409        };
27410        // The cell a row records, with recipe additions the row does not
27411        // record, rendered under `context`.
27412        let rendered = |row: &CellResult, context: &RunContext, edit: &dyn Fn(&mut ModeRecipe)| {
27413            let mut cell = cell_recorded_by(row);
27414            edit(cell.test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap());
27415            with_executor_invocation_for(row.clone(), context, &cell)
27416        };
27417        let skid = |index: &str| {
27418            let mut attempt = attempt_from_script(
27419                "ptrace",
27420                &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
27421                Some(&skid_report(2)),
27422            );
27423            attempt.index = index.into();
27424            attempt
27425        };
27426        let has = |row: &CellResult, token: &str| row.argv.iter().any(|arg| arg == token);
27427        let has_pair = |row: &CellResult, flag: &str, value: &str| {
27428            row.argv
27429                .windows(2)
27430                .any(|pair| pair[0] == flag && pair[1] == value)
27431        };
27432
27433        // Every shape the executor writes.
27434        let base = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid("1")]);
27435        assert!(has(&base, "--verify-strict") && has_pair(&base, "--backend", "ptrace"));
27436        accepted_skid("the fixture row", &base, 2);
27437        // Runs record their CPU profile (`cpu_profile_record`): the flag sits
27438        // right after `run`, and a row written before it carries none.
27439        assert!(has(&base, crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG));
27440        accepted_skid(
27441            "a row written before runs recorded their CPU profile",
27442            &with_argv(
27443                &base,
27444                without(crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG, 0),
27445            ),
27446            2,
27447        );
27448        let unprobed = rendered(
27449            &base,
27450            &context(&|context| context.run_verify_strict = false),
27451            &|_| {},
27452        );
27453        assert!(!has(&unprobed, "--verify-strict"));
27454        accepted_skid(
27455            "a row from a Hermit without the canonical comparison flag",
27456            &unprobed,
27457            2,
27458        );
27459        let kept = rendered(
27460            &base,
27461            &context(&|context| context.keep_logs = true),
27462            &|_| {},
27463        );
27464        assert!(has(&kept, "--verify-log-dir"));
27465        accepted_skid("a row whose verify logs were kept", &kept, 2);
27466        // The pair under `hermit verify-inputs`, sharing one sealed copy of
27467        // the host's /etc/ld.so.cache (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4693).
27468        let shared = rendered(
27469            &base,
27470            &context(&|context| context.shares_ld_so_cache = true),
27471            &|_| {},
27472        );
27473        assert_eq!(
27474            shared.argv[1..=SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()],
27475            SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.map(String::from),
27476            "{:?}",
27477            shared.argv
27478        );
27479        assert_eq!(
27480            shared.argv[0],
27481            shared.argv[at(&shared.argv, "log-diff") - 1]
27482        );
27483        assert_eq!(
27484            shared.argv[at(&shared.argv, VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER) + 1],
27485            SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG
27486        );
27487        accepted_skid("a row whose pair shares the host's ld.so.cache", &shared, 2);
27488        refused(
27489            "a shared-input holder whose run does not adopt the inputs",
27490            &with_argv(&shared, |argv| {
27491                let index = at(argv, SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG);
27492                argv.remove(index);
27493            }),
27494            "lacks `--native-exec-shared-inputs=9`",
27495        );
27496        refused(
27497            "a run that adopts shared inputs no holder sealed",
27498            &with_argv(&base, |argv| {
27499                let index = at(argv, VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER) + 1;
27500                argv.insert(index, SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG.to_owned());
27501            }),
27502            "without the `hermit verify-inputs` holder",
27503        );
27504        refused(
27505            "a holder that is not the run's Hermit",
27506            &with_argv(&shared, |argv| argv[0] = "/elsewhere/hermit".to_owned()),
27507            "seals its shared inputs with a Hermit other than the run's",
27508        );
27509        let test = cell_recorded_by(&base).id.test;
27510        let parity = rendered(
27511            &base,
27512            &context(&|context| {
27513                context
27514                    .parity_retained
27515                    .insert((test.clone(), "ptrace".into()));
27516            }),
27517            &|_| {},
27518        );
27519        assert!(has(&parity, "--verify-log-dir"));
27520        accepted_skid("a row whose logs the parity post-pass kept", &parity, 2);
27521        // The parity golden's profile (`names_parity_golden_profile`): a
27522        // reference kept with no candidate planned keeps auto; one planned
27523        // beside a candidate names x86-64-v2 right after the manifest flag,
27524        // and only there, only on the reference, and only in a run that
27525        // virtualizes CPUID.
27526        assert!(!has(&parity, PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG));
27527        let compared = rendered(
27528            &base,
27529            &context(&|context| {
27530                context.parity_retained.extend([
27531                    (test.clone(), "ptrace".into()),
27532                    (test.clone(), "kvm".into()),
27533                ]);
27534                context.parity_compared.insert(test.clone());
27535            }),
27536            &|_| {},
27537        );
27538        let after = |anchor: &str, token: &str| {
27539            let (anchor, token) = (anchor.to_owned(), token.to_owned());
27540            move |argv: &mut Vec<String>| {
27541                let index = at(argv, &anchor);
27542                argv.insert(index + 1, token.clone());
27543            }
27544        };
27545        assert_eq!(
27546            compared.argv[at(
27547                &compared.argv,
27548                crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG
27549            ) + 1],
27550            PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG
27551        );
27552        accepted_skid("a parity golden naming its CPU profile", &compared, 2);
27553        // The token stands only on its anchor. Without the manifest flag the
27554        // row is no command line the executor writes; with neither flag it is
27555        // a row written before runs recorded their CPU profile, as above.
27556        refused(
27557            "a parity golden naming its profile without the manifest flag",
27558            &with_argv(
27559                &compared,
27560                without(crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG, 0),
27561            ),
27562            "without `--manifest=always` right before it",
27563        );
27564        accepted_skid(
27565            "a kept golden written before runs recorded their CPU profile",
27566            &with_argv(&compared, |argv| {
27567                without(crate::cpu_profile_record::MANIFEST_ALWAYS_ARG, 0)(argv);
27568                without(PARITY_GOLDEN_PROFILE_ARG, 0)(argv);
27569            }),
27570            2,
27571        );
27572        // Out of its place it is refused: the checks read the executor's
27573        // order, so the token stands where the next one belongs.
27574        refused(

28147            "carries `--no-sequentialize-threads` where the executor writes nothing",
28148        );
28149        // The guest and the rendered shell command.
28150        refused(
28151            "a command line without the guest separator",
28152            &with_argv(&base, without("--", 0)),
28153            "has no `--` before the guest command",
28154        );
28155        refused(
28156            "a command line that runs another guest",
28157            &with_argv(&base, |argv| argv.push("--extra".into())),
28158            "does not end with the attempt's guest argv",
28159        );
28160        let edited = |edit: &dyn Fn(&mut CellResult)| {
28161            let mut row = base.clone();
28162            edit(&mut row);
28163            row
28164        };
28165        refused(
28166            "a guest argv the command line does not run",
28167            &edited(&|row| {
28168                row.attempts[0].guest_argv.push("--extra".into());
28169                row.guest_argv = row.attempts[0].guest_argv.clone();
28170            }),
28171            "does not end with the attempt's guest argv",
28172        );
28173        refused(
28174            "a stale shell command",
28175            &edited(&|row| {
28176                row.attempts[0].shell_command.push_str(" --extra");
28177                row.shell_command = row.attempts[0].shell_command.clone();
28178            }),
28179            "shell command is not the one rendered",
28180        );
28181        refused(
28182            "an attempt environment its shell command does not render",
28183            &edited(&|row| {
28184                row.attempts[0].env.insert("FIXTURE".into(), "1".into());
28185                row.env = row.attempts[0].env.clone();
28186            }),
28187            "shell command is not the one rendered",
28188        );
28189        // The row's copies of its first attempt.
28190        let copies = "is not its first inner attempt's";
28191        refused(
28192            "a row argv of its own",
28193            &edited(&|row| row.argv.push("--extra".into())),
28194            copies,
28195        );
28196        refused(
28197            "a row guest argv of its own",
28198            &edited(&|row| row.guest_argv.push("--extra".into())),
28199            copies,
28200        );
28201        refused(
28202            "a row environment of its own",
28203            &edited(&|row| {
28204                row.env.insert("FIXTURE".into(), "1".into());
28205            }),
28206            copies,
28207        );
28208        refused(
28209            "a row cwd of its own",
28210            &edited(&|row| row.cwd.push_str("/elsewhere")),
28211            copies,
28212        );
28213        refused(
28214            "a row shell command of its own",
28215            &edited(&|row| row.shell_command.push_str(" --extra")),
28216            copies,
28217        );
28218        let recorded = "effective args or log level";
28219        refused(
28220            "effective args that are not the argv",
28221            &edited(&|row| {
28222                row.effective_args.pop();
28223            }),
28224            recorded,
28225        );
28226        refused(
28227            "a debug log level",
28228            &edited(&|row| row.log_level = Some("debug".into())),
28229            recorded,
28230        );
28231        refused(
28232            "no log level",
28233            &edited(&|row| row.log_level = None),
28234            recorded,
28235        );
28236        refused(
28237            "a row without inner attempts",
28238            &edited(&|row| row.attempts.clear()),
28239            "retains no inner attempt",
28240        );
28241
28242        // A retained PASS is refused by the same check.
28243        let none = DeclaredStdout::default();
28244        let (plain, _) = expected_exit_row(None, canonical_verification_report(), "exit 0");
28245        assert!(has_pair(&plain, "--backend", "ptrace"));
28246        accepted("a verify PASS the executor wrote", &plain);
28247        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&plain, &none), None);
28248        for (label, row) in [
28249            (
28250                "a ptrace PASS whose command line selects liteinst",
28251                with_argv(&plain, replace_after("--backend", "liteinst")),
28252            ),
28253            (
28254                "a PASS that selects a second backend",
28255                with_argv(&plain, insert_before("--", &["--backend=liteinst"])),
28256            ),
28257            (
28258                "a PASS with a run flag its row does not record",
28259                with_argv(&plain, insert_before("--verify-run", &["--no-rcb-time"])),
28260            ),
28261        ] {
28262            let error = retained_verify_pass_error(&row, &none)
28263                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label} was re-decided as a verify PASS"));
28264            assert!(
28265                error.contains("not a verify invocation the executor writes"),
28266                "{label} was refused by another check: {error}"
28267            );
28268        }
28269        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
28270    }
28271
28272    /// The verify row `run_cell_inner` publishes for `attempts`: the same
28273    /// outcome, reason and error-kind fold, then the same typed result and
28274    /// failure class, the same declared-stdout record for a cell that
28275    /// declares no stdout assertion, the same runtime and divergence
28276    /// position copied from the attempts, and the command fields the executor
28277    /// writes ([`with_executor_invocation`]).
28278    fn verify_row_from_attempts(attempts: Vec<AttemptResult>) -> CellResult {
28279        let outcome = if attempts.iter().all(|attempt| attempt.outcome == "PASS") {
28280            "PASS"
28281        } else if attempts.iter().any(|attempt| attempt.outcome == "ERROR") {
28282            "ERROR"
28283        } else {
28284            "FAIL"
28285        }
28286        .to_string();
28287        let reason = attempts.iter().find_map(|attempt| attempt.reason.clone());
28288        let error_kind = attempts
28289            .iter()
28290            .find_map(|attempt| attempt.error_kind.clone());
28291        let result = observed_result("verify", &outcome, &attempts, error_kind.as_deref());
28292        let failure_class = failure_class(&outcome, result, error_kind.as_deref());
28293        let declared_stdout = attempts
28294            .iter()
28295            .any(attempt_has_infrastructure_report)
28296            .then(DeclaredStdout::default);
28297        let runtime = attempts.iter().find_map(|attempt| attempt.runtime.clone());
28298        let position = cell_divergence_position(&attempts);
28299        with_executor_invocation(CellResult {
28300            outcome,
28301            result,
28302            failure_class,
28303            error_kind,
28304            reason,
28305            runtime,
28306            first_divergent_scheduler_turn: position.scheduler_turn,
28307            first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds: position.virtual_nanoseconds,
28308            first_divergent_record: position.record,
28309            first_divergent_syscall: position.syscall,
28310            first_divergent_left_message: position.left_message,
28311            first_divergent_right_message: position.right_message,
28312            attempts,
28313            declared_stdout,
28314            ..cell_result_that_located_nothing()
28315        })
28316    }
28317
28318    /// The stderr Hermit writes when it refuses a verify comparison after two
28319    /// overshoot reports, copied from the failed validate attempt in
28320    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>.
28321    const SKID_STDERR: &str = "printf '%s\\n' \
28322        'HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT rcb_actual=39951476 rcb_target=39950647 skid_margin=1000 overshoot=829' \
28323        'HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL class=policy-refusal cause=skid-overshoot count=2' \
28324        'Error: observed 2 HERMIT_SKID_OVERSHOOT report(s); refusing the result' >&2";
28325
28326    /// Hermit's skid report after a completed comparison of two runs that
28327    /// both exited 0, the shape every observed overshoot had.
28328    fn skid_report_value(count: u64) -> VerificationReport {
28329        let mut report = parity_fixture_verification(Verdict::Matched);
28330        report.verified = false;
28331        report.bitwise_parity = false;
28332        report.verdict = Verdict::InfrastructureError;
28333        report.infrastructure_error = Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count });
28334        report
28335    }
28336
28337    fn skid_report(count: u64) -> String {
28338        serde_json::to_string(&skid_report_value(count)).unwrap()
28339    }
28340
28341    /// The report Hermit's `write_skid_overshoot_without_comparison_json`
28342    /// writes: no comparison, and the guest disposition it was handed (run 1's
28343    /// status, or none when the run returned only an error).
28344    fn skid_report_without_comparison(
28345        count: u64,
28346        guest_exit_code: Option<i32>,
28347        guest_signal: Option<i32>,
28348    ) -> String {
28349        let mut report = VerificationReport::no_result();
28350        report.verdict = Verdict::InfrastructureError;
28351        report.no_result_reason = None;
28352        report.infrastructure_error = Some(InfrastructureError::SkidOvershoot { count });
28353        report.guest_exit_code = guest_exit_code;
28354        report.guest_signal = guest_signal;
28355        let json = serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap();
28356        current_verification_report(json.as_bytes()).unwrap();
28357        json
28358    }

28360    /// Hermit's report of a divergence that a host file replaced during run
28361    /// 1 explains (`detcore_model::host_input`).
28362    fn host_input_change_report_value() -> VerificationReport {
28363        let identity = |ino| detcore_model::host_input::HostFileIdentity {
28364            dev: 33,
28365            ino,
28366            size: 100,
28367            mtime_sec: 1_700_000_000,
28368            mtime_nsec: 0,
28369            content: None,
28370        };
28371        let mut report = parity_fixture_verification(Verdict::Diverged);
28372        report.verdict = Verdict::InfrastructureError;
28373        report.infrastructure_error = Some(InfrastructureError::HostInputChanged {
28374            run: crate::canonical_verdict::VerificationRun::Run1,
28375            path: "/etc/ld.so.cache".into(),
28376            before: identity(57_899_095),
28377            after: identity(57_907_831),
28378        });
28379        report
28380    }
28381
28382    /// A divergence Hermit attributes to a host file changing during a run is
28383    /// an infrastructure ERROR, not a product failure, and is the one row the
28384    /// host-input retry accepts. A plain divergence stays a product FAIL, and
28385    /// a row whose reason, report or SaBRe path evidence does not match its
28386    /// own evidence does not qualify.
28387    #[test]
28388    fn only_a_typed_host_input_change_is_a_host_input_row() {
28389        let change_report = serde_json::to_string(&host_input_change_report_value()).unwrap();
28390        current_verification_report(change_report.as_bytes()).unwrap();
28391        let changed = || {
28392            attempt_from_script(
28393                "ptrace",
28394                "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 1",
28395                Some(&change_report),
28396            )
28397        };
28398        let row = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![changed()]);
28399        assert_eq!(row.outcome, "ERROR", "{row:?}");
28400        assert_eq!(row.error_kind.as_deref(), Some("infrastructure"));
28401        assert_eq!(
28402            row.failure_class,
28403            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
28404        );
28405        let change = host_input_change_report_value()
28406            .infrastructure_error
28407            .unwrap();
28408        assert_eq!(
28409            row.reason.as_deref(),
28410            Some(host_input_changed_reason(&change).as_str())
28411        );
28412        assert!(
28413            row.reason.as_deref().unwrap().contains(
28414                "host input changed during run 1: /etc/ld.so.cache (dev:ino 0:33:57899095"
28415            ),
28416            "{row:?}"
28417        );
28418        assert!(host_input_change_only(&row));
28419        assert_eq!(skid_overshoot_only_reports(&row), None);
28420
28421        // A plain divergence is a product failure, never a host input change.
28422        let diverged_report =
28423            serde_json::to_string(&parity_fixture_verification(Verdict::Diverged)).unwrap();
28424        let diverged = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![attempt_from_script(
28425            "ptrace",
28426            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 1",
28427            Some(&diverged_report),
28428        )]);
28429        assert_eq!(diverged.outcome, "FAIL", "{diverged:?}");
28430        assert_eq!(diverged.failure_class, Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure));
28431        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&diverged));
28432
28433        // A reason the report does not produce is not evidence.
28434        let mut relabelled = row.clone();
28435        relabelled.attempts[0].reason = Some("host input changed during run 1".into());
28436        relabelled.reason = relabelled.attempts[0].reason.clone();
28437        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&relabelled));
28438
28439        // Nor is a report whose bytes are not the ones the runner hashed.
28440        let mut swapped = row.clone();
28441        swapped.attempts[0].verification_report = Some(diverged_report);
28442        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&swapped));
28443
28444        // A timed-out attempt is not one.
28445        let mut timed_out = row.clone();
28446        timed_out.attempts[0].timed_out = true;
28447        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&timed_out));
28448
28449        // The skid report is not a host input change.
28450        let skid = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![attempt_from_script(
28451            "ptrace",
28452            &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
28453            Some(&skid_report(2)),
28454        )]);
28455        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&skid));
28456
28457        // SaBRe path evidence. The executor summarizes a row's retained
28458        // evidence into its execution path whatever the row's outcome, makes a
28459        // row whose evidence does not summarize an invalid-backend-evidence
28460        // ERROR, and judges the path's eligibility only on a PASS. So a
28461        // genuine SaBRe host-input row qualifies, with a clean or a fallback
28462        // path, and one whose evidence does not summarize, is not the bytes
28463        // its digest names, or is not the row's recorded path does not.
28464        const CLEAN_PATH: &str = r#"{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":0,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}"#;
28465        const FALLBACK_PATH: &str = r#"{"schema":1,"guest_rpc_observed":true,"ptrace_fallback_sites":1,"trusted_shared_object_sites":0,"trusted_shared_objects":[]}"#;
28466        let clean_evidence = format!("{CLEAN_PATH}\n{CLEAN_PATH}\n");
28467        let fallback_evidence = format!("{CLEAN_PATH}\n{FALLBACK_PATH}\n");
28468        let mut sabre = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![attempt_from_script(
28469            "sabre",
28470            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 1",
28471            Some(&change_report),
28472        )]);
28473        sabre.backend = Some("sabre".into());
28474        let sabre = with_executor_invocation(sabre);
28475        let with_sabre_evidence = |evidence: &str| {
28476            let mut row = sabre.clone();
28477            for attempt in &mut row.attempts {
28478                attempt.sabre_path_evidence = Some(evidence.to_owned());
28479                attempt.sabre_path_evidence_sha256 = Some(hex_digest(evidence.as_bytes()));
28480            }
28481            row.execution_path = summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&row.attempts).unwrap_or(None);
28482            row
28483        };
28484        let genuine = with_sabre_evidence(&clean_evidence);
28485        assert_eq!(genuine.execution_path.as_ref().unwrap()["eligible"], true);
28486        assert!(host_input_change_only(&genuine), "{genuine:?}");
28487        let fallback = with_sabre_evidence(&fallback_evidence);
28488        assert_eq!(fallback.execution_path.as_ref().unwrap()["eligible"], false);
28489        assert!(host_input_change_only(&fallback), "{fallback:?}");
28490        // Evidence without the record schema, under its own digest.
28491        let malformed = with_sabre_evidence("{}\n");
28492        assert!(summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&malformed.attempts).is_err());
28493        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&malformed));
28494        let mut misdigested = genuine.clone();
28495        misdigested.attempts[0].sabre_path_evidence_sha256 =
28496            Some(hex_digest(fallback_evidence.as_bytes()));
28497        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&misdigested));
28498        let mut mislabelled = genuine.clone();
28499        mislabelled.execution_path = fallback.execution_path.clone();
28500        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&mislabelled));
28501        // A guest argument is not a backend selection: a ptrace row whose
28502        // guest takes `--backend sabre`, on the command line the executor
28503        // writes, has no SaBRe path and qualifies.
28504        let mut guest_args = row.clone();
28505        guest_args.attempts[0].guest_argv =
28506            ["fixture", "--backend", "sabre"].map(String::from).into();
28507        let mut guest_args = with_executor_invocation(guest_args);
28508        let argv = &guest_args.attempts[0].argv;
28509        let separator = argv.iter().position(|arg| arg == "--").unwrap();
28510        let log = argv.iter().position(|arg| arg == "--log").unwrap();
28511        assert_eq!(argv[log..log + 4], ["--log", "info", "--backend", "ptrace"]);
28512        assert_eq!(argv[separator + 1..], ["fixture", "--backend", "sabre"]);
28513        guest_args.execution_path = summarize_sabre_path_evidence(&guest_args.attempts).unwrap();
28514        assert_eq!(guest_args.execution_path, None);
28515        assert!(host_input_change_only(&guest_args), "{guest_args:?}");
28516    }

28518    /// A host-input attempt whose compared runs break the cell's declared
28519    /// stdout assertion is not a host-input row: the host change explains the
28520    /// divergence, not a wrong output. It keeps the infrastructure ERROR with
28521    /// a reason naming both, and the predicate refuses it even relabelled with
28522    /// the plain host-input reason, because it re-decides the row's recorded
28523    /// assertion from the attempt's own report. The same attempt with the
28524    /// assertion met is one.
28525    #[test]
28526    fn a_host_input_attempt_that_breaks_a_declared_stdout_assertion_is_not_host_input_only() {
28527        let golden = "sar-ok\n";
28528        let wrong = "sar-bad\n";
28529        let change_with = |first: &str, second: &str| {
28530            let mut report = host_input_change_report_value();
28531            let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
28532            outputs.left.stdout_sha256 = hex_digest(first.as_bytes());
28533            outputs.left.stdout_bytes = first.len() as u64;
28534            outputs.right.stdout_sha256 = hex_digest(second.as_bytes());
28535            outputs.right.stdout_bytes = second.len() as u64;
28536            report
28537        };
28538        let change = host_input_change_report_value()
28539            .infrastructure_error
28540            .unwrap();
28541        let plain = host_input_changed_reason(&change);
28542        let declaring = |mut row: CellResult| {
28543            row.declared_stdout = Some(DeclaredStdout {
28544                exact: Some(golden.to_string()),
28545                contains: None,
28546                stderr_exact: None,
28547            });
28548            row
28549        };
28550
28551        let met = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
28552            Some(golden),
28553            None,
28554            change_with(golden, golden),
28555            golden,
28556            "exit 1",
28557        );
28558        assert_eq!(met.reason.as_deref(), Some(plain.as_str()), "{met:?}");
28559        let met_row = declaring(verify_row_from_attempts(vec![met]));
28560        assert!(host_input_change_only(&met_row));
28561
28562        // The same retained attempt answers to the declared stderr too:
28563        // both compared runs print the declared diagnostic, while another
28564        // declared diagnostic refuses the row.
28565        let diag = "sar-diag\n";
28566        let change_with_stderr = |stderr: &str| {
28567            let mut report = change_with(golden, golden);
28568            let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
28569            for output in [&mut outputs.left, &mut outputs.right] {
28570                output.stderr_sha256 = hex_digest(stderr.as_bytes());
28571                output.stderr_bytes = stderr.len() as u64;
28572            }
28573            report
28574        };
28575        let stderr_attempt = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
28576            Some(golden),
28577            None,
28578            change_with_stderr(diag),
28579            golden,
28580            "exit 1",
28581        );
28582        assert_eq!(
28583            stderr_attempt.reason.as_deref(),
28584            Some(plain.as_str()),
28585            "{stderr_attempt:?}"
28586        );
28587        let mut stderr_met_row = declaring(verify_row_from_attempts(vec![stderr_attempt.clone()]));
28588        stderr_met_row
28589            .declared_stdout
28590            .as_mut()
28591            .unwrap()
28592            .stderr_exact = Some(diag.to_string());
28593        assert!(host_input_change_only(&stderr_met_row));
28594        let mut stderr_wrong_row = declaring(verify_row_from_attempts(vec![stderr_attempt]));
28595        stderr_wrong_row
28596            .declared_stdout
28597            .as_mut()
28598            .unwrap()
28599            .stderr_exact = Some("sar-other-diag\n".to_string());
28600        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&stderr_wrong_row));
28601
28602        // A row without the recorded declaration never qualifies.
28603        let mut undeclared = met_row;
28604        undeclared.declared_stdout = None;
28605        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&undeclared));
28606
28607        let broken = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
28608            Some(golden),
28609            None,
28610            change_with(golden, wrong),
28611            golden,
28612            "exit 1",
28613        );
28614        assert_eq!(
28615            (broken.outcome.as_str(), broken.error_kind.as_deref()),
28616            ("ERROR", Some("infrastructure")),
28617            "{broken:?}"
28618        );
28619        assert!(
28620            broken
28621                .reason
28622                .as_deref()
28623                .is_some_and(|reason| reason.starts_with(&format!(
28624                    "{plain}, and its compared runs violate a declared stdout assertion: "
28625                ))),
28626            "{broken:?}"
28627        );
28628        let row = declaring(verify_row_from_attempts(vec![broken]));
28629        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&row), "{row:?}");
28630        let mut relabelled = row;
28631        relabelled.reason = Some(plain.clone());
28632        relabelled.attempts[0].reason = Some(plain);
28633        assert!(!host_input_change_only(&relabelled));
28634    }
28635
28636    /// Only a verify row whose every attempt is Hermit's typed overshoot
28637    /// refusal, with its exit status and both stderr markers, is skid-only
28638    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>). Each other row here
28639    /// differs from the qualifying one in one respect and must not qualify.
28640    #[test]
28641    fn only_a_typed_skid_overshoot_and_nothing_else_is_a_skid_only_row() {
28642        let skid = || {
28643            attempt_from_script(
28644                "ptrace",
28645                &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
28646                Some(&skid_report(2)),
28647            )
28648        };
28649        let qualifying = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid()]);
28650        assert_eq!(qualifying.outcome, "ERROR");
28651        assert_eq!(qualifying.result, None);
28652        assert_eq!(
28653            qualifying.failure_class,
28654            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure)
28655        );
28656        assert_eq!(skid_overshoot_only_reports(&qualifying), Some(2));
28657        assert_eq!(
28658            qualifying.declared_stdout,
28659            Some(DeclaredStdout::default()),
28660            "a row with an infrastructure report records its declared stdout"
28661        );
28662
28663        // A row without the declared-stdout record, as an older producer
28664        // wrote it, cannot have its stdout assertions re-decided and so never
28665        // qualifies, however its attempts are labelled.
28666        let mut legacy = qualifying.clone();
28667        legacy.declared_stdout = None;
28668        assert_eq!(skid_overshoot_only_reports(&legacy), None);
28669
28670        // Every inner attempt must be a skid attempt, and their counts add.
28671        let mut second = skid();
28672        second.index = "2".into();

29154        refused.no_result_reason = Some(

29156                detail: REFUSAL_DETAIL.into(),
29157            },
29158        );
29159        let refused = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid_with_stderr(
29160            &[
29161                OVERSHOOT_LINE,
29162                "REFUSING to compare: both logs were truncated at the configured size bound. This is a NO-RESULT, not a difference and not a match.",
29163                REFUSAL_LINE,
29164            ],
29165            &serde_json::to_string(&refused).unwrap(),
29166            122,
29167        )]);
29168        assert_eq!(
29169            (
29170                refused.outcome.as_str(),
29171                refused.error_kind.as_deref(),
29172                refused.reason.as_deref(),
29173            ),
29174            (
29175                "ERROR",
29176                Some("incomplete-verification-evidence"),
29177                Some(REFUSAL_DETAIL),
29178            ),
29179            "an overshoot whose comparison was refused keeps the refusal: {refused:?}"
29180        );
29181        assert_ne!(
29182            refused.failure_class,
29183            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure),
29184            "{refused:?}"
29185        );
29186        not_skid_only("an overshoot whose comparison was refused", &refused);
29187        // The same refusal without the banner line is still not a skid row:
29188        // the report, not the stderr scan, refuses it.
29189        let mut refused_report = VerificationReport::no_result();
29190        refused_report.no_result_reason = Some(
29191            crate::canonical_verdict::NoResultReason::ComparisonRefused {
29192                detail: REFUSAL_DETAIL.into(),
29193            },
29194        );
29195        let unbannered = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid_with_stderr(
29196            &[OVERSHOOT_LINE, REFUSAL_LINE],
29197            &serde_json::to_string(&refused_report).unwrap(),
29198            122,
29199        )]);
29200        assert_eq!(unbannered.outcome, "ERROR", "{unbannered:?}");
29201        assert_eq!(
29202            unbannered.error_kind.as_deref(),
29203            Some("incomplete-verification-evidence"),
29204            "{unbannered:?}"
29205        );
29206        not_skid_only("a refused comparison report with skid markers", &unbannered);
29207        // The markers and the typed report, but not Hermit's refusal status.
29208        let wrong_status = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid_with_stderr(
29209            &[OVERSHOOT_LINE, REFUSAL_LINE],
29210            &skid_report(2),
29211            1,
29212        )]);
29213        classified_as_skid("a skid report with a non-refusal exit", &wrong_status);
29214        not_skid_only("a skid report with a non-refusal exit", &wrong_status);
29215        // The stderr refusal line names a different count than the report.
29216        let miscounted = attempt_from_script(
29217            "ptrace",
29218            &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
29219            Some(&skid_report(3)),
29220        );
29221        not_skid_only(
29222            "a refusal line whose count differs from the report",
29223            &verify_row_from_attempts(vec![miscounted]),
29224        );
29225        // The stderr markers with a no-result report.
29226        let no_result = attempt_from_script(
29227            "ptrace",
29228            &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
29229            Some(&serde_json::to_string(&VerificationReport::no_result()).unwrap()),
29230        );
29231        not_skid_only(
29232            "stderr markers with a no_result report",
29233            &verify_row_from_attempts(vec![no_result]),
29234        );
29235        // The stderr markers with a diverged report.
29236        let mut diverged = canonical_verification_report();
29237        diverged.verified = false;
29238        diverged.bitwise_parity = false;
29239        diverged.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
29240        diverged.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = Some(4);
29241        diverged.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = Some(7);
29242        diverged.first_divergent_record = Some(9);
29243        diverged.first_divergent_syscall = Some(2);
29244        diverged.first_divergent_left_message = Some("left".into());
29245        diverged.first_divergent_right_message = Some("right".into());
29246        let diverged = attempt_from_script(
29247            "ptrace",
29248            &format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {SKID_STDERR}; exit 1"),
29249            Some(&serde_json::to_string(&diverged).unwrap()),
29250        );
29251        let diverged = verify_row_from_attempts(vec![diverged]);
29252        assert_eq!(diverged.outcome, "FAIL", "{diverged:?}");
29253        not_skid_only("stderr markers with a diverged report", &diverged);
29254        // Hermit's reports for an overshoot beside a second failure, in the
29255        // shapes its writers produce, each with both markers and exit 122.
29256        // Every one reaches the predicate as a typed skid row, so only the
29257        // completed-comparison and guest-disposition guard refuses it.
29258        let marked = |report: &str| {
29259            verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid_with_stderr(
29260                &[OVERSHOOT_LINE, REFUSAL_LINE],
29261                report,
29262                122,
29263            )])
29264        };
29265        for (label, report) in [
29266            // Run 1 exited 1, which the verify policy rejects: no run 2.
29267            (
29268                "an overshoot after run 1 exited with a rejected code",
29269                skid_report_without_comparison(2, Some(1), None),
29270            ),
29271            // Run 1 died from SIGSEGV: the rejected disposition is a signal.
29272            (
29273                "an overshoot after run 1 died from a signal",
29274                skid_report_without_comparison(2, None, Some(11)),
29275            ),
29276            // Run 1 failed for another reason and returned only an error.
29277            (
29278                "an overshoot attached to a failed run 1",
29279                skid_report_without_comparison(2, None, None),
29280            ),
29281            // Run 2 failed for another reason; the report keeps run 1's
29282            // accepted status but has no comparison.
29283            (
29284                "an overshoot attached to a failed run 2",
29285                skid_report_without_comparison(2, Some(0), None),
29286            ),
29287        ] {
29288            let row = marked(&report);
29289            classified_as_skid(label, &row);
29290            not_skid_only(label, &row);
29291        }
29292        // Both runs were compared, but run 2 died from SIGSEGV.
29293        let mut crashed = skid_report_value(2);
29294        let outputs = crashed.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
29295        outputs.right.exit_code = None;
29296        outputs.right.signal = Some(11);
29297        let crashed = marked(&serde_json::to_string(&crashed).unwrap());
29298        classified_as_skid("a compared run 2 that died from a signal", &crashed);
29299        not_skid_only("a compared run 2 that died from a signal", &crashed);
29300        // Two shapes Hermit's writers do not produce, so each remaining
29301        // guard is exercised alone: compared outputs without the comparison
29302        // they came from, and a guest disposition that contradicts them.
29303        let mut uncompared = skid_report_value(2);
29304        uncompared.comparison = None;
29305        uncompared.compared_log_messages = None;
29306        let uncompared = marked(&serde_json::to_string(&uncompared).unwrap());
29307        classified_as_skid("compared outputs without a comparison", &uncompared);
29308        not_skid_only("compared outputs without a comparison", &uncompared);
29309        let mut contradicted = skid_report_value(2);
29310        contradicted.guest_exit_code = None;
29311        contradicted.guest_signal = Some(11);
29312        let contradicted = marked(&serde_json::to_string(&contradicted).unwrap());
29313        classified_as_skid(
29314            "a guest signal beside clean compared outputs",
29315            &contradicted,
29316        );
29317        not_skid_only(
29318            "a guest signal beside clean compared outputs",
29319            &contradicted,
29320        );
29321        // Both runs exited 7 and were compared, in a cell that declares no
29322        // expected exit: 7 is not a disposition this cell accepts.
29323        let mut sevens = skid_report_value(2);
29324        sevens.guest_exit_code = Some(7);
29325        let outputs = sevens.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
29326        outputs.left.exit_code = Some(7);
29327        outputs.right.exit_code = Some(7);
29328        let sevens = serde_json::to_string(&sevens).unwrap();
29329        let undeclared = marked(&sevens);
29330        classified_as_skid("a compared exit 7 the cell does not declare", &undeclared);
29331        not_skid_only("a compared exit 7 the cell does not declare", &undeclared);
29332        // The same report in a cell that declares exit 7 is skid-only, and
29333        // the clean-exit report is not. Each row carries the command line the
29334        // executor writes for its declaration, so only the disposition can
29335        // refuse it.
29336        let mut declared = marked(&sevens);
29337        declared.expected_guest_exit = Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None));
29338        let declared = with_executor_invocation(declared);
29339        classified_as_skid("a compared exit 7 the cell declares", &declared);
29340        assert_eq!(
29341            skid_overshoot_only_reports(&declared),
29342            Some(2),
29343            "{declared:?}"
29344        );
29345        let mut clean_in_declared = qualifying.clone();
29346        clean_in_declared.expected_guest_exit = Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None));
29347        let clean_in_declared = with_executor_invocation(clean_in_declared);
29348        assert_eq!(retained_verify_invocation_error(&clean_in_declared), None);
29349        not_skid_only(
29350            "a compared exit 0 in a cell that declares exit 7",
29351            &clean_in_declared,
29352        );
29353
29354        // A skid attempt next to a passing one is a mixed history.
29355        let mut passed = skid();
29356        passed.outcome = "PASS".into();
29357        passed.error_kind = None;
29358        passed.reason = None;
29359        passed.index = "2".into();
29360        not_skid_only(
29361            "a skid attempt next to a passing attempt",
29362            &verify_row_from_attempts(vec![skid(), passed]),
29363        );
29364
29365        let mut timed_out = qualifying.clone();
29366        timed_out.attempts[0].timed_out = true;
29367        not_skid_only("a timed-out attempt", &timed_out);
29368        let mut signaled = qualifying.clone();
29369        signaled.attempts[0].signal = Some(9);
29370        not_skid_only("a signaled attempt", &signaled);
29371        let mut binary_changed = qualifying.clone();
29372        binary_changed.reason = Some("Hermit binary changed while the cell was executing".into());
29373        not_skid_only("a cell whose Hermit binary changed", &binary_changed);
29374        let mut blocked = qualifying.clone();
29375        blocked.result = Some(ObservedResult::InfrastructureError);
29376        not_skid_only("a row that also carries an environmental block", &blocked);
29377        let mut replay = qualifying.clone();
29378        replay.mode = "replay".into();
29379        not_skid_only("a replay row", &replay);
29380        let mut unreadable = qualifying.clone();
29381        unreadable.attempts[0].verification_report = None;
29382        not_skid_only("an attempt with no retained report", &unreadable);
29383        // The row and its attempt both name a count other than the report's
29384        // and the refusal line's, so only the count/reason guard differs.
29385        let mut relabeled = qualifying.clone();
29386        relabeled.reason = Some(skid_overshoot_reason(1));
29387        relabeled.attempts[0].reason = Some(skid_overshoot_reason(1));
29388        not_skid_only("an attempt whose reason names another count", &relabeled);
29389        let mut no_attempts = qualifying.clone();
29390        no_attempts.attempts.clear();
29391        not_skid_only("a row with no attempts", &no_attempts);
29392        let mut product = qualifying;
29393        product.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure);
29394        not_skid_only("a product failure", &product);
29395    }

29397    /// A backend this runner could not start and a backend that ran but recorded
29398    /// no comparison must stay visible while carrying different error kinds.
29399    ///
29400    /// The old shared incomplete-verification-evidence kind turned an unstaged
29401    /// backend into an apparent product defect. Classifying every nonzero exit
29402    /// as unavailable would be the same bug with the sign flipped, so this
29403    /// bracket exercises both directions through real subprocesses.
29404    #[test]
29405    fn an_unavailable_backend_is_not_reported_as_a_silent_one() {
29406        let no_result = serde_json::to_string(&VerificationReport::no_result()).unwrap();
29407        let unavailable = attempt_from_script(
29408            "sabre",
29409            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; \
29410             printf '%s\\n' 'HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=backend-unavailable backend=sabre' \
29411             'Error: backend \x60sabre\x60 is unavailable: HERMIT_SABRE_BINARY=/nonexistent/sabre is not an executable file' >&2; exit 1",
29412            Some(&no_result),
29413        );
29414        let silent = attempt_from_script(
29415            "sabre",
29416            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; exit 0",
29417            Some(&no_result),
29418        );
29419
29420        assert_eq!(unavailable.outcome, "ERROR");
29421        assert_eq!(silent.outcome, "ERROR");
29422        assert_eq!(
29423            failure_class(
29424                &unavailable.outcome,
29425                observed_result(
29426                    "verify",
29427                    &unavailable.outcome,
29428                    std::slice::from_ref(&unavailable),
29429                    unavailable.error_kind.as_deref()
29430                ),
29431                unavailable.error_kind.as_deref()
29432            ),
29433            Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodPrerequisiteFailure)
29434        );
29435        assert_eq!(
29436            failure_class(
29437                &silent.outcome,
29438                observed_result(
29439                    "verify",
29440                    &silent.outcome,
29441                    std::slice::from_ref(&silent),
29442                    silent.error_kind.as_deref()
29443                ),
29444                silent.error_kind.as_deref()
29445            ),
29446            Some(FailureClass::NoResult)
29447        );
29448        assert_eq!(
29449            unavailable.error_kind.as_deref(),
29450            Some("backend-unavailable"),
29451            "an unrunnable backend must carry its own kind: {:?}",
29452            unavailable.reason
29453        );
29454        assert_eq!(
29455            silent.error_kind.as_deref(),
29456            Some("incomplete-verification-evidence"),
29457            "a backend that ran and recorded nothing keeps the evidence kind: {:?}",
29458            silent.reason
29459        );
29460        assert_ne!(unavailable.error_kind, silent.error_kind);
29461
29462        let unavailable_reason = unavailable.reason.clone().expect("reason");
29463        let silent_reason = silent.reason.clone().expect("reason");
29464        assert!(
29465            unavailable_reason.contains("backend unavailable on this runner")
29466                && unavailable_reason.contains("sabre"),
29467            "unavailable reason must name the backend and environment: {unavailable_reason}"
29468        );
29469        assert!(
29470            !unavailable_reason.contains("verification report is missing"),
29471            "the old wording pointed at a missing file, not the backend: {unavailable_reason}"
29472        );
29473        assert!(
29474            silent_reason.contains("no_result"),
29475            "silent reason must still name the producer state: {silent_reason}"
29476        );
29477        assert_ne!(unavailable_reason, silent_reason);
29478    }

29480    #[test]
29481    fn backend_unavailable_requires_the_requested_backend_and_empty_stdout() {
29482        let no_result = serde_json::to_string(&VerificationReport::no_result()).unwrap();
29483        let wrong_backend = attempt_from_script(
29484            "sabre",
29485            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; \
29486             printf '%s\\n' 'HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=backend-unavailable backend=dbt' \
29487             'Error: backend \x60dbt\x60 is unavailable: no SDK' >&2; exit 7",
29488            Some(&no_result),
29489        );
29490        let guest_output = attempt_from_script(
29491            "sabre",
29492            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; printf 'guest-started\\n'; \
29493             printf '%s\\n' 'HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=backend-unavailable backend=sabre' \
29494             'Error: backend \x60sabre\x60 is unavailable: spoofed' >&2; exit 8",
29495            Some(&no_result),
29496        );
29497
29498        for result in [wrong_backend, guest_output] {
29499            assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR", "unexpected result: {result:?}");
29500            assert_eq!(
29501                observed_result(
29502                    "verify",
29503                    &result.outcome,
29504                    std::slice::from_ref(&result),
29505                    result.error_kind.as_deref()
29506                ),
29507                None,
29508                "mismatched producer evidence must not manufacture a product result: {result:?}"
29509            );
29510            assert_eq!(
29511                failure_class(&result.outcome, None, result.error_kind.as_deref()),
29512                Some(FailureClass::NoResult),
29513                "mismatched producer evidence must remain no-result: {result:?}"
29514            );
29515            assert_eq!(
29516                result.error_kind.as_deref(),
29517                Some("invalid-backend-evidence"),
29518                "unexpected result: {result:?}"
29519            );
29520            assert!(
29521                result
29522                    .reason
29523                    .as_deref()
29524                    .is_some_and(|reason| reason.contains("does not match this attempt")),
29525                "mismatched producer evidence must name the mismatch: {result:?}"
29526            );
29527        }
29528
29529        let mut unspecified = VerificationReport::no_result();
29530        unspecified.no_result_reason = None;
29531        let unspecified = serde_json::to_string(&unspecified).unwrap();
29532        let ordinary_failure = attempt_from_script(
29533            "sabre",
29534            "printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; printf 'guest-started\\n'; exit 8",
29535            Some(&unspecified),
29536        );
29537        assert_eq!(ordinary_failure.outcome, "FAIL");
29538        let observed = observed_result(
29539            "verify",
29540            &ordinary_failure.outcome,
29541            std::slice::from_ref(&ordinary_failure),
29542            ordinary_failure.error_kind.as_deref(),
29543        );
29544        assert_eq!(observed, Some(ObservedResult::CrashError));
29545        assert_eq!(
29546            failure_class(
29547                &ordinary_failure.outcome,
29548                observed,
29549                ordinary_failure.error_kind.as_deref(),
29550            ),
29551            Some(FailureClass::ProductFailure),
29552            "an ordinary process failure without contradictory producer evidence remains product-attributed"
29553        );
29554    }

29671    /// Run a fake Hermit that writes a matched canonical report carrying the
29672    /// given guest disposition, then ends with `ending` (a shell statement).
29673    fn attempt_with_expected_exit(
29674        expected: ExpectedGuestExit,
29675        guest_exit_code: Option<i32>,
29676        guest_signal: Option<i32>,
29677        ending: &str,
29678    ) -> AttemptResult {
29679        attempt_with_expected_exit_report(
29680            expected,
29681            expected_exit_report(guest_exit_code, guest_signal),
29682            ending,
29683            5,
29684        )
29685    }

29687    /// A matched canonical report carrying the given guest disposition.
29688    fn expected_exit_report(
29689        guest_exit_code: Option<i32>,
29690        guest_signal: Option<i32>,
29691    ) -> VerificationReport {
29692        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
29693        report.guest_exit_code = guest_exit_code;
29694        report.guest_signal = guest_signal;
29695        let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
29696        for output in [&mut outputs.left, &mut outputs.right] {
29697            output.exit_code = guest_exit_code;
29698            output.signal = guest_signal;
29699        }
29700        report
29701    }

29720    /// [`attempt_with_expected_exit_report`] for any declared exit and comparator.

29722        expected: Option<ExpectedGuestExit>,
29723        comparator: Comparator,
29724        report: VerificationReport,
29725        ending: &str,
29726        timeout_seconds: u64,
29727    ) -> AttemptResult {
29728        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
29729            "hermit-runner-expected-exit-{}-{:?}",

29732        ));
29733        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
29734        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
29735        let verdict = dir.join("verdict.json");
29736        let spec = CellRunSpec {
29737            command_binding: None,
29738            id: CellId {
29739                test: "fixture/expected-exit".into(),
29740                mode: "verify".into(),
29741                backend: Some("ptrace".into()),
29742            },
29743            lane: "portable".into(),
29744            category: "fixture".into(),
29745            cwd: dir.clone(),
29746            env: BTreeMap::new(),
29747            argv: vec![
29748                "/bin/sh".into(),
29749                "-c".into(),
29750                format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; {ending}"),
29751                "sh".into(),
29752                serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap(),
29753                verdict.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
29754            ],
29755            guest_argv: vec!["fixture".into()],
29756            timeout_seconds,
29757            verdict_path: Some(verdict),
29758            verification_log_dir: None,
29759            verify_runs: None,
29760            single_run_capture: None,
29761            sabre_path_evidence: None,
29762            cell_dir: dir.clone(),
29763            expected_guest_exit: expected,
29764            expected_stdout: None,
29765            expected_stdout_contains: None,
29766            expected_stderr: None,
29767            comparator,
29768            attempt: "1".into(),
29769            fixed_workdir_source: dir.join("workdir/1"),
29770        };
29771        let result = execute_spec(&spec).unwrap();
29772        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
29773        result
29774    }
