29776    #[test]
29777    fn expected_guest_exit_passes_only_the_exact_disposition() {
29778        let exact =
29779            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(Some(7), None), Some(7), None, "exit 7");
29780        assert_eq!(exact.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", exact.reason);
29781
29782        let other_code =
29783            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(Some(7), None), Some(6), None, "exit 6");
29784        assert_eq!(
29785            other_code.outcome, "FAIL",
29786            "{:?} {:?}",
29787            other_code.error_kind, other_code.reason
29788        );
29789        assert_eq!(
29790            other_code.reason.as_deref(),
29791            Some("guest ended with exit code 6, but the manifest expects exit code 7")
29792        );
29793
29794        // The report and Hermit's own status must agree; a report alone is
29795        // not enough to call the attempt a pass.
29796        let hermit_disagrees =
29797            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(Some(7), None), Some(7), None, "exit 0");
29798        assert_eq!(hermit_disagrees.outcome, "FAIL");
29799        assert_eq!(
29800            hermit_disagrees.reason.as_deref(),
29801            Some(
29802                "guest ended with exit code 7, but hermit exited with status 0, which does not report exit code 7"
29803            )
29804        );
29805
29806        // Fixtures that make the fake Hermit die by a signal use signals that
29807        // never dump core. A core-dumping signal hands the dump to the host's
29808        // core_pattern helper, which ignores RLIMIT_CORE when it is a pipe and
29809        // took from 0.5 to over 5 seconds on a loaded host, past this
29810        // fixture's 5-second backstop.
29811        let raised = attempt_with_expected_exit(
29812            expected_exit(None, Some(15)),
29813            None,
29814            Some(15),
29815            "kill -TERM $$",
29816        );
29817        assert_eq!(raised.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", raised.reason);
29818        assert_eq!(raised.signal, Some(15));
29819
29820        let shell_status =
29821            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(None, Some(11)), None, Some(11), "exit 139");
29822        assert_eq!(shell_status.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", shell_status.reason);
29823
29824        // An exit code of 139 is not a SIGSEGV death, even though Hermit's
29825        // process status is the same number.
29826        let code_not_signal =
29827            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(None, Some(11)), Some(139), None, "exit 139");
29828        assert_eq!(code_not_signal.outcome, "FAIL");
29829        assert_eq!(
29830            code_not_signal.reason.as_deref(),
29831            Some("guest ended with exit code 139, but the manifest expects signal 11")
29832        );
29833
29834        let other_signal = attempt_with_expected_exit(
29835            expected_exit(None, Some(15)),
29836            None,
29837            Some(10),
29838            "kill -USR1 $$",
29839        );
29840        assert_eq!(other_signal.outcome, "FAIL");
29841        assert_eq!(
29842            other_signal.reason.as_deref(),
29843            Some("guest ended with signal 10, but the manifest expects signal 15")
29844        );
29845
29846        // A matching signal in the report is not enough when Hermit's own
29847        // status reports a success, a different signal, or 128 plus a
29848        // different signal number.
29849        for (ending, hermit) in [
29850            ("exit 0", "exited with status 0"),
29851            ("kill -USR1 $$", "was killed by signal 10"),
29852            ("exit 138", "exited with status 138"),
29853        ] {
29854            let hermit_disagrees =
29855                attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(None, Some(15)), None, Some(15), ending);
29856            assert_eq!(hermit_disagrees.outcome, "FAIL", "{ending}");
29857            assert_eq!(
29858                hermit_disagrees.reason,
29859                Some(format!(
29860                    "guest ended with signal 15, but hermit {hermit}, which does not report signal 15"
29861                )),
29862                "{ending}"
29863            );
29864        }
29865
29866        let succeeded =
29867            attempt_with_expected_exit(expected_exit(Some(1), None), Some(0), None, "exit 0");
29868        assert_eq!(succeeded.outcome, "FAIL");
29869
29870        // A matching exit code in the report is not enough when Hermit itself
29871        // was killed by a signal.
29872        let hermit_killed = attempt_with_expected_exit(
29873            expected_exit(Some(7), None),
29874            Some(7),
29875            None,
29876            "kill -TERM $$",
29877        );
29878        assert_eq!(hermit_killed.outcome, "FAIL");
29879        assert_eq!(
29880            hermit_killed.reason.as_deref(),
29881            Some(
29882                "guest ended with exit code 7, but hermit was killed by signal 15, which does not report exit code 7"
29883            )
29884        );
29885    }

29887    /// The expected disposition is checked only after the comparison has been
29888    /// admitted as canonical and matched. Each report below carries exactly
29889    /// the expected exit and Hermit exits with it, so only the canonical
29890    /// checks stand between the attempt and a pass.
29891    #[test]
29892    fn expected_guest_exit_cannot_pass_a_diverged_or_noncanonical_comparison() {
29893        let mut diverged = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
29894        diverged.verified = false;
29895        diverged.bitwise_parity = false;
29896        diverged.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
29897        diverged.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = Some(4);
29898        diverged.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = Some(7);
29899        diverged.first_divergent_record = Some(9);
29900        diverged.first_divergent_syscall = Some(2);
29901        diverged.first_divergent_left_message = Some("left".into());
29902        diverged.first_divergent_right_message = Some("right".into());
29903        let result =
29904            attempt_with_expected_exit_report(expected_exit(Some(7), None), diverged, "exit 7", 5);
29905        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", result.reason);
29906        assert_eq!(
29907            result.reason.as_deref(),
29908            Some(
29909                "canonical verification did not match: verified=false verdict=diverged bitwise_parity=false"
29910            )
29911        );
29912
29913        let mut stripped = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
29914        stripped.comparison.as_mut().unwrap().strictness =
29915            crate::canonical_verdict::LogCompareStrictness::Stripped;
29916        let result =
29917            attempt_with_expected_exit_report(expected_exit(Some(7), None), stripped, "exit 7", 5);
29918        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR", "{:?}", result.reason);
29919        assert_eq!(
29920            result.error_kind.as_deref(),
29921            Some("incomplete-verification-evidence")
29922        );
29923        assert_eq!(
29924            result.reason.as_deref(),
29925            Some(
29926                "verification did not compare canonical non-vacuous INFO evidence: strictness=stripped compare_logs=true record_envelope=all_records_v1 messages=1/1"
29927            )
29928        );
29929    }

29931    /// Run a real verify cell through `run_cell` against a fake Hermit that
29932    /// writes `report` and ends with `ending`, returning the serialized row.
29933    fn expected_exit_row(
29934        expected: Option<ExpectedGuestExit>,
29935        report: VerificationReport,
29936        ending: &str,
29937    ) -> (CellResult, serde_json::Value) {
29938        expected_exit_row_in_mode("verify", expected, report, ending)
29939    }
29940
29941    /// [`expected_exit_row`] for a `mode` cell. The declaration is always on
29942    /// the verify recipe, the only place validation admits it; a replay cell
29943    /// gets a verify recipe beside its own.
29944    fn expected_exit_row_in_mode(
29945        mode: &str,
29946        expected: Option<ExpectedGuestExit>,
29947        report: VerificationReport,
29948        ending: &str,
29949    ) -> (CellResult, serde_json::Value) {
29950        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
29951            "hermit-runner-expected-exit-row-{}-{:?}",
29952            std::process::id(),
29953            std::thread::current().id()
29954        ));
29955        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
29956        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
29957        fs::write(
29958            root.join("verification.json"),
29959            serde_json::to_vec(&report).unwrap(),
29960        )
29961        .unwrap();
29962        let hermit = root.join("hermit");
29963        crate::exec_safe_fs::write_executable(
29964            &hermit,
29965            format!(
29966                r#"#!/bin/sh
29967set -eu
29968verdict=
29969logdir=
29970rundir=
29971while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
29972  case "$1" in
29973    --verify-json) verdict=$2; shift 2 ;;
29974    --verify-log-dir) logdir=$2; shift 2 ;;
29975    --verify-run) rundir=$2; shift 2 ;;
29976    *) shift ;;
29977  esac
29978done
29979if [ -n "$rundir" ]; then
29980  # One run of the pair: its record, then its status; the comparison below
29981  # says what `run --verify` would have said.
29982  mkdir "$rundir"
29983  printf '{{}}\n' > "$rundir/verify-run.json"
29984  status=0
29985  ( {ending} ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
29986  exit "$status"
29987fi
29988if [ -n "$logdir" ]; then
29989  mkdir -p "$logdir"
29990  printf 'INFO detcore: shared\n' > "$logdir/run1_log_fixture.log"
29991fi
29992cp "{}" "$verdict"
29993{ending}
29994"#,
29995                root.join("verification.json").display()
29996            ),
29997            0o755,
29998        )
29999        .unwrap();
30000
30001        let mut cell = ptrace_cell(mode);
30002        if mode != "verify" {
30003            let verify = ptrace_cell("verify").test.modes["verify"].clone();
30004            cell.test.modes.insert("verify".into(), verify);
30005        }
30006        cell.test.id = "fixture/expected-exit-row".into();
30007        cell.id.test = cell.test.id.clone();
30008        cell.timeout_seconds = 10;
30009        cell.cpu_timeout_seconds = 5;
30010        cell.test
30011            .modes
30012            .get_mut("verify")
30013            .unwrap()
30014            .expected_guest_exit = expected;
30015        let mut context = run_context(&root);
30016        context.hermit_bin = hermit;
30017        context.run_verify_strict = true;
30018
30019        let result = run_cell(&context, &cell).unwrap();
30020        let row = serde_json::to_value(&result).unwrap();
30021        fs::remove_dir_all(root).unwrap();
30022        (result, row)
30023    }
30024
30025    /// A verify cell that passes on its declared nonzero disposition must say
30026    /// so on its row. Without the declaration a reader of `results.jsonl` sees
30027    /// a matched attempt with a nonzero status and no authority for it, and
30028    /// must refuse the row -- which is what the series writer did to every
30029    /// validate batch that contained one of these cells.
30030    #[test]
30031    fn a_declared_expected_exit_is_carried_on_the_result_row() {
30032        let (code_result, code_row) = expected_exit_row(
30033            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30034            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30035            "exit 7",
30036        );
30037        assert_eq!(code_result.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", code_result.reason);
30038        assert_eq!(code_result.attempts[0].status, Some(7));
30039        assert!(
30040            code_result.attempts[0]
30041                .argv
30042                .iter()
30043                .any(|arg| arg == "--verify-allow=failure")
30044        );
30045        assert_eq!(
30046            code_row["expected_guest_exit"],
30047            serde_json::json!({
30048                "code": 7,
30049                "signal": null,
30050                "reason": "the fixture guest fails on purpose",
30051            })
30052        );
30053
30054        // The 128 + signo spelling of a signal death carries the declared
30055        // signal, not the status Hermit happened to use to report it.
30056        let (signal_result, signal_row) = expected_exit_row(
30057            Some(expected_exit(None, Some(11))),
30058            expected_exit_report(None, Some(11)),
30059            "exit 139",
30060        );
30061        assert_eq!(signal_result.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", signal_result.reason);
30062        assert_eq!(signal_result.attempts[0].status, Some(139));
30063        assert_eq!(
30064            signal_row["expected_guest_exit"],
30065            serde_json::json!({
30066                "code": null,
30067                "signal": 11,
30068                "reason": "the fixture guest fails on purpose",
30069            })
30070        );
30071        let reread: CellResult = serde_json::from_value(signal_row).unwrap();
30072        assert_eq!(
30073            reread.expected_guest_exit,
30074            Some(expected_exit(None, Some(11)))
30075        );
30076
30077        // A cell without a declaration keeps the historical row shape: the key
30078        // is absent, not null, and such a row still reads back.
30079        let (plain_result, plain_row) =
30080            expected_exit_row(None, canonical_verification_report(), "exit 0");
30081        assert_eq!(plain_result.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", plain_result.reason);
30082        assert!(
30083            !plain_row
30084                .as_object()
30085                .unwrap()
30086                .contains_key("expected_guest_exit"),
30087            "{plain_row}"
30088        );
30089        let reread: CellResult = serde_json::from_value(plain_row).unwrap();
30090        assert_eq!(reread.expected_guest_exit, None);
30091    }
30092
30093    /// A retained verify PASS, as a result history keeps it after a skid
30094    /// retry, is re-decided from the row's own evidence by the checks the
30095    /// executor applies before it writes PASS (`retained_verify_pass_error`):
30096    /// the row's labels and execution path, each inner attempt's labels,
30097    /// first stderr line, report digest, the comparator the row's
30098    /// relaxations record, the declared stdout, the disposition the row's
30099    /// expected guest exit names, and the dispatch record of the row's
30100    /// backend. Each refusal below names the check that made it
30101    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>).
30102    #[test]
30103    fn a_retained_verify_pass_is_redecided_from_its_own_evidence() {
30104        let none = DeclaredStdout::default();
30105        let (pass, _) = expected_exit_row(
30106            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30107            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30108            "exit 7",
30109        );
30110        assert_eq!(pass.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", pass.reason);
30111        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&pass, &none), None);
30112        let (plain, _) = expected_exit_row(None, canonical_verification_report(), "exit 0");
30113        assert_eq!(plain.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", plain.reason);
30114        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&plain, &none), None);
30115        let refused = |label: &str, row: &CellResult, declared: &DeclaredStdout, check: &str| {
30116            let error = retained_verify_pass_error(row, declared)
30117                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{label} was re-decided as a verify PASS"));
30118            assert!(
30119                error.contains(check),
30120                "{label} was refused by another check: {error}"
30121            );
30122        };
30123        // Replace the attempt's report bytes and digest only, as a rewritten
30124        // history would.
30125        let with_bare_raw_report = |row: &CellResult, raw: String| {
30126            let mut row = row.clone();
30127            row.attempts[0].verification_report_sha256 = Some(hex_digest(raw.as_bytes()));
30128            row.attempts[0].verification_report = Some(raw);
30129            row
30130        };
30131        // Replace the report and, when it is a current report, the copies of
30132        // it the runner writes onto the attempt and the row.
30133        let with_raw_report = |row: &CellResult, raw: String| {
30134            let mut row = with_bare_raw_report(row, raw.clone());
30135            if let Ok(report) = current_verification_report(raw.as_bytes()) {
30136                let attempt = &mut row.attempts[0];
30137                attempt.runtime = report.runtime.clone();
30138                attempt.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = report.first_divergent_scheduler_turn;
30139                attempt.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds =
30140                    report.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds;
30141                attempt.first_divergent_record = report.first_divergent_record;
30142                attempt.first_divergent_syscall = report.first_divergent_syscall;
30143                attempt.first_divergent_left_message = report.first_divergent_left_message.clone();
30144                attempt.first_divergent_right_message =
30145                    report.first_divergent_right_message.clone();
30146                let position = cell_divergence_position(&row.attempts);
30147                row.runtime = row.attempts.iter().find_map(|a| a.runtime.clone());
30148                row.first_divergent_scheduler_turn = position.scheduler_turn;
30149                row.first_divergent_virtual_nanoseconds = position.virtual_nanoseconds;
30150                row.first_divergent_record = position.record;
30151                row.first_divergent_syscall = position.syscall;
30152                row.first_divergent_left_message = position.left_message;
30153                row.first_divergent_right_message = position.right_message;
30154            }
30155            row
30156        };
30157        let with_report = |row: &CellResult, report: &VerificationReport| {
30158            with_raw_report(row, serde_json::to_string(report).unwrap())
30159        };
30160
30161        // Labels the executor never writes on a verify PASS row.
30162        let mut replay = pass.clone();
30163        replay.mode = "replay".into();
30164        refused("a replay row", &replay, &none, "not a verify PASS");
30165        let mut failed = pass.clone();
30166        failed.outcome = "FAIL".into();
30167        refused("a FAIL row", &failed, &none, "not a verify PASS");
30168        let mut no_result = pass.clone();
30169        no_result.result = None;
30170        let mut classified = pass.clone();
30171        classified.failure_class = Some(FailureClass::UnderstoodInfrastructureFailure);
30172        let mut kinded = pass.clone();
30173        kinded.error_kind = Some("fixture-kind".into());
30174        let mut reasoned = pass.clone();
30175        reasoned.reason = Some("fixture reason".into());
30176        for (label, row) in [
30177            ("a PASS row without a typed result", &no_result),
30178            ("a PASS row with a failure class", &classified),
30179            ("a PASS row with an error kind", &kinded),
30180            ("a PASS row with a reason", &reasoned),
30181        ] {
30182            refused(label, row, &none, "not labelled as a verify PASS");
30183        }
30184
30185        // A SaBRe path on a ptrace row, which no attempt of the row decides.
30186        let mut labelled_path = pass.clone();
30187        labelled_path.execution_path = Some(serde_json::json!({"eligible": true}));
30188        refused(
30189            "a ptrace PASS row recording a SaBRe path",
30190            &labelled_path,
30191            &none,
30192            "execution-path evidence",
30193        );
30194
30195        // Inner attempts the executor never writes under a PASS row.
30196        let mut empty = pass.clone();
30197        empty.attempts.clear();
30198        refused(
30199            "a PASS row without attempts",
30200            &empty,
30201            &none,
30202            "no inner attempt",
30203        );
30204        let mut repeated = pass.clone();
30205        repeated.attempts.push(repeated.attempts[0].clone());
30206        refused(
30207            "a repeated attempt index",
30208            &repeated,
30209            &none,
30210            "blank or repeated",
30211        );
30212        let mut blank = pass.clone();
30213        blank.attempts[0].index = " ".into();
30214        refused("a blank attempt index", &blank, &none, "blank or repeated");
30215        let mut attempt_reasoned = pass.clone();
30216        attempt_reasoned.attempts[0].reason = Some("fixture reason".into());
30217        let mut attempt_kinded = pass.clone();
30218        attempt_kinded.attempts[0].error_kind = Some("fixture-kind".into());
30219        let mut attempt_timed_out = pass.clone();
30220        attempt_timed_out.attempts[0].timed_out = true;
30221        let mut attempt_error = pass.clone();
30222        attempt_error.attempts[0].outcome = "ERROR".into();
30223        for (label, row) in [
30224            ("an attempt with a reason", &attempt_reasoned),
30225            ("an attempt with an error kind", &attempt_kinded),
30226            ("a timed-out attempt", &attempt_timed_out),
30227            ("an ERROR attempt", &attempt_error),
30228        ] {
30229            refused(label, row, &none, "is not a PASS without");
30230        }
30231
30232        // Hermit's generic command-line error class on the first stderr line
30233        // keeps an executed attempt ERROR even beside a matched report and
30234        // the declared exit status, so a retained attempt carrying it is
30235        // never a pass either. Only the first line carries Hermit's
30236        // classification, for the executor and for this re-decision alike.
30237        let cli_error = "HERMIT_INTERNAL_FAILURE class=cli-error";
30238        let (executed, _) = expected_exit_row(
30239            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30240            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30241            &format!("printf '%s\\n' '{cli_error}' >&2; exit 7"),
30242        );
30243        assert_eq!(executed.outcome, "ERROR", "{executed:?}");
30244        let mut producer_failed = pass.clone();
30245        producer_failed.attempts[0].stderr = format!("{cli_error}\n");
30246        refused(
30247            "an attempt reporting Hermit's command-line error",
30248            &producer_failed,
30249            &none,
30250            "internal-failure class",
30251        );
30252        let (executed_later, _) = expected_exit_row(
30253            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30254            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30255            &format!("printf 'guest output\\n%s\\n' '{cli_error}' >&2; exit 7"),
30256        );
30257        assert_eq!(executed_later.outcome, "PASS", "{executed_later:?}");
30258        let mut later_line = pass.clone();
30259        later_line.attempts[0].stderr = format!("guest output\n{cli_error}\n");
30260        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&later_line, &none), None);
30261
30262        // The retained report must be the bytes its digest names, and a
30263        // current report.
30264        let mut unreported = pass.clone();
30265        unreported.attempts[0].verification_report = None;
30266        unreported.attempts[0].verification_report_sha256 = None;
30267        refused(
30268            "an attempt without a report",
30269            &unreported,
30270            &none,
30271            "no verification report",
30272        );
30273        let mut misdigested = pass.clone();
30274        misdigested.attempts[0].verification_report_sha256 = Some("0".repeat(64));
30275        refused("a misdigested report", &misdigested, &none, "not the bytes");
30276        refused(
30277            "an unreadable report",
30278            &with_raw_report(&pass, "{}".into()),
30279            &none,
30280            "not a current report",
30281        );
30282
30283        // The comparator the row's relaxations record. A canonical report
30284        // under the stripped relaxation, and a stripped report under none,
30285        // are refused; a stripped report under the stripped relaxation
30286        // passes only when it matched and its exact outputs agree.
30287        let stripped_relaxation = format!("{STRIPPED_COMPARATOR_RELAXATION_PREFIX}fixture reason");
30288        // Each row carries the command line the executor writes for its
30289        // relaxations, so only the comparison can refuse it.
30290        let mut canonical_under_stripped = pass.clone();
30291        canonical_under_stripped
30292            .relaxations
30293            .push(stripped_relaxation.clone());
30294        let canonical_under_stripped = with_executor_invocation(canonical_under_stripped);
30295        refused(
30296            "a canonical report under the stripped relaxation",
30297            &canonical_under_stripped,
30298            &none,
30299            "the row's Stripped comparator",
30300        );
30301        let stripped_report =
30302            with_ptrace_dispatch(serde_json::from_str(PRODUCER_STRIPPED_REPORT).unwrap());
30303        let stripped_under_strict = with_report(&plain, &stripped_report);
30304        refused(
30305            "a stripped report under no relaxation",
30306            &stripped_under_strict,
30307            &none,
30308            "the row's Strict comparator",
30309        );
30310        let mut stripped = stripped_under_strict.clone();
30311        stripped.relaxations.push(stripped_relaxation);
30312        let stripped = with_executor_invocation(stripped);
30313        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&stripped, &none), None);
30314        let mut stripped_outputs_differ = stripped_report.clone();
30315        stripped_outputs_differ
30316            .compared_outputs
30317            .as_mut()
30318            .unwrap()
30319            .right
30320            .stdout_bytes += 1;
30321        // The report reader already refuses a matched report whose two
30322        // operands differ, before the comparator check is reached.
30323        refused(
30324            "a stripped report whose exact outputs differ",
30325            &with_report(&stripped, &stripped_outputs_differ),
30326            &none,
30327            "operands differ in status, stdout, or stderr",
30328        );
30329        let mut diverged = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
30330        diverged.verified = false;
30331        diverged.bitwise_parity = false;
30332        diverged.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
30333        diverged.first_divergent_record = Some(9);
30334        diverged.first_divergent_left_message = Some("left".into());
30335        diverged.first_divergent_right_message = Some("right".into());
30336        refused(
30337            "a canonical divergence",
30338            &with_report(&pass, &diverged),
30339            &none,
30340            "the row's Strict comparator",
30341        );
30342
30343        // The declared stdout, decided from the report's digests and, for
30344        // the contained text, from the attempt's captured stdout when it is
30345        // both compared runs' stdout.
30346        let golden = "golden\n";
30347        let golden_stderr = "diag\n";
30348        let mut golden_report = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
30349        let outputs = golden_report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
30350        for output in [&mut outputs.left, &mut outputs.right] {
30351            output.stdout_sha256 = hex_digest(golden.as_bytes());
30352            output.stdout_bytes = golden.len() as u64;
30353            output.stderr_sha256 = hex_digest(golden_stderr.as_bytes());
30354            output.stderr_bytes = golden_stderr.len() as u64;
30355        }
30356        let mut golden_pass = with_report(&pass, &golden_report);
30357        golden_pass.attempts[0].stdout = golden.into();
30358        let exact = |text: &str| DeclaredStdout {
30359            exact: Some(text.into()),
30360            contains: None,
30361            stderr_exact: None,
30362        };
30363        let contains = |text: &str| DeclaredStdout {
30364            exact: None,
30365            contains: Some(text.into()),
30366            stderr_exact: None,
30367        };
30368        let stderr_exact = |text: &str| DeclaredStdout {
30369            exact: None,
30370            contains: None,
30371            stderr_exact: Some(text.into()),
30372        };
30373        assert_eq!(
30374            retained_verify_pass_error(&golden_pass, &exact(golden)),
30375            None
30376        );
30377        assert_eq!(
30378            retained_verify_pass_error(&golden_pass, &stderr_exact(golden_stderr)),
30379            None
30380        );
30381        assert_eq!(
30382            retained_verify_pass_error(&golden_pass, &contains("gold")),
30383            None
30384        );
30385        refused(
30386            "stdout other than the declared bytes",
30387            &pass,
30388            &exact(golden),
30389            "declared stdout assertion",
30390        );
30391        refused(
30392            "stderr other than the declared bytes",
30393            &golden_pass,
30394            &stderr_exact("other diag\n"),
30395            "declared stdout assertion",
30396        );
30397        refused(
30398            "stdout without the declared text",
30399            &golden_pass,
30400            &contains("silver"),
30401            "declared stdout assertion",
30402        );
30403        let mut uncaptured = golden_pass.clone();
30404        uncaptured.attempts[0].stdout = "gold, but not the compared bytes\n".into();
30405        refused(
30406            "a capture that is not the compared runs' stdout",
30407            &uncaptured,
30408            &contains("gold"),
30409            "declared stdout assertion",
30410        );
30411
30412        // The disposition the row's expected guest exit names: that guest
30413        // ending and the Hermit status reporting it, or Hermit exit status 0
30414        // when the row names none.
30415        let mut undeclared = pass.clone();
30416        undeclared.expected_guest_exit = None;
30417        let undeclared = with_executor_invocation(undeclared);
30418        refused(
30419            "exit status 7 without a declaration",
30420            &undeclared,
30421            &none,
30422            "did not end as the row requires",
30423        );
30424        refused(
30425            "a guest that exited 0 where 7 is expected",
30426            &with_report(&pass, &expected_exit_report(Some(0), None)),
30427            &none,
30428            "did not end as the row requires",
30429        );
30430        let mut hermit_succeeded = pass.clone();
30431        hermit_succeeded.attempts[0].status = Some(0);
30432        refused(
30433            "Hermit exit status 0 where the guest exited 7",
30434            &hermit_succeeded,
30435            &none,
30436            "did not end as the row requires",
30437        );
30438
30439        // The dispatch record a passing attempt of the row's backend carries.
30440        let mut dispatched_report = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
30441        dispatched_report.runtime = stripped_report.runtime.clone();
30442        let dispatched = with_report(&pass, &dispatched_report);
30443        assert_eq!(retained_verify_pass_error(&dispatched, &none), None);
30444        let mut forged: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(&dispatched_report).unwrap();
30445        forged["runtime"]["run1"]["dispatch"]["backend"] = serde_json::json!("liteinst");
30446        let forged_pass = with_raw_report(&pass, serde_json::to_string(&forged).unwrap());
30447        refused(
30448            "another backend's dispatch record",
30449            &forged_pass,
30450            &none,
30451            "dispatch evidence",
30452        );
30453
30454        // The runner copies a passing attempt's runtime and divergence
30455        // coordinates from its report onto the attempt, and onto the row the
30456        // first runtime and the divergence position its attempts give. A row
30457        // the runner wrote from a report carrying a runtime agrees with every
30458        // copy.
30459        let (executed_dispatched, _) = expected_exit_row(
30460            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30461            dispatched_report.clone(),
30462            "exit 7",
30463        );
30464        assert_eq!(
30465            executed_dispatched.outcome, "PASS",
30466            "{:?}",
30467            executed_dispatched.reason
30468        );
30469        assert!(executed_dispatched.runtime.is_some());
30470        assert_eq!(
30471            executed_dispatched.attempts[0].runtime,
30472            dispatched_report.runtime
30473        );
30474        assert_eq!(
30475            retained_verify_pass_error(&executed_dispatched, &none),
30476            None
30477        );
30478        // The forged history with only the report's runtime removed: the
30479        // attempt's and the row's copies still carry the other backend's
30480        // record, which no check of the report would see.
30481        let mut unruntimed = forged.clone();
30482        unruntimed.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("runtime");
30483        let stale_copies =
30484            with_bare_raw_report(&forged_pass, serde_json::to_string(&unruntimed).unwrap());
30485        assert!(stale_copies.attempts[0].runtime.is_some() && stale_copies.runtime.is_some());
30486        refused(
30487            "an attempt runtime copy the report does not carry",
30488            &stale_copies,
30489            &none,
30490            "retained runtime or divergence coordinates differ",
30491        );
30492        // The attempt's copy removed too: only the row still carries it.
30493        let mut stale_row = stale_copies.clone();
30494        stale_row.attempts[0].runtime = None;
30495        refused(
30496            "a row runtime copy no attempt carries",
30497            &stale_row,
30498            &none,
30499            "the row's runtime or divergence coordinates",
30500        );
30501        // A divergence coordinate only a copy carries.
30502        let mut attempt_coordinate = pass.clone();
30503        attempt_coordinate.attempts[0].first_divergent_record = Some(9);
30504        attempt_coordinate.first_divergent_record = Some(9);
30505        refused(
30506            "an attempt divergence coordinate the report does not carry",
30507            &attempt_coordinate,
30508            &none,
30509            "retained runtime or divergence coordinates differ",
30510        );
30511        let mut row_message = pass.clone();
30512        row_message.first_divergent_left_message = Some("left".into());
30513        refused(
30514            "a row divergence message no attempt carries",
30515            &row_message,
30516            &none,
30517            "the row's runtime or divergence coordinates",
30518        );
30519    }

30521    /// A row whose attempt carries an `infrastructure_error` report records
30522    /// the cell's declared stdout assertions, so a later reader can re-decide
30523    /// them from the attempt's own evidence before treating the row as
30524    /// skid-only (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/1845>). Every
30525    /// other row keeps the historical shape, without the key.
30526    #[test]
30527    fn a_skid_row_records_the_cells_declared_stdout() {
30528        let (skid_result, skid_row) = expected_exit_row(
30529            None,
30530            skid_report_value(2),
30531            &format!("{SKID_STDERR}; exit 122"),
30532        );
30533        assert_eq!(
30534            (
30535                skid_result.outcome.as_str(),
30536                skid_result.error_kind.as_deref()
30537            ),
30538            ("ERROR", Some("infrastructure")),
30539            "{skid_result:?}"
30540        );
30541        assert_eq!(
30542            skid_row["declared_stdout"],
30543            serde_json::json!({"exact": null, "contains": null, "stderr_exact": null}),
30544            "{skid_row}"
30545        );
30546        assert_eq!(skid_overshoot_only_reports(&skid_result), Some(2));
30547        let reread: CellResult = serde_json::from_value(skid_row.clone()).unwrap();
30548        assert_eq!(reread.declared_stdout, Some(DeclaredStdout::default()));
30549        assert_eq!(skid_overshoot_only_reports(&reread), Some(2));
30550        // Each member is required, though it may be null: a record that
30551        // omits one is refused rather than read as a declaration of nothing.
30552        for (omitted, record) in [
30553            ("exact", serde_json::json!({"contains": null})),
30554            ("contains", serde_json::json!({"exact": null})),
30555            ("exact", serde_json::json!({})),
30556        ] {
30557            let mut row = skid_row.clone();
30558            row["declared_stdout"] = record;
30559            let error = serde_json::from_value::<CellResult>(row).unwrap_err();
30560            assert!(
30561                error
30562                    .to_string()
30563                    .contains(&format!("missing field `{omitted}`")),
30564                "{error}"
30565            );
30566        }
30567
30568        let (plain_result, plain_row) =
30569            expected_exit_row(None, canonical_verification_report(), "exit 0");
30570        assert_eq!(plain_result.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", plain_result.reason);
30571        assert!(
30572            !plain_row
30573                .as_object()
30574                .unwrap()
30575                .contains_key("declared_stdout"),
30576            "{plain_row}"
30577        );
30578
30579        // The record is the verify recipe's declaration for the cell's
30580        // backend, exactly what the classifier checked.
30581        let mut declared = ptrace_cell("verify");
30582        let recipe = declared.test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap();
30583        recipe.expected_stdout = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".to_string(), "golden\n".to_string())]);
30584        recipe.expected_stdout_contains =
30585            BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".to_string(), "gold".to_string())]);
30586        assert_eq!(
30587            cell_declared_stdout(&declared),
30588            DeclaredStdout {
30589                exact: Some("golden\n".into()),
30590                contains: Some("gold".into()),
30591                stderr_exact: None,
30592            }
30593        );
30594        assert_eq!(
30595            cell_declared_stdout(&ptrace_cell("verify")),
30596            DeclaredStdout::default()
30597        );
30598    }

30600    /// Only verify and replay cells carry a declaration (a replay cell its
30601    /// own, where declared; here its recipe's field is what
30602    /// `cell_expected_guest_exit` reads, with no verify recipe beside it);
30603    /// the same recipe field on any other mode is not authority for a
30604    /// nonzero pass there.
30605    #[test]
30606    fn only_a_verify_cell_carries_its_declared_expected_exit() {
30607        let mut verify = ptrace_cell("verify");
30608        verify
30609            .test
30610            .modes
30611            .get_mut("verify")
30612            .unwrap()
30613            .expected_guest_exit = Some(expected_exit(Some(3), None));
30614        assert_eq!(
30615            cell_expected_guest_exit(&verify),
30616            Some(expected_exit(Some(3), None))
30617        );
30618        for mode in ["chaos", "naked"] {
30619            let mut other = ptrace_cell(mode);
30620            other.test.modes.get_mut(mode).unwrap().expected_guest_exit =
30621                Some(expected_exit(Some(3), None));
30622            assert_eq!(cell_expected_guest_exit(&other), None, "{mode}");
30623        }
30624        assert_eq!(cell_expected_guest_exit(&ptrace_cell("verify")), None);
30625    }

30627    /// A test with both a verify and a replay recipe, selected as its replay cell.
30628    /// A replay cell passes on its verify cell's declared nonzero disposition
30629    /// only through the same gate a verify cell does: a matched canonical
30630    /// replay whose guest and Hermit both end that way. A wrong exit, a
30631    /// diverged replay, or no declaration at all is still a failure.
30632    #[test]
30633    fn a_replay_cell_passes_on_the_inherited_exit_only_when_matched_and_exact() {
30634        let (exact, _) = expected_exit_row_in_mode(
30635            "replay",
30636            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30637            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30638            "exit 7",
30639        );
30640        assert_eq!(exact.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", exact.reason);
30641        assert!(exact.attempts[0].argv.iter().any(|arg| arg == "record"));
30642
30643        let (wrong_exit, _) = expected_exit_row_in_mode(
30644            "replay",
30645            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30646            expected_exit_report(Some(6), None),
30647            "exit 6",
30648        );
30649        assert_eq!(wrong_exit.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", wrong_exit.reason);
30650        assert_eq!(
30651            wrong_exit.reason.as_deref(),
30652            Some("guest ended with exit code 6, but the manifest expects exit code 7")
30653        );
30654
30655        let mut diverged = expected_exit_report(Some(7), None);
30656        diverged.verified = false;
30657        diverged.bitwise_parity = false;
30658        diverged.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
30659        diverged.first_divergent_record = Some(9);
30660        diverged.first_divergent_left_message = Some("left".into());
30661        diverged.first_divergent_right_message = Some("right".into());
30662        let (diverged, _) = expected_exit_row_in_mode(
30663            "replay",
30664            Some(expected_exit(Some(7), None)),
30665            diverged,
30666            "exit 7",
30667        );
30668        assert_eq!(diverged.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", diverged.reason);
30669
30670        let (undeclared, _) = expected_exit_row_in_mode(
30671            "replay",
30672            None,
30673            expected_exit_report(Some(7), None),
30674            "exit 7",
30675        );
30676        assert_ne!(undeclared.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", undeclared.reason);
30677    }

30679    /// A result row may carry a declared guest exit in verify or replay mode:
30680    /// a replay cell carries its own replay recipe's declaration where it
30681    /// has one, else its verify recipe's. A reader credits it only
30682    /// from the invocation the runner writes for it: a verify comparison with
30683    /// `--verify-allow=failure`, or a replay's `record start`, whose
30684    /// comparison takes `--verify-allow=both`.
30685    #[test]
30686    fn a_replay_result_row_may_carry_its_inherited_declaration() {
30687        let expected = expected_exit(Some(7), None);
30688        for mode in ["verify", "replay"] {
30689            validate_result_expected_guest_exit("row", mode, Some(&expected)).unwrap();
30690        }
30691        for mode in ["chaos", "naked"] {
30692            assert!(
30693                validate_result_expected_guest_exit("row", mode, Some(&expected)).is_err(),
30694                "{mode}"
30695            );
30696        }
30697        validate_expected_guest_exit("recipe", "replay", Some(&expected)).unwrap();
30698        let zero = expected_exit(Some(0), None);
30699        validate_result_expected_guest_exit("row", "replay", Some(&zero)).unwrap();
30700        assert!(validate_expected_guest_exit("recipe", "verify", Some(&zero)).is_err());
30701        assert!(validate_result_expected_guest_exit("row", "verify", Some(&zero)).is_err());
30702        let verify = ["hermit", "run", "--verify-allow=failure"];
30703        let replay = [
30704            "hermit-verify-pair",
30705            "hermit",
30706            "log-diff",
30707            "--verify-allow=both",
30708            "hermit",
30709            "record",
30710            "start",
30711        ];
30712        assert!(invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit("verify", &verify));
30713        assert!(invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit("replay", &replay));
30714        assert!(!invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit("replay", &verify));
30715        assert!(!invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit("verify", &replay));
30716        assert!(!invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit(
30717            "replay",
30718            &["hermit", "log-diff", "--verify-allow=both", "hermit", "run"]
30719        ));
30720        assert!(!invocation_admits_declared_guest_exit("chaos", &replay));
30721    }

30723    /// A replay recipe may declare its own expected guest exit where record

30725    /// included; it wins over the verify recipe's declaration for the
30726    /// replay cell alone, and its result row may carry that success.
30727    #[test]
30728    fn a_replay_recipe_may_override_the_inherited_expected_exit_with_success() {
30729        let base = ptrace_cell("verify").test.modes["verify"].clone();
30730        let mut verify = base.clone();

30742            cell_expected_guest_exit(&cell),

30746        assert_eq!(
30747            cell_expected_guest_exit(&inherited),
30748            Some(expected_exit(Some(1), None))
30749        );
30750        validate_result_expected_guest_exit("row", "replay", Some(&expected_exit(Some(0), None)))
30751            .unwrap();

30754    fn replay_cell_with_verify(verify: ModeRecipe, replay: ModeRecipe) -> SelectedCell {
30755        let mut cell = ptrace_cell("replay");
30756        cell.test.modes.insert("verify".into(), verify);
30757        cell.test.modes.insert("replay".into(), replay);
30758        cell

30761    /// A replay cell records the program its verify cell checks: it inherits
30762    /// verify's guest inputs and expectations, and a guest input it declares
30763    /// itself wins.
30764    #[test]
30765    fn a_replay_cell_inherits_its_verify_guest_inputs_and_expectations() {
30766        let base = ptrace_cell("verify").test.modes["verify"].clone();
30767        let mut verify = base.clone();
30768        verify.guest_args = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["workdir".into()])]);
30769        verify.workdir = Some("/srv".into());
30770        verify.env = Some(BTreeMap::from([("MODE".into(), "x".into())]));
30771        verify.expected_guest_exit = Some(expected_exit(Some(3), None));
30772        verify.expected_stdout = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), "p\n".into())]);
30773        verify.expected_stdout_contains = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), "ok".into())]);
30774        let inherited = replay_cell_with_verify(verify.clone(), base.clone());
30775        assert_eq!(cell_guest_args(&inherited, "ptrace"), ["workdir"]);
30776        assert_eq!(cell_guest_args(&inherited, "dbt"), Vec::<String>::new());
30777        assert_eq!(cell_workdir(&inherited).as_deref(), Some("/srv"));
30778        assert_eq!(Some(cell_mode_env(&inherited)), verify.env);
30779        assert_eq!(
30780            cell_expected_guest_exit(&inherited),
30781            Some(expected_exit(Some(3), None))
30782        );
30783        assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&inherited).as_deref(), Some("p\n"));
30784        assert_eq!(
30785            cell_expected_stdout_contains(&inherited).as_deref(),
30786            Some("ok")
30787        );
30788
30789        let mut replay = base;
30790        replay.guest_args = BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), vec!["--record".into()])]);
30791        let overridden = replay_cell_with_verify(verify.clone(), replay);
30792        assert_eq!(cell_guest_args(&overridden, "ptrace"), ["--record"]);
30793        // Validation refuses `workdir` on a replay recipe, so the inherited one
30794        // is the only one a replay cell can have.
30795        assert_eq!(cell_workdir(&overridden).as_deref(), Some("/srv"));
30796
30797        // Chaos keeps reading only its own recipe.
30798        let mut chaos = ptrace_cell("chaos");
30799        chaos.test.modes.insert("verify".into(), verify);
30800        assert_eq!(cell_guest_args(&chaos, "ptrace"), Vec::<String>::new());
30801        assert_eq!(cell_workdir(&chaos), None);
30802        assert_eq!(cell_expected_guest_exit(&chaos), None);
30803    }

30805    #[test]
30806    fn backend_env_is_scoped_in_argv_and_replay_inheritance() {
30807        let context = run_context(Path::new("/repo"));
30808        let mut cell = ptrace_cell("verify");
30809        let recipe = cell.test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap();
30810        recipe.backends_enabled.push("liteinst".into());
30811        recipe.env = Some(BTreeMap::from([("TMPDIR".into(), "/tmp".into())]));
30812        recipe.env_by_backend = BTreeMap::from([(
30813            "liteinst".into(),
30814            BTreeMap::from([("FIXTURE_CELL".into(), "on".into())]),
30815        )]);
30816        validate_mode_extensions("fixture/test", "verify", recipe).unwrap();
30817        let verify = recipe.clone();
30818        let render = |cell: &SelectedCell| {
30819            build_spec(
30820                &context,
30821                cell,
30822                PathBuf::from("/repo/results/fixture"),
30823                vec!["/bin/true".into()],
30824                "1",
30825                None,
30826                15,
30827            )
30828            .unwrap()
30829            .argv
30830        };
30831        let ptrace = render(&cell);
30832        cell.id.backend = Some("liteinst".into());
30833        let liteinst = render(&cell);
30834        assert!(ptrace.iter().any(|arg| arg == "TMPDIR=/tmp"));
30835        assert!(liteinst.iter().any(|arg| arg == "TMPDIR=/tmp"));
30836        assert!(!ptrace.iter().any(|arg| arg == "FIXTURE_CELL=on"));
30837        let addition = liteinst
30838            .windows(2)
30839            .position(|pair| pair == ["--env", "FIXTURE_CELL=on"])
30840            .unwrap();
30841        let mut without_addition = liteinst;
30842        without_addition.drain(addition..addition + 2);
30843        let mut unchanged = cell.clone();
30844        unchanged
30845            .test
30846            .modes
30847            .get_mut("verify")
30848            .unwrap()
30849            .env_by_backend
30850            .clear();
30851        assert_eq!(without_addition, render(&unchanged));
30852        let mut replay = replay_cell_with_verify(verify, ModeRecipe::default());
30853        replay.id.backend = Some("liteinst".into());
30854        assert_eq!(cell_mode_env(&replay), cell_mode_env(&cell));
30855        replay.test.modes.get_mut("replay").unwrap().env = Some(BTreeMap::new());
30856        assert!(cell_mode_env(&replay).is_empty());
30857        assert!(!render(&replay).iter().any(|arg| arg == "FIXTURE_CELL=on"));
30858    }

30861    fn backend_env_refuses_invalid_scope_names_values_and_collisions() {
30862        let mut recipe = ModeRecipe {
30863            backends_enabled: vec!["liteinst".into()],

30865            ..ModeRecipe::default()
30866        };
30867        for (backend, name, value, needle) in [
30868            ("ptrace", "FIXTURE", "on", "not in backends_enabled"),
30869            ("unknown", "FIXTURE", "on", "not in backends_enabled"),
30870            ("liteinst", "", "on", "not a valid NAME=VALUE"),
30871            ("liteinst", "lower", "on", "not a valid NAME=VALUE"),
30872            ("liteinst", "NAME", "\0", "not a valid NAME=VALUE"),
30873            ("liteinst", "HOME", "x", "runner sets itself"),
30874            ("liteinst", "TMPDIR", "/tmp", "repeats common env name"),
30875        ] {
30876            recipe.env_by_backend = BTreeMap::from([(
30877                backend.into(),
30878                BTreeMap::from([(name.into(), value.into())]),

30881            assert!(error.contains(needle), "{error}");

30890            .env_by_backend
30891            .get_mut("liteinst")
30892            .unwrap()
30893            .insert("FIXTURE".into(), "on".into());
30894        for mode in ["replay", "naked", "chaos", "custom"] {
30895            recipe.env = None;

30897            assert!(
30898                error.contains("env_by_backend, which only a verify mode accepts"),
30899                "{error}"
30900            );

31004    /// Where the host has /etc/ld.so.cache, verify and chaos pairs run under
31005    /// `hermit verify-inputs` and both runs adopt its one sealed copy; a
31006    /// replay pair, whose first command is `record start`, does not
31007    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4693).
31008    #[test]
31009    fn verify_and_chaos_pairs_share_the_hosts_ld_so_cache_and_replay_pairs_do_not() {
31010        let mut context = run_context(Path::new("/repo"));
31011        context.shares_ld_so_cache = true;
31012        let spec_of = |context: &RunContext, cell: &SelectedCell| {
31013            build_spec(
31014                context,
31015                cell,
31016                PathBuf::from("/repo/results/shared-cell"),
31017                vec!["/bin/true".into()],
31018                "1",
31019                (cell.id.mode == "chaos").then_some(7),
31020                15,
31021            )
31022            .unwrap()
31023        };
31024        let hermit = context.hermit_bin.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
31025        for backend in ["ptrace", "liteinst", "in-guest-trap"] {
31026            for mode in ["verify", "chaos"] {
31027                let mut cell = ptrace_cell(mode);
31028                cell.id.backend = Some(backend.into());
31029                let spec = spec_of(&context, &cell);
31030                assert_eq!(spec.argv[0], hermit, "{backend}/{mode}: {:?}", spec.argv);
31031                assert_eq!(
31032                    spec.argv[1..=SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()],
31033                    SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.map(String::from),
31034                    "{backend}/{mode}: {:?}",
31035                    spec.argv
31036                );
31037                assert_eq!(
31038                    spec.argv[1 + SHARED_INPUTS_PREFIX.len()..][..3],
31039                    ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT],
31040                    "{backend}/{mode}"
31041                );
31042                assert!(
31043                    spec.argv.windows(3).any(|window| window
31044                        == [
31045                            "--verify-run",
31046                            VERIFY_RUN_DIR_PLACEHOLDER,
31047                            SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG
31048                        ]),
31049                    "{backend}/{mode}: {:?}",
31050                    spec.argv
31051                );
31052                for (token, count) in [
31053                    ("verify-inputs", 1),
31054                    (SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG, 1),
31055                    ("--in-guest-exec-stop", 0),
31056                    ("--native-exec-shared-inputs=197", 0),
31057                    (VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT, 1),
31058                    ("log-diff", 1),
31059                ] {
31060                    assert_eq!(
31061                        spec.argv.iter().filter(|arg| *arg == token).count(),
31062                        count,
31063                        "{backend}/{mode}: {token}"
31064                    );
31065                }
31066
31067                // Without the cache ordinary cells acquire no input holder.
31068                let mut plain_context = context.clone();
31069                plain_context.shares_ld_so_cache = false;
31070                let plain = spec_of(&plain_context, &cell);
31071                assert_eq!(plain.argv[..3], ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT]);
31072                for token in [
31073                    "verify-inputs",
31074                    SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG,
31075                    "--in-guest-exec-stop",
31076                    "--native-exec-shared-inputs=197",
31077                ] {
31078                    assert!(
31079                        !plain.argv.iter().any(|arg| arg == token),
31080                        "{backend}/{mode}: {token}"
31081                    );
31082                }
31083            }
31084            let base = ptrace_cell("verify").test.modes["verify"].clone();
31085            let mut cell = replay_cell_with_verify(base.clone(), base);
31086            cell.id.backend = Some(backend.into());
31087            let replay = spec_of(&context, &cell);
31088            assert_eq!(replay.argv[..3], ["bash", "-c", VERIFY_PAIR_SCRIPT]);
31089            for token in [
31090                "verify-inputs",
31091                SHARED_INPUTS_FLAG,
31092                "--in-guest-exec-stop",
31093                "--native-exec-shared-inputs=197",
31094            ] {
31095                assert!(
31096                    !replay.argv.iter().any(|arg| arg == token),
31097                    "{backend}/replay: {token}"
31098                );
31099            }
31100        }
31101    }

31103    /// Explicit pair API callers seal the image, stdin and optional loader
31104    /// cache through one manifest. The cache changes no inner pair command;

31106    #[test]
31107    fn explicit_mapped_verify_and_chaos_pairs_share_one_manifest_with_the_loader_cache() {

31129                spec

31131            let plain = spec_of(false);
31132            let cached = spec_of(true);
31133            for spec in [&plain, &cached] {

31135                for (token, count) in [

31150                assert_eq!(&spec.argv[separator + 1..], guest.as_slice(), "{mode}");

31161            assert_eq!(
31162                without_mapped_input_holder(&plain.argv),
31163                without_mapped_input_holder(&cached.argv),
31164                "{mode}: adding the cache must preserve the pair script, comparison and run"
31165            );
31166        }

31169    /// A canonical matched report whose two runs printed `first` and
31170    /// `second` on stdout.
31171    fn stdout_report(first: &str, second: &str) -> VerificationReport {
31172        let mut report = canonical_verification_report();
31173        let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
31174        outputs.left.stdout_sha256 = hex_digest(first.as_bytes());
31175        outputs.left.stdout_bytes = first.len() as u64;
31176        outputs.right.stdout_sha256 = hex_digest(second.as_bytes());
31177        outputs.right.stdout_bytes = second.len() as u64;
31178        report
31179    }
31180
31181    fn attempt_with_expected_stdout(
31182        expected: &str,
31183        report: VerificationReport,
31184        ending: &str,
31185    ) -> AttemptResult {
31186        attempt_with_stdout_assertions(Some(expected), None, report, "", ending)
31187    }
31188
31189    /// Run a fake Hermit that writes `report` as its verdict and prints
31190    /// `captured` on stdout, against a dbt verify spec declaring `exact`
31191    /// and/or `contains`.
31192    fn attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
31193        exact: Option<&str>,
31194        contains: Option<&str>,
31195        report: VerificationReport,
31196        captured: &str,
31197        ending: &str,
31198    ) -> AttemptResult {
31199        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
31200            "hermit-runner-expected-stdout-{}-{:?}",
31201            std::process::id(),
31202            std::thread::current().id()
31203        ));
31204        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
31205        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
31206        let verdict = dir.join("verdict.json");
31207        let spec = CellRunSpec {
31208            command_binding: None,
31209            id: CellId {
31210                test: "fixture/expected-stdout".into(),
31211                mode: "verify".into(),
31212                backend: Some("dbt".into()),
31213            },
31214            lane: "portable".into(),
31215            category: "fixture".into(),
31216            cwd: dir.clone(),
31217            env: BTreeMap::new(),
31218            argv: vec![
31219                "/bin/sh".into(),
31220                "-c".into(),
31221                format!("printf %s \"$1\" > \"$2\"; printf %s \"$3\"; {ending}"),
31222                "sh".into(),
31223                serde_json::to_string(&report).unwrap(),
31224                verdict.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
31225                captured.into(),
31226            ],
31227            guest_argv: vec!["fixture".into()],
31228            timeout_seconds: 5,
31229            verdict_path: Some(verdict),
31230            verification_log_dir: None,
31231            verify_runs: None,
31232            single_run_capture: None,
31233            sabre_path_evidence: None,
31234            cell_dir: dir.clone(),
31235            expected_guest_exit: None,
31236            expected_stdout: exact.map(str::to_string),
31237            expected_stdout_contains: contains.map(str::to_string),
31238            expected_stderr: None,
31239            comparator: Comparator::Strict,
31240            attempt: "1".into(),
31241            fixed_workdir_source: dir.join("workdir/1"),
31242        };
31243        let result = execute_spec(&spec).unwrap();
31244        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
31245        result
31246    }

31248    /// Two runs that agree with each other on the wrong bytes are a failure
31249    /// when the cell names the exact bytes.
31250    #[test]
31251    fn expected_stdout_passes_only_when_both_runs_print_it() {
31252        let golden = "hello world\n";
31253        let matched = attempt_with_expected_stdout(golden, stdout_report(golden, golden), "exit 0");
31254        assert_eq!(matched.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", matched.reason);
31255
31256        let golden_sha = hex_digest(golden.as_bytes());
31257        let other = "hello_world\n";
31258        let other_sha = hex_digest(other.as_bytes());
31259        let agreed_wrong =
31260            attempt_with_expected_stdout(golden, stdout_report(other, other), "exit 0");
31261        assert_eq!(agreed_wrong.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", agreed_wrong.reason);
31262        assert_eq!(agreed_wrong.error_kind, None);
31263        assert_eq!(
31264            agreed_wrong.reason,
31265            Some(format!(
31266                "verify first run stdout (12 bytes, sha256 {other_sha}) differs from the declared expected_stdout (12 bytes, sha256 {golden_sha})"
31267            ))
31268        );
31269
31270        // A matched report whose two runs printed different bytes never
31271        // reaches the stdout check: the report reader refuses it first, and
31272        // the cell has no verdict rather than a pass.
31273        for report in [stdout_report(other, golden), stdout_report(golden, other)] {
31274            let result = attempt_with_expected_stdout(golden, report, "exit 0");
31275            assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR", "{:?}", result.reason);
31276        }
31277
31278        // An empty declaration is a real assertion, not an absent one.
31279        let empty = attempt_with_expected_stdout("", stdout_report("x", "x"), "exit 0");
31280        assert_eq!(empty.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", empty.reason);
31281        let silent = attempt_with_expected_stdout("", stdout_report("", ""), "exit 0");
31282        assert_eq!(silent.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", silent.reason);
31283    }
31284
31285    /// A report that omits the compared outputs cannot show the declared
31286    /// bytes. The report reader already refuses such a report, and the check
31287    /// itself also refuses to decide rather than pass.
31288    #[test]
31289    fn expected_stdout_without_compared_outputs_is_never_a_pass() {
31290        let mut report = stdout_report("ok\n", "ok\n");
31291        report.compared_outputs = None;
31292        assert_eq!(
31293            check_expected_stdout("ok\n", &report),
31294            Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(
31295                "verification report omitted compared_outputs, so the declared expected_stdout cannot be checked".into()
31296            ))
31297        );
31298        let result = attempt_with_expected_stdout("ok\n", report, "exit 0");
31299        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "ERROR", "{:?}", result.reason);
31300        assert_eq!(
31301            result.error_kind.as_deref(),
31302            Some("incomplete-verification-evidence")
31303        );
31304    }

31306    /// Each compared run is checked on its own, so a second run that alone
31307    /// printed the wrong bytes is named.
31308    #[test]
31309    fn expected_stdout_names_the_run_that_differs() {
31310        let good = stdout_report("ok\n", "ok\n");
31311        assert_eq!(check_expected_stdout("ok\n", &good), Ok(()));
31312        let second = stdout_report("ok\n", "no\n");
31313        let Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error)) = check_expected_stdout("ok\n", &second)
31314        else {
31315            panic!("second-run difference was not a mismatch");
31316        };
31317        assert!(
31318            error.starts_with("verify second run stdout (3 bytes"),
31319            "{error}"
31320        );
31321        // Equal length is not enough; the digest decides.
31322        let first = stdout_report("no\n", "ok\n");
31323        let Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error)) = check_expected_stdout("ok\n", &first)
31324        else {
31325            panic!("first-run difference was not a mismatch");
31326        };
31327        assert!(
31328            error.starts_with("verify first run stdout (3 bytes"),
31329            "{error}"
31330        );
31331    }

31333    /// The exact stderr check mirrors stdout's: each compared run is
31334    /// checked on its own stderr digest, the mismatch reason names the
31335    /// run, and the shared parser reads that reason back.
31336    #[test]
31337    fn expected_stderr_names_the_run_that_differs() {
31338        let stderr_report = |left: &str, right: &str| {
31339            let mut report = stdout_report("ok\n", "ok\n");
31340            let outputs = report.compared_outputs.as_mut().unwrap();
31341            outputs.left.stderr_bytes = left.len() as u64;
31342            outputs.left.stderr_sha256 = hex_digest(left.as_bytes());
31343            outputs.right.stderr_bytes = right.len() as u64;
31344            outputs.right.stderr_sha256 = hex_digest(right.as_bytes());
31345            report
31346        };
31347        assert_eq!(
31348            check_expected_stderr("err\n", &stderr_report("err\n", "err\n")),
31349            Ok(())
31350        );
31351        let second = stderr_report("err\n", "no\n");
31352        let Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Mismatch(error)) = check_expected_stderr("err\n", &second)
31353        else {
31354            panic!("second-run stderr difference was not a mismatch");
31355        };
31356        assert!(
31357            error.starts_with("verify second run stderr (3 bytes"),
31358            "{error}"
31359        );
31360        assert_eq!(
31361            parse_expected_output_failure_reason(&error),
31362            Some(ExpectedOutputFailureReason::ExactStderr {
31363                run: "second".into(),
31364                observed_bytes: 3,
31365                observed_sha256: hex_digest(b"no\n"),
31366                declared_bytes: 4,
31367                declared_sha256: hex_digest(b"err\n"),
31368            })
31369        );
31370        // An empty declaration is a real assertion, not an absent one.
31371        assert_eq!(check_expected_stderr("", &stderr_report("", "")), Ok(()));
31372        assert!(check_expected_stderr("", &stderr_report("x", "x")).is_err());
31373    }

31375    /// Matching bytes never rescue a diverged comparison or a failed Hermit
31376    /// status: the stdout check is one more requirement, not a substitute.
31377    #[test]
31378    fn expected_stdout_cannot_pass_a_diverged_comparison_or_failed_status() {
31379        let mut diverged = stdout_report("ok\n", "ok\n");
31380        diverged.verified = false;
31381        diverged.bitwise_parity = false;
31382        diverged.verdict = Verdict::Diverged;
31383        diverged.first_divergent_record = Some(3);
31384        let result = attempt_with_expected_stdout("ok\n", diverged, "exit 0");
31385        assert_eq!(result.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", result.reason);
31386        assert_eq!(
31387            result.reason.as_deref(),
31388            Some(
31389                "canonical verification did not match: verified=false verdict=diverged bitwise_parity=false"
31390            )
31391        );
31392
31393        let failed = attempt_with_expected_stdout("ok\n", stdout_report("ok\n", "ok\n"), "exit 3");
31394        assert_eq!(failed.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", failed.reason);
31395        assert_eq!(
31396            failed.reason.as_deref(),
31397            Some("verify exited with status 3")
31398        );
31399    }

31401    /// Only a verify cell reads its backend's declaration, and only its own
31402    /// backend's entry.
31403    #[test]
31404    fn only_a_verify_cell_reads_its_own_backends_expected_stdout() {
31405        let mut verify = ptrace_cell("verify");
31406        verify.test.modes.get_mut("verify").unwrap().expected_stdout = BTreeMap::from([
31407            ("ptrace".into(), "p\n".into()),
31408            ("dbt".into(), "d\n".into()),
31409        ]);
31410        assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&verify).as_deref(), Some("p\n"));
31411        verify.id.backend = Some("dbt".into());
31412        assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&verify).as_deref(), Some("d\n"));
31413        verify.id.backend = Some("kvm".into());
31414        assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&verify), None);
31415        for mode in ["chaos", "replay", "naked"] {
31416            let mut other = ptrace_cell(mode);
31417            other.test.modes.get_mut(mode).unwrap().expected_stdout =
31418                BTreeMap::from([("ptrace".into(), "p\n".into())]);
31419            assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&other), None, "{mode}");
31420        }
31421        assert_eq!(cell_expected_stdout(&ptrace_cell("verify")), None);
31422    }

31447    /// Agreeing runs pass a declared marker only when the captured stream
31448    /// both is the compared runs' stdout and contains the marker.
31449    #[test]
31450    fn expected_stdout_contains_requires_the_marker_in_the_compared_stdout() {
31451        let printed = "heap 0x555555559000 0x555555559000\n";
31452        let passed = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
31453            None,
31454            Some("heap "),
31455            stdout_report(printed, printed),
31456            printed,
31457            "exit 0",
31458        );
31459        assert_eq!(passed.outcome, "PASS", "{:?}", passed.reason);
31460
31461        let unmarked = "0x555555559000 0x555555559000\n";
31462        let unmarked_sha = hex_digest(unmarked.as_bytes());
31463        let missing = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
31464            None,
31465            Some("heap "),
31466            stdout_report(unmarked, unmarked),
31467            unmarked,
31468            "exit 0",
31469        );
31470        assert_eq!(missing.outcome, "FAIL", "{:?}", missing.reason);
31471        assert_eq!(missing.error_kind, None);
31472        assert_eq!(
31473            missing.reason,
31474            Some(format!(
31475                "verify stdout ({} bytes, sha256 {unmarked_sha}) does not contain the declared expected_stdout_contains text \"heap \"",
31476                unmarked.len()
31477            ))
31478        );
31479
31480        // A capture that is not the compared bytes proves nothing about
31481        // them, even when it happens to contain the marker.
31482        let foreign = attempt_with_stdout_assertions(
31483            None,
31484            Some("heap "),
31485            stdout_report(unmarked, unmarked),
31486            printed,
31487            "exit 0",
31488        );
31489        assert_eq!(foreign.outcome, "ERROR", "{:?}", foreign.reason);
31490        assert_eq!(
31491            foreign.error_kind.as_deref(),
31492            Some("incomplete-verification-evidence")
31493        );
31494        assert!(
31495            foreign
31496                .reason
31497                .as_deref()
31498                .unwrap()
31499                .starts_with("captured verify stdout ("),
31500            "{:?}",
31501            foreign.reason
31502        );
31503
31504        let mut omitted = stdout_report(printed, printed);
31505        omitted.compared_outputs = None;
31506        assert_eq!(
31507            check_expected_stdout_contains("heap ", printed.as_bytes(), &omitted),
31508            Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(
31509                "verification report omitted compared_outputs, so the declared expected_stdout_contains cannot be checked".into()
31510            ))
31511        );
31512        let second_differs = stdout_report(printed, unmarked);
31513        let Err(ExpectedStdoutError::Unevidenced(error)) =
31514            check_expected_stdout_contains("heap ", printed.as_bytes(), &second_differs)
31515        else {
31516            panic!("a capture unlike the second run must be unevidenced");
31517        };
31518        assert!(
31519            error.contains("is not the second compared run's stdout"),
31520            "{error}"
31521        );
31522    }
